The butterbeer is yummy, I would recommend the frozen version as the other one isn't as good, and you get a Butterbeer cup too! it tastes a bit like a frozen vanilla milkshake.  The first time we went to Islands of Adventure we ended up being in the park for 12hours!! A very long day! The second time we went we decided it was not worth going so early and so instead we went about 1 in the afternoon and we purchased the express pass for the rides. This is 100% worth it! We got straight on pretty much everything and we managed to do all the rides we did the first time but in less than half the time. Unfortunately, the express pass doesnt work on everything in the Harry Potter bit yet but I think it will once its been open a bit longer.  So if you are going to Islands of Adventure go a bit later on in the day and buy the express pass! You will be very glad you did!  Make sure you leave Harry Potter till the end of the day as this is when its gets a bit quieter and make sure you go on the ride in the castle!

We had a great time at Universal Studios and IOA! The rides at IOA were a blast, lots of coasters and speedy thrills. US was also really fun for its nostalgic rides/attractons and overall vibe.  WWHP was really a site to behold! After reading all of the books and watching all of the movies it was really quite cool to be walking through Hogsmeade and Hogwarts drinking a Hogs Head Ale or frosty Butterbeer.  BUT, they have a lot of work to do with WWHP. It is way too small for the amount of demand there is now and in my opinion will be for a long time. It is crammed at ALL times and feels pretty claustrophobic after an hour or so. I really wouldve liked for them to include some additional streets, like maybe a Diagon Alley area within. Also, There are only 2 rides (one of which is really for young children:flight of the Hippogriff) and theres the Forbidden Journey which is a simulator (beware for those that get nauseous on this type) and not even a ride. THEY NEED MORE RIDES! Great Idea but a lot more needs to be done before the idea becomes a true realization.  Also, City Walk was great times, nightime entertainment was top notch and we generally enjoyed the heck out of what it had to offer.  All in all a great park, but...Cant Be Comapred To The Park That Need Not Be Named!

My sons, age 17 and 13, and I just returned from Orlando. We visited Universal's Islands of Adventure and the Harry Potter World on Monday (Aug. 2). We had been warned not to even attempt to go in the morning, due to the long lines, so we showed up around 1pm. The lines were still awful then, but we didn't have to wait in line to get into the Harry Potter section then. We did not purchase the extra Fastpass (approx. $40/each), so each non-Harry Potter ride line we stood in was about 45 minutes to 1 hour long. Even if we had the Fastpass, it can't be used on the main Harry Potter Hogwarts ride, anyway. About 4pm, the park began to slowly clear out somewhat. We went to dinner at the Three Broomsticks Restaurant then, and there was no line. Earlier and later than that, the lines were very long there. The line for the big Harry Potter Hogwarts ride went down to 45 minutes (as opposed to 1 1/2-2 hours) at about 7pm, so we went on it then. It is a totally awesome ride--the best one we have ever been on.  Keep in mind that the Harry Potter section of the park is a very small area in the back corner of the park. It is extremely crowded to even walk through. There are only three rides in it--the big Hogwarts ride, the Dueling Dragons roller coaster, and a small roller coaster with a Hippogriff theme. The lines to even get into the stores in Harry Potter are super long. There are some carts on the street where you can buy some souveniers and one butterbeer cart. These didn't seem to be as long of lines.  I don't see the crowds going down in the near future. Our hotel said that they are booked for the next year with visitors from the United Kingdom coming to see the Harry Potter World. I would say that about 75% of the visitors when we were there were from the U.K., and about 75% of them were adults without children with them, so, even when school starts up again, there will probably be lots of crowds there.

Yeah, there were a lot of people so we waited until after 3pm to check out that area.There was a huge line the hours up until then just to get to that area of the park! We went on the Hippogriff rollercoaster,( 20 min.)and the duelling dragons (15 min) that was really crazy for me as I'm 40 and get motion sickness easily! But I made it! And lastly we got into the major line for Harry's adventure in the castle. The line was long 105min, longer if you had to stow away an item in a locker, do yourself a favor and don't bring extra stuff with you. The line was fun for the most part, LOTS to see, especially once in the castle. I was amazed!! Well worth the wait!! My only regret was that the ride, for me, was too intense. I had to close my eyes halfway because I was getting motion sickness, majorly! Even with my Dramamine. I REALLY didn't want to miss it but had no choice! It rocks you all over and the visual is intense. I couldn't do it a second time! ( I almost lost it on Jimmy Nutron too) But my daughter and I agreed.. it was .well worth everything, people, heat and insane admission prices! We did the all inclusive deal too BTW, mine as well give the money to them all at once and get it over with! We were able to eat whatever we wanted from the various listed restaurants, maybe contributed to my sickness as it's all greasy junk food :) too bad Butterbeer wasn't included as we are now addicted! I though the park was clean and fun, the people were friendly and the bathrooms were fine. I wouldn't dis Universal over Disney, but if you have older kids I think this park has bigger, more thrilling rides for them. Mickey's cute but I never lost my stomach on it's a small world!

Don't be misled. The Harry Potter Theme park is really nice to look at. Just that the hype leading to it was bigger than the theme park. Long lines to enter shops. This is expected considering that it was new. About the rides. There are 3. 2 rebadged ones which people queued to ride. The old dueling dragons ride was rebadged as the Dragon Challenge. The Flight of the Hippogriff was the same ride a years (when I was there) . Over all, I might give Harry Potter a pass were it not for the new ride "forbidden journey". This last ride is fantastic and alone, made the whole Harry Potter experience worthwhile. A word about the express pass. I dropped by a booth and they were selling it for $50+. this was at 9 a.m.! Allows us to bypass lines all over the park EXCEPT the Forbidden Journey. I did a double take and a repeat-after-me to the girl selling the express pass. This was for the best and new ride in Harry Potter. Good thing I gave it a pass. I will recommend this attraction to a friend only because of the Forbidden Journey ride. Nothing else.

You know I think it very sad that these huge conglomrates have the audacity to strip you of every penny you have. I know Universal is not Disney but I am sure that old Walt would turn in his grave at the simple fact that hard working families, who save up all year, are taken for every hard earned penny in their pockets. How dare they charge 15 dollars to park your car(20 dollars for rich twits), and then search your bags, not for security but to make sure you do not have your own food or drink, and thus are forced into buying their own overpriced rubbish, and yes it is all rubbish convenience food. And the final insult is the Express Card. Is not 80 dollars enough to pay these fat cats for the priviledge of entering this outdated and worn attraction. No! Another 50 bucks if you do not to wait in line for two hours, as we did, admittedly in August. OK, there are a couple of new rides, but that old plastic white shark has got to go. Harry Potter ville is very good but is far too small and should have been built in the UK. I am pretty sure that JK Rowling would be ashamed that her fans were waiting for up to 3 hours to get in the castle. However, the actual ride is excellent and the detail that has gone into this new section is superb, but to wait for 2 hours to get into Ollivanders shop is not acceptable. To conclude, I think that this park is fine for starry eyed first timers, but just be aware that your pocket money will trickle away at an alarming rate as your kids will demand every available treat. And when you get home and see your bank statement, the fat cats will be laughing all the way to the bank. Have a nice day! Pedro of Pobla

Went to IOA this past week on a friday. Good thing we had the early admission to the park. We went through all of harry potter within 1 hr and could've ridden all the rides again with no wait. Probably around 10 am, is when it started to get crowded. Universal did a good job with harry potter. We went around the rest of IOA after harry potter, basically no wait to the other rides, spiderman and Jurassic park. Going a friday, mostly teens, older adults and some college kids, minimal amount of very little kids. Mostly the crowds were at harry potter, waiting period around 11-3 pm for the harry potter rides 30min to 60 mins.

It may have been a bad day when we were there but a lot of the rides had problems. The Rip Ride Rockit was not working properly and so you could not choose your own music and I see others have said there have been problems with this ride. There were also problems with Men In Black and I am sure The Mummy was slower than normal. I do love all the classic rides here though like Jaws. The Simpsons ride is great. Assuming it is not peak season you can do this park in half a day although if you have the time you may as well take it slowly as it will be hot. Universal staff are not particuarly friendly and unfortunately I am used to the friendliness of Disney so find this quite disappointing. This park is beginning to look a bit dated in places (I have been 4 times in the last 8 years) but I am not sure what they need to do. Although there were hardly any queues here when you do queue it is quite often out in the heat of the sun so a hat is a good idea.  Any questions just ask

This review for Univ Studios park, not the Island of Adv park which is at the same location, but separate park and fee.  Other than the Rock it ride (which was closed the day I went) and the Mummy ride - all other rides at Universal Studios are theather shows or you sit in a car/carriage for a bumpy simulation. And walmart must have had a firesale on misters because every show/ride has mist spray (which gets old). The signage states" you will get wet" - should read you will get annoyingly misted like every ride in the park.  Solo snub - whether it is a conscious effort or just park employee training - they do not support or cater to a solo traveller. Examples include being ignored at the gate walk in by picture takers, picture helpers, service desks for additional ticket sales, most rides (with a few exceptions) you will get back row corner, and the restaurants.  Universal just doesn't get it. As a solo traveller I am here because I want to be and probably spending more money than that family of four. I have no one to take my picture so I will buy that photo at the gate, you have single rider lines - used them (they were closed not for use) And at a sit down restaurant I am coming in to sit down and have dinner. NO I don't want to sit at the bar, if I did I would go to the bar - i just stood in20 min line at the restaurant door, at least give me the chance to say NO i don't want to go to bar ---- but instead you put me there with the very loud band no offer of a table like the other guests. ((To the credit of bar tender, I asked for re-seating in the sit down area and was accomodated.)) Ticket sales for shows - guess what, I am travelling alone and a show is an awesome entertainment option -- but you ignore that solo traveller.  When I mentioned this to one of the booth attendants (who i had to ask if she would take time to sell me a ticket to Blue Man as she walked away from counter when I walked up) she said that I looked too nice and well dressed and she thought i was an employee or business person. Are you kidding ??? because I am not wearing my PJs in public, dressed like poll dancer or some one who just got out of the pool - I am not worth your time or sales ? ( I was wearing BR slacks, white blouse and comfortable shoes - nothing fancy here folks, just modest and comfortable).

Those visiting for HHN, be warned. They have teams of security looking for under age drinking and parents who may pass a drink to their kids to hold. Even if your kid is holding the drink for a second, they'll take you to a large processing area, take away your tickets, and ban you for a year. If you argue, you'll be arrested. Many people have been arrested for arguments with security. Do yourself a favor and stay away. The new HP shopping mall has long lines. The new roller coaster is always broke, because it's a carnival coaster.

End of September is a great time to visit Universal. If you start off early when the gates open you can avoid long lines and get a lot more done! I had a great time. The rides were fun and it wasn't too hot to walk around!

We arrived at Universal Studios about 2 hrs. prior to opening on the opening day of The Wizarding World of Harry Potter. Once we were in, we were informed that it would be about 9 hours before we would be allowed to enter that section of the park. I feel that park officials should have been better prepared for the crowds. I saw virtually no one in line to purchase tickets. This means that almost all of the tickets for that day were prepurchased. We did return the next day, and things were much better. Once we got to the main ride, my husband tries the test seat outside the ride and fit. We waited in line for the ride, and when we were almost to the front he tried a second test seat. No problem. As the rest of our family boarded the ride, his seat would not fasten. He is not "Pooh Sized." He is 6'2" and has a tall upper body. I have heard that they have changed the seats, but I would verify it before going again. The ride was amazing! But it was disappointing that we all could not ride.
Amazing night of fright at Universal Studios....definitely worth the visit!

We visited Universal Studio's Wizarding World of Harry Potter in August 2010...my mom, my 15-year old daughter and myself. The theme park is really fun, but it was also unbelievably crowded. My daughter and I are huge Harry Potter fans and grandma is a fan as well, but not quite as serious.  We stayed at a Universal hotel so we got early access and could skip lines on some of the rides. The early admission and line skipping made the whole day worth it. We got in really early and went straight to the Forbidden Journey ride which we couldn't skip the line on. It was an amazing ride and well worth the short wait that early in the morning. Later in the evening we went back to do it again and wait over two hours!  During the middle of the day when it was most hot and crowded, we went back to our hotel, went swimming and took naps, then went back to the theme park in the evening.  We spent a fortune to have this one day in Harry Potter world, so it's not something I'll do again, but it was really fun.

We woke up early to get to Universal as the rope dropped to get to The World of Harry Potter. We literally raced to the end of the park to go straight to the big ride. (Which was amazing - I didn't go ON the ride; daughter and hubby did, but I saw parts of the attraction from the other side.) The details from the books and movies were incredible, however...  The Park Started to Fill Up within an Hour and... there were LINES TO GO INTO THE SHOPS!!!!! Are you kidding me??? The shops are the size of a small bedroom. How do they expect people to go in??? I couldn't believe that we actually waited 20 minutes to go into one. And, not the wand store either which had a line around the bend and didn't move for hours.  Either Universal screwed up or I just don't know. We visited on a Monday which one of the workers said was the best day to come as the crowds get worse as the week progresses. There really is no excuse for this. The tickets were expensive enough (and the roundtrip taxi from Disney came to $75!)  The park is awesome, but the waiting is crazy!

Had a fabulous time in Orlando in October, when the weather is cooler and the crowds are down. The Wizarding World of Harry Potter is AMAZING! The Forbiden Journey ride is soooo cool - very high tech and realistic. Lunch at the Three Broomsticks, complete with butter beer, was great! For Harry Potter fans this place is Mecca, Graceland, and Neverland. Can't wait to go back! We all want to live at Hogwarts!

For those who want either a change of pace from Disney World or are looking for less kid-oriented rides/rollercoasters, Universal is the place to be. If you're like me and my boyfriend (we're 27), you won't need to a lot a ton of time there, unless you go during the busy season. We went in late January and were able to see everything and ride most of the best rides twice in only 1 day. This was before the addition of the Harry Potter area and the Simpsons ride, so this may have changed a little. All in all, I would definitely recommend Universal - if only for The Mummy, The Hulk, and Dueling Dragons alone.

Visited for first time. Looks just like you stepped into the movie. Butterbeer tastes like a creamy root beer with whipped cream on top. Stores are super small and you have wait on line to get in. 1 1/2 hrs to get into Olivanders, 20 min for Dervish and Banges. 40 min wait for 3 bromsticks which is a cafeteria type line. Dont forget to order somehing or you'll have to wait on line again. Food was good and atmosphere was great. Look for Dobby's shadow in the rafters. If you just want to buy a wand without the experience, they sell them at stores at front of park. Castle ride is great but has funky seats n people we saw who were not even big people had to request modified seats. They did a good job but have some things that need fixing.
Hadn't been to Universal since I was a kid and Halloween Horror Nights was a great time to revisit. I would recommend getting the express pass.

Just got back from 2 weeks in Orlando, We booked with Virgin holidays and bought our universal tickets from virgin which entitiled us to a complimentary breakfast at the three broomsticks and early entry in to the park( though the park gates open 45 mins early so we didn't technically have that time). please read the small print you have to see a rep within 2 days of arriving to organise it. Not a problem for us as it was our sons b'day 2 days after we arrived and we planned to do the visit on his b'day. We arrived as requested at 7am, the breakfast was terrible but we managed to get in the queue for Olivanders before it opened so only had to wait 20 mins. The Birthday Boy badge worked because fortunately out of the 30 odd people who entered the wand shop our son and his sister got picked for "the show". The main ride in the castle broke down so we weren't able to ride that day, but when we went back another day it was amazing and no queue we walked straight on, We thought the whole depiction was amazing but then we weren't experiencing the same amount of visitors in November as possibly the summer visitors did. I would say go 2nd week in November, not huge amounts of people and thoroughly enjoyable all three rides were fabulous when they worked. :-)

We went to Universal on Xmas break. Over $600.00 for our group to get in and we spent the whole afternoon to get on one ride. Express tickets, sold out. Priority parking,sold out. Human gridlock, music so loud you had to scream to converse and long lines for everything from bathroom to food. Biggest waste of a day our whole vacation.  Save this attraction for off peak season, if at all!

We have just returned from Hard Rock Hotel to visit Universal Studios Wizarding World of Harry Potter with a party of eight. Even though this was absolutely the worst time to visit this park, I must tell you it was worth the wait, the money and the sleep deprivation. The Hotel is expensive, there are cheaper hotels nearby, but the perks for staying at the Hard Rock made it worth it. The Hard Rock Hotel staff even though they seemed to push smiles, did not have the information needed for travelers to Universal or their hotel (they need the 411 for their customers). The reason to stay at the hotel is the distance to the parks; Hard Rock is the closest to the parks, the early entrance to the parks and the best part, express ride access to most rides. The Hotel standard rooms are larger than typical, very clean and the beds were heaven. We asked for our room to be on the first floor which gave us immediately exiting to the path that leads to the parks. Short cuts are noteworthy. The pool is large and the kids loved the music underwater. We did not have a chance to visit the health club but it was busy and other families liked it. IF you have a car, parking is $15.00 per day and valet is $22.00, if you are not going to use your car, why pay for the upgrade? The Palm restaurant (expensive) held up to its reputation in service and food, I highly recommend it. I highly recommend this Hotel for families and adults alike. Universal Studios theme park: We were able to enter the park at 7am and beat any outside crowds. Well let me tell you all three hotels were sold out so we had a crowd anyway. Our main reason this visit was to see the Harry Potter world. We were just down here last spring break to see it, but because of its delayed opening, missed it. The crowds were unbelievably large for the holidays. Just to get into line for the 7am entrance we had to wait 10 minutes. The park did have a system to handle the crowds and it did work until 9am. At 9am when the general public entered the WWHP, they literally ran to the rides causing some kids to fall down. We felt terrible watching the kids and adults very happy to enter the WWHP but not aware that they were running and causing a possible stampede. The park did not seem to have enough employees to guide the crowds or keep them informed on the length and time they were to stand in line. The main attractions are; a ride called forbidden journey, which takes you through Hogwarts School into the halls with talking pictures, Dumbledore’s office with details such as the memory pool, a classroom with Harry, Hermione and Ron and other rooms. Take pictures, this is the place! The ride is tough for tiny ones, but walk through it anyway to see it because before you actually get into the seat, there is a room for those that are not able to take the ride. Kudos to Universal to be thoughtful and provide a room with a HP movie playing to keep you occupied. The shops such as Ollivanders, which 20 people enter the shop and only one is picked to receive a wand. Actually the wand picks you, very cute, just like the book, done very well. Only half of us got into see this due to the lines. Honeydukes the candy store must buy a chocolate frog ($10) even if you save it for Valentine’s Day. Dervish and Banges a store that has not only sells wands ($30.00) but shirts, sweats, hoodies, scarfs($31), ties, key chains and more. We were trying to find a scarf only to find they were out and would be out for a week. Believe it or not all ages want this, from grammar to high school and even the college kids. I think we need to remember the college kids grew up with Harry Potter books and still adore them. I even tried to buy a scarf off of an employee’s neck and they refused. I still need 4!!! No coffee or Tea shop for adults to sit at. The restaurant is The Three Broomsticks. Even though they offer two outside carts that sells Butter Beer, you should buy it at the bar in Three Broomsticks, just like Harry, and sit at one of the tables. You avoid the long lines and can revive your party. The details such as the corner table where Harry sat and the shrunken heads are in the pub area. They offer food on one end and a pub on the other. They do have a breakfast with reservations only, so please call ahead to reserve, it books quickly. The hotel did not know this! If you go at night the lighting is horrible, no joke. It was hard to see the walkway at times and the signage had absolutely no lighting to read it. Wheelchairs, scooters and strollers had a very difficult time at night managing the crowds due to poor visibility. I do recommend this part of the park for anyone who enjoys the books and movies of Harry Potter. Hope to return soon myself!
organised, fun, and everything was in working order

We visited Universal for the first time on January 18th and 29th, 2011. My family thoroughly enjoyed both the "Islands of Adventure", and the "Universal" parks. We spent one day at each park so we could take our time to fully explore what each "side" had to offer. My best advice here is to avoid weekends and holidays if possible. The "Wizarding World" is a huge draw and the crowds reflect the curiosity of Harry Potter fans. Having said that, we loved the Wizarding World. It is so authentic. If you're not a Harry Potter fan you wouldn't understand. We had Butterbeer, bought a wand, ate at the Hogsmeade restaurant, and rode the 3 major rides. This area of the park just gets busier and busier as the day goes on. Go there first when the lines are the shortest. The shops get very crowded, but my family agreed it was worth it! As for the rest of "Islands of Adventure" and "Universal"; lots of fun for everyone. The parks are very clean. Rides and attactions terrific. The prices are not too bad. The Universal side has some really nice restaurants. If you are a theme park buff you will enjoy Universal immensly!!

I bought online a two-day park hopper ticket, online prices can save you dollars and time queing. You can have your tickets mailed, or pick theme up using a reservation number and credit card on the will-call kiosks near the entrance of the parks. No queues at all in the kiosks.  I have to say that I visited the park off-peak, mid-week and as a solo traveler, which means I was able to shorten the 30 minute wait times to 15 minutes or less. Which definitely makes the visit more enjoyable.  The Harry Potter area was crowded at certain hours and there were queues for getting into the Dervish and Banges store and Ollivander's but not for entering the other stores. As a HP fan and was able to enjoy the park and notice the small details (decoration and theming is very detailed).  The Three Broomsticks restaurant is nicely themed but queues form on lunch time (so go mid-morning or mid-afternoon). For $17 I had OK fish and chips and a Butterbeer. Butterbeer is worth tasting. And just a dollar more expensive than the sodas on the rest of the kiosks.  TIPS: You can enter Dervish and Banges from the backdoor to avoid the queues or just after riding the Dragon Challenge.  Instead of eating $9 hot dogs at the kiosks, I went to the Mythos restaurant on the lost continent Island. For a few dollars more I had much better food (Panini + 2 cokes for $15)  I definitely recommend going there off-peak and use the single visitor lines unless you want to buy the pictures after the ride. By the way, if you need to store something in the lockers use ones on the entrance of the park and not the ones near the attractions as those are more expensive and don't allow you to repopen.

I will never book a vacation with Universal Studios ever again! It is frustrating, tiring, and maddening!  It all began on December 26, 2010, the night before our scheduled flight to Florida. A gigantic snow storm closed down the airport we were to fly out of. The earliest flight the airline could get us out of was December 30th around midnight. We were scheduled to come home on January 2nd which left us 2 whole days in Florida. 2 days is really not enough so we decided to cancel the whole trip instead.  We spoke with a representative at Universal Vacations and she told us there’d be a $200 charge for cancelling but everything else would be refunded back to our American Express within 3 weeks. We thought that was fine and asked her to go ahead with the cancellation.  3 weeks later – no refund in sight. When we spoke with another representative at Universal, she told us that because so many people have cancelled, it might take a little longer. “Just wait another week,” she said.  Well, another week went by and still nothing. This time another representative actually told us that we never cancelled the vacation package! Why would we have called those two times if we weren’t cancelling? I certainly wasn’t calling just to chat with someone about the weather! So she said that she’s sorry, blah blah blah, and she’ll try to expedite the refund – we’ll have to wait another 7 business days.  Two more weeks went by and well, you’ve guessed it, still nothing. I called again. This time they told me I should receive it by next week. @#$%&$#&@%#&@%$#@!!! I decided to speak to a supervisor to complain about the situation but she kept telling me the same sentence over and over, “We will process the refund today.” The supervisor said that she shouldn’t even be talking to me because their policy states that she should only speak with whoever booked the package (we had gone through AAA to book the package because of the discounts AAA provided). First they keep putting off the refund, now they don’t want to speak to me?!? GRRRRRRR!!!  I think I’ll stick with Disney from now on. Disney has great customer service & goes out of their way to help every time – even if it’s a small problem. Universal will never become as good as or better than Disney at the rate they’re going.

I'll try to be brief. I feel robbed or at least cheated with our recent visit. It cost over 500.00 and received almost nothing but aggravation. Parking was slow and took at least 20 minutes. Attendants were yelling at guests. We were yelled at to get our stroller off a walk way. We were solicited to buy a credit card. After a long walk we were confronted with another long wait to buy tickets (45 minutes) and more sales attempts (this same process took about 5 minutes at Disney at half the cost). After the hike to Harry Potter we were turned away to go wait in another long line for a timed entrance pass in a very crowed area, also getting yelled at because the whole family was in line not just a representative. (Why this couldn’t be addressed at ticketing or at least the info for the need to get another ticket!) During the day I was only able to go on 3 rides, my family 4. At Disney the hours were always extended due to crowds, at Universal it was the opposite. An employee told us closing was at 8:00 but after assuming there was time to eat (at the worst food in the world, Burger Digs.. We left finding the park closed at 7:00 and unable to do ANYTHING else. At Disney parks we could see characters, shop and linger, nothing at Universal. Harry Potter was somewhat well done but not made for crowds at all, again yelled at for going the wrong way or wrong door. Then the family was subjected to walking thru all the bars and party atmosphere on leaving, not meant for a family. I will never return, I truly feel foolish for throwing away hard earned money to be miserable and feel like I was an inconvience not a guest. If there were a money back guarantee I would be asking for my money back, what a rip off. We left Disney feeling happy with a wonderful experience we left Universal feeling like the only interest was to make money, which of course it is.

The 6 of us just returned yesterday from a week long vacation to Orlando. We used touringplans, com to come up with a way to cram 4 WDW parks and the 2 Universal Parks into essentially five days. After carefully reviewing several guide books, the touring planning site and some discussion boards I opted to visit Islands of Adventure at Universal on Thursday March 3rd 2011. I was grateful for this choice later on!  We arrived at the gates about 45 minutes early before the park opening at 9am. We were the second people in line for our line. Be advised the parking structure is a bit of a ways from the gates, you go through several moving side walks and then citiwalk with shops and restaurants first. I was SO GLAD we arrived early because as the time got near to opening the lines behind us stretched over the bridge and into Citiwalk to get in! We got right in and took the path through Suess Land straight for Harry Potter. I would advise either doing Harry Potter at park opening (or before if you're a resort guest) or right at the end of the park day. I DO NOT recommend attempting to visit mid day or on a weekend unless you like to wait in lines or have no other choice.  We were amongst the first people in Harry Potter that day. Hogsmeade was virtually empty and it was fun to walk through. What a great recreation! The snow is fun to look at in 80F weather. All the details are incredible and we were very impressed. We headed straight for Forbidden Journey and walked right on. Hogwarts has a great queue, and be sure to stop and see the little shows, sorting hat, Ron making it snow, ect on your way. This ride is intense if you're prone to motion sickness. I would also advise not taking younger children who are easily scared even if they meet the height requirement. The spiders who "spit" at you right in your face and the dementors were quite frightening. My 9 yr old closed her eyes, but didn't scream or anything and she's very hearty. We rode this ride again at park closing and walked right on repeatedly about 30 mins before the park closed. During the morning we got right on the flight of the Hippogriff, and rode both sides of the Dragon coaster numerous times with very little wait. Butterbeer was awesome..i preferred regular, but I tasted the frozen (gave me immediate brain freeze and hurt my stomach!). There was no queue for buying that either. We wandered in the shops about the time the crowds started pouring in Hogsmeade. Yes the shops are very small and hard to shop in. We skipped Ollivander's Wand shop because the queue was immediately ridiculous and my girls didn't really care about that experience. We took photos with the conductor in front of the train as well. We then headed out of there as it began to get so crowded it wasn't enjoyable anymore, and we noticed it remained that way for most of the day.  We did the rest of Islands of Adventure according to a guide book that suggested going counter clockwise. We road Jurassic park (yes you get wet especially if there's heavier riders in your boat!), did the Popeye raft ride (absolute soaker don't ride unless you have spare clothes, a rain jacket or poncho, or it's blazing hot!), the ripsaw falls had just opened and was doing test runs but closed to riders for the day which was disappointing. Dinosaur was scary...in the dark, in a "car" dinos jumping out at you and very jerky if you have neck problems. My girls did fine in there however. We enjoyed the toon section, Cat in the Hat ride, train ride, one fish two fish. We loved marvel super hero island. We rode Spiderman several times and it was up there with our favorite rides for this trip. Amazing realistic effects! The Hulk was also a huge hit and ridden repeatedly. My 9 year old loved it! We had a reasonably priced lunch of a whole pizza as well. Back to Harry Potter before our departure to do it all again with little to no crowds.  All in all a great park experience. Our favorite of our entire trip. Universal has done it right. Everything was clean, organized, no huge lines if you plan it right, fun and neat adventures and shows. I would highly recommend a visit here if you go on a week day or early morning hours. But plan it! Don't go on a whim and then be disappointed by super crowds limiting your experience.

I went to the Islands of Adventure side only on March 15, 2010 with my husband, two teen boys, and young boy. We invested in the fast pass to bypass all lines. Seuss Landing was very neat, and our youngster enjoyed that section. Super Hero Island was a favorite. The Spider Man ride was very neat. Most realistic 4D ride I've ever been on. The teens loved the Hulk ride, too. We didn't spend much time in Toon Lagoon, as that is mostly restaurants and carnival style games. We took a lot of pictures in Jurassic Park and enjoyed the River Adventure ride there, too. Harry Potter was the big letdown for us. The area looks awesome. You can see the snow-tipped castle from a long ways away. We saved that section until later since none of us were very schooled in the Harry Potter saga. Unfortunately, there are apparently strict limits as to the number of occupants allowed on the island. We were nearly denied entry but convinced a guard to let us in. If Harry Potter is high on your list, make sure you get there immediately to get "return tickets" that give you a time to actually get in the island. Once on the island it was very cramped. The "streets" are quite small, lines are very long, and it was hard to even know where stores/ restrooms/ attractions were because of the crowds. Overall, this was a good day. Everyone found something he/she enjoyed. I do recommend saving some time at the end of your day to explore the City Walk. This was a neat boardwalk/ ped mall kind of section on the way into the parks. There were some neat stores there and an enjoyable atmosphere.

We went in November 2010 we had got the tickets through Virgin and early access to the park one day. It was excellant, everyone we met or spoke to couldn't have been more helpful, the whole place was spotless and all the team members appeared to be enjoying their jobs, it was a pleasure to walk round. We stopped and had our caricature done by Ron near the rip saw falls and he was lovely and we went a couple of other times to the park and he remebered us and made a point of saying hello. Just the little things made it great, like the Grinch being mischeivious when we were trying to take a picture and the team offering to take a picture of us with Shrek or scooby do, The park wasn't that busy when we went and we hardly had to queue so I wouldn't recommend the fast passes. If you go to florida you have to do Universal Studios, if you stay on International drive get the I ride Trolley to Wet and Wild and its a 15 min walk from there to the entrance which saves $15 on parking.

we expected it to be expensiveand it is, but the quality of the food there is dreadful - mostly 'fast food' rubbish, including cold, slimey fries, dry sandwiches,and very very few choices. We recommend taking 'good food' with you and water as well. Our biggest disappointment was with the Harry Potter ride. It was difficult to judge what it was like from the outside as all rides seem to have the same 'warnings' on them. I would suggest a rating of say 1 to 5 based on motion, scaryness, or some other variable to give people more information about rides before they go on them. Neither of us are particularly squeamish but this ride is a violent and vomit-inducing experience that I wouldn't recommend to anyone. We felt we had somehow 'survived' the experience, rather than enjoyed it.

Universal Studios is poorly laid out, lacking staff, lacking knowledgeable staff and not a great value. It was confusing, crowded and expensive. The Harry Potter area was visually interesting, but so crowded that there was 45 minute wait just to get into a gift shop. Harry Potter is a separate ticket and you have to stand in a long line to get a ticket and then stand in a line to get into the area, and then stand inline for a ride, food or shopping. It was so crowded there was a two hour wait for the Hogwarts ride and staff said "It was very crowded compared to other days." They definitely over sold the Harry Potter area. If they were truly limiting tickets to certain hours, it was too many people. Good luck in finding first aid, a shady rest spot or anyone to answer a questions.

My daughter was looking forward to going to the Harry Potter attractions at Universal. Yet when we arrived we found the park to be misleading and unorganized. We were shuffled through numerous lines in order to even enter Harry Potter World, and once we arrived at the final stand-by line we had to stand in the unbearable heat for over an hour. To top it off, while we were in line the one drink stand ran out of water! When we finally got into the park all of the rides were over an hour wait and the heat was so excruciating that it was impossible to wait, can't they install some fans for those waiting? Overall, my daughter only got to go on one ride at the entire park of Universal because the line waits were ridiculous. We would have bought the express package if the prices weren't already so absurd. This park is NOTHING compared to Disney. Universal should take a training course from Disney so they can learn how to run a park.

I found Disney to be too spread out and a lot of the rides that werent aimed at kids were old and tired looking. Universal on the other hand was as handy as it could be with both parks right beside eachother and within walking distance from I Drive. Most days I went to the park mid afternoon to avoid most of the queues (and the heat) and was rewarded with shorter lines and a much more pleasant experience. The rides here are way better than anything I experienced at Disney (with the exception of the tower of terror) the mummy ride, hulk, jurassic park, dr doom, harry potter, simpsons and rip ride rockit rides were all first class. Don't shy away from the cartoon area in IOA like I nearly did, it has some pretty good rides like rip saw falls and the bilge rat barge, however expect to get wet, no matter where on the ride you sit expect to get soaked! The eateries in the two parks are average, with all seemingly serving the exact same choices of food. A better bet would be to venture out unto city walk and give the hard rock cafe or nascar a try! Overall these two parks are well worth a visit, even more so with a fast pass to beat the long queues in that heat!

I went to Universal a few weeks ago and they had some great rides. I loved the Mummy ride, Simpson ride and Spiderman was awesome! We went to Universal Studio's the 2nd day of our trip after Harry Potter. It was nice because it wasnt crowded and the most wait time was15 minutes. I liked the way the rides were set up because as hot as it was outside we stayed cool with most of them being inside or under cover. Even know i liked the Unversal Islands better this was a nice park and i will be back next year!

Really enjoyed the visit to Universal. The attractions were spectacular and we found that we could not see everything in the day. We even saw some celebrities. Found that the cost of food items was fairly expensive and this was perhaps the only down size.

The universal theme park is not adrenaline heavy, that's what island of adventures is for. You will need a full day to complete all the shows/rides, it is more entertaining than you would think at the behining, you'd be smiling and enjoying the time in there. Expect lengthy intro to each attraction. It doesn't get as crowded as IOA but still a long queue at the roller coasters.

My wife and I visited on a Thursday at the end of June. I was coming back after 10 years and remembered some of the attractions, which were getting dated, such as Twister, Jaws, Terminator, ET. The newer stuff (Shrek 4-D), Rip Ride Rocket (excellent), and Simpsons were serviceable but with the exception of the roller coaster, were much more pointed towards children. As adults without children, I would suggest Islands of Adventure if you had to make a choice. With kids, Universal would have been good for them.
The park was very clean and the workers were all very nice and helpful. Plenty to see and do. City walk is great with its returants and shops and night clubs.

I recently visited the Universal theme park in Orlando as I have done many time before and this time I was very disappointed with the Fireworks display they put on for the 4th July celebrations. This used to be one of the best firework displays around but this time it was very poor. The firework display in SeaWorld that is put on every evening during the summer months is far, far better than what universal offered. So for the 4th July fireworks in Orland I would recommend Disney and totally forget about Universal. Other than that the Universal theme park is a great place to spend your vacation.
This is the best park I've been to in my life and I'm sure my family will agree with me aswell.I mean more people need to go to this park because they will find they will love it

My family has been to most of them and we all agree that Islands of Adventure rated the worst. We opted for the lower level fast-pass to shorten our wait times, but approx 600 hundred dollars for just the tickets for a family of four - I got ripped off. Most hi-end parks we end up closing the place because there's so much to see & do but here we were done by 4pm.  My teens love fast roller coasters, so deuling dragons and the HULK were fun! But most of the other rides felt outdated. Poseidon looked so cool on the outside! But it comes across as silly inside. Jurassic Park - yawn. Dr. Seuss land was visually stunning, but nothing for teens there. Superhero section was also weak - but we rode HULK multiple times and that was great.  Half my family are Harry Potter fans - so we waited 45 minutes in line JUST TO GET A TICKET TO ENTER Harry Potter village later in the day. When it was our time it was so crowded you could barely get through it - constantly squeezing your way through the crowds. There were 30 minute waiting lines to get into any of the shops. Probably about 15 minute wait for a mug of butter beer. We threw away a couple of hours there and saw next to nothing. The HP ride was ok. I find rides that rely on you watching video screens tend to make me nauseous.  Lunch was another disaster. We waited in a line for over a half hour in the hot sun and only two people walked away with food. Haven't they been doing this a while? Haven't they figured out how to sell product to the masses day in and out? Apparently not. We bailed out of line and grabbed a water and a pretzel at a cart. TIP for those still willing to waste their hard earned money and go: for lunch go back to the entrance because there are more dining options.  Save some money, increase your fun, and go to a Six-Flags - most that I've been to were a lot more fun than this. Disney & Sea World also kick butt on this place.

I was extremely impressed! I am so glad we did 2 days here. 1 at each park. From the covered parking garage to the rides, it was all such high quality. I felt like we were being pampered! The park was clean, food was great, rides were fun. We went with a 12 and 15 year old. My 15 year old and myself had more fun here than the other well known place in Orlando. We could all ride everything together. There are so many simulator rides here and those are so cool! Harry Potter land was packed but so worth the wait on the main ride there. It was amazing! It feels like you're right in the movie. I suggest hit this part first thing, early a.m. It gets really packed later. I wish we wouldhave stayed at one of the universal resort hotels because with some of them you get a "Fast Pass" which isn't free otherwise. Something to definitely look into! The stores there were great too. We even stopped at the "dinner reservation" cart in the park and asked about the Hard Rock. They told us they don't take reservations but they gave us a preferred seating ticket with a $5 coupon and we got right in. It's so convenient to have all that right there. We spent about 8 hours in each park and did almost every ride there. They even have free lockers up to a certain amount of time. I never paid for 1 and used one several times. Also the moving "flat escalators" were very nice for my son who was recovering from a fractured ankle. We had a blast!

Universal is far superior to Disney. Lines where not too bad 15-40 mins and directions where plentiful and clear - unlike Disney! Had good time in both parks but Universal ( + adventure land) gets the family vote . Initial pricing seems high but for 10-12 hrs a day it's GREAT VALUE!

We did btw parks which easily need a day each, we eat in the Hard Rock and also saw the Blue man group. The Islands of adventure is great with some great roller coasters. The twilight zone tower of terror great fun. Harry Potter was mobbed so we did not wait for the 90 mins fete ed for a 40min wait. This was a truly excellent simulator, we spent a lot of money on photos, VIPs and a wand so be warned it's a costly trip. We did upgrade for a fast pass for the day which was a good idea or you spend all day waiting. However I now wince at the credit card bill. A great park.

We visited the parks mid-July and did both in 1 1/2 days not feeling like we missed out on much. The most helpful tip I had received before leaving proved true: we got there early on both days (8:30am) and the longest line we did was for The Forbidden Journey (about 50min).  Universal Studios: we did this park at the end of the 1st day (got there around 4pm and it wasn't that crowded) and on the 2nd day (we left around 2:30pm). We really liked how it has older and newer attractions and our favorites were the Rip Ride Rockit, Spiderman and The Mummy. The park was very clean, and the longest we waited there was probably for the Terminator because it's a show. There is plenty of shade (more than in IoA) and I feel the park is more family oriented than IoA. Because the lines weren't too long we could use the lockers for free, which allowed us to always have our water and food with us. I found the staff to be friendly and helpful. My main critic is that you have to pay for the express pass, but there are also single riders line on some attractions that are as fast as the express line. ->Tips<- - get there early morning or late afternoon - have a good breakfast, pack snacks and drinks - bring flipflops for water rides, sneakers for the rest - bring a rain jacket (so you don't buy junk rain ponchos) - eat outside of the park if you can (had lunch at the Hard Rock, was very filling, we got free refills and the price was reasonable: $35 for 2) - bring a backpack - use single riders line when available (cuts wait time and it doesn't make a big difference who you're sitting next to anyway) - take plenty of pictures and enjoy!  Islands of Adventure: see review on the specific page

is a great park, but the should have more different restaurant that were you can do the meal deal , not just 3 places or at least let you get more soda in different location so you can refill anywhere, but over all is a decent price for the the meal deals and will probably get it again, park was slow so we were able to go in the attraction much quicker but it better to plan the whole day before heading to the parks and if its slow not to get the express pass, i cant wait to go back down for hallowing horror nights.

I have been to Universal studios and Islands of Adventure approx 20 times. Easy parking and its covered so your car not like the surface of the sun when you return Rides are fantastic especially the Mummy and The Hulk - best roller coasters EVER!! Food plenty choice and reasonable price for a theme park Make sure you take a change of clothes and put them in a locker then do all the water rides so you can put on dry shorts and undies so at least you have a dry B-M for the day. Facilities are great. We went in 2010 to go to see the new Harry Potter/Hogwarts etc - Very disappointed. There are 3 rides and 2 of them are old rides with a new name on them. The 3rd ride is a "flying" ride that was out of focus on the screen and kept breaking down - really bad The town setting is really well built and very acurate but the queues to get into any of the shops is a nightmare so we left very disappointed and £300 lighter. Would wait at least 12 months before you see this to let the mobs die down or go in winter.

I hate to say it, but this park was disappointing and not very much fun; especially as compared to Universal's Islands of Adventure (these rides are great). The rides and activities at Universal Orlando Resort were typically "one and out." Whereas, you will find yourself doing the rides at Universal's Islands of Adventure several times.

I went here with my family 10 years ago and thought it might be an entertaining vacation again....WRONG. The rides are old...the food is dreadful...the shows are also outdated and hokey. Roughly $1000 for two days-parking, lunch,stupid chahka...What was I thinking!!!!?? Spend your dough on a beach vacation in Naples. Orlando is really a boring place

this was our first visit and we did not realise that universal is split into 2 parks until it was too late. we bought tickets and entered one side of the park when we wanted to see the other, but didnt realise what had happened for a couple of hours. we really wanted to see harry potter, and the dr suess attraction. we accepted it was our mistake and asked if we could pay the difference and upgrade to the2 park ticket for the final 2 hours, and were told no we would have to purchase a full new ticket, which we could not afford. very poor customer service for niave first time middle aged visitors.

If you have children over 10, this is the place to go. They have something for everyone. There are attractions for younger kids (Like Dr. Suess land, Awesome), but the lines can be long. I go with my pre-teen & teenagers and we have a great time. Unlike Disney, there are only two parks, they are right next to each other, and you can pay one low fee to get into both. If you are staying for a week, buy Annual Passes. Purchase passes online at universalorlando.com to save even more money. We go every year.

I spent a perfect day here! I loved Terminator 2 3D, Shrek 4D and The Simpsons Ride. It was very funny! E.T. Adventure was really cute. Whole park had a great movie atmosphere. At the evening there was an amazing Mardi Gras Parade and Ne-Yo sang there.

Universal Studios offers fun for family members of all ages. All attractions are accessible by wheelchairs.. etc. Express pass is a must. This comes when staying at an onsite hotel. Jaws, The Mummy, Men in Black, and ET were really fun. The October month is great because Halloween night time events are incredible. There are complimentary lockers available at most rides. Food is not priced too bad-no worse than other parks. Food plans and refillable cups are available-may be good option.

So I came back to Orlando after 12 years and we visited Universal studios and Islands of Adventures. The first park is a rip-off. So aparently there was only one park, 10 years ago, and they added some attractions and divided them into 2 parks, to charge more money. They should be one park, because Universal studios has ery few attractions, most of which are really old. Jaws and ET, for instance, are unimpressing, considering today's technological standards. They have a few shows, and 4D attractions like Shrek and the Simpsons. The Simpsons is great, but it doesn't justify the 90 USD that you pay to get in. Twister, even it it is old, is still very nice, but again, 2 cool attractions do not justify the 90 USD. Nor does the rollercoaster. In Islands of adventures, there are better rollercoasters. If I had to go back again, I wouldn't waste my time going to Universal Studios, I'd just go to Islands of Adventures. Now, that park isn't great either. There are some cool attractions, several actually, but the only one that is really well done is the Harry Potter land. They have not paid attention to detail, like Disney does, at the other attractions. There is no "concept" behind the rollercoasters, for instance the Hulk rollercoaster has nothing to do with the Incredible Hulk really. Disney parks are so much better at creating an atmosphere and telling a story as you ride. My advice: go to Islands of Adventures and skip Universal studios, it's just not worth it. And if you have small children, you might as well skip Islands of Adventures, since most of the rides have height requirements that would leave your kids out.
Lots of options for kids of all ages! Great rollercoasters and shows!
Our 11 year old loved the thrill rides. Our 4 year old loved the little kids area. Rides seem to break down often, though. Some really long lines.

We don't have kids and we've found that Disney doesn't offer us much. We took this trip to spend time at the Universal Parks. It was great fun. Harry Potter Ride is amazing and SCARY! We love Revenge of the Mummy. It is probably our all time favorite ride. Halloween Horror nights was like a dream (or nightmare) come true! So much fun being scared and the production values of the 8 houses was fantastic. We spent 4 days at both parks and didn't get bored at all.

There are a lot of older rides in this half of the Universal--Orlando themepark, but do not miss "The Simpsons ride!" It is a super-fun and thrilling simulated ride and my favorite ride in all of Universal--Orlando! "Revenge of the Mummy" is towards the back of the park, and could be overlooked, but don't! It's a fun roller coaster. The newest coaster in the park is the "Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit;" it's worth a try, but I think it's a very jerky ride, and I only rode it once.

Over the years we have found early November to be the perfect time to visit WDW. The weather, though not great for swimming, is warmer than the Northeast and there are very few crowds to contend with. Last week was our first visit to Universal and we found the same held true. My adult daughter and I purchased the 2 day park to park pass which we took advantage of. Our first day was spent at Universal Studios, but at 5pm we went over to Islands of Adventure for 2 more hours. Then the next day we started at Islands, but jumped back to the Studios to re-ride the Mummy. We did not purchase the Express pass at $20/day and did not regret that decision. Our longest wait was 10-15 minutes for the Mummy ride and some group-type shows, but basically, we walked onto every other ride without a wait. Our greatest surprise was in the Harry Potter area. We had to slow ourselves to see everything on the long walks to the rides in the castle and the coasters so we wouldn't miss what people there on high traffic days would be entertained by during their long wait. With the lack of crowds we were able to see everything we wanted and several rides we did twice.

Just returned from Universal Studios where we stayed at the Royal Pacific! Very convenient to both parks and the City Walk and quite enjoyable to commute by Water Taxi to the park areas. Enjoyed both parks and being in Hogsmeade was fantastic! We felt like we were in the books and movies with Harry, Hermione and Ron. However, the Meal Deal is DEFINITELY NOT WORTH IT!. Here's the math: over 26 dollars per day per person with taxes. Does not include drinks or water. Average meal cost is 7.50 and they don't open until 11am so breakfast is not available. Food is bland and healthy options are very limited. Bad burgers, chicken sandwiches, fries, pasta and pizza are the only choices in 3 participating restaurants in each park. Since most may eat only 2 meals, the meal deal is only a deal for Universal. Other park restaurants are good with food that generally seems to be well prepared.

Island's of Adventure was Epic! Universal Studios itself was a waste of money. We didn't go on the city walk as we were with someone who was under aged.  Island 100% go all day! Lots to do. Sometimes the lines are quite long though.  Universal Studios was quite disappointed. There were no lines, however, everything was very outdated. I don't really regret going, but I would not go again. And, if it's off season, nothing is open! The twister ride was the coolest thing and it was VERY old!  It's quite a bit more for both parks, so I would recommend only islands park and unless it's really busy, don't bother with the fast past.

After a long day of riding all the rides, and other activities for the whole family there is nothing quite like a show. Stop in for the blue man show, it was awesome.  great food, hospitality, just plain good fun. Enjoy!  blueman intro:please copy and paste the link below http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rDyI3UU5nPw
Unless you want to pay through the nose of all the hard earned money you made last month, go. This place is nothing but a shopping mall that charges admission.

We went to Islands of Adventure on our first day. I thought Universal Studios Orlando Resort was much small and less to do, but it really isnt. You will do more casual walking around and not as much stress and as crowded as Islands of Adventure, but still lots to do. The Simpsons Ride (replaced the older back to the future ride) is a must. Only drawback is, if you get there when they open, which I highly recommend, you can literally do all the rides you want and see what you want to see in less than 4 hours.
