No problem though, just head out to City Walk, eat at Hard Rock Cafe, Jimmy Buffets, Pat O'Briens, or catch a movie at the huge theater, then head back in.

At first glance you may look at the prices for entry into this park and think its expensive, but let me tell you its worth every penny. The venue is spotless and the customer service is second to none, but thats just the start. The rides are excellent, and there really is something for everyone of all ages and yes rides for the whole family to enjoy. My top tip would be to go the extra mile and either arrive real early or prepare to stay really late or buy a fast pass, in the heat of midday it will be most welcome.

We went between Christmas and New Years. Biggest crowd the park has ever experienced. Regular Lines were over an hour long, made even longer by those using express pass. Resort was really neat, just too crowded on this trip.

This side of the park was a blast.The mib ride was super fun me and my kiddo really enjoyed this one. we rode it twice and it was cooler the next time around. Disaster was fun Christopher walken being part of the ride and the rock i the preview was a nice suprise .we wished we could get a copy of the movie preivew we stared it but what can you do.Only down side to this side of the park was the jaws ride closed the day before we went :( Had to do the et ride and heard it might be the next ride they change . While walking through the park we ran in to Lucy , shrek fiona , doc brown and the blues brothers, any movie fan should put thi on there list

The Universal Orlando - Islands of Adventure was a fun park to visit. There were fun rides and the Wizarding World of Harry Potter entertained us. The butter beer, wand shop, Hogwarts, etc.... had our 15 year old in awe. OK I loved the way they created a world so identical to the the movie world. it was more fun than I expected.

Visited on Dec. 27 & 29, 2011.  I'm not a big "review" writer, but TripAdvisor helped me plan one of the better Christmas gifts to my family. As a gift to our kids (ages: 9, 10, 11, 13) we took them to Orlando for a theme park vacation. Universal was awesome, but it could have been a disaster.  Considering we are not wealthy, I began planning this trip in early 2011. Reading reviews from the general public (which I am a member of) helped guide me to making smart decisions. I suggest you do the same if you are visiting anywhere near the Holiday season.  First, express passes are a must. Yes, I know they are expensive (unless you are staying at the resort, which I did not). We forked over the cash for VIP express passes (unlimited express rides at both parks) and it paid off. I cannot fathom how any family could enjoy withhold from assaulting each other if they had to endure those seasonal lines. We took tax return money, birthday gift money, yard sale money, etc to make sure we had a fighting chance to enjoy both parks. It worked. There is absolutely no way any of us would have enjoyed the two parks if we waited in the holiday lines. An example: When we stepped to The Incredible Hulk the line was billed at 110 minutes. With express passes we were on in 18 (yes, I timed it). I'm sure the single rider line would be faster, but for families with younger children this is virtually impossible. If you must visit during this time of year and absolutely can't find a way to buy the express passes (ask specifically for unlimited rides in both parks) then you better be prepared to spend most of your days waiting in line. Period.  Now on to the "non-financials."  The Universal side is still a great day! The Mummy blew us away. The Simpsons and Men In Black, excellent as well. Rip Ride Rocket did not accept our express passes, but the wait was worth it. 15 seconds of climbing completely vertical freaked even the parents (me) out! We were lucky enough to ride Jaws before it's closing although the kids had never heard of the movie (I swear I can't be THIS old)!  The Island of Adventure side takes some navigating. If you are a huge Harry Potter mark, make sure you get there early (8 AM opening times during the Holidays) and head straight to that part of the park. We arrived at 8:30 AM and had to stand in line for 10 mins to get "return" tix for 10:30 AM. At 10:30 AM we returned and entered but while doing so discovered that all "return" times were full and the "standbye" line was 120 minutes. After entering we immediately went to the Forbidden Journey where we waited for 2 hours. The good news: the line continually moves and the scenery/staff make things seem incredibly quicker. The bad news: say what you want, you're still standing in line two hours. Super bonus news: That's the greatest ride I've ever ridden. Period. At 40 years old, I felt like I was a child. It was simply remarkable, and well worth the wait.  The rest of the park was fantastic as well. The Incredible Hulk is the 2nd best roller coaster in Orlando; succeeded only by the Manta at SeaWorld. Spider Man, Jurassic Park, Ripsaw Falls and Dr. Doom are also musts.  My tips: EXPRESS PASSES (I cannot stress this enough at this time of year). Make sure everyone in your family wears comfortable shoes (there is a lot of walking/standing time involved). Pack LIGHTLY. We spent two entire days/nights in these parks and I made ONE trip back to the car to grab hoodies for the evening hours. If you plan on eating at Universal, be prepared for typical theme park food. We weighed the options. Eating in the park was just slightly more expensive than leaving, and we saved a ton of time. However, regardless of what restaurant we dined in, the food was average at best (that includes the CityWalk venues we visited: Hard Rock & NBA Cafe). Be patient and prepare yourself for exhaustion. The teens and preteens may be able to go all day, but us 30/40/50 somethings are going to get our collective a$$e$ handed to us!  I had a great time, but it took a lot of saving and planning. These are great parks to visit, but unless you are willing to do your research then you are better off visiting during Summer or off-peak months.  Good luck, and Happy future Holidays to everyone. I hope this helps!

The Hollywood Universal Studios is MUCH better than the Orlando park. We felt that the atmosphere was lacking a bit here. The shows were just okay, whereas the Hollywood Universal shows were awesome. The Beetlejuice show was awful, Animal Actors had a great start then fizzled. Disaster was much ado about nothing. Hollywood monster make-up show was fun though. The rides were just thrill rides, but we did really enjoy MIB and The Simpsons (not for those prone to motion sickness, just to warn you!) It didn't help that a big chunk of the park is closed for a big new project, strongly rumored to be Harry Potter phase 2.

I am a Disneyland regular and this is the first time venturing out to Orlando. We spent 4 days and Disneyworld and noticed that their were less positive interactions with castmembers as we normally experience at Disneyland. That being said we did have a few magic moments where castmembers went out of their way to make sure we were having a good experience. The next two days were at Universal and our interactions with the employees was bad. I blame this more on Universal policies then I do individual employees. Universal has great rides but their pushy sales policies while in the park were a big negative for me. Having "barkers" standing out in the middle of walkways trying to get you to buy photos or enter their stores was tacky. Not allowing you to even view your on-ride photo without having to talk to a sales person who tries to get you to buy it was also a big negative. All in all I will not be making a very big effort to return to Universal Orlando the next time we venture out to Orlando.

The whole experience was overwhelming and as an oldie I did not think that I would enjoy it however I could not have been more wrong. I wished I could have stayed in the park for a week because there was so much to see and do. Harry Potter was exceptional and I will return for a longer period very soon.

Seen the 1st fil but didnt see the fasination so didnt bother watching the rest. Well how wrong was i... It is the most fantastic place, i was seeing things that i couldn't believe, a book with teeth??? Butterbeer??? Honeydukes??? Snow covered roofs and the hogwarts express. Can say i was gutted i didn't know what was going on! Was very busy in the potter land and qued for 2 hours to get onto the ride and it broke down twice while we were in the queue but was well worth the wait. Sent a postcard from there and it was stamped with the hogwarts stamp but the stamps to buy are quite expensive but its a novelty so you pay it don't you.... Really impressed and have now seen every film and am very upset they have ended! Am going back september this year and will be exploring harry potter land a bit better this time... The butterbeer is delish and you can buy it in a plastic tankard 2 keep, didnt buy the pumpkin juice but will try it this year...

I have visited Universal's Islands of Adventure before and love it. I was equally impressed with Universal itself. I do think the rides on this side are more fun. HOWEVER, there is a lot of construction going on so it seemed like a lot of the park was closed or inaccessible. I am looking forward to attending when it is completed.

We took out children and grandchildren to Universal. We had a lot of fun, there is something there for all ages. Be sure to buy an ez pass, it eliminates standing in long lines, they are $69 but there is no way to do both parks in one day without one. Be sure to use lots of hand sanitizer. Jimmy Buffets Margirettaville is great for dinner.

If you plan to visit Universal/Islands of Adventure, you DON'T WANT TO BE THERE for the Mardi gra parade/concert series if you have young children. We went for the Kelly Clarkson concert....Universal allowed WAY too many people that border lined on TOTAL UNSAFE CONDITIONS!! You could not get thru the crowd and most were between the age of 20 - 30...DRUNK AND RUDE!! People were being pushed, trampling could have easily occured, security could barely get thru the crowd and little fights starting due to drunkeness. I DO NOT RECOMMEND!! My boys are 10 and 12. The 10 yr old was frightened to death and we ended up leaving after 2 songs. That being said, Universal/Islands Adventure a place to go have fun during the day. Coaster rides and shopping are fun, food ok. Beware of Movie Rides if you get motion sickness. Most of the rides are this way...research first, we didn't and I regret it!!

My family and I went to Universal Studios Orlando on the weekend of Feb 17 and 18. Kelly Clarkston had a concert scheduled in the part at 8 pm on the 18th. That is the exact time the park closes. The crowds quickly formed at the site of the concert. The geniuses at Universal were forcing everyone to go throught the concert site even if all you wanted to do was leave the park. That is all we wanted to do. There was no way that we could make it thru the crowd to leave. We tried to back track to try to go around but the Universal emplyees stopped us and sent us back. I tried to explain that we just wanted to leave and had no desire to see the concert. My young children were overwhelmed by the crowds but the emplyees didn't care. It took us about forty five minutes to get to a restaurant that happened to have two doors. I thought we could cut thru but the crowds jammed the door ways and no one was going anywhere. If there had been a fire or an emergency, there would have been many many people hurt or killed. I even asked one of the emplyees if there was anyone we could call to let us out of the park and she said that I would have to wait until the concert was over. We kept trying and finally back tracked around the entire event not paying attention to anyone that tried to stop us and after an hour and a half finally made it out. I I was planning on getting my kids some souverneirs but by that time the store where we wanted to get them was closed. It was 10:30 pm before we had dinner. Their lack of planning ruined an otherwise good day. It will be a very very long time before I ever return there. This would have never happened at Disney.

We were somewhat disappointed with Universal Orlando Resort. The place really starting to show it's age. Jaws, King Kong, Back To The Future & Earthquake ALL GONE...I really enjoy the NYC area and the Blues Brothers, but overall this park is a let down. I guess it must be tough to keep up with the mouse, but Disney parks and attractions easily trump Universal's meager offerings.

The Mummy ride was decent and the Rockin Roller Coaster was fantastic, but on the whole i think this park was lame compared to the competition. I dont know how to describe it, but the atmosphere is just more enjoyable at the Disney parks and at IOA. It's a little problematic I guess when your rides depend on 'modern' movies - movies get out-dated quickly. Our other issue is that our younger kids got bored pretty quickly.  This is probably a decent half-day park, but if I only had a day and I had to go with Universal, I'd go with IOA.
Harry Potter was great. Food prices are really high but it was fun.

Bought a 2 day, both park (and 1 day express pass) ticket and was super happy with my purchase  In my opinion, Island of Adventure is the better park overall, but you can't not go at Universal Studios  I liked the MIB ride as well as the Simpsons, but hated the Disaster one (what a wadte of time)  Don't think we waited more than 10 minutes to get in any of the rides with the express pass!  I dudn't return to this park on the second day, but still am happy to have been there

(March 2011) I went last year for my spring break. The lines were average I guess. The average wait time was 30 minutes, but we were going to be there all day, so it didn't bother us much. We passed the time by getting to know other people in the lines. I didn't ride the Rip Ride RockIt, because something about going straight up (the beginning) bothers me lol. I loved the Mummy ride, pretty cool. We rode JAWS, but I heard they have done away with Jaws :(. We also rode Men in Black and saw some animal show that was going on. We didn't get a chance to ride Disaster (the line was horrendous). I recommend Terminator!! OMG that was funny and fun.

It's not good to have the feeling you're ripped off right from the start of the day. When we first purchased tickets, we were told that if you want to skip the long lines, fork over $40 more. That's on top of the $120 per ticket (we got the two park pass). I had already visit Disney where tickets were $90 each and they offer the short line option called fastpass for free to everyone. So right off Universal left a bad taste in my mouth. The rides are more geared for adults and teenagers. The grandparents and my kids (younger than 5) didn't enjoy most of the rides with the exception of Spiderman and Cat in the Hat in Island of Adventure. I was excited to ride Harry Potter but the anticipation was better than the actual ride. The wait can be really long unless you go into the single rider line or paid the extra $40 to skip the regular line. The roller coasters were okay. We couldn't do a lot of the rides (height limit as well as not age appropriate) as a family so that took away the experience. They have a parent swap where one parent can ride while the other stays with the kids then they switch but this is not as fun as riding together. Overall I will not visit this place again.
this park is so quiet compared to the islands of adventure.

This was the second time in two years that we visited Universal Studios in Orlando. We went to "Islands of Adventure" this time around because we wanted to ride the Harry Potter ride we missed two years ago (it wasn't open yet). The park was very clean, well organized, and the mass of people flowed well on a gorgeous Saturday.  Things not to be missed: 1. The highlight of my day was spraying strangers with water while they were riding one of the water rides. They have quarter operated single-shot sprayers that you can use to hose down complete strangers with. My brother and I went through over $50 and laughed the whole time. Yes, they have bill changers next to the sprayers!  2. All of the rides were good. In my opinion (in order from best to least) - The Hulk Roller Coaster, Harry Potter, Sprider Man, The Dragon Roller Coaster, etc...  3. I found the food and drinks to be actually pretty good for park food and actually reasonably priced.  4. They have a dog/cat kennel on site that is great for only $15 for the day.  Things we didn't like: 1. They sell a "Pass the Line" ticket for $50 per person per day. If you purchase this pass you basically can go to the front of any line at any time for the entire day. I'm sure the park is making a lot of money offering this service, but it wasn't much fun to watch people run by us all day long. The longest we waited all day was an hour for Harry Potter. So, I didn't feel like the $100 (for my wife and I) would be worth it.  2. Parking for $15 seemed high to me.  3. If you go to the Universal Studios side of the park - know that there is a maximum height allowed for the rock in roll roller coaster there. I waited for over an hour for that ride two years ago and then was told when I got to the platform that I was too tall to ride. I'm only 6'-5". There are a lot of people much taller than me walking around...

Always my favorite, the park is not so big as to get too overcrowded. We go frequently and enjoy it. Animal Actors is cute as is the Beetlejuice. Looking forward to many exciting new things opening in 2012!

As an annual passholder, I obviously enjoy going to this park at least every few months. While much attention has been given to it's Isle of Adventure, it's nice to see Universal is finally getting some new life breathed into it. Jimmy Neutron is closed for it's change to Despicable Me and Jaws ate it's last victom in January to make room for Transformers (I've been told). While ET and Terminator have definitely ran their course, I don't see any other major changes until their current projects have been completely. Simpson's is still fun and with another MIB movie coming, this will keep the ride interesting. I wouldn't plan on needing more than one full day to see and do everything there is to do in Universal, ......but as far as Isle of Adventure, well don't get me started on that hot spot.

My headline might be a bit downbeat but it’s true – Universal Studios is definitely second best to Islands of Adventure. The highlight at U Studios is the Revenge of the Mummy, which, with a fast pass, I did numerous times and enjoyed every bit of this thrilling and imaginative ride. The Simpson’s Ride is great, but do try and sit on the front row of the cars otherwise your view is restricted. Terminator is still holding it’s own and still looks brilliant. The Ripsaw ride nearly made me pass out! Honestly! About half way through so much pressure was in my feet I felt very light headed and it was only because the ride calmed down for a moment that I regained full blood pressure in my head! I guess that makes it a great ride?! The only problem with this ride is that the music never worked, but that’s really not important! Overall, as an adult, you’ll struggle to fill a day here, especially if you have a fast pass. So I do recommend you do both this park and IOA in one day.
Outstanding as usual---WE REALLY ENJOYED THE HARRY POTTER RIDE!! Lines were not to bad for most rides averaging about 20 to 25 minutes!!

I actually prefer this to HP-IOA, why ? Lines are not as long (20 min, in-n-out of the Men In Black ride, for example), and the park itself is not as crowded. Of course, this side is older. They did a better job keeping you occupied while on line, e.g. robotic aliens at Men-in-Black, animation at the Simpsons ride. We also caught the Plain White T's concert, quite a treat for my teenage son!

We have just returned from a magical holiday in Florida We have never been to Universal Studios before but being avid Harry Potter fans it was a MUST Asthetically it was brilliant, looked every bit the same as the movies, the image of Hogwarts and the diagon alley shops looked amazing. Disappointingly the only shops open were Ollivanders and Honeydewks sweet shop Waited for 90 minutes for the Forbidden Journey ride. It broke down for 45 minutes and then my 10 year old was traumatised by the actual ride itself. Not enough information on the sheets about suitability. Consequently spoilt the holiday as she ouldnt go on any ride. Ollivanders the wand shop was brilliant, great experience for HP fans. Cant help wondering why Disney didnt get this experience he would have made it TRULY MAGICAL
Great attraction with fun rides and if you buy the fast pass or stay at a related hotel it is free and worth it.
very dated with movie themes that I saw but my kids did not such as terminator, men in black and storm chaser. Not very much to do, not great rides and kids wanted to leave by lunch.

Took the kids there for Spring Break and it was great. I think I had more fun than they did. Going later in the day was definitely a good idea as the lines were shorter and we only had 15 to 20 minute waits for rides. Even enjoyed "Fear Factor", realized that the "Simpsons" ride is where "Back to the Future" used to be. Our two day pass was more than enough, actually got to see most of the parks this time. Universal and Island of Adventure are great parks and really fun filled for the whole family, we had a great time.

We had a fabulous time at Universal! The longest we waited in line for a ride was 15 minutes for the Spiderman attraction. Most of the time we could walk right up and get on the ride.  Absolutely loved our time at Universal!

Finally was able to afford to go to Universal Studios in Orlando, Florida. Haven’t been there in a very long time. Also, been to your park when it first opened. Made 2 reservations for the park tickets and hotel directly through the Universal Orlando Web Site for 6 of us in total. My wife, 2 nephews, and my in laws. After making the long drive arrived on Monday April 23 until Friday April 27, 2012. Went to Harry Potter World/Islands of Adventures on Tuesday and to Universal Studios on Wednesday. Been wanting to go to your Harry Potter World since it first opened but hasn’t been able to go until now.  To summarize the whole thing, let’s just say that it was a very bad experience and at the end a waste of money. To make things worst, my father in law was on a wheelchair and did not found out until leaving the park on the last day that you offer an “express” pass for people in wheelchairs to make things easier and with assistance. No one said anything about that when we got to the park the first day. Also on your ride at Universal Studios – The Simpsons – had us standing up waiting in the room that you go in before getting on the actual ride for a long time when found out afterwards that could have go in there with the wheelchair and sit and wait.  We also purchased on the first day your meal pass with the drink cups. The food was terrible, cold, and not really worth the money. Was told that the next day will get free drinks since already got the cups and to bring them back. The next day when went to get drinks was told that there was not free and will cost $.80 cents per refill. This shows that was lied about it. Since on the first day the food was horrible and not good, did not purchased the food meal deal the next day. You got rid of the Back to the Future ride and replaced it with The Simpsons. Same type of ride but different “theme”. Your Terminator 3D you seemed to have cut the “show” in half and got rid of a lot of it. We are all very unhappy and dissatisfied with our visit. What it was supposed to be a fun vacation it wasn’t.  For what it cost in total going to your theme parks would have gone to somewhere else like Disney and I bet it would have been much better.  I will tell everyone I know about my terrible experience with you and to beware and consider not going and go somewhere else.  The only reason ended up going to Island of Adventures is because that is where Harry Potter World is and no other way of going to it without going to Island of Adventures.  Universal it is NOT what it used to be when started, that is for sure. Going down the drain !

Universal Studios, as in the park has became very poor. Most of the rides are alright ( The Mummy is probably my favorite of them all ) this park is just a collection of rides, no real theme or connection between them. The parks one real bit of theming which is the Streets, has been ruined by the building of the Rockit rollercoaster ( see picture ). If you want just rides then it wouldn't be an issue, but if you had to chose between here and Islands of Adventure then its no contest in both theme and rides.
Amazing park. Time spent in Univeral Orlando Resort we will remember for a long time. We were in the park in February and there was not a lot of people. I recommend this park to everyone.
Great way to spend a day if you are a movie buff... Awesome Rides!!!

What can I say about this place that people don't already know. Well, I have been twice with my family and we are all adults and we have the most incredible time. The atmosphere is fantastic, the rides are amazing and the weather is just awesome (but most weather is better than the UK) We went in September and queues were small which is a bonus. The Americans are sooo polite, think some English people could learn a thing or two from them.  HHN is also very worth a trip if you are there around this time if your little old hearts can take the surprises. The costumes are out of this world and Jack the Clown really is freaky (it's a clown thing)  Make sure you visit IOA as well  Going again in Sep 12 and cannot wait!!!

This is my third trip to Universal however it was my first visit to Islands of Adventure and the Harry Potter section. It was great. Very well done. My favorite ride was the Happy Potter simulator. I am too much of a coward for real rides, but this was tons of fun. I also enjoyed the Spider Man ride. The Poseidon Adventure was not to my liking, a long wait for a staged show with animation and special effects. We had to stand the whole time and I could not see the whole stage over the people. As for those who like the roller coasters, the people on them seemed to be having a ball! My kids did both parks over two days and said they enjoyed that very much. There is a drop off/pick section for those who wish to leave the kids for the day. (My "kids" are 18 & 20) Also, I purchased the meal deal but would not do that again unless I need more than two meals per day.

Our flight was in by 830 am and we were at Universal Studios by 10 am....after renting a car! Celebrating Mardi Gras......easy parking,.....long walk in tho...but we were so excited it didnt matter.....Was an excellent day....visited just about all the attractions we wanted to.....just one complaint.....we were there from the airport and I had my handbag and wasnt admitted to an attraction...had to put it in a locker that was outside the attraction.....I was not comfortable with leaving my bag with all my credit cards and cash out there so we did not go on the ride. We stayed all day and nite for the parade and concert with Cyndi Lauper! Perfect first day in Orlando with my teenager son! We will be coming back in July with both my sons!

We decided to do Universal Studios and Island of Adventures in one day, and started off with Universal Studios. A great idea, as there were little people, and waiting lines for the rides were short since we did it backwards. The rides I loved the most were The Simpsons ride (awesome), the Mummy, and the rollercoaster (a good warmup for the IoA). Men in Black was also worth it, Shrek in 4D was pretty nice as well, while Twister was a bit boring (but I suppose it's also a little old). It's nice to run into movie characters along the way and feel like you're inside the movies.

Went on May with 4 teenagers -- had a blast. our time was limited so we scheduled well the rides to hit 2 parks ( Islands of Adventure and the regular Universal) in one day. It was doable bec the place is compact (unlike Disney). Saved money and time. Most favorite ride is The Harry Potter one and all the wet rides... There are free lockers to store belongings -- leave huge bags home/hotel bec they will not fit. When hungry and tired after the whole day of gallivanting? No worries -- a lot of restaurants to choose from in the Universal City walk. Parking is covered building -- NICE !!!
crowded but due to the holiday weekend. saved time in lines by going single rider.

Well I must say I'm writing this rewview from a biased point of view as Universal Orlando is my favourite place to visit. It's a magical place that just seems to make everyone smile. As a resident of the UK it's on a different planet to our theme parks,With rides like " Thje rides are in a different class, even queuing is fun, but also the frienliness of the park staff is so much better. They seem to genuinely enjoy helping people enjoy their time at the park.

I get it... They have all Of these Tourists in town and they are trying to keep up with Disney. Yes, Universal Is a great place but I always feel so dollared to death. 14.00 for parking!! Really? Islands of Adventure in my opinion is the better park here as Universal Park seems to Always be lacking. The hotels are truly beautiful But again, way way over priced!!

My wife and I and, at times, our extended family have been visiting Universal in Orlando for 14 years. In the early days it was a very enjoyable experience, but for the past few years it has disintegrated into a mad scramble to part guests with their cash.  All items in Universal are significantly dearer than Disney parks including food and drink.  The worst feature now is the 'Express Pass'. Once upon a time this was free, as is Disney, but for the past few years it is now a very expensive extra payment for the privilege of skipping the lines for most rides in the park.  However, it can only be used once per ride and is NOT valid for the two most popular rides at Universal, ie the Rocket and Harry Potter. The cost of the Express Pass varies according to the time of year and is obviously most expensive at peak holiday times. It can be up to $50 per person per day on top of the price of admission.  Not good value for me. The worst feature is that the Express Pass is still heavily advertised on days when the Parks are quiet and waiting times are short.it is an absolute waste of money.  The Universal experience has diminished in its attraction for my family over the years. all due to the money grabbing attitude that now prevails.  Universal constantly compare themselves to Disney but there is no comparison.  Universal would do better to try and celebrate the differences between them, rather than try to trash Disney.

I had high expectations, me, my husband and 10 yr old son. There wasn't much to do in there. The day we went, we walked on to everything, no lines, and we even had fast passes and didn't need them. I thought it was old, and outdated. The ET ride is OLD! The Jaws ride is gone, and that whole area is under construction. The MIB ride....kinda lame....Disaster...ugh, kind of a disaster. Twister....o.k. kind of lame. Shrek was fun, and that was about it. We got pix with the characters there, that was okay. We saw everything and left the park at 3:00pm. I won't go back there, I would rather go to something else. Local news reported 2 price hikes in a month on tickets and people were screaming about it. The bathrooms were shut down twice for flooding...This place in't worth the money.

First of all when I reviewed IOA I forgot to mention the Express Pass System. This is well worth the extra money in my eye's and is much better than Disney's Fast Pass system. Why do you ask? Because you have to pay extra for it. Disney's is available to everybody and you have to time things just so to get maximum benefit. The Express Pass you have to pay for and let's face it some people just don't want to pay. So while some people are waiting over and hour for a ride, with the Express Pass your wait can be cut down to like 15 minutes. With that being said, Islands of Adventure no doubt was much busier than Universal Park, mostly due to Harry Potter. It was probably a waste in Universal but I'm not complaining. To me it was well worth the extra money.  With that being said let's review some rides shall we.  Rip Ride Rocket: A very good roller coaster not as intimidating as it looks. You can buy a video of your ride for like $30.00 if you so choose.  Twister: Is getting old. However, I can remember when this used to be Ghostbusters'  Revenge of the Mummy: A very good indoor/dark roller coaster. Very well themed. However, I do miss Kongfrontation.  The Simpsons Ride: I have never watched an episode of the Simpsons. We were in a place called Krusty's Land. It was funny and entertaining, but I liked Back to the Future instead.  MIB: A good ride. You are shooting at aliens while being spun all over the place.  ET: Probably one of the last original rides left at Universal. Still good and brings back memories of watching the movie for the first time. If you can try to sit on the left side for the best views.  Disaster: Is what used to be called Earthquake. Basically the same thing just reworked to keep it fresh. The "Disaster" is still the best part. If you can try to sit on the left side for the best effect.  Shrek 4D: Good 3D movie with effects. Water sprays, air hissing, things of that nature to make it 4D. Funny!  Terminator: Needs to go. Not very good, not very impressed. Live action show with 3d effects.  Woody Woodpecker: Good kiddie coaster if they even know who that character is anymore.  Horror Make-up show was excellent very funny and informative in the same breath. NO DRINKS ALLOWED!!!!!! In 90 degree heat. Come on.  Fievel's Playland and Curious George Goes to town: are playlands for the kiddies. Although, I don't know if little ones these days even know who Fievel is.  The Minion ride wasn't open yet. I don't know what the delay is there.  IOA is more geared towards kids and teens. Universal is more the "Adult" park. Some of the attractions are out of date: Terminator and Twister. I'm sure they are in the works to replace them.  There are character photo opps/autographs if you want.  We went off season on weekdays when the parks were not open as late. With the Express Pass you could do both of these parks in a day easy when they open their full operating schedule and do not close at 8PM.  We did each park on separate days and were done by 5 by both days.  It's not as jammed packed as Disney or IOA for that matter, but has some exciting things. But I left there as if something was missing. Can't quite put my finger on it.

Just got back from two weeks in florida and we had bought a 14 day hopper ticket for universal studios plus the islands of adventure next door, waste of time because you can do everything in one/two days. The park was opening for 9 so we got there for 8 30 and found the rides already on and loads of people making their way in to the parks. Parking is 15 dollars and they have just put up thier admission prices and having a mini war with disney regarding who can charge the most. The universal studios side nedds a major overhaul because the attractions are very dated and only because the men in black 3 film is out the ride is popular again but everything else has been tarted up or closed down for example the Jaws ride is no longer there and that site is under revamp but no information on what is being put there. The ROCK IT ride is amazing and if you can use the single rider queue because i went onit twice within 5 minutes. The islands of adventure park is the busiest because of the Harry potter section but personally i thought it was all overated, I queued half an hour ( supposingly it was taking over an hour according to thier time system) when you get into hogwarts its a walk around but only two things to really look at then its the ride. The ride is a combination of rollercoaster and simulator and for young kids it can be a bit too much. The harry potter area is quite small so hence the large crowds and major queues. The other rides were busy and because my family are very young and wife pregnant i was the only one allowed on the rides so took full advantage of the single rider queue system but anyone can use this as long as you dont mind being stuck with someone else. Universal do provide the disney version of fastpass but they charge you for it.  We tried the meal deal they offer and my daughter has a food allergy which disney cater for very well in deed but universal only offer this in two restuarants and they do not accept the meal deal so i complained to customer services and they could only offer me a gift card with the amount, what a con. In general do not expect huge things from universal if you have been to disney because no way can universal match disney like for like. Universal is not worth the money unless you go for a week and stay there because you can do it all in 2 days max, one day if you lucky on the queues
anniversary celebration with fire works and light show
the cleanliness, the rooms, and the closeness to all Disney places.

It was an amazing trip! I went with my class of 2012 as our senior trip we went for 5 days. It was more than what i was expecting for it. very nice people, very comfortable place, the prices were like ok they were not that expensive and I would love to go back with my family. Time goes by soo quickly like a blink of an eye. Also I got on all the rides they were amazing I really want to go back I reccomend it to people that likes fun and likes going on rides and having a great time, because you sure will.!!!!
Undoubtly best theme park in the world ,not to miss Harry potter It was really mind blowing rides there on the whole it was really very entertaining n we really enjoyed every ride we did.
Great day. Loved the characters around the park. New Spongebob shop opened a week before with everything you could ask for and Shrek 4d and Terminator 3d shows were brilliant.

Disappointing - The original Universal Studios park is a fairly tired looking park in need of some TLC and investment. The Terminator ride is looking pretty dated as is ET and the newer rides such as The Simpsons were pretty good although lack a bit of magic. We struggled to fill a day here and all the family felt a bit deflated and left early.  Given the hugely frustrating ticketing system at Universal where express passes go straight onto rides and therefore distort projected waiting times, this park was hugely disappointing. I really begrudge paying up to $50 extra per day per person for express passes for moderate rides where not all family members wish to use very ride. It created frustration on rides where waiting times were unrealistic given express pass holders were walking on to rides and they have created a 2 tier system unlike Disney who have the fabulous fastpass system where everyone is treated the same and it is up to you how and when you make use of them. It also does not have Disney’s knowhow and organisation and of course Disney’s magic.  It appeared to me that Universal have spent all their money on Harry Potter and everywhere else has suffered.  If it were me I wouldn’t bother and would visit Disney and Seaworld and leave Universal off your itinerary.  That said, for adults or teenagers there was more there for them than younger families.

We took the kids for spring break to go and see Harry Potter. That was the main attraction. It was ok. It was so crowded. I guess that goes with the was it is. Everything was an upgrade. not too cheap. The food was not good. Especially for the price. But all in all it was a fun day and the kids had a good time. It is a good one time place to go. Next time we will go to Cedar Key instead.

There are 3 separate areas, first you walk through the restaurants and bars, then choose to go right to Universal Studios where the rides are based on 10-20 year old movies--or--you turn left to the Islands of Adventure where you can see Harry Potter, Spiderman and several roller coasters to jumble your tummy. Much different than Disney, but quite worthwhile.
watch the parade- Its small but worth it, Loads of shops, miss the jaws ride was stopped Jan 2012
a must visit for adults and children alike. with live shows and movie themed rides. had a wonderful day there and will definatley be going again
It's simply a must for all. Take lots of patience with you - Harry Potter is amazing and there is something for everyone!!!! Enjoy it!!!

Rollar coasters and simulator rides, not much in-between stuff for kids that don't want to do thoses things. Got through it in about a day with the Express pass that came with our Royal Pacific hotel. Great thing - blew by 50 people to the front of most lines!!
Love the Mummy ride, shame Twister was not working due to technical problems, overall a fantastic day out for all the family

we visited the studios on one of the Fright Nights, it was amazing. It was so much fun but scary at the same time. The park is not as good as Universal in California but we had an amazing time. I would definately go back for Halloween.

Wonderful park! Great attractions for the kids, teenagers and adults. We even had fun in the rain. There were lots of rides open and activities to do in the rain with ponchos. Everyone enjoyed themselves!
This is by far the best Halloween event in the country. We return every year and even went for our honeymoon.

Although I'm not an avid film goer, I had read about the attractions here, and as a bit of a ride junkie, universal was on my bucket list. We arrived early, and turned right towards the ET ride - this meant we missed a lot of the queues, and managed 3 rides in the first hour. The great thing about Universal Studios in the summer is that most of the attractions and queues were inside in air conditioning, and were largely unaffected by the frequent storms. As long as you get your head around the fact that Universal Studios is a park to showcase film effects, and not a theme park based around rides, you will not be disappointed. My own personal disappointment is that we are Brits in America on the 4th July. We wanted to see a July 4th Firework display and Universals website said that there would be an addition to their normal evening spectacular. Unfortunately, this was not the case, and we had to make do watching other fireworks in the distance. Had we not been mislead, we would have chosen Seaworld for the 4th of July, as their display was apparently themed for Independence Day.

We visited Universal on the last day of our holiday and were sorely diappointed. Universal Studios was the only one we visited where we found dirty disgusting toilets. The queues were horrendous with well over an hour for most of the popular attractions. Yes, you can buy an express pass but it costs $70 per person where Disney has the fastpass system which is free. This almost doubles the cost of your day. Also some of the attractions are dated and have not been changed for many years, Twister and Disaster being the more noteable of these.

This was my first time at this park, I've been to the one in Hollywood many times and was not a big fan however I came here for the Harry Potter and was surprised on how much fun the rest of the park was! We started our day off at the main park and hit the big rides like the new minion and shrek and a few others. The minion ride was had the longest line I've ever waited in for any ride, They do offer a express pass for most of the rides however I didn't want to spend the extra money for it but I overall felt it would have been a waste since those lines were just as long as the regular. If your a single rider you are allowed in this express line, so if your with a group and you don't mind being split up then this could be a cheaper option.  For eating options we chose to eat at one of the restaurants in the new york area. This restaurant was in our hotel discount packet so If your planning on staying in one of the hotel's around the area check to see if they offer any discounts at restaurants in the park and some even offer discounts at the stores in both parks.  The second day we went to the Island of Adventure and went straight to the Harry Potter which everyone seemed to do as well right when the park opened. The World of Harry Potter was AMAZING! I am a huge Harry Potter fan and I was so impressed with the amount of detail that went into everything from the candy to the items in the store. The lines were kinda bad but the rides were worth it! We ate at the three broomsticks, which was pretty pricey but again worth it! I was just so amazed by this place with the rides to the stores and the food it was worth the trip alone! After Harry potter we went to the other attractions and loved them! The amount of detail that went into all the rides was amazing and really sets them apart from other theme parks.  Overall we really enjoyed ourselves around both parks! They can easily be done in a day however we didn't want to rush everything and choose to do two days which was nice because we usually arrived at the park at 8 and then finished around 5 or 6 and were still able to go to dinner outside the park and a swim at the hotel. The only problem I had with the park was the price at the stores in both parks. It seemed insane to pay 10 dollars for a little coffee mug or $30 for little stuffed animal. However if you have triple A you can get a small discount which helps a little.

We bought two day tickets in advance. My wife did not feel well after the first day and I took a night flight from New York to go with kids to the park on the next day. When I arrived I was told that the tickets are not refundable or transferrable. Even more: Susan, the guest services lady told me in a 'harsh and cold' voice that I should not be bothering her but rather go with my child to the common line (about hour long) to buy a brand new ticket. I have three question: 1. Why tickets are not refundable or transferrable? I would understand that if we would talk about French or US Open tickets because it helps to avoid speculation. 2. Why the tickets lines that long? 3. Why people like Susan work with customers?  I personally do not plan to return to this park any time soon.

In comparison to Islands of Adventure, Universal is a disappointment. Queues for all rides often exceed 60 minutes and there is little air conditioning and no fast pass (express queue is available for an additional $50 per person per day). Staff were incompetent, slow and unhelpful. It's a shame that Jaws has been removed from the park and the Twister and Disaster attractions were disappointing. The refillable mugs are $8 (buy two get a third free) and refills are 95c. While the mug says they are only usable on the day of purchase, we used the same cup every day we visited the Universal Resort.
This is a great place to have a great time! I love the Universal Meal Pass, this is a great value and you have to purchase it while you are at the park. My kids had a great time!!!

We went to Universal Studios Islands of Adventure last week (07/27/12) because our children (ages 11, 20, and 22) really wanted to go to The Wizarding World of Harry Potter. Our master plan was to ride the Dragon Challenge (both the Chinese Fireball and the Hungarian Horntail), the Flight of the Hippogriff, and the Hogwarts Castle Tour Ride (aka Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey).  However, we were immediately drawn into Hogsmeade village as soon as we walked in. We had our photos taken on Platform 9 3/4, alongside the conductor for the Hogwarts train. Then, we walked into various shops - Dervish & Bangs, Honeydukes, Zonko's, and of course, Ollivander's Wand Shop. All of the shops were mobbed. For those of you who MUST purchase a wand, it should be mentioned that you can obtain 'popular' wands (such as the Harry Potter wand) at ANY of the Universal Studios shops on site. However, if you want one of the other more obscure character wands, you need to go to Ollivander's.  Back to the rides - we enjoyed all the rides in Harry Potter World. IMHO, the Hungarian Horntail was the best ride, but many preferred the Hogwarts Castle Tour ride. We loved the village of Hogsmeade and enjoyed the Three Broomsticks restaurant. It was nice and cool and not crowded at all when we were there. Out of the five of us, only two of us enjoyed Butterbear. Be advised - it is very sweet and tastes like butterscotch. I enjoyed it very much, but my daughter became a little queasy after drinking it, then walking around in the heat and riding the rides.  Because we were @ Universal Studios from a cruise ship, we were on a very limited time schedule, and just planned to spend our entire time @ Harry Potter World, and did not ride any of the other rides except for Poseidon's Fury which we all enjoyed. I had wanted to ride the Incredible Hulk ride, but couldn't guilt any of my family members to ride it with me.  All in all, the Islands of Adventure Theme Park was tremendous fun, and we would have enjoyed spending more time there.

I live 2 hours away so I come here all the time! And when I do, I always stay on-site for the night! We came early June and now I'm going to say we will not really go during summer. Probably only on weekends during the school year. I'm going to start by telling you about the hotels! There are three of them. The Loews Royal Pacific, The Hard Rock Hotel, and Loews Portofino Bay Hotel. I have stayed at the Royal twice before this trip. But this time we did the Portofino. I'm going to say the Portofino is a little bit better then the Royal. The rooms were big and the hotel was beautiful! I would highly recommend you stay on-site! It is more money, but the add ons make it worth it! I would say go for the Royal if you want to stay close to IOA and you have a budget. But Portofino if you want to get away from the parks and be able to relax without the sound of screams next door. I walked in the Hard Rock and it doesn't have that uniqueness like the other two, but it was nice.  Now for the parks! The studios and Islands are very different! Visit both! They are WAY BETTER THAN DISNEY!!!!!! The studios is like movie and music themed and I think it's my favorite between the two. I have not been on the new dispicable me ride yet but soon I will! I have done every other ride. Shrek 4-D was fun! The line looks very long outside but they fit everyone in! Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit is a MUST DO!!!!! I absolutely love it! It's my favorite roller coaster ever! It's so different! You get to choose the song you want to listen to! Livin in fast forward is what I always listen to! Make sure you ride it no matter how long the line is! It moves fast! Next is mummy. I think this is one of the coolest rides here! I always fast pass all the rides and this is a must fast pass! Be careful in the line! They will try to scare you! It's really funny though! The ride is really fun! It is a roller coaster and it has a few surprises that I'm not going to give away! But you will love it! Next ride is Disaster. It was okay. The whole thing lasts about 30 minutes so don't do this as a quick ride. You are making a movie in this do it's interesting. The next ride is men in black! This is one of those shooting games like toy story mania. It's fun and you get into it! It's spins and turns! You are competing against another car! So make sure you do well! And after this is the Simpsons ride! This is a simulator! And the line takes some time. You will be outside in the heat for quite some time but once you get to the waiting area it's cold and feels great! The ride is fun and beware of the baby powder! And next is ET. It's a slow ride. It's not that exciting, but I would say try it if you want. Then pretty much the other rides are kid stuff and movies. I have not dined at this park. I usually take a water taxi to the hotel and eat. And you do not have to be a hotel guest to do this! I recommend Islands at the Royal Pacfic for lunch or Mama Dellad at the Portofino for dinner!  Now for IOA! This is the most popular park but if you are there for a long period of time it will get boring! I'm going to give you a list of the big thrills! They are the Hulk, Dr. Doom, Dragons Challenge, Forbidden Journey, and Spiderman. My favorite of those is Forbidden Journey. It's in the Hogwarts Castle and stay on-site so you don't have to wait. This does not have fast pass! On-site hotels get early access to this!!!!!! I would do these rides then the water rides! They are Rip Saw Falls, Popeye, and Jurrasic Park! My favorite is Rip Saw Falls! You get soaked! The drop is really fun too! Jurassic park has the most intense drop. You will get jerked at the bottom so be prepared. Popeye is a river rapid ride and I don't find it that exciting. Other than those rides is the dr. Seuss land. That is for the younger kids and for non thrill seekers. For dining at the park. I recommend the Three Broomsticks or Mythos. For Mythos, make reservations a few days in advance! It is a great resturaunt!  Now city walk, I can't really say anything about it. But it's really just shops, resturaunts, and a movie theater. But at night, they have multiple clubs open. And for on-site hotel guests. The water Taxi lines are really long at this time!  Well now I'm going to give you a few tips!  - STAY ON-SITE!!!! - Get to the parks early! - Get fastpass(unless staying on-site) - Go for the popular rides first - Dont do single rider line at Rip ride rockit! It will be longer! - Bring AAA card for discounts!  I have some photos too! I will Have some of the hotels and if not look at the reviews on trip advisor! They are on there too!  I hope this helped and if you have any questions just ask!

Don't hesitate to visit Universal either the Studios or Islands of Adventure. They are terrific theme parks. The entrances are situated close together so that you don't have to walk much between the two, so getting a park pass for both is definitely a plus. Here are some tips: 1) do NOT buy the meal plan. The choices are poor, and the food is generally terrible. Moreover, you will just about break even, so don't bother 2) Definitely DO get the express pass to beat the lines. You will be thanking yourself over and over again. Unfortunately there are a few attractions that do not take the express pass, including the most crowded of them all: the Harry Potter ride. That said, it is still worth the money. You will finish the park muchmore quickly, and then ride a second time while others are still waiting for single rides. A great time in guaranteed.

July is not the time to sightsee in Florida! That being said, we had a blast. The Harry Potter ride is overrated but the rest of the park was fun. Our kids (7,10,13) were troopers given the heat and long lines!

The organization of this attraction is dangerous. To start, there are three exits to this ride, one of which is before the waiting area for parents so your kids can exit without you seeing them. There are height limitations so parents cannot enter, you send your kids off for 45- 60 mins unsupervised. My wife and I split up to ensure our kids couldnt exit without out finding them, no seating area at one of the exits. Upon questioning a worker about the set up he also said it was not good. This is an attraction that is poorly arranged, limits supervision for parents, and is a lawsuit waiting to happen. Dont send you on this ride, its not work worrying for an hour, which is what all parents were doing--No FUN.

Overall worth going but note the studios bit is undergoing some major refits so lots of stuff missing. Two attractions in the studios bit go give a wide berth, they are Twister and Disaster. They are rubbish. There was also no stuntshow. A tip, go around the park anticlockwise. Go to the city walk in the evening as its always buzzing with nightlife.
The Simpsons and Despicable Me are brilliant we loved them you really feel like you are on a roller coaster. Our kids had a fab time the highlight for our 8 year old was seeing spongebob.

Just came back from living in Kissimmee for 2 weeks. My five friends and myself visited all the parks but here I will talk about universal studios. We had the Orlando flexiticket plus which means we had already paid and got in free...before we had even arrived at the park we had to pay to park the car which we thought we could park in the street.... Nope we had to park in the parks car park which costed $15 every time we came to the park. We had two cars so had to pay $30 just on parking then finally we arrived. Everything seemed great in the park until we realised the prices. To buy a 16oz drink was $3.95 every time but then you could buy a park cup for $8.95 and then pay only a dollar for refills but still slot of people aren't loaded. The food at the stalls were overpriced aswell. We went into stores and even a keyring with your name was $8.....all in all it was a great time on the rides as we went in September so the biggest line we waited in was only 10 mins as the kids were back at school. The only let down was the prices of food, drinks, parking and merchandise. Overall a great day and also I must add all the staff we so fantastic....everyone of them were very helpful and courteous.

Loved it!! Only complaint was the walk from the garage to the actual location. I was tired by the time I got to the attractions. Once there, it was very refreshing to have so many options of things to do to choose.
I loved Universal Orlando, both the Islands of Adventure and Studios is great both for singles and families. Although a little pricey....the entrance fees especially.....but a great place to visit.

Everyone's going to Islands for Potter so we chose to do Universal first. We finished the entire park by 2:30 pm. Had lunch and decided to go to city walk and look around. They need to add some attractions or just make the entire thing Harry Potter. The one ride we did twice was Minions mayhem. That was great.

I must say Islands of Adventure is by far the most fun park I have had the opportunity to visit. After a week at the Disney parks I wasn't sure what to expect. The rides were fantastic. I have never screamed or laughed more. My grandson became ill on the Harry Potter ride and he was treated with great compassion. The staff came over and talked with him and ask about clothing size. They promptly returned with a new t-shirt and apologized for not having shorts in his size. We were instructed to go to a close by shop and get him a pair of shorts to change into and called ahead for a fast pass on any ride of our choice. We had an awesome day. I personally loved the Harry Potter ride and rode multiple times but avoid if you experience motion sickness. The Hulk, Dr. Doom, Spider-Man were also great thrill rides. The water rides are fabulous. You will get wet!
If you love to be scared and like gruesome things this is the best place to go. You do have to be there early because the lines are ridiculous or better yet go sunday or thursday

Love this place lots to do for all the family my favourite was the classic E.T you need to spend a full day hear as thers lots to do and see its one of the smaller parks but still has some great rides.
Fantastic Park, Brilliant Rides unfortunately height restrictions on most rides meant our 3 year old couldnt ride, so not very fair having to pay for ticket when they have to miss out on most rides

good day had here, this side of Universal has a slower pace to it with more shows, however the big roller coaster is a must for thrill seekers.... Dispicable me is a must do for all ages, absoluetly brilliant

I have taken my family to Universal Studios every year since 1997. After the blatant political bias that was evident during the HHN Bill and Ted show, I will never be back. This was supposed to be family entertainment not a ridiculously obvious infomercial supporting Obama!! Never again will I spend money here!

These are always a good parks but I would say they are not tailored so much for the younger children. Some great rides here at both parks I am not going to name them as I would list most of the rides here. The Halloween horror nights are great this year was not as good as previous years but still worth going to. My only slight moan is the shows at both park leave a bit to be desired I would say they are ok but would not want to see them too often. But don’t let this put you off seeing them for the first time.

Not being a fan of roller coasters etc we decided to do the studios. Having a knee injury had to hire an ECV scooter. As we arrived early we were lucky enough to be able to rent one but it is advisable to book one in advance, Disney Parks won't do pre booking. There have been several changes since our last visit, Back to the Future one Simpsons, great family fun, Jaws ride has gone but something else being built in its place. As it was low season the stunt show was not on But of course there are holding Halloween nights this month. Even so, there was still plenty to do and see. The queue for "The Mummy" was very long.the ride itself was only a couple of minutes . The good old Blues Brothers still performing and it was absolutely great. Didn't find there was quite as much ECV access there had unless you have a wheelchair it is a long walk from the disabled car park through City Walk to where you can pick up the ECV. On the whole a very enjoyable day.

I have been to Universal a few times and never I was disappointed. Attractions are incredible, only problems can be with waiting too long in queue, but if you're willing to spend some extra cash get a priority ticket and glide through. Fun for both adults and kids

The 2 parks are amazing loads of rides, shops and restraunts. There are 2 parks here you wil, need a day each to get round them. You can purchase a food plan which is a good offer. Great photograph opportunities to save your memories. Highly Recommended !!!!!

Great: Harry Potter area, Forbidden Journey, Dueling Dragons coaster (only in the front row of seats), stores and Three Broomsticks restaurant. Hulk roller coaster is still terrific. Noticed this time that head snapping is accentuated in the seats closer to the back.  Good: Spiderman, Minion Mayhem, Simpsons, Storm Force (very short, so only good if no line), Hippogriff (for kids or weenies), Rip Ride Rocket (no Express Pass, not worth a long wait), Camp Jurassic (for kids who like to climb and explore).  So/so: Mummy, Pteranodon Flyers (good for kids, but wait can be ridiculous -- we walked on during early admission), Jurassic Park River Adventure.  Terrible: ET, Poseidon's Fury, Suess Landing (whole thing, except for smallest kids, and if your kids are this small, you have no business paying big money for you all to come to this park), Twister, Men in Black.  So many areas are crying out for demolition/staring over. I think they would have been better off keeping Jaws (had kitsch appeal, like Disney Jungle Cruise) and wiping out Lost Continent, Suess Landing, and other areas which are really pathetic and have become places to walk through on your way to other areas.

Great park, great rides, great day! We love this park, we are a family of 5 with teenagers and there is always something to do in this park. Great pizza's when your hungry and they are huge!!!! Looking forward to going back one day to see the Transformers 3D ride!

I loved every ride and show I saw in this park, but didn't love every person, or thing I saw. The parks weren't that clean, and I found a roach walking through the gift shop at the exit of the mummy ride. Also, they have problems managing their lines, as they moved the lines for Harry Potter, and had to lines merge which made some people REALLY mad. I loved Harry Potter, and Spiderman was super cool as well. If you like thrills... make sure to ride the Hulk. It was AWESOME!

We spent nearly 3 days at Universal (Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure) with our kids (8 and 11). It was a fantastic visit. The lines were very manageable, the staff was helpful and friendly, the food was good (and not overly expensive). The rides were perfect for my kids with lots of variety. The park is very walkable and manageable. 2-3 days was perfect for November because the lines weren't long. You may need longer during peak season. Harry Potter world was beautiful. Kids (and us) loved it, but definitely the most crowded part of the park, so we preferred other areas. Highlights were the Hulk, Disaster, and Mummy rides. What a blast! We used the "preferred" parking which got us in faster and saved some walking (which really helped since our kids are young, but obviously no longer in strollers).

I recently travelled to Florida with my son (15) and nephew (14) to Universal Orlando. The boys wanted to go to HHN so I surprised them with tickets when we arrived. We did three houses pretty quick (2-3 hours) and they were good. We really enjoyed the street actors who scared us and were amazed at the makeup and costumes. Then we hit the busy side of the park to see the other houses, we stood in line for 2 hours to get into one house and after 2 hours it's hard to remember you are having fun. There were so many people who bought an express pass that those of us without were really stuck. We finally gave up when all the wait signs said 1.5-2 hour wait. The line we waited in for 2 hours had a 1 hour wait time posted when we entered. I am glad we did not spend full price on these tickets as it would have set a bad tone for our vacation. I am also surprised at how Universal seems to push alcohol.  Things we liked: It is a fun evening (at $35-$40). The houses, costumes, makeup is great and scary.  Things we disliked: Long wait times, drinking, obnoxious behavior. It is bad enough to stand in line for 2 hours but to be surrounded by drunks with foul mouths makes it seem like an eternity.  I came away feeling like Universal could not care less about me, my safety, or my comfort; it is all about money. They say no one under 13 will be admitted but there were families with baby carriages, toddlers and young children. I have no issue with this, but if you are going to have families, you must accomodate their needs as well as the needs of the adult partiers. I think Universal should decide exactly who they want their customer to be for HHN and do some honest marketing. Why risk alienating future customers for the price of admission.  I am glad I went or I would have thought that I was missing out but I will never go back. The boys, on the other hand, would return.  Let me finish by saying that even though HHN was a bust I enjoyed my vacation at Universal Orlando. I think it is a wonderful park - well run, the staff is wonderful and very entertaining. I have only good things to say about Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure!

Went during the offseason (the week before Thanksgiving) and got a pretty good deal. Bought two days and got a third free. The parks are pretty close together so the multipark pass is worth it. I went back and forth a couple times as each park has its highlights. Enjoyed the Hogwarts castle roller coaster. I agree the parking was a lot. There are I-trolley stops nearby that go near most lodging at $1.50 / person each way times family of 4 makes $12.00. The flexibility of having my own vehicle was worth it. Also, you can go out and come back the same day without having to pay again. I was there on business so it was nice to be able to go for awhile, leave and come back without having to pay to park again.

My wife and I have been to this park so many times and its worth it. The rides are exhilarating! The staff was always around to answer questions. Although the food is just ok. I wouldn't recommend it for young children. More for the adults to do than the kiddies.

We love Universal Studios! There is literally nothing about Universal that we didn't like - even the food was great! The park is very well laid out and as we visited the week before Thanksgiving the christmas decorations were out in full force and looked wonderful. And as for the rides and shows - brilliant! The two Universal parks are streets ahead of the Disney parks in my opinion - we had a great time in both, can't fault them!

Visited this place in April. To be honest it was my first ever visit in park like this and since I was visiting with my mum and family friends in age group of mid 50's I didn't think it was going to be so much fun. I was wrong. The attractions are brilliant especialy the rollercoasters. You can't miss the Harry Potter,Spider Man and the Simpsons ride out. It was great. We did buy the express passes since we were visiting Orlando for a day only and wanted to see the most of it but at the time we were visiting it wasn't that busy and there were hardly any qeues. The resort was kept clean dispite so much folk wondering around. Plenty of restaurants and kiosks to stop for a snack or drink. Big variety of attractions to choose from for any age group. I recomend to do the water attractions at the end of your day as it can get very wet and also bring some other pair of trousers and shirts to get change after you've done these. You'll be soaking wet. Rain coats won't work.

We took our 5 year old twin boys to Universal Studios along with 4 adults the week after Thanksgiving. It was a great time to go because all rides were walk on which was nice. There is not a whole lot there for younger kids to do especially during Winter/Fall when the water attractions are too cold to do. My kids did love the balladium area in the Curious George playground. They played there for a solid hour and would have gone longer! They also enjoyed the Men In Black ride. They rode that 7 total times! Adults loved that ride too. The Mummy coaster was very fun. I was not a huge fan of the Rip Ride Rockit coaster.  We watched the nighttime movie tribute show and it was okay but I was not super impressed. Same for their parade. Just not up to Disney quality. But maybe they are okay with that. The employees were friendly and efficient. Not great for food allergies at counter service restaurants because all their pizza dough is processed in a factory with peanuts so our go to peanut free food (pizza) was not even safe. So we had to eat at Finnegans where they made him a grilled cheese by special request that was safe.  I think this is more for older kids or adults and teens because of the thrill rides but they do have enough so that there is something for the whole family. They were building a huge new ride while we were there. The worst ride is the Shrek 4 D. It was just terrible. No other way to describe it. Despicable Me was the better 4 D show so I say just do that one and skip Shrek.

We bought a three day ticket, but were done with both parks after one day. It was the first week in December - so the park was relatively uncrowded. But other than Harry Potter, a couple of Roller Coasters, and a few decent rides (Spiderman, MIB, Mummy) most of the park is nothing much. My wife enjoyed the Macy parade and a couple of shows. I'd say go to the Hard Rock Hotel for two nights - and do the park in a day using the early access and the express pass. Hit the City Walk both nights if that appeals to you. Don't plan on Universal being worth more than 2 days max.

Having spent our time in Orlando, we took the kids to the main theme parks in the area. Disney and Universal are probably the more famous parks in town and we loved our time in each of them.  The kids loved the spiderman and hulk rides, and I have got to say I actually preferred the rides here than in Disney. However I will give it a lower rating as I was a little dissapointed by the food choice compared to what we had at disney.  Overall a magical trip, must come back!

Soooo wonderfull the Halloween event, we just loved it!! Its scary.... vey scary.... certainly not for seniors or little kids, also there is a looot of alcohol in the park. For me and my husband it was an awsome experience, I got scared soo may times that I almost Cry... the actors are so well dressed an the make up is awsome and soo real! The park lower the lights, there is a lot of fog, and there are a lot of scary characters all over the park. We didn´t have enough time to visit all of the haunted houses, the wait lines were incredible, up to 120 minutes, and the event only goes on from 7 pm to 1 am, so you cannot wait soo much in line for the haunted houses, but we got to visit the one of the walking dead and it was awsome, so scary, and real zombies haunted us! Also we got to ride all the main rides in the park with little to nothing wait time since all the people is in line for the haunted houses. Alcohol everywhere, a lot of drink stands all over the place and refill cups made the night, It is like a night out but with scary characters behind you!.... and in front of you,...... beside you,..... behind again, and again.... jajajaja loved it!
Brilliant theme parks. Hard rock cafe is classic.  Saw TNA being recorded as well fulfilling a life long ambition.  Do it.

Universal did not meet our expectations at all. The employees did not seem happy.  Harry Potter was amazing the whole area was done very well. However it was very crowded. This is not a place for toddlers and grandmas. I really wish we would have known this before we went. My baby ended up spending all day in the stroller and my mom was bored. We liked the rides but I don't think I would spend the money to go back.

We paid $850 for the family. Took us an hour to get in. Then proceed to wait in lines that were as long as 3 1/2 hr long. All the big rides were 2 hrs +. We road only 3 rides. We could not even get into Harry Potter area. They had it closed off so only people holding a pass could get in. They ran out off passes. They could have said something about this before we bought our tickets. There is no doubt they were way over capacity and very surprised a fire marshal would not have seen a safety hazard. Not exaggerating the place was packed. It was no fun for our kids. One of the little ones only went on one ride. It was a was of money and you could clearly see it was only about the money for Universal Studios. Fast passes were a $109.00 for each. We will never go again. Stay away for the holiday.

Why after 10 months would Universal Studios or GE not respond to my concern about our visit last year. Just to reiterate, they've turned this them park into a long wait, hard sell and very annoying experience. We were about 20th in line when the ticket windows opened and waited an HOUR to get in. Every ticket seller was trying to upsell and customers were at the windows for 15 - 30 minutes. This is ridiculous and wasteful. When I asked to speak to a manager I was denied. When I asked for a name to contact I was denied. I'm sick of large companies that are perfectly comfortable trampling on customers rights. If hat wasn't bad enough when we got in the trash barrles were overflowing with trash with garbage and cups on the ground. I think it would be good training for all Universal employees to spend a morning at Disney World. Fix this GE or at least respond to me!! Ronp7214aol.com

We visited Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure. The rides are good - for 11-12 yr or older. Hogwarts and Hogmeads is quaint and nice to walk around. Ollivander's is tiny and extremely crowded with long wait times. We bought the meal plan at Universal Studios and 4 people in our group got sick the same night - they all ate the pizza there. The parade is very very ordinary. The parks overall do not have the magic of Disney but are worth visiting once.

Don't go there on holidays ; you expect long lines but you haven't seen them until you go on the holidays (P.S. Go to Harry Potter first if you want to get into the ride; they close that section off if there are to many people).

We were there Jan. 9th and again on the 13th, 2013 and had a fabulous time. The longest wait time for any ride was 40 min. and most were only 5 to 15 min. so no fast pass was needed anyway. Everything was very clean and it wasn't overly crowded. We were very luck to have great weather. When I am back in the area I would definitely go back.

We actually had more fun here than at Islands of Adventure which seems different from most reviews. There were a ton of shows and we loved them all. There were also great rides and fun coasters. I would suggest getting an express pass. We didn't get one the day before at Islands and had plenty of time to get everything in. It was still a fairly slow day when we went here, but because there were more shows we wanted to see, it did take longer to see everything. Also, there is no early entry to Universal like there is at Islands, so even if you have a one hour early admission pass, it will not work here. This seemed to be a surprise to everyone standing in line. Definitely see the Beetlejuice show if you like music shows and the Fear Factor show was great too.
You will enjoy a lot. Orlando is a great place to be. Try buying tickets from International Drive, it would be cheaper.

We had not been since 2006, and I must say we were extremely happy to return. We avoided the water rides, it was a bit chilly. But we were able to ride everything multiple times. Many of our favorites (jaws, back to the future, king kong, etc) had been replaced, but we had a blast. Once again I suggest the dining plan. For three days for a family of 5, we payed about $300. We could eat at three restaraunts as much and as many times as we pleases. Which is great with picky kids. Take my word, and ride Harry Potter as much as possible, and walk around diagon ally. It was great.

We had not been here for about 12 years. In 2001 we only went to the Universal Studios movie theme park. Not a lot had changed there since 2001. They still had the "Twister" attraction (which is pretty lame). Who in the younger generation remembers the movie, "Twister"? I consider this park mildly entertaining. Perhaps my favorite attraction is "Terminator 3D". One other thing that turned me off about this park was the people at the "Shrek 4D" attraction. When we paid for our admission, we were told that there was a special customer lounge for those who paid with an American Express card at the Shrek 4D attraction. When I asked someone at the Shrek 4D attraction about this supposed customer lounge, the person went "into his character" and played the part of a smarmy resident of the kingdom of Duloc. I never did get a straight answer, and was too tired (nearing the end of our day) to dig any deeper. Great help, Universal; that kind of B.S. should be saved for those 15 years old or younger.  The Islands of Adventure park was far more entertaining. Perhaps out favorite was the Spiderman 3D ride. Unbelievable technology. It really feels like you are immersed in the action, with characters jumping on your car as you ride through. The Harry Potter ride was good, although not 3D. I went on the Hulk roller coaster, and felt weak in the knees for a while after getting off! That is one wicked roller coaster. I do not recommend the Jurassic Park River Ride, unless you like getting soaking wet. Personally, I thought that sucked.
