Regarding the part about your wallet... admission cost to this place is really ridiculous. I think mentioning prices in these reviews is frowned upon, so I'll just say that you should look for discounts. Also, unless you purchase an express pass for another exorbitant fee, expect to wait in long lines to get on rides.

went back last year for the 7th time (i think might be more) can't get enough of them! the hulk has to be my favourite! just love the way you think your going slow and then your spinning about outside. the rock and roller is also brill! if you want a break from the coasters go to the Rocky horror show the entertainment is great too as are the animal shows. for a cool down there is a few water rides but be prepared to be soaked! Definitely going back again. The great thing is your park ticket you buy to get in lets you on all the rides...........nothing extra to pay!

Once the sticker-shock wears off a bit, you can appreciate the more adult rides/attractions than those found at Disney (not as clean, though). I enjoyed the rollercoaster, and the Mummy ride.. But that was about it.. I was a bit dissapointed by the Terminator 2 show. I'd forgotten how annoying Ed Furlong was (at least his voice had changed by the time they got around to doing this show), and it was pretty corny.. (SUPER annoying pre-show Cyberdyne spokesperson (how do they DO that 6 times a day?? They must have to switch them out often to avoid suicides). We got chased out at 6pm (even though the stated closing time was 7) because there was some big shots having an event by the Men in Black section.. Big gaping nothing where the Jaws ride used to be.. The food was alright.. I had a good cappucino and danish in a cafe near the enterance. Thw Twister show was terrible.. Waste of time..

I love Universal Orlando Resort everytime ive vissited the parks ive seen many improvments and why i keep going back. I love how the fact that both parks Universal Studios Florida and Islands of adventure are close that you can walk to both of them. Not like Disney where you have to either drive take a bus or monorail from park to park. I love the Wizarding World of Harry Potter very authentic to the point. the Dragon Challenge coaster was awesome. And Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey is the best ride there. I like the fact they have lockers to put personal bellongings in when you ride you dont have to worry about things falling off. Disney doesn't have lockers! They updated the amazing spider man ride now its in HD 3D which is amazing. The food is excellent we had dinner at pat obriens food was amazing. If you are a member of AAA bring your membership card with you. you save 10% on everything from food-souviniers. As i came over the years Universal never had an end of the day fireworks/special show. Well they answered my call in Universal Studios Florida there is now a new Fireworks tribute show called Universal Studios 100 years spactacular. The show is amazing with clips from movies and lights and fireworks i reccomend ending your day at universal by going to this alone. I cant wait to go back to Universal to see things wow me and they are constantly improving the parks and the resorts.

We had family visiting from Chicago and decided to take them to Universal Studios. We had the perfect day. The crowds were minimal. The most we had to wait in line for any ride was 30 minutes. The nice thing about Universal Studios is that most of the lines are in covered areas or inside so you are protected from the sun. It's not your typical amusement park with lots of fast rides. All the rides or shows are themed around Universal Movies or TV shows. There are lots of 3-D and special effects. There was just enough to see and do to fill the day.

Universal as a whole craps all over Disney which is made for kids to be fair. But Universal is more for teenagers up to pensioners. The rollercoasters are so much better such as Rockit Rollercoaster, Mummy Returns, The Hulk and the Dueling Dragons many thrills to be had. The simulators are also great and full of laughs like the Shrek 4-d and Simpsons ride. The Terminator ride was also really good. If you like coasters then go here also if you love your films go here. Harry Potter section is bloody brilliant as Hagrid would say. So much effort has gone into it, I also know they are building a track for the Hogwarts express from islands of Adventure to Diagon Alley which will be constructed in the Studios and transformers ride looks almost completed.

If your kids are over 9 this is the park for you. Lots of thrill rides and shows. It is the best theme park in Orlando hands down. I was a Disney nut for years until a friend told me to try Universal and now I am hooked. Last week we spent 4 days in Disney a 4 in Universal and regret the 4 in Disney. Lots of Great places to eat in City walk with no need to get on a Bus. Don't miss the mini golf either.

This park is probably great for teenagers. Not so great for younger children. There are shows and rides for everyone except the young. There are probably only two or three rides/shows geared towards younger children. There are several "playground" areas with water features geared towards the young. The water features are probably great in the dead of summer but not so much in January. There are also misting machines all over the park that you can't avoid. Not necessary in January. There were a lot of eateries and features that were closed. No signage displayed. You only knew when you walk up to the building and it was completely dark and barren. This is a small park by most large amusement park standards. The sister park (Islands of Adventure) is much better for all.

We had won some tickets to go to the blue man group. I must say it looks like they all work really hard and it was a great show. They did a good job and had great time which you do need to make this a show worth watching. The only thing is that we always wanted to go but did not know what to expect. If you are a family with kids, you are absolutely going to have a blast and so are the kids. If you are a couple you might want to go to another show. I am still happy we went and enjoyed our time there.

I visited Islands of Adventure. The rides looked like fun, but I could not tell you for sure. After spending almost $200.00 to get in the door, there was a 2 hr wait for any ride. 30 mins if you spend an extra $55.00 per person. Universal has no crowd control and they expect you to pay extra for their lack of planning. I went back a couple months later and tried Universal studios. Wow what a let down. I took my girlfriend and my 5 year old son. My 5 year old was bored on the rides. I don't know how to explain that any better. Once again there is no crowd control, the food was inedible(My son wouldn't eat pizza!!!) I could put cheese on cardboard and he would eat it, but not pizza from universal. The people were rude, the rides were boring, and the food bad. Cost $400.00 for 2hrs of misery. Universal is really good at getting you in the door and taking your money, but thats where thier service ends. There are a lot of great theme parks, but this is not one of them. Go to Busch Gardens or Disney. You and your kids will have a much better time for less money.

Universal studios was great but please realize it is more shows than rides, We brought along a 3 year old and she could not do a good amount of the activities. I recommend 5 and older for this park. If choosing between universal and islands of adventure, i would go to islands of adventure because that has more rides as well as harry potter world. Nonetheless, all the shows and rides are amazing. A few of the best are the horror makeup show, revenge of the mummy. ET adventure, woody woodpecker's nuthouse coaster, fear factor live, and the simpson's ride.

Visited Universal Studios in October 2012, we had a great day & visited several times in our trip with the flex ticket.  There was quite a lot building work going on when we visited but am looking forward to end result it looks good!  We found the Rockit quite rough & jerky so avoid if you are sensitive to those kind of rides. The Mummy is one of the best dark rides I have been on. The new Dispicable Me attraction is very well done & there are "real" minions to dance with at the end :)  We found the food prices to be quite resonable, counter service offerings being around the $8 mark which isnt that bad to be honest!  All in all an excellent day out, cant wait to go back when all the new stuff opens!

visited jan 2012,was staying in disney port orleans resort.I had 2 park tickets, took a cab ride there and back from disney, cost $68 return plus tip.We had an early start, and stayed all day, entry queues were fairly long, but ticketing was simple, we bought neck pass holders for $3 each to store tickets in,good move..This is a looong day, especially doing both parks,too much to take in really, queues were minimal,probs 10 to 15 mins wait on most rides, this is the place to come if you like rides,in the end we ran out of time,i travelled with a 9 yr old and a 16 yr old, they loved the rides.Harry potter world is brilliant, we bought wands to bring home, queues for ollivanders were ridiculous, so skipped that,butter beer was lovely.I found the walk into the park neverending,and because of this and the cab fare, didn't go back, even though our tickets lasted 2 weeks.It was no cheaper to get an organized coach, and travelling solo, i would not use another transport.There were a LOT of teens in these parks,a lot of running around excited kids,not really the family atmosphere you get in the disney parks.I'm going back to disney this year, i have not bought tickets for universal this time, so overall,a very expensive, but totally amazing day out!

I read some of the bad reviews but to me they are all pointless. Universal studios and Islands of adventure should not be compared to Disney and if people read up on the park before they went they would know its not really suitable for young kids.  For both parks if your from the uk the best time to go if you can is before the kids summer holidays start (hard to do). June and September aren't as busy as July and August and the queues are smaller.  Universal studios: More suitable for people who don't like big roller coasters as there's only really 2 (mummy returns & rock n rolla) but the rides aren't really for young kids. I go with my family every year and my mum Hates roller coasters, she did the mummy returns once but never again but she loves universal there's loads she can do. Her favourite is shrek. A family favourite is men in black and we always enjoy jaws. ET is a must for the whole family it's fantastic and beetle juice has something for everyone. Food isn't sprawled out across the park there's specific food courts/areas across the park which I think is better but it's personal preference.  Islands of adventure: Not for people who don't like roller coasters really. However! My mum hates them but there's still things for her to do like spider man, the log fumes, Harry potter etc. and she enjoys having the chance to sunbathe while the rest of us go on the bigger rides.  If you like roller coasters this is the park for you with the hulk, doom (wouldn't q for this ride) and Harry potter triwizard. There's still other things to do and walking around Harry potter land is great!  These parks aren't as decorated as Disney which is a shame but that's not what these parks are about.  Citywalk is great at night bubba gumps is a must if you like shrimp and the cinema is nice to fill some time. Hard Rock Cafe is what you expect and u shud book in advance.

Please bear in mind we are a couple in our 30's with no children and Universal had been recommended to us as a place for people of all ages.  We visited Magic Kingdom and hated it. We visited Epcot and thought it was great and we visited Disney Hollywood Studios and it wasn't quite as good as Epcot. We really did think that the Magic Kingdom was poor until we visited Universal Studios. Then we realised it was poor but not the worst and most over-rated place.  Things started off badly at Universal. We had already got the tickets at Seaworld the day before (A 14 day Orlando Flex Ticket for admission to multiple parks). We queued up in the long queue at the gates only to be told that our tickets were not valid because we got them from Seaworld and it's Spring Break. I was quite annoyed because I wouldn't purchase tickets for 14 days if I knew they weren't valid by the next day. I went to Guest Relations and queued up again and they said there was nothing wrong with them. Queued up again at the gates with a different person and got in straight away.  We were expecting Universal studios to be about shows because the next door Islands of Adventure was about rides. However there was some nice themed streets but overall it was just more rides but indoors rather than outdoors. We expected to be able to see how they produced the movies and see some informational shows. The only real show was a show called Fear which was a live show with real visitors, but we only watched it for about 10 minutes before getting bored and leaving. Instead Universal studios was just a series of buildings with themed rides based on old movies. It was rather boring. The only benefit was really the surrounding area of Universal Citywalk which was a very well laid out area with plenty of restaurants, cinema, crazy golf and shops to choose from.

There is something for everyone here great roller coasters to calm kids rides Our 8-12 year olds are big enough to ride all the rides and still have a great time playing at camp Jurassic and curious George ball pit for hours. There are even a few good places to eat inside the parks
2 days at Universal is plenty. Perfect for bigger kids. Lots of fun. Great rides. Good food. Fun to be had by all.
In my opinion this is the best of all the parks in Orlando absolutely fantastic, everyone is so friendly and helpful and the attractions are first class

Only one good thing to say about our family visit. The ribs were good. That is it! This park is expensive, over crowded, has rude employees. Now, I know it was spring break, not the best time to go if you don't like crowds, but this was impossible. One of our first experience with the park staff, was when we waited 15 minutes for the man to scan in our tickets to enter the park, and the machine would not work...he said "go to the Back of the line" and walked away WHAT? Waited over two hours for the Spiderman ride~ Loud music playing while we were waiting~Could go on about all of this, but read other reviews~ I guess they don't care much for our, the customers experience.........they are just in it to get as much $$ as possible out of your pocket. Also, to get the line cut pass where you can go to the front of the line, just pay $100.00 per person~ talk about creating a negative class system. Again, I know it was spring break, but to treat customers like this is appalling! Also, just wanted to add, I went to another large sea mammal park the next day and even with the crowds, I was very impressed with how they still were able to create an awesome experience. Just Saying!!!

The ONLY reason we went to Universal Studios was to take in the Harry Potter/Hogwarts area. We are die hard Harry Potter fans and were so excited to go see it. Upon walking miles to get there, it was packed cheek by jowl and one could hardly move. Not entirely unexpected but the area isn't that large. Somehow I expected MORE. I loved the little shops that showed Hermione's dress and Harry's tux with the hidden action in the 'store' windows, the cauldron shop and scrivener's shop were fun to peer into their windows, too. We loved the other stores for wands, photos and keepsakes. But it was too claustrophobic. I don't suffer from this but it made me very uncomfortable. We tried the Pumpkin Beer and Butter Beer! Every single theme person was wonderful and a delight to talk to. I would recommend it but with the understanding you walk the entire depth of the park before you get there and get back to your parking. And don't expect too much...it's wonderfully done but just not big enough!

Universal and Islands of Adventure certainly know how to do it. Staff are funny and attentive. The attractions definitely suit older kids and adults more than Disney. The pre build up to rides and shows is entertaining and well done. We returned after a break of 12 years and it's definitely advanced since then. A couple of attractions are the same but with added extras to modernise and appeal to today's visitors. Great day out and longest queue was 30 mins and that was rare. Can't wait to return in the future to experience Transformers, which is a huge construction in progress for this Summer

I don't even know where to begin. We started at Universal Studios on our holiday, they have a wide selection of rides for all ages, and are constructing new ones at the moment. The Simpsons Ride is a fantastic family ride, along with Men In Black: Alien Attack and Despicable Me: Minion Mayhem, however my favorite ride in the parks (and all of Florida) is the Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit, it looks a lot worse than it actually is and you shouldn't miss it out. it's a rollercoaster where you choose a song to listen to, which is synced perfectly to the ride, and I find it fantastic. We also went for the Mardi Gras parade which was a great event, and watched the "Universal Nighttime Spectacular" in the lagoon afterwards.  Next Up, Islands of Adventure, this park is generally busier than Universal Studios due to The Wizarding World of Harry Potter, however shouldn't be missed. My advice is leave Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey right until the end of the day, when I went the wait time was 125 minutes in the morning, and went down to 20 around 9pm. I usually start the day by heading over to Superhero Island, which features the Incredible Hulk Coaster, another fantastic ride, one of my favorites, there's also other attractions and "The Amazing Adventures of Spiderman" which was recently refurbished into HD 3D, and is a half virtual half track ride, in which you follow Spiderman around the streets of Manhattan. As you continue, you'll enter Toon Lagoon, the 2 main rides are Dudley Do Right's Ripsaw Falls and Popeye and Bluto's Bilgerat Barges, Log Flume and Rapids rides. Nothing Special. Through the Jurassic Park area, you'll come into The Wizarding World of Harry Potter. The Butterbeer always has long lines, but is worth it, it's also nice to look around the shops as well. The Dragon Challenge coaster (Formerley Dueling Dragons) Usually has a wait of <20 minutes, as most of the crowd goes to Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey.  Universal Orlando resort host's my favorite parks in Florida, and my favorite coaster in the world. If you have teenagers, this is a MUST SEE. Do not miss out!

We went during the later part of Spring Break so it was pretty crowded. We arrived the first day at 9:20 am (parked open at 9:00 am) and there was already a 1:10 min wait for the Despicable Me attraction. Needless to say, we didn't see that attraction. The kids did the Roller Coaster, Men In Black, The Simpsons, ET, Shrek and the Disaster attraction. Each one was a 20 - 30 mins wait. They liked them all. Saw the Blues Brothers show had lunch and that took up about 7 hrs from all of the walking and looking in a few stores. The Express pass is very expensive and we opted not to do it. We did do preferred parking for $20 as I recently had knee surgery. A 6 slice pizza was $30 so food prices are expensive inside the park. They do a meal deal for $22 a person that includes 4 different places to eat all day long. We only had one meal so didn't do it. The games are expensive as well averaging about $5 a person. Those booths were not too crowded and we opted for one game at $3 a piece. It is a long day even for teens and a lot of walking. There were a lot of foreigners visiting the parks I would say about 50 - 60% of the crowd was from overseas. They don't all follow American customs on courtesy so be prepared.

was chaperone of our hs senior's class trip. much to see besides rides, especially on the universal studio side, which i did first. crossed over to island of adventure in late afternoon - ride lines weren't bad by then. nice shops on both sides.

We must have spent over 10 hours in the park, riding every ride at least twice, and each of the roller coasters 6 times!! The Minion Mayhem ride is great too, but had the largest lineup in the park. Near the end of the day someone leaving the park gave us their express passes, and I can't explain how much they help. I would consider buying them next time we go. You get to skip all the lines!!

Went primarily for Harry Potter, which was enjoyable. 80% of attractions at Universal seem to be action rides like Roller Coasters. I liked the Lucy Exhibit and the Horror make up show at Hollywood side. Probably wouldn't go again.
Super fun time at IOA. Loved the rides! City Walk was so much fun at night. Spring break was a blast here. I am defenatly coming back next year.

I would suggest buying the meal plan. Its good value if you are going to spend the whole day there. We drank water so it was just the food. Pop is ok if you buy the cup they refill it for a lower cost. Theres 2 parks. The original was MGM studios years ago. It hasn't changed much since then. The other park has Harry Potter and Spider Man attractions in it. We didn't go to that one. So the original one, is the only rating we can give. My kids are teens so we had no problems with anything. And having the meal deal with teens is great.

My family which includes 2 teen boys had a marvelous time at this park. We especially liked despicable me ride, the Simpsons ride,, disaster, the mummy ride, Men in black and and Shrek in 4D. They place had some great shows too ie fear factor. The only ride which needs major updating is terminator 2d.

having been visiting the Orlando area for the past 12 years my favourite theme parks have to be universal.  I'm not going to criticise or compare Disney, this is after all a review on Universal and I think anyone who doesn't enjoy the parks needs something extra special to put a smile on their faces because the two parks have it all in my opinion.  I think the one thing you need to do to make it even better is make sure you have a fast pass for the rides/shows, this can literally save you hours standing in a queue.  I've been with my family on occasions, just with my wife at other times and with friends at others, each time I've enjoyed it all and will keep going back.

What a hackneyed word, but the only one which really describes this experience. I thought this was superior to Disney, but was influenced by the fantastic job they did with recreating a realistic Harry Potter experience. Bearing in mind that my wife and I are in our mid 60's, and was accompanied by my daughter & husband, and their two children, all of whom had an even better time than us!!! Initially I had some reservations when I discovered how expensive it was, but in retrospect, it was money well spent. We had a two day ticket, which I would suggest you need as a minimum, in order to enjoy the many facilities available. Average wait was circa 15 to 20 minutes per ride, with some of the more popular stretching to 30 mins. I would rate 'Harry Potter Land' as currently the major attraction available.

Great place to visit - there is a multitude of things to see for all ages. Blues Brothers act, Shreck 4d show excellent, and many others. I would recommend "Flanigan's" Irish pub for something to eat/drink.

We spent one day at each of the Universal Studios parks and I wish we could have went back to visit the Harry Potter section again and again! It was so life like, it was unreal! Every inch of the ground and landscape and architecture was straight our of the movie! The rides put you in the movie, especially the ride recommeded for older kids. We ate at a restaurant that served fish and chips and it was delicious. Great environment, friendly wait staff. I can't wait to go back!

My husband, my 11yr old son, and I visited Universal for 2 days last week. The park was clean and the lines weren't too long. We really enjoyed the new Despicable Me Minion Mayhem ride and the 3D spiderman ride. The Twister was a little disappointing, I thought there'd be more wind and less water (I got a bucket load dumped on the back of my head). My son loved The Simpsons ride. The Beetlejuice's Graveyard Revue was surprisingly great. The Superstar Parade was awesome with characters from Despicable Me, SpongeBob, Hop & Dora. Catch the Character Party Zone where the characters come off their floats and get pictures. VERY disappointed that the minions weren't in the parade or available for pictures in the park. You can only get a picture if you catch them immediately after the Despicable Me ride at the exit to the ride. It's a very short period of time to catch a picture then they leave.

I live in Fl and I always make a habit to visit this park and Islands at least once a year for a shot vacation. Every year I go, the parks get better and better. I would advise to come to the parks later in the day, everyone tries to get in the parks at the same time as soon as it opens. Most travelers leave in the early afternoon to go back to their hotels or to another theme park. The parks stay open until about 8PM I believe, so there's plenty of time to see and do every thing later in the day. I would also recommend to never buy a fast pass in the off season, it's just not worth it when most of the time you can just about walk right on most rides. The Transformers ride opens June 20th which will give the park a little more traffic, and trust me, it's not going to be as big as Harry Potter, but it will bring in the crowd. However, the Transformers gift shop an meet and greets with Megatron, Optimus Prime, and Bumble Bee are available so I would definitely check that out!

YES! We were so thankful that we went when we did, in early May. Our family went to both parks (Islands of Adventure & Universal Studios) TWICE on one day! We walked on every ride, never waiting longer than 10 minutes. As a family with a 6 year old, we did not care for the thrilling roller-coasters, but my husband got on a few of them by himself. He walked on to the Hulk ride with no wait. We had a great time but be prepared to spend some money. The food, the multiple stores, everything costs. As long as you are prepared for it, you wont get frustrated. I think the express tickets would be worth the money on a busy day, but I felt bad for those that bought it on May 9th. You just did not need it! I hate crowds, so thank goodness we went when we did.  The Harry Potter simulation ride was great, even though it broke down while we were on it. We were dangling in the air for 15 minutes! The staff were wonderful though, offered to let us go on again. In fact, all of the staff everywhere at the park were exceptional. At that same ride, an employee accidentally put his finger in our frozen Butterbeer. Before we could say anything, he had called the Three Broomsticks restaurant to have a free Butterbeer waiting for us when we exited the ride.  This park was great, and thrilling, and fun.

Universal is a great theme park especially for tweens, teens and adults. It is meant for a little older audience than DIsney but there is still something for the young ones so parents do not despair. Despicable Me is the newest ride and it truly is an awesome 3D ride. My favourite is the Simpsons another 3D ride and a must try for anyone who calls themselves a true Simpsons fan. Men in Black is cool too and blows away the 2 Toy Story rides at Disney. Before this park was a tad behind Islands of Adventure but now it has surpassed it in number of first rate attractions, especially since Transformers will be coming soon. Must sees are the 3 rides mentioned previously along with Shrek, the next tier holds Teminator 3D, ET, DIsaster and Twister. I am not a big coaster fan but Rip Ride Rocket and The Mummy generate lots of screams. The park itself is less crowded than Disney so is less irritating. The Universal Xpress pass is a rip-off compared to DIsney's free fast pass - you should boycott it, Honestly you do not need it if you plan your day well. The shows are average but the Rock and Roll show is good for adults, the horror make up show and Fear Factor are also fine. The animal actors is great for kids and animal lovers. Generally, they do not compare to DIsney or Seaworld shows so do not fret if you miss them. The food at the park is average at best, the best lunch is spaghetti and meatballs at Louie's italian - it is not that great either but you get tired of burgers and fries and it is a good change. Eat on Citywalk if you want dinner. The kidzone featuring a nice area for the kids to get wet and also sports a beginner roller coaster is a good diversion for the young ones. Overall, you should love this park if you like the best 3D and thrill rides. Highly recommended and for my money the best theme park in Orlando.

This one is just amazing..No words to describe.. The Hollywood shows were awesome.. 3-D and 4-D movies are just awesome. Terminator, Shrek shows are awesome..Dont forget the quick magic shows on the streets. They are quickie and worth the visit..  You would need 1 full day for this park. Do not ever do a shorter version as you will miss a lot if you try to cover this up less than a day..  Make sure to carry Hats, Sunscreen and sun glasses. These are MUST for Florida Summer!!!  Have fun..

Less lines, great entertainment for all. New rides and attractions constantly updated keep both Universal parks cutting-edge. Shows should not be missed, especially Beatlejuice. Dispicable Me ride was great. The Curious George water playing area amused my 11 & 13 yr old and younger kids for more than an hour. Some rides did break down this year as opposed to five years ago, at our previous visit. Citiwalk enhances the parks. No need for Disney for a great time.

Universal is more for kids 8-16 years of age. It is a down-sized Disney. Most of the rides were simulated and involved 3D Glasses. Each park had one coaster. Universal Studio was better than islands of Adventure. We purchased the food ticket and drink ticket. We had no trouble finding the restaurants and drinking refills at Universal but Islands was hard to find and scarce drinking refills. The Maps for each park are really crummy - they definetely need more details to help you find places or find yourself! Signage is not helpful. Going into Islands - the music is way too loud; hasn't the Park realized we are teaching our kids to turn down the volume to save their hearing. Most of the attractions were a lesser copy of a Disney Ride. Not enough attractions. Shops were a bit high priced. Food was good at the Universal Restaurants on the Meal ticket.

We had a blast here! We got the 3 day pass, so the cost wasn't too bad and it was definitely worth it! The park was clean and pretty easy to navigate. The Rock It rollercoaster was so amazing, but we did wait in line the longest for that one. Other than that, the lines weren't too long. I found out later that you could buy a fastpass outside of the park at places like Denny's for cheaper than inside the park. Also, the mealdeal that is available is a great option if you want to eat out at the CityWalk and see a movie. The Despicable Me ride was probably my overall favorite, but the Mummy Ride was in my top three.

I must point out our first minute there ruined our day. We arrived at the ticket entrance and in our line there was obviously a problem as the employee was having trouble with everybody's passes on the bar code scanner, after 15 minutes we presented our pass and there was a issue and we couldnt get our pass to work. Ok so try again,,,,,, we were asked by the employee if we were using the correct finger to scan on the machine, we said yes we used the pass yesterday, we were then told to use our thumb, we said we know which finger we registered our passes with. We were then told by the employee to try our other hand!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!. We said we know for definitely which finger we used,the employee then said maybe you have forgot, !!!!!!! Now this was embarrassing as the employee was talking to us like a child, there were loads of people listening to this and we were not happy. We told the employee that there must be a problem as the previous 6 guest have had the same problem , the employee was rude and her customer service skills were nil, zero , zilch. We reported this to the guest relations who listened to us and apologized. The embarrassment and humiliation had been caused. You are a captive audience and have no ther alternative but to purchase your 400 pound pass for 2 weeks if you want to attend the park. Watch this space see if our complaint goes on deaf ears as they assured us they will look into it.

Amazing rides, we went in May so the queues weren't too bad. We had a great time. It's loads better than Disney and so much cheaper 2! Only negatives are the fast pass is super expensive and unlimited food you can buy is a total rip off. You can only use it at 3 food places and they are super picky about what you can have and it isn't detailed clearly. Loads of people were getting their food, then getting to the till and have to pay as they picked the wrong thing

For my very first Universal trip, I really enjoyed the original park. We did not buy the express pass and we only waited for one ride. I enjoy the fact that Universal goes out of their way to make their guests comfortable, far exceeding what I've seen at Disney and Six Flags. Air conditioning, big fans, and quick lines are awesome!

Loved both parks! Harry's world ride was worth the wait!! lots of fantasic rides and great customer service. Only complaint I had was for the Despicable Me ride. We waited in line for over an hour and then when we finally got to ride the ride we could see that they were only filling it about half full. Don't know why. I think the person at the front of the ride was very slow and seemed to take forever to let people on. Everything else was awesome! i'm not a huge fan of big rollercoasters so I didn't ride the really big ones like the Hulk, but my favorites were Harry's Quiddich game, Spiderman, Mummy, Jurasic Park and the shows were awesome too! We ate at Finnegan's and the food and service there was outstanding. I personally think the Express Line people didn't get on the rides much faster than we did. If you can - go through the single rider lines - very fast way to get on. Of course you can be split up doing this, but for most of the rides it didn't matter to us.

First day here and it was a freaking blast! I got a chance to ride my first roller coaster(The Hulk) and after that I was hooked. BY far the highlight of the trip was the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. As an avid Potter fan, I felt like I had died and gone to heaven. One tip though, the crowds are pretty bad in certain areas, so if you can, go ahead and spring for the early park entrance tickets. Bit pricier, but well worth it.

Gutted! Out of all the parks we had done as a family we were looking forward to this park. We paid for the tickets beforehand luckily as queues were long. Entered the park early (0830). We were at the Island Adventures side. Baring in mind tickets are expensive we were shocked at the queues already in place, especially for Harry Potter 'rides' location. If you choose to fast pass this park it is called 'express pass'. A further $96 per ticket.(Disney Fast Pass included in price) Although we done most the rides the park is not as enjoyable as Disney attractions and we believe unless a mass Harry Potter fan it can be avoided.

Be sure not to miss The Mummy, Rip Ride Rockit and Men in Black! But I also love the ET ride! If you can only visit one Universal Studios park, make it Islands of Adventure (marvel, harry potter etc) but if you can visit here too! Xx
The rides were interactive and fun. I recommend getting the express pass to bypass the long lines. Wear comfortable shoes! We had a great time - even my teenager!

Lots of fun rides. We got to ride transformers before the grand opening. Amazing ride. Fun park for all ages. The new expansion of Harry Potter is going to make this park even better. Just the framework was started but it looks massive. A reason to come back next year.

My party and I went to Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure and bought a 3 day park-to-park pass. Although we missed the "US & Canadian Residents Buy 2 Days Get the 3rd Free" deal going on, the money was well worth it! There were so many memorable attractions and with the help of the Universal & Undercover Tourist apps, we were able to ride each attraction with minimal wait times. Even the brand new Transformers ride (which I recommend to hit RIGHT when the park opens) was only a 60 minute wait compared to the average 140+. Every ride there is enjoyable and fun, the parade was adorable and I even got a few autographs from Betty Boop, Bart Simpson, Captain America, and Woody the Woodpecker! Along with the rides there were very cool things to see such as Fear Factor Live and displays of the cars featured in the famous movie franchise "Fast and Furious". Even though we stayed for three days, there was something new and memorable each day. Can't wait to come back.

We visited Universal Studios/Islands of Adventure in June 2013 with our last visit here coming in 2008. While a lot of rides have been added, we were frankly a little disappointed in the presentation. Simply put - it lacks the style and imagination of Disney. Nothing wrong with that, but the whole experience just fails to rise to the same level as a Disney park.  Little things are irritating, such as Universal's seeming inability have all of its people-mover sidewalks working at the same time. On each of the days we visited, one of these sections were always turned off or closed for maintenance. May not sound like a big deal, but after 12 hours of slogging around a theme park, you want the people movers to be working - especially when they are an integral part ot Universal's parking scheme.  The new Despicable Me ride was a big disappointment - too much of the jolting 3-D reality ride stuff that could have been so much better with less jarring and more heart. In Islands of Adventure, we zipped into the Circus McGircus restaurant during a rain shower and found the tables and floor were filthy. Birds were flying throughout including in the food service/prep area - that can't be safe! On one day we arrived to park and waited for close to 15 minutes to get through the gates, only to find one attendant trying to work both lanes. (As a reference, on this same week we visited Magic Kingdom and zipped through the gates in less than 30 seconds.)  All of this said, Spiderman is still one of the most amazing rides in the amusement park world. Harry Potter? OK, but not being a family of HP fans it was just another ride for us. The way that they've made the area around the HP ride look is very cool. Note: if you really love water rides, you'll be thrilled in Islands of Adventure and you WILL get very wet between the Bilgewater Barges, Ripsaw Falls and Jurassic Park. If you don't like getting soaked - well, you've been warned!  Note on food: we splurged and bought the $24 unlimited dining pass for one day and found it was probably worth the price, but only because we used the pass for early lunch, early dinner and an 8 pm meal and did not do our usual stop at a restaurant after leaving the park. The pass does not include drinks. Restaurants honoring the pass are limited - Monsters Cafe was by far the best. The smoked chicken was actually done very well, quite a surprise for a theme park. Mel's Diner was second but only if you like burgers etc.  The evening show at park close? One word: dud.  Bottom line: Universal isn't Disney but it doesn't pretend to be. It's a fun experience and OK for the price, it just won't leave you with the same magical feeling you'll get elsewhere.
Loved this place. Attractions were close together and it was colourful,modern and clean.  The Harry Potter ride was worth the 90 minute wait! Get there early!!

the thing about universal studios that is better than disney is the lines are not that long and the attractions are much closer together than at disney. you could see everything in one day if weather permits, where as disney is so spread out you could spend days and never see everything. my teen actually prefers universal over disney

First day with the Express passes, the second day we did the VIP tour.  Day 1: Express Passes A fun day, but VERY rushed. Felt like we ran from ride to ride to get everything done. Some queues were still long, albeit shorter than regular. Namely, Ripsaw Falls (1hr + due to breakdowns and people going through) and Despicable Me (40 mins). Seemed as though our average wait for about 20 minutes with express pass, but some of the queues longer as noted. Would recommend the poncho for the wet rides (J-park, Ripsaw, and Popeye) in which you get wetter in each (Popeye like jumping in a pool with your clothes on!) Was disappointing that Ripsaw falls was experiencing difficulties, we had 3 "log-jams" on the ride, and several when we were in line, contributing to a disjointed ride experience and a long queue.  Day 2: VIP Passes. Wow, expensive. Quite unimpressed as its much more expensive than the L.A Universal VIP tour with less perks! (I.e. Los Angeles has a (fantastic) buffet lunch, here we had to pay for our lunch, L.A has the backlot tour with behind the scenes access, we got to walk along Wysteria lane!)  Despite this, it was still a worthwhile purchase for us. We had a lovely tour guide (Cyndi) who was both knowledgeable and friendly. She talked us through everything, chauffeured us around the park, and gave us a jump straight to the front of the line for most rides! (Some we didn't do)  Particularly on this 4th of July we thought it would be even more worthwhile to avoid queues, learn more about the park, meet nice people (in your group). We were paired with another couple who were great to spend the day with! Groups up to 12 from memory.  Remember, you have to buy the VIP Tour ON TOP of the regular park entry fee.

Some of this review may repeat what I have already posted in a previous review on Islands of Adventure. But attraction wise it is obviously related to USF. My daughter and I had a 1 day visit to USF and IOA. We visited 2 years ago and had 1 other visit over 10 years prior to that. With 1 day to visit, we decided once again to purchase the Park to Park VIP Express Plus Passes. We did this 2 years ago and loved it. If it were off season I probably might not bother with the passes. We purchased our VIP PTP Passes online and picked them up from the will call kiosks at the entrance to the park. It worked great. No lines at the Kiosks and plenty of long lines at the ticket counters. We also decided to try Valet Parking on this visit. It cost $30 dollars and I thought it was well worth it. The Valet Parking is located across the road from the main parking structures. After dropping off your car, you go up a short section of stairs to your own security screening. Short, sweet and fast. You are then basically at City Walk. We decided to take a midday break away from the park for lunch and a rest. With your valet receipt you may return to park again on the same day. No other charge. We were 1st in line at USF. We qued up at the turnstiles to the far right as you are facing them. I heard a female employee mention that those turnstiles would indeed be used, but most arriving visitors were suspicious of only a handful of people waiting to the right and qued up on the left side turnstiles. We had not been to Despicable Me Minion Mayhem, so we went there 1st off and were in and out in no time. It was Tuesday and Transformers: The Ride 3-D was set to officially open up on Thursday. They had soft openings for Transformers for days ahead of this and were unsure if it would be open. It was indeed open and were able to ride it 3 times without a wait. It was fantastic! From there we made a counter clockwise trip around the park. Finishing at Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit. My 1st time on that coaster and it was a blast. That was probably the longest wait time in any line all day. (using the VIP Express Plus Pass) And that was probably a 10 minute wait. We left the park at noon to go off site for lunch and a rest back at our hotel. We were back in the parks by 3 pm and after a visit to IOA we returned to re-visit a few things at USF. Including the Clogger Burger at Krusty Burger. Very yummy! Then finished the evening at IOA and the WWOHP. I love both USF and IOA. I will return and have just as fun on the next visit. It makes you young all over again.

Our family of 4 visited Universal in August 2012 as a side trip for few days from our Gulf coast vacation. The kids were 15 and 11 so they were ready for the rides! This place is a full on assault on your senses and your bank account. We chose to stay off-site in Orlando and drive into the park for three days. I was trying to save some money over staying in the park hotels, but after the first day at the park, I realized that the long lines are meant to demoralize cheap/poor people. The line skipping feature called Universal Express lets people skip to the front of the line. To buy this upgrade in the park is ridiculously expensive BUT if you stay in their hotels you get this feature for free. The Express upgrade would have cost $150 per day for my family on top of the park ticket prices. If you don't want to feel abused by line skippers, stay at their onsite hotels. Both parks were exciting, but Islands of Adventure (IA) had newer, more exciting rides than Universal Studios (US).  Here are our hits and misses for IA: Hits: Spiderman, Hulk, all Harry Potter village rides, Ripsaw Falls, Popeye River Raft, Jurassic Park River; Misses: None!  Here are our hits and misses for US: Hits: Despicable Me, Hollywood rocket, Simpsons, Shrek, Revenge of Mummy; Misses: Men in Black=Waste of time!, ET & Twister=Time to retire these!  Eating: We had a big breaksfast before going to the park and brought lots of water and some fruits and buns we "borrowed" from the hotel. Food at the parks is expensive and fatty and the cleanliness in the eating areas is terrible. Would it kill them to change that grey stinky rag once a day? Food service staff are apathetic! Apparently having a job is a waste of time!  We were gouged $40 for hotdog meals! The only place where there was some sanity and value was the Confisco Grille just inside Islands of Adventure gates.  We had a great time but I had to put aside my sensibilites and accept that I will stand in line for an hour, I will pay $10 for a hotdog and flat pop and staff will glare at me even though I'm blowing $400 per day to be there. These theme parks are a right of passge for parents I suppose, if you go, pack your patience and a sack of money ... good luck!
Likes the Mummy ride and the Simpsons ride. Fear Factor Live was very neat to see but I wasn't blown away by the park. Some lines were over an hour late, we went on a somewhat rainy day.

Recently went to Orlando Studios, Adventure Land, Orlando, Florida & had a very good time. Liked the rides, shops, magic show, etc there. Didn't even have enough time to take it all in on one day so plan to return there in the future! Offered a variety of different rides for all family members & loved the Harry Potter castle & ride!

Transformer Ride is fabulous rode twice in morning early after that forget it ....we bought express unlimited pass its the only way to get it done.....enjoyed this park twister is great and T3...and the mummy ride rough but exciting. clean park buy the coke cup well worth it. Food ticket isn't worth the money for all day.....choose to eat when and where you want no food ticket is better.

If you are visiting Orlando, FL this is one of the places you really should go! I am a HUGE Harry Potter fan so I went back after the opening of HP Land! It was right out of the book! The ride is phenomenal, and the line just to get on the ride is going through the castle so it is almost part of the adventure! I wouldn't recommend this park on a weekend, you will spend most of your day waiting in lines. We went on a Friday in December and the longest line we waited in was 15 minutes for the Despicable Me ride. This park is incredible, I would expect to spend the entire day there.

Park and rides were very clean and well maintained. The workers were very helpful and courteous. The express pass was well,worth it as it easily cut the wait in half for most rides. The food was,standard for amusement parks but was good and not too overpriced.

Make sure you buy the Express Pass or book a hotel room on Universal property for unlimited pass uses or you'll waste your days waiting in line. It pays for itself if time matters to you. Arrive BEFORE the park opens for fastest ride access. Rides are faster, thrilling, more outrageous, and slightly more irreverent than at Disney parks. Simulators like Transformers, The Simpsons, Despicable Me, and Shrek 4-D will excite and nauseate large crowds at once. Thrill seekers with flexible necks and backs will love Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit Rollercoaster and The Mummy coaster. The park is best enjoyed by people who don't mind lots of walking and standing, large crowds, Florida heat and humidty, and loud music. Tweens and teens abound. Bring a small backpack filled with water and Gatorade.

Family of five, one day at both parks - $1,100. Yes, you read that right. I was $140-ish plus $79 for express passes for each person. The daily cost does go down when you go more days - just like it does at the Disney parks, but man oh man, was this expensive!  Universal is practically all simulation rides. That gets old pretty fast. A lot of people also throw up (we saw two people throw up!). I even felt a bit nauseous! There were some great roller-coasters and lots of really cool 'lands' (like walking through the Simpsons land and the Harry Potter world were really magical experiences). We especially loved the Simpsons land. We spent a lot of time there as our whole family are big Simpsons fans. I'd say that alone was worth the price of admission (okay, not $200+ each, but it was still pretty cool!).  The express passes are well worth it, especially if you're short for time. But like I've already said, you have to pay for it. Considering we did about 15 rides, that turned out to be about $5 a ride to use express and then still $149 for both parks. We walked on to most rides. Some rides that had short lines, we didn't even need to use express. Some rides they didn't even check! That was weird considering the cost!  The Harry Potter ride was amazing. But...it also stopped and broke down on us for a few minutes. That kind of spoiled it a bit (esp. considering that wasn't an express pass ride and we waited for 45 minutes to get on).  I thought staff there were good and bad. I think it depended on which ride, restaurant or services you needed. Very inconsistent.  Going in the summer is a bad idea for several reasons: it's really hot, it's really crowded and it's thunderstormy. The thunderstorms wrecked a couple of our waits in line for rollercoasters. We had to abandon one line because of one. The thunderstorms do bring relief from the heat, though. When we were there in the morning it was already super hot and uncomfortable. Thankfully we spent a lot of time in the Quik-E-Mart and at Krusty Burgers and got to relax in air conditioning!

Universal studios is mainly show type rides but they are out of this world. T2 is an old favourite, its fun to see the actors mimmick arnie, furlong and Linda Hamilton. 3d effects r very good. There r a lot f characters to meet and take photos with. Scooby doo, despicable me characters, spongebob, Dora, Simpsons. Transformers is absolutely amazing, kids rode this 4 times. You can also take pics with bumble bee, optimus and Megatron. Men in black is alot of fun and rip ride rock it is an intense rollercoaster. There is also a superstar parade at 5pm. With so many awesome attractions, you need at least 2 days here. We had a 14 day multipark ticket so ended up coming here 6 times. Our favourite park of the holiday. BTW, the 100yr celebration show with fireworks is also amazing. Check it out.

Overall we had a good time, but this was not close to the Disney experience. I like the the layout of having the two parks connected by city walk but once inside the park the flow of traffic slows drastically. Glad we went off season, I can't imagine how hard it is to get around when it is packed. Part of the park was closed for upgrading which is understandable, but several rides broke down through out the day. Very frustrating when waiting in line for a while. The staff was ok, never overly friendly or welcoming. The characters were fun and had a good time with the kids. The rides that were working were very well done. Also, city walk smells a little like bourbon street, I think from all the beer being served.

Had a brilliant day there Transformer ride is the best simulator ride you will go on ,queueing times were not bad at all just a shame the jaws ride isn't there any-more and spider-man ride wasn't working .Extremely hot but didn't put as off and had the odd welcomed shower would go back again .Although they need to have free wi-fi like Disney resorts so you can download app for ride queueing times and restaurant reservations.
My eight year old, husband and I had great time. Harry Potter Island of adventure was fantastic. Transformers ride highly recommended

The Despicable me and Transformer rides are incredible. The rest of the rides are OK. Neat layout to the park and easy to get around. We have a special needs child and the staff was very inconsistent in how they managed the special needs pass. They are not clear on the 30 minute rule and were told conflicting things from the staff at each ride.

We decided, instead of visiting D.W., to check out Universal Studios. We knew, ahead of time, about the height requirements of the rides and U.S. was better suited to us rather than Islands of Adventure. Pros: The employees, such as Don (security) and Eric (transformer's ride) were courteous and helpful. The Mummy ride was detailed and exciting. I was able wait less as a "single rider".  Cons: We fully realized how expansive the walk from the bus depot to the entrance of Universal. I wish there was a way to "by-pass" City Walk...especially in the hot sun of Florida. It appears to be such a scam to have to purchase another ticket to "fast pass" through the ride lines...when this feature is included in a disney ticket and sea world ticket . We knew that ride lines would be long in July. However, Universal should have had features to entertain you and keep you cool as you wait. There is no shade here...neither man-made created nor foliage. There were too many motion/virtual simulator rides given the exorbitant amount of money paid.

Oh wow! The best in Orlando......we did them all, Disney, Universal, Sea World and Busch Gardens and Universal Islands of Adventure were by far the best.  Harry Potter is the big draw and it was well worth it. The place is fantastic from Hogwarts Castle to Hogsmead, the rides, the shops and scenery and the finishing touches like the Butterbeer on sale in the street.  We all had a fantastic day and I would go again and again if I could.

It has been awhile since I have been to Universal. A lot of the older rides are still there, Earthquake has been renamed to Disaster. Twister is still there, sadly the Back to the Future ride is gone and replaced with The Simpsons. Even Jaws is gone, with replacement of the Harry Potter expansion. As sad as it is, these changed have to be made to keep up to date with current things. The new Simpsons area, with Moe's tavern, Krusty Burger, Kwik e Mart etc is really sweet. They are still working on it, you can see the Duff Brewery and another ride in the works behind the wall. I am hoping they build a replica of the Simpson Home on Evergreen Terrace, where you can take a picture on the infamous brown couch in their living room and get a tour of all the rooms we have come to know over the last 25+ years. The Transformers ride, sits almost in the center of the park, very large, grey building with a giant Prime on top. Really looks pretty cool, tho the 2 hour wait time detoured me from riding it. Universal has a Speed Pass option that you pay for on top of your ticket price, was like 100$PP more and I was surprised to see how many people forked over the money for it. We got the hopper option and after doing almost everything we wanted in Universal, we headed to Adventure Island. It is true to say I think Universal have lost the plot! I agree with other contributors - 2+ hours queuing for a 4 minute ride! The lines for getting into attractions are just way to long to make the experience enjoyable; especially with a six year old!! To buy a fast pass is just unbelievably expensive and cannot be afforded by the average family! $100 + each unbelievable and outrageous! As a Family we managed 2 main attractions yesterday because of the times spent in lines! Personally I will not be going back; much preferring the Disney Parks and SeaWorld!

after visiting all the major parks with just me and the wife we decided to review them all. Universal's content put it joint top in what it had to offer.  IMO it has the 2 best rides in Orlando, Being the Rock roller coaster and The Mummy ride. Being chosen due to its amount of "crap your pants excitement" without the wanting to throw up afterwards effect.  The Beetlejuice show is awesome so don't miss it.  The rest of the shows and rides are a nice mix and made the whole day and enjoyable mix.  Now to the bad points.  The cost- Breaking down what we paid for the tickets and Fast Passes (and unfortunately you need these which i hated. que times for the top rides were between 60-120 mins, with a fast past this was between 10-15mins) came to $115 a day per person compared to Disney $50 a day.  Without the fast past we would have had no chance of seeing all the rides but $59 per person is a bit extortionate.  The character organistation. Disney park has organized lines, a helper for the characters and a professional photographer who is happy to take a picture with your own camera. Universal had non of these.  On the food a drink front they do offer $9 special drinks container where you can refill for $1 all day long (and just by chance if you are there for more than one day take it back with you and keep saving on your second day). Food was overpriced like everywhere $10 for a krusty burger!!!!!!! we stuck with sandwiches and saved $30 a day roughly.  so to sumarise if your coming to Orlando to do the fast rides and your willing to fork out $115 a person do it. I think if your here with a family stick with Disney.

The only way to get on some of the more publicised attractions is to buy an Express pass, over and above the entrance fee; this costs $69.99 per person + tax and there is no discount for seniors or children. During July, when the American schools are also on holiday, it's probably the only way to guarantee that you actually get on a ride. Without the Express pass, you have to queue and the advertised wait times are less than the actual wait times. Our visits to these parks were also spoiled by large tour groups, mainly consisting of teenage girls, chanting and marching 10-15 abreast, expecting everyone in their path, young or old, able bodied or disabled to move for them. They also don't want to queue and try to push their way in front of everyone else. Whilst Disney also suffers from these groups, it's fair to say that their parks are better organised and their queuing system is fairer.

First time visiting this park and we really enjoyed it! 2 adults and 2 8-year-olds. Everyone loved it. I highly suggest buying the park to park 2 day pass as both parks offer equally great rides and its almost impossible to get it done in one day without an express pass. The express passes were $90 each during our visit so we opted to NOT get them. No big deal as most of the waits are less then 40 minutes and well worth it. I'd skip Twister because it wasn't a ride and was short and kind of pointless. Rides not to miss: Harry Potter and the forbidden journey, transformers, revenge of the mummy, and Spider-Man! We stayed near the park so we found it best to get there early, leave by 1 for a few hours and then return around 5. The middle of the day is the hottest and busiest, best to avoid if you can. When we got back at 5, tons of people were leaving and ride line times were down. Despicable Me and Transformers lines are always long so I suggest getting to the park before it opens and heading straight to one of those rides. The line is a lot shorter first thing in the morning or last thing at the end of the day. If you do have to wait in line, no problem, there are tv's and plenty of visuals for adults and kids alike! Our 8 year olds didn't complain once in line because there were tv's and such to keep them occupied! Also, not too bad on a hot day since most of the lines waiting is inside!  Only downside: tickets were $150 each! A little too pricey to think about returning again!

Been visiting the park for years and it gets better every time we return - they are always changing, improving and adding to their attractions and you are never stuck for things to do. Highly recommend paying out the extra for the express tickets to jump the queue, it allows you to do more in a single visit as you aren't standing around in a queue for hours on end.

I have been visiting Orlando since I was 4 now I'm 22 and I get mega excited especially for Universal Studios! The plastic are fantastic, nothing is a problem always outgoing and happy to help! Queue time differ on the time of year, the past 2 years I have been in April and May and found it to be full of I'm guessing schools? Loads of groups of kids walking around which tends to annoy people! I think the company souls organise specific days and allow a certain number in the parks as it can be annoying hearing hundreds off hyper kids when your trying to queue! All the attractions are brilliant, Deffo recommend despicable me, the mummy and rip ride rockitt.. Fab experiences and deffffs the Beetlejuice show it's amazing! I am hoping to return this September for Halloween horror nights! I've never experience it but hope people can give me some advice :)

Follow the advice of so many other reviewers and get there early! My friend and I arrived at opening and were able to do 75% of the rides by about 2pm including a stop for lunch. The line for the Transformers ride was too long (well over an hour) so we skipped it, and I was able to get on the Rip Ride Rockit coaster by myself in the 5-minute single riders line. The crowds were definitely getting thick in the afternoon, so getting there early pays off. We had a 2-day pass to both parks, so we finished off the day by going back to Islands of Adventure for a second time (which we loved; see separate review). Everything on the Universal Studios side was clean and really well-done - definitely visit the Springfield area if you're a Simpsons fan!

For those of you who have been to Disney, you might be disappointed to when you check out Universal Studios. But I think you have to put this in perspective. Disney is actually a collection of many different parks, and is huge because of it. Universal Studios is much smaller, but will certainly keep you entertained for two days. In fact, the standard ticket is for two days. Typically people spend one day in Island of Adventure and the other in Universal Studios Florida. You do one one day, and one the other. There's also Wet 'n' Wild, but that's a water park. It's not included in this review.  When you first come in, you go through Universal CityWalk, which has no entry fee, and is a retail area. Of course, you still have to park your car, if you took one, but if you come in after 5 pm (check for exact time), they only charge $5 for parking. But why would you go? Well, they have some nice theme restaurants like the Hard Rock Cafe, and Jimmy Buffet's Margaritaville. We liked the latter. We went for lunch at noon, which was ideal, because pretty much everyone else was in the theme parks. In the evening, there are long waiting lists for tables at probably every restaurant there. But they take reservations  The two parks have a different theme, with the Studio set up like, well, a backlot studio for places like New York or San Francisco. They say that they actually film things there, too. The Island of Adventure is most famous for the Harry Potter ride, which really is good. It, like most of the newer rides, has a combination tracked car (or broom) that you share, combined with full screen 3-D, which really does get all your senses going, sight, sound, motion, touch and even in some cases smell.  If you want to eat in a park, you want to make reservations for the Mythos Restaurant. The food is very good, and the interior is stunning, making you feel like you are in a place from, well, a Greek myth. It's rated the best restaurant in a theme park in the world, and I don't doubt it, partially because, well, most restaurants inside a theme park know that you're a captive audience. Mythos could make it in the real world, I think. We really liked it.  People can go to Universal and have completely different experiences. That's because they have the 4-D rides (like Potter), which are loads of fun and don't put too much stress on people who are motion challenged. But they also have traditional park rides, like roller coasters and flume rides. With small kids, you'll go one place, with teenagers, well, they're probably off on their own anyway.  So, here's some advice:  - Get the two day ticket without the ability to switch parks. You'll save money, and you can easily spend a whole day in one park, and a whole day in the other. Besides, switching between parks means more time walking and less time on rides.  - Buy your tickets from a ticket agent in your hotel, or just anywhere else that has an authorized dealer, for that matter. They'll generally have a discount, and you won't waste your time waiting in line to buy tickets at the venue.  - Make reservations for dining ahead of time. Spending your time waiting for an opening in a lobby while in a theme park is a complete waste of time. But if all you want is snack, or you bring your own in your backpack, no worries.  - Get an app on your phone for the park. Seriously! Shop around, but you should be able to find one that has maps, descriptions of rides and restaurants, a GPS feature that shows you where you are the map, location aware searches for restaurants, bathrooms, whatever and more. They even list wait times for the rides, based on cooperative crowd sourcing.  - Consider going in the "singles" line. Most, but not all rides at Universal have three, yes, three lines. The first is the usual line, which is guaranteed to have the longest wait. But you'll also be sure to be seated together on rides. The next line is one where you pay extra (or as part of a deal) to get into a line which is usually shorter than the first, because people either don't want to pay extra, or they didn't know they could. But there is very often a third line. It's always the fastest and you don't need to pay anything extra or be a VIP. It's the singles line. Basically, you agree to be put on the ride to fill in spaces that would otherwise be empty, because couples and family members like to right next to each other on the ride. This is a no brainer if you are alone, but it works even if you are not. You won't sit with your friend or family, but you'll get on and off the ride at roughly the same time, and even if you have to wait a little for the last person, it's much, much shorter a wait than the other lines.  So that's about it. Of course, do your usual reading about the place before you go, and deciding which things you most want to see, and making sure that you don't get soaking wet on a river ride before dining at Mythos, but the place is really fun.

For over $300 for two with Express passes it's not cheap, but so much to see and do. Loved the Transformers ride and the Despicable Me ride was fun. Top tip for the summer; get an Express pass and avoid 90 minute + waites. You really will need all day for this park AND and unlimited budget!

Me and my fiancé visited universal last week and had a great time. We visited both islands of adventure and universal studios in one day but we prefer universal studios. Prior to visiting we decided to get express passes, these are expensive and annoying to buy as it is free at disney. But as we are from the UK and we needed express passes to get on everything. It was well worth the expense as we got on all the rides and some twice. The new transformers ride is great, it's one of my favourites from all of the orlando parks. The mummy was also great and quite scary. Shrek, the Simpsons, rip rocket and MIB were also top rides there. Even the older rides such as disaster, ET and twister were good fun and rides I member when I visited 20 years ago when I was five. I found the staff to be friendly and the park was clean and ran well. I would say this park has the best ride selection out of all parks in orlando

I was lucky enough to have the opportunity to take a VIP tour of Universal. I felt like a VIP indeed. Our guide took our small group of 6 through the park and escorted us to each ride we wanted to enjoy, including the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. We never had to wait in lines, so that alone was worth it! We were able to enjoy many for attractions on the VIP tour, than if we were on our own. Our guide also took us backstage to avoid crowds and even knew great lounge areas with AC so we could cool off and use a clean bathroom.  The VIP package included food. The food options inlcuded with this are not the best, other parks (like Disney) offer better food choices. But you have to remember, you are at an amusement park, not a tour or the world at Epcot.  If it is in your budget to splurge for a VIP tour, I highly recommend it. It makes a day at the parks much more relaxing and enjoyable!

I go to Universal probably 5 times a year because I have an annual pass. We just went for the first time without an express pass and the lines were too long. I love Universal but the lines were too long. So here are some steps to having a great time at Universal.  1. Dont stay 1 day  If you are going to Universal Studios do NOT only stay one day. There are 2 parks and so much to do.  2. Stay in one of the on-site hotels  If you stay in one of the on-site hotels, you get the advantage of getting a unlimited express pass. What that means is that you can go on a ride more than once with this express pass. The one you buy in the park can only get you on that ride once.  3. Buy a souveneir cup  When you buy a souvenir cup you get 79 cent refills. Less money = Why not?
The studios are fantastic glad we stayed so close so that we could come and go as much as we wanted. The Express passes are essential as there are long queues for the most popular rides.

The park was OK. Nothing great. Most the rides are quite tired, old or short. Not much for thrill seekers. The main, and newest ride, the new rollercoaster with the vertical lift was brilliant, probably my favourite coaster of the holiday; but other than that, it didn't have much to offer in terms of rides. The new transformers ride was just OK. Very much identical to the spiderman ride across the road. We had completed the park by 10.30am, such was the type of rides that were there.  The fireworks/laser show on the lake however was fantastic. Much better than the Disney show, and is a must see.

Ah, I do love Universal studios and it had been a long time since we last went. A lot has changed since our last visit six years ago, but nonetheless it's still a brilliant park. The variety of rides is great, and everyone has something that they'll like, and if they don't then they're not looking hard enough, honest.  It's easy to get around, and everything is has a natural flow about it making for easy navigation around the various parts. Rides can also be spotted from a distance considering their distinct architecture on the outside, each contributing to the feel of the park. Which is great.  The only gropes I'll have about this park is the amount of time it takes to go through security at times, the lack of support for certain cards in their cash machines and the locker situation. I'll start with the locker situation, as it's the more alarming.  1:: When I went six years ago, they didn't mind you taking your bags on with you, or leaving them at the platform so that you can collect them on the way out. This has since stopped, and forces you to use one of their so called "Free" lockers, which aren't. They're free for the first hour, but past that they make you pay X amount for every X minutes over you've had it, but a lot of people hold the line up when it comes to that because they've trapped their money inside these lockers, unable to pay. They then need to grab a security guy, to then grab an attendant, and so on. So, if you're going I wouldn't recommend taking a bag with you, of any size, because they'll force you to use their lockers.  2:: We were in utter disbelief as our card, a money passport (since we were merely tourists), wasn't accepted by any of the cash machines within the park. It did work over some shops within the park, but not all. When we went to the 'Guest Relations', they merely told us 'tough luck' and made us go on our way. This was appalling in my eyes. They're happy to screw money out of you, for lockers (for the smallest of bags, no exaggeration), but when you require help around these, they really couldn't care less.  3:: Whilst this isn't mentioned on my initial list, I'll warn you now. Do not go if you believe it will thunder. As soon as we got to the park, and went on one ride a single bolt of lightening was seen and every ride in both parks were shutdown and subsequently closed. Even the rides which were inside were closed, leaving many in lines, hoping they'll open again. After this it started to rain for at least an hour and a half, everything seemed as if it was about to open again, when another bolt was noticed. Everything closed again. After this we left, as we had no interest in waiting six hours for the rides to open again.

Universal Studios was an awesome experience. While some rides are more modern than others the overall experience was great despite the heat and crowds. I noticed that things were less crowded in the late afternoon. The fast pass option really helped the day go smoother. I highly recommend the extra expense.

May not be quite as good as IOA in terms of rides etc, but the rides they do have are all iconic. Simpsons, Mummy, Men In Black and Terminator 3D to name a few and soon to have the second phase of Harry Potter to compete with its sister park.  Not been on Transformers yet, but I've heard it's excellent, and the day itself is just a great day of fun. It was a shame that they got rid of Jaws, as this was for me the best ride at the park (nostalgic reasons), but they have to move on somehow.  Overall the day in Universal is great for everyone, and certainly worth your time

I thought of this part mostly boring, but what can I say, I have been to universal studios in Los Angeles . What I would recommend to go there if you arrive early is go to the transformer, but if you want fun I would recommend Rock It; it's very creative. Island of Adventure is really fun, and has a lot of fun rides like Harry Potter, Hulk, Spider Man, and etc.. If you arrive to Island early I would recommend you to go to the Harry Potter ride first because it takes about a hour to wait if you go about at 1:00 PM.

This may not be a big deal for most families, but for us, who were traveling with our 3 year old daughter, it was the worst thing that could happen. Being so young, she does not care about the rides as much as older kids. The sole reason we went to Universal Studios was because of the parade which my daughter saw the commercial on NickJr. over and over again this summer. We purchased the Characters Breakfast to ensure she was going to meet some of the characters and the special area for the parade was perfect. We arrived in front of Macy's at 6:45pm as instructed to "check in". By 7:20pm, we found out that the parade was canceled, not by a park employee. No official apology, reason, nothing! What I heard was because some of the park lost power. NOT MY PROBLEM! It's just extremely upsetting that even the stores that had no power still found a way to sell and make money, yet a float, which I am sure has nothing l do with electricity, doesn't work?!?! Our daughter cried a lot and she saw the commercial again on NickJr. and was sad all over again! We spent a lot of money between our stay at the Royal Pacific Resort, the park tickets and souvenirs; too much to see our daughter this sad. We had a choice between many parks, and we chose Universal because of the parade and the characters advised. Everyone will always love Mickey, but the Minions will not be around forever. And not to get an explanation, an apology or anything is just terrible.

Not as fun as Universal Islands of Adventure for a family with high school kids but had some good points. Lombard's Seafood restaurant was really good. I don't care for the Simpsons so there was ALOT too much of that for me. Also the only employees on the entire Universal vacation we encountered who were bad were at Ben & Jerrys in the Park. 3-4 people working and only one of them trying. The rest trying to close the place at 5:40 and didn't care about the line backing up out the door  Everything else was really good but not as good as Islands of Adventure.

This is our second visit to universal and what they don't say is if u want to avoid the queue's u have to purchase a fast pass ticket which if we did this would have cost us another £ 300 which we don't have coz we have spent the money on ticket already to get into the park , comon universal stop ripping off ur customers !!!

I must warn anyone about the prices when you get home and look back, universal isnt worth going to its $16 to park its $297 for two people to go into bothe parks for 1 day and fast passes cost $206 for two people for 1 day. also they lied to us at the booth there are 3 rides the fast passes dont cover the most important one being Harry Potter we bought the entrance tickets from an agent at a discount but you cant buy fast passes only at the ticket booths

I should have done this review a while ago. rs This is by far my favorite place in Orlando and I try to go at least once a year, since I live in LA and I am a annual pass holder of the Hollywood park. Well, both parks have amazing rides, the staff is great and the food is also good. Island of Adventure are walking distance of the main one (Universal Studios) and since they opened the Harry Potter World, that's my favorite place inside the park.
