My other favorites rides are the Spider Man, and the Jurassic Park. (I am not a fan of hollercoaster). Tip: when buying your ticket go for the 2 parks 2 days and buy the ticket that allow you to go to both parks same day as well because If you are lucky and the park is not busy you can go on your favorite rides more than once. :) Favorite time of the year is late April / May which is less crowded.

This theme park is perfect for teens, pre-teens and their parents, The roller coasters were phenomenal and the restaurant selections were amazing. Much like Disney World, there are different "themes" within the park that cater to all ages.  The only complaint is the cost for a fast-pass or express pass. While expensive for these "add-ons" I would highly suggest getting them. With them, my wife, two kids and myself were able to go to a ride and be done within 15 minutes while those individuals without passes were often waiting up to 1 1/2 hrs. The other comment is that you should try to arrive at the park as close to opening as possible because it get's quite busy by lunchtime.
The greatest ingredient is the AE lounge which gives free water, granola bars n chip, it has AC, good place to rest

I visited universal this week for the first time in 11 years. I was disappointed to see the old favourites like Jaws & Hanna Barbera had been removed. A lot of the new features are simulator type rides which are great & very impressive but it's not quite the same as an old fashioned ride with the wind in your hair!  The Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit ride looks amazing. Unfortunately I only got to look at it as it was not working all day. We didn't even see a test run go. I was very disappointed in this as it was the only proper ride at the park & the main reason we decided to go.  The rest of the park was fun though & lots of interactive sections. Disaster movie was a great show & great audience participation. Worth a return visit for the big ride.
Went as an add-on to Islands of Adventure. New Transformers ride was awesome. The Mummy never disappoints. Food was good. Overall a worth getting the park-to-park pass.

The park goes out of its way to make all the attractions accessible to those who are limited. You can rent an electric mobility chair for $50 and a deposit. You can reserve it for the day you want but must pick it up by 11 am. It is on a first come first serve basis without the reservation. They have 2 styles one with and one without a canopy. I preferred the one without the canopy (even though there is sporadic showers) as it enabled me to put a backpack on the back of the chair. If you are in one of these chairs you can easily get to the attraction by an alternate entrance. First go to the regular entrance and they will direct you to the alternate entrance. There are many people who rent these for the ease of getting around so that if you are limited you need to stop by guest services to get a pass. You then do not have to wait on long lines. If an attraction is in demand they will give you a time to return. There is also a section for handicapped parking. You can take a wheelchair from the parking lot, rent a regular wheelchair after entering the area but before entering the park and then upgrade it for an electric mobility chair in the park itself. The electric cars are not available outside the park itself. Be prepared for showers. We used ponchos and had an extra one to cover the car and our things when parked outside the attraction protecting it during showers (which don't last that long). We also brought small umbrellas as well.

What a fun place to take the family, we did both parks over two separate days and had plenty of time to enjoy the rides and take in the atmosphere, one important tip if you choose to do the park with the Incredible Hulk ride, bring your swimmers as there are 3 rides which we went on and got absolutely drenched from head to toe, thank goodness it was hot and dried out after a couple of hours, other wise i would definitely recommend Universal Studios, also to take into consideration we had a 6 yr old who was just a little short to go on some rides, but there was plenty of other rides etc she could go on.

We were pleasantly surprised with how professional the entire experience was at Universal Studios in Orlando, It is like they took the "Disney" Model and stepped it up a notch. I must admit, we thought it would be an overflow attraction, but it was better in most areas. Other than the old school attraction of rides and familiar Disney brand, Universal is more updated, current and fresh. Down to the waiting lines being more interesting and fun and the associates' uniforms having more details, etc. The associates themselves seemed to be "in-character" to a higher degree added to the enjoyment. Minor perks like free lockers next to each ride was a great convenience. Our on-site hotel, the Royal Pacific was also top-flight and detail oriented also.
A great day out at the film studios where the rides are based on famous movies. Thoroughly enjoyed the visits we have made here. An adventurous day to say the least.

Been to this park endless times and its still one of the best. Always adding and improving. A little disappointed Jaws is gone as I grew up with it but this park can really do no wrong. Great deals to do all the Universal parks which are all worth visiting. Been hundreds of times, will go hundreds more.

I had so much fun at universal! The crowds were not bad at all for september! Perfect time to go! The park is clean, well laid out and staff is very helpful. Prices in the giftshops and for food is FANTASTIC. Disney you have to sell a kidney for a toy or crappy made in china mickey ears. The rides are so much fun and the park isnt to overwhelming. Theres city walk on the outskirts which is nice because you dont need a ticket to go to city park so if you want to see a little bit of universal you can for free.
We always visit universal on our visits to Orlando. Each time we visit there is always something new. This time it was transformers ride and the simpsons village which had been superbly recreated.

This is a great park. We and our older kids (10 yo) had a wonderful time. Each and every attraction was interesting.  There were hardly any queues, so we managed to do both thus park and the Adventure Island within a day.( using the park to park option). There was no need for an express ticket.  Nevertheless, this park is not suitable for kids younger than 8. Although they can ride according to their height, the overall experience can be quite scary.

A fantastic park for movie buffs of universal as well as thrill seekers with some of their new rides. The simpsons area and harry potter are ever expanding and are adding new interest along with old favorites, even though they loss of jaws the ride.

Enjoyed by both children and adults as there are attractions for both It has good places to eat or enjoy a cold beer or a drink. The attractions are super fun and you have to spend all day so they can be enjoyed by all. Has bathrooms and water fountains everywhere. You should not stop visiting this park
I love universal, everything about it is fabulous, for all ages, best experience ever that's why I keep coming back, gotta see it to believe it.

You have to go just to experience the transformer ride and the live moving robotic Optimus he talks and walks. Simpsons was awesome as well as despicable me rides. Love this place! Adventure island was also nice, spidery ride and potter ride was great.
Visited both parks for three days and feeling is "Been there-done that-and don't need to do it again". Almost every attraction there spins and jars you senseless. Certainly not like Disney World.
Despicable Me ride, such fun. As was the Transformers ride, excellent. Great time of year to attend as the time to get on the rides was averaging about 20mins if you attend early in the morning.

I came during Halloween Horror Nights23&I had the best time! Tix price is cheap&no hassle with online ordering. Only complaint is skyhigh parking rate! Should be discounted for tixholders going for more than 1 night!!!

We did both parks in one day.  We bought the express passes but if you get there for opening at one park I wouldn't buy an express pass for that park but for the other park that you plan on visiting later in the day as at opening it's very slow.  Bring a change of clothes for island of adventures water rides. You will get soaked.  It's a great time.
What a place ! Everything here is fun lots to do and see . Food amazing .there is nothing here to dislike.

Theme parks are not my thing, so I was unsure what to expect here. We had e-tickets so had to get to the box office to redeem them before it closed at 5pm. We were glad we arrived at this time, as a lot of folk were just leaving, it meant the rides were quiet and maximum queue was 10 minutes for the Mummy. We had come for the Halloween Horror Night, so around 6pm the staff started to cordon off the park in preparation. What a fab night! The zombies are great, they are totally in their roles, I can't count the number of times I got a fright! American werewolf in London was great fun, tons of scares there, with one of our party holding up the line because she was so scared she couldn't move! I won't spoil it for you by telling too many details, but it's great fun, and can be pretty scary sometimes, so might not be suitable for the lower age limit of 13. Tip - don't eat too much just before you go, as some of the 3D rides might make you a bit ill on a full stomach. Despicable me was fun too, with great animation.

I loved the rides that me and my partner went on, transformers was my favorite and the mummy was his. We were planning to go to the Horror night at Universal Studios, we were told by a member of staff that it was best to come on a Wednesday (which we did). We got to park and we were going to ask if you need to pay for your ticket as the theme park ticket as I had been told that it would not cover it, only to find out that it was not on that night and on top of that you needed to pay an extra $40 to see it. I was not happy that I paid for a ticket which would not cover it, it just goes to that universal love to make money off people. We weren't really bothered that we were missing out, we decided to go on more rides and enjoy our day. The next problem I had was on the Men In Black ride, which I had been on before (about 11 years ago). I got through no problem waited in line for 10 minutes, only to get told as I got to the very front that my bag was unsuitable for the ride. I knew the ride was a rollercoaster so it should of been alright, plus I was wondering why the member of staff did not stop me from the beginning. So annoyed I walked through the exit, went straight up to the member of staff who was letting people in what had happened. To be fair he did calm me down and told me that there was a free locker I could use while on the ride, he then told me to go back up the exit to get on the ride. When finally on the ride me and my partner sat down and enjoyed it, but one thing I did notice that it was clearly alright to have my bag on that ride.

We had a great time here. Despicable Me, Shrek, Transformers, MIB, Simpsons, etc rides were amazing!!! A great way to spend time with your loved ones. A word of Advise: Take the Express Pass. The best $50 I have ever spent. We literally did not even had to wait at any lines. Easily saved us couple of hours or more worth of wait.

I will agree that many of the rides here are similar and not much fun. However, the Mummy is awesome. This is also a great place for concerts throughout the year. And the annual pass is cheap compared to Disney. One tip I can offer, you can use those lockers next to the Mummy and Men in Black for a little longer than just the ride.

I am a year long passholder and I always love going to this park. Worth the money spent on going. My sister attended the Halloween night there and she loved the Walking Dead zombies walking in the streets at night. And because everyone was at the haunted houses the lines for the rides was even shorter than normal. The rides never get old for me but all I can say is that I wish this park had faster roller coasters. Other than that make sure your kids are not too young because there is not a lot for them to do.

My main reason for this Review is for others similar to myself who have mobility difficulties, and found beforehand, no information other than scooter/wheelchair hire!  There is far too little information regarding accessibility, that can either make or break a day out!  I chose to rent a mobility scooter for my entire stay, booked through Virgin Special Assistance team, and was dropped off & collected from hotel (Enclave Suites). The downside was it being far too big & lumpy for Park transportation, so big thanks to the bus drivers AND fellow passengers for their patience whilst being loaded/unloaded.  So, to Universal Studios  Please note, ALL bags are checked at ALL Parks. However, unlike the UK, once you have purchased your 14 day pass, etc, queue entrances are vitually nothing.  There is no specific 'priority' ride access for disabled people, however, saying that, only a couple did I have to wait in line, those were Despicable Me & Shrek. At some rides, myself & companions were put in a separate line, which was helpful, as there are many ignorant people who don't notice you until they get their ankles 'clipped'. Several times I had to transfer from scooter to one of their wheelchairs, as walkway to simulator, etc, could be considered narrow.  After your first ride, I would recommend purchasing 'Star Photo' package, particularly if there are a few of you to share the cost, $60/£38. This might initially sound steep, but sharing the cost allows you to have UNLIMITED ride pics at both Island of Adventures and Studios, and also Character photo areas, such as the Transformer. We have around 40 pics in our album, which of course works out about £1 each!! However, I would recommend obtaining a non personal email address for everything connected with your holiday, as when you get back you may find an increased amount of junk.  As I have mentioned Tranformers, please be warned this ride frequently breaks down! It took us 3 visits before we got on. We chose not to wait in the 105 min queue in the heat, which is what happens when it breaks down and then re-opens!  Another Reviewer has stated food at the Parks are a rip off, I would have to disagree unless they go in 'proper' restuarants. Quite simply, if they are charging $7 dollars for something at a food stand, you can bet it would actually be £7 in the UK, not £4.40 after currency exchange! The three of us could easily eat (considering you don't feel like much in the heat) for around £10 including drink! Pint of coffee/hot chocolate in various Parks, less than £2!! Perhaps invest in one of their refillable drink bottles for unlimited refills, if making return visits?  Toilet facilities are excellent & clean, despite the number of people visiting. Staff are helpful, though not OTT on their 'Have a nice day' business everyone assumes. The most positive thing about US, you will see disabled people being employed at the Parks. No discrimination here, or insults, etc that I have experience in the UK, and no, I'm not a large, let alone obese person on a mobility scooter.  Renting a locker is perhaps the most expensive addition on the whole holiday.  Please note, during 'inclement' (rain) weather, rides shut down. Thank goodness this policy does not apply to UK theme parks!! We visited both parks about 5 times altogether, as some evenings we had rain/thunderstorms.  Overall, excellent family fun, can't wait to go again in a coupla years when new rides appear. Harry Potter is undergoing an extension which is apparently going to mean a train from Island of Adventures in to Universal Studios, so we will return then, I suspect!

Lot of interesting and exciting rides including 3D stimulation rides that are enjoyable and can be enjoyed by people of all ages. Everyone should go and visit this theme park at least once and enjoy the remarkable experience on offer here.

We arrived at Universal to find many good attractions removed. It is crazy to pay $100 each just to get in the park. Fortunately, it was low season, so it was not crowded. In high season, forget about getting on the rides in less than an hour. The Jaws ride was removed, so the New England Area was completely gone. There was construction going on,and the park is not really very big. About one fifth of the park was the Simpsons themed, and that is war too much for a show past it's prime. The "other" theme park was ridiculously priced too, but it was much larger with more rides and attractions for the same ridiculous price.

I've been in more than 5 times and I am not tired of it. It's adsoluted must visit to see the new Transformer. Best of all, when I visit I could see that in the next year will have provably other attractions. I never tire of seeing a twister or the mummy and if you want the trill you have to hop to the rock and roll roller coaster If you're an adult with a few days but want to have fun I recommend a day at Universal, one day at Islands of Adventure, one at Sea World. If you enjoy swimming pool access (I do not) then extend your stay and visit Aquatica or Wet and Wild.

There is not enough space to right my love and admiration for this park. Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure has become a staple in the lives of my friends and family. I have been coming here ever since I was a little girl, almost thirty years ago, and now each year, it is a ritual to visit once or twice with friends or family. This October was special because it was the first year I got to share the magic of this with my 5 year old daughter, Solvanna. My recommendation is buy a Park to Park ticket, that means you can enter both, Universal and Islands of Adventure all day. I ALWAYS buy UNLIMITED EXPRESS because Universal has perfected the art of fast passes, that allow you special entrance to the rides or shows with a 15 min or less wait, this is more important for a blazing hot July visit versus an October visit. We have never stayed on property, it is expensive and not worth it. We always stay at Hyatt Regency on International which use to be Peabody or there are an abundance of other hotels on International Drive near Universal Blvd. to choose from. The park has changed over the years, Universal Studios was a solo identity (before they built CityWalk and Islands) with main attractions that included: Kongfrontation, Back to The Future (now Simpsons), Jaws, Psycho show, Horror Make Up, E.T., Earthquake and Ghost Busters, now it has a new formula where it incorporates modern and trendy like SpongeBob, Transformers and Minons to classic, E.T. and Disaster (if you love Christopher Walkens, you will love that ride). Our favorite rides are E.T, Harry Potter Journey, and Men in Black, our favorite show is the Horror Make Up Show, and best dinning experience is Hard Rock Café which sits between the walk way between parks. Best dining if you are not going to explore City Walk would be in Jurassic Park, Thunder Falls has amazing chicken, turkey legs, rice and beans, corn and potatoes. You can also watch the enormous splash from Jurassic Park drop while eating. Universal is far more manageable than Disney, they also know how to handle large crowd control better as well as better accommodations for handicapped guests, etc. For example, when you travel to Disney you have to take a golf cart style cramped tram from the parking lot to a monorail where rude employees herd you like cattle, where at Universal, you pay either 16.00 or 22.00 to park (or valet), then take the people mover right into the park. Simpsons land/Krusty Land and Harry Potter World were both $$$$ genius, they draw large crowds to those areas, if you try a butter beer, get it frozen. if you do not like the taste of butterscotch and marshmallow, you will hate it, you have been warned. Photo package was offered to us by Nicole in E.T. Toy Closet, she treated us and my daughter like guest royalty and was very knowledgeable. The Star Card offers a 60.00 fee for 5 days worth of unlimited photos in 4x6 size. I cannot express enough how much money that saved me and how exciting it was to capture our vacation memories in such a fun way. you can take pictures literally anywhere in the park and they print them for you with or without fun boarders. What I dislike, almost seems impossible to say about this park, is that they copped out and do parades like Disney now. My daughter enjoyed them but they are a hassle if you are trying to go from one part of the park to another. Other thing is the Starbucks employees are rude and try to over charge you almost every time I catch them in a mistake. Other than that, Dr. Seuss Land is cute for children 1-8 or even for the big kid in you that loves that theme. if you love Marvel comics and heroes, they have that land in islands of Adventure where you can meet them all, buy collectables, and ride Spiderman, Hulk, Doctor Doom, etc. I always recommend you start at the back of the parks first and work your way forward. Always arrive 15 minutes prior to park opening to get from your car and through City Walk which is a restaurant, shopping and club atmosphere which is open til 2AM. While in Universal, check out the Lucy exhibit across the street from a delicious cake shop, E.T. Toy Closet, Universal Store near Minons, and first big store on the left of Islands. Enjoy the parks, maybe I will see you there one day, and safe travels to all!!

Each visit to Universal is a new experience as more attractions are added year on year. Latest rides are always extremely busy, but that means older ones are quieter .. MIB, Simpsons, Terminator 4D, Shrek and Twister were all walk ins, whereas a few years ago the lines were huge. Next year the Harry Potter experience moves in to Universal and this will again take pressure off the new rides .. Transformers and Despicable me.. A very full day .. or two .. lol.
Halloween Haunted Nights at Universal Studios is top notch! First experience there for this event. Loved it
Amazing day spent here. Will visit again and again. A must do while in Orlando. Loved the rides, the staff were friendly and helpful and the food was great.

How I loved the event. If you like walking dead, you must go. It is amazing. The actors, costumes, music, decorations and set up are definitely Hollywood. It feels so real and I enjoyed every moment. You must get the fast pass. If you don't, don't go!!! Lines are too long and you won't be able to see all the houses and get on the rides. Yes, a lot of the rides are open such as the minions, Simpsons, mib.

We got the annual passes we have now in May, and we've used them many times since then. Each time we go we really enjoy everything that Universal has to offer. I do recommend coming early in the day, because later of it's really busy and parking can be a little more difficult.

We went to Florida on the 23rd of December. We got a 10 day pass for Universal and kept going back every night, and spent at least 2 full days there. It was so worth it. The rides are fantastic and like nothing you've seen before. The atmosphere in the park is thrilling and excites everyone of every age, there was not a moment that we were not bustling with enjoyment. As I said, we went every night and spent 2 full days there, and still did not get to go on all the rides. The one regret I have is not getting Fast-Passes! We were stuck in queues for hours on end, however this did not dampen our delights. When I go back, and I certainly will, I will go at an off-peak time to ensure full enjoyment! The food in all the restaurants was authentic and so tasty. All the restaurants are themed, some even from famous movies like 'Bubba Gump' from 'Forest Gump'. The props you see all around the park are wonderful, its so amazing to be able to touch and get photos with props you've seen in all the big movies! There is something for everyone there including a Superhero section for all those nerdy fans. Each area in the park gives off such an atmosphere that you feel that you are really in the movies. Like the Jaws town, you can feel the eeriness! The best ride, I think, would be the mesmerising 'Mummy' ride, filled with fire, screams and extreme speed. Best holiday yet.

This park lacks the magic of disney or the character of the other parks. Easily completed the park in a day and felt the rides were lacking in comparison to other parks. The disaster experience was the most entertaining. I see there is construction underway so hopefully this will replace the atmosphere of a few years ago. Wouldn't rush back.

We were in America for one month and started our journey in Miami, we drove up to Orlando and started from there. Universal was awesome, great souvenirs, awesome rides, yum food. Such a rad day!! MAKE sure you wear sunscreen!! :)

So the whole park was great, and nicely theamed... but I went on Transformers 6 times within 2 days! Best ride they have in my oppinion hands down! Enjoyed MIB, Simpsons, Twister and Despicable Me as well!

From all the parks available, this one was the most disappointing. A bit of a weird lay out and just lacking the atmosphere and detail find in the other parks.  it really isa shame they don't have a fast pass system, only the pay through the nose to jump the queue option as after a few rides, the queues just build up. At one point the Minions ride was almost 2 hours long. We had to skip some of the rides we were looking forward to doing because of the queues.

brilliant!! u have to go on the Simpsons ride its fantastic! this park seems less crouded than the Disney ones we had a fab time here and queues went that long to get on rides! would def go bk to this park! x

Expensive tickets, long lines, only one good venue. Transformers 3D. All others were terrible. The meal tickets and drink tickets weren't worth the price. Meal tickets only good at three locations and drinks at five. All fast food that wasn't tasteful. An additional $16 to park. What a ripoff!!

Harry Potter world is unbelievable. The rides are INSANE! The food at the Three Broomsticks is fabulous! We had dinner, The Feast, which was salad, corn on cob, fresh steamed veggies, roasted potatoes, grilled chicken and ribs. Oh, and some butter beer. YUMMY! Don't miss this park if you visit Orlando.

Just got back from Florida and spent a few nights at this attraction . On arrival be prepared to pay for parking either $15 or $5 if arriving after 8 pm. Also be prepared for the giant queues - queues to get through the security at the arch, another at the 2 desks that exchange your voucher for the ticket you need. Then queue to get through the turnstile and into the attraction. Time spent one evening - up to 2 1/2 hours to this point from the car park. Find somewhere to eat and avoid the walkers that jump out at you whilst trying to avoid the real life walkers that stroll aimlessly round with a beer in one hand and texting in the other. Find the "house" that you want to experience and join the queue. While queuing enjoy the close proximity of beer soaked sops that have no idea of personal space and get through the next hour to an hour and a half whilst the 157 fast passers shoot on through. I know I could have paid out and upgraded the tickets to do this but after being bent over and shafted with the parking and the fact that you can't even take a bottle of water in with you into the park I decided they had enough from me already. And I don't agree with fast passes - my choice. If you survive long enough to enter the house you've selected you get to virtually run through it in an elongated conga with the crowd in-front of you. Don't attempt to slow down and actually look at what's supposed to be scaring you in the first place as there's minders to chase up anyone not that's moving fast enough. One house was done in 3 1/2 minutes after a 2 hour wait outside. The promo videos show the great effects and make up and they are really good, you just don't get time to enjoy it. You actually see more on you tube promo vids than on the night. If you like a beer and watching teenagers stagger around whilst queuing then give it a go.

My husband and I hadn't been to Universal for a few years now so it was nice to see all the new attractions there. Once again though, we did stay at the Loew's Royal Pacific Hotel so we could use the express pass system to bypass all the lines at the park. What a time saver! Plus, you can use their water ferries to go back and forth from the parks and Citywalk and the hotels. We just loved the new Simpson's ride and that section of the park. It really was like being in the cartoon, especially Moe's bar. There's a non alcoholic citrus drink that bubbles and smokes called the Flaming Moe which is a big hit since it's also a souvenir glass. So much fun. We were happy to see that some of our old favourites are still there... ET, Twister, Disaster, etc. in addition to the hilarious Despicable Me and exciting Revenge of the Mummy. We found the Rock It roller coaster just terrifying! We liked the new touch screen locker system too for storing your items on certain rides. Just be sure to remember which section of lockers you used and your locker number. You have to use the touch screen in the section you left your items. There's no charge if you're just storing things while you're on the ride. You use your fingerprint to access the box again when you're done so it seems quite a secure system. I was a bit worried at first since I had our passports and all our cash with us that day but we didn't have any problems at all. You can also give your camera to an attendant at the character photo ops and they will take a picture of you and your group. They also take another shot with their cameras which you can buy as well if you like it better. Great time once again! We'll be back.

Vegans please be aware that Universal Studios lies about food to get you to go there. 4 times Bob Burdick, chef at Universal Studios, Orlando told me that all the cheese on pizzas is vegan. On my 5th message to him I checked if he knew what a vegan was and explained it to him, highlighting that I believe the cheese had cows milk in it. Bob Burdick then admitted that the cheese was not vegan at all and blamed it on his suppliers giving him the wrong information I complained about Bob to customer services and several days later I received a phone message from customer services stating that they had spoken with Bob Burdick and all the cheese is vegan. Doh!!! It clearly is not. Why is he lying about this to people? He has admitted to me it is not vegan but is continuing to tell people that it is vegan. I wouldn't not expect all the cheese to be vegan and that is not what I am asking - Just be honest, as you could make people with milk allergies really ill....

I have been to universal studios the past three years and I just can't get enough of it! It is a wonderful holiday experience with lots to do. All the rides are based on movies which is great because it makes you feel like you are in the movie. Both parks are really clean and the staff are really friendly. The restaurants are nice and the food is delicious! I would highly recommend the Hard Rock Cafe and the three broomsticks at the wizarding world. I would recommend not going in the summer season because it can get really busy and the queues get really long. So going out of season would be more beneficial. Although the parking is expensive at $16, it's still good as it's all uncover and is linked to the parks with walkways so you don't have to walk far. The parks are well sign posted and maps are provided in order to get around easily. I love this place and I'm going again next year!!!!

We went as Florida residents with a coke can and got 50 percent off on a Wednesday night. We also splurged and bought the fast pass tickets. We can say we had an AMAZING trip! We went through all the houses at least once and zoomed through the lines. I would definitely recommend going through the weekday because as the night went on lines got longer, but not as bad as I hear weekends can be. The nice thing is the lines for the attractions that are open i.e-minion ride, men in black, simpsons ride etc...are not long at all so if you like those rides you can definitely hit them up more than once! All in all a great trip and we can't wait to go back next year!

Our family was very excited about Halloween Horror nights but left disappointed. The event is too crowded and the lines are way too long. We only made it through two haunted houses. Waited over an hour for one and over two hours for the second. The rides were not crowded so we enjoyed MIB and the Mummy with little to no wait. The scare zones were very good. I think there need to be perhaps limits on admission or assigned times to insure people don't have to wait 2 hours for a two minute haunted house experience. Probably won't do this again.

We had a great time at the horror nights, will definitely be back next year. The zombies walking around are awesome and really get you jumping when you're walking through the park. I highly recommend it as a group activity, get a hotel for the night, drink, and make sure you get the express passes. If you don't get the express passes you will definitely regret it as the wait can be VERY long for the houses/rides (~2 hours). With the passes we were able to go to all the houses and do the roller coaster twice, and a couple of the other universal rides that were open. The Cabin in the Woods was just amazing, so true to the movie, and really scary. Again, we loved it, and it will probably become a tradition to go every year from now on!

We went the first week in November and crowds were light. We walked right up to the Rock It- the only real roller coaster on the property. Our 7 and 8 year old boys were terrified walking up to the Mummy ride and kept their eyes closed for the entire ride. At this point my husband couldn't do any more simulated roller coasters because they made him nauseous and gave him a headache. The boys and I did the Simpson's Ride and even that seemed to be over the top in effects. We really enjoyed the Animal Actor's show. The host was very entertaining and the kids loved seeing the animals do tricks. Our last ride was Despicable Me. We did have to wait 35 minutes but in my opinion that was the best virtual roller coaster. The story was entertaining. There was motion but it didn't make you sick. The 3D effects were wonderful. This was our first day using our meal deal plan and were surprised to learn that we could get Ben and Jerry's as our snack. Yum!!

We went to both parks (Islands of Adventure being the other) and if I had to pick only one I could go back to, I'd pick this one. I'd say it's a bit more movie oriented as far as the rides and the live demonstrations. It's hard to pick a favorite attraction, but the whole Simpsons area is awesome. Aside from that, the rest is also awesome- don't miss Despicable Me or the Mummy ride.  I'd advise going in early November on a weekday like we did and you too can look at the unused metal queue railings with amusement and pity for those coming at busier times.

Loved to be there. Was one of the best places i recon, the best to me was the back to the future. It was incredible. If your going there, prepare for adventure, and has alot to pick from! Regards, Pet-r-us

Less lines than Disney and the attractions were just as good. There were playground areas for the kids which was a nice place for our grandson to get out of his stroller and use his own energy. Babyswap was clearly supported and the staff was very helpful. Because the lines were non existent we were able to get on almost all the attractions. There were parades and we caught one with a clearly juvenile theme. The characters engaged nearby children.

Really good and loads to do. The "Despicable Me" ride is spectacular!! New things being built, like the train station from Harry Potter in Islands of Adventure to Universal itself, Always something new to see.

Visited both parks on a quit day. The waiting times were very low we could walk from one attraction to the other. Food is average and high priced but that is standard in the parks. The price for parking is very high up to $ 22 for preferred parking.

This park was definitely awesome. My family enjoyed the adventure and thrill. There was a variety of activities for every age group and the experience was breath taking. Recommendations include arriving early and purchasing the fast pass for easy access to all rides.

There are some amazing rides here. The Despicable Me attraction is a "virtual roller coaster" which feels just like a real one. The seats move and tilt like you are going up and down and around the curves. The Shrek attraction is more stationary but has other "special effects that make you feel like you are in the story. There are a variety of dining choices and of course shopping opportunities. Kids, both big and small will enjoy these 2 parks.
I'm not a "ride" person but I really enjoyed the shows and people watching. Learning and experiencing the ways of making a movie is worth every penny.

The park is very nice but if you have been to Universal in Singapore then you can probably give this a miss. It all depends on how much time do you have on hand and how much are you wanting to spend. Each day at a theme park is not cheap, but if you must then opt for a 2 days Universal ticket. If you are alone or want to speed things you can do both the parks ie the Universal and the Islands of Adventure in a day but you have to be there at the park as soon as it opens and have to have your lunch on the go. Also, go for Single riders rather than wait in the queue. We did not get a chance to see the fireworks as it was not happening on the day we were in the park and the third day we did not want to go again.
Most kids don't know what ET is....needs to be removed and another ride put in it's place. It is slow loading and just not worth the wait.

Two of my favorite things, Take your time wonder around see characters pop up all over the places or take a picture with the a prop from one of your favorite movies, go on the rides eat the great food. I am want to go back once the work has been finished to connect the two parks together with the Hogswart express!

We had a lot of fun on our recent trip to Universal. They have so many different and unique rides here. There is something for everyone. They have a variety of shows to see, including the Beetlejuice show which was really cute. The Minions 3-d ride was so fun, as was the Shrek ride. It takes longer to go through this park than the island of adventure as there is more to do here.
this is my first universal studio for me and i really really enjoy my time in there! great place with superb rides!  this is more fun than the ones in Osaka and Singapore.

If you have no kids and can only visit a park, make it Universal. The rides are very different than Disney, much more thrilling. Where at Disney you laugh as you climb on a ride, I will admit I was pretty scared at the Hollywood Rip Ride RockIt. Even the simulators (of which half the rides at Universal are) move much more and throw you around a good bit.  The biggest downside, holy heck do they like to waste your time before rides. It seems like every ride you do has a 5-10 minute introduction when the ride itself only lasts a few minutes. That got very tiring after a while.  The express pass is a genuine rip off at 50$ but unfortunately, it's worth the money. We calculated the wait time was reduced by about 75% than not buying it. But when a ticket is 99$, this makes them cost a lot more than Disney.  It's also nowhere near as efficient as Disney, from parking to cleanliness to organisation, it's a few bars less but that didn't bother us much.  And finally, don't waste your time on the Disaster! ride. In good ol whining teenage fashion- if that had been any boring or lasted any longer, I would have like, totally, killed myself and made a real disaster out of it. Seriously though, it was the most boring 25 minutes of our trip (including the 7 hours wait at the airport).

But it was worth every penny! Definitely get the frozen butterbeer and make sure to visit the ladies room! We had lunch at The Three Broomsticks. It was ok. Loved the character actors and Ollivanders!

they have several food choices that were amazing to eat at. The ride waits we not that bad plus if it was a specific ride to a certain movie then while you are waiting they would have things you can look at or even watch while you are waiting.

The lines are extremely long. The lines in both parks for pretty much everything were at least 90 mins. They let the people with express passes pile in, increasing your wait time exponentially. Why did we even buy tickets then? Seems like a waste of money unless your willing to pay even more for an express pass. They really could take a lesson from disney and offer shorter lines to all. The parks have some cool rides, but whats the point if you can't get on them. We will probably just stick with disney in the future.

If you are in Orlando to visit theme parks, do not overlook Universal Studios. It is a must-see for those over the age of seven. If you have younger children, then you may want to stick with Disney World or try Islands of Adventure, which has a section for children.

Harry potter world is worth the trip. My twenty something kids loved it! Day after Christmad so it was insane, but we tougher it out, got there really early and had no problems! You HAVE to stop ai Ollivanders and get a wand!

What a great park! So much to see and do! But plan on arriving early or go latter in the day as some of the lines were long - Harry Potter ride was 150 min wait time! But overall my teens were happier here than other parks like Disney and Sea World. Also, even though we were there during a very busy season we found this park's design could better accommodate the crowds.

I'm not sure how I feel about The Universal Studios park, even though I had a fast pass we still had to wait quite a while to get on the Despicable Me ride, which broke halfway through and we had to experience it all over again, Shrek 4D is a waste of time, it takes about 15 minutes until you can go in to the theatre and then when you are in the show isn't all that great, the chairs are meant to move but ours (in the back row) barely even moved, which we weren't told about. The Hollywood rollercoaster was great, probably the best ride there. The Transformers ride was very good, but like the Despicable Me one, broke halfway through and lost it's sound, which was disappointing. The rest of the park I can't really comment on as it was way too packed to walk and very tiring, the Macys christmas parade was a little overrated and not very good, just blow up animal shapes and a few naff characters, the park is a lot less christmassy than Islands of Adventure and has less food and drink options, slight disappointment and wouldn't really go back again.

This is our 2nd visit and 1st visit with my 7 yr old. He enjoyed Despicable Me the best and then Transformers. The characters were out for photo opportunities so we liked that. One thing to remember is buy the package if you want the pictures Universal takes, because we did not and we left the park thinking we can go online, review and purchase like Disney and we lost all the pictures because we didn't buy their package or make sure you take photos with your own camera. The lines were minimal in wait time, 20-30 minutes max and we visited the 2nd weekend of Dec. They allowed water bottles and some food. That saved money because food/bev in the park is obviously quite expensive. Our favorite show was Fear Factor because it was live and we are fans of the show. Plan your visit by going online and reviewing the map of the park and the shows offered at the park. This will make for a more relaxed visit especially if you have small children. They are building on so we can't wait to come back in a few years to see what they have added.

The Universal Studio theme parks are definitely something to visit at least once in a lifetime if you are a movie buff!! The Harry Potter section is extremely well done and the major ride (in the castle) is totalling amazing!! We did it 4 times!!! Not for people with 3D "motion-sickness" though!! LOVED our 3-day stay there!!
Amazing variety of rides and attractions, I loved every minute. Just wished there was more minutes in the day and that I didn't get tired :)

We went to Islands of Adventure on Dec 28th, 2013. We have never felt so ripped off in our lives from start to finish. First off, we had to wait in line for 40 mins to park. We were then charged $16 to park. We paid almost $100 each for 5 entry tickets. Upon entering the park, it started to rain, which granted, we were not prepared for. We duly had to pay $8 each for plastic bags to cover ourselves, $40 total. Universal is likely buying these bags for about 2 cents each. They could easily make them complimentary to their patrons. The average wait time for the majority of the major rides was an hour and a half, and 2 hours for Harry Potter. We felt compelled to purchase 2 express passes at a mind boggling cost of $139 each!!!! Even with these passes, we found we could not use them for the Harry Potter Forbidden Journey. When we got wet on some of the water rides, we decided to use the drying facility at a cost of $5 per use! Again, this could easily be complimentary or at worst $1. It just seemed that they shamelessly wanted to screw customers out of every last dime. Toon land is a complete joke. Incredible Hulk, Jurassic park and Spider-Man are good rides. Seuss land is great for smaller kids. We left the park at 9pm after having spent close to $1,000 and we brought our own food!!! We will not be back and we will be recommending that none of our friends go there. Disney is so much more customer friendly and organized, with knowledgeable staff. It is altogether much more worthwhile with a speed pass system that is fair to all, not just the few who can afford to fork out exorbitant fees for express passes.

Alright, I'll be fair- US is a GOOD park. This is my first time ever going, and I am strictly comparing it to DisneyWorld as they are direct competition in terms of expectations. We did DW last year, and just finished 3 days at US. Here's what I see..... 1. US creates and fosters a definite 2-tiered 'class' distinction for guests. If you have enough money on the day you go, and can afford to pay upwards of $100 EXTRA per person for the Express pass upgrade, you get to bypass SOME of the lines for rides, and get preferred seating in the shows. While that's all well and good if you have $400-$500 to spare, what about the rest of us poor 2nd class citizens? Let me tell you, there was a lot of discussion about this in lines, and no one liked it. However, had US not had this system, i think the lines would move a lot quicker for everyone, instead of just the elite. This pass system is not applicable to all rides, either, and i heard complaints about that too. Disney has a FastPass system which is accessible to all, free to all, and works very well. I understand they also have some other kind of express pass, but frankly-its not needed. 2. US grabs money wherever it can. There is a water ride where you can use water cannons to splash the guests at the end of the ride. THEY CHARGE YOU MONEY TO DO IT. Yes, its only 25c, but i'm sure Disney would do it for free, and just for fun. US has lockers which you can use for 25 minutes for free on the rides where they don't let you take on your bags....if you are late- you pay to retrieve your stuff. Guess how many rides have lines that you can get through in 25 min or less? Not too many....especially with the Express riders jumping ahead! We put our stuff in a locker when the ride wait was posted as 5 minutes, but by the time we walked back to the line (about 40 feet away) the posted time was 15 minutes. Luckily we made it through, but we saw a lot of people who didn't and were angry and arguing with park staff. 3. Cheesy rides. Ugh. There are some really great new ones: Spiderman, Minions, Transformers, Harry Potter etc....but some seem really old and outdated. Especially the 'show' rides like Poseidon's Adventure (i kept waiting for it to start, before realizing i was "on" the ride), and the stunt show Sinbad. It was ok, but just seemed really dated. Not knocking the actors here, the guide for Poseidon was VERY good, and the physical stunts in Sinbad were decentlyl executed, but the choreography and overall production was lacking. 4. Park cleanliness was good, washrooms not so much. Park staff friendly, and tried to help, but had their hands tied at times which was very strange. For example - we wanted to know the times of the Frog Choir and shows in Harry Potter....not posted nor in the guidebooks. We asked a staff member who pulled out a times guide and rattled off about 25 showtimes, but said we couldn't have a copy nor even take a photo of their printed guide because 'it was their personal guide and they can't share it'. Why on earth not??? Why can't guests to the park know when shows are on??? 5. Entry to the park and lines in general weren't handled all that well....we (standing in a line waiting to meet Capt. America) were told off by him to "get in a single file line along the curb, if its too hard to figure out, then move on!". Literally. Barking at us like an angry teacher. I totally understand his frustration and i don't blame him, but he didn't have a handler (like Disney always does) and people were mobbing him. Not fair for the actors. We saw that a few times from different characters. I felt badly for one guest in a wheelchair who was trying to get a photo of a character, and because there was no crowd control, she kept getting stepped in front of and never got her chance. We couldn't get to the front with her in time, and the character had to leave. Getting in to the park was a mob scene, but i guess that's everywhere....and it is definitely a fair walk through the city walk to the actual park entries. Parking was managed well. 5. The ride lines were crazy long at times, and that's not the park's fault, but there was more to look at and experience in many of Disney's ride lines. Some of US were ok (Spiderman), but others were just stand and wait, and hopefully you have nice people to talk to. Again, this is the trend with newer rides - better things to see on the way...older rides....meh. More signage would be better, rather than relying on cast members to continually shout and repeat themselves at all the guests, resulting in frustrated and grumpy staff! 6. The little extras - Disney is very good at creating ambience and providing things to see along the way...US tried but missed the mark. Many of their Harry Potter artifacts and extra scenery are behind layers of chain link fencing so you can hardly make out what it is, and certainly not take decent pictures of it. Filch's emporium was a disappointment as its really just a store (selling $35 plastic wands and $40 stuffed owls!) with some things tucked up above your head where you can't really see them. I feel Disney would have displays with things labelled as to what they are, who they were confiscated from, etc (you'd have to understand the backstory to this store).  On the upside- the Harry Potter show staff were superb. Excellent singers, dancers, and hosts. People stayed in character, and were true to the books. They were all excellent with kids (we had a 6 yr old boy) and patient with him and nice to us...but we were also nice and polite with them!  Overall, it was fun, but we won't be going back. It can easily be done in 1 day per park...and keep in mind we didn't use express pass and we were there on Dec 31 and Jan 1. We had the 3rd day 'free' tickets, and used only another 1/2 day to wander a little....we had seen it all the previous 2, but felt like we should use it since we had it. Maybe its more fun for the thrillseekers who are there to ride the Hulk 10 times...but for us it was just ok. :)
This theme park is one of the best in Orlando it has rides for youngsters and older visitors and the entrance fee is very reasonable.
Harry Potter world is being extrended to include the Hogwarts Express and Digone Alley. Loads of rides and attractions for all ages.

We took the kids to Orlando for Christmas, 5 kids ages 13-19. Once I recovered from the sticked shock, just under $140 per person for 2 parks, we had a great time. We had heard scary stories about huge lines so we arrived just before 8am on New years day, It was ideal. We only had to wait 5 to 20 minutes for most rides. The park was so beautiful, great decorations for Christmas. Suess and Harry Potter areas were amazing. The rides were lots of fun, but not like the extreme roller coaster at parks like 6 Flags. A hard core adreneline junkie may be disappointed because there is only 3 real roller coasters, Hulk, Dragon Challenge and Rip Ride. Overall it was a great day for everyone.

If you like some of the Universal movies, you should come here. Or if you don't, you should come here too. There is lots of things to do. The new Simpsons area is great! If you're a fan of the show, you will certainly like it. There is Duff products and burgers at Krusty burger. The new Transformers ride is amazing!! Good use of technology. Makes you feel like you're part of it! My favorite ride is the Mummy rollercoaster. For the thrill seekers there is the Riptide Rockit rollercoaster. The Minions ride is so cute! But there are also the old school attractions that are still worth the visit: Terminator, Twister and Disaster. Stay for the night and watch the Cinematic Spetacular, a retrospective of the 100 years of Universal. One of the most beautiful night presentations from all of Orlando parks. If you're a big movie fan, you will love it!

We went in November and there were hardly any queues. Highlights were Rockit, MIB, the Simpsons, the Terminator, Transformers, Despicable Me Minion Mayhem and you have to do ET! The parade was a bit disappointing but kids loved it!

We went to Universal for the first time at the end of December 2013 and beginning of January 2014. All of the Christmas decorations were still in place and I must admit they do a lovely job of decorating. That being said - THE WAIT TIMES FOR RIDES ARE HORRENDOUS!! Over 2 hours for Despicable Me/Minions and Harry Potter! Why does Universal NOT GET A CLUE?? When you trap people in lines for rides, they are NOT SPENDING $$ ON THEIR OVER PRICED FOOD AND SOUVENIERS!! Charging people for an "Express pass" isn't going to work - people will almost always choose to wait over shelling out more money to ride an attraction. Be smart Universal and copy the FREE Disney fast pass system so you can squeeze more $$ out of the guests!!

We went because we were in Florida and so help all three of us, we were going to Harry Potter World at Universal. The HP experience was amazing - the ride is fun, the stores are very good, the frozen and cold butterbeers are good and, for the adults, the Hogmeade Ale was tasty. Yes, we bought wands in Olivanders and we did all the rides and spent way too much on HP merchandise but it was worth it.  One tip: I get motion sick on roller coasters now (very sad, cause I love them) and the HP ride did make me will. HOWEVER, I'm glad I did it because it was so well done. Hub and teen wanted to ride again so we all went through the line -- and glad we did. At the ride you MUST put everything in a locker when you go in (lockers are free) but if you aren't riding, you can take your stuff. That's what we did - the Hogwarts castle that you walk through is amazing and we got many many pictures during the second time through. As soon as we got almost to the end, I went to theside room and waited for Hub/Teen to ride.  Parent with small children tip: The HP ride DOES let you go through with your child (who may be too young, not tall enough) to ride but one parent can keep kid and go to the side room while the other parent rides. And then, when that parent gets off, the staff will let you swap out parents to the waiting parent can ride. Very nice.  The Hulk roller coaster was loved my teen and Hub; I didn't ride. The rest of the park, though, is dated. Full Disclosure: We should have done more in Suess World, even with the teen. They need to update the rides. Also, there are two parks and admission gets you to one or the other - this is really ridiculous when there are only X number of rides in the park.  Food recommendation - great dining at the Jurassic Park restaurant. Fresh veggies and good chicken - with fresh grilled corn on the cob.

My wife insisted we visit Harry Potter world at Islands of Adventure while we were in Florida, so we opted for the two day ticket to take in Universal Studios as well. It was great, and although they may not appreciate the reference, their attention to detail and creating atmosphere was very Disney-esque. My favorite "land" was the Simpsons and Krustyland. I had no idea how much of Springfield they had recreated, and of course my favorite was Moe's Tavern. The Simpsons ride was one of the best in the park. The Transformers Ride was good too, but the wait was tremendous. It stated 90 minutes at the door, but we waited over 2.5 hrs. The rock n roll roller-coaster was memorable as well. Overall, we were very impressed and look forward to going back to Universal Studios if we are ever back in Florida.
loved the attractions and for an adrenaline junky like me the Hollywood rip ride rocket and fast ride indoors The revenge of the Mummy were just the ticket. also loved Shrek 4D
Fantastic theme park. Would highly recommend buying the fast pass as it saves so much time,yes it is very pricey but so worth it! A lovely place to go in the evening as well as during the day.
There are several great experiences, Fear Factor Live, Transformers, Twister and Disaster. Overall, just a great day. Maybe less orientated to younger kids compared to Disney Parks.

We visited in December and got pelted all day by rain, yet this didn't hamper the great time we had. We had little kids and with all there was to do and see the rain was not any deterrent to the fun. A MUST.

I had heard so much about this event that my boyfriend and I decided to go to it instead of Howl O Scream ( won't make that mistake again). The line for every house was no less than 100 mins and that was with the fast pass. We only got to 4 of the 8 houses. There were more booze stands than anything else and the place was full of drunk people that at one stage you could not tell the difference between them and the staff dressed as zombies. The only saving grace was the Rocky Horror Tribute which was FANTASTIC. I love Universal Studios but this is one event I won't be returning for.

We hadn't been here in a few years. Jaws is gone, Back to the Future is now the Simpson's ride, Mummy is still pretty cool. Some other rides need to go...Twister is boring and half of the special effects aren't working. It would be great if they would change the show for Disaster. It's still the same from 5 or 6 years ago. The Simpson's Springfield area is awesome. My kids loved seeing the restaurants and shops from the show. The Barney area is outdated. Who watches Barney anymore? I would love Universal to replace that area with a Spongebob bikini bottom themed area and rides. Now that would be awesome! Food is expensive as theme parks usually are. We took advantage of the refillable popcorn bucket. $5.99 first, then 99 cents a refill...good for the rest of your life! So I have that saved with our vacation stuff if we ever go back. Ice water is free. The night show was a great tribute to movie history. I think seeing it once was enough. I would probably skip it next time and ride rides.

I don't get it. too expensive, too busy and no value for dollar. went day before Christmas - added express passes to our tickets to the tune of $400.00 more dollars to our already too expensive tickets and blue man show which ended up being cancelled - still have to get money back for that. Kids stood in line for hulk - express line - ride failed and they waited an hour+ had one ride and the youngest felt too sick to go on too many more. Went on several walk through adventures which were a joke. Not interested in Harry Potter where t was even crazy busier. Stayed for fake Santa Claus parade...all in all not a really fun and very expensive day.

Haven't been to Universal in over 22 years and my how it has changed. We arrived before the park opened and that was a good idea as the gate opened up 10 min. early. Make sure that you go straight to Despicable Me as that is the best attraction and the line builds very rapidly. Gone are our favorites- Back to the Future, King Kong, and Jaws. In their place we have The Simpson's, Transformers which was OK. and Twister which was boring. We saw all that we wanted to see before lunch. Can't quite put my finger on it but the charm that we remember seems to be missing. May be another 22 years until we return.

I love Universal. There is so much to do and see, and the rides are incredible. I think the parking is a big high, and the waits for the attractions are the only downers. You can get the express pass, but it is very expensive for a family of four. If you go during a busy time period, the express pass can cost you almost as much as the ticket itself. So it's a very expensive day ...... but it's a blast!

Visited here on a thursday. Perfect, no people in line and we had time to do all kinds of stuff and did some rides more than one time. Great places to eat and the rides was awesome. 3D-rides rule. Try Simpsons, The Mummie and Transformers.

Yes this ride is dated! Yes, most children don't have a clue who E.T. even is. But the ride is WAY cool. And the que line is really near as well. If you really want a cool experience, go to the park on a slower day, and you will prbly get a whole ride vehicle to yourself! It's nice to see such a classic dark style ride, one minus big projection screens. Just thrills and magic.

We went to Disney's Magic Kingdom and really didn't feel like going to American theme parks ever again. We had already purchased tickets prior our trip, so we felt that we had to go as it is a lot to let 500 $ go to waste. Universal was a very pleasant surprise! Not very crowded compared to Disney, we went on a lot of rides, and the children's activities were very good, our 5 year old loved it, she didn't want to go home, where as she was very keen to leave Disney. We aren't big fans of Universal, but this was so great! It was very well done, not a detail missing! The Simpsons and the Transformers area especially felt like you were on the real set! We loved it and would definitely go again!

Hadn't been to Universal for few years so really impressed by 'new' Harry Potter world. The rides here are absolutely fantastic (although one of them broke down on 2 different occasions when we were on them, which was pretty scary!). The setting is just magical with the incredible Great Hall, snow topped roofs and butter beer. Other new rides were Transformers and Despicable Me, both of which are fantastic. We went to the evening Cinematic Spectacular show which tells the story of 100 years of movie memories, most worthwhile and outstanding, as expected. Get a good viewing point early near the lake.

Traveled with a trade show sponsored event to the park and Universal knows how to make thousands of people feel that the park was opened just for them. Our visit proved to be a great opportunity to network and have a really great time.

I went to Universal Studios the week of February 1st thru 7th. I bought a 4 day park to park pass online months before I visited the park. Construction is still going on at USF, Springfield USA was done and it looked awesome. The park was pretty much empty up until noon everyday and then the park was some what busy. As soon as the park opened everyone went to Minion Mayhem, Twister: Ride it out was closed but it didn't surprise me. I won't be surprised if they decide to remove it and put something else in its place. I rode everything in the park in less than 2 hours and I was there by myself. Most of the people who came to the parks were from Tri-State area (New York, New Jersey, PA), Great Lakes and South America. If everyone wasn't escaping from the snow I bet the park would pretty much be empty. I still had fun rode every ride I could ride before I got bored. I would come back to USF every year if I could.

We visited on Feb 15. The equipment kept breaking down and the lines take forever. They told us transformer line was 45 min. But after 3 hours they finally said the ride was having mechanical issues. We had made it to the ride but couldn't wait any longer.

We just came back from a quick trip to Orlando. We went to Islands of Adventure first to experience all that is Harry Potter, and my kids decided to check out Universal Studios on day two because of the Minions ride. We got into the park around 11:30 or so and by 3:00 we were headed out the door with a quick stop at the store to get a few last minute souvenirs (merchandise from Islands of Adventure is also available in Universal Studios). The place just seems randomly organized and quite run down. The rides seems to be either thrill ride roller coasters or 3D adventures that rely on similar tricks (spritzing water). We happened to be there during a parade and let's just say that the good folks at Disney have NOTHING to worry about. It was fairly lackluster and underwhelming - even the performers looked bored or embarrassed. Later, we were sitting on a bench having a snack (they DO have turkey legs) and a woman dressed as Betty Boop along with a handler came down the street. She had difficulty attracting any interest. One family insisted their children pose and it was the most uncomfortable scene I've witnessed. Betty tried gamely to get them to smile and pose and the kids just had no clue who this strange woman in red was. I imagine if you lived locally and loved roller coasters or were interested in the musical acts that perform (it was Mardi Gras and Daughtry and Robin Thicke were among the featured performers) it would be worth a visit, but otherwise you can easily skip this park and do something else in Orlando. All of this could change with the addition of the Harry Potter attractions slated for this summer (including transport via Hogwarts Express to Islands of Adventure). I suspect that the reason for bringing Harry into this park is to try to spread out the crowds and reinvigorate Universal Studios. For what it's worth, the Mummy ride was fun and the Rock Roller Coaster has a fun feature that allows you to select a song from about 20 options to play while you are having your neck and spine re-aligned on the ride. To be fair, we didn't experience some of the big attractions (Transformers, Fear Factor) as we just had become bored.

There are two parks here... The rides are very good with both actual rides (roller coasters and kids' rides) and 3D rides. There is literally something for everyone. Good food choices as well. Wait times were minimal. We did not enjoy Disaster (the ride was good, the intro was LONG and not enjoyable); same went for Terminator (not worth the wait - which is intro time not considered wait time). We went as a party of 4 with two adults, one 18 year old and one 15 year old. We all had our favourites. The Wizarding World of Harry Potter was phenomenal but a smaller area than expected. The teens loved the Butter Beer (not the Pumpkin Juice). We ate at The Three Broomsticks Restaurant. Good value for the money and wonderful atmosphere. This park is much more relaxed than Disney. If you want a beer, shop around...prices vary significantly. They have 'free' lockers requiring a finger print to acquire and release the lock. They are free for different periods of time depending upon the attraction. We did have a problem and we were charged $9 for a few minutes longer than the time allowed, even though we do not believe we were longer. The ride line was 5 minutes in length, our party went on twice and returned to find we were fined. A credit card is then required to release your lock.

If you are travelling with kids, this park is not worth it. I am here with a 6yr oldsnd a 10 yr old my parents in their 60s. So we wait online for 1.5hrs to ride the last transformes. We did not mind since we only had that and dispicable me to ride. Well the transformer ride broke down in the middle of the ride. We waited ten munutes to walk down three flights of steps and then were given an express ticket to cone back or use in another ride. So we went to dispicable me. Still not bothered just disappointed. But then were tdld wecould not use it on that ride. So we wd hv to wait another hour! No consideration that we had just waited an hour half for ride that dodnt work. Also kids were bored of all the same type rides. Staff not as well trained as Disney's. Not worth the 98 pp admission. At all.

We spend enjoyable hours in Universal studios because we went through week days, we didn’t spend much time waiting in Qs maximum 30 minutes, but if U plan to get there in weekend U will lose your time in waiting in Qs, I liked most games specially Mummy & magic show, we have seen Blues Brothers in nice show, fire working was amazing, when I visit Orlando again I will definitely go to Universal Studios.

This place is great for late night partying for adults. Its expensive but drinks and good times to be had!! I stayed across street at hotel for 1/2 price and tram to take you there. Have FUN!! Only live once!!

Universal Studios Florida is not as fun as Universal Islands of Adventure, but still a great day out. My family with a 16 year old, 14 year old, and 12 year old spent five hours there. However, we did get the Express Passes, which were awesome. Our favorite rides were the Hollywood Rip Ride Rock It, the Revenge of the Mummy, and the Despicable Me Minion Mayhem. We also enjoyed the Shrek 4-D show, the Transformers 3-D ride, the Men In Black Alien Attack, and the Simpsons Ride. I also loved the atmosphere in the New York section of the park. We ate at Mel's Drive In, which was standard park food. It was a fun day, but I wish there were more rides. Something we all agreed on: Universal DOES NOT need another simulation ride. They're okay, but not as good as the real roller coaster experience.

We visited on a wednesday, and it was not busy at all. We walked onto every ride, ate at any restaurant without waiting. The weather was awesome, the rip ride rocket was actually running. They have a child swap on rides, which is great for parents with small children. Allows them to have some fun too. Great place to have some fun!

This review is for the Universal Islands of Adventure Theme Park. My family and I came to Orlando in October 2013. We came to visit the theme parks. It was my two daughters, my six grandchildren and myself. Over all the best liked park was Islands of Adventure. We all loved the newer Harry Potter area and of course "Butter Beer". The River Adventure was also a big hit, because Grandma got soaked and the kids thought this was hilarious. The temperatures were well into the 90s' each day so the water rides and other water areas were of course very welcome. The staff were friendly and helpful and the park is very clean. We are looking forward to coming back soon and I'm sure that Islands will definitely be at the top of the list of parks.
It Is so cool they have done a wonderful job bring the Harry potter movies to life. I can't wait until it is completely finished. Which will be July of 2014.

Universal Studio Parks in Orlando are Exceptional. We have been to Universal Studio in Hollywood which is excellent but the Orlando Parks cannot be beaten for the rides, shows and especially the Harry Potter Theme and rides. Bush Gardens have some hair raising roller coasters too and is a brilliant day out. Discovery Cove and Aquatica are high up on our list plus all the numberous dinner shows e.g. Pirates, Sleuths, Magic Show which are all on I-drive
Twas a memorable one for me and my husband at the time. We were like kids again enjoying all the rides and adventures... A MUST SEE when you are in Florida... Absolutely awesome!!!!

This park is more about experiential effects and immersion into the rides. They are really good at doing this. I recommend riding all the rides, even the kiddie ones as you will find them fun and entertaining. My husband has never been to universal and he loved it. We rode everything except for the water rides. I highly recommend going midweek to skip the large crowds and arriving as early as possible. Waiting in long lines could make this not so fun, as it does for any theme park. We went during off-season on Wednesday and Thursday and never had to wait for a ride!  Islands of Adventure: This park is very well designed and every single area looks amazing. If you are a harry potter fan head there first! It is the best part of the park, and it fills up. I would avoid being here at all for the grand opening of the HP expansion this summer, as it will be packed. The comic book area is really well done and there are plenty of photo opportunities everywhere. Love the marvel universe. The hulk is my favorite roller coaster! Ride the coasters as single riders if there is a long wait. Go see the stunt show at the lost continent.  Universal Studios: This park does not look as well-designed as Islands of Adventure but offers many nostalgic and fun rides. Head to despicable me first, this line gets very very long very fast since it is near the entrance. After that either transformers or head to Simpsons ride. Although if you rode the spiderman ride at IOF you could skip transformers it is basically the same experience. Simpson's world is very well done. Don't forget to get a Lard Lad's donut!!! (so good) Plenty of characters to meet in both parks, don't forget your autograph book for them to sign.  Food: Food is really pricey as usual and is largely the same items. As a vegetarian I sampled veggie burgers at Jurassic Park in IOA and a black bean burger at Krustys in Universal Studios. These were good. Their cheese pizza was no so great. You can always leave the park entrance and go to citywalk for more variety. Snacks were not so great either, it was churros and soft pretzels and thats it. So for a snack I highly recommend lard lad's donuts in Simpsons world as this is the best snack you can get, and so cheap, too.

the rides were absolutely amazing,it was a day of fun,fun and fun,we particularly enjoyed the revenge of the mummy,men in black,shrek 4D and hollywood rip ride rocket,unfortunately transformers were opening a few days after we were coming home,which was shame,however we are returning this year,June 22nd so we cannot wait to enjoy the thrill of the new transformers ride,we will also enjoy the new diagon alley in universal studios and islands of adventure.
Loved the Blues Brothers show. Beelejuice is great too. I loved ET, but I guess I'm a big softy! Great for families, something for every age.

It's an expensive way to waste away a full day in the Florida sunshine and we are entitled to look for something for our $100 per person per day. To be honest, not enough has either changed or improved. Well apart from the 'security' measures. The poor system of issuing tickets (where they try to sell you whatever extra they can) to the 'finger printing' ticketing is poorly managed and hopelessly time consuming. The park is pretty good if you haven't seen it before - so it is a must - but as for a repeat visit, it has to be a no-no. Even our favourite bit of renditions by 'The Blues Brothers' was only saved by a fantastic performance of a supporting lady - Jake & Elwood were pretty average to be honest (and that's being very generous). The rides are good - well apart from the pathetic Twister with it's 'cow on a string' (you have to see that to believe how poor it is) but the waiting times for the rest are horrendous. 90 minutes are the norm for the good ones which is a big chunk out of your day for a few rides. Having said all that, do go once but plan your schedule.

I have visited all of the Orlando theme parks multiple times since I was a kid. Never have I been so disappointed with Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure. First, we got there and were required to take a "3 question survey" that actually turned out to be around 30 questions. I have no problem with surveys when the time is appropriate. My family spent PLENTY of money to spend the day at these parks so the last thing I want to do is take time to fill out a survey. Although that was annoying, that wasn't what ruined our trip. As we continue to walk through the parks we were asked to take several more surveys. We decided to visit Harry Potter attraction. My advice - DON'T GO. I am a Harry Potter fan and found it be completely overrated. There was a winding line to just to get into the candy shop or to get a "Butter Beer" aka overpriced cream soda. You can hardly walk through "Diagon Alley" without rude people constantly bumping into you or stepping on your feet. Still, that's not the thing that made me lose my cool. We waited in extremely long lines for them to tell my father he was too big to ride certain rides. My father is a tall man who is a bit larger, but not obese. His knees were crammed into the roller coasters that seemed to be made for 5' 5" tall people that weigh less than 200 lbs. Just know that these rides are not created for all body types. We also waited in line to ride "Revenge of the Mummy" in Universal Studios. They stopped the normal line for more than 10 minutes to let all of the "Fast Pass" users to go before everyone else. I understand that they paid extra to cut the lines, but you should not stop an entire line for over 10 minutes to let every single one of them go. The line shouldn't have gotten that long in the first place. The thing that irritates me the most about this experience is that they don't tell you this kind of stuff beforehand. They take your money and don't care whether you can enjoy their attractions or not. I am someone that cares about the ethics of businesses and I believe that Universal Studios strictly cares about making money and will do whatever it takes to do so.

Its been awhile since we've been to Universal, and after our visit to Epcot I have to admit I was a little apprehensive that we'd find that it hasn't aged well either. I was very thrilled to find that while there are still some remnants from the past Twister and Terminator that should arguably retired, they are more than balanced out by newer additions such as the The Simpsons, The Transformers, and Dispicable Me. Rounding the whole thing out are classics such as The Mummy- my wife made us ride that one twice- and E.T. The Simpsons ride is very cool, and the Springfield area of the part is awesome- make sure to visit Moe's Tavern for a Flaming Moe and a Duff beer and Lard Lads for a giant donut. Oh, and how can I forget the Hollywood Rip Ride Rocket?
