Just hang on and enjoy the ride of your life while listening to some great tunes; be careful though if you are a big guy like me as the seats are a little tight and you have to be a little careful of the leg restaints. I've never even seen the movie Dispicable Me but I really enjoyed the ride. Rain was eminent all afternoon, but held off until the day was almost over for us- then the monsoon came. We waited it out and ended our day with E.T. which somehow managed to be nostalgic and almost quaint for me. Two final words for you: Fast Pass.

i'm not into thrill rides but these appear to be the main (only?) strengths of this park. live entertainment was lame, parade canceled as soon as it started. food poor and pricey. less crowded than Disney, for a reason.
Universal Theme Park was a lot of fun! If you can get the express pass (especially during high season) do it! This way you don't spend most of your time waiting in lines.

Liked all rides etc, but felt tickets are expensive, especially for one day, also considering not cheap felt that universal should spend some money and update certain old rides/shows ie terminator etc plus certain things like wand and extras were overpriced
great park, its fun for all ages, I highly recommend getting the express pass, well worth the cost of it.

I coudnt wait until my kids were old enough to go to Disney. Would have been my first time too. Boy was i disappointed! The sun was hot, the lines long and everything ridiculously expensive! I spent so long waiting in lines but the end of the day we had only gone on two! The show was great though! The kids enjoyed only that! Dont think I will be going back

The Fireworks show at Universal Orlando resort:    Let me begin by saying that i love both Disney parks and the Universal parks. We are spoiled with the highly creative shows en excellent quality at Disney. But please keep in mind that at Universal all fireworks are at close proximity to the audience, and there is no space for shooting high aerial fireworks as seen at the Magic Kingdom or Epcot. The fireworks products being used at Universal can be compared ( are the same) with the Fantasmic show over at Disney Hollywood studio’s. Those products are very expensive and of the highest quality. And is also the only product that can be used at that distance to the audience.  I think that the concept of the Cinematic spectaculair at Universal is briilliant. The music, narration, the movie-clips en how its blend into each other It has enough potential to give the audience goose-bums and take them on a journey into the Universal films. Overall i think its very entertaining and worth waiting for.  Perhaps a new pyrotechnic designer and show designer can do a better job and give the park and spectators a fireworks show that it deserves.

This is one of my favourite parks, I must say.... If you buy the express plus pass, you don't have to get in line at all (in Disney parks, you're granted with three fast passes, and that's all), so you can easily make through all attractions before the sun goes down. And you can buy beer almost everywhere, which is also pretty nice! :)

We went to see my sister that lives in Orlando. We got dropped off in the morning & saw everything. Did not go to Adventure Park. I mainly wanted to see Simpson Land in Springfield. It was so much better than I could've imagined! We had the most fantastic time. the ET ride was great too. There were a few rides we wanted to see that were closed but on the whole we walked through the whole entire place in one day. At 6 we met my sister at Hard Rock had drinks & dinner that was of course overpriced but good. Lots of walking so wear comfortable shoes. One park in one day is all you can do.

This is a nice park with some really fun rides. I especially enjoyed the Rip Ride Rockit. My children did several interesting character greetings. My daughters favorite was Shrek and Donkey. We got to them just before the Shrek show let out, so we didn't wait in line. They spent several minutes talking with her since no one was waiting. Once the show let out the line became extremely long. We will definitely return.

My husband and I went to universal florida today. We purchased an express pass which to be honest was not really worth the almost extra $100. We needed it for maybe 2 rides, otherwise it was a 10 min wait. It was nice that a few of the employees working the rides told us not to use it because in case some of you dont know if you get a general express pass you can only use it once per ride. Its not unlimited. Only purchase it if you go after noon. We got there for 9 and did the majority of the rides by 11am. I wish they had more coaster rides. My husbands stomach got quite bothered by the motion simulator rides and thats pretty much all they have. We didnt need an entire day on this side of the park.....now Island of Adventures may be a different story. We may actually spend all day there because its alot busier then universal studios florida. Weather was amazing! Not too hot, quite cool in the shades actually. I recommend the Fear Factor Live show. It was like the actual show. They have actual guests go for casting to compete. Quite enjoyable.

We had a great time. There is a little something for every age. Lines were somewhat long and it's annoying that you wait 45 minutes to an hour in line while express pass people keep flying by. Now I know they paid for that right but other parks, like Disney, seem to alternate pass riders and line waiters in a more efficient and equitable manner. Universal needs to work on that! The staff members were generally friendly even though many of them were quite young. This park needs more covered areas throughout the park where visitors can get out of the rain when needed.  On a side note, mainly for anyone from the park who reads this, when exiting the park in the evening we were approached by a young woman about taking a survey about our experience. We were moving quickly to try to make our shuttle bus on time so we wouldn't have to wait another hour for the next one. She asked nicely if she could ask us some questions and I very politely said, "No thank you ... we're in a terrible rush for the shuttle." She responded as we walked past with an extremely snide comment that I won't repeat here. This annoyed me because I was very polite to her and didn't just ignore her, but it really bothered me because I later had to take time to explain away her rudeness to my 7 year-old daughter who was also bothered by the incident. I try to find a silver lining by looking at it as a teachable moment for my daughter but it never should have happened.

Fifteen years after our first family visit to Orlando we repeated it, so now 3 young adults and 2 real grown-ups. This was the first park we visited during the week. Parking the car - we arrived early and selected premium parking which means it is on same level, no escalators and supposedly close to the entrance - we were fine but the close part isn't always so and you might decide not to spend the extra $6. Usual parking is $16, premium is $22. It is a long walk to the entrance. Bag search comes first - those without bags have a much quicker line. Then several moving walkways and through the boulevard of shops, takes about ten minutes to get to entrance. Buy tickets in advance. Buy Fastpass. Here fast pass holders have separate queues as opposed to in Disney when you book your time ahead. We saved about two hours of queuing by having fast pass. But note that buying fast pass in advance means you have to commit to a specific day to attend the park so cannot change mind if raining. We went at end of March - good weather though cloudy, this park was least crowded of them all, but also we went here on a Monday. Rides are a personal choice, but my favourite was the Minions one and then the old fashioned Twister show. Parade is a cacophony of noise and dance, better for the smaller visitors! Food outlets limited to burgers and fries but that's the same in all parks unless you are going to spend on fine dining! Enjoyed the day. (the options in trip advisor don't permit me to select a family group of adults - only family with young children or with teens, so have defined our family as friends!)

I've been to universal studios many times and I still love it here, it seems that the new despicable me and transformers rides have made it a lot more busy and the wait times are long (at least 60 minutes) I found this very disappointing as not known it like this before (maybe all parks have just got a lot more busy over the years). I wouldn't bother with men in black as it's dated but everything else is brilliant, I love the mummy ride and transformers is amazing!!!. If you have never been before, be ready for a long walk from the car park to the park.
Very long lines n to hot we paid to much money to be waiting so long! Fast pass that is only good after 4 is crazy! My kids can't be up so late!

Theme parks are always a gamble. We expected long lines and a bit of chaos, but we found neither here. We got Fast Passes with our hotel and we rode each and every ride to our hearts' content. For those unwilling to purchase a Fast Pass, we noted that the regular lines were all well under an hours wait as well. The Transformers ride was our favorite and nothing short of amazing. We had no trouble getting around and did not encounter any unruliness at any time. We also participated in Halloween Horror Nights and had a ball! We went on Thursday night and without a fast pass we were still able to see every house we wanted. The lines were a bit lengthy, but nothing over 45 minutes. We can't wait to come back!

After 4 faultless days at Disney we decided to buy fast track passes for the day at Universal at a cost of over $1,000! As the park opened we ran and I mean ran to the Harry Potter ride and had to wait in line for over 2 hours. We were told the queue was interactive with lots to do, that just is not the case. There are a few things to look at but the staff are shouting for everyone to keep moving so you don't get the chance to read any of the information. There are a few holograms but that's it. The actual ride is good but I am not sure it is worth the queue. After that things just went down hill, as the park filled up the queues got longer and longer even though we had the fast passes. Then in comparison to Disney there were queues for everything, toilets, drinks, food and rides. The staff were younger and could not guide you around as they seemed not to have been trained but just thrown in the deep end. To get drinks and ice cream took over half an hour. After lunch things got even worse and I went to customer service were I found many other disappointed people. In fairness they were apologetic and gave me a full refund and comped us a round of mini golf and some dinner, the mini golf was great. The highlight was Spiderman 4D and the Hulk, my youngest loved Dr Seuss and ET though I thought ET was very very dated. Overall I have rated this as poor because I just expect more, some of the rides were amazing and the customer care was good but when you have spent all that money travelling and on tickets you just want a day that will live long in the memory.

It does feel like many rides here are getting old.  I suspect the new Harry Potter themed area will give it a big lift.  Still worth a visit, but seems to have faded compared to it's sister park right next door!

Amazing experience. Does get very busy the parade is a bit minute in comparison to Disney and not all characters are there. Harry Potter gets ridiculously packed and cannot move and queues can be lengthly. Character meet and greet very good just watch out for the barging rude people they do not wait their turn be prepared to queue agressively at times.

What can you say about a Adventure that can take many tangents and lift the spirits in so many ways. Thankyou Universal for not just having a great place to escape and enjoy, but continuously upgrading your facilities and attractions, as I have visited your Studio's now 8 different times on my 21 visits to USA. My wife and I are heading back to Florida on May 07, for a Convention and hopefully we will get to revisit for the 9th time and see the improvements since our last visit in 2012.

We went to Universal on Apr. 22, 2014 with wife and son. My wife had prepaid for tickets. $108 CDN per ticket. We had heard that Universal was good and that if had lower wait times then Disney. Well only slightly. When we go there parking was good. We paid $5 more for "preferred" parking which we found out was only marginally better then the reg parking. Money grab. Getting in was fun. Long lines where people push and shove you to get in. Then the BS security check. Felt like I was a criminal getting into the park. Then the ticket check. They try and get your finger print and I'm like no way. I say here is my license to prove who I am. They were nice about it though. Then the mad dash to the rides. We had the Universal App that gave us ride wait times. The new minion ride was 85 mins? Brutal. All other rides were 10-25 mins so not too bad. Transformer, Mummy and Men in Black rides were good. They wanted $70 per person for there speed pass. In truth that class got you on almost a instantly still that is a gauge! Tip: go on as single riders and you can get right on. Most rides. Not all. Food was overpriced. And there is a gift shop after every ride which I found very tacky and it was difficult to get my 7 year year old through the store. All in all it was OK. Will I be back. Nope.

The parking situation here is atrocious. The lines were super long and because we feared the same on our way out we paid $5 extra for preferred parking.  The lines to buy tickets were insanely long. Once we got to the windows we found out why--the ticket sellers try and upswell you everything from the dining plan to the express passes, which took an average of 10 minutes per party. So buy online and in advance!  We purchased the express passes and while super expensive, I'm glad that we did. We never waited long for any ride and got to ride every ride in the park, which is great when you have two small children.  Every employee we encountered was great, so no, Disney isn't the only place that strives for amazing customer service. The food was also okay tasting and not insanely expensive. I was pleasantly surprised.  Lastly, the park was great for my two little ones as it's mostly 3D and 4D attractions. But being a roller coaster person, I was left wanting more than the two at the park.

My husband and I went to Universal Studios on Apr. 24th. We had gone to Islands of Adventure 2 days before, which I, personally enjoyed more. I found out that I get motion sickness on the 3D rides - sucks to be me, since Universal Studios rides are 90% 3D rides! Rock-It roller coaster was cool from the front seat. The Mummy was great because you had no idea where you were going to go. The food, snacks, and drinks were expensive like all theme parks. It was an enjoyable day out. Feet hurt, tired, hot (no water rides). Go to the animal show! It was great.

We visited the Universal Studios side of the two parks the day after we did Islands of Adventures. We enjoyed this side more as it seemed to have something for everyone (there was a 12 year old, 35 year old, 39 year old, and a 70 year old in our group). There were less people around which made moving throughout the park easier. Favorites of my family were the Simpsons area, Transformers area and ride, and the I love Lucy Tribute.

Enjoyed universal but sad to see jaws gone. Being replaced by another Harry potter venue that will connect both sides with Islands of adventure ( which I do not like). Too bad because jaws was a classic. Had fun on the old faithfuls such as ET, Disaster and twister. The shows are always good and loved Fear Factor live which I saw for the first time.

This park, along with Islands of Adventure, were for us, the best and most varied parks to visit. However we like thrill rides! Rip Ride Rocket was an experience - I did it once (and never again) but my husband and 10 year old daughter went on it about 15 times! Minion Mayhem is an absolute must (desire the queues - even with the Express pass). Shrek 4D was fun, as was Transformers (although Spiderman - which is similar - was better). Revenge of the Mummy, the Simpsons Ride and ET adventure were also good. Highlight however was watching the Mardigras Parade followed by Kool and the Gang performing live in front of the Rip Ride Rocket - fabulous!

Islands of adventure is better, but only because of the Harry Potter stuff. The Minions ride (Despicable Me) is a ridiculous wait for a ride that's absolutely not worth it. But it must be the newest ride there, because it's always an hour+ wait. We got there early one day and got on in about 30 minutes. Wouldn't do it again unless it was about a 10 minute wait. Transformers ride and revenge of the mummy are way better. Overall very good, although it seems all the ride technology is essentially the same (motion simulators).

I think we were rip off by paying the extra money for the fast line fees, at the end of the day you only save about 5 to 10 minutes to go to the express lane, everybody seems to pay to go over the fast line so there is really no fast line. The park itself is awesome, however if you go with a large group I feel the over charge for the fast lane is a rip off and it is not a fast lane. DON'T PAY THE EXTRA MONEY NOT WORHT IT!!!

I have been going to Universal regularly for several years and one thing I can count on is that there will always be some sort of construction going on at the park. I really enjoy the park overall and love the Springfield area but only appreciate coming here because I have an annual pass that makes it a good value.  I don't think it's worth the price of a 1 day ticket. Many rides like Simpsons and Transformers are great. I just watched the Beetlejuice show for the first time and was actually impressed at how good it was but they lack the attention to detail that Disney gives to the appearance of their parks. The streets just look dirty and old. A lot of the buildings have giant printed tarp coverings on them, I don't know why.  The quality of the staff has been declining over the years also, I guess that they don't emphasized friendliness in training and evaluations anymore.  Overall I still enjoy going and liked that the lines were reasonable when I went without needing an Express Pass but I hope that management takes a break from building new things after the Harry Potter section opens to improve the visual appearance of the rest of the park.

My wife and her sister had the bright idea of going to a couple of Florida Theme Parks. The second of the parks we visited was Universal Studios in Orlando which we hit on a rainy Friday. Ticket prices were $96 for each of us 4 – 60 plus adults for the single day. We arrived at the park and paid $22 for preferred parking (we thought that would be a great idea considering the weather). Save your money and just pay $17 as it is still a long walk to the parking garage. I will be brief. We skipped the major roller coaster rides as we are in our 60’s. When we were younger we enjoyed them, but it isn’t our thing now. Perhaps my sons would love them and, someday, my grand kid. We did hit the following (in no particular order): -Disaster (fun attraction with live audience “stars”). Don’t be afraid to volunteer. This is a fun show. -E.T. Adventure Ride : a gentle ride on “bicycles” for kids of all ages. -Revenge of the Mummy Ride: A roller coaster ride in the dark. Not violent, but good enough to get one person sick at the end of the ride. -Men in Black: A flat ground ride through the town and you have laser weapons. Shoot those bad guys and score points. I got over 3400 points. Beware, your vehicle will also get hit and when you do, you spin around… enough to get you sick if you get dizzy easily. -Shrek 4D: a boring three D show. -Terminator 3D: a more exciting three D show -Transformers 3D ride: another rather tame show/ride. -Beatlejuice Graveyard Review: A fun show with some ad-libbing. -Blues Brothers: I was on a mission from God to see this show but it was closed due to rain. -Twister: This attraction was closed for unknown reason.  Bottom line: Four senior adults spent $406 (not counting food and beverage and driving from Dunedin). While we did hit quite a bit of the attractions, I would have preferred to hit a really great French restaurant. I think this is for the younger set and they don’t give us seniors a break in the price (hint for Universal Studios).
This was my first time to Universal Studios and thoroughly loved it. Though I am not a fan of roller coasters, there are plenty of other rides to keep you entertained and enjoyed going on them.

What can I say; had higher expectations. Been about 20 yrs since last visit and the place looks like it had not been updated nor maintained since then. Tried to have my kids ages 5&9 meet a fee characters and they would close the line when we arrived. Tried to use my dining plan at an indoor place and the crowds and lines were unmanageable. Then when I did redeem at a pizza place the service was awful and took forever to figure out what the deal was with the plan.  Employees are in faded and worn out attire. No one seemed pleasant and happy to serve.  Ended with a stop for a slice of cake and coffee at the cafe near exit and both cakes tried were awful; worse than the cheapest blandest piece of cake ever tried. Waste of $10+.  Terribly missed the Disney experience. Never again.

Very nice place to visit for one day. Don't go more than that. Purchasing their VIP ticket is a must or you will hate your day. Rides were fun for a variety of ages. I liked how they had water misters everywhere. Must visit location in in Florida.

Each time I return to Universal, but this time it was a lot of people, this is the first time in February that I see so many people, the last five times I had to have my vacation before the big arrival for spring break.In the case where you have a lot of people, I recommend:  Take u ticket for two parks in two days and if you have a little money more then take fast-pass (~ $ 70 per person), but if there is the people then you'll be happy does not expect too much, attention even with fast-pass some attraction was still a long queue.  I recommend the following attraction: The Simpson, The mummies, Despicable Me... The Jaws are not available, a new attraction under construction.

As well as Island's of Adventure, this comprises one of the must visit places in Orlando, but if you visit Island's first, you'll get kind of disappointed of this one. Hollywood rip ride rockit is the best game in both parks, and it was a really pleasant surprise; being able to pickup your own music during the ride (over still a limited playlist) is one of the great features that also includes a 90º rise and a fast drop that's probably the most exciting drop in all both parks. Transformers is similar as Spiderman, and does a nice job, as well as The Simpsons Ride and The Mummy; however, there are some games that truly needs renovation, such as Twister, MIB, Disaster and ET, you can tell that these games where done several years ago and are out of date. Despicable Me is good but really crowded, expect at least an hour of waiting in line. If they could change the out of date games, it would be a lot better. However it is still enjoyable.
Brought my 8 year old & we all loved it. I've been to Disney World & I enjoyed it more! We are planning a trip back to Florida in December & I hope to have time to go back.

Went out there to enjoy the park, it was very good, some of the rides were very nice. The restaurant are okay. Meals and drinks are very costly plus paying for your tickets to get in the rides were costly also and if you want to move fast in the line was another large amount of $$$ for you to up grade your pass. This place is very costly and if you have a family it can make you spend large amount of $$$.
Hi are the fast passes worth it. We are going July 1-10? Please help any advice on certain days or if it's worth it would.be great going with 14 & 12 year old who love rides

Fun is available for people of all ages at this attraction. Tons of rides and things to see and do. Food is pricey as can be expected at a theme park. Be prepared to do lots of walking and standing in line.
This is just a fun spot! All of the movie rides were so cute! I had not seen many of the movies, but enjoyed the rides anyway! Love the Mummy rollercoaster!!

October 2013. We went to universal studios the Harry potter ride was my favorite. I am so glad they added this ride. We also went to the haunted houses and we had so much fun the only issues is the long lines. If I had to do it again. I would buy the upgrade to pass the lines

Went last October and had a great time! Thought it was good value for money, for the ticket, food and drink. All rides were really good, loved the 3d/4d Harry Potter and Spiderman rides! The staff were all very friendly and helpful, plenty of bathrooms around the parks and places to get snacks and drinks. Maybe not much in it for very young kids but plenty in it! Found it much better than Disney's Magic Kingdom! Would love to go back
The new attractions are amazing, the old ones are still pretty good, that rock it rollercoster is a thrilling ride, from shrek to transformers, all attractions worth the wait.

We enjoyed the new rides but were also happy to see some of our old favorites still in place like Men in Black. Enjoyed the character dances and easy engagements. Like the multiple selections of food options.
We did all the Disney Parks and then only 1 day here. This place is the best. If your kids are 8 or older spend your park money here ! Do the Fast Pass and have fun.

I purchased tickets through AAA for my honeymoon, when I got to the front gate I waited an hour to be told I dident new to be in the line becuase I already had tickets (unlike Disney) then after waiting another 30 minutes in the ticket scanning line I was told my tickets where not valid. I was then sent to guest services where I waited another hour before getting to the front just for them to tell me the tickets I purchased for 2 days get third free where not valid and would not be honored. The previous hour of people before me all had that exact same problem. I had to argue with them before they would honor the tickets and then I was told I was rude by the manager (mike) for complaining so much. They acted like they where doing a huge favor for me just for honoring my tickets that I payed for 5 months in advance. Their express pass is just a way to let the wealthy skip in front of everyone. They take your money and then try to throw you to the curb. The lines for all the adult rides where huge and I watched person after person from the express lane go in front of us. If you want a good fun family trip and aren't ultra wealthy go to Disney l. The customer service is better the staff friendly and it seems like they want you to have a good time as much as they want to make money hand over fist.

Overall this park was great. The only negatives with the Disaster "ride"...experience? Whatever that was, took a lot of time and wasn't much fun for myself and my wife; and ET. ET might be great for a really little kid that just watched the movie; if you're over age 11 it's probably not for you. The animatronics are horribly outdated and show visible signs of their age. 30 years ago it would have been a decent ride, I'm sure. But it needs updated or replaced. Transformers might be the best 3D experience ride ever, Despicable me was entertaining, the Mummy, Twister, T2, Shrek 3D were all fun. The Simpsons ride was really cool (that whole area was neat) and the Rock-it roller coaster is crazy. We missed Diagon Alley opening by a couple of weeks. Something to note, the characters for photo ops are on very short shifts, 10-15 minutes on 10 minutes off. So make sure you get in line immediately if you want a pic. The $60 package that includes all character and ride pictures is a great option if you're into pictures as souvenirs.

They mange the front gate very well. They had extra personal to get people in. The lines moved very smoothly. All the staff we encountered were friendly and very helpful. I have to give cudos to the child swap experience. This is the first time we used this because we now travel with small children. I am a grandmother of 59 and I still ride everything. We did not have to go back into line when it was my turn or my daughter's turn,they have a room for you to wait in. I thought that was awesome. Another thing with water costing $2.75 a bottle the cups of ice were free. I was able to share one bottle at a time between three grand children (that was awesome). At the end of most rides they had the characters there for picture taking, again that was a great idea. My favorite rides were Harry Potter &Transformers. Still love Despicable me, Mummy , Spiderman, Simpsons, Jurassic Park and Men in Black. Shrek in 4d was Awesome. It did not scare the grand kids. One more thing fresh fruit was a good idea. This was a good source of hydration in the heat. For the 100 years of Movies Light Show that night we had cupcakes as we watched the show. One day we stopped into Ben & Jerry's for ice cream, and we visited the old time soda fountain. Drug Store style on another day. one of our favorites is Mel's Drive In, we eat here every visit. I do not remember the name on the Isles of Adventure's side, we stopped into a bakery, My grand daughter had a funnel cake and I got the cheese cake. I was so glad I did not have to carry cash. I was able to use my debit card everywhere. And the Triple A card saved us a lot of money as well. We did not go to disney this visit to Orlando, but we do not feel like we missed out on anything. Thanks Universal for an Awesome vacation experience.
Me and my family had a great time there. I really enjoyed the 3d rides. It was adventurous. Will differently visit again!

I had the true pleasure of experiencing one of the Pre-Opening parties on Friday evening 6/20/14. I am an HP fan true to heart, read the books, saw the movies, purchased the movies and yes, I have a wand and robe! I have also been to the actual studio outside of London and have ridden the Ft. Williams train in Scotland, over the Glenfinnian Viaduct. Oh, almost forgot, personalized HP tour in London and 9 3/4 at Kings Cross Station. So, as someone who has actually seen or visited the "real" places I was apprehensive. I have been to Hogwarts and Hogsmead in Islands of Adventure, it allows you to experience the locations from the movie. This is a recreation of "real" sites...not an easy thing to pull off....move over "Mouse"...they have put the time and money into creating a totally immersing experience, the train ride...truly brilliant special effects. London street scene, very detailed, Grammercy Place, The Black Residence, good old "Creature"...brilliant! The shops in Diagon Alley, much larger than the small shops in Hogsmead, more true to size. No detail has been left out. The bank, Goblins, animated to reality. Butterbeer Ice cream delicious.... I unfortunately am not able to experience the bank ride due to motionsickess, but truly.....I did not need to go on the ride....it was such an amazing adventure to feel like you were actually experiencing the scenes from the movies....and know this park had made the commitment to give you the best possible experience...and witches and warlocks in full dress. I feel like they did justice to the story, they hightened the bar for a theme park experience....kudos to the creative team and the people who made the commitment to do the right thing by their guests! I know the lines will be long, but you will walk away with amazing memories. Yes...it's way worth it! And, no...this is not a paid advertisement...Orlando resident who has family, travels and loves Harry Potter.

we enjoyed being in universal parks , we want there for a week , the people are the best very helpful. I would recommend every one going at lease ones . we are planning to go back again. May be in march of 2015 .Had the best time ever.

What can I say about Universal Studios that 7,500+ folks haven't already said. It was a fun day for all. Lots of 3D/4D rides and "low impact" fun. Although I can no longer ride the fast paced roller coasters, due to spinal stenosis, the implementation of 3D rides allow me to feel the same thrill with out the impact.  Simpsons - Awesome. It is a roller coaster simulator. My wife and kids loved it. Men in Black - Awesome. It is like a drive through shooting gallery. Transformers - Great ride. The atmosphere leading up to the ride, may make it a little scary for kids who have not seen the movies. Shrek - Not bad. More geared toward younger children. They laughed throughout the whole ride. Mummy - Pretty good. I would only suggest that they move the child swap closer to the entrance. One of the kids started crying because the entry is really scary. Despicable Me - 80 minute wait. The line did not seem to go down all day long. Did not ride that. E.T. - I have a feeling this one will be retired soon. Still it was a great time to remember the movie. At a minimum, it gives you a chance to see what the "height" of technology was 20+ years ago.  Dinning - Best bet, exit the park and get some real food. I was also disappointing that the only way to use the "all you can drink" cups could not be activated until almost 11:00 am. So we walked around the park with our empty cups (purchased at Island of Adventure two days before). It is almost like a broken promise.  Having wanting to visit Universal studios for years, I was disappointed that the Jaws ride had shut down. But it is expected. The younger generation expects to be dazzled at every turn. Park operators have no choice but to shut down attractions which don't generate as much hype.

Bought a 3 day ticket with express pass. The express pass was worth it for us, but we really only needed two days to ride/see everything. If you have the stamina to stay all day, you could buy the 2 park pass with express and see it all (both parks) in one day! The rides are amazing, my favorites are Potter and Simpsons, because you don't need to wear 3D glasses. My only complaint is about the lockers next to each ride. Several times they would not re-open for us and we had to go find an attendant. The water rides are great. Jurassic Park and the flume one get you perfectly wet to tackle the hot weather. But if you go on the Barge ride, bring a change of clothes!!

Mixed feelings about US overall. Too many 3D ones for my liking though. I had express pass which is a must have. A few great rides: Dragon Challenge, The Mummy, Rip Ride Rockit (i LOVE this ride, it was the best one in the parks), Jurassic Park Biggest let downs were: Hulk, Spiderman, Dr Dooms Fear Fall, Ripsaw Falls  Frozen Butterbeer is delicious, though it could be shared as it's pretty sweet and rich. Lunch at Three Broomsticks was a good hearty meal

I went to the Universal Studios in Los Angeles and it was so much more fun and awesome! Being that I had such a great experience in L.A, I thought my family and I would go check out the one in Orlando but it was... mediocre. The best part of the one in Los Angeles is that they had the King Kong and also, the private tour. It's pretty much a regular theme park with added 3D rides. I would suggest skipping out of Universal Studios Orlando and taking kids to Disney instead!

Arrived before it opened so assumed we would beat the queues. Spent the first 30mins waiting to get on despicable me ride. Good ride. We then managed to get on the mummy twice without queuing - awesome ride! Thereafter the day became much slower. Twister a waste of 30 mins. Was looking forward to beetle juice however was pretty poor - Dracula needs to find a career that doesn't involve singing. Shame was much better 20 years ago. Simpsons ride was good - no actual Simpson characters to be found? Great Duff beers and Krusty burgers. Mixed bag really.

We visited Universal Orlando 23rd May to 6th June 2014 (2 adults, 2 seniors and 2 children aged 9 & 10). My mum has problems with her knees and walks with a stick so we went to guest services and they gave us an assistance pass which meant she didnt have to stand for long in queues which was fantastic. The Transformers ride was amazing and could have done again and again. The only ride which i found a bot dated was The Twister ride and i think perhaps has had its day but we didnt mind as we didnt have to queue. The Fireworks in the evening are great but it was raining the night we saw them so everyone huddled under the canpoy but the atmosphere was great. There are too many great rides to mention but highlights were... Transformers, Mummy ride, Rip ride rocket, despicable me, Simpsons, Horror movie makeup, Shrek 4D and ET. We ate at Mels drive in and the food was as you would expect from fast food but really tasty and not too expensive. We did buy the refillable drinks cup at the start of the day and when we went back on a different day we took it back with us ($8.99 then $0.99 refills) Really cant wait to return.

To take advantage of your stay and experience, I suggest to do the 2-park ticket, which is about $140. I paid $102 just for Universal Studios. If I would have known in advance that the difference was very minimal, I would have done the 2-park option. There are definitely a lot more roller coasters at Islands of Adventure. Universal did have great indoor rides that were too enjoyable. The Express pass was also worth it and saved a lot of time. I recommend to purchase that as well. It's about $70. Saves you hours from waiting in line. Lines with the pass were only about 15-20mins. Without it, you're spending double the amount of time, plus the heat. Overall, you're able to really take advantage of your time and get as many rides in as possible.

I absolutely loved both Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure. Definitely my favorite park over Disney world. Visited multiple times over a two week period and enjoyed every second of it. I have never been a big theme park rider, I'd usually be the bag holder but universal changed my mind. My favourite rides where the Harry Potter and the forbidden journey which was AMAZING and the equally amazing Transformers ride.  Stay for the fireworks and pyrotechnics show at the end of the day, this is an amazing showcase of movies with special effects. And if you love Pizza, why not check out Red Oven Pizza in City Walk. Quick and delicious!  The staff where friendly, the merchandise well priced and the facilities clean. I would return in the future, maybe to experience the new harry potter exhibit that is being opened this Tuesday.  I would recommend a multiple day pass, it can be very tiring and is quite nice to come back on multiple times both evening day. Also choose preferred parking if you do not want to walk a long way to get to the attractions.  Overall a thoroughly enjoyable experience and a highlight of my holiday.

We were a party of 7. 3 kids aged 8,10 & 15. Firstly parking is $17 and $22 for preferred parking which is nearer. For the additional 5 dollars it is worth it. You will also exit quicker especially when busy. We went 4th July and there was no special celebrations. There is a bag search on entry and fingerprint taken.  Get a park map on entry and this also shows you the times the characters such as optimus prime etc will be about for photos.  Queues are busy first thing and as everyone says the despicable me ride had the longest queue but for us it was a huge disappointment. Its great for the very young kids but you can see the people in front of you and the carts so it lacks the excitement of other rides such as transformers which is without a doubt fantastic. Do not miss the transformers ride.  Plan your trip to the park and what you want to go on. If the ride wait is too long, leave and come back later. They have a show at the end of every night with fireworks or cinematic display around 9pm. Its a bit cheesy but good to watch.  There is loads of places to eat and drink. The city walk is busy in the evenings and is between the 2 parks. When Harry potter diagon alley opens you can go from one park to the other on the Hogwarts express provided you have a 2 park ticket.  How you do this park is up to you. It can be done in 1 day but you would not get to do every ride due to wait times. Also as with all parks in Florida, rides are closed when lightning is about.  Some rides do not allow bags so if you don't have someone to leave it with then there are lockers or take a bum bag.  Wheelchairs are available and appeared abused as I saw several people share wheelchairs and jump in and out of the seat?  If you have small children a buggy is a must as they will tire very easily with the heat and walking.  At this time of year a rainmac is a necessity as most days there are storms but they never last long.  I hope you have as much fun as we did.

We did this as our yearly summer vacation and had an absolute blast! We loved the rides and managed our time well amongst the lines! The food was a little expensive but the park was a great adventure! Harry Potter land was by far the fave!

This is my favourite theme park. The Simpsons, the Mummy, T2 3D, ET and Transformers are all excellent and well worth the price of admission. The new Springfield area is also brilliant - try a Duff beer (alcoholoc) and Flaming Moe (non-alcoholic) at Moe's!

Both Universal parks were very well staffed. Due to the opening of Diagon Alley this week, there were record crowds. The staff was appropriately matched to the large numbers of people. Everything was organized and well managed.

The main reason was to visit both parts of the Harry Potter world and ride the train. The staff was excellent, and the two day park hopper with fast pass ticket was expensive, but unlike Disney the fast pass can be used over and over not just 3 rides like Disney. The staff played their parts well, and were helpful and fun even during the brutal Florida July sun and heat. A lot of walking, and some of the rides cannot handle fat people like me. I am not HUGE, and can fit any Disney ride, but they do have seats outside rides that you can try before going to the line. The fast pass was worth the price if you only have a day or two, food good for a theme park, but like Disney expensive. The people the employees make the park and experience, hopeful upper boss will learn these.

We travelled from park to park on the Hogwarts Express which wasn't as popular as we'd expected. Most people were there for the Harry Potter Diagon Alley opening. We got a return ticket so we trawled the rear of the park and returned only to find that it was another four hour wait for the Gringotts ride. Life's too short!

Excitement for anyone who loves rides! Rip rocket, the a Hulk and many more. The mummy ride is a normal ride without the upside down action. Great for people who like to ride but don't like to ride the big coasters. Cost is high go get in, so naked sure you have a full day to spend here. Great fir families with teens or couples.

Brought my family of 4 here and spent most of a day at this park. We liked it. We had a blast on the Minion ride and the Simpson's ride. We thought the Disaster ride was cute. My 8 year old son, loved the Twister "ride"? Overall it was a very good day. We did not know that on the day we scheduled to come to Universal Studios that Daigon Alley was opening to the public. So, needless to say we did NOT get to do that area. If we had wanted to we could, but it literally would have taken the entire day. That is how big the wait times were. I would say that some rides need to be updated like: The Shrek ride, the Twister ride, the Disaster ride, and the ET ride but that being said, our family had fun and was entertained. My kids also enjoyed the kids play area and loved the water slide! The MIB ride was fun and my boys enjoyed it. As a fan of the Simpson's I loved the Springfield area of the park.

We went on a long weekend to Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure. We had not been to either park in 9 years and the trip was really worth it. The rides were lots of fun and the number of indoor rides was greatly appreciated in the summer heat. We got into the new Harry Potter area (Diagon Alley) and it was lots of fun.

I ranked it a 3/5, and it is an entertaining place to go. The attractions are excellent but the wait times were ridiculous unless you buy the express pass (aka paying them a 2nd time).  What I learned: 1. the Universal app is a good thing to have - it gives wait times and allows you to plan your day. Download it and use it. There is free wifi in the park (although patchy) 2. you can bring in a small 6-pack size cooler. Bring lots of frozen water and small snacks (especially fruit, as that is hard to find in the park to make way for the chips and soda and cotton candy). Food there is pretty expensive too, so snacks are useful. **I learned that after 5 PM though, you are NOT ALLOWED to bring in any food, and they will turn you away. The entrance security guards may be nice and let you hide it in another bag, but the cooler has to stay** 3. Diagon Alley was well represented. Food in the Leaky Cauldron is quite $$$ - it was $100 for 5 adults, no alcohol. There are lots of places to do magic with the interactive wands ($55 each). The dragon on top of Gringott's spouts fire every 15 minutes. Great to see. They even made a Knockturn alley (the dark evil spot). 4. I agree with other reviewers that after paying big $$ to get in, it is ridiculous to see wait times of 300+ minutes for some of the newest, hottest rides, and after trying for 2 days, we still couldn't get into Gringott's ride. I'm not waiting 5 hours in line to ride the thing once, and waiting 100 minutes was painful enough for Despicable me. And paying for Express pass seems kind of wrong. 5. You can not take the Hogwart's express from park to park without a special 2 park pass. Again, this seems wrong to me and they should be connected. 6. Bring a rain poncho. For $4 at Publix, it is a bargain in Florida with all the torrential rains (and I mean torrential, with lightning) 7. **consider going to the park after 5:30 PM. All parking after 6 PM is $5 only (reg $17-22). The park empties out a lot after this time, and stays open until 10 or 11 PM. If you have your young kids take a nap in the afternoon, then the wait times are 10-20 minutes (or less) for everything. We waited less than 5 minutes for Dr. Doom and Spiderman, and <20 min for Harry Potter (Islands of Adventure). However, Gringott's was still not an option, as the ride stopped accepting new riders after 6:30, saying "full capacity". This was very very disappointing, after spending >$800 for our group, not being able to do everything.  So, if I had to do it over, I would either a) get there 30 minutes before the park opens and hit the most popular rides first or b) plan to get there at 5:30-6PM and ride until close.

Universal studios is a nice place to visit. We enjoyed all the movie attractions. Getting into Harry potter was nearly impossible, because they just opened it to the public last week. If you are able to go to universal studios you will have a great time.

This was our first time and it was amazing! We were lucky enough to go to the new area of Diagon Alley and it is breath taking! The new ride in that area is fantastic and defiantly worth the wait. The transformers simulator is really good as well as the mummy ride and disaster! Would defiantly recommend buying the freestyle unlimited drink as it is definitely worth the money and would defiantly recommend having an express pass as it makes your experience 10 times better!

This is the 3rd time I have been to Universal Studio's and I cant fault it.  Two parks to this location, Universal Studios & Islands of Adventure.  The rides you must go on are as follows:-  Islands Of Adventure The Hulk, Spiderman, Transformers .  Universal Studios Hollywood Rip (Rollercoaster), Simpsons, Mummy (it's not bad).  The park also shows TNA Wrestling shows which are filmed for TV. You can get free tickets to be in the audience on the day if you go to the Audience Ticket Centre at the front of the park as you go in. If you have never been, worth going to see just for fun.  A must is the Blue Man Group. This show you will have to pay to go into, its about £55/60 a ticket but well worth it.  Advise on park drinks & food (like all the parks) the stuff is over priced (compared to outside in Orlando). Take frozen drinks in with you and let them defrost during the day otherwise you will be spending £'s on drinks due to the hot climate.  Get your pictures with the characters, the kids love this ( I loved it)  You can purchase Fast Pass Tickets for around £55ish (I think). These are useful if the lines are really long, but I think that the cost is alittle cheeky as you have already paid to get in.
This is a must see if you go to Orlando. Our day in Universal was much better than the day we spent in Disney World. Perfect!

From great roller coasters like the rock it and the mummy to the fun of Simpsons,shrek,despicable me etc this place really does have something for everyone....but the show stopping part of the day was certainly the new diagon alley inside the wizarding world of Harry potter....Our 10 yr old daughter is Harry potter mad and she thought this was the best part of our 2 week holiday to Orlando!!!!a definite must see place....watch out for the dragon

Great park, lots of fun rides, down side, is the very very long queues , some over 2 hours, so you are forced to buy fast pass , which for a family of 4 will cost you £ 240 for one day only and does not included harry potter rides, feels like a ripe off. They also charge $5 for use of lockers to go on some rides. A great day out and some of the best rides but very very expensive.

Universal Studios is awesome. Had a great time. Rides for all ages. Wait time was not bad. New Harry Potter ride was incredible. If you are a Harry Potter fan you must go to Diagon Alley - it was awesome.

Got a fast pass for here and not for Islands of Adventure.. wish I did vice versa.  This park is 'ok' with some decent rides but Islands of Adv much better. Simpons ride made me nautious. Transformers, Despicable Me, the Mummy, Shrek 4D all had v small queues at opening (9am) so I would recommend not purchasing the fast pass in this park, providing you can get to the park at opening time.  Animal magic show (whatever it was called?) well worth it to see some familiar animals from the movies. Horror show was ok.

We did universal studio after spending 2 day in island of adventure. It was great. Not as adventurous as island of adventure but certainly exciting and fun. The new minions mayhem was a 2 hr wait as well as the rock it rip coaster but every thing else was under a half hr. Krustyland was cute. It's a great time. If you visit Orlando this is a must do

The best part about this park is Diagon Alley. It houses so much Harry Potter themes it will blow your mind. Butterbeer, Escape from Gringotts' Bank, Leaky Cauldron, Ollivander's Wand Shop, are all amazing places to take in. In the general park are themes like Simpsons, Transformers, among others. We had early park admission and park to park pass to Island's of Adventure package and highly recommend that if still available. The best ride and worth the wait is Gringotts. However, be prepared to stand in line if you don't plan ahead. With our early park admission we had NO line and were the first group to ride for the day. We also didn't have children along so we walked quickly with the crowd and ended up in the front of the line. After we got off the ride, the wait time increased to about an hour. The ride is totally worth it. Universal staff and employees are so helpful. I truly believe they want you to have a good time and will make sure you do. After every ride you complete they clap for you and raise a spirit of fun and excitement. Rip Ride Rollercoaster was a pretty aggressive roller coaster. There are lockers for backpacks, cellphones, wallets, etc. We had fanny packs and were allowed to ride with them but beware if you have any lose items (keys, hats, sunglasses) they will fall out. Transformers was a great ride. It was fairly mild and a lot of fun. There are also appearances by many park characters including Optimus Prime. We absolutely loved this park and for sure the highlight was Diagon Alley. We recommend by an interactive wand and using them along with the map to make spontaneous things happen in the Diagon Alley window shops. There are plenty of cool misters along with bathrooms and air conditioned shops/restuarants.

After visiting Universal Studios Fla, my immediate impression was that there was no need for Guantanamo Bay because there's Universal Studios.  The good: The rides are fun, especially for older kids. I really liked the Simpsons area because I'm a huge fan. The Harry Potter area was entertaining as well, but again you'd have to be a fan. The Transformers that they bring out for pictures were very realistic.  The bad: The lines were terribly long when we visited. The wait was more than an hour at every ride. The "fast pass" should be renamed "slightly less slow pass". A lot of people upgraded to the pricy fast pass (about $90), so you'll still be in line for a while. Long lines and malfunctions are a common complaint with the reviewers, but they still give the place 4-stars, which makes me wonder if people had overheated during their visit to the park.  The ugly: What would happen if every airline scheduled a 9 am departure at an airport? Come to Universal Studios and find out. The crowd to get into the park in the morning is crazy (see attached photo), all because of a small bag-check area. I'm surprised that no one has been trampled to death.  For me, the pain wasn't worth the fun, and Universal is worst in managing crowds compared to the other theme parks. The wait time is so long that it's simply not a good value. But, there must be something there, because everyone keeps going back.

We were on our honeymoon, so we knew we were going to spend a lot of money if we wanted to have the best time. But jeez, something like $130 per adult?! Then we made the decision to upgrade to a Fastpass, which was an extra $69 each I think it was. Such a massively expensive day! But we didn't want to have to do a 2 day pass, so figured it was worth getting the fast pass. The security/bag check area before actually getting into the park was appalling, way too overcrowded - this can be improved! We were surprised that Universal Studios wasn't as crowded as we thought, and then got worried that the fast passes were a waste of money. But once we got to specific rides, like the ET ride and the Transformers 4D ride, it was definitely worth it, people everywhere. The Simpsons land area was so awesome, we loved going into Moe's Tavern and taking photos! Lots of great rides - the ET one was super cute and reminded me of my childhood, Transformers 4D was AMAZING, Shrek 4D was also really cute. We did spend more time over at Islands of Adventure though (if you only have 1 day, get the park-hopper option) and there were bigger rides there. But I liked being able to do both of them at once, because they were both quite different. The only thing we missed out on was a stunt show, which I remember seeing at Universal Hollywood in 2001 and would have been cool. A great day overall!

I enjoyed my third visit to Universal Studios en Orlando, however I do not think I will go back because there is so much to see and do that I was too exhausted in the evening. It seems I am getting old! I made the mistake of purchasing entrance for two parks, and I hardly was able to enjoy just one. I would recommend to purchase at least two-days entrance, otherwise you will not have time to do what you paid for. Please take the best walking shoes you have, sun protection hat/umbrella, and cream. If you do not want to wait too long for a ride just go single. It is a great decision. Have fun!

The hype for The Harry Potter attractions at Universal was huge so we were on a mission to see what all the fuss was about. We got to the park at 7am and went straight to Diagon alley. Thinking we were ahead of the queue we were told by the attendants we had a 2 hour wait... To our horror 2 hours turned into 4, the lines seemed to move quickly to start but the ride kept breaking down so we were left sitting on hard floors for up to 45 mins at a time. It was utterly utterly awful. People were treated like herded cattle , no information or updates on what was going on, and because you cannot see how long the queue is, you keep in the line. There was no option for express passes on any of the new Potter attractions only the old re purposed roller coasters . Whilst the attraction itself was good, the awful queue experience completed negated any positive memory . It really is an awful awful way to treat people and completely ruined the Universal theme park experience for us. If you have 4-5 hours of your life to waste sitting in searing heat for an approx 7 min ride go for it. It's bad enough for adults but even worse for poor kids...For die hard Potter fans the ambience and attention to detail in Diagon alley may be worth it for you. I certainly would not recommend it to anyone else . The rest of the universal rides were awesome in particular the Mummy, Spider-Man and Despicable me , however the morning experience really ruined our day. Sort yourselves out Universal, do not bring these poor unsuspecting tourists on the promise of great things to your attractions that break down constantly and make people wait 4 hours in Florida heat... It's utterly dispespectful and a complete con!

Knowing that we were going in the middle of their busy season, we knew it would be busy.  IF you are going in peak time, YOU must utilize an express pass..If not, you will spend a chunk of your time in lines.  IT was packed!! But we wouldn't have missed this!!  The lines for Gringot's were over 2 hours, a express pass is required! One of our favorite rides!  Do not miss the Hogwarts Express.. Very cool.. Take it more than once to see the things you missed!  The teenagers loved Mummy and Transforrmers..  We did Terminator at the end of the day.. There was hardly anyone there.. It i, well, a let down after seeing the newer rides..

My first time checking out Universal Studio and it was great! Had a lot of fun with much to check out! I don't have an amazing enough adjective to describe the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. Spent our entire day here checking out both sides of the park. Friendly staff as well.

OK, you know before you go to any of these parks that you are about to get ripped off. You pay a fortune to get in, and if you want to do anything other than spend most of your day in queues you probably have to spend almost the same again on a fast pass. If you are going to Orlando with kids you don't have much choice but to put up with it, but it's not something to look forward to!

Just returned from a 3 day Universal trip. I reviewed Royal Pacific Hotel already, so if your interested in that hotel feel free to read the review.  I traveled with my two teenage daughters and overall I thought Universal was allot of fun. It is definitely a park for the older/teenager age group due to the type of rides at both Universal parks. I went in the summer so it was very crowded and very hot. I knew that going in so I stayed on site to access the early entrance to both Harry Potter attractions and the express pass. Honestly that being said if we didn't have those perks I don't think it's worth going in the summer. Even with the early access to both Harry Potter rides/attractions we still had to wait and the place was packed. Granted, we did not have to wait as long if we didn't have early access but we still had at least a 30- to 40 minute wait to ride both attractions. After riding the new Gringotts ride in the morning we came out and there was already a 240 minute wait!! Honestly the new Gringott's ride is not worth the long 4 hour plus waits. It is a very short, roller coaster type ride that is in 3 D. Try the single rider line, you will get to ride it much faster.  The Hogs meade ride was much better and much longer. More thrilling and worth the 30+ minute wait. Both areas are very well themed and fun to walk around in, just get there before the crowds!! We did ride the train and it was fun and the wait was not that bad, took us longer to walk to the ride through the pre loading area.  We used our express pass for all the other rides and it was definitely worth it. We were able to ride without much of a wait, especially in the morning. I still feel the Mummy ride and Spider man rides are the best.  Stay on site if you can, go early, use your express pass and you'll have fun.

I went to Universal Studios and Islands of adventure with my husband as part of our Honeymoon. We purchased the park-hopper ticket so we could go to both parks, and also because we wanted to be able to do the Harry Potter Hogwarts Express train ride that goes between the parks (you must have a park-hopper ticket to go on this). We also went for the Fast Pass Plus option which gave us the opportunity to go through the fast pass queue on any ride as many times as we wanted. (Be aware that currently the fast pass it not redeemable on the 2 Harry Potter rides, Escape from Gringotts and The Forbidden Journey, or on the Hogwarts Express train). I would definitely recommend getting tickets to both parks as they are equally good and it's well worth the money.

This is a great park, plenty to do. Buy your tickets online to get the best deals. The fast pass is arou d 50 dollars per person which in my opinion is overrated as the cues were long everywhere. There is a massive fuss over Harry Potter there which means if you want to go on these rides be prepared to cue for 3-4 hours. Good park, a must if staying in Orlando.

The Rides in this park are phenomenal, especially the " Harry Potter Ride " the simulator's used in the park are exceptional, unbelievable infrastructure. The Roller coaster rides are Jaw dropping. I recommend everyone to get an express pass, if you don't wanna wait long(1-1'1/2 Hrs) for every ride in the park and its better to get the express pass along with the Park tickets online, rather then getting it there in the park as the express passes are little bit expensive when you want to purchase them in the park. Me and friend covered the 2 parks in one day, with express pass.  I love this place, I would definitely recommend this, and of course TRIPADVISOR is the best \m/

Like what I said in the title... no other places can beat the Universal Studio park in Florida... Then again Florida really has the best theme parks in the world... A week does not suffice... although Universal Studios is more for kids because the rides aren't that terrifying... the movie-type feel gives you thrills already! ;)

Overall good experience. The downfall was the time to wait in line.. The Minion ride was 3 hours at one point. You don't have time to visit both parks in one day. But it was fun and the whole family enjoyed. The Simpson's ride was awesome! Transformers was pretty great too!!!

I love it here at universal!!! There has been some fantastic new editions to the park like the transformers ride and diagon alley they are both fantastic aswell and lived up to what we where expecting. I would advise anyone who wants to dodge the queues to get there either early in the morning or late at night as the queues are quieter at these times of the day. Me and my family love it here perfect for the whole family

This was my second time attending, but the hot sticky weather was difficult to get around! the queues for the rides were around 45 minutes which isn't too bad and the experience is worth it! the food is quite expensive but quite tasty if you find the right place. The staff are very friendly! very welcoming. recommend to anyone in the area!

It's been 5 years since we last visited Universal and it the interim Universal has stepped up their game. Not only have they add great new attractions but more importantly I felt there was a real up-grade in the level of service. Disney has always been the benchmark, but Universal has matched them. The cast members are friendly, courteous and extermly helpful. I am handicapped and everyone went above and beyond to make my visit pleasurable. One area Universal now has it over Disney is parking especially for handicapped. Two times on my visit to Disney I wasn't able to use the handicap lot and instead had to use a overflow lot. One time I almost didn't make it back to my van because my batteries were low and I was parked so far away. Universal on the other hand has more spaces available in covered garage.  The new attractions are now on a par with the best of Disney World. The Harry Potter areas are like stepping into the movies. The attention to detail is unbelievable. There are costumed cast members interacting with the guests. And there are spots around Diagon Alley where purchasers of magic wands can do magic. The crowds were huge though so if your are bothered by that you need to wait awhile for the novelty to wear off. We ate at the Leaky Cauldron and the food was excellant. My only complaint with food at Universal is that there are no full service resturaunts. Make sure you try the butter-beer.  Also new to me this time is Springfield, home to the Simpsons. This was a real fun area. With Moes Tavern serving Duff's beer, the Quicky-mart, Duff Brewry Beer Garden. You find yourself right in with the characters. My wife raved about Krash thru Krustyland that replaced Back to the Future. ( I got a call from work and didn't get a chance to ride).

We've visited both parks in 3 days, and had time to make all the attractions, some of them more than once. 3-day ticket is a good deal, but remember you must choose the park hopper option to visit more than one park a day. If you didn't choose this option, you won't be able to take the Harry Potter's train that links both parks!

We could not understand how people could spend a full day here unless they stood in a long queue for every ride. Mostly just shops and overcrowded places to eat which we thought were overpriced. Certainly not worth the entrance fee.
Spent a few days here, lots to do, queues not too bad outside of school holidays, prices for food not too bad (considering it is a park!) great restaurants at city walk on the way out too.

We visited yesterday. As it is our vacation, we opted to sleep in and arrived at around 10am. The first hurdle was the tickets at the gate. Skip this unnecessarily, ridiculously slow process if you can and buy on-line. We watched people spend 30 minutes at the window getting their park questions answered. It was hot and annoying. :P  Our group compromised me (mom) and the two kids , 13 and 16. We decided to do Universal in a day-both parks. We knew this would require fast pass, so $750++ later we had our tickets and were moving through the park. Some of the best rides at Universal (Spiderman, Harry Potter, Gringotts, Transformers and Simpsons) all use 3D technology that in the past has made my head hurt and my stomach iffy. This time I came prepared and took a low drowsey version of Dramamine. It made all the difference. I had ZERO issues on any of the rides this time.  We started our day in Islands of adventure and circled the park until kings crossing, then took Hogwarts to the Studios, did all the great things there and then took Hogwarts back (different ride each way on Hogwarts). We noticed that the Fast pass was not as fast as it once once. We still had 10-15 minute waits on some rides that in the past were zero wait, but using it was still a huge improvement over the 80 minute waits those without it were enduring. Our three longest lines of the day were Gringotts (about 1 hour 45 at around 2:40 pm), Harry Potter (about 40 minutes at around noon) and then getting the tickets to start the day which was around 40 minutes at 10 am. All in all not too bad! One of the great things about Universal is that so many of the lines are indoors in air conditioned areas and if not, they are all shaded. My pale family and I didn't get burned at all after 11+ hours in the parks. Few other quick notes. Water rides at Universal are very very very very wet. Popeyes in particular seems to be designed to get you soak and no, your poncho will not prevent that. The reason the line is ten minutes long? Lots of people don't want to get soaked. Still my kids LOVE that ride. If you have neck or back issues, think twice about some of the 3D rides. My husband stayed home for this trip because his hockey injury to his neck and jerky rides are not a great mix. There is a charge for parking at this park but those complaining about it have me laughing. It is $17 for COVERED parking that gets you within walking distance to the parks (no trams). In Chicago you would pay twice for that!! We opted for the $24 premium parking to get a little closer. In hind site,that saved maybe three minutes of walking so probably not worth it. The food here is decent as theme parks go, you have to look around. Some spots are better than others. All are expensive. We did lunch at the rib place by jurassic park. Our lunch was $55 for two burgers with fries, 1 rib with fries, three drinks and three desserts. Not horrible. We had to take one of the burgers back because it was undercooked and they handled it smoothly and with grace. We didn't spend much else on food because we brought some snacks and water, but you could drop some serious cash here if not careful. All in all, in summary. We went in August during the height of Potter mania and found the crowds fine, the lines fine, the weather not an issue and the prices, well pricey. Its the premium theme park in Orlando and we paid more for some convenience that was well worth it. Oh and we still got to sleep in and ride/see everything we wanted. :)

My family of 4 including myself, my husband and kids aged 11 and 9 went to Universal with another family. Of course wait times were very long but my husbands medical pass made it possible to avoid all of the lines and we were able to "fast pass" Harry Potter and the escape from Gringotts. The ride was rather disappointing and actually not worth the wait if we would have waited. The Wizarding World is a must see and detail was excellent. The Harry Potter ride at Islands of Adventure was much better. Despicable Me broke down while we were on the ride, Shrek 4D shoppes mid show, we got stuck on Men in Black for about 20 minutes and also got stuck on ET. The day was a disaster and I'm not sure what was going on with the rides that day. Revenge of the Mummy was great but Twister and ET are lacking and need to be replaced. They only have 1 big roller coaster. Of you are looking for fun and excitement for your money then visit Islands of Adventure

Universal Studios (and Islands of Adventure) are much better than the Disney Parks, from the ease of parking and being able to walk into the parks, the proximity of City Walk, the on site restaurants being a million times better than those in Magic Kingdom or Hollywood Studios, the way the park is organised with very little "dead" space between attractions, Universal has done it right, but it could be much better.  Why they don't offer fast pass tickets on the big Harry Potter rides is a mystery, making people queue for upwards of 3 hours to get on the Escape from Gringotts ride must be a lost revenue opportunity for them, and be aware that Diagon Alley and Escape from Gringotts get stupidly busy.  Universal offer an hours access before official opening hours for resort hotel guests, so even if you get there at 8am for general admission and speed walk to Diagon Alley you'll find a 30 minute queue just to get into the Alley and another 3 to 4 hour queue for Escape from Gringotts.  We had a shockingly bad experience on our first visit, where we arrived at the park for 8am, entered the Gringotts queue at 8:05am and it was supposed to be 150 minutes, after 4 hours we were still about 30 minutes (estimated) from getting on the ride when they announced that the ride was temporarily closed due to technical difficulties and wouldn't reopen for at least 45 minutes. So we left, picking up complimentary Express Pass tickets for the ride as compensation. After some googling I found out this happens every day! The ride is so advanced and cutting edge that when something goes wrong, they pretty much have to reboots the whole system, and it takes 20 minutes to do that!  So we went for lunch came back and used the Express Pass tickets to get to just before where we'd been when we bailed. It still took c 45 mins to get on the ride from there, because everyone else who'd done the same was using their free passes.  The queue once you get inside the bank is good, the main hall with the goblins is great, the tunnels quite good and the show with the goblin and the Weasley is good. The ride itself is awesome, clearly not worth 4 hours queuing up for (nothing is) but is just about as immerssive into Harry Potter that you can get, and is marginally better than Forbidden Journey (but the queue is not as good) because Gringotts is in 3D so when Nagini attacks....you jump! A lot.  The rest of Diagon Alley is well done, the little wizarding points for those who buy the interactive wands are great and very interesting. Borgin and Burkes and Ollivanders are ace. The Leaky Cauldron is good also. Watch out for fire from the Dragon atop Gringotts.  Outside Diagin Alley you'll find the Knight Bus complete with Stan Shunpike - go and talk to him because the rasta head talks to you and is clearly voiced by someone who can see you as it will interact with you about your clothes and call you by your name. There is the Order of the Phoenix House, and a few other things.  Kings Cross Station is well done and the visual effect of walking through the wall at 9 3/4 is great. Hogwarts to Hogsmeade is brilliant, watch out for Dementors! The journey each way is different, so make sure you do both if you have duel park tickets (which as a Potter fan you must get).  Away from Potter other good things in Universal Studios we went on:  Rip Ride Rocket Rollercoaster - great, worth a 45 min queue The Simpson Ride - good, wouldn't queue for more than 30 mins for Men in Black - average - 15 mins queue max ET - old and weak - 10 mins Revenge of the Mummy - scary, our 8 year old son screamed! worth 45 min queue Minion Mayhem - Funny and good, huge queues though, not worth more than 45 mins Shrek 4D - OK - 20 mins max Beetlejuice Graveyard Revue - poor - don't bother.  We ate at Lombards Seafood Grille which is a proper table service restaurant and very good!  One negative note, we had reason to complain, as we'd been told we could get access to the park from 7am from 1st Aug, so we could get into queue for Escape from Gringotts early as some compensation for the 5 hour wait we had on the first time, so after complaining at Guest Services (and getting the brush off) I emailed Universal. After some toing and froing I was offered some Express Passes for another visit, and upon collecting then was told they were NOT valid on Harry Potter rides (FJ and EfG) despite the telephone conversation the previous day not mentioning this at all, which was rather annoying considering the issue arose due to a fault with EfG. Guest Services couldn't help me further so I had to wait half an hour and ring customer services again, I was then told that she "would make an exception and do me a favour by allowing me to swap two of my Express Passes for ones that would work on EfG" I was not happy at now having to go back to Guest Services and at the fact that she said she was doing me a favour, so I asked to speak to a manager in Guest Services and Corey did the right thing and gave us Express Passes for both of the big Potter rides. Took 3 emails, 3 telephone conversations and 3 face to face conversations to finally get someone who delivered good service!

The new Diagon Alley attraction is awesome, and is actually much better than Hogsmeade. The lines are long to get in the stores and ride, but well worth it. I'd highly recommend getting a hotel room on site, because you get 1 hour early admission into Diagon Alley. (Also, you get free Express passes for everyone but they aren't accepted at Diagon Alley; they'll help a lot in the rest of the parks though.) Get to the line for Escape from Gringotts as soon as you can, because even with a 1 hour advantage you will easily have a 1-2 hour wait! If you don't have that advantage you will have a 4 hour wait, easily. The ride itself is only ~2 minutes, though it is exciting and moderately fast.  The other rides are good too. I couldn't ride Rip Ride Rocket because there was lightning. I loved Mummy; it was indoors so weather doesn't affect it and it was quite thrilling, more thrilling and high-speed than Gringotts.  They have a lot of 3D rides/attractions, such as Shrek, Simpsons, Transformers and Despicable and the like. If you do these all in a row your senses will feel over-stimulated at the end. Most of these are suitable for small children too.
My family are all big Potter fans so Diagon Alley and all things Potter were a huge hit. Be prepared for a long wait at Gringotts. I must admit I thoroughly enjoyed this part of the park as well.

What a fantastic park like everything in orlando done so much bigger and better than anything the UK has to offer. The theming is excellent and the rides are awesome. The rides seem to jump to life great experience.

I'm 22 and the last time I was at universal studios I was 10. Went there and did almost every ride. Only rockit was closed due to the weather. I did not have express passes but went into single riders line everywhere it was available. My favorites were the Transformers and the Mummy. Choose less crowded days or ue single riders line to save the money of express passes.

Our family had a lot of fun for 2 days here, but we only were able to ride a few rides. For over 200 per person for a 2 day park hopper, then another $100 if you want their express pass, that is a lot of money for a family of four. It was fun to do (customer service was great), but we probably won't do it again.

Firstly rides were amazing my favourite was despicable me minion mayhem there were plenty of restaurants and the food was great park was clean and tidy and staff were extremely kind only thing I didn't like was one of the rides which was twister as I felt it was dated but apart from that amazing.

This park doesn't have the "magic" that other nearby parks have, but they make up for it in "cool". They have great rides, from kids to the adrenaline junkie, and very funny shows for everyone.  The most amazing parts of Universal are the two Harry Potter attractions. The attention to detail, and the special effects are so much like the movies, that you can not possibly enjoy all of it in two or three days.
