You can buy wands, robes, butterbeer and almost anything else. The actors they place here and there go above and beyond, especially that mean witch at the entrance to Knockturn Alley. Get the Express Pass and Park to Park pass. Definitely worth the money. You can also buy beer (real beer) in the park, which makes for a much more enjoyable day when the Florida heat takes over! Go see Universal!
Outside of standing in long lines EVERYTHING about Universal Studios was AMAZING!! The Transformers ride, Diagon Alley, Spider-Man...I can't wait to return.

We visited this park yesterday and got there early to avoid the queues. Obviously alot of people had the same view but that was ok. i didnt expect it to be empty due to being such a popular park. We paid 17 dollars for parking which i find high but can understand as they need to maintain the park and pay for the staff etc, i used the tactic off turning right as soon as we entered as most people head for the first ride which is the Despicable Me ride. Within the first hour we managed to complete three rides including the Simpsons ride which was brilliant and MiB. The disaster ride was broken at first but by the time we went back it had finished. The average wait time for us was about 30 minutes. Dragons Alley was too long 150 minutes so we didnt bother. Despicable Me was the longest wait 60 minutes but was well worth it as it is the best ride in the park. We even managed to watch the Beetlejuice show. All in all we had a fantastic day and thought it was far better than next doors Islands of Adventures.

I went to Florida 3 times in the last 20 years, going to all the parks. I found it really clean and great value (pound was strong against the dollar, first time 1998). Everyone could not do enough for you, so happy and friendly! The food was excellent, anything you wanted and at any time. You need to have your I.D with you all the time for drinks, as they need to see your age (the server is responsible legally if you get drunk in their bar). Would go back, this time I will take my daughter, but children need to be older to experience it fully (12 and over should get a lot out of it).

We queued for far too long! It broke down 5 times while we were queuing. The ride it self was a very poor relation to the ride in the other park. It last 3 minutes and didn't thrill or excite, so when asked if we wanted to queue again on the fast track our group voted with its feet and went back to the other Harry Potter ride in the other park!

I have never been to a visitor attraction where every member of staff has no interest in visitors offering zero customer service. How can you queue for 4 hours to go on a Harry Potter ride in the 90 degree sun and not see a single member of staff . On arrival we were told that both parks closed at 6 pm for a private function. We checked with two other staff who confirmed they had just been told that both parks closed at 6. Then at 6 having changed plans we found out only one park closed at 6.All staff appear totally disinterested and any question asked appears to be a major inconvenience to them . Universal have a lot of lessons to learn from Disney

Surprised our kids (girls: 19, 15, 11) with a four day trip to Universal. This was our first time here and we had a great time.  Wizarding World of Harry Potter: Diagon Alley reviewed separately. All food is also reviewed separately.  Get there at early open (we went to Islands of Adventure and took the Hogwarts Express over). Head straight to Diagon Alley.  Despicable Me was such a cute ride; 3D animation was awesome. Took a lot of bumps but I laughed a lot.  E.T. Adventure you can tell has seen better days, but who doesn't love the little alien? If anything, take some time to cool down.  I can't do roller coasters: so no reviews on those for me. Sorry!  Shrek was not all that cool, but I was never a fan of the movie.  Twister Ride-it-Out was disappointing. Stood in the back row and was wondering when the show was going to actually start. Thought it would have been a lot more than it was.  Transforners ride was loud and bumpy, and thankfully a tall person was in front of me, so the full effect of 3D was lessened.  I thought the Horror Make-up Show would have been more interactive instead of a little skit, but the audience participant made it worth the time.  Now, The Simpsons ride was (outside of Harry Potter) was the ride of the park. I haven't watched The Simpsons in a long time and my kids have never watched them, but the wait was 10 minutes so we went on it. I laughed my BUTT off the entire time. I had no idea the ride was going to be what it was, which made it ironic and funny, since I'm not a coaster fan. Best ride, IMO.

I like this park, but I always feel like they are just missing the boat. So, I gave them an average rating. We got park to park w/ fast pass as we were only going there one day. My daughter is 9 and does not like the scarey rides so that eliminates a lot right there, which is fine. Fast pass is still good for the 300 times we rode "flight of the hippogriff" and the woody woodpecker coaster. Harry Potter world is packed. Diagon Alley is packed. We expected that. We got into Diagon at 9:30 in the morning and the gringotts like was a 4 hour wait. We didn't want to ride it so we didn't really care. No fast pass for the castle, gringotts, or Hogwarts Express. Hogwarts Express is super cool and you ride it several times if you're going back and forth between parks. The line moves fast, but they should allow fast pass for this one. Here's where I think US falls short - the wizarding world of hp has so much potential for character involvment. The should have wizzards and muggles walking around, really create an ATMOSPHERE. That's where they fall short - atmosphere. Some of the employees play the role, but for the most part they don't. It would make a difference in the details. The new wands allow kids to do spells throughout the park. I think our wand cost 44.00 and it's fun to do. I think they need to find a way to make it easier because you see the parents taking the want and finishinig the spell. They have witches walking around helping, but they don't maintain a "character". I want to get off that darn train and have someone yelling "first years this way". Come on Universal make this a better experience! In Kings Cross Station, they should have street performers, people pushing luggage, etc. Even add some of those spells for kids to do while the wait in line...Butterbeer is awesome. The dragon on Grigotts spits fire - wait for his growl, he spits it right after that. The rest of hte park is ok, but again, it just seems to lack in the details. We ate at the seafood place on the dock - it was ok. Nice break in the day, but I wouldn't go back. The food options I didn't find to be great at either park. HPW has weird food and fyi, no soda in HPW. Which makes me like JKR even more :-) My other gripe is that they don't seem to have good merchandise items. They could sell tons more of this stuff if they had better options. Who do they have making this stuff? Whoever it is must not be a fan. There are so many cool shirts they could sell but they all stink in my opionion. I could not find one single hogwarts shirt that I would buy. I'll find a better one somewhere online. I did buy a cool coffee mug at the airport - never saw it at the park. Overall, it's a fun day, but I don't need t go there too often.

More roller coasters, love it, enjoyed all of them even though some were a bit dated, the characters wandering around were really good, again yes it was busy & yes you had to queue, but didn't bother me!

We loved universal studio's in previous years but this year I was disappointed with the trip service and then with the park service. the tickets are expensive enough that we were charged a fee to rent a locker to go on a ride, one of the parks closed early on a busy saturday night and most of the restaurants either ran out of food towards the end of the night or were closed altogether so we had to go to a more expensive restaurant. it use to be that Universal was a better vacation than Disney price wise but not anymore.

Visited Universal Park on a park hopper pass and had a fantastic time. The Harry Potter Diagone Alley was the most amazing rendition of the shops and the in and out streets off the alley gave you the feeling of being on the movie set. The park has some incredible rides like the Transformer and the Dispicable Me, the Men in Black, ET and Gringots Bank. I loved the Dragon atop Gringots Bank that spews fire balls. The park is very friendly and very clean for as many people as visit daily. I liked that they post waiting times for the lines so you knew how long you would be waiting. The Islands of Adventure side is as much fun and with Hogsmeade and the Castle and Lost Continent and Jurrasic park are amazing. Prices are comparable to other theme parks.

Although I was definitely disappointed that the classic Jaws ride was missing, there is still a great mix of modern and nostalgic in this park. By far the best ride in the park is Revenge of the Mummy, the enclosed coaster definitely surprises with its twists and turns.

We went to Florida to take my 9 year old daughter to The Wizarding World of Harry Potter The week after Diagon Alley opened. We expected long lines and alot of people but we still had a great time!  The interactive wands made the trip worth while and I love that everyone stays in Character in whichever part of the park you are in. Frozen butter beer, Fish and chips, earwax flavored jelly beans and all of the Harry Potter clothing you want. Both side of the park were great the rides on the Hogwarts Castle side we awesome, The coolest thing we were able to do was go into Diagon Alley at night. Dragons breathing fire, lanterns lighting up with a flick of the wand, the creepy knockturn ally and Borgan and Burkes. If you are a Potterhead this is the place for you.
We came here Feb 2014. No queues, not too crowded. Had a whale of a time. Ticked off the bucket list :)

My family and I attend universal 2 to 3 times a year because of all of the special programs offered day and night for every person in the family. With its close proximity to several dining and extended activity options...it is the perfect vacation for everyone! What we do is stay always within a 2 mile radius of the park (most close hotels have free shuttles) to save us on parking fees or cab rides. We pack light lunches as most of the hotels have small kitchenettes... This helps to cut the cost of food as there's no use going to the parks without the vip pass..... and this can be pricey...it's what you need though to get the absolute most out of your vacation. Short wait times on rides, exibits, and your made to feel as though your attention span is consistently entertained! For the pass, our family also carries lanyards to hold onto our passes, this promises that they won't fall out of your pockets on the coveted loop De loop!! Good luck! Have fun!! (:

We visited Universal Studios in July 2014 with designs on riding the new Escape from Gringotts attraction; arriving before the gates opened to be near the front of the line. It took 15 minutes to walk to Diagon Alley and even though there were only a couple of hundred people walking with along with us, the wait was already 90 minutes. Once we turned the corner and could see the rear of the line it was apparent that Universal doesn't know how to estimate time. There were over 2,000 other guests already in line! After 5 breakdowns and 4 hours in line, we finally gave up. The ride was clearly not ready to handle non-stop use but instead of closing it and making repairs, they just "fixed it as it went" and hoped people didn't complain. Wrong! Unfortunately, there was no ride manager with whom we could share our anger. For over an hour we were stuck inside the dark bank vault and none of the attendants offered any explanation for the delays or assistance to those who were suffering from the cramped quarters. A bottle of water would have been a welcomed sight. Having 3 backpacks in our group, we asked before entering if they were permissible on the ride and were told to keep them and half way through, someone would hold them for us; NOT! Before being permitted to enter the lower level of the bank, we were stopped and told that backpacks aren't allowed and we would have to put them in lockers - which are outside! So while four members stepped out of line and waited, I secured the bags. The lockers are fingerprint access and although it didn't seem like an issue at the time when someone needed something important from her purse 90 minutes later, I was the only one who could retrieve it! Again, no one on the Universal Team had any compassion for the problem. When we found our way out of the Alley, the next ride (Disaster) was also broken down but at least they had the decency to bar people from getting in line. By now it was after 1:00 so we broke for lunch. Note, we'd been in the park for 5 hours and hadn't ridden any rides! After our food, two of us decided to try our luck on the Rip Ride Rocket. The rest of the group sat and waited because the line was only 45 minutes long. When we hadn't returned 90 minutes later they came looking for us. The cause for the delay? We got stranded on the track and had to be rescued. This was no fun either. It was pushing 4 pm and we still hadn't successfully completed a ride so we marched to the customer service office. The representative didn't appreciate our incredible disappointment of being at her park for 8 hours and all we did was stand in lines and give them money for food. We wanted our money back but that was out of the question. Even letting her know that "the internet is a powerful tool for rating attractions" didn't sway her. The level of customer service at Universal is beyond terrible and I would not recommend the park to anyone. No one cares if you're happy or sad, they're just glad to have your cash. Three teenagers got to see the Wizarding World of Harry Potter but at $70 per person, it was a huge waste of money.

Visited Orlando in August 2014, went to Universal Studios, what a fun place, will have to visit again to finish the fun. Spent all my time in Adventure Land, there was just so much to see and do. If you visit, make sure you do Spiderman, Harry Potter and Jerasic Park, three of my favorates and the Hulk roller coaster it's a must do also. Just way too much fun.

Universal studios has something for all ages. This is my family's favorite theme park. The new rides like Tansformers,The minion ride and the Simpsons ride were awesome. The workers there are so wonderful. My daughter's asthma got really bad due to the heat and we took her to the first aid office to check her vitals. They checked her out and got us a special pass so that she could skip,the lines.we were just going to leave because we were concerned about her being out in that heat and humidity. The heat was agrivating her asthma. I was very happy that they have such a kind staff.

The park is beautiful to walk around in and the rides are a ton of fun! Get the express pass so you don't have to wait on the long lines. And take it all in while you are there because if you miss anything, you will regret it.

Great place to take kids!! Fun place for all the family!! Personally, my family and I actually enjoyed Universal more however Disneyland was still absolutely superb!! Would definitely recommend a trip at least once in a lifetime :)

But I was pleasantly surprised by Universal Studios Florida! The feel of the place was very nice, not too crowded (although the crowd levels were higher) and not as hot (if that is even possible). We rode more rides here than at IOA and loved nearly every one. Transformers was first and it was a thrill ride and a half! Loved the theming in the queue and the ride experience was fantastic. We rode ET, very tame, but cute. It needs to be updated, I think, to make it relevant to the generations who may never have seen the movie. Twister, well, we were very disappointed by this experience. We expected something more than what was delivered. The Mummy was absolutely fantastic! Great Coaster! MIB was fun (even though I didn't win). Daughter and her boyfriend rode The Simpson Ride and said it was a blast. The longest wait we had all day was for the Hogswart Express train ride from Diagon Alley to Hogsmeade. The wait time was posted as 10 minutes, but we were in line for fully 45 minutes and it was not worth it. Also, the posted wait time for Escape from Gringotts was over 2 hours, so we opted to not even try it. But the Dragon was spectacular! All in all, I would recommend The Studios over IOA any day.

If you're going to visit Universal Studios or Universal's Islands of Adventure, my suggestion is to go with Islands of Adventure. By comparison Universal Studios just seems empty ... not a lot of rides or things to do, so it seems like you paid a lot of money to go to some high priced, not so great restaurants and shop for over priced trinkets. As a side note, why does it seem like they only sell burgers and chicken fingers?  Anyway, the only reason we went to Universal Studios was for the new Harry Potter/Diagon Alley. That was awesome. My daughter is 13 and was just as mesmerized by Diagon Alley as she was by Hogsmeade several years ago. If it weren't for the darn "Harry Potter" train from Diagon Alley (Universal Studios) to Hogsmeade (Islands of Adventure), we would've saved the extra $$ and just gone to Diagon Alley. Clever marketing there Universal!  Really though ... if you're not a big Potter fan, skip the studios and head to the Islands. Way better.
I didn't use to like it, but Harry Potter attractions changed that for real. Every detail is amazing.

Great as ever, had to queue for 3 hours for Gringotts bank.... only worth it if you are an ardent HP fan as other ride in Islands of adventure is better. Hogwarts express very good. Visiting end of Aug great as parks not so busy as US children back in school. Single rider option great if not desperate to stay as family unit; you can pretty much get on all rides without a wait. Park well maintained and restroom clean.
E.T.,great ride,Shrek 4D great,The Mummy, and the Terminator. I like the shops and candy store.Food was a little too expensive.

We spent a few days at Universal and still didn't get on everything! The rides are something else, minions, shrek, transformers. simpsons etc, all fab and very well thought out. The queues are something else too (90mins+) so if you can buy a fast track ticket for the day as it will allow you to get around more rides. Great mix of rides for all ages and attractions, Harry Potter train a must!

Arrived at with great excitement at Universal at 8.30am. Battled our way through the security, crowds and finally got into the park at 9am and headed towards Harry Potter. The Despicable Me ride had already got a queue for 80 minutes which was hard to believe since the park had only opened at 9am! We decided to buy Express Passes at $70 each totally $300 with tax for 4 people and headed to Diagon Alley. The Gringotts ride had a 4 hour wait by 9.30am and we were then informed that our Express Passes where not valid on Harry Potter rides!! We abandoned Gringotts and looked around Diagon Alley which was excellent! You are able to visit inside the shops which was magical and better than the Warner a Brothers Studios in the UK! We then headed to the Kings Cross station which was a very good replica of the real thing with the destination board showing departures on my local line which was very amusing to my daughter! We went onto Platform 9 3/4 and magically disappeared onto the other side! Great for all Harry Potter fans! The Hogwarts steam train is fantastic where you travel to the a Islands of Adventure with Harry and crew passing past the window. On arrival you are faced with Hogwarts castle in the snow and yes yet more queues which my Express passes are not usable! We spilt up and my husband went the castle ride and queued for 80 minutes and I went with my other daughter into the Wand shop to see the magic demonstration which took 1 hour in the burning sun! We decided against buying any Butter Beer as we had sampled it at the Studios! We returned back to Universal travelling back on the Hogwarts express and made our way to Disaster! By now it was 11.30am and even paying $300 we had only been on 1 ride and the train. We used the a Express Pass and went in with the normal queue still waiting 30 minutes to use the ride! By 1pm we attempted to go on Despicable Me and again waited 40 minutes with the Express Passes so at 2.30 we had managed 2 rides which had cost $300. My husband went to guests services who eventually got a full refund of $300. We then managed to meet Curious George, Shaggy and Scooby Doo, Dora and Sponge Bob and went on the ET ride and Shrek by 5pm and exhausted we left the park feeling very let down! We did not have time to eat a meal at Universal due to all the time queuing. I think Universal could learn by the success on the Disney FastPass+ which are free!
Again like islands of adventure highly recommend fast @ $88 each. Would have only done 3 rides if no passes as the queues were quite long.
As expected, great for families with teenage to younger kids. Not so good if you are in the retirement age.

My family loved it here! Plenty for the little ones to enjoy and likewise for us grown-up kids!!! The little ones loved the ET ride and Woody the Woodpecker land! We went during the holidays and the decorations were beautiful!

I haven't been for many years, ie before Harry Potter area opened, but it was amazing!!! I really couldn't recommend it highly enough! The tickets are a high price per day, so we got the 5 park 14day passes, can't remember exact price but it was a much better deal because it gave you the freedom to go to the park as many times as you want, which if you're like me, you definitely will want it! Everything from the rides and shows to even the way the bins were in each area was amazing! such attention to detail!

Like Islands of adventure, we had so much fun at the universal studios! Harry Potter comes out on top, the diagon alley is sensational and the gringotts rode fantastic and well worth the 120 Minute queue!! All other rides were brilliant, the 4d ones out of this world!! Can't wait to go back! No need for young kids, as we traveled as a couple and thoroughly enjoyed every minute!!

After waiting for Diagon Alley... It's here! We went the day after Labor Day ( both Canada & USA) = NO lines! We never waited for more than a couple minutes. We drove right in, pd the extra fee to park neat entrance -= easy to find at end of tired day! Pre-bought from our hotel - 2park/1 day with Hogwarts Express train pass. Names right on the ticket & finger printed us at the gate. Did 5 rides in the adventure side - including 2 water ones = soaked! FUN!! But perfect for a hot day. Then 6 rides on Studio side - of course we went to Ollivanders/wand room - where our wizarding wands picked us! :) then we used our wizard map to follow and cast spells around both parks! Perfect for ALL ages - make it rain, dance the skeleton... Awesome! Tons of options for food including vegetarian. Make sure to ride the train return - diff experience both ways. We took water/granola bars - had not problems. Keep your tickets - you'll have to show them. Several rides required bags to be left in lockers - free for first 30...45 mins - think the time is gauged on the wait times for rides (there's electronic billboards that tell u) definitely recommend 2 parks/1 day. Go early, stay late. *other than the water rides - we only did the adult ones - including my 70+ mom who had more fun than us I think! Ps. Don't forget to chat with Myrtle in the the public convenience stalls... Very entertaining ;)

Universal Studios is a lot about shows but there are also plenty of rides for all ages. Of course Fun for everyone - if you are at all interested in Harry Potter then you will definately love all of that part of the parks. Don't miss the Hogwarts Express. If with younger kids get them the interactive wands although pricey $40+ mine used them for hours both days. If you can afford the unlimited express pass it will be WELL worth it but don't bother with the pager type one that is $40 each it is only good for one ride at a time and didn't seem to help much for the money spent. Food of course is crazy expensive in the park but no surprise. Water rides can get you really wet and it can rain a lot in Florida so an inexpensive poncho in your bag can come in really handy. You will walk a lot but there is plenty to do for even a 3-day vacation and more than you can do for a 1 day. Plan out as many shows as you can and fill in rest with rides and if short lines 10 minutes or less ride again. Enjoy
We enjoy the park and could have done it in three days in a leisurely maner. Like all the parks in Orlando have your wallet ready and full.

I am a huge Harry Potter fan. I had visited Hogsmeade at the Islands of Adventure in 2010 and 2012. I'm back again to visit Diagon Alley, September 2nd thru 4th. I bought a three day park to park ticket. I went to Hogsmeade Station first and took the Hogwarts Express to Kings Cross Station. It was awesome. I was the only one in the compartment. I exited the train and walked around through the brick wall to Diagon Alley. Amazing! I walked around, had a butterbeer and caught the story of The Three Brothers. Went to Gringotts and within 15 minutes I was on the ride. Great ride but I think I like the Forbidden Journey better. Had the butterbeer ice cream, saw the dragon blow fire, very hot! My husband and I went into Shutter Buttons and made a DVD of 12 scenes from Harry Potter. Got to wear robes and act out scenes in front of a green screen. This DVD is $70.00 but I thought it was a fun thing to do. You can do it for free and not buy the DVD, but I think you will. I bought four new shirts. Visited Knockturn Alley. Ate at the Leaky Cauldron. Good chicken sandwich. Took the train back to Hogsmeade. Walked through 9 3/4 which my husband took pictures and video of me walking through. Awesome!
Had the most fun at: 1. The Wizarding World of Harry Potter 2. Revenge of the Mummy 3. Despicable Me Minion Mayhem 4. Transformers  Try Express lane or Single Rider lane to avoid the long wait.

Awesome theme park. We spent 3 days there including the islands of adventure. If you're visiting around Halloween I would highly recommend going to the haunted houses. The experience just walking along the streets is unbelievable.

We had the best time here! The best ever 3D/4D simulators in universal and the biggest and best roller coasters in Islands of adventure. The food is pricey but we took our own water and went for a big breakfast before we got there, so you get by. Can't actually wait to go again!

I love Harry Potter and I love universal studios so as you can guess I think Diagon Alley is fantastic! I you are a fan of the Harry Potter movies you will want to visit Diagon Alley and Hogsmeade as they are both amazing, the rides are good, the food is excellent and there are fantastic souvenirs to be purchased (these are a little bit on the expensive side but hey thats theme parks for you!) We have annual passes so I will be back again and again to see this attraction now that summer is over and all the tourists have gone home. I would recommend this place to anyone young or old who has an interest in Harry Potter as Universal do this sort thing so well it amazing to walk round ant look at it all, you really feel like you are right there in the movies! A fantastic day out for all the family. I'm adding lots of pictures so you can see what it looks like.

Amazing time had by us all at Universal Studios. I have a broken leg so we took our rented wheelchair along as we weren't sure if there would be an EVC available. Looking at the advice onine, we had read that we should go straight to 'Guest Services' (which is on the right at the park entrance) . We qued for about 20 mins to ask and found out they are $70 to hire. Didn't fancy paying $50-70 each visit, so my partner and son took turns to push. The entire park is wheelchair friendly and some rides we had to que with everyone in the normal manner but some took us from the que to a different entrance for easy access to attraction. I unfortunately couldn't ride most things but what I did manage to do was great. Transformers, Spiderman and Harry Potter (The Forbidden Journey) were my favourites. A TIP is on the Harry Potter ride, you ask a staff member to show you the lift and there is a special, separate ride entrance with a non-moving floor allowing you to access the ride :) The overall experience was great even though I have a broken leg!
I love Despicable Me most!!!!!!! It is soooooo cute. We also took a picture with the yellow baby. but I don't like The Incredible Hulk, it scared me.

This is one of my favorite parks in Orlando. There have been two new additions since my last visit, Transformers which I highly recommend if you like the Spiderman ride in Islands of Adventure and the newest part of the Harry Potter areas Diagon Alley. The themeing throughout the park is outstanding but once you step foot in Diagon Alley you will be amazed at the attention to detail. Looking forward to seeing what Universal has in store for the future. One tip I can offer is to head into the park and check out the wait times before investing in the express passes. We 2 days after labor day and we didn't wait for any of the rides so paying $70 per person for the express pass would have been a total waste. They sell them all throughout the park so if you start making your way through and the lines become long you can always purchase then. Also the express passes do not work for the Harry Potter attractions.

Loved Universal Studios - its perfect for the big kid in every adult! We particularly enjoyed the Mummy ride which was surprisingly addictive! Also loving the plethora of 3D rides being added to the park now, Transformers was particularly good, and the Simpsons ride great fun.  We want to go back now!

We went to Universal Studios, mainly to go to the new Wizarding World of Harry Potter. The new Diagon Alley at Universal Studios is very neat and the Gringotts Bank ride is a lot of fun! (It's part roller coaster, part simulation, in case you're wondering.) We bought park-to-park tickets so that we could ride the Hogwarts Express train to Universal Studios Islands of Adventure. The train ride shows you scenes that you would see if you were actually traveling to Hogwarts, so that's cool.

Sad no more Jaws? Why?? add to that Back to the Future, etc??? Nice park just to walk around and notice all the little things--i.e streets of NYC, etc. Rocky pet shop/ Godfather olive oil, etc. Now add London with the streets of LA/ NYC/ SF and better what lurks behind the streets of London.

The whole family had a fantastic time, car parking well organised and in the shade! Waiting times for the majority of rides was only 10 minutes and even this flew by with all the entertainment whilst waiting, only the minions and escape from Gringots were long (over an hour). We enjoyed Universal more than Disney, perhaps because the kids were older this time, all the film themes were fantastic.

Having stayed at Hard Rock Universal, we were within 5 minutes walk, and have got to say that the rides are a lot better in Universal Studios. Harry Potter is such a large sector of the theme park and is truly amazing. We were allowed extra hours of a morning, including Harry Potter, which made the day so much easier to fit everything in. The staff are extremely friendly and know how to make you have a better day. So many amazing souvenirs to buy as well so leave luggage space

I visited the park with my family and i was amazed, it was so well done, the saff was expelent and helpful, i was on a trip down my memory lane ! many cool rides and cool attractions. will visit again when i return to the US !

We got to the Universal Studios when it opened and that's the way to do it. Having arthritis we had to take it slow and just go in order of appearance. I started off at the roller coaster which had no line, it was great. I'll give highs and lows: when we arrived at the Harry Potter area we couldn't find it, all we saw was a double decker bus and then we went right past it. It wasn't until I reviewed the map again and said we passed it that I realized its like a secret entrance, still there should be signs. So it was the most crowded part of the park. We went right to the only ride they have there, had to put our things in a locker and got in line. The line didn't move much, then we found out the ride was having issues. Ugh. Luckily it didn't have issues for long because once it starts moving the line goes quickly. The issue is the seats, they are new and unforgiving. Don't be overweight or you will not fit, It's not a normal ride seat it also lifts up your legs a bit, hard to describe but it's definitely made for a certain body type. The ride itself it great and a lot of fun, I really enjoyed it. My most favorite ride, in which I clapped when it was finished was Transformer. Wow that's a great ride!! How do they do it?? The worst ride was the Mummy. The seats were the same as Harry Potter but the ride jerks you around so much I had the Heimlich maneuver once, elbowed the guy next to me a couple times and just hated every minute of it, all dark and jerky movements. What's fun about that? A couple rides we wanted to go on were closed, one had the smoke alarm start when we had just started in and the other was closed for a bit so we missed a few on our list. Twister had no wind, I guess it was broke? Time to get rid of Twister and do something new. By late in the day the evening people were arriving and it was getting crowded, so we got some Bubba Gump shrimp and called it a day.

I visited this attraction while in Orlando for a conference. I mostly came for the Harry Potter Diagon Alley park but explored the rest as well. The park was okay and offered lots to see and do for all ages. The Harry Potter Diagon Alley park was awesome. I would definitely recommend getting a pass for both parks so you can ride the Hogwarts Express train to Universal Islands of Adventure park next door and the adjacent attraction of Harry Potter Hogsmeade park. The train is an attraction as well and definitely something to see. Even if you don't like rides, there is still lots to see and do. In comparison to Islands of Adventure, I liked the other park better. I felt it had more to see and do if you didn't want to do the rides. Parking for both parks is $17/day and was very organized and orderly. All you have to remember is the character name of the parking area you are in. Lines were not very long and it was easy to get around. Something to see if you are in the area.

We bought tickets from Orange Lake at the hotel and were not told that we required identification. Luckily the lady accepted a driving licence and credit card with my bus pass. We wasted 45 minutes lining up to obtain the proper tickets.  We then went to the old part of Harry Potter to see Hogwart. We enjoyed the atmosphere of this and all the extras in the castle, where all the pictures talk. We liked the magic set up for the children to follow. Several children were in front of the shop windows trying to find out how to magic items. They have brass plates which you stand on to operate the mechanisms. Children were enjoying this activity.  We bought tickets for both parks so we could ride on the train in both directions. The organisation was excellent and different scenes were seen on both journeys. When we arrived at the station it took us a while to find Diablo Alley, which was atmospheric and creepy. The dragon blowing fire from the roof was very realistic. It was fantastic. Apart from this and Sinbad's voyage we felt some of the rides were tacky and entrance to both parks were overpriced.  Without Harry Potter this would not be somewhere I would want to visit. Harry Potter made the visit worthwhile.  Debbie Quinn

I love this park. It is a great place to visit. If you like movies and entertaining rides it is wonderful. The new Harry potter diagon alley is excellent. Very crowded but definitely worth. The single rider lane at gringotts is a quicker way to get on the line. For the other lines the express pass is definitely the way to go. Definitely worth the extra money. The hogwarts express is really cool make sure you ride it both ways. The photo connect card is a bit of a rip off. Not many photographers were out and most of the characters don't have a photographer with them. They also don't give you all the details. However this is a great place. We will be back.

Visited last year and Universal is just incredible for both adults and kids. We did the two parks in one day and it was exhausting but we had so much fun. The Simpsons Ride just blew us away and the Minion Ride was fantastic. All in all the best park in Orlando. Obviously if you go during school holidays you have to deal with the queues but you can get the fast pass and well worth it for the likes of Harry Potter, Simpsons etc.. City Walk is just buzzing great atmosphere lots to see and do.  Looking forward to our next visit in 2015.

We went there with 3 teenagers and it was great, we had a great time and was never bored, the weather was great, food is a little high but that was to be expected, Hulk ride, transformers was the best

Well they did it again this year and it was awesome again. This is truly the best Halloween attraction in the world. All 8 hours were great. All four scare zones we're cool. I will definitely be there again next year.

I visited Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure on 15th September (I think). Myself and my sister visited guest services in order to obtain our complimentary concession tickets, however, we hit a bit of a brick wall before we even got there. We were required to apply for these through our place of employment, which we did, and fill out a 'quiz'. We did this and sent them off only to hear nothing back. We tried emailing and phoning on several occasions with no joy. When we got to guest relations, we were greeted by Tykia, she took our details and managed to find my sister on the system, so she printed off her ticket. When she got to me, there seemed to be a problem as I was not on the system. Tykia asked her colleagues for help and went off to phone through to the UK and to my place of employment. Whilst she was gone, Dakota came to introduce himself and kept us company through out wait, he gave us a map and told us to plan our visit and gave us tips and advice on wait times and what to look out for (i.e. the dragon breathes fire at Gringotts). When Tykia returned she informed us that she'd obtained a reference number, but this had to be processed in the UK before they could find me on the system, she said this could take up to 20 minutes. After having waited around an hour already, we decided to wait that bit longer. For being so patient, Tykia discounted the price of my dads ticket by 15%, which we thought was very generous of her. She was so nice and patient with us, talked to us as if we were friends of hers and was so apologetic, which is all you can really ask for. After all, this wasn't her fault! After 25minutes, Tykia phoned through to the UK again as they hadn't got back to her, Dakota again stepped in for a chat with us and to assure us that we will get our tickets very soon. When Tykia returned she said it would take another 20minutes and issued us 12 fast-track tickets for our wait. 3minutes later, my ticket was processed and we were sorted!  What could have been a very stressful and frustrating situation was made all the more pleasant by such wonderful customer service. Tykia and Dakota are definitely a credit to the company!

We were very lucky with timing but the quality of rides was fantastic and the Harry potter attractions were fabulous. Summer would not be good as Florida is hot and humid. But crowds are down in September and you can get through a lot of the park in one day with an early day pass.

Visited in September 2014, together with my wife. Most children had gone back to their respective schools and therefore it wasn't too crowded, but the first shock after travelling to the venue by coach (no car parking charges), was the admission price. Undoubtedly, if you book tickets in advance at a venue such as a shopping mall, it will probably be cheaper, but turn up at the entrance on the day and it is, per day, an eye watering $136 dollars for each adult and $130 dollars for each child aged up to ten (I think), to enter both Universal and the adjoining 'World of Adventure'. Now for a family of two adults and two or three kids, I regard that as extremely expensive for a day out.  You can 'do' both parks in a day and there are a few 'white knuckle' rides which may appeal to teenagers and the like, but not a lot else. Certainly, in my opinion, not a patch on Disney and much more expensive. Any 'Harry Potter' fans will be very pleased with the latest attractions which are very impressive and although the rest of the Park is generally good, the entry cost alone will ensure I never return.  By all means, visit and have fun, just remember to take out a mortgage first.

I was disappointed with Universal Studio's Florida we were there this Sept 27-14 . We got there early as the Park closed early at 1700 and we didn't want pay extra for the Harry Potter Halloween night thing as it was an extra 40$ per person. Didn't get our value for the money we paid. The Best Ride was the Simpson Family ride the biggest disappointment was the Harry Potter Ride HARRY POTTER AND THE ESCAPE FROM GRINGOTTS™ that had broken down and we had lost some valuable time. I found that the rides were short in duration but what really bothered me was leaving the park early and wasted time at the broken rides. Would I go back NO!

We had a two park pass to ride the Hogwarts train between the two parks. Diagon Alley was nice, we rode Gringotts several times. The ice cream shop there was good, with some unique flavors like orange marmalade. t2 3d was a nice show, and Twister was also a show type of attraction. We rode the Mummy(that was pretty wild). We rode most of the rides there several times. ET is still around, it is a easy going ride, and nice and cool inside.  Special thanks to All of the staff at both parks!

I went to Harry Potter World (which was far better than my expectations) as part of a work event and lost my phone (actually thought that it fell out of my pocket on a roller coaster). A few days later, I got a call from the lost & found saying that they had found the phone and had gotten my number from the "Lost My Iphone" message on the screen. When I returned their call the customer service person was fantastic; she was patient, professional, asked questions to be sure it was my phone, went out of her way to tell me the condition of the phone, and best of all, they shipped it back for free.

We went last Friday and even though it rained all night, we had a fantastic time. Showed up before the scheduled opening time, and they actually opened the park at 6 PM instead of 6:30 PM. It was busy and most likely if we go back next year we will purchase the Express Pass in the future. They start the street off with The Purge:Anarchy when the open the gates. It was pretty cool the way they did it, and The Purge street was awesome.  As far as the houses go, the best without a doubt was The Walking Dead and it was a very big house and walking through it took some time. The worst house was the Dracula house and unless there is no line no waiting, do not waste your time on it. From Dust till Dawn was the second best house, Halloween was good, Giggles & Gore was freaky with the clowns, Alien vs. Predator was cool, the Dollhouse was okay and I really liked the ending and Roanoke was nothing special and would not wait more than 10 minutes for it.  The Face Off street was good, Bayou of Blood was okay, did not see the other street. We saw all eight houses, and it took about five hours. The longest line was Halloween and it was a solid hour wait. If you hate clowns or are scared of them you have to do Giggles & Gore. I hate clowns but I really enjoyed the house, and would have liked to seen it a second time. I would also have like to seen the Walking Dead, Alien and Dust to Dawn again.  The women in the Dust to Dawn house are amazing, the bar scenes were created very well, and it was a very cool house. But you cannot leave the park without seeing the Walking Dead House, in the 20 some odd years we have gone to HHN, this without a doubt is the best house they have ever done.  There is plenty of security and Orlando Police at each house, and if anyone got out of line they were dealt with accordingly. I cannot recommend HHN 2014 enough, it is far better than last years event. If it was not so costly, I would go back again preferably on Halloween Night.

We arrived on a beautiful September morning and were very impressed, much more so than Magic Kingdom. Park seems to be a lot better spaced with an excellent choice of eateries and places to get cold drinks and ice creams. Then came the rain! We were in Daigon alley and so dashed onto the Harry Potter ride, which swiftly broke down. We waited 30 minutes and then came the announcement that the ride was working again. We moved 10ft and then it broke again....so we gave up. This is an indoor ride so I'm not sure why this happened. So, we dashed to the train that links the park to Islands of Adventure, got to the front of the queue, and then the announcement...it had stopped due to bad weather. So, off we trundled on foot to Islands of Adventure. By the time we arrived the sun had come out so we grabbed a bite to eat and then headed to the Sinbad show. There were lots of people waiting but dead on 3pm when the show was due to start....cancelled due to bad weather. Why wasn't this announcement made in advance to save wasted time? We had a great day but it was dampened in the middle by these set backs. There is small print on entrance saying they can't be accountable for the weather which is understandable but when inside rides are breaking down at the same time as rides stopping due to bad weather it is rather frustrating.

The rides are intense and fun! But I only found it fun to ride the rides. Didn't do any shopping. Disney has much to offer. I'd only suggest getting a 2 park pass for a day going to US and IoA and city walk after. Rides you must ride: Mummy, transformers, dueling dragons, Harry potter

If you can afford this upgrade it is well worth it,( we were able to do by using mileage points for rest of our trip) This semi private tour maxes out at 12 so you need to reserve ahead of time, but does not mean you will have 12, our group had 9 and it was so much fun! Our tour guide Aaron was great and made sure we got to all the Harry Potter attractions. You are escorted directly to front of line for entire tour, there are no fast passes for the new HP rides, but this access is for everything you do there during tour, you go right up on the ride. You also learn little factoids along the way which are great. The tour is for 7 hours and you hit the major attractions, but it flies by (in a good way)! It was also my birthday, so I felt even more of a VIP they give you a Happy Birthday button so all of employees and guests around park comment all day to you, it's kinda fun. Have been to Universal before as well as Walt Disney World, but I have to say this was impressive, Universal has outdone themselves with Diagon Alley and Hogsmeade, it's like walking onto movie set, and the rides are fantastic. If you are not a fan of simulator rides or roller coasters, I would not take the tour as the focus is to get you on the rides quickly for the experience, which I loved, but some people in our tour did not ride anything, not sure what that was about...

My Husband and I are on honeymoon and purchased a 14 day unlimited pass to universal studios, plus islands of adventure, seaworld, aquatica, Busch gardens and wet & wild. We love universal studios, we are staying onsite in one of the universal hotels and it's so convenient to get to via water taxi or a short walk. We really enjoyed transformers and minions ride, we are not huge fans of roller coasters but it doesn't matter because there is lots of other rides and shows, also parades and lots of shops to look in. You are also spoilt for choice for eating, and the Harry Potter world is amazing, the hogwarts express train to island of adventures is a must however you must have a pass to both parks to go on the train!x

This ride was a good start to the Universal experience. It was tame but in a way very nostalgic for someone who grew up in the 90's. Don't walk past, the lines aren't long and its cool.  Not transformers by any means though.

If you are going to Universal Studios at peak times you will be sorely disappointed if you haven't bought a fast track pass. Yes, I know that they are an extra expense to the already high ticket price but without stating the obvious, the queues for the favourite rides will eat up your day and as its Halloween your time in the park is limited anyway. Talking of Halloween Horror night, we hummed and hawed about going ( we were staying at one of the onsite hotels ) but they wanted an extortionate amount on top of our 2 park pass, plus extra again for fast passes, we already had these but they aren't applicable so be warned ! All in all, we would have had to cough up approx. another £300 pounds for two nights, and as I'm normally frightened of my own shadow it would have been a false economy. So back to the park, if you cant upgrade and are on limited time I would suggest giving Disaster a swerve as the majority of this show is a disaster.... we fast tracked and still had to wait 20 mins. for a toe curling experience, go see the Blues Brother show instead that was fabulous. Now, for the proper star of the show our very own Harry Potter, that alone is worth a couple of hours just to digest the breath taking detail of Diagon Alley also bearing in mind ,there is no fast track to the ride, so save a bit of time and go to the locker area first to park your bags etc. this is a must as you will be turned away and have to go back again. A word of advice it is CHAOS trying to retrieve your bags , so make sure you know your locker no. its also fingerprint secure, this really needs to be your first port of call when arriving at the park. Try not to miss character photo shoots i.e Homer, Bart, Marge and Maggie, Scooby , Shrek, Fiona and Donkey and LOADS more. There is so much to see and do something for every one and is doable with careful planning.
Love the new Harry Potter section. The theming is even better than in Hogwarts. Gringotts has been closed both times we tried to go to it though. Do not miss the Simpsons Krustyland ride.

I will start by saying I haven't ever had a desire to go to an Orlando theme park, especially Disney, but since I'd never been, I really had no idea what I was missing. I tried not to have high expectations so as not to be disappointed. Expectations met, exceeded, blown away. I didn't know about the 3D & 4D rides/attractions so it was all a huge awesome surprise! Everything Harry Potter was amazing! Things we learned: the Express Pass that was included with our Portofino Bay hotel was priceless. On most rides, we zoomed to the front, bypassing lines of people. We also got into the Harry Potter Diagon Alley 1 hr before the general public as a perk of staying at our hotel. So, no lines to see the stores, no lines for "butter beer", no lines to purchase wands for our sons. Time-saving beyond belief. We also learned you must expect to spend a LOT on food each day or pack heavy snacks into the park to picnic on. We learned that Dramamine is my friend because day 2 the Spider-Man was so awesome I got nauseated! The gift shops sell all your OTC med needs (Tylenol, Pepto, etc)...just ask. It's kept out of sight for some reason. Lastly we learned you can't do it all...we didn't get to do 3 things because they were either temporarily closed when we were in the area or we just ran out of time. We DID do every other big ride & coaster though (Universal & Islands of Adventure both) in only 2 days! So we've now visited once! Now we look forward to the next time years from now-with grand kids maybe!

Got the 2 park ticket which shares with Isalands of adventure for 14 days. Brill park,every time we went we shared our time wirh both parks hoping between both. Universal studios has great rides etc. Despicable me,the mummy (best) new transformers ride (3d) simpsons (3d) men in black etc and the new harry potter area. Got to the park at 8am one morning to do the gringotts ride to beat the que really dissapointed in the ride,not as good as the other potter ride at I.O.A diagon alley is fab though. The whole park is really dwar to buy things so take drinks/snacks if you can. As the hallowean horry nights were on therebwas a lot of props for it lying about. Didnt make it to one.overall a great park worth visiting. Have a great say.

I'm not a coaster guy... and you can only do so much with motion simulators. But the buzz about the Harry Potter attractions finally gave me a reason to visit Universal Studios. And I have to say, Diagon Alley lives up to the hype. It's done with an attention to detail that would make even Disney proud. (My wife also enjoyed the coasters... and we both got a kick out of the "Despicable Me" and "Shrek" attractions.) The Hogwarts Express is a fun trip between parks... but plan on waiting in line for a long time, unless you ride fairly early in the day.  Universal has really taken their game up a couple of notches with the Potter attractions. Just be sure to arrive early so you can enjoy them before they get too crowded.

Had a nice time at Universal Studios. I hadn't been there in a while and it was nice to see some of my old favorites as well as new rides and stores, etc. It is an enjoyable spacious park with lots to see. There are rides, shops, restaurants, shows and fun interactive scenary throughout the park that make it a great place to be. A good place to eat is Mel's Diner which as delicious milkshakes and 50's style meals! The Animal Actor's show is an interactive animal show which is always a classic and one of the enjoyable rides there is "The Mummy" which is a high thrill rollercoaster! We also didn't have to wait too long for any of the rides which was nice. We went in February and got to enjoy the free Mardi Gras live concerts which was a fun nice treat. My advice if you want to attend one of these is line up early in the evening to get a good spot to see the stage. If you don't you will be all the way in the back or may even have to watch on a big screen from the walk ways in the park.

Thank you Universal, for bringing the magical Diagon Alley to this park. We knew it would be special as we walked up to Grimmauld Place, and waited to see Kreacher peek out of the window in Sirius' house. The Knight Bus across the street with Stan and the talking shrunken head were awesome. Gringott's is amazing- I love everything about the bank you go through as you wait in line. September was a good time to go, with max wait time for this new ride at 45 minutes. If you get a chance to participate, the Wand Chooses the Wizard demonstration next to Ollivander's (which is a much larger store than the one in Hogsmeade) is super and the wizard made it very realistic for us. There were 4 adults on our trip, but everything about this part of the park made us feel like young wizards. We ate lunch at the Leaky Cauldron- good food and a great atmosphere! The rest of the park is enjoyable as well- Seussland, Twister, Despicable Me, Mel's Diner, ET, Men in Black & the parade were some of our other favorites. We spent 4 days touring both parks, staying about 1/2 of the hours they were open each day. The multi-park ticket allows you to ride Hogwarts Express, which has different scenes and actions when you go in the opposite direction, so take it both ways if time allows.

Epic holiday.we spent a lot of money but hey it's only money and the holiday was amazing! Best ever and can't wait to go back! Everything was so cheap. Recommended eating spot for a family is the golden corral, value for money and the selection and quality was by far the best. But if you want a burger go to sizzler melts in your mouth.Water parks are great.wet n wild has a lake at the back and for £7 you get a band for a whole day to paddle board knee board and wake board.plan,plan,plan if your going to Florida think of what you want to do park wise and plan your days no point paying for 14 day passes if you don't go to one till your second week!like us.doh!can upgrade your car at airport by slipping them $10 fuel was so cheap.pay first for your fuel inside however much you want then fill up ,pu st automatic. Check on line before you go for discount vouchers in the malls can save even more with extra 20% off.Nike trainers cheap.Levi's jeans some models and colours cheap cheap but not a lot in it really on most.can save if you book everything separate villa,car,park tickets search net for best prices.also check if tickets allow entry to Disney world kids will love it 5-6 levels of FREE arcades all sorts for all ages!I loved it. A few shops to visit in mall: Apex for sunglasses.Tommy!Ralph!under armour. Calvin for handbags. Nike damn cheap!Big Walmarts alcohol 1.75 litre bottles for £14 rude not to..take good walking trainers or buy some straight away you will need them.have a great time we did.you will go back! One last thing if you have children with needs or you have special requirements GOTO customer services in each park and they are more than happy to give you a fast pass for the whole family!made are holiday if not get there early and get inline for the rides you want to go on most,its busy and hot!invest in a sat nav over there in Walmart as you can return it to them within 14 days !they told us to do that?but it's easy after a day or two..

My son (13 years) and i went to universal on sun & mon (10/12 & 10/13) and waited in line for over 1.5 hours for the harry potter train ride to be told it wasn't working & they did not know when or if it would be working. And then we went to Diagon Alley to ride the new Harry Potter ride and was told the same exact thing. The next day which was our last day we actually made it on to the new ride for it to break down in the middle of the ride.Never coming back it was totally disappointing.

I went specifically for Harry Potter and those sections of the parks blew my mind. I can only hope my kids can talk my husband into taking us back there eventually! However, my husband is not into Harry Potter and I was counting on the rest of the park to impress him and it's failed miserably. We had a 3 day pass and only went 1 1/2 days. Thumbs up for HP fans and families with kids old enough to enjoy it though!

The lines were WAY to long - even watching those with express pass - seems most everyone waited. Some of the rides were NOT worth the long wait. The Harry Potter section of the part was awesome. The lines there were extremely long. Save yourself the time and trouble of the train ride (Hogwart's Express) - it was short and LAME - and that was the longest line that we waited in - VERY disappointing. Diagon Alley was very cool to walk around in. The Forbidden Journey Ride was excellent! Too many ticket prices and options Universal - get your act together.

This is a must, but be advised you will need the fast track tickets to get around. Some of the queues were over 2 hours without the tickets so getting round in one night is almost impossible without them.  The houses were all good apart from Alien v Predator which was pretty poor. The Walking Dead house was awesome, my wife was scared out of her skin and had her eyes closed clinging on for dear life at the end.  Some of the streets are also themed and my wife thoroughly enjoyed these. I would not advise taking under 15s as I think it would be too much for the majority of them.  It was expensive with the fast track, but you're in Orlando so it's to be expected and as a one off is worth it.

I love Universal, I must say it does top Disney in my book. Que"s are not bad, it ain't as crowded as disney and it's not as expensive to eat etc. Surprisingly I even found the staff more child friendly. Traveling with a child with ASD, who isn't very good with waiting, crowds etc, they gave me a card which I showed the staff on each attraction which allowed us to take him straight through to the ride. How very thoughtful, it really made his holiday and the rest of the family's too. And the horror night is fantastic too

We took a two day park to park pass as it does take quite a bit of walking to get around everywhere. The line ups were only an average of 15-30 minutes. So save yourself $80 on the express line pass.  If you enjoy the characters from movies like Despicable Me, Shrek, Transformers, Mummy and ET then definitely do these rides. I personally only cared for the Harry Potter theme parks- Hogsmeade and Diagonal Alley. It's very carefully planned with excellent attention to detail. Eat at the Leaky Cauldron, drink Butterbeer (tastes like liquid butterscotch candy and heavy cream combined) and get on the simulated ride at Hogwarts.

Went on a Sunday night with wife and another couple, visited 4 houses and spent over four hours in lines waiting. Will not go again, but will return to the Park. If any one does want to go, buy the Fast Pass.

Even though our children are grown we have still continued our vacationing in Florida. Today was universal day and I believe it was better without the children in tow. We enjoyed the attractions and are planning on returning another day.

The Harry Potter areas in both parks are the big attraction and very well done. There were few shows and character meet-and-greet opportunities. Plenty of healthy food options as well as traditional park food. Off-season hours were dissapointing and early hours for those staying in Universal-brand resorts were limited to one area in one park (Diagon Alley).

Be sure to ask for a control room tour when you exit Twister. They'll take you into the control room, explain how the show works and let you watch as the ride runs through its program and resets all the effects. The staff were very friendly and extremely helpful. I highly recommend it.

I visited Halloween Horror Nights yesterday, and all I can say is "AAAHHHHHHHHHH". I definently was frightened. Being chased by purge members, baby dolls and just by men in costumes. It was definently worth the thrill and losing my voice.

This was our first visit to Universal Studios, we went October 11th. We had fun but it was a little busier but not too bad considering it was a Saturday. I refused to pay more money for the express pass, talk about nickel and diming you and it is expensive!!!! I am glad that we experienced it but it doesn't beat Disney World in my opinion.
Ok I love Harry Potter so I am somewhat biased. I don't do the rides but just love the atmosphere, the butter beer (frozen) and people watching.

This is our 3rd trip in the past 10 years. Each time, its better and better. In my opinion it is more teen to any age adult, especially with Harry Potter in both parks. Yes there is some areas for little kids, but those places are about things that were on tv 10 years ago.. I see there is a listing for City walk, but since we only go to Jimmy Buffett Margaritaville Restaurant we skip the rest, and so will I skip City walk except to say it cuts down on getting to one of the two parks. I do like the new security implemented for the parks, with so many people the terrorist factor is down. However I am trying to get a response as to how long the keep the fingerprints as I do believe in personal freedom.

Having spent 2 weeks in Florida. The 2 visits I spent in Universal Studios were by far the best. It didnt seem to be as busy as the Disney parks yet seemed to have more going on for everybody. The highlight had to be Springfield and all the associated Simpsons stuff. You also have some great attractions to see like the Minions ride and the new Transformers ride which was awesome. Theres also the new Harry Potter section and the train ride from one Potter area to the other was really good. In all a fantastic visit well spent.
Make sure you get a fast pass! Did all 8 houses and 6 rides in one night. Michael Meyers house was the BEST! Definitely doing it next year.

My husband and I spent two days here recently and had a great time......We are both in our sixties and had not seen a lot of the movies, shows etc. but that really did not matter....everything was fun! The park itself was immaculate, the staff friendly and accommodating...The first day we were on the Behind the Scenes tour so we did not have to wait on any lines.....that was great.....the second day we did have to wait on lines, but they were not long so there was no problem in doing what we wanted......A few of the rides my husband requested and got the stationery seats which made him happy.......We enjoyed the shows we saw and especially liked the characters who walked about the park and gladly posed for pictures....We did see the Parade and was amazed at the energy and enthusiasm all cast put into it! We were there in late September and it was humid and rainy but that did not deter us nor anyone else......you just put on the poncho and off you go! I was also impressed that the bathrooms were clean in spite of the large number of people.....

Thought I would try HHN this year and wasnt to bad starting out. Went into the line for the 3rd house and asked what the wait time was and they said it was 45 minutes just like the sign said. We have now been in line over an hour and a half and still not near the front of the line. They keep letting all the Express Pass people in and very little people in the stand by line in. Last time I come to this event!!! Unless you buy the Express pass would not recommend coming to this event!!! I will not be back!

We went to Universal Studios as soon as we could after the opening of the new Harry Potter portion. We walked past it and had to ask a staff member where it was. It is actually hidden behind a wall almost. I am sure later in the day with everyone going in there it is a bit more obvious. You walk through and it is amazing because it shows the brick wall looking like it just opened for you. It was awesome! The new ride is great! Not as long or motion crazy as the other ones. The shops are all extremely small though. I thought they would make them bigger but they didn't. Still great. The amount of work and detail that went into the entire expansion was breathtaking. Everywhere I looked was something new and amazing. It was great! The signs on the buildings were fun. Painted on. Old school looking. I basically loved everything.  I think last time we went to Universal we gave most of it a skip. This time we had more time and actually had a lot of fun on the Universal side. The Simpsons Ride was cute and fun. It was a bit of a stomach turner if you are motion sensitive like me (Had my Dramamine luckily!) but not terrible. The Transformers ride was also a lot of fun. Not sure why we didn't go on it last time but it was a blast. Plus we ran into Optimus outside and got a picture with him.  The entire day was a blast and I can't wait to go back. Need to convince my husband this should be a yearly trip.
even weather was horrible we love this place. great attractions and you need more than 1 day to spent there time.

U will love it here! Rides for young and older. The rockit roller coaster is amazing! Harry potter part on both sides awesome. U have to use the train between both parks if u go. The ride is magical Harry potter. Love it here so much. Will really miss it.

Universal Studios is simply amazing! Our daughters 5-7 enjoyed Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure more then Disney, yes it's true! Hogwarts castle is spectacular and the butter beer is delicious!

According to policy all items must be removed from pockets and loose items must be stowed before riding which is completely understandable. We were asked to get off the ride and go to the lockers because a staff person, Nicholas, noticed a phone in my husband's pocket. Although we were disappointed, we went to the lockers and stowed all items. After waiting in line again, we got back on the ride and this time they harassed us again saying there was stuff in our pockets although there was literally nothing. Staff refused to let me off the ride when I said I didn't want to go. Nicholas along with another unknown staff person have some sort of power struggle and use their authority as universal studios staff persons in an abusive way to bully people. If we saw this person outside the park I really doubt he would act that way. Who do you think you are? This ride pretty munched ruined the day. Thanks Nicholas! Thanks rip ride rockit. Worst roller coaster ever.

We had done some of the other parks in Orlando, but had never been to Universal Studios before.  We came here the week of October 20th and were very pleased at what we experienced.  Firstly, having the huge parking lot to our advantage was a relief. Not to mention the moving floors along the way to CityWalk. They were more convenient after our touring day. I wasn't too keen on the parking fee of $17 per day we visited, but I was used to not paying for parking on previous all-inclusive vacations...so it is what it is and I won't dock marks. Obviously I can't change that.  The day we arrived wasn't crowded by any means and we enjoyed walk on experiences at many of the attractions. The staff we encountered were friendly and courteous.  Obviously, highlights for us included the Diagon Alley area and the Transformers attraction. In fact, one of the first "meets" we had was with Bumblebee, who had no wait time to meet him and took time after our photograph to wave and interact with us before going back inside his facility. Megatron was also a big hit.  Diagon Alley is themed superbly and identical to how it is represented in film and literature. Lots of fun. Crowds weren't extremely heavy...however the shops can get a little crowded but honestly that adds to the atmosphere and excitement. Try the frozen butter beer!  I could go on but don't want to spoil the surprises for anyone. Come and enjoy Universal Studios. There is plenty for families to do and lots of great places for photographs together.  Thanks for giving us a great experience and lots of memories!

Visited here with my hubby and 2 young children. The Harry potter part of the park is just fantastic and was loved my all of us. My 4 yr old was unable to do alot of rides here but she still loved it. The Curious George part of the park which is full of water kept them amused for literally 2 hours. Take a change of clothes though because they get soaked. Really great clean park that we visited a few times on this holiday.
Amazing attraction and worth the money anyone who loves Halloween will love this. Worth the money and worth the wait in line for each haunted house. Street performers were a,axing as well.

This was a last minute decision and we had no idea about the opening of the new Harry Potter ride just a few weeks before. So the park was very crowded but we had the express pass. Highly recommended!!!! There were lines but with the pass they were bearable. We were at this park 10 years ago as a toddler and now as a teenager the park is a perfect fit for both age groups. It was great to see how we evolved to the "big kid" rides! We will defiantly will be back and it will not take us 10 years to get there.

The ever upgrading and new rides makes this the best theme park going .With harry potter gringotts ride the best I,ve been on ,others to check out are minon myhem ,transformers,Simpsons,men in blk and disaster movie plus beatle juice .Great rides ,great entertainment, great time.

The whole experience of Harry Potter was simply amazing, the detail which has been put in to this is outstanding! Remember to get both passes for Universal and Island of adventure so you can follow the story through both parks by jumping on the train ride (another amazing experience). All the rides are like you are participating in the films. The park was well organised in dealing with a vast amount of people. Went to The Halloween Horror Night as my son was pleading me to go, and im glad i did. Another fantastic experience, again attention to detail, was almost real like, spooked me anyway. Well this place certainly brought back the kid in me.....loved it!!!

Went here with friends because of the Potterverse. I'm 6' 3" this park is not really geared toward us bigger folks. Mummy ride and Howarts Express the only things I could ride. Not worth $136. They wanted an additional $75.99 for Halloween Horror Nights. Frozen Butterbeer was the only redemptive feature.

I'll start out by stating that I visited Universal on Christmas Day, so by no means was I expecting the park to be empty but it still fell greatly short of my expectations. I had already spent two days in Disney and the crowds were bad there but nothing like at Universal. Wait times exceeded two hours for most of the rides and you have to pay extra for Universal's version of a fastpass, despite the very high price of admission. Also, crowd control (especially during the parade) seemed nonexistent. My family members were all separated from one another in the stampede that followed the parade. It wasn't a big deal as all of us are older and have cell phones, but it's a cautionary note for a parent with young children. I would have loved to relive the great experience I had here on a prior trip, but as it stands I won't return to Universal.

The rides are brilliant, Harry Potter world was fantastic, we all loved it. Had breakfast in the Three Broomsticks and Hogwarts castle is just amazing, the attention to detail is awesome. Really want to go back. Even had Moaning Myrtle in the restroom, lol Halloween Horror Night 100% fantastic

Loved this park, i want to work at this park. DM is amazing so funny, and have a small boogie with the minions at the end. Rock it (like the Hulk) you just want to get on again and again, choosing your own music is awesome and then getting a dvd of that ride is amazing. Wasn't as impressed with Twister as i thought i would be, but still entertaining. Mummy was better than the one in LA, even the staff around that ride are great. Simpsons and Transformers are the best as well. The one that got me though was Harry Potter and Diagon alley, oh my god AMAZING. The detail in everything is amazing, the way the staff are all dressed is great. Had a butterbeer and was delicious, Gringotts bank ride is amazing, 1st time on waiting wasn't to bad but the 2nd day i went was waiting nearly 2 hours. The dragon on top of the bank is amazing and a real surprise, keep your eye on her. Overall if your willing to pay for the express pass go for it your waiting time is cut in half of everyone else, if not do what i did and got a game on my phone to keep us occupied called heads up (what am i). We were told we were going in a quite time of year so wouldn't be so busy, not the case. Prepare to wait for the more popular rides.
Harry Potter and the Minions . . . what an experience. Just remember to get your admission ticket out to ride the Hogswart Express

This park has changed so much. With the advent of the Harry Potter attraction which deserves a park in its own right, there is the added bonus of the expanded Simpsons themed area. A Flaming Moe's drink on offer in Moe's Tavern including a drink at the bar Homer often frequents is a must do. But one of the best discoveries was Curious Georges play area. This was a part of the park largely ignored by us in the past but with our grandson with us it became a must do and it is absolutely brilliant. It is basically an excuse to get soaked. There are no rides as such, it is simply a huge play area with themed buildings with various tanks that open without warning or telephones that squirt water when you pick them up. A word of warning, take the kids at the end of the day, too early and you will struggle to get them out. Our grandson is still talking about it now.

We went last weekend and were very impressed...the park was really under construction a few years ago and we were even bored! Now, with amazing Diagon Alley and Springfield, we had a blast! We are big Harry Potter fans, and Diagon Alley did not disappoint! It truly was a magical experience. I will not write too much so I don't give much of the experience away. The new Gringotts ride was unlike any other. The line was pretty long for this ride, rightly so. I recommend waiting in the line at least once, as the experience is pretty awesome. If you want to ride the ride again, the single-rider line is shorter... :) Make sure you have a park-to-park pass for the Hogwarts Express!  I also have a gluten allergy and I was able to eat a chicken sandwich at the Leaky Cauldron in Diagon Alley. I also ate at Bumblebee Man's Taco truck in Springfield.  The reason I'm not giving the experience an "excellent" rating is because we stayed on campus at a resort and were able to take advantage of early access to the park. Unfortunately, Universal could not handle this on Sunday, 11/2. We were in a highly unorganized stand-still line to even get in to the park. There was no structure, and people were very upset. The Universal Staff did nothing to help, except open a couple more lines 25 minutes into our wait...no apologies or anything. When they opened the new lines, people rushed and cut people in line...it was terrible. We ended up getting in the park at 8:40 when we arrived at 8:05/8:10. We missed out on most of our "early admission" and by the time we got back to Diagon Alley, the Gringotts ride was already at an hour wait. We were annoyed. That provided no benefit and was ridiculous. Something like that wouldn't happen at Disney!  All in all, a good trip. Another tip is to get the Express Pass...it doesn't work on the HP rides, but it's worth it...it lets you get on rides quickly, so that you have time to spend waiting in line for the HP rides! :) Enjoy!

As a family with a teenage son we much prefer Universal over Disney and this is our favourite.love all the rides,love walking through all the attractions.rip ride rocket,Simpsons and of course Harry potter.we went in a October and the lines were very short,maybe it's the quiet time of year or were we just lucky.love the Simpsons area for the ride and the food court.My son liked the water rides so your spoilt here,same great atmosphere as always.This is our fourth time here but my fist review.If you can go to the fright nights near Halloween make it a must do(separate review).Our best park by far.

We went on a weekday during November and it was not very busy. However I was surprised how unfriendly a lot of the employees were. We barely saw the whole park in one day (one day for each park) and we didn't have longer than a 30 minute wait at any ride. We had a great time and are thankful that it was very slow.
