I couldn't imagine waiting for these rides for hours and hours. It would not of been worth it. My advice is plan your vacation around a slow time of the year....early November and early December seem to be slower than the rest of the year.....check disney world's website ...they have a crowd calender that was very accurate.... Trans formers was the best ride u have been on. Awesome! Island adventures was more rides and the universal studios was more shows and videos. Great change of pace between the two parks.

Visited 11/01. Did not disappoint. Drove from VA. as this was on our bucket list. This is a very crowded event and even though it is expensive I highly recommend that you purchase the express pass to avoid the very long lines. Without the express pass it would be impossible to see it in one night. As it was we saw 8 haunted houses, 2 live shows, and took 2 rides, but we did hustle to do it and would be impossible without the express pass. This is a great event ,but is definitely not for pre-teen and younger. They should see the mouse. The haunted houses are well done, but as they get crowded, not as scary. The dollhouse was really freaky. The shows are definitely worth seeing. I particularly enjoyed "The Rocky Horror" show. Do it but bring money, it was close to $400 for the two of us with tickets and express passes, but worth it.
Great place for the young and old..not as crowed as disney..you don't half to worry about long parades..a lot to do just walking and eating

We went to Universal Islands of Adventure and Universal Studios the first week of November 2014. There were seven of us ranging from 5 to 63. We all had a good time but the 8, 10, and 41 year males had the very best time. The rides were excellent, full of special 3-d effects and explosions. A little too much for the 5 year at times and I admit that after a while I just wanted a break from the noise too. The Hogsmeade and Diagon Alley attractions were wonderfully done. They were crowded but we were able to ride all the rides we wanted without too long a wait. The rest of the parks were less crowded so again it was easy to do experience the rides. There weren't very many shows to see at Universal. I enjoy Disney more for that reason but the horror show was funny and a nice break. The Seven Voyages of Sinbad could have been much better and actually it was better done the last time I saw it. Overall, Universal beats Disney in price ( they were running a special - 3 days for the price of two) and excitement for older kids. I love Disney but they are pricing themselves out of the preteen and teen market and are falling behind on special effects ride.

My 2 kids and I (15 and 12) Had a great time last night at HHN. We expected a heavy crowd which proved true for a Thursday night. The value at $45 for FL residents is good. Lines are long though and suggest to be there prior to 6pm as they opened early at 6. My son went off on his own with friends. My daughter and I were able to get into 3 houses and most rides. Both shows were good though I don't think that Bill and Teds was as good this year. Had a few laughs.

We absolutely loved universal we bought a 2 day pass. My daughter & husband are a Harry Potter fan, they couldn't wait till we got in to go to Daigon Alley. Yes we got in at 8 am so we could miss the massive que's. We found that whole place exciting. The Gringotts ride was excellent so was the other Harry Potter ride it felt like you were flying on broomsticks and part of the action. Oh yeah, don't forget to try the Butter Beer it was to die for. You won't be disappointed make sure Universal studios Florida is on your to do List. Definitely we will be back.

Visited here in early November. Absolutely love Universal, I prefer it to Disney as I find the rides a lot better quality and more variety. Took advantage of Virgin's early access, so went in at 8am. There were a lot of other people there at that time, but this was to be expected, especially with the new Harry Potter Diagon Alley section opened. Rides amazing, would visit time and time again!

Lets start off with Diagon Alley. I'm not a massive Harry Potter fan but even I found the new Diagon Alley area amazing. The level of detail, the quirky little shops, everything about it was incredible. Next time I'd definetly want to have a go on the Gringotts ride but it had just broken down and the queue was 60 mins long.  Aside from Harry Potter there's loads of other great rides in the parks like The Simpsons, Despicable Me, The Mummy etc plenty to do for the whole day. Probably more suited to older kids and teens, whereas Disney is for all ages. Wouldn't hesitate to go back to Universal.
If you can get a day pass and visit both parks, you will not be disappointed. There are so many simulated rides, even those afraid of heights would enjoy this. I know I did.

Got the two park pass for Universal Studios and Islands of Adventures! For a family of four I spent around $550 just for a 1 day entry! It probably would have benefited us to get the express pass, but this day I opted out. Lines aren't crazy bad, about 30-45 minutes. Other than that. We had an amazing time. Especially my children. Can't wait to come back, hoping to find a great deal.

As a 40 plus old dad I had just as much fun as my 5yr old. Rides are incredible!!!! Go for superman and transformers and get your pics taken with transformers ,,, if it had been warmer water rides looked awesome.

We went to see the Harry Potter attractions, which were amazing. Since we weren't interested in the rides, just touring the buildings and attractions, we didn't have long waits. The Hogwarts Express train ride was lots of fun and a great way to go between the two parks. Very long lines for butterbeer, which was good but very, very sweet.

I went for harry potter. But left having experienced so much more. What can i say went on all the rides loved them all. Have to say transformers was absolutely amazing. I never rated these kinds of rides until universal. They are amazing so well done. My 5 year old loved the minions and et. Great experience. But please car park charges are a rip off

What a wonderful family trip to Universal Studios Florida. It took us two 9 hour days to see and do everything in the park, 4 days total with Islands of Adventure, and frankly, it wasn't that crowded. We rode every single ride and saw every single show, and loved it all. The few coasters they have are TERRIFIC. My kids LOVED all the motion simulator rides (minions and simpsons were their top picks) and of course the Harry Potter themed rides, attractions and shops were AMAZING! I hated having to pay extra for park hopper tickets to ride the Hogwarts Express. It is a fantastic, not to be missed attraction, but I had no other reason for the park hopper pass. We bought interactive magic wands for each child. They will likely never use them again, but they had a BLAST making magic during our visit to the park. I'm not sure if it was $50 worth of magic, but very magical, none the less. If you can, let a wand choose you in Olivanders shop rather than purchase at the push cart. My hubby loved the butterbeer. We also had ice cream from the shop in London. Long line and expensive. I picked chocolate chili, which the clerk seemed to be trying to talk me out of (too spicy, he warned) but it just tasted like chocolate. I would have ordered the lavender instead, but no taste tests allowed. We had lunch at Moe's on day and the Irish pub one day. Moe's was good, except weird holding pen area before they would let you approach the food counters. Lunch the other day at the Irish pub across from the Mummy. Took forever and just OK food. The evening water and light show when the park closes was great. worth staying around for. The worst ride was probably Twister. I miss JAWS! But overall, GREAT TIME!

If you are into Harry Potter, this is YOUR park! They have a great amount of space dedicated to just this group of movies. I enjoyed most of the rest of the park and would have liked to see some of the older materials incorporated into it. They have a great deal on drinks, buy the souvenir soda cup and get refills for 99 cents for the day. It is worth it. We really enjoyed the Spiderman ride and I did like this park more overall than Magic Kingdom.
I went there and all the rides and shows were worth the price of admission. Lines were somewhat long but quick to get thru.
Probably the best park in Orlando. A lot of Fun and very nice staff overall. Great rides and food. Highly recommend.

My family of four, two kids 9 and 10, spent two days at Universal Studios Orlando. We bought the express line pass which we felt was worth it. We loved LOTS of the rides. The Harry Potter parts in both parks were amazing! They have truly created exactly what you'd imagine. You definitely need two full days - we still missed some rides. We also has a lovely lunch at 'Fisherman's Wharf'.

this was a fun trip booked through Virgin holidays to celebrate the end of my daughter's exams. so we stayed in the Pacific Lowes resort a short walk from the parks...and we had a lot of fun, we rode on every roller coaster, and took every ride available, taking a side trip to Sea World - and rode the roller coasters there too - Manta was fantastic, it is as close as I could imagine being a manta ray could be rolling through the sea. Harry Potter world was great although we missed the opening of Diagon Alley by 2 weeks...but we had such laughs and ate well, and it was so relaxing to be away with no

This was really like Disney for grown ups. Transformers was the best ride I have ever ever been on I was screaming and laughing and crying from screaming and laughing. Loved it. My younger children, though, would have hated pretty much every ride. I am so relieved we didn't bring them even though they were excited about the Minion ride. That would have been the only thing they would have enjoyed. I will stick to Disney with them, but for a group of parents we had a BLAST here! The production value on the rides was amazing and it is just way less crowded than Disney so we felt we had a lot more room to move around. The Simpsons area was great too. Lots of fun photo ops. Also glad we didn't pay extra for the FastPass, we didn't have to wait in any long lines (maybe 1 or 2 were 20 minutes) and we went on a beautiful Sunday.

If I had to measure Islands Of Adventure against this park, I'd have to give it to Islands of Adventure. However, I will say that I definitely think this park is better than the Universal in Southern California. It's almost impossible to get bored here. We rode a couple of attractions here, but spent the majority of our time at Islands of Adventure since we had the hopper option. It did drizzle on us, but I'm one of those that actually appreciates the rain when it comes because what happens when it rains? People go home. What happens when people go home? The park gets empty and when the park gets empty your wait times are next to nothing. See what I did there? I took something that could have been a downer an made it something positive! It's what you do when you're on vacation. Why? Because we can't control mother nature so might as well make the best of it. What I thought was pretty cool was when we got off of the Rock It coaster that not only can you buy your photo but, you can get the DVD of your on ride experience as well. Did I buy it? Yes. Was it expensive? Yes. It's a theme park. You have to expect that souvenirs and food are not going to be the prices we'd like them to be. I think the one attraction that I felt was a little bit of a waste of time was the Disaster! ride. We waited what was quoted at 20 minutes and ended up being longer than that. You wait in the queue, then you go into a room where a gentleman introduces himself and asks for volunteers to star in a "movie" directed by a Christopher Walken (he uses another name of sorts). You then go into another room where you sit and watch these actors act out what they are asked to do. When you're done there then you load into another room and board a "subway" and are asked to look scared when the props "explode" and water "floods". When you're done there is a video made that you view on the "subway" of the actors and yourselves. It's amusing don't get me wrong but, had I known it was going to cost me an hour of my time I wouldn't have done it. After that we made our way back to Diagon Alley. I did a separate review of the Wizarding World of Harry Potter and let's just say I'm really, really impressed with all of it. I do want to point out that I had a blast riding the Mummy roller coaster. It's not a very long ride, but it is pretty theatrical and fun for being an indoor coaster. I can also appreciate that those operating that particular ride made me laugh by keeping in character as you leave the station. I know I'll be back eventually. I love these two parks!

We started at Gringotts to avoid lengthy queues. Loads to take in for Potter fans. Make sure you see the dragon at night for the flames and try the ice cream shop. Amazing. I had apple pie and chocolate. Nice. Went on a tour after this, Men in Black (v good), Simpsons (amazing ride), ET (don't bother) The Mummy (A must do), Transformers (brilliant), Twister (worth it), Despicable Me (Oh yes), Terminator (Fantastic). Stop to admire it all. Great fun and a great day out. Make sure you do the Blues Brothers & Beetleguise review..Excellent entertainment. Enjoy...

I would actually say that this is better than Disney. The park does not take its self as serious as Disney and seems less focussed on seperating visitors from their money. Good gluten free food available in most restaurants. One tip is DO NOT buy snack food a hot dog costs $9.99 without a drink, while for £13 we sat down in Finnagans restaurant had a full meal and drink with waitress service. Best bits Harry Potter rides and Hogwarts, Dispicable Me and The Simpsons. Plenty of Rollercoasters too at Islands of Adventure. One of the other plusses is that there are regular character appearances and plenty of chances for photos with the characters, unlike in Disney where I saw The Chipmonks and Mickey Mouse each for less than 10 seconds as they walked through a wired off section of restaurant. The entire park is geared for everyone old and young. I absolutely loved it.

the rides were great. Transformers as really good. Harry potter same. Twister was ok at best. The Mummy was great. Buy the express line to bypass some of the lines (except Harry potter). Very expensive day. Over 200 a person before food and souvenirs. Lots of fun.. but not sure it's worth it.
Had a great time, will be back next year. Disliked the long lines. We ended up getting special tickets to skip the lines. Expensive but worth it :)

Need I say anymore! The Harry Potter section of Universal is absolutely brilliant, fantastic. The Simpsons ride is great, really makes you think you're with them. The Rockit ride was great. In fact everything about Universal Studios was brilliant. Spiderman, Transformers, Minions, Terminator, Men in Black, all amazing! It's definitely not Disney and is more for the older children who are adventurous. The shows were good too!

Lots of fun. Get express passes and save time and limit stress. Diagon Alley and Hogsmeade are great. My 13 yr old didn't want to leave. The detail is incredible. Felt transported. The other areas are OK. Enjoyed the minions. Take your AAA card as most of the sit-down restaurants offer a discount if you have the card. Recommend a 2 -day stay to take it all in.

We have been life long Disney travelers, but decided to give Universal a try. We arrived the night before Thanksgiving and left the Sunday morning after. We stayed at the Cabana Bay Resort (highly recommend for early morning entry) which we loved.  The bus system was fast and convenient, even when it was crowded. You will be walking a lot, I think we covered 30 miles over our 3 days there ... which is no worse than what we did at Disney. I would highly recommend the Express Passes. Worth every cent if it is crowded. We waited 30 minutes MAYBE two or three times.  We purchased the Dining Plan. It was convenient, but I doubt we saved much money. It was a little slow, it would be nice for Universal to combine entry, room keys, meal plans all on one card, but that is a minor nuisance issue.  Both parks are great. We enjoyed Harry Potter World at both parks. Fantastic. Rides are fun, attention to detail is astounding. Both of the major rides were worth the wait, even without Express passes. Definitely ride the train between the two parks.  The rides at both parks were great. The Hulk was a great ride, as were the Mummy and the Simpson's ride was great fun. The Despicable Me ride was funny. Spiderman and Transformers were neat as well.  Some of the things are a little tired, Shrek could use updating. Twister is a complete waste of time ... who doesn't make a roller coaster with the Twister theme? The wait for the flight of the Hippogriff was amazing sometimes. That ride is for small children, pretty boring.  Every park employee we met was polite and nice. Honestly, the people we met at Universal seemed more pleasant than the employees at Disney based on our last trip.  Could you see this and Islands of Adventure in one day? Maybe. Two days definitely. We were there for three days which was plenty. We felt like we were able to see everything we wanted and then some.  I would be hard pressed to pick Disney over Universal to be honest. Both provide an enjoyable theme park experience. Since I have older children, I think Universal may have an edge at this point.  I wouldn't hesitate to advise people to visit Universal. We had a great time.

I was worried that Universal Studios Florida was going to have outlived it's fun. I was wrong, we had a great visit with the new attractions and rides they've added in the recent years. We came to visit the new Harry Potter Diagon Ally, which was truly awesome for my kids who love Harry Potter. We also had a great time exploring the world built around the Simpsons characters (Krusy, Moe, Lard Lad, etc). We loved the Transformers ride and the Despicable Me ride, also new to us. And the fun rides I recall being there before were still fun - ET, Rip-Ride-Rocket. We spend three days at both parks and I was surprised how much fun we had at Universal Studios Florida.

Make sure you make the trip to Universal Halloween horror nights. Always fun and lots to see. Can get expensive since it's a separately ticketed event and express pass is a must; otherwise you will be waiting for 1-2 hrs per haunted house and there are 8 of them! As for regular visits; always awesome as well. The wait for Harry Potter is absurd and we could never get on the roller coaster; either 90 min wait or broken!!!!

Lots of different rides and things to do for all ages and interests. They have various options for food from fast food to healthier at a reasonable cost for a theme park. May I suggest booking your passes in advance on the internet to save money. Bring your print out like we did and you will save a little money. They use finger print identification to get into the park. USE CAUTION when you buy your passes if you are wanting to also go to Island's of Adventure next door also. If you buy the wrong type of ticket you will not be able to the second park without buying another ticket. The big attraction between Universal Studios and Island of Adventure is "Harry Potter" with a train ride going to and from the two parks. I suggest if you are interested in "Harry Potter" head there first as it is very popular and crowded. A little less crowd when the park opens. Fun day to just have fun and enjoy the surrounding

My partner and I went for a birthday vacation and decided to go to Universal specifically for Harry Potter wizard world. Because we stayed on the property we were able to get into the park an hour early (worth it as the lines do get long) The Harry potter section was just amazing, it was so detailed and interactive, you felt as though you were part of the world and in the movie. Everything was done so well and I highly recommend getting a pass to both parks; Universal and Island of Adventures as both have Harry Potter attractions. I have been to many theme parks but this was by far the best.
what an adrenaline rush.Love this park no ends.the faster the ride the better.Hogwarts great especially the ride.
Great rides, good restaurants, clean, not too crowded. Loved the two Harry potter areas, the hulk ride and Rock It.

I highly recommend searching for deals for your tickets. We were able to purchase three days for the price of two, and it was really the perfect amount of time to spend in the two parks. We spend one day at Island of Adventure and two at Universal. The kids bought wands at Universal and we spent about five hours just in the Harry Potter area so they could perform their magic.  While I liked the 4D rides, there are so many of them they got a little predictable after about the third one. The shows were entertaining, but not thrilling. I do wish there were more roller coasters.  What I really appreciated was that my four-year old (who is 41" tall) could ride a majority of the rides and those that he couldn't allowed a parent swap so that we could all wait in line as a family and both my husband and I could ride... and my teen loved it because that meant she got to ride twice.  We went in the middle of November and the lines were so short many were walk-on. The longest wait was 30-minutes for the Gringotts ride. We were glad we didn't spend the extra for the fast pass.  We did stay late one night to watch the parade and light show. It was worth the wait. Very creative and engaging. The kids also enjoyed it.

We were very young when ET came out and remember I enjoyed the film. Now as a adults, we thought we would give this a go. The first section of the ride through the recreated film action was very enjoyable and a good laugh. The experience went down hill and silly when it went to the alien planet. It was what I would expect a bad hallucination would be like. More like a weird nightmare. I think it's time ET is retired and fresh ideas are brought in.

Diagon Alley is terrific! I am not even among the Harry Potter fans, but my children are. I enjoyed this part of the park as much as they did. The Gringott's ride is really well done, and not too rough (my daughter hates big drops and loved this ride). Even being in the line up is very cool, almost as good as the ride. If you get to the park first thing in the morning this is the ride to do first! The lines do end up being very long, we managed to do this ride twice. If you get a park to park ticket you get to ride the train and the ride each way is different so make sure you go back and forth at least once. The shops are spectacular, only complaint is that the wands are soooo expensive, and I just couldn't justify buying 2 interactive wands for my girls at $47 each. So we just watched the other kids when they were doing the interactive parts in front of the shops. Rest of the park was pretty good, kids liked the MIB ride, but the rest of the park is looking a little dated. Girl who introduced the Shrek ride needs more training, she was reading off a script and it fell flat. Overall would definitely return.

My son and I cannot get enough of this place. We come to Orlando 3 times a year just for a Universal Vacation. The time we are here, we never leave the park. Universal has something for EVERYONE! We have not encountered one rude employee in all the times we have been here. Their staff is over the top nice & very accommodating should you need anything. I must recommend you stay at one of the park hotels/resorts to get your Express passes. The passes are key! Such a great place!!!

What can you say about the universal experience ? As a recently retiree i was not expecting to be impressed with the raz and the matazz of this... However, on exiting the Potter world i had a silly grin and felt like a child again.. Absolulety exceptional. Every detail perfect. If the magical world existed this is what it would be like. AND thats only potter.. Try the minions ride, the transformers ride , the ...... It just goes on and on...a magnificent three days.

I loved universal studios. We did the base package which was visit one park per day. We did the but two days get the third day for free. The only thing with this package is you can't ride the train from park to park. It gets really busy during the weekends and holidays. The rides were great. I loved the new Harry Potter section. It was really busy but worth it. Some of the shops had unique gifts. Some things in the stores you could get cheaper outside the park. The staff were friendly and very helpful. I would highly recommend going to universal Studios. The other park Islands of Adventure has more roller coasters but Universal Hollywood has more charm and shows. Both are great but I think out of the two Universal Studios Hollywood was the best. They had the Despicable Me ride, Transformers ride, Mummy roller Coaster, the Rockn Roller coaster, ET and many more rides. It actually feels like you are in Hollywood, London, New York City and San Fransisco

Its like a cattle market to get in with no organisation at all.  Queues are 2 to 3 hours long within minutes so you are lucky to see three of the 8 haunted houses all night and you will spend 5 plus hours in queues.  Typical hype where they make big promises but just want your money and don't care how many people attend, the more the better in their $$$$$ eyes and they have the audacity to charge you to park as well!!!  DON'T waste your money

This was my family's favorite place to visit in the Orlando area, followed by LEGOLAND Florida and then the Magic Kingdom. I don't even think I can do it justice. If you do Universal, make sure you get the park to park so that you can enjoy the Hogwarts train ride between here and Islands of Adventure so that you get the full experience. Also, the extra wand purchase is entirely worth it to enhance your Harry Potter adventure to try out spells throughout the area. Besides going on about the Harry Potter experience, I have to say, we also enjoyed a lot of other things in the park, including the Shrek and Minion experiences, the Revenge of the Mummy, and the MIB Alien Attack (coolest shooter ride/game ever). Here my kids did not mind waiting in line, they were the masters of entertainment while waiting. One caveat, our first day started with an hour and a half wait at Gringott's without getting any further than just behind the main hall before we left. Apparently the ride broke down (and we were told by a local that it breaks down 5 times a day), but we couldn't hear the announcements about it while we were in line because people are so loud (they need to turn up their announcement volume). So we had bunches of questions, but no team member was around to explain what was happening and then when one did show up, he didn't have any information. They need to make sure that ride works, or get someone to come in and give those waiting in line Express passes to come back and to shut the gates so that no one else tries to come in while the ride is VERY broken and wait for no experience. We never went back to experience that. The dragon on top of Gringott's never breathed fire while we were there. I don't know if it's timed and we missed it or if they shut it down on a regular basis. But after all that, we spent 2.5 days enjoying both Universal Parks. The rest of our experiences only went up from there and in the end Universal was my kids' favorite attraction.

We visited Studio Theme park and Islands of Adventure with our two twenty-something daughters following a cruise.  Had a blast. Went for Harry Potter because it is new since last visit and because my kids are really of the Harry Potter generation.  My list of do's  1. Stay at Hard Rock. Get express pass. 2. Use the early entry. 3. Do all the Harry Potter stuff early before it is too congested. 4. Drink alcohol. Because you can! Great benefit of this park.  Best rides -- in order.  1. Minion ride 2. Dragon Roller Coaster -- red one 3. Rockit Coaster 4. Mummy ride 5. Simpson ride 6. Gringotts ride -- kind of a stomach turner 7. Hulk coaster 8. Other Harry Potter ride 9. The wand thing 10. Spiderman ride 11. Transformer ride  Thing is the simulation rides start wearing you out. So you gotta space them out. Food in park is good and cheaper than City Walk. Plus there are bars and alcohol in park. Happy Hour at Backwater Bar.

Universal has great rides especially the Harry Potter parts. The Minion ride was fun and you get to have your picture with the Minions after. It is worth by the dual ticket to see both sides of Harry Potter. By far their rides outshine Disney parks.
Great park for film buffs , young & Old. Take your own drinks and snacks to keep your costs down. Small queues at this time of year too. Harry Potter wands are fab !

First let me say the park is fun. The rides and other attractions are awesome, but one thing ruined the whole experience for me. I was at the park while there were family issues going on at home. I was trying to have a good time before I had to head home. Everything was great until I went to take a picture with the transformer guy. I got to the front of the line and a staff member made a smart ash comment to me that was totally uncalled for for reasons unknown. The transformer did nothing while I was taking a picture, it would move around and talk to others. I was already having a horrible day and this was the last straw for me. For the money I paid this was a joke. I won't be back.
The crowds were small, easy access during the day to many of the best rollercoasters, had a great time riding multiple times in a row.

Extremely clean,well run facility,exceeded my expectations,all the staff was friendly and helpful.Food and drinks were all top quality,Harry Potter side was amazing,the attention to detail,including the construction fit and finish was impressive.Enjoyed all the rides,including the crazy roller coasters!Don't go here if you are looking for a cheap day out,they are not shy with the ticket prices,all in all,was an excellent experience,definitely way more to see and do than can be done in one day!

Returned to both Studios and IOA aftre a 6 year break and forgot how much I love this place. The Parks have a more chilled out feel than Disney, but in my opinion they are as beautifully created and maintained, if not more-so. As there were only 2 of us this time, we invested in the Express pass which cost about $200inc taxes and I wasn't sure if this was a wise move as the Parks were pretty quiet, but on hindsight I think it was indulgent but smart because we got to do all the rides on both parks, many of them 2 or 3 times in one day, literally walking on to every ride with the exception of the Potter rides. But we didn't mind a bit of queuing for these as Universal have thoughfully created a true experience from the minute you arrive at the ride.I'm not a HP afficienado but their attention to detail was incredible, and I would imagine if you are really into the HP franchise then there is tons of quirky details that would keep you entertained as you wait for the ride, The rides themselves were really good, and Universal have really perfected the 3D interactive ride experience - one cannot compare say. Soarin at Disney with the HP Forbidden Journey ride albiet they are similar types of rides.Well done Universal!! One quick tip - on our 2nd visit, we didn't invest in Express and did single rider on both HP rides and walked straight onto the ride, but you do miss the overall experience - at least you have the option, which Disney have stopped on a lot of their busier rides. Transformers 3D, Rocket and Despicable Me were all new attractions to us and all awesome in their own right.Plus I was really glad that old the old favourites were still there with the exception of the Jaws ride which is a shame as I am a huge fan of the film, but it was a very slow loading ride and I can uinderstand why Universal have utiilised the space with the new attractions. Really, really impressed with what Universal have done with these two parks and in stark contrast to the Disney Parks where little has changed in 6 years and if anything they have gone back-over with their new Fastpass system. Our No 1 Orlando destination - no question,.

I enjoyed my visit to Universal Studios Florida. They have some fantastic rides and themeing. They give WDW a real run for their money.  The Transformers ride and Harry Potter Gringotts were SO fun - some of my favourite rides in Orlando. The train between the two parks (from the Harry Potter areas) was convenient and amusing, but in no way outstanding.  I liked the Universal Studios park more than IOA.

Was a really great time but my only downfall about this was the express pass. I felt like the express pass lanes were a tad unorganized. We could have saved the money because the lines we could use them on we're not long at all. That is my only negative thing to say. Other wise was a fun time.

We visited just before Christmas as the crowds were building. We stayed at the Hard Rock Hotel just for the free fast passes that came with the hotel stay. It was soo worth the money. We waited in line no more than 5 minutes as the standby times were all in excess of an hour! As many reviewers had recommended, we started at Diagon Alley and was on the first car at Escape from Gringotts. And yes, it DID breakdown. We were offered an opportunity to re-ride and we did without any issues. We continued to Kings Crossing station to go to Islands of Adventure to complete our Harry Potter fix. We were able to ride all rides without any wait beyond 20 minutes. We then continued to Olivanders to grab a wand and continue to explore. We were exceptionally impressed with this part of the park! The remainder of the park was just as we remembered from a visit over 10 years ago. Staff was pleasant and helpful. AMEX lounge benefit: We bought our tickets with our AMEX card and accessed the lounge in Universal. We were a bit underwhelmed with this perk. It had a few seats and served water, chips and granola bars. The bathroom needed a good cleaning and was overdue for an update. The walk between the Hardrock Hotel and Universal: This was so beautiful and well manicured. Simulator rides: Due to the fast pass, I rode all rides at Universal and Islands of Adventure and had no motion sickness issues with any of the rides. Do you need a two park pass: Absolutely! How many days is right for you? One was the appropriate answer for us. While we did have a three day pass, we only used one day. We were able to ride all rides with the fast passes and didn't need to return. All in all, a great experience and glad we made the stop.

We LOVE Universal Studios and its sister park Islands of Adventure. The new Harry Potter attraction, Diagon Alley, which links the original Hogsmeade in Island of Adventures via the Hogwarts Express is excellent. Their attention to detail is wonderful although my 2 youngest children found the dragon guarding Gringotts a bit frightening!  Use of technology is great meaning all rides no longer have to be high rise and fast.  Plenty for the younger guests too and the Pets Ahoy show is a must for all animal lovers.  All in all a great place to spend the day with the family.
Great rides, great shows, great food and all around great family fun with something for all ages. A definite must.

Called 2 days prior to arrival to inquire/purchase tickets. 20 minutes on the phone, was convinced to purchase 1day, 2 park ticket with Express Pass for $639.00. We originally thought a 2 day ticket would be the way to go, but the Universal representative's explanation of the Express Ticket convinced us to purchase that ticket.  I was told that I would receive an e-mail confirmation, but that never arrived. Unable to use the self serve kiosk without a confirmation number, we headed to the manned windows to pick up our tickets. The person behind the counter was very friendly, even helping us pick out 4 lanyards for $20.  Our next stop was the entrance turnstiles. Imagine our surprise when our tickets wouldn't work... Off to Guest Services to figure out what went wrong. Discovered that we were sold 4 Express Pass tickets, but that did NOT include admission to the park! It would cost an additional $600+ to purchase 4 admission tickets. Doing some quick math, I realized that it would take a mortgage payment to gain admission to Universal Studios with the Express Pass!!!  Our decision to purchase the Express Pass influenced our decision to change our hotel reservations, so now we can't do the 2 day option even if we wanted.  Adding salt to the wound, we were told that lanyards that we no longer need since we don't have the $650 Express Pass option are non-returnable. Really???  Overall, incredibly disappointed by what I feel is the classic "bait and switch" tactic to get more money from us. My wife and I have saved all year to take our family on this vacation. We couldn't absorb an additional $600+. Now, not only we will be waiting in long lines, but probably won't get on every ride because of the crowds.  Next time in Florida, we will skip Universal Studios and spend the time in Disney, where we have had nothing but positive experiences.  With all of that said, I will be thankful that we are able to spend Christmas in beautiful, sunny Florida!
My party (friends between the ages of 15-25) and I had a great time exploring this park. It was a great deal of fun and I would certainly go there again if I ever wanted to visit Florida again.

I went to all the Disney parks and to SeaWorld, but the rides where not that thrilled and fun as I found them to be in Universal Studios.  I loved how the parks are built up and everything is so identical to how it's look likes in the movies and books.  I loved the Harry Potter parts of the parks where I could spend hours just wander around and be amazed of all the details.  This was the first time I've been here so I'm not sure how often they add new things to the parks, but when I was here there where a few new attractions. The biggest was the new Harry Potter world.  There will be a lot of people here all the time, so expect long lines. For the new Harry Potter ride, there where lines for about 4 hours. If you and your friends / family can be away from each other for the few minutes the rides take, you can make use of the single rider system instead. It will shorten the wait time a lot.

I love everything from E.T. - The Extra-Terrestrial to the big roller coasters! There is something to please everyone. Warning, the Rocket jerks, especially the second car; I ride with my hands cradling my head to cushion it from the bouncing.

I don't do rides, but had fun anyhow. We mainly went to see Harry Potters at Universal and even with the huge crowds had a good time. We bought a two day ticket, two park pass and spent 6 hours each day and did plenty of walking. We were amazed at the attention to detail in the park. There are lockers throughout but some are cheaper then others depending on location. I noticed the lockers near the entrance of Universal Studios cheaper then the ones located in the Harry Potter area. So watch for that. The frozen butter beer was delicious and they cost around $6.50 each, so if you have a family bring extra money. The crowds were much better if you get there early. We got there at eight when it opened and found even at Christmas time it was busy but noticed most of the people come around 11:00 and then we found it difficult to walk around. If you have children, go find the fountain in Islands of Adventure, its interactive and they will get wet but it was great fun to watch and see the little kids interacting with the talking fountain.

We went with our 9 year old, 7 year old and my inlaws over Christmas. To keep our sanity we bought Express passes which were well worth the money but expensive - albeit cheaper than a divorce lawyer! Harry Potter is very crowded but worth the queue for fans. Gringots ride worth a wait. Some imaginative merchandising saw my wife spend a fortune. Away from that we enjoyed Transformers and Simpsons rides!
Better buy a "fastpass" if you want to save money or get there early. Not managed as well as Disney but better than legoland.

This park has less rides than IOA, but my kids love the ones they do have. If you have younger kids, definitely check out Fievel's play area. If you are going to Diagon Alley, plan on it being very crowded. Check out everything...lots of people miss out on the quirky stuff because they are in such a hurry. Relax and look around. Be aware that Knockturn Alley can be a little dark for the little ones. If you haven't watched the movies before, you will still enjoy Diagon Alley, but you will enjoy it more if you watch them first. The train ride from Diagon Alley to Hogsmeade is different than the ride from Hogsmeade to Diagon Alley so take both of them...look out the "window" but also keep your eye on your door "window".

Universal studios offered a lot of fun for the older crowd. There are a lot of trill rides & 3d rides. You can avoid the little kids area if you want. The Harry Potter areas are very nicely done and the Hogwarts a Express is a nice little treat. I didn't give it 5 stars because of the up charge for the express pass.

Its easy to lose yourself being in the states for 2 weeks and trying see everything you can but it soon mounts up. it was expensive eating at universal studies so we ate out for the meals as applebys not to far away.  the rides and attractions were great and the queues not too bad however the gift shops were stupidly priced, we found a walmart not to far away and drove out for the same gifts at one 5th the price

99% over priced shops themed around their various media properties and a few rides you can wait hours to ride. Did I mention the crowds? And the lines? Even to get into a shop? The highlight was duff brewery cause after paying what we paid to get in I needed a beer and to say "dooh"!

It is worth the trip just to see the new Diagon Alley area and experience the new Escape from Gringott's ride. Really well done. Get a wand that allows you to do magic at many shops, try the exciting flavors of ice cream, and just be a kid again. lots of rides for the hard core thrill seekers. Be careful when you go, it can get very crowded. If staying on site, definitely take advantage of early admission and express passes.

rides are great, fun, but lines are very long during peak season, popular ones like Harry Potter, Dispicable Me, and Transformer are at least an hour wait, sometimes can be two hours wait time. Get Express ticket if you want to avoid the long lines and ride as many as you want during the day.

Universal has outdone themselves with both parks now! If you read the Harry Potter books and/or saw the movies don't miss out on this magical experience. Get the park tickets that cover both park admissions so you can ride the Hogwarts Express from one to the other. Additionally, there are so many other fun rides in each park there is something for everyone! We went at Christmas so it was quite busy but having the Express Pass saved each and every day as we zoomed to the front of the lines-a must! It does not cover all rides but is well worth it overall! I would suggest at least 2 full days here to cover both parks and not feel rushed. We did 3 and felt it was just enough.

We went there recently during holiday period and must say that we were disappointed. having been to all 4 Disney parks in Orlando and to local theme parks in NJ, we expected good number of rides/attractions . The good and bad part for us was that due to holiday period, as expected, there were long lines for almost all attractions we wanted to see/ride. This means we spent more time waiting but had it not been for the wait, there are only a few rides/shows that interested our family (included two boys 15 and 11). I agree that the Diagon alley and entire Harry Potter hype is somewhat understandable, don't know if that is enough for most people to travel that far and make a vacation out of it. Their parking is in garage (a plus) but it is so far from either park entrance that during busy times, one could easily spend 20-25 minutes just to get to the park entrance after parking. Citywalk area is nice and has several food options including famous franchise eateries (Moe's, Panda Express, Cold Stone, etc). Since this is a review of Universal studios, I will not include my comments for Islands of Adventure park here, but it is pretty much the same.

This park was so packed, body to body. Lines were 1 to 3 hours long. New Gringot ride was 3 hour wait. Despite the park being busy, Universal was still selling tickets to people in the afternoon. On some rides, you had to walk to a different section of the park to get a ticket so you could wait in another line to get on a ride. We left the park at 2 pm as it was utterly miserable.

Universal has upped their game since I last visited 14 years ago.  Get there early, Universal packs in as many people as they can and lines get pretty long - but the rides are worth it.  We grabbed a Park hopper pass and were able to squeeze in both parks in one (13-hour) day.  Have fun.

We have yearly pass to universal. i 'been there multiple times. (disney is too expensive for my family). we usualy start with island of adventure to wizzarding world of harry potter and takes the rail way to universal studios. i love mardi gras during the springs and macys day parade at winter and water rides during summer. if your kids are older than 8yrs old i would recomend taking single riders to avoid long lines. .. jurasic park is our faviorate. But the ride "disaster" is mostly close down so donot wait on the line,...even though we had great laugh when we go to this ride.. its a shame. overall my family loves universal...transformers also a good ride.

It is an great place to go, most favourite part was the backstage tour of the movie lots, however you will get wet a bit. The rest of the park was really good with some good rides available. TThis was our first time there and it lived up to our expectations.
had a really great time first visit will definitely return everything exceeded my expectation family fun for everyone

I was extremely impressed with this park. My friends and I came here to visit a few days before Christmas and it was a great experience. We had bought the two-day, two park pass for universal studios and islands of adventure) with a third day free which ended up being plenty of time to visit each park, and we only went for a few hours one night for our "third day free." The park wasn't as busy as we expected for a Saturday and Sunday. However, it was the weekend before Christmas, so maybe it's not as busy right before the holiday?  I was really impressed with the new rides and just overall organization of the park. There are lockers available before most rides that are free for a certain amount of time (sufficient enough time to wait in line and enjoy the ride). If you want a locker for a longer amount of time, you have to pay a fee. *And there are also drinking fountains in many of the lines so don't worry if you had to put your water bottle in a locker, you can still stay hydrated.We never had to wait more than an hour and 15 minutes for a ride, and for most rides waiting in line was part of the experience. They pay so much attention to detail that there is so much to look at and pay attention to while in line, so the waiting goes by faster than we expected. The express passes for rides would have been nice at times, but definitely not necessary for us since we didn't mind taking our time through the lines.  The busiest part of the park seemed to be Diagon Alley, part of the Wizarding World of Harry Potter, and for good reason. If you are a Harry Potter fan, this is a must see! They did a great job of making the books/movies come to life in designing this part of the park. Even people that aren't familiar with Harry Potter will enjoy this park. And the entire park has something to offer for everyone: roller coasters, 3-D rides, shows, performances, shops, restaurants, nice scenery, really everything for all interests and ages.  My suggestions for anyone visiting the park is to get the two-day two park pass. It gave us plenty of time to see everything and not feel rushed. The park crowds start to die down after 7:00, so staying later is a good way to avoid longer lines for food and rides.

This place is quite amazing and I only regret only allocating a single day to see everything so i did have to rush. The queues for some of the rides were long but we found it was better if you took the single person queue. We nearly always ended up riding together anyway I think there was only one ride where we actually got split up. I bought one of the refillable cups in the morning for the drinks and this was fantastic value for money. The food at dinner we eat in the Harry potter restaurant which was good value. We did in the evening eat again though and this time I had the cornish pasties and if you have ever had a real cornish you would be disappointed as they are on the small side.
Lines were very long. Tickets purchased onsite & definitions of what is included in the ticket was confusing. Tickets very expensive. Lines for rides were very long & not woth the ticket price.

We love this resort destination. We love the area in general so it is hard to beat with two vacation destination powerhouses almost next door to each other. The Harry Potter additions to both parks has given new life where it was actually beginning to get a little tired for those like us that are annual pass holders. Food is good, rides are great and the people working there are okay for the most part. IMHO Universal really needs to focus on good, quality, customer service training. They are lacking in that area. Other than that we go often.

If you want a real adventure and want to the get the best of all action and sci-fi movies from Universal, this is the place. You will get to experience the best of everything related to Universal at this place. Transformers, Shrek, Harry potter, just to name a few were the best rides i enjoyed. Apart from that the water park that was another end of the park. Paid $175 for it and had a lot of fun and excitement. All worth it. The best rides, 3D theatres, Water park, Roller coasters etc, all come packed in this place. I experienced 4 different Roller Coasters and it was amazing. It has restaurants into it going with the theme of the ride. For Example If you are touring Harry potter, The place will look like a complete copy of what you see in the movie. The restaurants and the people look as if they have come out of the movie. 1 day is not enough to experience it all and i didn't have time to go through all the rides. I was lucky to have as there were not many people in the queue. Harry potter was the one in demand as you start the ride from an actual Train so had to wait for an hour. Overall Great Experience. The best part is Universal changes its themes every few months so as new movies come in, so does a small real world for them and we get to experience it. Their park was so detailed and the staff was awesome. Will definitely go Again.

Had a great time in the new Harry Potter site. The express is a wonderful experience. Makes you feel your reliving the books. Much better than the original on the other side. I did do both and appreciated it much better this time. If you have Harry Potter fans its a must see. The park was a nice as always. The rides are fun. They are updating city walk so there is a little construction in that area. but nothing to slow you down. We went the week before Christmas - which is perfect. Crowd isn't too bad until you get toward the end of the week.

we loved universal. they had great rides, good restaurants, shows, etc. it was easy to navigate, clean and fun. if you are staying on property it is best to go early as the park gets crowded by 1030 and then dies down a bit by 330. so if staying on property you can go back and forth and not stand in crazy lines (express pass is best) there are some good thrill rides (that's what our kids like) and there are some cool movie type attractions to show how special effects etc are created. the harry potter section (even if you don't know much about harry potter) is definitely worth seeing. there is so much detail in the park and it is really fun for adults and kids.

First I should start out by saying I love Universal and am not much of a Disney person. I average a trip to Universal every couple of years and have been at least 5 times and still love the stuff that has become old, as well as new attractions. This 29 year old adult felt like a little kid as soon as I stepped foot into Diagon Alley (after taking the Hogsmeade Express from Islands of Adventure - which requires a ticket for both parks to be able to ride). The authenticity to the books and movies is amazing and the Escape from Gringotts ride was worth the hour wait each time I rode it. The decor is amazing, the ice-cream is worth eating for breakfast, and stepping foot into all the alleyways and shops will make any Harry Potter fan grin from ear to ear. The rest of the park is great too, with some simulation rides, shows, and roller coasters, but Diagon Alley is my new favorite. Get there early in the morning (and if you are staying at a Universal hotel, use the hour early park access to your benefit) as this is a most crowded and congested area by sheer numbers and design too.

I have never seen a more detailed and immersing theme park area than Diagon Alley and Universal Studios. Escape from Gringott's Bank was an excellent ride. The butterbeer icecream is one of the best things I have ever tasted and the treacle fudge in so good, I would buy it buy the cargo container if they sold it as such.  So many good rides like Transformers and Despicable me, but the family favorite was the rip ride rocket. We think it is the best theme park in the world.

We had one person in our 6 person group who had difficulty walking. We went to customer service and asked if they could assist in any way. They immediately issued an express pass voucher for the whole group. They did not even ask for doctor's note (although we had it). We were very grateful and impressed with their customer service.
Highlight was easily the Harry potter parts, they were so well done. The hulk ride was great, and the water rides. Don't worry about MIB or Spider-Man rides through.

It took over 30 years to get to Orlando and it was all about getting to see Mickey and the gang (which was a disappointment - read in one of my other reviews). Lucky for us, we also wanted to see Universal. Universal ROCKS! Both parks! We had so much fun, we are planning to go again next year and make it a full week of it. I'll try to stick to the Universal and do up another review for the other park. Everything about Universal is down to a science. From arriving at the multilevel parking lot, to the security checks, to the ticket booths, CITY WALK, and finally going through the turnpikes. It is all well executed and planned. Then utter chaos as thousands of people go nuts at the park! When you walk into Studios, make a beeline for Despicable Me! Get into it early and experience it right away, the lines will not get smaller as the day goes on. Other must rides - Transformer, Crustyland, Hollywood Ripride Rockit, and the must see Diagon Alley and the Gringotts ride! Talking about Diagon - Potter World on both sides is amazing! My wife isn't even familiar with Potter but she was thoroughly impressed with the remake of the villages at Universal. I can go on about all the stuff to do but I think I will share with you the survival strategies. If you want to spend the cash, get the Express pass - it helps on most rides except in Harry Potter's world. If you want to save some cash, you can do the single park tickets but that means you can't ride the Hogwarts Express Train. This is where they sucker you for a bunch of bucks! If you want to experience Potter, you need the Park-to-Park pass. Oh BTW, the more days you buy the cheaper per day it gets. Now, arrive early! The earlier the better. Be the first ones in the park if you want to get on any of the rides - especially in peak season. If you can go off-peak, you will have the park to yourself. Arrange to take a long lunch break and maybe get in a nap during the high-temperature hours. Go back late afternoon until closing. You will find that most people with small kids will be leaving as you are returning to the park. This helps reduce your wait times and you get to see the park in a whole new "light!" The park really is fun once the sun drops! Especially in Diagon Alley! Pick up your marauder's map and Swear to No Good and have a great time! Orlando is UNIVERSAL! Sorry Mickey - at least you have your Princesses.
Very expensive but express pass well worth it. You get to enjoy day. Only ridiculous waits were harry potter experiences where express passez not accepted. The train was cool but unreasonable wait

Universal Studios in Orlando is a fun theme park for everyone. The Harry Potter areas in both Islands of Adventure and Universal Studios are sure to satisfy the most rabid fans. Get the park-to-park tickets to access the Hogwarts Express which connects both Potter worlds.

A group of four of us stayed at Loews Royal Pacific Hotel and bought the park-to-park tickets for a fun day at Universal. Thanks to the express passes we had thanks to staying on property, we got through both parks in one day! The rides were really fun and great for more adventurous people. We were impressed with the level of customer service and organization we saw throughout the parks. We ate at the fast food area in the Simpsons section of Universal where we went quickly through a long line to order the most yummy chicken and waffle sandwich. After paying for our meal, we were quickly escorted to a reserved table. No more hoping to have a table after paying $15 pp for lunch!!! They really were so organized and pleasant and that was the best meal in a theme park...ever. (And we are all Floridians that have grown up going to theme parks on an annual basis.) We also appreciated the free lockers and the advanced technology used (finger print recognition) to lock up our things. We were really blown away with the overall experience at Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure. We look forward to another trip soon!

An excellent place to spend a few days on your vacation. The two Universal parks are very different in nature, so prepare ahead of time by looking at the online guides and maps. Hollywood Studios is more shows, medium thrill rides, and places to sit and relax/eat (with a couple of roller coaster rides). Adventure Island is geared more toward rides and thrills. Hogwarts and Harry Potter spans both parks, with the majority of the shops and atmospheric street section on the Hollywood Studios side. VERY dark and wonderful area. Even the crowds added to the atmosphere..you really feel like you're shopping for your owl, wand, and "stuff" to make your stay at Hogwarts more comfortable! Escape from Gringott's is spectacular fun. Hogwart's Express Train to the other park is great fun. **Warning**: there are a LOT of stairs to climb..both up and down. If you have anyone in the party who has trouble with stairs, there are lifts.  We had 2 seniors who weren't keen on rides, but loved the shows and walking down the "old time" streets, 2 adults who loved everything, and 3 adult mentally challenged men who were in 7th heaven all day. As with Disney, there is a lot of walking to do to get into the park, and around, but it's certainly worth it. Buying tickets online and either printing yourself, or picking up at the "will call kiosk" saves you $20 off the gate price and is easy to do.

Well, Since 2005 I've been at Universal 9 times so it is clearly our favorite theme park. This time we had a few issues, but the gust relations service is taking very good care of us. The Harry Potter atractions are simply amazing, and I only miss the Back to the Future ride, which turned into The Simpsons ride a few years ago. It's a nice one, my wide loves it, but BTTF was just awesome. For those who have lived the 80's it was a very nice one. The one I can't explain how can it still have people interested on is the MIB. That one is not worth a 1 minute line for me.

We weren't happy as we purchased tickets for the park and to get fast passes you need to purchase express pass which is another expense (didn't buy) then while we were going to the rides all of them said 10 minute wait but yet when you went in it wasn't a 10 minute wait but 25 minute or more. We went to MIB ride and we are not allowed to have any bags with us and we have to put them in a locker which says free for 30 minutes. Well the waiting time that they announced was not correct. When we came out of the ride to get our stuff it said we were there for 45 minutes and we had to pay $6.00 as we had to take two lockers. We were lucky that my husband had some change on him as my wallet was in the locker. We were really disappointed with Universal this time and don't think we will go back.

This place is seriously well made! I prefer this to Disneyland as it's cheaper, and well suited for older kids. Disney is more for younger children who still believe in magic (Unless you're going to the studios part..) I love the food, the kindness, the atmosphere! Too amazing! I love this place and I will be coming back soon!

We are big WDW fans. The first time we went to Universal, we figured it would be the last. Until they built the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. We are big fans of the movies and decided to go to Universal again. Both Sections of Harry Potter have Raised the Bar!!!! The 2 big Rides, Harry Potter and the forbidden Journey, and Escape From Gringotts are Game Changers! Both are incredible rides with different elements of rides combined into one, 3D, Interactive, and Thrill. We will go back again on our Next WDW trip, just for the Harry Potter stuff. Be sure to ride the Hogwards Express both ways as it's a different experience each way. The only downside is the shops are small and with big crowds, it's hard to even look around in them.  The Rest of the park is just OK. Not impressed with Island of Adventure with the exception of The WWOHP. The Hulk is a good Roller Coaster, and Spider man is a good ride however, it's like several of the other rides at US.  I like the Studios side better, Aside from Gringotts, the Mummy is still the best ride there, Again many of the other rides are the same type of ride. I always love to see the Animal Actors. Maybe time to get rid of Fear Factor, that show hasn't been on in 10 years.

We bought the 1-day PTP VIP and worth every penny, you can skip long lines, and get over the attractions anytime you want, except for the ones at Hogwarts Castle. We have so much fun, and we visited both parks, Universal Studios and Island of Adventures. This park is better for kids, because there are many attractions for them, and adults too. The Hollywood Rip ride Rock it is a must. You can´t miss the Hogwarts Castle and all the attraction from the wizarding world of Harry Potter, you can feel like you are walking down Diagon Alley, visiting Gringotts, the stores, everything. It was awesome.

E.T. Adventure is a really great ride and so immersive. I have watched E.T. several times so I knew the story well so to sit on a bike and 'fly', like what happens in the film is absolutely great, a must do!

We normally visit the Disney World theme parks but decided to also spend 3 days at Universal Studios this time. At this park all attractions are based on the film industry. This makes visitors feel like they are in a movie set with rides, shows, and attractions inspired by popular film, television, and music productions. We enjoyed the Amazing Adventures of Spider-Man. This is a motion-based 3D dark ride located at the Islands of Adventure where you get set to soar with your friendly neighbourhood Spider-Man. The Jurassic Park River adventure was also very enjoyable, where you are taken on an unforgettable river raft ride through the jungles and see dinosaurs in their natural habitats. You are stalked by these vicious raptor’s but eventually escape their terrifying jaws by doing a 26 metre (85 feet) sudden drop in total darkness in your craft ending in a huge splash. Remember to wear a protecting poncho during this ride. We were fortunate to have done the Twister special effects simulation attraction that was due to be closed. Here the guests line up on a tiered observation platform under a corrugated metal roof, overlooking a simulated outdoor scene featuring a view of a rural drive-in theatre. A well simulated tornado drops from the sky, and rain begins to fall where visitors are squirted with water from above. The tornado wrecks the drive-in screen, the diner, and a car, which causes a fireball to erupt, while a cow, lifted by the wind, flies past the spectators. Another popular attraction is the exhilarating Incredible Hulk roller coaster that does seven inversions, two vertical loops, and two corkscrews. As the name suggests, the ride is themed after the popular comic book superhero character, the Hulk. We are not supporters of the witchcraft and wizardry based Harry Potter series and did not do these rides. The advantage of the Harry Potter rides being there is that it attracts most visitors leaving shorter queues at the other attractions. The Universal Studios fast pass system costs extra and is not as efficient as those at the Disney World theme parks.
We forgot! Wall to wall people and literally couldn't move at times -- not enough staff around to issue tickets OR to help with directions. Most staff we did see acted indifferent or hid!

We've been here quite a few times before but were lured back to see the second part of the Harry Potter expansion. Our adult children had not been to the parks in quite some time and we only had one day and they wanted to see both parts. The cost was almost $600 for tickets for that one day; an extra $35 each to be able to ride the train and go to both parks. Diagon Ally was essentially one new ride (The Gringotts Bank ride lasted all of about 90 seconds) and a bunch of shops and atmosphere. Hogsmeade is essentially one new ride (Hogwarts), a few reworked old rides and a bunch of shops and atmosphere. I felt like I spent $125 for the four of us to ride a train. Worth one trip, period. You have to walk through the entire park to get to the HP areas (very smart, Universal because a lot of the other stuff is truly bogus or meant for small children). The other thing I noticed is that there were not many benches or other places to sit if you had to wait for others in your party to get off of a ride (I think this is to keep the visitors spending in the shops).  I don't think I will be back.

This is the larger of the two parks. and its Harry Potter section is a real treat. It is indoors and is like entering a different world, The rides and events are more plentiful than Islands of Adventure and hard to accomplish in just one day. Food, restrooms, and ways to spend money are everywhere. Check out the Universal web site for endless details. A great park!
Went as a family and every one of us loved it. Would recommend going at Halloween for terror nights - words cannot describe!! Fantastic for all ages but especially if you're a thrill seeker like me!

It has been many years since we were here and they did have new things to see. It is more for people who like roller coasters. If you can, we recommend getting a fast pass, otherwise, when it is busy, it is an hour wait.

My family and I absolutely loved universal studios.We loved it so much we returned in Nov/14.Bring plenty of spending money as food,drinks, etc can get pricey like any theme park.I would recommend universal studios to my family and friends.

We only had one day to visit, so we paid $229 PER ticket for an express pass to both parks figuring that we could get in most of the attractions faster and ride most of them. It wasn't until we got to the Harry Potter attractions and asked the attendant where the express pass line was, that we were told the outrageously priced tickets that we purchased did not cover the Harry Potter rides and we would have to wait in the regular lines, which were 60-70 minutes all day. When I told the attendant that we were not told this, he said "it's written on the ticket." Hello Universal, how can you read the ticket until you have purchased it and they give it to you? And it is buried in the rest of the fine print along with the verbiage that you can be injured and die and you accept full responsibility. I really feel this was deceptive, deceitful, sneaky and greedy. We likely won't be back. Fair warning to everyone else. Other than that, the new part of Harry Potter was well done. Some of the other attractions definitely need replacement or upgrading.

This was my favorite park of the two. I like the 3D animated rides that tell you a story. They do have a few older rides that really need updated, but the newer ones are very cool. I would recommend doing the park fast pass if you can. We got it included with our room staying in Park property hotel and it was so worth it. I think there where only 3 rides you could not use it on and they where all in Harry Potter. The rest you can and you just show it and get in a special line. We never waited more than 20 minutes and some of the rides had posted 60-90 min waits. We where easily able to do everything in one day and a few rides twice with these, not the case without.

Loved the rides here! The Harry Potter portions are awesome. So much friendlier to adults and older kids than Disney, in my opinion!!! The only "rides" (not sure why the park categorizes these parts this way) that I wouldn't recommend are Twister and Disaster. These two segments kind of suck, frankly. Tip: staying at one of the on-site hotels is definitely the move because you can walk to the park and you get free fast passes. Loved it at Universal!!!

Universal is so much fun! There's so much to do and see and is perfect for all ages - would definitely recommend getting fast passes if it's not too expensive as they make the day so much better because you save so much time in the queues and it means you are more likely to go on every ride you want to.
We had fun at Universal just wished we had booked two day at their parks. We didn't get to do everything

This place is amazing. We had the best time! Experiencing Diagon Alley was absolutely magical, I didn't want to leave :) We got to see the Knight Bus right on the streets of London, got to call the Ministry of Magic, hung around number 12 Grimmauld Place in order to see Kreature peek at us, and visited so many fun shops (Knockturn Alley, anyone?) and got to ride the Hogwarts Express. We had the BEST time in the Harry Potter part!  The rest of the park is pretty awesome, too! ET is such a fun little ride, the kids had a blast. Transformers and the Men In Black riders are awesome as well!  This park is laid out very well, not nearly as crowded as Islands of Adventure feels :)

We spent three full days at the park and were very impressed with how clean and how enthusiastic most of the workers were. We stayed for the movie and fireworks the first night and it was very enjoyable. By far being Harry Potter fans we enjoyed Diagon Alley and Hogsmeade the most. The Forbidden forest ride was awesome--even enjoyed walking through the castle to see the things along the walk that entertain you as you wait. Dragon challenge added fun roller coaster thrills and Escape from Gringotts was also great. Everytime we went on the train between the two places we would see something new. We enjoyed the food at the three broomsticks more than the leakey cauldron as one of the party loves turkey legs--which were excellent. We tried all three types of butterbeer and liked them all. In the other part of the parks we liked the transformer ride, and the animal actor show a lot. We did the ET ride for nostalgia as we all loved the movie. Some of the rides were awful though--Twister was the worst as they herd you into one area and then another area and then you get to stand to watch a lame storm and lightning and trees falling over. We did not have small children in the group so have no information about the rides for little kids. All in all we had a great time and would return again. There is a lot of walking involved in the park experience so make sure you have good shoes.

We were four adults with no kids spending five days at Universal Studios and Walt Disney World. It was great to be a kid again! We had a blast. The whole Harry Potter experience was on my husband's bucket list and he was not disappointed! From the Hogswort's Express between Diagon Alley and Hogwort's (an event in itself) to lunch at the Leaky Cauldron (must have the hot Butter Beer! a butterscotch delight) to the fire breathing dragon atop Gringotts Bank to the amazing animated goblins in the bank (or maybe they were real?) to the Gringott's ride with its awesome 3-D effects, our first day at Universal was so much fun. If possible, Hogwort's School / Castle was even better. That 3-D experience was outstanding and you really felt like you were flying as part of the Quidich games (among many other special effects, but I won't spoil the surprise).  But Harry Potter was just the beginning. We loved the roller coasters. I was surprised at the reviewer who felt that Universal needs an overhaul! The roller coasters were far superior to Disney's offerings (talk about dated and lame - the 45 minute wait to ride Space Mountain was ludicrous..) The Incredible Hulk, the Aerosmith roller coaster, the Rock-It and the roller coasters that were part of the Harry Potter experience were thrilling. The entirely forgettable one that dropped you several stories and lasted 15 seconds was one of the exceptions. Plus the kid in us loved the Dr. Seuss area - we even did the carousel.  The Express Pass was a rip-off. We did it the first day at Universal to the tune of $280 for the four of us. NOT WORTH IT! However, we were lucky because we went mid week in Jan. and so even on Thurs which was a little more crowded, the waits (without the pass) were reasonable (10-30 minutes compared with the 100 minute waits for rides at Magic Kingdom on Friday!)  Don't miss the shows either - we saw the stunt shows including Raiders of the Lost Ark were great fun. The Great Movie Ride highlighting some of the best of Universal Studio movies was among our favorite (but then we LOVE old movies!) Don't bother with Disaster (we waited too long, it took too long and it was VERY lame!)  What is worth the money is to do the preferred parking for a few dollars more $25 instead of $17. It was much easier to get to your parking with this pass and even closer to City Walk. And also worth the money was the excellent Blue Man Group show on City Walk. We had no idea what to expect and it was absolutely delightful fun. Special effects, music, audience participation that was hilarious, comic and whimsical and indescribable. So you have to see it for yourself.

Loved the newest attractions of Harry Potter! WOW! They've done such a wonderful job from the beginning when you walk around the corner, you're transformed into a different world! They've tied it all together and the Gringotts ride is amazing! We ate at the "Leaky Cauldron" and had a beer there too! We also did the thrill rides too, very, very good! You have to have a 2 park ticket to ride the "Hogwart's Express"! Fun for all ages!

1ST holiday in Florida and from the walk through Citywalk to the park it just amazing. From the Minions ride to the Transformer 3D its just brilliant but I have to say the best ride there has to be Transformer. Food prices alittle steep but then again its the same at all theme parks but still found it was cheaper then Alton Towers lol. The park was clean and being it was August when we went, Florida does get the odd thunderstorms and when it does the rides normally closes until it passes but the storms do not last very long at all so it didnt spoil our time in fact it cleared the humid air and it was a lot fresher after the storm. Harry Potter had the longest q time but it was worth it. Throughly enjoyed our time here and we cannot wait to return in the future.

With the addition of Harry Potter's Diagon Alley, Universal Studios has jumped back into the list of excellent, world class attractions. Beautifully themed, particularly the New York, Hollywood and San Francisco areas, it is a joy to walk around and has a good selection of rides, stores, shows, for all ages and tastes. It is Diagon Alley and the Hogwarts Express that are the jewel in Universal's crown. With such a rich back-story to draw on, thanks to JK Rowling, the detail is incredible and extensive. The London entrance to the Alley is absolutely authentic and is a clever way of hiding the real attraction until the last possible moment, with a spectacular 'reveal', which is not signposted (but follow the crowd). The flagship ride in Gringotts Bank is wonderful and not too traumatic for those with weak stomachs (i.e. motion sickness), unlike its ultra hi-tech sister in Hogsmeade. No review of the park can omit the Hogwarts Express ride betweeen London and Hogsmeade in Islands of Adventure. Ride it both ways for the full experience, which is just like an 8 hour train journey compressed into a few minutes. One downside of the park is the requirement to stow loose articles in a free locker before riding the roller coasters etc. There is no queuing system and narrow entrances to the locker rooms making the whole process a free for all.

If you like simulators then this is the park for you! There are some absolutely fantastic attractions in this park.  The new Transformers riders is top class & The Simpsons ride is also fantastic.  There's too many to name but they're all really good.

We've been coming here for years, but we usually only get either a one or two day 2 park ticket. This year we were staying for the whole week, so we got 7 day 2 park tickets. That was the best thing we couldn't done. We came specifically to go to the new Harry Potter park in the Studios park. It did NOT disappoint! It is a fantastic park, better than the Hogwarts one in islands of adventure in all but one respect. The Forbidden Journey ride in the Castle is still fantastic after all this time, but the Gringott's ride is not worth the wait. It's boring and the time you spend in line is boring as well. I know no one expects the time you spend in line to be fun or interesting, but the line for Forbidden Journey is fun once you get into the greenhouse. While the greenhouse could use some more interesting plants, etc., the castle is fantastic! I love going through Dumbledore's office and the part where they have a video of Harry Hermione and Ron talking to you and it starts to snow. That is definitely magical, even though I've been on that ride several times. I'm telling everyone I know not to bother going on the Gringott's ride unless there is NO line.
