Other than that, everything is incredible! I do not know how they could've possibly made it better. The only things that had disappointed me the first time we went to the Harry Potter park at islands of adventure was that they had very few stores with stuff you could buy and they didn't have a train ride. They have addressed both issues wonderfully. The train ride is fun to take each way and the new Diagon Alley park is so much fun. It is full of stores where you can buy all kinds of wizarding supplies. My favorites were Quality Quidditch supplies and Fortescue's Ice Cream. The ice cream was delicious and you can get strawberry and chocolate, just like Harry. I like that you can get all kinds of quidditch related shirts at Quality Quidditch Supplies, including t-shirts from the world cup! Tons of people were purchasing entire wizard outfits and walking around the park in them, so that, of course, added to the fun. There are also interactive things you can do in the streets(alley) and you can also go looking for dark things down Knockturn Alley. It was so much fun. We used our 7 day pass by going first thing in the morning every day as soon as they opened and going on as many rides as we could before 10 am. If you stay at a Universal hotel you can actually get in an hour earlier than that. Around 10 am, the park starts to get more busy, but since we've already filled our ride cravings, we just relax and walk around the park for a while before heading out. A few days, we ended our park day by going to the movie theater next to the entrance and seeing a movie before heading back to our hotel. A tip: we do not bring any bags with us so we do not have to stand in the bag line. It gets us on the rides much quicker. The one thing I was sad about was how hard it was to find my favorite Harry Potter candy, Pepper Imps. They were not to be found in any of the Harry Potter stores but, thankfully, I found them in one of the stores in the other side of the park.

The rides are good and the sights are interesting but between broken rides, employees who didn't know the facility and being nickel and dimed at every opportunity we will never go back or give a recommendation. They lost things that were to be delivered to our room and we had to spend time tracking them down. Employees couldn't answer questions and sent us away instead of finding answers. Character appearances were few and very short. The evening show was down for maintenance. Rides were not operating. And the biometrics system created huge delays everywhere it was used. Two days to let the kids see the characters then go to Disney. And as I type this they missed our taxi reservation and forced us to use the Loews service at a higher price.
We had a great time spending the day at the park. The park was only open till 6 so it was a bit rushed but the day went by quickly and everyone had a great time..

I hadn't been to Universal in years until last week and wow has it gone from great to amazing! The addition of Harry Potter is no doubt the highlight but it doesn't stop there. So many improvements have been made and so many great rides added, my husband and I are in our 30's and we seriously felt like kids again. Free lockers at all the rides requiring them, excellent friendly staff and great food. MUST SEE.

this park is fantastic! We went here really excited for all of the new attractions that had been brought out since the last time we came and we couldn't have been happier! My family loves despicable me and we couldn't wait to try out the ride and we absolutely loved it. the mummy is a great ride too, usually with not much of a wait. the rip ride rockit is amazing, just so different to anything I've ever been on. So much better than Disney in my opinion - a must visit!

I went here with my older daughter who was 14 years old. We decided not to take the small children and it wasn't for them. This was a wise decision. Its geared for teenagers and older. It was an entertaining day, film sets, acting scenes good rides. The evening entertainment was additional and very expensive.

We enjoyed the park very much. It impressed us every day how kind, patient and friendly the staff were- every one of them that we encountered or saw other people speaking with!! It surprised us that some of the 4 D rides were 'vigorous' to ride to say the least! Especially the "minions" ride! Fun, fun, fun!!

Not only is Universal awesome, its simply a better value than Disney. The one day ticket is about the same but when you expand it to a 3 day ticket its hard to beat. The Harry Potter World is simply the best attraction I have ever seen in any park in my 37 years of life. Incredible and not to be missed. If you have children that are 7 or older, you might want to consider this park instead of the traditional disney visit.  We had a great time and we will most definitely be going back.

They've got it nailed. Great experience for young and old. I had so much fun at Dr. Suess I was embarrassed, it's a "Kids" area but it made me a kid again! It has ten thousand reviews, not much else I can add that has not been mentioned before.
This was our third visit to this park. We see something new each time we visit. It is best to go during the off-season if you can. The crowds are much smaller and lines are shorter.
Shrek, Horror Make-up, Disaster. The restaurants were pricey as expected. The lines were short this time of year.

We ha fun, my husband and I are in our mid twenties and overall it was a good time. The lines are long for all the rides, but we still had a good time! We will definitely bring the kids back, also the ticket prices are kind of high!
Guess I hit it at the right time, the most time waited on a line was 15 minutes! Transformers 3D was Excellent!
So many worlds to explore. Just enjoy yourself and do as much as you can. Try not to rush and pay attention to show, parade and ride times

Stayed at Cabana Beach Hotel. Plain rooms, ugly dining area, nice pool, good bus service to park. Park has great architectural features, especially in the Harry Potter area, and was very clean. We were very disappointed with the downtime of some of the features. In the two days we were there, the escalators were down twice as were the moving sidewalks, the Hogwarth Express between the parks went down after we waited in the line for a half hour, several of the rides were down when we were in the park (Twister, Disaster, Transformers). You understand machines may have downtime, but when you pay this kind of money for a limited time to enjoy all the available features, you don't have to accept it.  Make sure you understand all the options when you make your reservations. The reservation people in St. Louis have probably never been to the park and don't understand how all the options interact. In retrospect, we would have chosen the upgraded hotel which includes some of the options for which we paid extra.  Also, we would not have gotten the dinner package. In order for it to be economical, you need to use all features completely. We tried to get a drink at one of the food carts. Turns out this particular food cart only accepted cash. The next one was out of the product we wanted. Just too much trouble.  In summary, very neat place but go but get a book before you decide to sign up. The park doesn't provide much detail, so we picked up a book by Kelly Monaghan that was very helpful.

I went during the first week of February, so the line was not long. I pretty much went on all the rides in one day because I used the solo line, plus like every year, the first week of February during the weekdays is not long at all.  Favorite ride was "Disaster".
My 5 Year old loved it. I recommend the speed pass, lines are way too long well worth the price. Harry Potter was amazing and my son enjoyed the interactive wands.

Second time we have came over from the uk for a theme park holiday,this time staying in a universal hotel mainly to go to universal. I just love both parks,we went 11 straight days and no day was the same.all the staff are so polite and enthusiastic that you must have a good time(good job). There's so much to do here and for an even more special time come at Christmas with all the extra stuff on,like nothing you would ever see in the uk. Everything is overblown which I just love about the place. Problem is you will never want another holiday because universal is like Lapland it's where the magic happens.

If like me you like a bit more of a laid back park, then this might be a bit more to your taste than islands of adventure, the men in black is a fun ride for all the family, but I do miss the old jaws ride and king kong.

I had a great time when I went to universal studios, and the rides were great. The lines got long but that's the same at every park. It's a great way to become part of the movie excitement or experience. Go ahead and take your family!

The Despicable Me ride and the Simpsons ride were excellent as was the Men In Black ride. Many of the other rides were too intense for my youngest child or he was just too small for them. We stayed at the Loew's Royal Pacific and had the express passes which was wonderful because the lines for most of the attractions were long and whenever it rained (which was almost every day with pop-up summer thunderstorms) the coasters shut down which made the lines for the other attractions even longer. The nice part about the express passes is that you can ride the same rides over and over without waiting in the regular lines. The evening celebration was less than spectacular, especially if you have been to Disney and are expecting that level of production. Glad we got to see it, but once was enough.
Family had a great time here. There were more fast paced thrill rides. We didn't bother with fast pass and we still did everything in one day

It's a nice place in the off season....Just don't go during Halloween nights or around Christmas weeks until after New Years, it's good for a few weeks until mardi crowded nights on the weekends. We have a season pass. Been too all the Disney stuff but we like Universal the best overall the parks here in Orlando. Disney parks are okay if ya never been there, animal kingdom is just like abig zoo but not worth the money to me but a good time is had with kids. For teens go to Unaversal both parks with at least two day pass but three days is better to make it through long lines in the busy season. For example you can wait for Harry Potter rides for 3 hours during busy times or during off season can wait for 30 min. My favorite rides at Universal is all of them! Universal city walk has great places too eat too but bring a big wallet. Everything is overpriced in the whole place, just bring in your back pack a lot of snacks and just split meal. It's all fun.

Can't event repeat how much it cost our family of 5 for the day for just Island of adventure park. 75% of the park is food or stores while only 25% are actual rides. We bought the fast pass so the kids wouldn't be discouraged waiting on lines but not sure we actually needed them for all that money and the lines weren't as bad as they could have been. The Jurassic ride the kids were forward to closed. We could have done so many things with all the money we spent for only one day in Universal.

This amusement park is top class, with a theme that is nicely held together through the entire park. The attractions are top class and in a good variety. Our 5 year old tried everything except the Mummy. The tour around the film sets was all about selling of course, but was a great tour still with a lot of interesting things to see, from film sets, attractions, filming tricks and some history.

I visited this with my son and daughter 2/11-2/15 and was impressed once again. Disney gets a 5 because of cleanliness and overall attractions & experience. That said, I like the experience for adults of using child swap (children who don't meet the height requirements) so grown-ups can have a little fun too! We didn't purchase the Express Pass (additional cost), but on our next visit, we will invest in that ticket option to further enhance our experience. On Valentines Day, which was an extremely busy day, too much of our time was standing in lines. If you can, pay for the Express Pass and enhance you're experience.
With the exception of the long lines, Universal is fun for all family members of all ages. Lots to do and lots to eat! Love the huge and tasty turkey legs. Oh and the Butterbeer!!!

Went to Florida in the middle of winter to escape all the snow in Jersey. I enjoyed all the rides and Harry Potter was my favorite. 2 Hulk and 1 Spiderman ride made me throw up but the fun didn't stop there. I had water and ate a little and I was back in action! lol

When two of the major attractions at the park are closed for the day, then the tickets should not be full price. I really do believe it would be cheaper and a lot more fun to visit Potter attractions in Scotland (save on a charge card for flyer points).

Great value especially if you buy the 2 park annual pass! It includes parking and you get discounts on sit down restaurants and store front merchandise sales. It pays for itself in 3 days. Multi venues of things to do and see and ride for everyone.

Our national annual convention returns to Orlando approximately every 4-5 years. Every year that we are in Orlando, we take the Youth Leadership Council (mostly seniors in high school or freshmen in college) to Universal and Island of Adventures.  POSITIVES: * The kids were so excited about the variety of rides. Highlights included anything Harry Potter, the Spiderman ride, Hulk roller coaster, Transformers, and Minions. * They liked that most of the rides were geared toward their demographic (not younger kids) * The parks are easy to navigate (big circles with LOTS of walking), and they're close together.  NEGATIVES: *Harry Potter was divided between the two parks which was very confusing for the kids. *The parks close at 7 p.m. We went on a Sunday and a Monday, and by the time we finished our meetings, the kids had precious little time at the park because of it's short hours (the Disney parks were open much later) * The way into the parks is through a very crowded and congested Universal City Walk... it was impossible to keep the group together and several kids weren't sure where they were supposed to go to see the specific rides. Considering their closing time, time was a precious commodity and not everyone got to the rides they really wanted to see. * We were here a couple of years ago when the minion ride first opened. I was so disappointed to see how run down it looked after just a couple of years. Props were coated in dust and things were faded. At the end of the ride, there is a "Minion Dance Party"... my first time I saw that, the room was filled with staff dressed in overalls and hardhats and would dance with you as you got shepherded into the gift store. This time around... there was one lone girl dancing. People seem to miss the fact that this was supposed to be a dance party and just sort of walked around the girl, wondering why she was dancing by herself. Sad. * The parade... what a let down. The Minion float looked so sad and tired. It was obvious there were places for two "live" minions on the float, but only one was present. The person inside barely moved and never turned from side to side. The float looked faded. The other floats had characters that surprised me they were still using (such as the Easter Bunny from the movie "Hop".... didn't that movie bomb? Why are we seeing a character from it? Odd.) * Staff... there were times it was very difficult to find someone when we had questions or needed directions. When we did find staff members, they weren't too pleased to interact with the public.  The worst part of my trip was the Minion Ride. I already explained above about how it is looking worn and tired, but there was more. The family who was in line in front of me decided to call their relatives back home just as we were finally at the front of the line. They FaceTimed their relatives and spoke so LOUDLY that I couldn't hear any of the pre-ride animation from Gru, the minions and the girls. The parents were so loud and the kids complained that the ride's soundtrack was too loud to talk on the phone. Um... yeah... turn off your phone. The family and I were forced to share one "car" of the ride. Three separate staff members saw this family talking loudly on the phone, but didn't say a word. The family held the phone up for their relatives during the ENTIRE ride. They were rude and obnoxious, and still the staff members didn't say a word. As we finally got off the ride - which I couldn't hear anything - I wanted to talk to a staff member to see if I could ride again so I could actually enjoy it, but they all turned around and went the other direction. It was awful.  After the park closed (again at 7 p.m. on the weekend), we wound our way back through the City Walk area. Several of our group got lost and had trouble finding the bus again on the first night. It wasn't a great experience for us this year. Very sad.

Great rides, less crowds than Magic Kingdom. I'd say it has less to do for the little tiny ones, which make it a plus if you have older children and teens, because the "stroller parade" is over at the other park!

Is the park expensive as pointed out by some disgruntled reviewers? Sure! But look at the expense of keeping the park up to the expected standards of cleanliness, and reliable operation; not to mention logistics and staff/performer pay. Is it a cash cow with opportunities to give up your cash at every turn? Sure! But what business doesn't charge what the market will bear? The entertainment provided was almost uniformly good and, despite the fact that I'm 62, I thoroughly enjoyed my time here - So much for one reviewer who feels that this is no place for a childless couple! I don't enjoy thrill simulators, but my wife does so I found other stuff to do, and we both enjoyed the "kiddie" entertainments. I would go so far as to say that, if you can't find a couple of days fun and entertainment here, without necessarily spending a dime on anything but food/drink, you may be a humorless grouch. Personally, I even had great fun in Woody Woodpecker's Kidzone and the Simpsons section of World Expo, which were primarily intended for a younger demographic or Simpsons fans! The Wizarding World of Harry Potter was so exceptionally well-done that it was probably our favorite area. Having seen everything we wanted to see, and knowing that changes would be minimal in the near future, we might not be back; but we still had fun.

We got express passes w/ our hotel so We got to see & experience just about everything Universal & Islands of Adventure had to offer. We were there during Presidents Day holiday week so it was busy but still got to see everything we wanted. The train trip between parks was so much fun and the creators / builders did an awesome job with it. Diagon Alley was amazing, was so packed you could barely get around one day but the next day we got into all the shops - really an experience. The Gringotts ride broke down & had to reset it but is a truly wild ride worth doing twice. Missed the Jaws ride but happy to see Universal changing things and keeping it current. The Despicable Me ride was fun but if you have back or neck issues most of the rides can cause some discomfort. The MIB ride was okay but only worth riding once. We were happy to see the security at one of the roller coasters turn back a too short child for their own safety. This shows that they truly take safety seriously, the parent wasn't happy but better than seeing the child being thrown from the coaster & spoiling it for everyone. We ate lunch at Finnigans Pub, good food, quick service & the servers were very pleasant. This was an expensive trip with the hotel, both parks & all the meals but worth saving & splurging occasionally.

We're Floridians but have not been to Universal since our children were young. So when our son and Fiancé` actually wanted us to join them for a couple of days; we were all in. The price of 2 day/2 park tickets were only $40 less than buying Florida resident annual passes, so we went for the annual pass and are glad we did because it took the pressure off everyone to see everything in 2 days. My husband and I don't know a lot about Harry Potter; even when the kids tried to tell us about different phrases and themes we were confused but that doesn't take anything away from this part of the park. We enjoyed the Harry Potter area; which covers both parks - so anyone wanting to go for the Harry Potter experience - you need to have access to both parks to enjoy everything. Butter Beer!! Awesome. We don't know much about Butter Beer except it tastes delicious!! We are kids at heart and it was very refreshing to see new eye popping rides; new themes, grown-ups with wands making parts of the park a "hands on" experience. We also just loved the Simpson's, the Minions 3D was terrific!! We were there on a Mardi Gras day; it rained the entire day but we hung in for the awesome food that is served; professionally crafted NOLA good eats!! The lines, at times, were very long but we had an Express Pass. I would recommend paying for an Express Pass if you are coming for only 1, 2 or 3 days. This park is so massive; there is so much to do and to be entertained by. You're paying to get in to enjoy, spend the extra money for the Express Pass if you won't be back for another year or so. There are lots of things to do that there isn't a line for as well. The park offers something for everyone, great food; great spirits, places with full bar and really nice places to eat that are not too expensive. Unlike another large park in Orlando; we were able to bring in food to munch on, water to hold us over if we needed a light bite. We liked that. The staff was very nice and accommodating; the park was very clean and well kept. We stayed at a resort hotel; so coming and going throughout the time-frame of our stay was the way to go. Especially with little ones who might get tired and need to "reset" - we're adults and needed to hit "reset" during our time Staying at a resort hotel also allowed us into a park an hour earlier; another plus!! We barely scratched the surface on everything there is here, so we'll be back for sure and love the annual passes so we can take our time and enjoy everything over a period of time because it will take more than 2 days to hit it all.

Although in the park during President's Day weekend with larger than expected crowds, we had a great time at the Harry Potter exhibits. All well done and looks like stepping into another era. No grandkids with us but we enjoyed the kids using their wands in the various parts of the park.

We came from the uk and bought a pass to cover both parks for 2 weeks... We got more than our money's worth out of this!  The rides were all great only a few not suitable for our kids (ages 6 and 9) plenty of characters to see we LOVED the transformers and marvel area x  Food and drink on park is very reasonably priced as were gifts and photos.  The staff here were all brilliant... Polite, helpful and enthusiastic about there jobs.  I accidentally took my phone of a roller coaster on the last day needless to say it didn't make the ride but we didn't notice until returning to our hotel... Customer services were very very helpful and even posted it back to me in the uk.  All in all I'd say that universal most definably have got this right and maybe Disney should have a little visit and see where they are going wrong.  Can't wait to return when our baby is ready to have the Florida experience .... Thank you universal for an awesome couple of weeks!!

Universal is a great park for families and people of all ages. Our family first visited this park when our kids "outgrew" the Magic Kingdom. I was astounded at how much better the rides are at Universal. The first time we went on the Spiderman ride I'm sure I left my jaw on the floor of the cart. Most of the rides are fast and furious, so buckle up, hold on, be amazed. The only show I would not see again is the Sinbad stunt show, which was seriously so boring that I felt sorry for the actors. A word about Harry Potter. We visited for the first time when the Harry Potter rides were only in the "Islands of Adventure" park. The last time we visited in November 2014 the newest Harry Potter rides were open in Diagon Alley, WHICH IS IN THE OTHER UNIVERSAL STUDIOS PARK! SO, to do all the Harry Potter rides in one day, you will need a two park pass. You will not be able to go on the Hogwart's Express train unless you have a two park pass as this is the "ticket" to get on the train. This doesn't seem to be explained on their website, and I would think it would be disappointing to not be able to go on the train, especially as it is one of the biggest Harry Potter icons. We made the decision to spend the extra money, and were able to purchase an "upgrade pass" to the other park at the Hogwart's Express ticket booth (an extra $140 for 3 people). Since we did this after lunch we had to wait in a very long line to board the "train" to the other park as most people were switching between parks around mid-day). I would recommend at least 2 days, as you will need two days to do it all (we did 2 parks in one day, but only went on the major rides, used the front of the line passes, and race-walked from one ride to the next. We left at close of day, just in time to see the fireworks out the rear window.

I enjoyed Universal Studios slightly more than Islands of Adventure because the transition from one themed area to another was seamless. From Hollywood to New York to London to Springfield, everything was fun and exciting. The hidden entrance to Diagon Alley was and awesome, awesome surprise! My only drawback was about the seating on some of the rides. If I can fit into the seats for Revenge of the Mummy, then I should be able to fit into all the other adult rides, right? The 5:00 parade and nightly cinema show are worth seeing, so make sure to make time in your day to see them both. Have fun and stay hydrated.

My favorite of the parks. The Harry Potter exhibit at both were excellent. There was a lot to see and do. I personally liked the Toon Lagoon area and all the great tributes to comic strips of days gone by. The Simpsons area was also a lot of fun. Of all the parks we have visited (and we have visited all of them), this was our favorite.

Even with the light rain at the start of the Mardi Gras parade, the parade is still an event worth going to and watching. Everyone around us got plenty of beads, and we were right by the Twister attraction. We were right next to the stage where Heart was going to preform, and got a great place to stand.  Ann and Nancy Wilson can still rock and the show was well worth going to see. It lasted right at an hour and a half, and for free who can complain about that. They played all the hits, even a tune from Paul McCartney and Wings, and the encore was three Led Zeppelin songs! Had a blast, and we will return again.

Having been to Disney a few times now it was time for Universal Studios. We are snowbirds and had already been to Citywalk for an evening and really enjoyed it. We went to Studio with daughter and teen granddaughter expecting so much. First had to pay $17 for parking. Then a lot of walking just to get to the entrance. Great first impression upon entering. Shops, food and more shops and food. Where is anything to try? Our first tour was Poseidon and what a disappointment. Finally got to HARRY POTTER ! WOW, the buildings are great. The ride was great. Then the rest was only so so. Day two was at studio park and first look was good. Of coarse Harry Potter area was really nice but shops, shops and more shops. On to other things it went downhill. A few good very short rides and that was it. We were so disappointed to be so disappointed. It cost $834 plus $34 parking for 2 days for 4 people. OW !!!! Biggest mistake: don't think it will be as good as Disney. It isn't even close. Wish this had been a great review but........

This attraction is great for young children who do not care if every ride is the same with just a change of characters. There is nothing clever, no surprises, no great fun! One exception: Blues Brothers mini show on the street. Staff were friendly for the most part. The biggest complaint I have is that there is none of learning about how pictures are made, no learning experiences at all. Where is the "adventure" and where is the "excitement?" Not a single "extraordinary" moment. Even the fireworks at the end were what you can see in small town America on any July 4th.

As we were staying at an onsite Universal Hotel we visited Universal Studios many times over our holiday. What a great place, especially now the Harry Potter area has all been completed. Still got many other decent rides and attractions too - Transformers is amazing, ET is a classic, Men in Black is addictive, the whole Simpsons area is surreal, with Kristy Burgers, Donuts, Duff Beer at Moes and of course the ride, the Mummy always surprises me with the speed and the Disaster ride is definitely a must. There are plenty more rides including the new Harry Potter train ride to Island of Adventure and all the amazing buildings in Diagon Alley. Plenty of good food outlets, not bad prices considering you are a captive audience. Free lockers available for those rides you can't take your bag on. Overall, great theme park - my favourite of the two... As we were staying at one of the onsite Hotels, we got the Express passes for free - these were brilliant so we didn't have to wait for any rides, (apart from Harry Potter) if you can afford it I would recommend getting some..

I also missed jaws! We went and it was far too hot so I feel I would have enjoyed it even more if the sun wasn't blistering my skin and making me gasp for water lol. Been twice and both times been amazing. Especially because I am a harry potter fan and love love love how they dress it all up. The harry potter ride is fantastic. I also love the Simpsons so loves going into the kwik e mart lol. You can't come to Orlando and not come to universal. We were staying in disney so it is quite a trek if you don't have a car but we were able to bus it through avid research. Enjoy!

Me and my BFF went to Orlando the last week of February 2015 - this turned out to be one of the best vacations I ever had! The hotel we stayed at was wonderful! Me and my BFF are 52 and we were like two kids while we visited Epcot one day and Universal three days! We had so much fun at Universal and the Island of Adventures! We were glad we bought the 3 day pass - we got our monies worth! We did both Harry Potter towns and most of the rides - you would think you were actually in a Harry Potter movie/book - down to every detail - it was amazing! Then we did Dr. Seuss land - so much fun! We went on several rides throughout the days we were there. My favorite ride was the Mummy - we rode it 8 times! There was a photo desk there to purchase your photos and the folks there were super fun and friendly! Everyone and I mean EVERYONE at Universal was so friendly and so helpful! From the souvenir shops, to the rides, to the restaurants....if you had a question, they answered it. If you couldn't find a store, they would give detailed directions on how to find it or in a couple of cases walked you to the store personally. I have never seen anything like it before! It was clean and pleasant and fun! I will definitely go back again - it truly is the happiest place on earth!!!

When I read about the different parks, I did not realize Universal is not just one Universal park ....it's 2 parks. My bad. And when you arrive, you can go left into Islands of Adventure with Harry Potter highlights or right into the other park....and if you'd like to go into the 'other' Hollywood side, it will cost you at least $50 more. When you times that by 4 it's bloody expensive. An ordinary bag of Lay's potato chips is $3.19!!! That's extortion. I really don't know how families can afford to do more than one park even with packages over several days. This is ridiculous. However, the park is clean. The few rides are impressive. The staff is friendly everywhere. If you go on the log ride, take along a cheap rain poncho purchased at any convenience store for about $1 because on the Universal grounds they charge you $8. The price is $106 per person for one side but a bit less expensive if you combine both parks. We used the valet parking which was convenient and right outside the grounds. When we finished, hot and tired, it was very nice to walk a short distance and have them bring us our car and off we went.

Can't seem to find a way to only review this ride, so posting it here: The Escape from Gringott's ride in the new Harry Potter Diagon Alley area of this theme park was a disappointment. We were in the park during the slow season, and even though were able to get onto the ride quickly, we only rode once. (During peak season, be prepared to wait hours!) The queue line is fun, and can be walked even if you don’t want to ride – just bow out when you get up to the final staging platform. [Note: don't select the single rider line, or you'll miss the whole queue.] You will walk past rows of “bankers”, with many of them seeming to look right at you, and one who speaks. There is also a holographic interaction with two of the Potter minor characters that is really well done! The ride itself is very much like Spiderman and Transformers – a 3D interactive ride that moves your car through various spaces while Voldemort and his friends torment you. We found the storyline of the adventure fairly boring, and many of the interactions with the bad guys rather tame. Spiderman was amazing (no pun intended) when it opened, and is still considered to be very good entertainment. Transformers learned from Spiderman, and is even better. As the latest 3D experience, you would think Escape from Gringott’s would have topped both the older rides. But we didn’t think so. We did it once – we probably won’t ever ride again.

If you go here make sure you get the 2 park hopper ticket to go on the hogwarts express. Especiallu if your a harry potter fan. Such an amazing day. Parade not as good as disney but definately 10 out of 10 for the performers effort.

I prefer Universal over other parks. The main reason is every time I go to another park I spend 9 hours there and go on 3 rides...I bought an annual pass for both parks. Great rides for all ages and other options like City Walk make it easy for any group to have fun. Usually 8 out of 10 rides have med wait time and 2 or 3 have very long wait times. The only reason I didn't do 5 stars is because their rush-speedy pass what ever it is called cost as much as the ticket. .

The parks and city walk were great. Wish the weather was warmer and there was more sun. We celebrated our 36th anniversary. The hotel gave us buttons to wear and all the staff wished us good wishes. We loved the Harry potter @ The Island of adventure, but the one at Universal park was closed for repairs. The parks were very clean and welcoming. hope to return in better weather. We definitely recommend the express pass and meal plan card. We would like to stay at the park in a hotel again...maybe one a bit less expensive that Portifinio

We have actually placed our review on both Universal parks already. And sharing our opinion of recent stay at Hyatt Place near Universal we mentioned that it was just a short walk to the Parks, but forgor to provide you, folks, with a navigation. Here it is. If you happened to stay at Hyatt Place Universal or Holiday Inn & Suites Main Gate, to get to the Parks you first have to cross Major Blvr, then (Double Tree Hotel at the Entrance to Universal's guests can join here), right there, cross Kirkman Road and keep strait along Major Blvr. until next crossroads (just two min), and there turn left on Universal Blvr. for another 2 or 3 minutes walk. Follow Valet Parking sign to make your walk shorter. From Hyatt (the most distant of all three hotels) it took us less than 20 min. to get there. Enjoy it!
Universal studios made our event a wonderful adventure for all ages. I can highly recommend as a "got to" for you next Florida event.

Visit London and go through the back of the Leaky Cauldron to Diagon Alley, where you will find all the wizarding shops. Don't forget to get a Park to Park ticket so you can go from Platform 9 3/4 through the brick wall between Platforms 9 and 10 (you really see people going through the wall) and ride the Hogwarts Express to Hogsmeade at the Islands of Adventure. Don't miss Minion Mayhem, MIB, Transformers, and The Simpson's town. there are movie props everywhere, blink and you will miss something.

I spent one day in each of the Universal Parks. I bought the buy 2 day, get one day free pass (never had time to use the third day). I didn't want to pay a lot of extra money for a park hopper ticket, just so I could ride on Hogwart's Express. I had two amazing days in each park - the highlights of each were the Incredible Hulk roller coaster & the Transformers 3D ride. There are single rider lines for a lot of rides, which really cuts down the wait times. There are lockers to use nearby the rides for free - each time you ride you can safely store your belongings, which was great for me as it meant I could bring my digital SLR camera into the park too. The food inside the parks was terrible. Luckily, if you walk outside to the city walk area, there are better options, eg. Moes Southwest Grill. I took the I-Drive Trolley bus to get here ($2 per ticket), so didnt have to pay for parking. The technology on the rides is simply amazing. Thrilling day out!! This is an extremely popular tourist destination, so expect crowds and queues - no matter what time of the year you visit!
Travelled as a group and we all agreed it was our favourite theme park. So many great things to do. Loved the Hulk Roller Coaster and the Harry Potter Ride.

on our 4th visit to florida we decided to visit universal studios and island of adventure. we brought a 14 day returns ticket allowing us to use the parks as much as we wanted over the 2 weeks. it cost $17 to park for the day.  it took us less than a day to visit all the attractions in less than one day in the studios. i found the day very boring as i have a visual impairment and many of the 3d rides made me ill.  my children had a good time but i was disappointed that there was not more to do. also some of the rides were closed.  we didnt return to the park despite having a 14 day ticket
Loved Everything! Lines were not outrageous and loved that they created lines inside with atmosphere to keep you occupied while you wait. It also keeps you cool! Harry Potter was amazing!

I was so excited to visit Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure. I went with my almost-eight-year old and her cousins and aunt and uncle: 10 people all together! My eight -year-old was just barely tall enough for all the rides so I caution families with young children to watch out for the height limits and make use of the child swap lines in some of the rides. We did all the Harry Potter and hit the highlights at Universal Studios in one day. All other reviews are correct in saying that it's too much to expect to get all parks done in one day, but I felt we did everything we wanted to, and still ate at the Three Broomsticks and had ice cream later. So, I loooooved the new Diagon Alley It was too fabulous. You must go. Hogsmeade and the train ride were also a delight. The Forbidden Journey in the castle in Hogsmeade was perhaps the "urp"iest ride... Still way cool and exciting and scream-inducing but also your lunch might jiggle around a bit and make you feel sick. We also loved Transformers and the rest of the party loved The Mummy Returns as well. Really awesome 3D effects in all of them. Will so go again. And maybe take it easier on the butterbeer before riding the Forbidden Journey!

For the third year in a row my wife Sarah & I visited Orlando and Universal Studios is a must-do for me as a huge movie buff and also for Sarah who is a big fan of the Harry Potter books & films. We visited in June of 2014 in the hope that Diagon Alley would be open but alas it was not to be. We returned last month and finally rode the Hogwarts Express which was not a disappointment. Diagon Alley is an amazing achievement (as is the whole park!) and even as a non-Potter fan it's difficult not to get caught up in it all. Try the peanut butter & strawberry ice cream from Florean Fortescue's - it's fantastic. I had to try a Flaming Moe in Springfield USA but was disappointed to be charged nearly $10 including tax for what is essentially an orange soda with a little dry ice in a themed cup.  Photo ops with various Universal characters are common - I had my obligatory pic with "Doc Brown" by the DeLorean - and the superstar parade is great fun. Looking forward to going back in a few years when we will have our first born to take with us - he's due in May (this trip was our last hurrah before parenthood!!!).  If you're travelling from the UK try magicaltickets.co.uk for your park passes - we have used them for all our Orlando trips with no problems and the prices are very competitive.

Our family enjoyed this park; we loved loved Harry Potter area. Understand that with the new additions it is even better. My kids are teens and kinda went through it rather fast (except for the attractions which involved lines etc.). Harry Potter was great even though the lines were ridic and area crowded it was still very special so great job on that. I think Jurrasic Park was here too - if so that was a hit too.
It's been a while since we visited universal studios. The alley was setup with all kids in mind. Rides where super. It's not spring season yet but its getting crowded. Plan and arrive early!

My adult daughter wanted to see the Harry Potter, so unlike our usual trips to Florida to visit the Mouse, we went to Universal Studios. Since Harry was our main reason for visiting, I'll talk about Diagon Alley first. The facades that make up the stores, restaurant, and ride, are beautifully detailed. That being said, there are not enough places for nonriders of Gringott's to wait. There are very few benches. My daughter commented that since there are so many facades that do not have stores, seating could easily be added. There are wands for sale, generally between $36 - $44. The wands are interactive at numerous spots throughout the section. However, after waiting your turn to do the same action as the previous half dozen or so Wizards, there is no mystery as to what is going to happen. The requisite robes are available from child size to adult 4X. Most sell for $109. They are made of polyester, which I think would be ridiculously hot to wear in Florida weather. But, not only did we see whole families with wands and robes, many also had scarves around their necks. I suspect heat exhaustion is a common occurrence in Diagon Alley. The only ride in Diagon Alley is in Gringott's Bank. The theming is remarkable and the chandeliers are gorgeous. My only regret is that you can't carry a camera with you to take photos of the queue, because all loose articles must be left in a locker or with a non rider.  Several of the rides throughout the park require that loose articles be placed in a locker or with a non rider. When we first got to the park, since our hotel room wasn't ready, we took the carry on with us and put it in a locker at the park entrance. I would suggest that you take a picture of the locker number, if you take advantage of one of these lockers because at the end of the day, after using about 6 lockers located at individual rides, we couldn't remember the number of the original locker. We almost couldn't get our stuff back. If we hadn't finally remembered the locker number, we would have had to wait until our things went to lost and found after the park closed, to be retrieved the next day.  While I am still a Mouse girl, I did enjoy my visit to Universal Studios.
You cannot fail for fun at Universal studios and Islands of Adventure. Make sure you get park-park tickets. :)
Really enjoy Universal, the new Harry Potter part of the park is excellent. We went at Christmas so was able to watch the Macy Parade which was excellent.

Valet parking is excellent but universal is noisy, dirty and full of long queues and fed up looking staff. Really disappointed by the whole experience couldn't find anywhere to sit and eat so left about 3pm. Spent my whole life believing the hype and saved long to bring my children. I will try Islands of Adventure as I have stupidly bought 14 day passes for the whole family but have no idea how anyone could spend more than a few hours in this place without going nuts, never will return.
With the new add ons this park is better than Islands in my opinion. I loved the Transformers Ride and the Simpsons area. Looking forward to going back!

This place is wonderful and actually might be better than Islands of Adventure. The new Diagon Alley Section is great but only has 1 ride. But There are tons of other rides that were fun like the Minion ride and Transformers. I will re iterate in what I said in my Islands of Adventure review. I think there are way to many shops/restaurants as compared to rides. But still a great place to visit even just to see the new amazing Diagon Alley. I also love the Hogwarts Express. Will definitely come back.

We had been at many of the attractions around Orlando all week and were looking forward to visiting Universal Studios.  We queued up for a while (not too long) and noted the cost for 1 park for a day and though that's a bit expensive considering the size of a park against Disney.  Secondly we noticed that you don't get any free fast passes for rides so have to pay nearly double for this making is ridiculously expensive.  I decided not to go in due to the crowds and price, I'm glad I didn't as fellow travellers said that unless you got a fast pass you waited forever to get on rides.

We stayed at an offsite hotel and spent about 3 days in total--about 1 at each of the two parks at Universal Orlando Resort. There are a lot of motion simulation rides. Certainly much more than what I expected. Line ups can be very long, upwards of an hour-and-a-half for the more popular ones. The train between Hogsmeade and Diagon Alley are worth the wait, but I would rather walk the long way back to the front of the park, and walk all the way to the other park's Harry Potter area (the Wizarding World is near the back of the park). If I ever go back I will buy express tickets. Just walking around was pleasant enough. All in all, Harry Potter = lyfe.
Had 2 young kids. Park was laid out very well, wait times were not as bad as Disney. Connects easily to Island of Adventure by Harry Potter train.

Had a wonderful time at Universal Studios is a great time! The roller coasters are so much fun. The new Diagon Alley section of Harry Potter World looks just like in the movies. The food is just like an English Pub. We really enoyed it and the entire family had fun.

Good old Universal is still awesome, more so than ever before. Remember that Islands of Asventure is a separate park that requires a separate ticket, just 5 minutes walking over the bridge from Universal. You can do both in one day if you purchase the express pass (highly recommended) but you should probably start with Islands of Adventure in the Wizarding World of Harry Potter and ride the Forbidden Journey because that ride gets long lines and does not accepr express passes. After you are done with Islands of Adventure come to Universal and ride: despicable Me Minion Mania, Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit, Revenge of the Mummy, Transformers 3D, Springfield, Men in Black Alien Attack and E.T. Adventure (because it's a classic). If you have spare time you may also consider Shrek 4D (show), Terminator 2 3D (show) and Twister (show). Overall great park with tons of dun things to do.

We were very excited to visit universal studio and therefore we made a note to reach there around 8 am and I am glad we did it because we were able to get in almost every ride and hardly we had any wait time. One thing for all future visitors try to reach the park early morning so that you and your family can enjoy the rides before the crowd hits and you have to stand in long queues. I loved the transformer ride and Harry Potter ride and rocket ride. Important thing to know for families who buy snaps from universal studios. They have a awesome deal of unlimited soft copies plus 2 8*6 prints for $69. So if you are planning for memories this deal can be good option for you. Happy Vacation to all future families coming to Universal Studios.

One word describes it - Fantastic.  £120 for a fortnights unlimited access is a bargain. We were staying in Universal's Cabana Bay Beach Resort so we had 8am access to the Harry Potter Rides in Islands of Adventure, so not Escape from Gringotts, and Hogwarts Express only from about 8.50. All the HP rides are worth the wait. The Forbidden Journey is certainly not for the faint hearted and Escape from Gringotts leaves you wanting more.  * Be aware that you require a two-park ticket to get on the Hogwarts Express as it connects Universal Studios with Islands of Adventure.*  From 9.30 onwards the waiting times are around 1 hour fro the HP rides and for the more popular rides and experiences including The Hulk and the Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit roller coasters and Despicable Me: Minion Mayhem.  It is worth getting the official Universal Park app, which gives you updated wait times as well as information on eating places other park attractions and events. WiFi is free and reliable throughout the parks.  Plenty of exciting of up-to-date rides and some old favourites.  Lots of reasonably priced eating places in the parks and on the Universal Citywalk, which is accessible without having park tickets. However, for most of the Citywalk restaurants you will need to book days in advance if you want to eat after 5pm.  *Express Passes and Single Rider Lines.  Unless you buy an Express Pass you will just have to wait your turn. With an Express pass on some rides you will get on more or less immediately but for the more popular rides you may still have a 20-30 minute wait.  A pass is only valid for a specific date, which you have to choose when buying it.  You can buy them in the park or on-line and the pick them up at the Will Call kiosk present outside the park entrance and at the Universal hotels.  There are only a limited amount available for each day.  They are not valid for the Harry Potter rides.  Strangely, they can be shared but only one person per pass per ride. Eg if there are four of you two can ride while the others wait, once the first two come out the other two can go.  They come in two versions: Standard allows you to skip the queue once on each ride. Unlimited allows you to skip the queue as many times as you can fit into your day.  If you stay at one of Universal's premium hotels (not Cabana Bay) Express Unlimited passes are included for the duration of your stay, but you still need to buy your park tickets.  Depending on the season and the day of the week the Unlimited Pass cost varies from $60 to $140 (+6% tax) per pass per day. The standard pass is around $20 cheaper. There are no discounts for buying multiple passes.  If you can fit it into your budget it is worth getting Unlimited Passes for one day. However, if you do not mind your party getting split up for the rides a good alternative to the Express Passes is the Single Rider Lines, which are available at most, but not all of the rides. The Single Rider Line is often shorter than the Express Pass queues, but they are not suitable for families or couple where you need to sit together.  Have a fabulous time.

Our visit to Universal Studios was great. My husband and I had a great time. We enjoyed so much TRANSFORMERS, HARRY POTTER, SPIDERMAN, THE SIMPSONS, SHREK...and if you are into more adrenaline you cannot miss HULK.

The Universal Studio offers a different variety of shows and attractions versus Disney. I suggest paying a little extra for the fast pass to get ahead of some of the lines. It is well worth it. However, don't get the VIP Fast Pass unless you really want to go on a ride more than once.

Ive been to Florida and the parks quite often with my own family. U we never took our kids as infants and I see why quite clearly now. Anyway you cut it the day is long and juggling having an infant is tough on both mom and grandparents. I must admit the park staff was gay about allowing parent share which is having one parent ride then once exited the other parent can ride. Better than waiting in long lines all day. We hit all the main attractions but took us with walking and waits from 9am to 9pm. You couldn't do this any faster without Express Pass which is cost prohibitive in my opinion. Renting an electric cart is a blessing and to be honest I'd get one, without canopy, even if it was for you ger families. Great place to relax and sit when only concrete is available. So in a nutshell, go in offseason, rent electric chair, don't buy Express Pass and kids should be 12-13 at least for Universal.

The park without the Harry piece was outdated and not a match for Disney. The rides were ok but the showed were lame. My favorite ride was the rock-it ride. The Harry Potter part was great. Every detail was great. Even the muggle London was like a real London feel. The Harry Potter restaurants were very good. Over all the park was good. Good to see but will don't be back for a while.

We came here primarily for the new Harry Potter area - Diagon Alley and were not disappointed. Honestly, could have stayed in just one area and never gotten sick of it. The amount of authentic detail was amazing. I probably spent way more than I should have as every shop had something interesting and must-have (if you are a Harry Potter fan). We also loved the puppet and singing shows by the Gringotts money exchange. My husband is a huge Simpsons fan so we did eventually venture out of this area and he really loved that area as well. I would recommend getting the unlimited express pass if you plan on coming at a busy time of year (especially if you have kids) as the lines for some rides were very long (at times over a 100 minutes). Had a blast and can't wait to come back again.

Fabulous day out. First visited the Terminator 3D show, worth every penny of the entrance fee just for this alone. Spent the day just wonderting around taking everything in. The Harry Potters Diagon alley is a must, feel the heat from the Dragon atop Gringots bank, buy any number of wizards wands (there were thousands of them).Only drawback I felt wasthe plethora of merchandise shops and it was almost impossible to get a cup of tea. Great fun for the youngsters though. If you had been a keen fan I would recommend at least two if not three days to see it all properly and to do all of the rides.

We went on March break and spent 4 days at Universal and 5 days at Disney World. We stayed on sight at Cabana Bay and used their shuttle service to the park. You can walk to the park but it is quite a walk for an onsite hotel. Their are 2 parks at Universal so if you don't get the park hopper you CANNOT go to both parks and you CANNOT ride the Hogwarts Express which takes you back and forth between the two parks. I prefer the main park Universal over Island of Adventure and it seems that more happens at that park. They also have two Harry Potter worlds one at each park. Diagon Alley at Universal and Hogsmead at Island of Adventure. I prefer Diagon Alley but both places are Great. We took advantage of the early entry perk and went straight for Hogsmead and went on the rides there. Then took the train over to the Gringotts ride at Universal. Only Hogsmead is open for the early entry at this time. When we arrived at the Gringotts ride we had to wait until it opened. We would be in the middle of the line so once the ride opens it's about a 15 minute wait. You should go to HP early in the morning or you will be waiting in a long line. My kids would go in the single rider line in the afternoon which was faster than the stand by line. I find most of the people are in the HP worlds so the rest of the park wasn't to busy. This amusement park isn't like other parks with a lot of thrill rides and coasters. They have more simulator rides which are very good. For those interested which Park is Better Disney or Universal. Well I had poor customer service at Disney World and not 1 but 5 incidents and you can read 2 main ones on my Disney review. Universal we had 0 incidents. I would say if you have teenage kids and older Universal. If your kids are smaller Disney. My teenage kids enjoyed Universal better and asked me when we can go back to Universal and not Disney. Also I found the food to be better at Universal and more reasonably priced. We had the dinning plan at Disney and the average sit down meal was close to $200 for dinner for the 4 of us. For that price I'd expect wow that was good. Not it's OK. And the quick Service Burger at Disney are pretty much all the same a regular burger at McDonald's which would cost you close to $11. Anyways hope you enjoy Universal Studios as my family did !!! WILL BE BACK

This was my first time in Universal and I wasn't disappointed. First of all if you want to see all of Universal in either 1 or 2 days buy Express no matter what. Although it is expensive you get to skip the queues which usually saves you around 2 hours. Universal is split into to two parks, "Islands Of Adventure" and "Universal Studios." Both of the parks are brilliant and defiantly worth a visit. "Islands Of Adventure" has more rides while "Universal Studios" has more simulators and isn't so busy. I would really advise to get up early and get there as quickly as possible because when a rush of people come it is very hard to get from one place to another.

This place is great and has a nice mixture of the old school movies and the new and current blockbusters. The rides here are amazing and again we were blown away with how cool this place was. I highly recommend the horror make up show, the roller coasters and harry potter!!!

We made full use of our two park ticket to spend the whole day at Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure.  Arriving early, we were able to get on the Despicable Me ride pretty quickly and then straight on to the Simpson's and Men in Black rides.  The queues for some attractions were prohibitive (over an hour) but overall, the wait times were acceptable. Food was reasonably priced, considering the captive audiences.  The Harry Potter rides and shops were very busy and very commercial.  Highlights for me included Men in Black and the Mummy.

There are a million reviews about this place so I am going to state what they don't say: City Walk is free to peruse. Here you can purchase souvenirs, eat at Emeril's, Hard Rock Café and you don't need to enter the paid parks. The lines are always long for the good rides so if you want to enjoy "A" park (don't let anyone tell you different, you cannot see everything in the park but most things in 1 day) then get a fast pass especially if you have kids. To stand in a line for 1hour minimum for a 5 minute ride will waste your day. Parking is about $17 a day and food in the park is about 25% more than outside. I would also advise taking a breather between rides and let your body recover from the rides, hydrate and enjoy

Great, personal, friendly help! Anne, any Tamika were working the guest device window at the entrance to universal studios, and went above and beyond to answer question on a future trip. Very impressed! Thank you.

Loved every second of my time there. Both parks are great especially if you are a Harry Potter fan! Get up early to do the gringotts ride. We did and the queue was still an hour long. Get up early everyday and make the most of your time there. Our hotel was close by so a small nap each day had us regenerated for the evening when everyone else is leaving and the rides are quieter. We ate at 11 and 4 each day so as to avoid the crowds...very handy. Bottles of water are allowed in. Your bag is checked on the way into the park each day. The single rider queue is a great time saver too. If you are going on the rip rocket ride pick your song quickly or the ride picks it for you. See the dragon in diagon alley by night!

We went to both Universal parks around Halloween 2014. It turns out that the 1st week of November is one of the slowest of the year at Universal, so other than Gringotts we never waited more than 30 minutes for a ride, and often had no wait at all. Gringotts lines were generally about 30-45 minutes with early park admission, but quickly got up to 2+ hours by mid-day.  Since our primary objective was to see the Harry Potter attractions, we bought the 2-park pass for 3 days thinking that was a lot but that would could come and go as we wanted. Universal's Islands of Adventure park is really kind of a dud other than the Harry Potter section. Universal Studios has Diagon Alley (which is as wonderful as one would expect it to be) but it is so much more than that! The Mummy roller coaster is dated but a lot of fun, Transformers and Spider Man are great 3D rides, Men in Black is a shooting-the-bad-guys ride, Simpsons and Minions are motion simulation rides. All of these were fun for both my 8 year-old daughter and for the adults in the group. And each "area" of the park is themed, so when you are in the Simpsons section you can enjoy a Duff beer and a Lard Lad doughnut. Universal leverages their experience with 3D, motion simulation, and special effects in a way that makes for a totally different experience than Disney or Six Flags.  To go between the two parks there is the Hogwarts Express (or walking, but that's not as much fun). You must have a 2-park ticket to take the Hogwarts Express, and you should take it both ways as the experience is different in each direction. The line for the train can be long, especially headed outbound when one park closes earlier than the other (as it does during Halloween).  We ended up spending all day, every day, in the two Universal Parks. We even decided to add on another day since our flight didn't leave until the evening (if you exchange your multi-day tickets before they expire, the park will add on days at the discounted rate - we spent $18/adult to add a 4th day). I'm sure the time of year contributed greatly to my experience, but we had a wonderful time at Universal Studios - kid, adults, and grandparents alike.

Express pass were a life savor. I wouldn't want to visit park without them. However, sometimes we would still have to wait 45 min to ride, but wasn't too bad.  Harry Potter ride at Universal Studios does not offer express pass. Lines were much shorter after 7:00 pm. You have to leave your stuff in lockers which were always full. They need more lockers. It's best to let one family member secure locker while the others wait in line and save him a space in line.  Souvenir cups with unlimited drinks were not worth the cost. The cups have a chip in them and would only let you refill it after a certain amount of time. So make sure you don't fill it up with too much ice because you have to wait if drink it all up right away.  The water rides at Island's of Adventure gets you soaked. Wear flip flops or bring an extra pair of socks. It's best to ride all of the water rides consecutively, because once you are wet it doesn't make sense to dry off and get wet again. The Harry Potter Hogwarts ride is better at Island's of Adventure than the ride at Wizarding World of Harry Potter.  It was the perfect time of year to go because most spring breaks were over and the parks were not super crowded.

I visited 4 years ago in Islands of Adventure.... A total Nightmare. We were never coming back. Being huge Harry Potter fans, we decided to give Universal a chance this year. Beside the cotinuous Harry Potter break downs, our day went very smoothly! Ate breakfast and walked across the street from our hotel to the park which is the way to go, being much cheaper than on site. They let us in early and we got through the Simpsons, Men in black, and revenge of the mummy in about an hour. Be prepared to use signal rider line sometimes. But not on Harry Potter: it moves very slowly and you miss the whole experience. Ate great food and the leaky choldrin and got through everything In 1 day except dispicable me which stayed above 70 minutes all day and did not feature a signal riders line. Overall a great day! Do not miss the animal show or fear factor. Get as many pictures as possible!

Went as a family of three adults and two children (ages 8 and 11) over spring break 2015, Booked a vacation package with US airfare, hotel (Universal's Cabana Bay) and three day park passes. No express pass included. Cost:: $7000 total. Express pass was going for $184 per person per day at our hotel. That would have been extra. Went because of Harry Potter attractions. Experienced that, enjoyed the frozen butter beer, and the interactive wands, but won't return This is an uncomfortable park to say the least. We have been to the Disney attractions, Nickelodeon, SIx Flags, Sea World, and Atlantis over prior years spring break. I would return to any one of them but not this one. First, it is Florida and the sun during the day is very hot ( oppressive humidity in the summer months also), You will walk miles and miles in the heat at this park ( one reviewer's pedometer clocked it at 11 miles per day). You will find very few places to sit and rest ( most people were sitting on the curbs in the sun). There were lines for everything including cold drinks. Harry Potter attraction was so mobbed you could hardly walk without banging into someone. The stores there are small so you are standing in lines to get in. Where is the shade and the air conditioning, Universal??? 70 to 120 minute waits for rides (on your feet the whole time) is daunting and longer when a ride malfunctions and several seem to do so every day. Granted, spring break is busy but there needs to be a better way for crowd control, moving people from one end of the park to another, and respite from the sun. Arcade games like you see at state fairs cost $5 per person for a 30 second event. Kids enjoyed the pools at the hotel more than the park. Not all that much to do if you don't like extreme roller coasters or getting soaked to the skin on the water rides. This is a park best enjoyed by teenagers and young adults. For the price, Atlantis was a better value and far more enjoyable.

Had a really memorable day out, and could easily rate 5 stars. The only reason to "downgrade" to a still-impressive 4 stars was the big food lines (and pretty horrid turkey legs as fast food) and the long "Express" lanes. Having paid almost exactly $900 for the four of us (two adults, a ten and eight year old), we thought the Express lanes would save more time. They WERE still worth it overall, but they weren't quite the time-saver they arguably should have been given they were a whopping 120 green backs per person.  But the rides were great, the Simpsons we loved, Transformers was really impressive, and Harry Potter’s coaster was truly amazing. Moe’s Mexican in the City Walk on the way out was great (and the Saporros from across the way were incredibly good value).  Highly recommended this place, and really a must when coming to Orlando.

Universal Studios is fantastic! As a massive Harry Potter fan I thoroughly enjoyed Diagon Alley/Hogsmeade. The Rip Ride Rockit and the Mummy rides were highlights as was the general atmosphere of the parks.

A visit to Orlando probably isn't complete without a trip to Universal, but if you don't like simulator rides then you might want to reconsider this park. I really don't cope well on simulators and ended up waiting outside many of the rides while the rest of my family went on them. I did go on the Disaster! ride and it was brilliant - so much better than it appeared to be outside. The Simpsons ride just made me feel really ill though. The Harry Potter section and Escape from Gringotts bank was amazingly done though - well worth the 45 minute wait. The Minions ride was also amazing, but the queue was huge, be prepared for a long wait with your kids.

Absolutely amazing! ! ! ! It's my new wife's dream to visit here as i have been 8 times before and I promised to take her because this place is excellent! !!!!! You don't need children to visit this place as the child comes out in you here!

We were disappointed in our repeat visit to Universal. It was spring break and so crowded the wait for rides was 60-75 minutes We only got to do one.. Harry Potter World was jam packed ! Couldn't appreciate it and the ride over to Islands of Adventure from there was a 90 minute wait. Also Universal is not as clean and appealing as Disney properties. Did enjoy The Blues Brothers!

Dear all, Save up some extra money and visit Orlando Universal Studio. It is 100% worth it! Our family had so much fun. The rides are thrilling and the water rides really get you wet, but no worries you quickly will dry. There is so much to do and to see, so go early and get the VIP pass for front of line, coz the ques are long and waiting time is up to 90 minutes, but with the special pass no more than 5-10 minute so. Please go and have a blast, I promise you will never forget it! We loved it❤️❤️❤️

Another of Universal Studios theme parks, it has more indoor activities to visit (in case of a rainy Florida day). We enjoyed "Despicable Me Minion Mayhem", "Shrek 4D", "Transformers: The Ride-3D", "Beetlejuice Graveyard Revue", "Disaster!", "Men in Black Alien Attack", "Lucy - A Tribute", and "Terminator 2 : 3D". Lines were never really long if you planned well. Our longest wait time was 10 minutes for "Shrek 4-D". Some attractions could have over too minute wait times like "Despicable Me Minion Mayhem", but we planned that visit for first thing in the morning and walked right in with no waiting. Definitely buy into the multiple day, park-to-park ticketing. Plenty of food choices for breakfast, lunch, dinner, and snacks.

We visited both Universal Studios and Island of Adventure over 3 days. We had a lot of fun and there were a range of rides for all kinds of ages. We bought unlimited tickets for 1 week so we could go on any rides we wanted for the week. I would advise you download the Universal Studios Orlando app which tells you how long the wait will be for the ride. The Harry Potter rides were fantastic although in the afternoon the queues get much longer. The Revenge of The Mummy ride was my personal favourite because it was enough for me to handle (coming from an 11 year old) and I'd totally recommend it. The Dragon Challenge and Incredible Hulk Coaster were the scariest rides there. I'd also recommend you get there a bit earlier in the morning because the queues get really long in the afternoon unless you have a fast pass.

Visited Universal Florida with my husband and 3 kids (6, 10, 13) during spring break/April 2015. Park was very crowded and lines were long. We did not purchase express passes as they were very expensive ($89-99 per person per day). In fact, the passes were more expensive than the park tickets themselves (we bought 3 day base tickets from AAA for $150 in advance)! We enjoyed all the rides here -- Return of the Mummy was my favorite. Unfortunately, we didn't ride the Despicable Me ride as the line was 110 mins (I'm patient, but not that patient). Didn't stay for the fireworks at park closing -- we could view them from our hotel (Point Orlando --highly recommended). Probably would be best to visit park early or go during non-peak months to avoid long lines. Also, consider staying at a Universal deluxe on-site resort (Royal Pacific or Portofino Bay) b/c express passes are included --> we wanted a larger suite so we decided to stay off-site.

Purchased a joint pass with the adjacent islands of adventure. Do your research and plan the day . Expect long queues at the most popular attractions. If you can't wait ( in some cases queues were over 2 hours) be prepared to get the fast pass. Get there early and leave late: pay for the preferred parking as you will be tired at the end of the day. Take minimum bags ; they get heavier as the day becomes longer

This wasn't my first time at Universal. Loved that they had a buy two days get the third free special (altho I did not use the third day, it was still nice to have the option). I also like that even though you tend to wait in line a lot, much of that waiting is in places that are air conditioned. I found many folks had no problem hanging out and lounging just about anywhere so we could cop a squat when needed for a rest. The Wizarding World of Harry Potter is so worth it for us Potter-geeks! So much to see and snap pictures of. Nice rides. Overall a very enjoyable experience.

The Harry Potter attractions are fabulous, but there is so much more to do in these side by side parks. You do want to get tickets to both because the Hogwarts train goes back and forth between Islands of Adventure and Universal Studios. It is vital to purchase the "fast" passes if you want to see everything. Well, as it was, I went for 4 days and didn't see everything, but you skip the long lines with a fast pass. The Mummy ride was exceptionally fast and if you get vertigo- skip that one. The Homer Simpson ride was jerky and I just don't get that humor. If you are a Homer fan and ride the big coasters- go for it. Even The Cat in the Hat area was fun for adults. You don't get too wet on the Jurrassic park ride- but you do on the other water rides. Stay at one of the hotels there- you get early admission to the parks. You really DO deserve to have this much fun, no matter how old you are.

We purchased vouchers ahead of time and were told to pick up the actual tickets upon entering the park. We ASSUMED that there would be a special place to do this! Not that we could find. We stood in line almost an hour to pick up tickets we already paid for! That was the worst part of Universal[s 2 parks!

Staff was friendly and we just loved the place .....for any one that was wondering there is free lockers around big rides you just have to get your stuff out under a certain time frame to not be charged.

The Universal and Disney parks have implemented practices where for an extra fee you can join the exclusive club of the “Line skippers – First-Class Customers”, one problem though is that the majority of us, hardworking middleclass, who have made an effort to pay the already hefty entry park fees are left as a second-class customers, enduring increasingly longer, slower and more convoluted lines. In the country where everything is for sale, the customer respect is too. It is not, I that I did not expect lines, but the fact that they were unfairly longer and slower just because, the “First-Class” had always-absolute priority over us: The Second-Class.  The park attractions are fantastic; however the parks management by implementing this customer differentiation is creating inequality and customer resentment, is it worthwhile for an extra dollar to risk the overall experience quality of the attraction park?  I have enjoyed the park attractions; yet, I did not appreciate the sub-standard feeling of being a worthless-second-class customer.

As mentioned, the lines can be pretty lengthy, but my family (including 2 middle school kids) LOVED the "Rip Ride Rock-It" roller coaster, the Dragon Challenge roller coaster and so many other attractions at Universal. As an American Express cardholder, we enjoyed the AMEX Lounge that is near the Shrek attraction. It's a little hard to find, but it's a nice air-conditioned lounge to relax in with granola bars & potato chips to snack on and refreshingly cold bottled water to cool you down.
Went back to Universal for Spring break. They have added a new area in Universal Studio of Harry Potter. The train was cool too. Fire breathing dragon on top of one of the buildings.

We bought a 3 day/one park a day pass to Universal. We went Easter Monday and Tuesday and the following Tuesday. Even with park crowds rated at a 10, we were still able to do everything we wanted, without the Express Pass. We considered staying at one of the Universal hotels to get the Express Pass for free but was not willing to pay $500 a night since this was not the main reason we came to Orlando.  I was a little weary not having an Express Pass when the parks were going to be insane but we made it work. We arrived at the park 30 mins before it opened (730am) and made sure we went straight to the Harry Potter area. We waited in line until the ride opened and got right on. After we did the Harry Potter area we went right to our other main rides. Since we knew we were going to come back to this park for a second day when crowd levels were not so high we did not stressed about doing everything. We did a couple shows when crowds became overwhelming then left after lunch time, went home and napped, then came back around dinner time since the park was opened until 10pm. The crowds were so much better at night. We were able to ride The Mummy coaster over and over without a wait. We had a 10 min wait for the Simpsons Ride and my daughter got right on kiddie Simpsons themed ride (forget the name).  When we came back to this park on the following Tuesday (when crowd levels were going to be far less) we arrived 30 minutes before park opening (opened at 9am) and was able to get right on Despicable Me, Transformers, Men in Black, E.T., The Mummy (3x), and The Simpsons Ride all before 11am. We then walked over and ate at Hard Rock Cafe and then went home. We enjoyed both Universal parks and as long as you plan your day, you can definitely get everything done without a Express Pass.  My daughter was 7 years old and was able to do almost every ride, she was a 1/2 inch to short for the Hollywood Rip Ride Rocket but we were fine with not riding that. I wouldn't recommend bringing children much under that age because they would not get to ride many of the rides.

The new Diagon Alley is the most awesome set up I have ever visited. It takes you straight into this land of magic and Wizardry, an absolute must visit. while the new ride at Gringotts bank is fun, you must try visiting all the little interactive stores they have there especially money exchange....and remember you MUST ask the Goblin a question. All other action rides are super fun as always

We loved Universal! It was fantastic! We'd last been 10 years ago and some of it was brand spanking new, some was like old friends. The hulk!! Spiderman!! Fab!! Especially loving the single rider thing!! Hubby doesn't do these rides mostly! Result!

We visited universal studios three years ago but seemed to enjoy it more this year as they had alot of new attractions. Really enjoyed the new harry potter part especially diagon alley and escape from gringotts it was so amazing blew us away. Also loved using the train it was fab really enjoyed all the rides especially transformers and despicable me also the hulk and rip ride rockit. Well worth visiting and using our early morning pass.
