If it weren't for "The Wizarding World of Harry Potter," these theme parks would be wildly overpriced! As it is, they come close to that. They have some good attractions, but if it were not for the lines, It could all be seen in just a few hours. Some of the effects in the attractions are quite good, but the overall impression is that it's a definitely a lesser version of the big brother down the road.

We stayed at the Hard Rock Hotel so had free express pass and early entry.  I think during our 2 weeks stay we explored every inch on the park.  Our favourite rides were Transformers, The Rockit, The Mummy Returns, Minions, Simpsons and Men in Black.  Harry Potter World was amazing, make sure you ride both ways on the Hogwart's Express as you see different things each way (trying not to spoil it for you).  Lots of toilets and water fountains.  The Irish pub/restaurant was really good.  Make sure you stay for the water/light show in the evening, its spectacular

Universal Studios is a fun park. There are several different simulator rides that can be a bit nauseating if you are a bit prone to that, but mostly they are fun. There are some rides for smaller children as well as the huge roller coasters.

Just like any of the other Disney Parks I have visited it was very crowded and you had to wait around 40 minutes to get on the more popular rides. Two of the most popular rides in the park the waiting time was over 1 hour. Tickets are pricey just like all of the other Disney parks. I think regular parking should be less than the $20 or $25 dollars I paid to park in addition to the cost of the tickets. As far as the rides go they did have an express pass you could purchase for an additional $35 or $39 dollars I don't remember the exact price. But even if you bought the express pass you could not have quick access to their most popular Harry potter rides that didn't make any sense to me. Also as much as the day pass regular tickets cost I think the express passes should cover every ride in the park and be maybe $10 cheaper which would still make the pass cost $25 - $29 additional dollars over the cost of your regular tickets. The park itself is beautiful and you feel just like you were in the Harry Potter movie so that was a plus. I think the price of their one day tickets are way to pricey and most folks who are on vacation do not dedicate 2 or 3 days to go to Universal while on vacation. For me and my family it was a once in a lifetime experience so I doubt if we ever go back unless the prices change.

This is an update to a previous review. While the park will do just about anything to make more money off you and you are bombarded with high end chain restaurants as soon as you enter, I think our daughter was the right age for it this year at 12. Long lines and very crowded especially at Harry Potter whose rides my daughter and her friend did care for. The people on top of people trying to move around. They enjoyed it overall so we hD a good time and will go back to the other side likely next year.  Do yourself a favor though and don't buy both park passes for the same day. You will never get through both parks in one day to pull this off and they know this.  Also don't buy the overpriced expedited line tags. They don't guarantee better line placement. It is the biggest rip off.  This is NOT a good park for small children.
Went to see Wizarding World. we all had a great time. Surprised how much fun the Simpsons area was. only disappointing ride was ET. very dated and a bit boring. old animitronics.

Great variety for all! I would suggest getting the express pass, especially if your going at peak. The lines are long, and the express allows 1/2 the amount of time that the spent in lines. Wear comfortable shoes, and even still your feet will hurt! The park is big and you should do both parks while here. The top rides require that you put your cameras, phones in lockers. They have lockers near each ride that requires them, at a cost, and its quite a mess getting in and getting out. Your really conflicted about what to bring so you can skip the locker mess and get to riding but you want photos. If your getting a 3 day pass which I had, (buy 2 days get the 3rd day free) I suggest your first days are spent clicking and the other days riding and standing in line. Something else I did was buy the food pass. That allows one full meal, a snack and drink. On my 3rd day, i brought my passes, food and rides, $20, and skipped the locker mess. Water rides are a guarantee wet ride, some people had the plastic ponchos, but WHY? Its hot, and getting wet allow for some cool walking! They do have some people dryers, again, why? Cool walking was really refreshing. I came middle of April and it was still very warm and humid, so I liked the water soaked clothes for a while. Remember on all rides you cannot take your photo/phone devices, and they do have you walk thru detectors, and have wands to check for metal. So express pass highly recommended, comfy shoes, sunscreen and sunglasses. Enjoy!

Exactly what was needed for a great couple of days out with the family. Surprisingly easy to get to considering how hard it was to access some other parks like Disney. My two teenagers enjoyed Universal more than Disney! Also worth spending a couple of days there if you want to see everything !

I should probably start by saying it's been about ten years since our last visit to Florida. There were some good and bad updates since then. The bad, was mostly nostalgic in nature. I still expected just one Universal Studios. I knew the price would be higher but was still hoping for just one. I miss the Back to the Future ride. However, the upgrades they made are very impressive.

The Dislike first! Too far to walk from parking lot to activities. Now, the fun. The Rides were great... and the TRANSFORMER didn't disappoint---once you got to the ride, except we were in line at least an hour and a half---OF STANDING...TWISTER had a few surprises. Enjoyed the Mardi Gras parade

upon arriving at the park we encountered an immediate problem, parking. We had up to about 20 minutes waiting just to find a parking space which is unacceptable. However after this it was plain sailing until we reached the ticket desks to enter the parks amusement area, we had a 2 and a half hour wait to get our tickets, despite it taking mere minutes for others. I strongly recommend not visiting this park.
Must try Wizard' brew...Exceptional. low crowd's in early may. Harry Potter rides great. Univesal knows how to keep bathrooms clean. Kudos to the staff.

We came back after several years, when our kids were too small to try both parks, and now we could enjoy everything that these fantastic parks can offer. We really loved the wet rides in Jurassic Park area, as it was a hot day, and it was a perfect way to cool off. We finished the day with a brand new movie at the City Walks.

My wife and I visited Orlando for our Honeymoon in April this year (2015) and I can honestly say we had a blast.  This was a first time visit for both of us and we were quite excited about visiting the big parks - first on our list was Universal.  I've read through a number of reviews on here (mainly the poor / terrible ones) and I think I must have been at a different park from these people. Although the two Universal parks didnt seem to be as big as I expected (maybe because I was still remembering wanting to go there as a kid, where everything was 10x bigger!), I thought the places were fantastic. From coming through the entrance into the CityWalk, then on into Islands of Adventure and finally Universal Studios itself, the visit well met how I imagined it would be.  I must admit, there aren't as many rollercoaster-type rides as I first thought and there seems to be an over-use of 3D / 4D rides these days, but that doesnt take away from the fact that the parks are above and beyond anything we'd been to before.  We had a great time wandering around the parks, having a go on various rides, but we were both amazed with the Harry Potter areas - the attention to detail in these areas of the parks is just fantastic and the Hogwarts train between the two parks is an added bonus (some people have raged that it's a con to get you to pay for tickets to both parks, but it's not a necessity, you dont HAVE to go to both, but why wouldnt you?) Yes, there are a number of shops, which sometimes comes across as just another way to get you to spend your money (t-shirts, wands, etc, etc), but let's be honest, we go to these places to enjoy ourselves, so if that means getting some overpriced souvineers, then so be it.  We had mutli-day passes for both Universal and Disney and both my wife and I found that we enjoyed the Universal parks a lot more (maybe the majority of the Disney parks were a bit too kiddy for us and Universal more adult). I could spend the next hour or two going into more detail about the rides, but have a quick Google and try them for yourself - you definitely wont be disappointed. We're already in the process of planning a revisit next year!  Overall, I can't really fault Universal at all - the staff were always pleasant and helpful, the rides were fantastic, the place wasnt too busy (we went at a more off-peak time....if you're going to complain about the parks being busy, dont go when all the schools are on holidays!).  I'd definitely recommend Universal Studios Orlando to anyone wanting to visit an excellent theme park :)
Came here as a kid and I loved it I am now 19 and would definitely go back if I liked rides I remember being so happy here definitely take your children!

I went here with access to both parks; the Harry Potter section of the park was well themed and really enjoyable (make sure you have some butter beer) however the rest of the park I found underwhelming and a lot of the rides seemed to be 3d (screen) based-therefore I felt seemed similar  Like most theme parks the food was disappointing and expensive; also we tried to take some of our water in, however we were told we were not allowed to bring our own water into the park  Worth a visit for Harry Potter!

It is all you would expect. Having the express pass that comes with the hotel stay was super helpful. Only rides that don't accept the express pass are the Harry Potter specific rides. Don't bother with the extra morning hour if you stay at an onsite hotel. They feed you to the Hogwarts ride. The line was much less early morning line. Only the Hogwarts area was open, so it wasn't as helpful as we had expected. We returned to their Diagon Ally just before closing and almost no one was there. Young Wizards who want to test their wands would have more fun at the end of the day.

Where a party of two, both 29. Rides are OK, Busch Gardens is better. The shows are OK. Universal is very expensive, also has different prices depending on the weekdays. What's nice is that you really dive deep into the shows, especially the 3D and 4D rides. Took us two days to see the things we wanted to see on both Universal and Island of Adventures.

I must say between our visit in 2008 and this week, Universal has really upped the ante in regards to Customer Service and Guest relations! I rented an ECV which made life for the day BETTER! The price wasn't bad and the authorization for the hold came off quickly and without delay.  Ok, now for the not so good- Universal, it's time to retire T2. Yep, I said it. The guy playing said character missed queues, could barely get up onto the stage from the floor, and the overall experience, while good for something from the 90s, is tired! One of the soldiers didn't work, which drew your eye to it, the wait time in the Cyberdyne Presentation area was long and very little was done to accommodate those who were without wheelchairs or ECV's! I gave my seat to an elderly lady after we were in queue for at least 25 minutes. The Mummy died around 4ish while we were in line, so that was a SUPER bummer- and we couldn't even return to ride it later because it closed that day at 5:30! We arrived on a Sunday morning and mostly everything was slated to open around 11 or later...  Also, please improve the quality of the Transfer wheelchairs...or make all the lines COMPLETELY accessible for ECV's!  VERY DISAPPOINTED NO MARVEL ITEMS FOR PURCHASE ONLINE! I waited to buy items because we'd not preplanned to have baggage (due to fees on the flight).  Otherwise A+! Ride attendants were beyond wonderful and helpful! The beautiful young lady working The Mummy had personality plus!

The staff was very helpful and they let us in on inside tips but the wait for Despicable me was 100 minutes and Rip ride rockit was 45 minutes and the park was a little messy BUT I would recommend you come to both parks.

As far as the parks go, they need to keep up with the times. Either update current attractions that have been there for 20 or 30 years with newer technology or replace them all together. I can honestly say that the harry potter areas of the parks were phenomenal and the only reason worth going to universal studios theme parks for. However, no matter how hard we tried, there just wasn't enough to do for three days. We spent over a thousand dollars to be amazed for the first day and bored for the next two. Aside from harry potter, the City walk area was the next best thing at universal studios, and that was only because of Emeril's and the mini-golf. MINI GOLF WAS MORE ENJOYABLE THAN AN ENTIRE THEME PARK!
My trip over here is remarkable. No words to describe how best the place is ! Every family couple should visit this place for sure.

First off, if possible get multiday tickets to print at home. Cheaper and no Standing in line at the front gate. Another important Thing from my pov is to get park-to-park tickets, especially since Diagon Alley openend, it's very cool, even if you are not a Harry Potter fan. Also the new Transformers Ride is great. My Family spent a two week vacation in Orlando and we got 4 day park-to-park tickets, which was totally worth while. Also we opted for the photo connect Card 2 week Option. Great Picture opps.

Of all the Orlando theme parks Universal was the one I was least looking forward too but I absolutely loved it. Great entertainment for the full day and would have no hesitation visiting again. Yes it might be on the expensive side of things as are all the theme parks but they are a must visit when in orlando.

This is not a review of the theme park - only arrivals at the bus/taxi area and of Universal City walk.  First - we arrived via a car service from our resort on a Friday evening around 6:30. Traffic was very heavy and there were a lot of people milling about in the bus/taxi area. There must have been a hundred buses and the cabs trying to drop off were wrapped around the entire area. The parking attendants were RUDE every single one of them (at least 10 that we encountered) and obnoxious when our car service wanted to drop us off in the designated drop off area. They waived him off, and told him that he couldn't use the drop off area even though the sign clearly said he could. Several were discourteous and you could see their sarcastic laughing as they mockingly told him to "have a nice day - now MOVE". Had I had the opportunity to ask for a badge number, I would have made a personal complaint. It left a bad taste in our mouth that a theme park could make such a bad first impression.  Once we were actually allowed out of the car after looping around a second time, (we had to exit the car quickly as parking attendants were running over to waive the car service around a third time) we ventured upstairs to the City walk. Good variety of music and dining venues - seemed like something for everyone. I hate crowds though and as we were walking towards the restaurants it was like a sea of humanity coming towards us. Very unsettling feeling. I guess if you don't like crowds then Universal is not for you.

Believe me, I'm not into theme parks or rides and get a sweat on from the motion of a bus, but Universal completely changed my opinion. It's quite simply brilliant.  We were lucky and could go at low season, in mid-April, when the crowds were probably pretty sparse, so my review reflects that and we didn't experience any horrific queues or lines to ride for 4 minutes.  Universal for me was like being transported back 40 years in time to when I was a kid and I found the whole park magical. Harry Potter and Diagon Alley is unbelievable - it's like walking into the book and being a huge Harry Potter fan, I was both really moved and ridiculously giddy about the whole thing.  The park is spotless and for somewhere that really only has perhaps 10 blockbuster rides and the rest is gift shops and food retail places, they do it SO well.  Our wait times were bearable - the longest was perhaps Gringotts at Diagon Alley one afternoon and that took about 45 mins but I consider myself lucky with that when I read some other reviews!  Walking through Platform 9 and 3/4 is breathtaking - make sure you take the train to and from Island of Adventures because the ride is different with each journey.  Transformers and Revenge of the Mummy were my other 2 favourite rides. Loved them both.  And surprisingly the Simpsons was highly amusing and the lard-boy donuts really tasty!  My big tip for Universal is to take a bum-bag/fanny pack - not so much a fashion item any more but I loved mine and think they should come back in! Some of the lockers are chargeable and having a bum bag removes the need to use them or worry about where to keep your valuables.  Great experience - it's a blast for any age. I loved it so much that we're going back to Orlando next March!
I think our girls didn't enjoy this park as much as they did Islands of Adventure or certain Disney parks. Would agree about getting there early.

This is the other side of the coin in Orlando, you have theme parks and well rollercoaster and 4d experiences then you have hulk, fantastic 4, Harry Potter, Popeyes, Simpson a lot of things to do and see, the difference between WDW and universal is that there's less people around the park, your waiting time are less than WDW. The only thing I suggest you to do is go to Harry Potter's first if you want to enjoy the rest of the day in other attractions because that's the most crowded spot in the whole universal area... Hope you enjoy my review!
You hop on your bike and go on an adventure to help E.T and his friends return home safely. A lot of fun and you are thanked personally by E.T at the end.
We visited the wizarding world of Harry Potter and it was AWESOME! !!! We drank butter beer and saw Gringots! This is a MUST SEE 4 HARRY POTTER FANS!

We purchased a 3 day park to park ticket (special was buy 2 days get 1 free), for a long weekend trip to Orlando. We stayed at Universal's Cabana Bay Reaort, which allowed early entrance into Island of Adventure's Harry Potter. We took advantage of that the first day, and the 2nd day we arrived at the park before 8:30, based on a tip that they would open up at least 30 minutes early, which they did. We were able to ride every ride we wanted to in the park within 4 hours, but by noon, the park was jammed and the lines were long. You need 2 days to see both parks, although it's only because of the long lines later in the day slow you down. The technology of the rides are amazing with the 3D/4D experiences - it is worth the trip.

We visited in the most perfect time. Great weather! No lines! Couldn't have asked for more! We did both parks on both days we visited. (see separate review for Islands of Adventure) Parking is easy and access to the park is achieved through CityWalk of even through the other park. They still have classics such as E.T. and the Beetlejuice show which Universal Studios Hollywood no longer does. And better yet! They have the new Harry Potter expansion: Diagon Alley!!! All of the intense rides came equipped with near by lockers, which were free of charge for the associated ride's wait time. Here is what we rode/saw: Disaster is actually quite cool. If you know the Studio Tour in Hollywood, this reminds me of that and the old Special Effects stages in one. Might be too intense for small children? Not too aggravating though. E.T. is just so nostalgic, how can you not wait in line for it? Jerky at times, and he no longer says your name, but still great. My boyfriend did the Rip Ride Rocket and said it was great, too intense for me. Revenge of the Mummy is soooo much better than the Hollywood version. Twister was a fun little show to watch. Again, may be too intense for small children? You can spend a whole day in Diagon Alley alone. You need to buy an interactive wand. You won't regret it. Check out all the shops and the ride "Escape to Gringott's" is the best! The queue alone is amazing, but the ride is cutting edge. Worth the wait.

The Express pass is a must!! Started to skip the considerable extra cost, but too many friends and family talked me out of being cheap. Glad that I listened. Got on rides and saw more of the park than we could of possibly seen otherwise. Bought tickets online in advance and had no problem scanning the e-ticket at advance purchase kiosk. Bought multi-pack of drink cups and was impressed with the chips that regulate the refills on future days. First day may refill cup at will, second or future purchase restricts one refill per hour. Recommend getting park hopper as rides may go down and going between park on new Daigon Alley train a must.
We spent 10 hrs in park and still could not see everything. I really enjoyed the 3-d presentations, so life like!
everything!!! What is not to like?? I love the bars around the lake. Love the park and the rides. I really loved going at night and walk around.
What a great day. Plenty for all age ranges . allow 2 days to do it justice, 1 day Harry Potter the other everything else.
The Universal Studios is a amazing Park! Fun guarantee to everybody. Especially to The Simpsons fans. I loved the Simpsons Ride! This particular park is plenty full of life!
What an excellent experience we had at this wonderful place, could not fault it one bit. Keep up the good work.
There is not much to say about Universal except WE LOVE IT!!! A lot of fun for the whole family, incredible rides, great service which is very rare for Florida.

I just loved it. Every 3-d ride that we had time to ride was awesome. The minion, transformers, shriek. Loved the mummy ride. Loved the scenery. I wish we had more time to ride more 3-d rides. We did not even cover half of the park. The Harry potter train from park to park was really neat. It is a bit over priced. It is ridiculous that you have to pay per day for the souvenir cups. You spend 10.00 on the first day and keep adding an extra day for 7.00 dollars more. Plus there is a chip in the bottom of the cup so they are ripping you off on that purchase. The food is way over priced. Be prepared for a lot of walking and major crowds. But it was great. I hope we can go back and experience it again and maybe get to the rides and shows and sight seeing that we did not get to. It would take a good whole week if not longer to cover it all.
Brilliant,breath taking,amazing!!!!! Words cant describe how good harry potter land was! Defiantly recommend! Specially if you like happy potter and avengers!

Kids are 8 & 10, we visited here the day after memorial day and the lines were surprisingly short, and the rides were way better than expected. Favorite was by far "The Mummy Returns". We actually spent 10 full hours here and weren't ready to leave. We'll be back for sure on a multi-day pass.

Again an amazing park never feeling overcrowded. Loads to do loads of places to eat and drink. When we were visiting there was a closed set for American Ninja so it made it more difficult to negotiate and we missed some things. Beetlejuice graveyard mash up is well worth a viewing and would highly recommend a visit to Flannigans bar. This is a great park highly recommend.

We took our 8 and 10 year olds and they absolutely loved it. This has been our best vacation yet. The employees are very polite and helpful, which is amazing considering they are around such a high concentration of customers so much.  The rides are fantastic and Harry Potter Diagon Alley is amazing. By amazing, I mean that everyone stepping into it stops and stares in awe for minutes. Just walking through it was one of the top 3 things about the trip.  The tickets are expensive but we'll worth it.  We didn't get the express pass but left wishing that we did. We will buy the express pass next time for sure.

Harry Potter was different and something worth seeing once but not worth the price for a return trip here. The staff and park were not the greatest and do not compare at all to Disney even though they profess to be.

An amazing park with thrilling rides that the entire family can enjoy. Customer service is a bit lacking at times but not terrible.  Visitors should download the "Universal FL" app prior to your visit. It has great info like the current wait time for the park's attractions and a handy GPS-like park map that will give you turn-by-turn directions through the park.  I don't recommend opting for the preferred parking as you're basically paying extra to park in the same parking deck as everyone else, just on a lower level.

if you're deciding to take a trip to orlando, be sure to prepare for the huge amount of money you're going to be spending. Universal Studios was more expensive than we anticipated especially because we wanted to go to the parks only for Harry Potter world in particular. Get there early and leave late. we went during the holiday season in december and it was packed. getting there when the parks open lets you cut wait times in line and there are less people. Usually, the park starts to get very full from 11-3 so taking a trip to the really popular rides during this time is not recommended. Try not getting any meals in the park, it's really overpriced for cheap food. (but do get specialty snacks such as butterbeer it is so good.) Try meeting characters and take pictures. overall it was a really fun experience Also worth mentioning, the citywalk is free and is really pretty and fun. If you're not willing to take a trip into universal studios, the citywalk at night is also a good choice.

Having been to both Universal Studios, I much prefer the Hollywood one. We did paid extra for the VIP Experience. At the Florida location we didn't get half as much as we did in Hollywood. We had to buy our own lunch and go on rides whether we wanted to or not. At least in Hollywood our guide asked if we wanted to and a very nice lunch was included in the price. Plus, in Hollywood they have a LOT more backstage stuff and different rides including Jaws. Plus you don't have to go to a different park to ride the Jurassic Park ride. Not as much fun.

My husband and I spent one day at Universal and had a blast. The Harry Potter addition is top notch, and were very impressed with the food at the walk up restaurants, which is unusual. We would definitely go back for a longer period to enjoy all it has to offer. I do wish, however, they offered half day tickets, we were there for a trip to Disney meeting family and wanted to go check out Universal, so had only a partial day to explore.

This is my favourite of all the theme parks and is more suitable for adults although there is also plenty to interest the kids. Our favourites were The Simpsons, Back to the Future (cheesy but good) and Mummy rides. The film set things like Jaws were also very good. There is something to suit all tastes without the saccharin of some of the Disney parks.

If you like movies, this is your theme park. Make sure to get here early and have a plan as to what you want to see. Don't go have lunch at noon, when the restaurants are busy. If you have limited time make sure you visit the rollercoaster + Shrek + Simpsons and Transformers. These are the most worth visiting.

If you are traveling alone you can do both parks (Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure) in 2 days or less, even on a busy weekend, with plenty of time to visit your favorite rides multiple times. Plan well and hit the busiest rides, and rides that don't have single rider lines before noon. No need to buy the express pass but I would recommend getting the park hopper. It gives you the flexibility to go between parks on the Hogwarts train, or it's a fast walk from gate to gate. Check ride times a week before to give you an idea where to start and how to plan your day. The Harry Potter experience in both parks in amazing, but Escape from Gringots and Diagon Alley at Universal is the better of the two if you can only visit one park.

My family took a vacation of a lifetime and we went to Orlando. We stayed two weeks and had tickets for both Disney World and Universal Studios. We timed our vacation to be there for the opening of Diagon Alley and the Hogwarts Express. Let me just say that Disney World was wonderful and Universal Studios can sink into the ocean for all I care. We have a ten year old daughter who has Caudal Regression Syndrome which means she is missing the lumbar and sacral vertebra. She cannot walk but she gets around great in her wheel chair and "walking" on her hands. Let me just say she is an amazing little girl who we have raised to believe she can do anything she wants. She is not handicapped but handicapable! Universal Studios refused to let her ride any rides including the kiddie rides. They said it was clearly stated in the ride brochure. It is NOT! We had spent a lot of money on 3 day passes that included both parks. We left with this beautiful little girl crying because she felt she had ruined her brother’s vacation. We stopped at customer service to lodge a complaint. After waiting in line for 30 minutes, I told the young girl at the counter that I was extremely angry and that I would like to speak to a manager because she was not paid enough for me to take it out on her. She said first I needed to let her know what was going on and I told her about the ride operators letting my little girl get on the ride only to have a supervisor come over and say no, they don't let cripples ride and she would need to get off. This happened not once, not twice but 5 times and that included the kiddie rides. I was furious but controlled myself since it was not this poor girls fault. She then went back to get her manager. We waited another 15 minutes then this young girl came back and said her manager authorized her to refund our tickets for the day. I said very nicely, where is the manager and she said her manager told her to do this. I asked if my complaint mattered and she said of course. I said apparently not since the manager couldn't even bother to come and talk to me! The young lady left close to tears and I almost felt bad but considering why I was there and the fact that I did warn her stopped my pity. The Public Relations manager came and with her came the ride manager Brian. Brian, I will never forget. The young man needs to learn to listen! I told them what had happened and Brian said yes that was company policy. I said where does it state this? In the ride brochure. i held it up and said show me where? I have looked and nowhere in there does it say handicapped people can't ride. It listed weight limits, operating instructions, height requirements but nothing about people who can't walk not being able to ride! He tried to take the brochure from me but I refused to give it to him. The public relations lady asked me what i wanted and I told her an apology to my daughter and I wanted Brian to escort her to any ride she wanted and make sure she got to ride it provided she met the restrictions posted and not the ones they made up to keep her off. She offered to refund all three days and I told her no this wasn't about money it was to teach my daughter that she was worth fighting for and that people like this park where wrong! Brian said no no no. He talked over me and could not even acknowledge what I was saying or even apologize because we felt that way. He was right and we needed to leave. I will never go back there and I tell everyone who considers going that they better be in excellent health or they will waste their money!

Visited Universal Studios for the 2nd time this year and loved it just as much as our first visit. We are a family of 3 and our little one enjoyed The Simpsons area and the Men in Black Ride. So much to see and do that you can fill your whole day and have a fantastic time. This ear we got to do the Transformers ride as it was not open on our last visit in 2013 and we all loved this ride. Wait times were not long wither 20 mins for most things, our longest wait was for Despicable Me which was 40/50 minutes but worth it to see our little boy enjoying it and meeting the minions after it.  Would recommend to everyone and we will be visiting again on our return trip.

Universal Studio at Orlando is a great place to visit. It has something for everybody. Our six year old son enjoyed Barney and the E T Adventure and we loved Transformers and The revenge of the mummy rides. They were absolutely thrilling and we had a great time. The x press pass makes the tickets more expensive but it does save on a lot of time for sure. A must place to visit in Orlando.

We really enjoyed Harry Potter themed Diagon Alley and Hogsmead. The interactive wands were a big hit with our 11, 13, & 14 yr olds. A bit crowded. Ridiculous prices (of course) and a slight resentment toward the Express pass system which made the wait in lines even longer. One plus, we learned on our final day, most all those Snack and Beverage stands will provide cups of complimentary ice water if you ask and it was good. Beats the price of constantly buying bottled water.

This park is a fantastic place to visit for all ages. Something for everyone!! Rides are great, food is great, shows are great, it's all great!!! I personally love the horror make up show the most!! Has to be one of the best shows around!!

My family visited recently, combining both parks in 2 days. Phew, it is a lot to take in! Universal Studios was my favourite of the 2, being a lot less crowded, a lot wider to walk around, and more relaxing in general.  I'm not a big fan of rides, so I didn't really get value for money from my ticket. The Terminator show was good, as was the Simpsons themed area. There is so much to see and look at when wandering round, that time passes quite quickly. Being nearly 100 degrees when we were there, the need for shade and drinks was important, of which there were plenty of opportunities.  Diagon Alley and the other Harry Potter attractions are stunning, and really do have a 'wow' factor; truly amazing if you are a fan, and not to be missed.  I have to say, now I've done it once, I don't feel the need to go back, although my kids would probably disagree!

Wow. On loved this park. The Simpson's ride is a total must. The despicable me ride is another must. The park has fantastic rides for all ages. The Dr Suse area is excellent for smaller kids. Plenty restaurants and toilet areas. Some rides you need to remove glasses. Wallets Etc. There is lockers. A small parade goes round park daily. Well worth the watching. The Hulk rollercoaster is not for feint hearted. (I watched the bags). Harry potter area stunning.Please do 2visits to really enjoy park and get round at decent pace.

My husband and I got a taxi to universal studios! We did have the 2 park ticket so we could go to both universal parks.  We loved the whole atmosphere and feel about the place. The first ride we went on was the transformers 3D ride, we only had a 10 min wait which was fine, the effects were amazing, you felt like you were in the film. I also liked that all the rides when queuing had air conditioning which was very much welcomed after walking round in the heat!  We saw the cars used in the new fast 7 film which was great. We enjoyed Simpsons world and we even managed to get a pic with the Simpsons family! We ate at crusty burger and had a crusty burger which was actually quite nice!  We went on the Men in black ride which was Ok but compared to the rest of the rides it was a bit disappointing. The ET ride is still there and we went on it for old times, it is dated compared to the other rides but has a nice feel to it still and loved the smell!!  We somehow missed the terminator 2 ride we couldn't find it! We got the hogwarts express train to universal islands of adventure which was a good ride in itself!  If you are a hardcore Harry Potter fan you will love both of these parks. The attention to detail and effort gone into putting the Harry Potter attractions together is amazing!!  Have a great time!!

Could spend all day at the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. Love the Universal theme parks. Definitely recommend getting the annual pass for Florida residence as you will want to come back over and over. Rides spaced perfectly. Cannot wait to head back for another visit.

We have been looking forward to visiting Universal Studios/Islands of Adventure for a few years and it was worth the wait. Staying on site at Cabana and Royal Pacific was a great way to access the park and lots of perks. My hubby and I - plus boys (12 & 14) had an action packed stay and loved every minute. We got in early, had express passes, and rocked thru every ride many times over. Everybody had their favorites - but Harry Potter (at both parks) was a thrilling experience, I loved the Mummy (haha), my hubby enjoyed The Simpsons, the boys loved it all. We did catch breaks at the American Express lounge (if you are member, free cold water and snacks throughout the day). We spent 3 full days going between parks and enjoyed the rides over and over again. Animal actors show and Beetlejuice were a fun break between the action. The rides make you feel like you are part of the movie: moving, shaking, spinning, flying, driving off buildings or cliffs, all kinds of crazy. We brought our excitement and Universal delivered.

Universal Studios is possibly the best theme park due to it's excellent mix of rides, shows, food/drink options, places to sit and rest (in the shade) and of course the WWoHP's Diagon Alley. Simply brilliant, albeit very crowded (to be expected I guess).  The whole park exudes excitement. Escape from Gringotts is very good and Rip, Ride Rockit is a super coaster.  The Hogwarts Express (you need a multi park ticket to ride) is very clever and worth the time to travel!

Main reason for going was Harry Potter. Got the three day pass- 1 was spent at HP, 1 for all other Universal/IOA, and 1 for repeating favorites again. Staff members were very friendly (special mention for Margaritaville bartenders, Hogwarts staff, Mythos waiter for excellent service). The park was clean and it was a busy 3 days with 12-15 hours per day at park/city walk area. Would recommend eating at Citywalk places, Three Broomsticks, Leaky Cauldron, and Mythos (reservations recommended). Went to see a movie at the movie theater. I did a review for HP separately, so here I will focus on the rest. Get to the park early/ have early admission with an onsite hotel. I stayed at Cabana Bay, which was fabulous! Parks were easy to walk around in and navigate and the maps are helpful. All rides had things to do/see in line while you waited- good ambiance and atmosphere. Here are a few ride highlights (many require lockers, lines can be 10-60 min. depending n what time of the day it is, for least wait time: go in the evening): Spiderman: 3D simulation ride, really enjoyed this one, some twists and turns Dr. Doom: More like a drop up- they race you about 3/4 of the way up really fast, you bob there a few times slowly, then come down slowly. Very quick ride and not what I expected. ET: Very fun for a ride for younger ones. You ride a bike like you are flying over everything. You have twists and turns through the woods, go over the city (very cool!!!), and go to ET's planet (great scenery), and ET says your name at the end! Men in Black: Some twists and spins, shoot aliens with a ray gun at your seat and it calculates your score- sort of like laser tag Simpsons: Movie screen in a simulation car, carnival atmosphere, jerky movements Minions: Great movie screens as you enter the ride through the line, 3D simulation ride with minion glasses, this had one of the longer wait times along with HP, jerky movements Shrek 4D: 3D movie with seats that jerk/effects to go along with the movie Poseidon's Fury: kind of like a performance, interesting architecture We usually went to the park 8am-11pm. Be sure to catch the parade at 7pm and the show at 9pm by the lagoon. The lagoon show was especially cool! Great trip! Really enjoyed it! There are things for all ages to do- would recommend especially if you have not been before. This was my first time at Universal and it was excellent.

We go to Florida every year and always make regular trips to Universal!! Even after several visits we still haven't seen everything. The park has so much in it and the way they have built the buildings to match the originals is brilliant. The restaurants in universal are over priced and the convenient food (i.e. cookies,crisps popcorn) are reasonable, but you can buy a wristband that allows you to eat at a select few restaurants throughout the day. This works out to be the best option if you are planning to spend the whole day and eat at the restaurants. Your bags are checked as you enter Universal so it's best to travel light as this skips one of the many queues you will be in. Obviously depending on what time of year you go. We usually travel mid September and the queues for the rides are between 5-20 mins. This is a great park and you will not be disappointed!
We stopped in the hard rock hotel which was a shuttle ferry away, but this a load better than disney went in three X and the Harry potter very good

WOW, way cool! Spring for the 2 parks pass. The train ride was neat. The restaurant that serves old world food, ribs, chicken, roasted turkey legs, roasted corn on the cob and potatoes was a really good meal! Like the Harry Potter areas... I'm not a huge fan but I did enjoy both parks that had Harry Potter experiences.

I had only visited here once 15 years ago, and returned this time with my adult daughter and 10 year old grandson. We spent three days between this park and the Universal Islands of Adventure, and I feel this was a good amount of time to see all of the attractions we wanted to see. If you could only visit one park, my preference would be the Studios, as I felt there was a better variety of attractions here. My grandson enjoyed all of the rides, and especially liked the Curious George water-play park. The highlight was, for all of us, Diagon Alley. We purchased an interactive wand, and my grandson had a great time performing the "spells" at various points around Diagon Alley. And butterbeer is delicious! He also enjoyed the train trip to the other park (to Hogsmeade- you need a park-to-park pass to do this) so much that he wanted to take it back later. We found food prices as expected for an amusement park, and bought the refillable cups for soda, water, etc. (good for only one day-free refills at locations throughout the parks), which seemed expensive but paid for themselves. If you like movies, amusement rides, live shows, playgrounds, and photo ops with your favorite movie and TV characters, you will enjoy some time at Universal Studios Orlando. Regular parking (in a covered lot) is $17 per day in addition to park admission.

Pros: mainly good rides and lots to look at. Harry Potter and Simpsons area had been developed since my last visit and were fantastic. Something for everyone.  Cons: this may be insignificant to most people, but it annoyed me so much it's worth mentioning... The carnival high striker/ hammer game in the Springfield area is an absolute con. No adults ever win yet a kid can go up and tap it and then win a prize. $5 wasted! My main issue with these parks however is definitely the fast pass tickets. Why should I wait longer because universal gets paid? What are universal doing to deserve more money? Nothing, but I am. I am waiting longer. Maybe universal should pay me the extra profit they make to compensate my extra queuing. It's a bad system.

An endless amount of fun for everyone! Mind blowing roller coasters, rides and replica neighbourhoods. There's so much going on in Universal that it's impossible to be bored! The Springfield town and Harry Potter world are just out of this world. My personal favourite rides were The Rock It Rollercoaster, The Mummy Ride and Escape from Gringotts. It is a must see if you're in Orlando and a must visit if you're looking for a fun holiday!

This was our first trip to Universal and we loved it here the most. This park had it all. It had good places to eat, plenty of room so you were not shoulder to shoulder all day and it had great rides and attractions. We ended up eating breakfast 3 different days in this park and we found the best place. It is right past the entrance to the park. It is teh Boulangerie Bakery. They do have baked goods, but they have eggs and sandwiches as well that were all very good and not too pricey. of course we visited Diagon Alley a lot and each time it was fun. Our children bought their wands at Olivanders and made spells around the whole section. The Escape from Gringots ride was excellent, we went on it twice and it was worth any wait you might have. Diagon Alley has all the shops that you want as well. Another section of the park that is great is over on the far right as you walk in the main entrance. There is the Horror Show Makeup show that was really fun. There is the ET ride, the Terminator show and eventually you walk through the Simpson's area. The Simpson's ride is very good. Also we loved the Men in Black ride. Minnion Mayhem was excellent as well. Stay away from Shrek. That was horrible. The Mummy ride was really good, we went on that three times. Just an overall excellent experience here.

I went with a group of 4 adults and 2 kids and it happened to be the 25th anniversary of the park. The lines were quick. The only thing we didn't get to ride was the new Minions ride since there was a 75 minute wait. The kids loved it. The parade was cute and the Celebration of 100 years of movies was great, fireworks included.

It's an amazing experience. We did a three day ticket with express pass for the lines. It's an added cost, but it's definitely worth it.  It's noteworthy that some rides require you to dump ALL your belongings into lockers, but they provide these for free (for roughly the time you'd be on the ride).
This park is amazing!!! It has been 20 years since my last time there and I got really surprise how it has changed for better!!

Thanks to Islands of Adventure, Universal studios is so much quieter and overall much nicer and enjoyable, not too busy, except for Minions, could wait over 90 mins for a ride so get in real early. We visited four times with our multi ticket, used the H.P train to visit H.P world, but always felt more at home studio side, we love it, all the old faves,Twister, Mummy, Simpsons, men in black, Shrek, and many more, miss Jaws though! Diagon alley is something else, you don't realise it's there until you get directed to go through this wall, you then enter another world, absolutely breathtaking, try the Butterbeer please! God I feel homesick already!

Second time here (well we visited at least 3 times both trips!) and never gets boring! We have a 6 year old and a 13 year old, both were thoroughly entertained. I prefer this to IOA, although that's also pretty awesome. Mummy, Spider-man, Simpsons Land and Curious George land for when you need to cool of, are all brilliantly done! Of course DIagon Alley is a must, fantastic attention to details and Escape from Gringots is an amazing ride. I find this park quieter than IOA although that could just be because it is laid out better, wider paths etc. We visited through 1st and 2nd week of June and as long as we arrived for opening, we managed to get all all the big rides pretty speedily (Max wait 20mins). Although we never manged to do the Despicable Me ride as queue was always 60mins plus. We ate at Mel's Diner, as we have before, love their shakes and burgers!  I highly recommend Valet parking. It may seem a bit steep at 35 bucks but the time you save getting into the park and the ease of bag check etc is well worth it if you ask me! Plus when you are tired after a full day, it's really nice to just sit and wait for your car to be brought to you, then whip out, no traffic at all. I budgeted it along with my spending money for the trip so it didn't seem to much of an expense.  I can't rate this place high enough. We have nothing to compare it to in the UK. It's absolutely awesome!

This is a great park for the whole family. The park has great rides and simulators that allow the family to share rides together. Teenagers will have a great time here. This was my son' third or forth trip here.
I liked all the Parks very well run prices inside for Food , drinks a bit expensive but overall the place in run very well would return again.
2 days atleast amazing for all been here 3 times and seen all movies been made gone on all the rides and interactions truly amazing place will be visiting again

We visited both parks during the Halloween season. The parks are wonderful and with the addition of The Wizarding World of Harry Potter a must see attraction while visiting the Orlando area. I must say though, we loved the "Horror Nights" that was going on during this season. We can't wait to go back.

My friend and I and our 9 & 13 year old grandsons had a great day at Universal Studios. There are a lot of great attractions for everyone. The roller coasters are great and the 4-D attractions were great. Harry Potter was a great area to visit.

I have visited this park at least 3 times and I would recommend it to anyone who visits Orlando. I usually plan to be there early in the morning in order to try all rides. I believe that the Transformer ride is the best. It worths buying two-park pass so you can visit both Universal parks in one or two days. If you visit both parks in one day, you should wear comfortable clothes and shoes because of the long walking distances.

The park was great! It has many thrilling rides, mostly 3D simulators. The best ones in my opinion were: Escape from Gringotts, Transformers, The Simpsons and Despicable Me. Recommended for the whole family. They have something fun for all ages!
It was a great fathers day treat from my Son and his family. With a fully day of sun and no rain all the rides were a real treat. Rode the new train ride and it was very enjoyable

Visited here beginning of june and queues of all rides was between 10-30mins with the odd technical difficulty with the harry potter ride which was 1hr and half. Lockers are free for a certain amount of time. No drinks are allowed but people still take them and put them on the side of the ride. Unlimited drinks start from 12.99 prob worth it as drinks are from 2.99 for water and then coke and powerade about 4dollars included VAT. Simpsons land is amazing! Their ride is out of this world. Food is about 10 dollars plus. Overall great day out. With queue times being short an gettin on majority of the big rides was worth money!

The only thing I really have to say is get the front of the line pass but make sure it's a day where rain isn't predicted because i paid $125 Australian dollars plus my $145 entrance fee for front of the line and we got rained out and everything closed. If your a thrill seeker go the the second park first incase this happens!
Our fourth visit to Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure and we still love it! Great rides, extremely friendly staff and good food.

We love Universal Studios, all the attractions are awesome and the fact that they have the child swap in great for families with young kids, in you are there in Christmas season don't miss out the Macys parade is very good.

Just got back from a 2 day trip to Universal with my 11 year old son. It was a perfect park for him. We got the express passes which in my opinion made all the difference. If we had waited in those long lines for all the rides I'm not sure it would have been a 5 star experience. We were able to ride all the express rides during the day and then go to the Harry Potter rides where the pass doesn't work later when the wait wasn't so long. The Harry Potter rides were my favorite. They are a mix of 4D and roller coaster and are really fun. My 11 year old liked the old fashioned roller coasters that knock you around the best like the Hulk and Dragon Ride. We did both Universal and Islands of Adventure. Both were good for different things so I recommend both and riding the Hogwarts Express was a cool experience. The first day we didn't do the meal plan but ate things that would have been on the plan so we opted to get it the second day. The refillable cups were great! We could get water all day or soda with lunch and not have to worry about how much it would cost. I highly recommend the cups. Two days was a perfect amount of time to see both parks and ride almost everything. Be sure to check out the Simpsons ride.

Really great attractions. This is not Disney. The rides can more intense and themed more towards PG. Universal does some things better than Disney. The humor is targeted and an older audience. Many rides are scarier and rougher than you'd find at Disney. The worker aren't there to create magic. Everyone was kind and helpful and seemed to enjoy friendly talk. There aren't as many atmospheric freebies as Disney. Diagon Alley is FANTASTIC! This is a part of the park where you are really immersed in magic. Theming is very good and will bring back many memories. One negative, they really seem to be chasing your money more throughout the resort. Be prepared to evaluate the value of your options. Unless the park is really crowded, I wouldn't recommend the fast pass for $89. This is in addition to park admission. Three days is plenty of time to see everything even when it is reasonably crowded. I had a great time and hope to visit again.
Like all the other Disney parks it was quite crowded this time of year. The climate can be hot during the day too. Expect the occassional shower. Fun for all ages and great photo opportunities.

My husband and I took our 13 and 10 year olds here 5/29/15-6/1/15. Overall we had a good time, but there were moments when I thought it was little more than a glorified Six Flags and I could have stayed home for that. We almost bought tickets for Disney World the day of to go there instead of another day at Universal that was already paid for. There were some rides one or both of the kids wouldn't go on (babies), but my husband and I managed to go on every ride at least once in one day at the park. This park has some rides for younger kids, but overall it's better for adults and older teens. There was an afternoon parade which most park go-ers treated as an inconvenient foot traffic disruption. Not anything like Disney World where there is a crowd of people watching the parade. Hardly anyone seemed interested in the parade. There are some shows worth seeing. I liked the horror show one. Citywalk is a big draw for adults. Harry Potter ride was good and Revenge of the Mummy. The dining plan is not a good value! the food is not good either. We also went to SeaWorld and Aquatica during this trip and preferred them over Universal. All of the rides that have any element of water in Islands of Adventure will get you drenched which makes the rest of the day very unpleasant. It was hot and I would not have minded getting wet except for the fact that my socks and sneakers were soaked and made my feet hurt. Overall good for adults and teens, but doesn't have the magic of Disney.

Was very and I mean very hot. The places where you stand in line should have more fans and maybe even shades besides sitting in the sun and baking while you wait in line for several minutes to hours. Prices of some things were a little high! Need to have more signes on the road to help navigate the place better, but was by far a great place to visit and get away for a couple of days. Loved the rides they were great and all the staff was very helpful!

This is a great place for all , rides ,restaurants, an night life and you don't have to go broke an also if you don't have an annual pass bring your AAA card because you get discounts on all your food in an out of the park
Wow what a great theme park! Traveled with 3 older teens and we loved going to the Universal Parks... did the 3 day tickets and it was well worth the money spent.
The Wizarding World of Harry Potter at Universal Orlando is out of this world. A must for any Harry Potter fan.
Amazing place to go with or without kids, there is always something for you and have fun, specially if you like the roller coasters!!!!!

Absolutely loved it~ The layout of the place is very similar to other Universal Studios (but that is to be expected) but most of the staff I encountered were friendly and polite. Food booths and location of help stations were convenient and useful; everything was extremely organized! I went there for an event where some of the Harry Potter cast came to the Wizarding World of Harry Potter section of the Park and the organization of the lines and management of customers and staff was well done! No unnecessary lines or space wasted.
Fantastic park, with lots of wonderful things to do and see! The rides are great and the Park was very well kept  We cannot wait to return!
don't forget to get one of those yummy turkey legs while enjoying the park. great place for family fun

I've visited the Universal Studios in Hollywood, California and loved it. I had high hopes for this location and I can say I was not disappointed. In fact, I can say that this is my new favorite theme park.  As a disabled traveler it's important to me to be able to get out and enjoy as much of what everyone else does and that includes theme parks. I purchased a 3 day park hopper pass and was impressed immediately.  The handicap parking was close by. All the rides had handicap accessible lines with most being through the exit. The staff at the rides were amazing and very helpful. The only one bad experience was the Harry Potter restaurant. I am on a mobility device and do not walk unassisted. The restaurant has a cue to go through similar to the regular rides. My mobility device didn't allow tight turns required so I had to ask the people behind me to please back up so I could get out. I asked at the front if I could just go in and find a seat while my companion went through the regular line to place our order. I proceeded to find a table and was immediately told by a wait staff that I had to leave my mobility device outside and transfer to a table. I explained I do not walk unassisted and she replied by rolling her eyes and asking me again to park my mobility device outside and walk in to a table. I left. I felt humiliated. It's hard enough not being able to walk unassisted but to be chastised for it by a wait staff at a theme park was humiliating and rude.  The remainder of the park was amazing. I went on the Incredible Hulk ride immediately and loved it. There were storms in the area so they had to shut down the rides periodically but we were able to ride most over the 3 days we were there.  I would recommend this park to those who are handicapped and able bodied over Disney World. This is cheaper, is handicap accessible and has working rides. Two thumbs up!

We had just one day free to select a park to go to and having been to Orlando on many occasions we selected Universal Studios.  Best Ride - The Mummy (so good we went on it twice!).  The Harry Potter area is fantastic, but very easy to miss. Look behind the brick wall to the right of the station, you will not want to miss out on that.  Although it was very expensive to buy a one day ticket (with Express Passes), it was a great day out, as always...

my family and I went here last year, it was awesome, my son was 7yrs old when we went, he rode most everything that was there except for 2 rides he was just a little shy of being tall enough for. he wasn't scared of any of the rides, we did both parks in 2 days...spent one day at each park, very much worth it, definitely made a lot of memories there

Universal Studios Orlando has plenty of fun and entertaining rides and attractions that are great for all-day family fun. Best time to go is November through February when the Florida weather isn't nearly as oppressive as summertime. It's also considerably less overcrowded during these months as well... with the exception of course being the few weeks around the year-end holidays.

Really enjoyed goung on all the rides especially the 3d Minions ride and Men in Black. Best to try and go on the Minions ride early in the day as it gets really busy.Harry Potter unbelievable but it gets busy, tried the butterbeer and thought it was sickly so maybe best to buy a half size. Diagon Alley amazing and Escape from Gringotts !

This was our 2nd time visiting as a family. We returned for Diagon Alley and it was worth our long trip. the attention to detail is amazing. The days we were there were rated 9/10 for business, but our longest wait was Despicable Me. I will say, both times we've been, that's been the longest, most brutal wait so if you go and want to ride Despicable Me, just know going into it that it's long and usually hot. I think Universal needs more shade, fans, and misters to help people waiting for this ride. All of those things are provided at Gringott's, where our wait was not that long. Last time we did not have park-to-park passes, but got them this time to ride the Hogwarts Express. Be sure to pay attention when going inside to get on the train as there is a place where they have used mirrors to make it look like people are disappearing into platform 9 3/4! Worth it because 1)the train ride is cool and saves walking when it's 100 degrees and everyone is tired and 2) being able to go over to Islands of Adventure, ride a water ride to get cooled off and then return, was totally worth it. U. Studios doesn't seem to have as many places to get cooled off, but maybe we just missed it this time around. Terminator ride was great and the Mummy is one of our favorites. We took in our own bottled water and snacks, but found out that small cups of ice water are available for free from vendors in the park and they were very nice about giving those out when we asked. Lots of walking, lots of fun!

Everyone must visit Universal if in Orlando. There is something for every age group. We had the bonus 2park ticket which gave us access to Islands of Adventure too. The rides, shops, scenery, eateries, Harry Potter world of course and the famous Hard Rock Cafe. Every bit fun and fabulous.
The new harry potter was realy nice . Just like the movies. Train ride was great g ave to go to both parks (shows a different story going there and coming back) Bring your money.

The Harry Potter attractions are great! Our kids had so much fun. However, the handlers for the characters such as the Simpsons and Despicable Me characters need to be friendlier with kids. They treated kids as if they were a secuirty threat or nuisance.

Just a magical place for any age. You can not do this in 1day. We went for 3days and would have happily done 4 if we had the time and energy. All the staff are lovely. The themes just fantastic. The thrill rides are great and worth the wait. The water rides are just as thrilling as the coasters.  It's worth the money.  The only negative is the line cutters. Not the parks fault as it happens everywhere.

We enjoyed our time at Universal Studios this Summer. The wait time for the majority of the rides was under 30 minutes. The expensive express pass upgrades are worth having if the wait times are excessive. Its best to wait until you get in the park before buying the express pass upgrades. If the lines are not too long you can enjoy the majority of the rides without spending the extra money. Also, if you purchase the express pass after 4 pm it is supposed to be half price. If the lines are long at the Harry Potter ride we suggest going on the single rider line that is found in the locker room inside the gift shop. Lots of great attractions in this park catering to everyone in the family.

Went mainly for the Harry Potter areas and loved it. The kids were in heaven and since they serve beer alongside the butter beer my wife and I were happy too. The level of detail is incredible. The ability to "use" the interactive wands all over the park was great too. The kids were never bored, tired or grumpy. Definitely looking forward to the Los Angeles Universal Studios getting this.

Harry Potter brought to life! It's amazing and I'm so glad we went! We visited Islands of Adventure/Hogwarts the year it opened up and were so excited to read that Universal Studios opened up Diagon Alley! It looks just like the movie and how you would imagine it from reading the books. All the shops are creative and imaginative and just amazing to see. My kids were so excited to visit Ollivanders because they watched so many You Tube videos of kids getting picked to test the wands. I warned them they might not be picked! It's not random! Whoever the first kid is in the room, the Wizard will line about 5 of you up on a row, positioning kid #1 in the front of the room. That kid is the one who gets picked to flick the wand and say the spells. It's very cool. We went through twice and timed it so we were first in line. Luckily it was a rainy day and not too crowded. Gringotts was cool mostly because it brings you into the movie. They've made the wait in line an experience by itself with all the goblins around and special props. That aside, the Transformers and Spiderman sims were our favorite! So much fun. The Minion sim is funny. My best advice is don't forget stuff like sunblock, an umbrella...because if you buy the stuff in the park - which is fun to do but SO expensive - you will pay triple the normal cost. If you're not staying at a theme park hotel, invest in the fast pass! It was so much fun to jump to the front of the line. It sucks to wait in line for so long. And this is Orlando, so expect thunderstorms in the afternoon.

Never had a great moment and fun with my wife since we married 2 years ago ! Like this time at universal studios ..it was really so fun we had a lot of fun and laugh ...little of scared ...lol for Rollercoasters :D we get wet too !! Just love it <3

This park was smaller than expected but we thoroughly enjoyed our time here. We absolutely loved the Simpsons section and had a 'big pink' donut from lard lads which was huge but tasted good. The Simpsons ride was one of our favourites. Diagon Alley is one of the most amazing things we have ever seen, the kings cross/ London bits outside are very realistic. We loved roller coasters but found rip ride rocket was quite rough and threw us around. Great day out.

Wow wow wow, this place is one of the best I have ever been to. Not a dull moment to be had fills me with excitement and sure does get the adrenalin going. This year I am going for the forth time. Cannot wait. Fun for all ages with plenty of excitement to be had.

Universal has improved this park a lot over the years, and I love it every time I go. The live shows are wonderful, and the rides are very well done. Dining options are also good for a theme park. Love it.
I love the Transformers area... I'm smiling like a 12 year old every time I walk up to it and leaving... what a ride! :)
That was one of the best parks I have ever visited. Worth a 2 days visit for each park. You should not miss all the 4d rides. Perfect experience.

Everything about it was simply incredible! The detail into each ride was mind blowing and we pretty much just sat with our mouths open the entire time. The transformers ride was by far the most impressive ride I have ever seen and the Harry Potter areas were amazing. Even for a non Harry Potter fan. A little strange to have it split over two parks with separate entrance tickets. I would recommend access to both parks and use the full day to see it all. This is for a group of 3 adults. If you have a family and kids it probably does take longer in which I would set aside two days for it all. Queue times were not bad at all (early July). Make sure you take the Hogwarts express to get between the parks- it's not just a form of transportation!

Great movie attraction themed rides. Fun for the entire family. The lines are long but move pretty quickly. However I would recommend the express pass for this side of the park. Or just go get on the other rides and usually by the time you make your way back the line is shorter and you can save money in your pocket.

great park men in black is stupid and Harry potter train ride...Harry potter 3D brilliant as most of it is brilliant....we found best time to go was around 6 in the evening....would recommend getting 10 dollar drink refill bottles you can fill them every 10 minutes and its only 6 dollars next day

Worth the money. I had an amazing time there. Great rides. Best theme park in the world. My top ten rides: 1. Harry potter 2. Hogwarts Express 3. Gringotts 4. Jurassic Park 5. Mummy 6. Simpsons 7. Spider-Man 8. Minion Mayhem 9. Rip saw 10. Popeye  U have to do these rides if u visit the park.

Amazing day out, lots of rides and shows and 3D shows. You will leave the park amazed. A lot of work goes into each section of the park. You can see many characters walking around, most of which you could swear they are the real people. Absolutely brilliant day out

My wife and I had been to the Universal Studios tour in California many years ago and I expected that this park would be similar. It was a complete revelation as it is so different and in many ways superior. There are rides, attractions, restaurants and a way for you to get around at your leisure, using early access passes, discount tickets and fast track entry. We went at our own pace, checked out the areas where there weren't long lines and had a ball. Universal Studios is very well organized with things to do to do for all ages and if you can stand the crush of many people milling around, a great experience.

We visited Universal Orlando in June15. We were staying at Loews Pacific who gave us fast passes plus early entry both days. The early entry meant we could visit the very popular harry Potter area before the gates officially opened. The multi dimensional 3D escape from gringotts ride is truly amazing and one of the best ride experiences you will ever have. The line was lengthy however you enter thru Gringotts bank so there is a lot to see on the way. We got to all all the rides in both parks over the 2 days we were there. One day we left the park for a few hours and came back in at night when it was a bit cooler. Both parks are very clean with lots of food options. Many of the rides also have free lockers at the ride entry which is very handy. Something I found very handy was the "universal orlando app". This app shows you real time where you are in the parks and also helps guide you to attractions and is very handy in finding the nearest bathroom. It also has descriptions of the attractions and wait times. As much as they add to the price, especially a family, the fast passes are well worth it. Some rides had 60min wait times and the fast passes brought the time down to 10-15mins.

Great!! We saved a bundle with the express pass. You can go all year long, multiple times a day. Another great thing is the free parking when you're a passholder. Otherwise you will find out its $17 a visit. The new Harry Potter section is well made. Full of excitement for all ages. Rip rocket roller coaster at night was a sight to see as well. Every night at 9:45pm there is a light show in universals lake next to the Transformers ride. Worth the visit at night. Wore the family out each day whether we arrived first in the morning or early in the evening. Have fun and save $$ with that annual pass (preferred annual pass). $152 down and $14 a month on a credit card.

The park was amazing! Everything was clean, it was separated in sections that made sense. The rides were great, ranging from thrill to peaceful enjoyment. If you are looking for Adventure you have to ride The Mummy & The Rocket roller coaster. If you are seeking a blissful ride you have to ride ET. Get on the Simpsons ride, if you enjoy that show. They have a section for kids. The Shrek & MIB rides were not that amusing, it was a bit of a waste of time.
This is a must do if you are in florida so much to see and do you will need a full day here so do not make plans for later that day.

One of my fave places in the world! Love it here, so many different things for all ages.The Mummy ride is one of the best! If visiting in Sept/Oct make sure you go to Halloween Horror Nights, not for the little ones but if into horrors and getting a fright then its the place to be.

My two daughters thoroughly enjoyed all the Harry Potter attractions and the Dr. Seuss ones as well. We remained outside the park and went to the movies while they entertained their selves. It was a terrific afternoon for all of us. the park is very spacious and has much to do.

Universal is a great theme park. every time you go back there is always something new. The first time we went the King Kong ride was the must do ride, but that was way back, then they had back to the future ride, now all gone. But they have been replaced by rides which are relevant for today, such as Harry Potter, Despicable me, That's what i mean its always reinventing itself. This is a must see theme park, every bit as good as the Disney parks. it seemed to be fairly compacted and easy to get around. we didn't do Universal islands of Adventure, much too old for that, when you pass 30 (+ another 37) it passes you bye. But I'll get one of my granddaughters to go and write the revue for you. In the mean time enjoy this park it's great.

Took my grandchildren because they wanted to see the Harry Potter Attractions. Nine and seven are a little young for anything but just walking around. Rides are for much bigger children. Had to get two park tickets to ride the Hogwarts express between the parks, which is the thing they enjoyed the most. Loved the parking ploy. You can park for $5 more in the parking garage but for the $17 you had to park at the very top of the parking garage with no shade. Of course, the enclosed parking garage was empty as you went up. Haven't they gotten enough of your money with out nickle and diming you to death.

If you have young children who watch the latest cartoon characters or are an adult who is in to roller coasters in a big way, the this park and "islands of adventures" is for you. However the rest of the park relies on past, and not very classic, films. The most annoying aspect for me was, having taken a huge amount of money for entrance tickets, they then bombard you with shops, eating places and long queues. You can avoid the queues by purchasing an express ticket but even that is not cheap. The quality of the merchandise in the shops was not high and the quality of the food was equally disappointing. The highlight was undoubtedly the hogwarts train journey between the parks. It is exceptionally well done as is the Harry Potter village. Beautifully constructed and the attention to detail is outstanding. The downside? You guessed it nothing but shops, eateries and three roller coasters - none of which appealed to my family. Even the "family friendly" ride was far to physical. Incidentally the cost of a simple "wand" is almost USD 100!!! So if you take you junior lovers of all things Potter, expect it to be a very expensive visit!!!  If this is trying to vie with the classical Disney theme park, it fails miserably. If it is trying to appeal to "Minions" enthusiasts then it probably passes. Hugh  PS I had never heard of Minions until this visit!!,

We had a wonderful time at Universal. The employees were all friendly. We absolutely love the fact many wait line areas are air conditioned! The park was very clean and well laid out. We also love the fact they cater to smokers and do have special areas throughout the park were smoking is allowed. This makes family trips so much easier since we do have smokers. They have such a variety of rides that cater to every age. We would love to have more water rides since the ones they do have are awesome! Food and drinks are over priced as are most parks. There is a variety of shopping there as well also a little pricey. They offer VIP parking for an extra fee. Pay it! It's worth it for sure. We are already planning our next visit. Must visit this place if in or near Orlando.
LOVE the Transformer ride. So worth the wait. It might be my all time favorite. Be mindful of the temperature and dress accordingly.

Great experience, family with kids is great visit, amazing attractions, the Transformers once is just magnificent, one advise the Fast Pass is a must, if not the queues are too long, only pizza, hot dogs, and sandwiches and coke products. Once full day is enough to visit everything, take the troller with small kids, too much to walk.

This is how theme parks should be, the staff are very attentive and the attractions are all close to perfection. The rides will please even the most faint-hearted, the attention to detail is amazing. It's expensive but worth every penny. If you suffer from motion sickness, you will be fine on most rides. Men in Black and Harry Potter (Gringots is fine) are the only two which you may not enjoy, the rest are fine.
I go to this park 2 - 4 times a week and I am a local. I love everything about Universal Florida! It's the best place to hang out with friends, meet new people, make new friends and enjoy the park!
Well worth the money. The Harry Potter exhibit was great. Our teenagers loved it. All rides were excellent.

So much to see and do, go to an onsite hotel overnight to get express passes for all rides - well worth it in July as wait times topped 75 mins in normal queues ( 10-15max in express). Favourites have to be the new Harry Potter area. The kings cross station and London street facade is so authentic, then you turn into Daigon Alley and and it is too amazing for words. Loads to see in each of the magical windows, and if you get an interactive wand you can perform magic at various places. Gringotts bank is brilliant from the bank workers, the chandeliers, the lift taking you down to the vaults. The escape from gringottts ride is excellent, as you would expect. Go to Olivanders wand shop as there is an unexpected wand master who performs magic, amd you can also choose a wand with properties that suit your personality. The Howarts express is not just a ride on a train from one park to another, it is a magical journey where you walk through the wall into platform 93/4 and the carriages are the old fashioned train carriages and you will see your journey to Hogwarts through the windows. So amazing!! Best rides are the Hollywood Rip Ride Rocket - INSANE and you get to see / buy a video at the end and the revenge of the mummy is also fab. Lots of 3d or 4d rides here also which are great - minions is sooooo busy, so either do first or later the evening. Enjoy!
