Ah Universal Orlando. Hello my old friend. Nothing quite says "welcome home" more than briskly strolling through City Walk in the morning sun, surreptitiously cranking up the pace to beat the excited multitudes and entering the greatest theme park on earth through that iconic yellow arch. This is - blimey - the tenth time I've been here, maybe more, and each time is even more special and every bit as electrifying as the first visit back in 1991.  The evolution is extraordinary. Since the last time we were here one of my favourite rides (Jaws) has been retired and replaced by the colossal expansion of Harry Potter, and The Simpsons Ride has now expanded into Springfield, complete with Moe’s Tavern and Kwik-E-Mart. We had much to explore and this time we had a supplementary almost four-year-old in toe.  In many ways this review is as inane as it is bias. Mardy bums look away now because (spoiler alert) there’s nothing critical to say about this astonishing park. It’s so good. I mean it’s SO GOOD. Universal Islands is as close to perfect as you can get, and just when you think it can’t possibly maintain it’s dreamlike zenith you discover brand new qualities that are as reassuringly reliable as listening to the second half of ‘Abbey Road’; you’ve heard it all before a hundred times, yet it still gets better.  So instead of trying to cram every single highlight of the resort into a single review (you can take it for granted that the roller-coasters are world class, the staff are impossibly chirpy and the dinosaurs in Jurassic Park still look convincing), I’ve picked out a few unsung highlights that don’t often get a mention but are important to us.  The child swap system is better than in any park we’ve been. Instead of waiting at the ride entrance, you queue together as a family and when you get to the front of the line one of you takes baby to a comfy, air-conditioned area usually with a TV and plenty of seating while the other enjoys the ride. You then literally swap (high-fiving is optional) and the other parent joins at the very front of the queue. This way you only ever queue once.  A place that we’ve rarely visited in the past, but where essentially became home base for us this time, was Woody Woodpecker’s Kidzone. Our boy LOVED the Curious George Goes To Town splash area – so much so that we ended up spending much of the day doing laps of the splash zone, Woody Woodpecker’s Nuthouse Coaster and the nearby E.T. Ride. We didn’t mind as the hours we spent here under shady trees meant we gave our feet a much-needed rest while the boy ran around lapping it all up.  I could go on and on about the quality of Universal; it’s mind-boggling scale, the watertight service, and an unwavering desire to make everything faultless, but that would be dull so I’ll wrap it up here (I haven’t even mentioned the thrill of meeting Spider-Man, the astonishing detail that’s gone into creating Harry Potter and the Escape From Gringotts or the remarkably real interpretation of Kings Cross train station, all of which deserve pages and pages of reviews just on their own). Plus as if to tease me into coming back for more, a new King Kong ride is set to open soon, and judging by the view from the Pteranodon Flyers it’s going to be every bit as insanely detailed and breath-taking as Diagon Alley.  So I’ll just say this: don't waste your time or hard-earned holiday money going anywhere else. Although Orlando has plenty of other parks and attractions they are all inferior to the unreserved master. Universal remains the summit. And we can’t wait to go home again.

Great park. Great rides. Great staff.  The park is well designed and laid out. All the rides are great fun. The lines were not too long when we were there and the iPhone/ smartphone app is an excellent way of managing your day.  Value for money. Thoroughly recommended. A must place to visit when in Florida.
Fantastic with brilliant rides more suited for teenagers than small kids.The only down side us the long queues and the fast track us nit worth it as not as good as Dusney Magic kingdom, a rip off.

The park was extremely busy today. 120 mins queue for despicable me! The Shrek 4D was so busy they wouldn't even let people queue in standby. Even the fast pass lines were long. So a say of shopping and no rides. Didn't even go in Harry Potter part, will do that another day. Hot, lack of shaded seating. A good day out though if you have the stamina to queue in the heat for 2 hours. Preferred parking has gone up again, now $25 but still worth the extra.

We traveled in July during the 4th Holiday, there are five us. I have a 14 and 2 six year old children; who totally enjoyed their time. You can child swap if you child is not able to ride. The child swap rooms are air conditioned and equipped with plenty of seating. We are from Florida and purchased annual passes. We will be going back in August again for a weekend. Food is expensive if you are understanding this is a theme park. But the Turkey legs were the BEST!! the refillable cups, buy one if you are a thirsty bunch, and keep it for the kids as a reminder. the refills ran us like $2 for a huge cup and lasted the entire time between meals. The park will refill them for FREE with ice water. GREAT TIMES!! We are all going back.
Holiday 2011  Stay for a three week break and visited this park during this time. I was amazed by the amount of ride geared up for every ages. Overall a experience not to be missed😀

Universal was on our list for the new Harry Potter experience, as well as some of the other rides we had not seen since we were last there, like Spiderman. The Harry Potter ride was so good that, on exiting, the four of us looked at each other and all said "Yep, guess we have to do that again." The park was clean and the service excellent. It should be noted that there are two components to Harry Potter - one in this park, and the other in the Islands of Adventure park. In order to ride both - and both are great - you need to have the park hopper pass. You get to ride the Harry Potter train between the two if you like. The ride in this park, "Escape from Gringotts" is well conceived, the wait line takes you through a Goblin bank, and every detail was taken care of. Also, you simply MUST try Spiderman. We really enjoyed the trip!

I was speechless, it was so fun and amazing. Spectacular for the whole family, any age and anyone would love it I'm sure. The rides are top notch and especially the Simpson's, I will not spoil it but it is INCREDIBLE! It is My favourite ride of all time, the queueing isn't too bad either. Such an enjoyable experience...10/10

we traveled with 5 kids, 18,16,12,10 and 5. There is something for everyone including adults, meal plans was the best investment. Take a hat and lots of sunscreen if you travel in the summer. We took water and snacks help keep food cost down. Harry Potter and Jurassic park was a hit with everyone.
We had Unlimited entry to tree theme parks and my kids had a blast. I had a great time at "wet 'n' Wild.

Loved the early entry provided by hotel. Loved Diagon Alley and the Gringott's ride. The workers are dressed in HP themed clothing. The shopping and buildings and everything HP was awesome to see and do. The rest of Universal Studios was okay, but the HP section is up-to-date and much more lively.

We only went for the one day and wish we had brought the ticket for two days as we had so much fun. The rides were brilliant and we loved everything there.Very busy with lots of people waiting to go on the rides. All well worth the wait. It was great and a lovely way to spend the day.

Stunningly detailed themes, exhilarating rides, lots of stuff to see and do when you want a break from standing in queues to take a ride. Rides are terrifyingly fun - that oxymoron is what you want to describe a roller coaster though! You want that adrenalin rush, that fear factor and a great time all rolled into many fast rides - and you will get your wish that's for sure! On the cute side Toon town and Dr Seuss Landing were my favorites. My least favorite ride was the one from Hogwarts - though the castle is spectacular, the interior detail is awesome, the Herry Potter experience ride made me so nauseous I was sick for the rest of the day and couldn't do another ride till the next day. All that in your face graphics was awful. Diagon alley is a not to be missed part of the Islands of Adventure park. Great parks, great value.
Our visit to Universal Studios was full of fun. Transformers, Minion, Rockit and simpsons are must. Harry Potter attractions are the best.

Great park especially if the weather turns as the majority of rides are inside, so are not effected if there's lightning in the area. We spent 3 days covering Universal studios and Island of Adventure so make sure you buy more than a 1 day pass. Stand out rides, Harry Potter Gringotts, Simpsons simulator. The Mummy. Dragons roller coaster.
Liked: Springfield section: Simpsons characters, rides, & food! Fear Factor, Beatlejuice, Horror Make - Up shows.

I can't say much about universal studios that probably hasn't been said a thousand times before:  1. The attractions are superb. Terminator, Harry Potter, the Mummy, Men in Black, the Simpsons.....WOW!  2. For a one day trip this place is remarkably expensive, ($100+/person), but I guess that isn't much different than Disney, a ski resort, or an NFL game.  3. This place is CROWDED in the summer, even on a Monday.  4. The experience would be so much better if they would do a fast-pass system like Disney. The lines are horrible, and to offer an "express pass" for $80/person is simply insulting.

A great compliment to Islands of Adventure ... Can't stress enough how impressed we all were with this, especially Diagon Alley! The attention to detail is incredible. It's a great place to go and spend an hour or so to get out of the sun... The interactive wands are a brilliant idea. Across both Universal Parks there's plenty to keep everyone entertained for a week... Take your time and select the must do's each day. Get there early to beat the crowds... The Hogwarts Express is a brilliant way to get to Islands of Adventure. We would recommend the Horror Make-Up show in the heat of the afternoon; very funny and informative. Food can be pricey ... And not brilliant, so try to survive on snacks that you can take in ... Get your main meal elsewhere!

Spent a week in Disney World then stopped by here for two days. Not very impressed. Rides were fun but the parks in general were just mediocre. Maybe it was because I had just left Disney but this park seemed small and below average. However, if you are a big Harry Potter fan (which I am not) you will love this place.

Have visited this place many times and it is always fantastic.. Very easy and layout has a great flow. Have never really had to wait a long time but understand it does happen.find it very well organised and would defo recommend over disny which is a nightmare.
I thoroughly enjoy my visits to Orlando, due yo universal studios. The Harry Potter attraction is AMAZING!!! Rides are great, food is plenty.
The roller coasters here a bit too much for me plus the staff is not as nice and can seem a bit standoffish.

Second day at universal studios and most disappointing to see that the Harry porter and the escape from gringots ride keeps breaking down. What is even more disappointing is that after standing in the queue for over an hour there is little communication on what is happening and when it will resume. Feel for all the paying public that spend so much money to come and get trapped inside this ride and forego their time and even express passes at other rides. All attendants are busy talking to each other and laughing.

I have to say I really enjoyed this park. The section of the park that has Harry Potter is awesome. The store fronts and alley look just like it did in the movie. The have an awesome feature for kids and adults too had fun with this. You purchase a wand from the store and there are spots within Dragon Alley that are marked where you stand with the wand and move the wand in the direction that this icon on the pavement shows you and you make things turn on. Water fountains turn on, rain fall, puppets play, etc. Real fun. The actual ride was awesome. The effects were awesome and the bank you walk through looks like it did in the movie. The transformers ride was another of my favorites. The Simpsons section of the park was cool too. They have a Moes Tavern where you can go grab a drink at the bar and go grab a bite to eat. The lines in the park are typical. Sometimes a 40 minute wait other times up to 65 mins. But the lines keep moving and they have it set up so that there is always something to look at while waiting in line. Seems like it goes by fast. All in all we enjoyed all the rides. The cost per ticket is a little high. Wish it was a little cheaper and we would go back and visit again soon.

We had 4 day park to park tickets with unlimited fastpass. Although this is expensive it is definitely worth it. The queues without fastpass were between 60 and 120 minutes for most of the bigger attractions, with fastpass the longest we waited was 20 minutes! The Transformers 3d ride was a big hit with my teenage sons as was the Mummy roller coaster. The live shows around the park are very good and the singers can give most professionals a run for their money. Don't waste your fastpass on the great movie experience or Shrek. Although they are ok you would feel cheated if you don't have unlimited. Lots of iced water stations around the park all free of charge. You do need to buy a lanyard for your passes but only buy 1 per couple as you can put them back to back and save some dollars. The terminator show is well worth it.

We especially enjoyed the Harry Potter section of Universal Studios. My 15 year old bought an interactive wand with her own money, $47., which I thought was expensive but she did have a good time making things move with it. We also really enjoyed the ride. Toward the evening hours, there was only a 30 minute wait for most rides.The children's macaroni and cheese is good and I had some. Parking is expensive $17. a day, perhaps use a hotel shuttle. We wanted the freedom to come and go so we paid it. The train ride has a different video each way which was fun too.
So much attention to detail in this park. You will love Springfield and Diagon Alley - our family think the Harry Potter attractions in Universal are way better than the original in London!

This place is incredibly overrated. The rides are minimally interesting at best, save for the fact that the themes are based on Universal movies that are well liked and remembered. There are no truly scary rides, therefore it is a park that is best suited for young children and people who scare easily.

"Pros" Huge theme park with something for everyone. Plan on at least one full day or a couple days to see every thing. Rides, shows, shopping and more shopping. All sorts of places to eat. WEAR - comfy shoes and clothes. Buy the ALL Day cup ... $13 and can fill around both parks for the day. If you plan to go on RIDES ... be sure to buy the "fast Pass... we paid over $130.00 a person for this add on but wouldn't have been able to ride anything without it. Lines were at least an hour or more long. These passes allow you to be in a separate line. (still wait but not near as long) You MUST rent lockers for have someone to stay back with your stuff because nothing can go on most rides. Lockers run about $4.00 at each ride... or you can rent a big one at the park entrance for about $15 or $20. But way too far away from anything to be much use. The train that runs between the two parks is great but again a long wait because Fast pass doesn't work on everything! "CONS" - price for fast passes. $130. for each person (price does change according to time of the year) or $3,000 for VIP up to $25,000... and if you plan to ride you need the fast pass. We didn't plan enough time for attend both parks and missed so many of the rides and shows. Spent way too much time waiting in lines !!

I wish i didn´t have to leave!!!!!!!!!!!! :'( It was a trip of a lifetime....others might disagree because it rained cats and dogs both days but i was determined to see everything! The tickets are kind of expensive especially the express passes but worth it since the lines are HUGE!...without it i wouldn't have seen anything. The MINIONS were everywhere and it was adorable!! Some rides i din´t understand before i entered that were (inside the buildings) rollercosters, witch i tend to be kind of scared of, be them with or without 3D effects...i was kind of nervous but had a blast even though some are quite scary like the Revenge of the Mummy. (had to close my eyes a second...lol) And the Harry Potter World on both parks....i almost died dead (XD) it was perfect! the details are amazing like - WOW. the rides are fantastic and super interactive...paintings talking to us and each other XD super cool. the food and sweets delicious, i was sad for not liking the butterbeer it was too sweet and the gas it was too much but i loveddd the pumpkin juice! super delicious like eating a pie filling in liquid form - yum! Also saw the singing sorceress: Celestina Warbeck and the Banshees in Diagon Alley they were amazing to watch and so fun. I just wish there was a park like these in Europe so i could go back every couple of months and take my cousin with me.... Here's to hopefull wishing ;)
Excellent rides and food. If only the afternoon Thunderstorms would have held off. Love the express option!! Way better than Disney's!! Just pay the extra money and get in line!!!
The best time ever! Parking is expensive as are express passes but the rides and facilities are amazing!! You have to go on the Escape from Gringotts ride ... I loved it 😉

Cost too high for fast pass option.Many wait times in excess of 50 minutes in Islands of Adventure. Not enough lockers for those riding coasters, especially with new rule that you cannot have anything in your pockets (wallets, keys, phones, etc). Great food and service from Ashley at Confisco Grille & Backwater Bar. She was extremely attentive and very customer oriented - gave special attention to kids. Overall - enjoyed the day with friends and family!

These parks are definitely worth a day trip, especially for any Harry Potter fans. But i think really a day is all you need for both parks. And there just isn't the same feeling as Disney. Now that Disney offer three FREE, pre bookable fast passes per day in their parks it really puts Universal to shame. Going from no wait in Disney to having to wait around an hour for pretty much every attraction in Universal it really puts you off. I also found wait times inaccurate. We cued for the Popeye water ride which was supposed to be a 20 minute wait but we were waiting double that, in enclosed and hot conditions. I felt like i was about to pass out by the time we finally got to ride. Please sort out a better fast pass system!

Went during haunted horror nights and had an absolute blast. The lines were a little long but they made the anticipation of the rides a little greater. The actual haunted attractions were a little sub par in my 2nd trip but still fun. If you go buy your tickets online vs at the gate you will save a ton of money. Never go in the summer. Off season trips are always the best route

A 2 day park to park passes were great as gave us the flexibility we needed. Both days enjoyed by all. Take advantage of the dining package. It's worth it. If driving, $17 to park, however you can leave and return later when parks stay open longer. The larger park is "Studios " so plan ahead. Harry Potter sets are amazing & the rides are incredible especially "Escape from Gringotts" & "Forbidden Journey ". Overall, we throughly enjoyed our visit. All staff we encountered were knowledgeable and helpful. Queuing for main rides was expected, but fast passes were to expensive @ $99 per person per day on top of entry price

Holiday of a lifetime! Fantastic place to visit with teenagers, so much to do with all the exciting rides and parks! Harry Potter is a must and the Hulk ride has to be done. So much to do here and at night a visit to Central Walk is recommended to try one of the great restaurants!

They have done an awesome job with the Wizarding World of Harry Potter area.....it's very unique & fun. Even though I miss the Back to the future ride, the Simpsons ride that replaced it, is awesome. Our favorite ride is the Mummy...always fun & exciting. The Transformers 3D ride is now open. It's a lot like the Spiderman ride at Islands of Adventure. It's a great fun filled day to spend with the family. The heat & sun in the summer can be brutal though. Thank goodness they have plenty of shops to step inside to cool off.

Just returned from our visit to Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure with my 13-year-old daughter. We had a 4-day park-to-park pass. We appreciated the 4-day pass as it took the pressure off and allowed us to pace ourselves. We spent the first day primarily at Universal Studios, the second at Islands of Adventure, the third between both and the fourth for mostly shopping.  First, I have to say that the two sections of Harry Potter are, in short, AMAZING!!!! Diagon Alley will transport you directly to the movie and the que for the Escape from Gringots ride is incredible. The train ride between both lands is a great treat and the castle in Islands of Adventure is awe-inspiring and offers an awesome ride. We also loved almost every ride in both parks, despite the fact that most require 3-D glasses to enjoy, they are still very well done. The only rides we didn't get on were the Minions Ride and Rip, Ride, Rockit at Universal Studios because the lines were easily 80 minutes for the majority of the time. Other than that, we had decent waits (no more than 30 minutes) and found that an express pass was not needed.  That being said, Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure need to work on their crowd control issues. The quick service restaurant we visited on our first day took our order within 5 minutes. But, I paid and came around the corner to a massive crowd of people waiting for food. I waited at least 20 minutes for two chicken salads, which felt excessive considering the salads are already prepared. The food was good though.  Next to the wait for food, the experience of using their free ride lockers would send anyone with claustrophobia into a panic attack. Several rides have a "no bags or items in your pockets allowed" policy and require you to store your items in a locker. Throughout both parks are areas with clusters of lockers. The lockers can be rented for the day or they kindly provide a free locker for a window of anywhere between 45 minutes - 2 hours.  However, the circus that occurs within these spaces of people packed like sardines trying to reach a locker rental computer is crazy. Many of these areas have multiple entrances, so people start lining up for a section from multiple places, leaving a lot of frustration for who is next in line. Also, once you reach a computer and successfully reserve or re-open the locker, there are people reaching all around you and pressing you in tightly to try and reach their locker. If you are someone who appreciates personal space, these places will likely make you nuts. They are definitely an exercise in patience. It's a good premise to offer these lockers, but it is just poor planning and laziness by Universal to ignore the incredibly frustrating experience they have become.  In the Universal vs. Disney comparison, Universal wins for us on rides, but Disney far surpasses Universal on knowing how to move a crowd around in a pleasant way. Hopefully, Universal will seek out a more comfortable process for this because it was the only negative experience we had at the parks.
As good as its sister park and now even better with the magical Hogwarts Express and the frankly astonishing Diagon Alley and Gringotts ride. Awesome!

Universal have done a great job on developing this place with a good balance of rollercoasters, various rides and shows (4D and other). Hogsmeade and Diagon Alley for Harry Potter fans and non fans alike is amazing. Their attention to detail is outstanding and really makes the difference. It is not cheap, so start saving if you're planning on going. Express passes are an essential. They're expensive but they save so much time. Some of the rides waiting times were up to 90 minutes long!!! A great idea is to buy a half day express pass for 45 dollars plus tax. You can use it after 4 o clock. This way you can do all the things that don't take an express pass in the early half of the day and do the rest come 4 o clock. The park stays open until 10 so there's plenty of time. Eating there is expensive too. Maybe eat well before you come to the grounds and have just one meal there. Bring your camera. Must dos in my opinion are Harry Potter in both Islands of Adventure and Universal Studios, Simpsons land, Toon Lagoon and there's so much more cool stuff. We did it in 2 days. ..all of it. But it was tight. 3 days would be plenty of time and you can relax, particularly if you're bringing kids. Fireworks at night are a nice end to the day too. They also offer lanyards for 10 dollars at the gates. Buy one or your tickets will get wet or damaged or lost. Well worth it. The staff are all so happy and helpful. They really do work well and make the place run smoothly. Well done to them. If you buy a multi park ticket it'll grant you access to a number of other places as well that'll give you value for money. Look into the options available before you buy. Most importantly enjoy it! It's brilliant!

The attractions are awesome. I'm a great fan of The Simpsons, the simpsons ride is the best. The transformers, despicable me, and Harry Potter are amazing. There are many things to do, and for all ages. The locations are spectacular.

We really enjoyed both Universal Studios and Island of Adventure. Our main purpose was to do everything Harry Potter (HP), which is mainly what we did. We had the early admission, which really helped but we did not have the pass to skip the lines because you could not use them on any of the HP rides. The lines moved fairly fast and like most parks now they try to keep you inside or cool with shade and fans. One thing we learned late in the day was to get in the single rider line, which moved faster than the regular line. I was with teenagers so,it was not important for us to ride together. However, even in the single rider line we ended up going at the same time.  The ride through the castle was awesome as was the train ride. The Gringots ride was fun but far too short, which was disappointing.  My biggest complaint is the self-serve soda option. We paid $11 for a souvenir cup with unlimited refills. However, you can ONLY use them at a self-service station which seemed to be few and far between and well hidden. I think I spent far too much time looking for a refill station than I should have, which was annoying. I ended up getting one soda (original fill) and a refill with water for $11.  We purchased the dining card, which seemed to be a good value for what you got. Please not that Butter Bear is considered a snack and not a drink on this plan.
This is a great place to visit if you like movie memorabilia, behind the scenes film making experiences, splashy shows from animated movies, and roller coasters.

went here last year with my family and little boy and can honestly say this had to be my favourite park out the lot and there is alot. my little boy loved it esp since he was a big fan of jurrasic world and spider man. well worth a visit

apart from the long walks the kids loved it and I was able to get on so many rides and thanks to the fast pass we were able to skip the long lines . everyone had fun and there's something for everyone to do at the park

So I just got back from Universal last night and I hated it so much that I felt the need to go out of my way to create a TripAdviser account just to type this.  First off, I could not believe just how unfriendly the staff was. At certain times I felt like I was at some town fair run by teenagers from Camp Crystal Lake. They seemed irritated all of the time. Now granted, not all of the staff was like this. For example, the staff at the WWOHP were extremely friendly. It was like I was at a whole different place.  Along with this, we had a terrible time with their fast pass program. For a family of 4 with fast passes and food and whatnot, it ended up costing us $1000. Even with the fast passes we still had to wait in lines that were 15 minutes long. You know what? That's not good enough. We expect to get on the rides immediately with no questions asked if we are paying a grand.  Secondly, and this one really pissed me off:  Universal seems to have some sort of unjustified anti-filming policy when riding the rides. I am a videographer and whenever I go on vacation I always film our experiences. Oh no, but not at Universal. They don't allow filming. Allow me to elaborate. On the ride "Jurassic Park River Adventure" I was filming this ride with a Gopro hero 4 strapped onto my Gopro extreme heavy duty chest harness built for extreme conditions such as mountain climbing and in this case, riding rides. So here we are, riding the ride and everything is fine, or so I thought. All of a sudden, we reach the final climactic drop involving the T-Rex. Just then, the ENTIRE ride stops and we here one of those Camp Crystal Lake employees over some sort of intercom telling me to put my Camera away for supposed safety's sake. There were so many things wrong with the situation:  1. I was unaware of this film rule. When I got on the ride nobody told me to put my camera away. It took them until the very end of the ride, right before the final drop to tell me to stop what I was doing. This not only destroyed the whole ambience of the ride but horribly embarrassed myself and my family.  2. I was told to put the camera away for "safety". Now granted, if I was carrying some sort of giant camera and flailing it in the air that's different. But this wasn't the case. This thing was strapped to my body like superglue. And when he told me to put it away I scrambled to find a way to get the camera off my chest. I ended up pointing the camera downwards because that's all I could do. I couldn't remove the camera from my chest unless I got out of the boat. So they had to stop the entire ride for that!  3. Lastly, I believe they might also be worried about "spoiling the ride" which is another reason why they might have this rule out in place. To that I say go on YouTube, there's dozens of videos of rides from the park.  Now to those reading you might be thinking "well rules are rules" to that I say, Disney World does not have an anti filming rule. I got on every ride at Disney World and was able to film with no questions asked. Not only that but the staff is extremely friendly no matter where you go.  Moral of the story? Take your money to Disney World because Universal is just ridiculous.

We have been visiting Florida for roughly 20 years and until this year hadn't bothered with Universal. Overall, it wasn't bad. There are a couple of GOOD thrill rides plus a lot of 3D and 4D rides - our favourite being The Simpsons (tip: listen to Homer's comments - they're hilarious!). I tend not to agree with the other reviews that claim there's a lot of walking and it's hot - well, it is hot but this is Florida..! However, you can get some respite from the heat by going in to the the indoor rides. As for the amount of walking, try the Disney parks and then say there's a lot of walking.... I do agree though with the comments about being overpriced. Most of the parks are overpriced but in particular we thought the fast pass/express pass was an absolute rip off. We didn't bother when we found it was going to cost the same amount as our park tickets cost for a three day pass each! Also, DON'T bother with the Photo Pass thing. This is similar to the Disney Memory Maker except: 1. you pay per day (as opposed to the one-off fee that Disney charge) 2. aside from the official photographers near the front gate, there are hardly any elsewhere - even at the character greets! We paid $99 for a three day pass and we made it work by accosting every official photographer we could find and getting all ride photos. The photographers don't even seem that good either. Talking of over pricing, the merchandise is excessive too. The Harry Potter interactive wands are nearly $50 and the Marauder's Maps are similar too (for a printed piece of paper?!!). Okay, we bought a wand for our son but drew the line at the map. Parents with multiple children are likely to leave with considerably lighter wallets! We found both Universal parks to be way more chaotic than the Disney parks e.g. try getting in to eat at any of the restaurants and you'll see... Also, one thing we were appalled about was this 'plus size' thing. If you're classed as 'too large' you can't ride some rides e.g. Harry Potter's Forbidden Journey. Diagon Alley is amazing and we felt better than Hogsmeade. The attention to detail is fantastic and make sure you take The Hogwarts Express between parks - it's not what you expect! Also worth doing is Escape from Gringotts. It's worth the wait time. Sadly, the Terminator ride is now very dated and a bit lame. Here are a few tips we'd suggest: 1. don't bother with the photo pass. 2. accept you're going to queue and don't bother with the fast passes. If you're disabled you can get a 'Call Back' which means you go to the ride, ask for a call back time and can then return anytime after that 'call back time' to use the fast pass queue. 3. if you're disabled, visit Guest Services to discuss your visit with them as they can give useful advice and tips. 4. buy a refillable cup and share it. 5. make use of the shops and indoor rides to cool down. 6. DON'T queue over 45 minutes for the Minion Mayhem ride. It's good but definitely not worth the 125 minute queue times we saw. 7. if there are rides you want to do that have long queue lines, get to them first thing! If you get there after 1000, arrange to to them the next day to save yourself the pain of waiting. 8. Visit Diagon Alley! It's got a lot of shade but is crazy busy BUT it's worth it. 9. try butterbeer. 10. if thrill rides are your thing, do Rock-it and The Hulk. They're certainly among my favourite roller coasters. 11. for the lockers (they're free and you have to use them for some rides), send ONE person in and NOT your entire family (as some intellectually challenged people choose to do!). 12. eat early (before 1145) to avoid the lunch time chaos - and an amount of time in the ride queues! The earthquake place is not bad if you're okay having burgers for one day and you can add as much/as little garnish as you want. 13. You can drink for free if you just ask for a cup of water at the drink stations.

Universal Studios FL had a lot to offer. It's best to get a 2-park 3-day pass, the Universal Dining Plan, and Photo-Connect. I travel on a budget and have found it most economical to bundle. At Islands of Adventure, there are lots of fun things to go like the Dr. Seuss trolley ride (low key) and the Incredible Hulk Coaster, but let's be real, it's Harry Potter that we come to see! If you stay on-site, you get early admission to the Wizarding World of Harry Potter and believe me, IT'S WORTH IT.  The lines for the Forbidden Journey ride can get looooong, and there's no express pass for HP. The castle is beautifully created with all the things you love about the magical world. There are moving paintings, coats of arms, gargoyles, Dumbledore- style office, and holograms - lots and lots of holograms. The ride is 3-D excitement where you go flying with Harry, Ron, and Hermione. Hogsmeade is so well done, you feel as if you've been given a week-end pass to relaxation. Grab a butter-beer (not my fave) or grab a bite to eat at the Three Broomsticks. The food is quite good. Now hop the Hogwarts Express to the other park.  At Universal Studios there's the Minion ride (cute), Men in Black, Mummy, and Transformers (exciting), but what are we there for? Harry Potter, of course. Diagon Alley is first rate. Go first to Escape from Gringotts because the wait can be extensive. (By the way, Diagon Alley is very far from the park entrance. Don't be distracted-head there straight away.) The inside of the bank is awesome, the dragon perched atop the bank is awesome (and even more awesome when it breathes fire), and did I say the ride is awesome?! Well, IT IS! Get some ice cream, a pumpkin juice, or a meal at the Leaky Cauldron. It's all good.  Overall, Universal is Awesomesauce. If you like Mexican food, try Antojitos at City Walk. Enjoy.

I must admit it's been a few years since I have been to a theme park & forgotten how bad the lines R, but if the ride is worth it can make up for it. This brings me to one of the worst rides in Orlando, how Universal can put this out just shows they really don't care how they get your $$ out of your pocket.  Well on to the experience itself, after our family of 5 had stood in line for around 40 minutes ( not bad over the entire parks lines ) we boarded the great looking train for what we thought would be a great treat, I mean who wouldn't want to ride the famous Hogwarts Train. I believe we paid a extra $35 bucks per adult, I can't recall if there is a discount for kids.  WHAT A WASTE OF MY HARD EARNED $$, the short ride to basically nowhere consist of basically a real nice TV up against the carriage window showing a short movie featuring the characters from the movies as the train moves the 1000 yds between parks.  Lets not forget that to even do this you have to buy a two park pass for the one day. You can walk out the main entrance of either park & enter the other in less than ten minutes & save hundreds of $$.  DON"T DO IT, no matter how much the kids beg, you will kick yourself.  Another thing, the locker situation is a absolute nightmare, you might want to think about renting one a day & use it as a base instead of putting your items up at every ride that requires it.  The TSA have a number of people working the coaster lines, when they say nothing in your pocket, they mean it. You get passed the first guy, but they have metal detectors & staff with wands just like the airport, some of these guys really love their job.  This comment is for anyone working at Universal who would hope keep up with Tripadvisor. The lines were driving me crazy, so I was going to get us all Fast Pass tickets. These are close to or right at a $100 bucks WOW. But get this, we had the two park pass, paid for the stupid train & they wanted another $400's + to get around faster right.  The Fast Pass was ONLY VALID AT ONE PARK, WHAT THE HELL.  A fast pass is a fast pass, why is it not valid in both parks, it's not as if we could be in two lines at once in both parks, this blew my mind.  NEVER EVER AGAIN.

If line ups are long, use the single rider line - very short - you won't ride together, but will save a ton of time lining up. On the Hogsmeade ride, make sure our pockets are secure as you go on your back - I almost lost my car keys.
