Have been there a few times and will be going back again The new rides were awesome and can't wait for new ones next year Harry Potter was great Fun for the whole family
Both parks are fantastic for all ages.Good fun. Get an express to skip the queues as its well worth it

The whole universal experience is amazing top to bottom, the rides, shows and atmosphere can't be matched even by other well known parks!  Honestly, if you're looking for a theme park you'll have more fun here than anywhere. Fun for all ages.  My only issue is that I couldn't fit on one ride so if you're a big guy that could be an issue.
I loved the transformers ride the best there. They need to get rid of the twister tho very fake and too old. Maybe if they did it as a 3D ride it would be better. Other than that it was great

I broke my own electric wheelchair while in the park. It took hours for them to understand that I wasn't going to just get up an walk away. They would not help fix the chair or provide me with transportation back to my on site Hotel. We never got to use our second day tickets.
Best experience! Get there early and you'll get great parking! So much fun for the whole family! Easy entry and re entry

Universal is great - what we didn't like is the deal where you have to buy a different ticket for each "side." And Harry Potter is divided across both. UNIVERSAL grounds and activities are great. But their marketing and pricing is terrible.

Picked a good time to visit as the crowds were not too large, weather was not too hot, and no storms. Kids were kept happy throughout as there was a good mix of character meet and greets and simulation rides to keep them entertained. Lots of places with air conditioning to rest and recuperate. I would highly recommend getting the meal plan.

Third trip to Universal first To Diagon Alley. I cannot say enough. We were in Orlando for 10 days and I did not expect to spend to most of it here. But we sure did. The second we walked into Diagon Alley it felt like another world. I had to stop and take it all in. I was not expecting it to be so big or detailed. Everywhere I looked there was something amazing to see and do. The interactive wand areas are fun. Specially the one in knockturn. And Knockturn itself was crazy. It was about 90 degrees out that day and Knockturn was a good 20 degrees cooler. Covered so when it rained it was neat place to hang out. I bought so much stuff it was embarrassing! We went back a lot at night because the area thins out before close and got some stunning photos. I wouldn't want to go back to the hotel give me a tent and I would of slept right there :) Also get some ice cream! The strawberry and peanut butter is like nothing Ive ever had before! Not Diagon Alley- Universal its self is my favorite side. I love the Mummy ride as well as Men in Black. We always have a blast on those. Simpsons itself is neat. I don't like the ride too much as it makes me a little sick But the detail in area is awesome. We had a good lunch and some nice drinks. I don't like the 1 beer rule. I get the reason but most places are 2 which would make it easy for a couple. Also if you go back to this area a little before close you can get some really neat photos. Transformers was a fun addition and I look forward to the Fast and Furious ride.
Great addition to the park. Spent most of a whole day in just that section. Of course, there are plenty of things to do at USF...but if you're a HP fan..you'll be a happy camper.
This is a great place to visit. Rides and attractions for the whole family to go together and as well as the big rides.

Of all the parks in Orlando, this is my favorite. This is the park with the most theme rides. Potter is very busy so it is best if you do it first thing. It's worth getting the unlimited Express pass even when the park is not busy. Not busy still mean that you will wait 10-20 min per attractions, which will take about 2-3 hours off you visit... Well worth it.
I went there for 2 days in a group of 4 one day and 6 the other day. We had a great time all the time. The place is clean and the has great rides for everyone in my party.
There's something for all ages here - some of the rides may close during thunder storms, could easily spend two days here.

Hi we visited the Harry Potter gringotts ride with one terrified 12 year old boy after lots of persuasion to no avail we we leaving the ride and spoke to Heather one of the park crew well she couldn't do enough to allay his fears so much so that he eventually went on the ride. Heather you're a fantastic person and a credit to the Universal team. Many thanks.

Universal Studios is a lot of fun. It is more geared towards older kids and adults. The shows I saw were great. We went in mid September and were able to walk right on most rides with zero to little wait, even the Harry Potter rides. We rode most rides 3 times. I like that they provide free lockers for rides where you can't take any bags with you. We brought our own water bottle and filled it up at the free style coke machines with cold water for free.

This is our fourth year to come to this attraction. My first suggestion is to buy the Express Pass. If not, I doubt you'll even get to see half the haunted houses as the lines are incredibly long. Another nice perk is that a few of the rides are open and there is almost no wait time because everyone else is waiting for the houses. Try to go to the most popular houses first. They are usually near the front of the park. The wait times for those will become unbearable as the night goes on. Is it scary? A little but none of the characters can touch you. The production value of the costumes and makeup is like none other. In addition to the rides and houses, there are a couple of shows to see. Try to do at least one as they give you time to sit down and rest. There's a lot of walking at this place. Universal does sell alcohol but minors beware- they are very diligent about underage drinkers. You'll be banned for a year if you get caught. Happy Haunting!

Visited the two parks four times during our two week stay. Queues were well handled and airconditioned. Staff were always so pleasant and the parks were spotless. Don't try to stay all day it's too tiring. Go for it opening one day to catch all the rides before it gets too busy. Next time go about 4pm. Crowds start dying down about 5ish so you can still get on rides without too much queuing and you get to see the fireworks at night. Buy the refillable cups. Saves so much money and if you bring them back the next time you visit they can be reactivated for even less money. Bargain. Also you can fill them up every ten minutes from one of the machines round the park. Water is free from these machines if you prefer to take your own bottle. All in all two wonderful parks with great shows and rides. Be prepared to have to use one of the drying machines if you go on the water rides though you do get soaked. Lol. The Mummy and the Hogwarts Express are a must.

Already did Disney so headed to Universal when we went back to Orlando this fall and saw on the tickets that we could purchase add-on tickets to Halloween Horror Nights. We had NO idea what it was like or what happens. This is the funnest event with nine haunted houses (names like Insidious, Great American Werewolf in London, Walking Dead, The Purge, etc.) and with scare events surrounding different areas. No costumes are allowed on visitors, so the only ones dressed up are Universal workers (which is nice so you know who is who!) They have really turned the park into a Halloween dream and it doesn't even look like the same place. All the rides are open too! But let me give you two very important tips: eat somewhere else before you go and arrive past opening time (lines are long long) and we were able to leisurely walk in. Second, BUY THE EXPRESS PASS for the evening. You can wait in lines for a long while, we bought one after our first house wait and it was worth every cent. Got to do everything we wanted to in just a few hours. The express pass is also good on the rides. (Remember, your express pass from earlier in the day is not valid at Halloween Horror nights, you have to purchase a separate one). They cut off the number of express passes they sell as well. Final tip, try not to go on a Saturday night if at all possible. We went on a Friday and the lines and crowds were much better.

Love, love, love this park. No matter what age you are there's something for everyone. From friendly and curtious staff, disabled friendly with easy access to rides and shops. Good variety of foods and drink, prices vary also do something for every pocket. The view from the bridge near MIB is worth a look in my view.
It's a nice place to go and have fun with the family, just you and your husband or wife. you can chose to stay in one of the onsite hotel or in one of the nearby hotels and enjoy your day.

Universal Studios is a sure bet for fun and entertainment for all ages. There are rides from easy to thrilling and stage and street shows. They even have a make up / horror show that's wonderful. The new Harry Potter additions are a sure hit as well and Gringotts is well worth the wait in line. Enjoy your day! !

This was my first trip to a Universal park in at least 15 years. Much has changed. I was very happy with the ride selection they have here now. More than I thought. The Harry Potter section is very well done. Make sure you stop here first thing in the morning to avoid long waits at Escape from Gringotts. Men in Black is outdated but still fun, especially if you have kids. Simpsons ride is alright but not worth a long wait. Transformers is exactly like Spiderman at Islands of Adventure, but not as good in my opinion. E.T. is a very old ride, but still enjoyable if the line is short. Twister has also been around for a long time, and if you have never seen it, then it's cool to check out. Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit does not really fit into the parks theme at all. It really feels out of place, but its a decent coaster. I wouldn't wait too long for this attraction. The best ride in the park by far is The Mummy. Great special fx and a great coaster. Definitely worth the wait.  If you want to visit this park, September is a great time to do it. Very light crowds. You could easily knock out the whole park in half a day and head to Islands of Adventure and do the same. Will be coming back in the near future for sure!

A big group of have just been here & we love the place. Something for all kids, big & small. So much to see & do. Kids had a awesome day. We'll be back again in a few days. Can't wait to go on the Jurassic Park ride.

We had too much fun here. We purchased the express passes to bypass the long lines...they are long. It's so much to do here even before you go to buy your tickets. I absolutely loved it here. Can't wait to go back. I am generally a thrill ride lover but the simulated rides are by far better....
Great park. Had fun with the family. Would definitely recommend the park. Of course it gets a little expensive staying a few days, but it is vacation.

My first time was last year. I was impressed with the costuming, the sets, and the effort put into the event. My visit this year was a bit different. I began to pay more attention to the themes and the methods of scare.  After going through nine horror houses, my total feel was that each house is basically the same scare. The individual theme, such as, the American Werewolf, has great costuming, but each scare is based on the surprise and suspense of not knowing when or what will jump into your face at any given moment.  That method got a lot of screams out of me, but after nine houses of it, I stopped screaming. Actually, I stopped long before that. I personally have not figured out how to do it better, but somebody needs to rethink a few things.  Also, we had a person in our group who required a wheel chair. She had an electric wheel chair rented but those were not allowed in the houses. Each house required that she transport to a manual wheelchair. At one house the manual chair was not available. She could not go in with our group. At another house we got the same answer until I complained that she paid her fee and was not given access to the house. They somehow "found" a wheelchair.  This is a very entertaining event, however, as with most things the minds that bring it together may need to tweak a few things.  Never go to this event without an express pass. You will wait in lines most of the evening if you do not have express pass.

We came in on october 5. In the web page they posted closing time 9.00 pm a month in advance, the day we came in the map said 8.00 pm and then the crew said it was actually 7.00 pm. Its horrible that they let you plan and spend in advance but change schedules while you are in the park. That is just a scam. This does noy happen at disney, really. And even more with the ridiculously expensive tickets.

First and foremost. The park is definetely worth the visit. The attractions and themes are well done. The employees are very friendly and happy to help. That being said, both universal studios and island of adventure could easily be considered one park. The only real distinction is the majoriety of rides in the studios are motion simulation. With a small mixing of actual rides throughout. The parks are traversed by the hogwarts express, which is in effect a ride. With a wait. Or by simply walking out either front gates and walking roughly 3 minutes to the other gate...  We did purchase both the park to park pass and the express pass. The express pass is well worth the extra $.  Ultimately i would advise people to visit both parks, however 2 days is plenty of time to see both. Additionally i found it somewhat aggrivating that the studios park closes at 5 pm to later re open for the 25 nights of horror. Which costs an additional fee starting at approx. 50 dollars , if you paid for the full day admission already....  In my opinion they should discount the full day passes, since in effect they are closing the park roughly 1/4 of the normal hours. And making an additional charge for the nightly visitors. ( kind of double dipping!) Of course they wont, but i am entitled to my opinion.

We spent our entire day at Universal Studios (the Studios side, not Islands of Adventures), once in the morning for a normal day at Universal, then back at night for Horror Nights. This review is solely for Halloween Horror Nights #25, at Universal Studios. First thing first:  One: Parking. We went with the Preferred parking, which was $8 more expensive than the regular, but it got us closer to the entrance than a normal pass would have. Less walking = Win win in my book. I'd definitely suggest getting it.  Two: Security. Not only does Universal have it's own security force working the gates of Halloween Horror Nights, it also uses officers from Orlando Police Department, which given the amount of alcohol present and the potential for rowdiness, it's definitely good to have! Upon entry, you are required to submit to a bag check (which is way more thorough than the normal day bag check), then a metal detector check. The officers and security are really friendly (which is a plus when passing through the checkpoint!)  Three: The Haunted Houses. Holy cow. Enough said... This is the fourth HHN event I have been to, and I can honestly say this one was my favorite. The Freddy vs. Jason house was EPIC! And keep the kiddies away from the Asylum in Wonderland 3D house, unless you want to twist and screw up Alice in Wonderland for them! Mwahahaha! xD There's a great selection of houses this year, but without an Express pass, good luck getting through them all, as the lines quickly back up. Within thirty minutes after the gates opened, lines were already over an hour long.  Four: The shows. Jack is back, baby! Jack the Clown (from HHN #10) is back with his lovely assistant Chance, to provide a horror gore-fest called "Carnage!". This show is standing room only, with plenty of viewpoints at Mel's Dinner. It was really entertaining, with horror, rock music, and FIRE! Then there's Bill and Ted's Excellent Halloween Adventure. I can't even describe this to you. It's funny as can be! Just go see it! You'll thank me later! The shows are well put together, and very entertaining!  Five: The rides. No wait times, period. Everyone is busy going into the Haunted Houses, so the lines are very small. Even the Transformers Ride was empty (it was literally myself, my girlfriend, and another couple on the ride, that's it!). The only ride that stays packed during HHN is the Rip Ride Rockit rollercoaster, so expect a wait there.  Six: The bars. If you're like me, you need to loosen up before getting the life scared out of you. Luckily, there is a metric ton of bars all throughout HHN. Some are small, only offering beer, but most are large temporary bars, stocked with hard drinks, including the signature HHN drink this year: the "Jack'd Up Carnage", which I had. All are staffed by knowledgeable and friendly bartenders, who can quickly recommend an awesome drink if you're not sure what you'd like.  Seven: Scare zones. If you don't like maniacs with chainsaws, stay outside the gate. That's your warning, son! On top of that, the Haunted Forest and the D I E - IN Theater is simply epic! And the only way you're getting to the other half of the park is through the zones! Good luck to ya!  Too long, didn't read? This year's Horror Nights is simply epic, with great houses, shows, scares, and staff. As I've said, this is my fourth event, and it's my favorite out of them all. Honestly, I'm thinking of booking another trip for this coming weekend! If you're a fan of getting the life scared out of you, then you can't do better than this! I hope you enjoy it! =)

Still the best theme park in Orlando. The rises are cutting edge the theming cannot be beaten. We did the cinematic spectacular show this year which included a meal at Lombard's which was great. Must visit park when in Orlando :)

The 25th anniversary of Halloween Horror Nights lived up to its expectations. It was a great experience. The scare zones were awesome, characters / make up, the haunted houses, shows, etc. It's also fun because you get to do some of the rides at night and if you want to beat the mile-long 50 minute wait for rides during the daytime, go at night and within 20 minutes, you'll be in. Great job to all!

So much to see! My family and I (myself, husband and teenage son) had a great time at Universal. We didn't necessarily start our day early but lines were still decent. I think I became addicted to the "beer" in The Wizarding World of Harry Potter. As a person that doesn't normally ride any coasters, I rode almost all of them. We had an awesome day and stayed basically til closing. We'll likely go back one day when we need our fix. I suggest getting the refillable containers (drinks/popcorn) to save money.

What a great park!!! The park is wonderful during the day and the Halloween Horror Night is amazing. I never could have imagined a more "thrill" seeking attraction. The horror houses are awesome and you still have access to most of the main rides and Harry Potter. The park closes at 5PM most nights during October (Wed-Sun) then reopens at 6:30 for the Halloween Night and stays open to 1AM or 2AM. My advice would be to try to purchase a Express Pass for both the park and the Horror Night. We stayed at the Hard Rock so we received a complimentary Express Pass for the day. If you want to do the Halloween Horror nights, my advice would be to purchase a Express Pass. If you do not purchase one, then you need to arrive to the park at 6:30 and you can probably make it through 3 or 4 houses only.
We went in the evening and we're in a cordoned off section for the group that include the Bob Marley bar. Definitely worth a visit if you're a Bob Marley fan.

My husband and I went. We loved the roller coaster and virtual rides. Staff were awesome. The guy who did the music coaster was friendly and told us about the park. We are bringing our kids back in December! LOVED IT! tickets are expensive and it will take a whole day.

Have been to Halloween Horror nights before and this recent trip was the best! Haunted house were scary and fun, lines moved fast (we had the fast pass), costumes were amazing, overall great trip! I will go back next year!

We don't do roller coasters so managed to do almost everything we wanted in one day. Check when park closes as it closed early for Horror nights and made us miss a few things. Longest line was for Minions. It was broke first thing in the morning and 45 min. wait later in the day. Harry Potter area was crowded but did the ride 3 times and tried the overpriced frozen butter beer. I was disappointed in the Hogwarts Express. it was more transportation then ride. Pay attention to the inner and outer windows to not miss anything.

I felt that this park is so much larger than the one in California. Also, there are differences. For example in California they have the Hollywood Tour (with Jaws and King Kong) in Orlando they don't. Also, the park in Orlando has two parks Universal and Island of Adventure (both are worth the visit). Bring your waling shoes and FYI go to the Minion Ride first. You don't really need the Express Passes to get on all the rides. There is actually a cool Universal App that tells you wait times. The app from Universal didn't work, but there was another one that did and it was accurate. Also, a lot of the rides are 3D. Some don't allow you to take things on with you such as a camera or other loose items, but they have free lockers available while you are on the ride. The Mummy was awesome. I feel this park is great for kids 10+, but there are some for the little ones. ET was fun, but my kids didn't really know who he was. The Dr. Seuss land is great for the younger ones. Harry Potter was fun, but you can't enjoy it fully unless you have a park hopper pass. Go during off season. Also, make sure you grab a park map and know what time the park closes.

We'd been wanting to try this for years and finally went for it. Glad we did, as it was a lot of fun.  We read up on how to avoid the crowds, as it gets incredibly crowded. (Getting in early was the trick for us.) If you don't have a game plan, you won't see many haunted houses, as the lines pretty quickly get to 60+ minutes. If money isn't a concern, get an express pass and you won't have to worry too much about the lines.  While the haunted houses were pretty cool, they weren't all that scary. They would have been much scarier, if we didn't have people directly in front and behind us. Remember, the saying "safety in numbers"... Universal could improve this by pacing the people entering the haunted house.  It would help for Universal to post ratings of the various haunted houses like other attractions I've been to do, and have at least one "It's Scary as Hell" haunted house.  We actually really enjoyed just walking the streets and going thru the various "scare zones". These were almost as scary as the haunted houses.  Of the two shows they had this year, Bill & Ted's was definitely our favorite (more so than the Carnage show).  Between the haunted houses, scare zones, and shows it was a really good time and worth the money.
Epcot is amazing with some great rides, but all the countries around the world showcase are really good. Fun for all ages.

They can really do theme parks here. The set up catered for everyone. Loved the valet parking no queues and no finding your car afterwards. We really needed the two days to experience it all. We would have missed so much if we didn't. Harry Potter world was exceptional. The ride on the Hogwarts Express is a must. This really is fun for all the family with so much you just would not think possible. Big thumbs up from us.
First time to HHN25 and will definitley be back. Such an amazing time. FYI eat at Finnegan's Bar and Grill before HHN starts, you'll get a head start on the houses.

This is our 2nd visit to Halloween Horror Nights and yet again it was amazing. This year is their 25th anniversary of spooktacular fun. If you have a teenager or even a tween that loves scary movies this place is a must see. We purchased the Express Pass which is a bit pricy but necessary if you want to see and ride everything. However, we were disappointed with a couple of the rides concerning the express pass. The Rip Ride Rocket and Harry Potter-Escape From Gringotts didn't treat express customers fairly. We were invited into the express line to enter (on the rip ride rocket)then disappointingly led into the general admission line, (escape from Gringotts) didn't even have an express line at all. The wait was over 45 minutes to ride each of these. That wouldn't normally be an issue, but when you pay nearly $115 per person (for express pass and lanyard) you expect an honorable company like Universal Studios to honor your purchase. It felt like a bit of a bait and switch, and that never feels good. Needless to say we didn't get to ride either of these and it definitely put a damper on the evening. Had Universal Studios stood behind the HHN Express Pass we would have seen every haunt and ridden every ride in 7 hours (they closed at 2am). I would've rated this event excellent had these issues not have happened.

There was a lot to see but not a lot to do. It was a good break from running around all day I did the whole park in half a day. A good thing I had gotten coupons for the entrance free because I first whent to see timesharing condos so if you go listen to them for thirty min you can get into parks for free !!!

My kids were so very excited to come and see the world of Harry Potter. It did not disappoint - looks exactly like the book/movie. IMO the best roller coaster in the park is at Hogsmead entrance - there are 2 red/blue. They are awesome. Also the castle ride is really an interesting experience. The one downside of Universal is that they use what feels like 75% of the real estate on upselling opportunities. Paid games not included in your ticket price, food, concessions, stores selling merchandise of any and all kinds. I have never seen a park with such a high % of their grounds focused this way. It felt a bit opportunistic. If you compare this to say a Disney or Magic Mountain or even a Knotts Berry farm - the amount of rides falling into the thrill/adult/teen is very very low. Many of the offerings are displays when you get down to it...atlantis looked like it was gong to be this amazing thing and then you went in and it was just a mini 1 man, cheesy play to anyone who was under the age of about 8 years old. Twister, same thing but at least there was interesting history and documentary on twisters while you waited. The Spider Man ride is a 3D simulation and was Excellent.
Our family, including three teenagers, had a blast during our time at Universal! There was so much to do, employees were beyond friendly, and the grounds are well kept and safe.

great day out with the family... I do think it's a bit unfair to charge for parking on top of a very expensive ticket into the park, however once in you forget and just enjoy the day... Harry Potter is amazing and well worth the visit alone. I do wish they had more variety of food to have instead of just burgers, especially for the kids

Spent a day and a half at universal. Great friendly atmosphere with good fun rides and simulators. Harry Potter world was fab. This was the first park that we found decent good food to eat (we ate at Lombards Seafood Grill). Great value for money and the city walk was buzzing.

This is my second time going to the Halloween Horror Nights. One of the highlights was An American WereWolf in London & 25 Years of Monsters & Mayhem.  Bill & Ted seems to be too P.C.  Asylum 3D in Wonderland was good.

If you are a Harry Potter fan the trip is a must, just to see Hogsmeade and Diagon Alley. They have done a brilliant job of bringing the settings to life and the the rides are not to be missed. We came for HHN 25, and it did not disappoint. We went through all nine haunted houses, all the scare zones, and saw everything but the Bill & Ted show. We will definitely return again, it was a great time.

First things first, the park is just amazing. You will be blown away with all the rides, the fun shows and the magic you feel by visiting this park.  Make sure to check out the opening times of your day of visit, as the change depening on the season and the day of the week.  I personally felt a bit dissapointed coming back to Universal after being there 3 times in the past. Mainly because of the prices. Entree free is over 100usd, parking is 20usd, having a picture taken with one of the characters (sold at 29usd)... avg burger price range is 12-15usd.  That would be all not so bad, but the rides have not changed much over the years. Out of Back to the Future became the Simpons Ride. Out of the Jetsons became Minions... and so on.  Also, if you want to explore the full Harry Potter rides, you need access to both Universal parks, which is barely impossible doing all in 1 day... so you would need a 2 day, 2 park access pass.

This was my first time visiting Universal Studios Orlando. It was a trip for my son, who is a hardcore Harry Potter fan just like me. Oh boy! It was great! Not only did the Wizarding World of Harry Potter was beyond amazing, the whole trip was awesome. We had so much fun and pretty much rode almost every ride at both parks. We went during Spring Break and it was great timing because the parks were not that packed. I guess most people go to the beach instead. We hardly waited at the rides, except for the minions and the transformers rides. Those two had really long waits. We weren't able to ride the Jurassic Park ride, it was going through maintenance and updates since the Jurassic World movie was coming out later. We're definitely going back next year, I can't wait!

I've been to Universal Studios many times. Every time that I go is better than the last time. I find the rides to be much more fun and exciting than they are at Disney. It's also less expensive. Since it's much smaller than Disney, it's easier to get around with kids, or people with disabilities.  The staff members are so much fun. They aren't required to be overly polite like they are at Disney, so they poke fun at guests and at their competitor. They crack me up!  The parks are meticulously clean and safe. The restaurants at City Walk are great and cater to all tastes. Dueling pianos at night at Pat O'Brien's should not be missed! So much fun.  There's so much to do, including shows. Blue Man Group is my favorite. Have fun!

We loved coming here for a visit this Fall. All the rides were so fun but the best part was the Harry Potter section. It was amazing. Every detail was perfect. Definitely eat at all the HP restaurants and get to Ollivander's first thing in the day so you can use your wand. Try the Butter Beer ice cream. We were able to meet so many characters around the park without even waiting in long lines (like Disney). Stay on-site so you can get in early and skip all the lines. Well worth it. We will be back!

Universal Studios Orlando was so much fun! Easy to get in and the Expess Pass was great as we never waited any longer than 30 minutes for any ride and those rides were The Simpsons and Shrek. The Simpsons was the most surprising ride to us; my sister got a tad woozy, the only experience that created such uneasiness. Plenty of food options digging the turkey legs, churros etc. We loved the following five experiences: The Minions, The Mummy, Rip Ride Rocket, Transformers and Harry Potter. So much fun and well designed as it was easy walking and orderly picking your route. The Makeup Show was fun and gave you a break.  Such a great day. Enjoy Universal Studios Orlando!

October. School in the US is in session, its not spring break, its not a major holiday, or summer vacation. Theme parks should be wide open, right? Nope. None the less, Universal, despite the lines, is a blast. Rides are great. The Halloween horror nights special event is outstanding. Wear your walking shoes, go ahead and pony up for the speed pass, it will be worth it. Particularly check out the Harry Potter world exhibits(one on each side of the park.) For food, got to Mythos in Islands of Adventure. There is a reason its been voted best theme park food last 6 years in a row. The grilled salmon I had (yes, in a theme park!) would not have been out of place in the fine dining establishment of your choice. For drinks, go to the Leaky Cauldron in the Diagon Alley area of Universal. Think 300 year old English pub, cold pints, and pub grub.

Universal just blew me away. It was just jaw dropping. The queue times were so so but we managed to do a lot seeing as we got there at mid day. The theming was amazing. Can't pick a favorite ride as they are all fantastic. Twister didn't really do it for me but glad of the experience. The mummy and transformers were just incredible and ended up going on the mummy twice. Met Scooby doo and shaggy, sponge Bob and Betty boop. Was a wonderful day.

Instead of going to disney this year, we decided to take the kids here for vacation. We would definitely stay at one of the three onsite propertys again (see my review on Loews Resort) because you receive hour early entry to harry potter worlds and express passes on certain rides.  We went during 4th of July week (I know crazy, right?) and here is how we did it and managed to ride everything and relax with no stress with four kids (16, 15, 12, 11):  * Two days at both parks is enough time to do everything worth doing unless you get the 3rd one free with stay then by all means take advantage of that.  * Don't stay up late and get in early. Go to forbidden journey first, hope on train to go to other park, and go on escape gringotts. You are going to be tempted to ride other rides and look at shops- Don't!!! Do these first and then explore. Trust me lines get crazy once regular customers get in the gates.  * Around Noon, ride all 3 water rides and since you are in wet clothes then its time to head back to hotel for a dip in the pool and order poolside food for Lunch. This will avoid chaffing of the legs, lol, feed your hunger while avoiding the crazy lunch venues in the park, and cooling off in the hot sun, and still entertaining the kids.  * After pool, take a nap, video gaming, or quiet time before heading back to park. You will be going with less people in park who are exhausted from sun in afternoon and plus it will be cooler to stand in lines.  * Bring your smart phone or camera because there are many cool photos to take in the parks.  * Soon as you come threw Universal gate, buy from the store on right, a card holder that goes around neck that you can put your express passes. No need to pull out of your pocket or lose them. They just scan them for you right in line around your neck.  * Our favorite rides worth the wait times: Both Harry potters (rode several times), hogwarts express train (going to both parks gives you two different story lines),dragon challenge (you will be dizzy when you come off of these roller coasters), revenge of the mummy (our favorite and we rode it several times), hollywood rip ride rocket (the 12, 11 refused to ride- sometimes the single rider line was shorter), men in black (towards end - they will say k hit the button - if you do it - you will get a ton of points), the simpson ride (rode 3 times), transformers (rode 2 times).  * Rides that we worth wasting some time on: ET (it will say your name- we knew this going in- so we gave attendant fake ones which made it funnier), kang and kodos, spiderman, and all three water rides.  * Rides with long waits and not worth riding at all: Poseidons Fury (we never even went inside- not a ride even- we used express pass and still was waiting an hour- we got out of line so can't even tell you what the walk through was like), shrek (out of date 4d theater), hulk (it was the worst rough roller coaster any of us have rode), and despicable me (seating is terrible to get full experience - you will enjoy better watching it on youtube). Amazing how long lines were for these rides and wish someone would have given us a heads up like I am doing now for you.  * In harry potter world, there is the huge dragon on the building. You will hear a "big grumble" and that will be your cue to get your cameras ready cause in the next moment, it will shoot a huge ball of fire from its mouth and makes an awesome photo.  * keepsake idea- at the wizard world you can exchange cash for harry potter cash in which you can spend at any of the shops (we kept ours).  * The kids wanted wands to make things happen inside city however as busy as it was- it really wasnt really worth it. Too many kids pointing them at all the spots or creating a crowd around place to make them happen. It was frustrating. They bought a keepsake I guess that they really didn't get to use.  * If you have a sweet tooth then try the butterbeer frozen. Brain freeze.  * Outside of Harry potter world before going around the wall and near the purple bus, check out one of the apartment buildings and you will see one of the goblins peaking back and forth of the window. Very creepy and picture opportunity.  * Other photo opts, is in the comic section of IOA. We had a blast standing under them working our model poses. ;-)  * They were currently building the King Kong part so someone please let me know how it was once it is finished and you have rode it. Thanks  Enjoy and Happy Vacation!

We went to Universal for the day while passing thru Orlando, we had a great time. We arrived at 8am when they opened and the lines were very short, we were able to get in a few rides before the lines got too long. Transformers was by far my favorite ride all day.

I was SO impressed by the Wizarding World of Harry Potter - truly impressed with the quality of the rides and the entire experience. I highly recommend the interactive wands as they really do make the experience COME TO LIFE.  It's only 3 stars because we had an unfortunate issue with ticket services. We were allowed to go in an hour early as part of our hotel package but they couldn't find our tickets, so I spent the advance hour at ticket services where it took them 45 minutes to address the problem (mostly because they had a completely unprepared young woman trying to solve a problem she had no strategies to solve)... thus eradicating the 1-hour advance entry privilege. They did apologize and give me the express tickets which allows you to avoid the lines in almost all the better rides (after I pitched a small fit). The express tickets are expensive, but it's worth it if you plan to do a lot of rides as the lines are really long.  Also, if you go in the dead of summer, I recommend an early start, a midday siesta and an early evening return after an early dinner. Temperatures are cooler, lines are shorter.
we had a very good day out here!! So much to see and do!! We really enjoyed the Harry Potter Ride and Men In Black and the queue was not bad at all!!

We went to Universal Studios Florida with another couple and friend. Both of us couples have children under 5. The kids zone was really amazing for the kids (Curious George and Fievel areas allow the kids to run around and have a good time. In the Curious George area the kids can actually wear bathing suits and slash around. The animal show was really neat as well. The rest of the park is really designed for kids that are slightly older (5 and up I would say and actually a little older too). I did get to ride the Rip Ride Rockit which was pretty amazing and unique (you can actually pick your own song to listen to when you ride). The parades are a little underwhelming, but again the park isn't really designed for the young crowd. Plenty of food opportunities in the park (may I suggest Bumbleman's Taco Truck). Overall good time and will definitely go back in the future.

Not a HP fan but the area is fantastic. Great themeing and visuals. The dragon is amazing and the shops equally so. Gringotts ride very good, a new concept in theme park rides. The rest of the park just doesn't do it for me. Transformers rides is essentially the same as Spider Man in IoA and Minions/Simpsons is also essentially the same - a simulator ride. Rip Ride Rock It is a great concept but the ride really shook me up and hurt my neck and head and I am a thrill junkie. Did not go on it again.

Lines weren't too long except in Harry Potter. Easy to move between parks. And with the city walk right there can always go out and get something different. Prices at concessions little more reasonable than Disney!
I enjoyed very much the park, I went to Harry Poter word by train it was amazing., I became a Miniom I loved it all so much.

Had the two park pass for here and islands of adventure and the studios side was definetly my favourite . Loads of good rides and attractions . The blues brothers show was also good fun . We didn't manage to do every ride due to lack of time which was mainly caused by the Halloween nights that were on . you had to buy a separate ticket for those .. Spider-Man ride was very good . Il be back soon .
love the rides, express pass is worth it always. it's expensive as hell for everything but thats a no-brainer because its a theme park

It was a very nice park with the best simulators! The problem is that you must pay to put your sutff in lockers for some attractions and I don't felt secure by doing this (due one locker have opened for me and it already contain someone stuff. I close it fast when I saw what happened and it was scary!).

This is the second time I've gone to the Halloween event at Universal. The first time I took my granddaughter. It is much better without the kids! I bought frequent fear tickets and went for two nights. I visited every haunted house, all but 1 ride, and 1 show. It is great! If you like Halloween you will love the Halloween Horror Nights at Universal.
This is the milder of the 2 parks here!! It has rides for all ages and the food is very good!! For a park with more thrill rides then go to their other park "Islands of Adventure"!!

We went with my 8 year old and spent a decent amount of money to get in. Did not get the fast pass and regret that we did not. We played hurry up and wait ALL DAY! For food and rides. The waiting in lines was enough to ruin your day. I will go back but will save up money and buy the fast pass for sure!!
it was a neat ride, but compared to everything else there, its time to replace this ride with something not 20+ years old

Our family are HP fans and spent most of our day between the two worlds. You have to have a park to park ticket to be able to access the train that take you between Hogsmeade and Diagon Alley. There are more rides in Hogsmeade. Lots of people go dressed in HP attire which makes it lots more fun. You will feel as though you are in the book or the movie. If HP is your focus do it all first and then hit the other attractions. You can dine at Three Broomsticks or the Leeky Cauldron. Try the frozen butter beer. It is awesome!! Line ups this time weren't too bad (20-30 minutes). I have also been when they are 75 minutes for Gringott's. Other attractions: The Hulk Roller Coaster is closed now for repair. Dr Seuss Land is good for little kids.

Well worth the cost of admission to be scared silly! Considering most haunted houses these days are $10 and up, the $58 for high caliber frights, sights, and scares was well worth it as only Universal studios can muster! I will be back for more tricks and treats next year!

Universal is well worth a visit. We were only in Orlando for 3 days of a Florida and Bahamas holiday and so we had to pick and choose what to do. We decided that the theme park we would do would be Universal as it seemed more geared to all ages and not just kids. It was our 23rd wedding anniversary on the Saturday so we decided that would be the day we went. It worked out really well as if you get the day ticket you get Mardi Gras in the evening as well. You don't have to stay all day and into the evening if you don't want to. We were really tired by late afternoon and so we went back to our hotel for a rest and a shower- then came back in the evening-just keep hold of your ticket to get back in. In the day we went on a few rides including The Mummy,Simpsons, ET which were all good. Fear factor show was good also. Best thing was The Harry Potter bit-walking in Diagon Alley and having a Butter Beer was brilliant. So funny seeing kids and adults alike loving it. The dragon on top of Gringotts bank belches fire every few minutes(can't remember exactly how often) and it's great when you manage to get that perfect picture or mini movie of it. Loved every minute of it-we were just like a pair of big kids. As i said we came back in the evening for Mardi Gras and live concert. The Mardi Gras was great - you get obsessed with trying to catch as many bead necklaces as possible which they throw into the crowd from each float. After the floats have finished head over to the concert. We were really lucky as Kelly Clarkson was the artist on that night-she was really good and it was such a lovely friendly atmosphere. You can check the website for listings of who's playing-they do have some really good artists. The Saturday before we went it was Jessie J. After the gig we went for a few drinks-expensive but you expect it in theme park. Would definitely recommend going on any day-but Saturday especially.

We took our family, including our 9 year old grandson, to Universal Studios. He loved the Harry Potter village. However there was not much in the park for adults unless you like the very high roller coasters.Almost everything seemed to be geared to children. Also, there was very little seating around the rides so if you were waiting for someone to get off from the ride, it was hard to find a place to sit. Having been to Universal Studios in California years ago and we loved it, we were very disappointed in Universal Studios in Orland.

It is a good place to go, to get an entertainment and great fun. To feel an earthquake, to see 3+D movies, etc. The whole day You can easily spend here. And.. perhaps, would have the wish to return! "Back to the Future" or somewhere else.

1. Most rides were designed to shake you in order to make you excited, which made them very similar to each other.......  2. Simpson's ride was extremely boring. AVOID IT!  3. MIB and ET were good.  4. Harry Potter park was the highlight. But overall the ticket wasn't worth it. Go to Disney

This was our first visit to Universals parks. Rides times were signifigantly less than Disneyland's due to the ride sizing. Prices on souviners are absolutely outrageous and fr more expensive than Disney, this is not only gouging the consumer, but quite classless. Rides were all working, Simpsons ride has the longest wait. Rides here are more motion simulation 3D style, then the Disney style, both are good, just different. Not enough proper shopping if that is your think, lots of junk. Overall nice park with some different rides to excite. Most rides are fast moving, so if this bothers you, this isn't the park for you

The tickets for the Universal parks are pricey but both are worth visiting. They cater for all ages really, not just the young . Plenty of adrenaline fuelled rides but more gentler fare too. Plenty of shops and themed areas to look round too. Food expensive so take note
would not recommend this attraction 2 roller coastesr and a train the rest is shops and restaurants. vey expensive to get in 312.00 for 2 adults.
This was yet another INCREDIBLE Halloween Horror Night put on by Universal, already looking forward to next years

this park was fun for the thrill seekers and the young ones. it had lots of shows and rides. the 3D rides were the best and the food was fairly good. the park has 2 parts one has lots of thrill rides (island adventures part) so check the height requirements before planning to go. holloween is not a good time for little ones because universal really does it up in a scary way.
This isn't a cheap day, and is even more expensive with queue jump, but it is absolutely worth it. It's a great family day out.

We went to the Halloween Horror Night and it did not disappoint. The shows and haunted houses were very well done and very scary. If you are in Orlando at the right time of year put this on your "things to do" list
From the Minions to Harry Potter...it was AMAZING!! Highly recommend staying at the Cabana Bay Beach Resort - very affordable and great for kids or couples.

They did an amazing work to transform the park into a spooky, creepy landscape. Haunted houses were good but the whole park was extremely overcrowded and fast pass tickets were three times the money we spent for the base tickets-on top! If you want to go there, be early. We have been there 15 minutes after official park opening and already had to stand in line for half an hour. Overall we had a lot of fun but just managed to do two houses due to the long wait times.

Myself and three other family members went to a Halloween Horror night on a Sunday in October. The theme park was decorated brilliantly, it was very realistic and very scary. I have to be honest though that I was very disappointed that we only got to do one of the haunted houses as all of them were at least a 2 hour wait. It was so busy. We looked into doing fast track but it's $100 per person on top of the $100 for the theme park ticket, it's a very expensive option!! I also witnessed children as young as 5 coming out of the haunted houses with their parents, crying in sheer terror. Leaflets state recommended ages for this event is minimum 13. It is ultimately the parents responsibility but I feel their should be a no kids allowed policy for the haunted houses. All in all Universal is one of my favourite theme parks and I would go back to Halloween Horror but probably with the view of not getting the full experience.

We decided to take our kids to Disney World Orlando at an age where they would remember it (ages 10 and 11). We missed the magical period people! Kids were not interested in Disney - bored with the baby rides - and 80 minute lines. We popped over to Universal Studios! What a breath of fresh air! We LOVED Universal Studios. The rides were more suited to tween kiddos and adults. It was somewhat of a rainy day (which I highly recommend going on rainy days) as it scared all the crowds away. We didn't have to wait in line more than 30 seconds, and got right back on the rides again. The new Harry Potter ride was amazing - even for 45 yr old parents. We rode it so much, the 3d effects were great, we almost barfed! Yes peeps, IT - WAS - AWESOME! If your looking to get away from the crowds of Disney world, and more grown up rides, I would most definitely recommend Universal Studios in FL!

So we are glad we went, we did feel like we got to sink into "real" Harry Potter world and had a great time sharing that with each other and our photos are life long keepers.  BUT with the exception of some great employees, what a horrid place. Nothing interested us except HP World. It cost so much money to do both parks, but we finally bite the bullet and decided to ignore that money has value. The parks themselves were brutal on us, no places to sit and except the Hogwarts express, no real transportation between attractions.  Also, technically things were brilliant except the sound quality was so bad EVERYWHERE that we could never really follow what was going on. They might as well not have had plots. And they know where your head is going to be down to the inch on those rides, but we still couldn't understand any but about one out of 10 words.  But bottom line, it all worked just well enough to bring delight to me and my 80 year old potter-head Mom. (Mom is not a roller coaster fan. She did both rides, loved Gringotts but thought Hogwarts was a little much but was glad she did it anyway. The lack of seating around the park was really punishing on her though.)

Universal Studios and Universal Islands of Adventure is a must if you visit Orlando anytime of the year. This review is for the Universal Studios though !!  We were a group of 4, all in late 20's and we purchased a 2 day park to park ticket, which I think is sufficient to cover both the parks. If you have kids / elderly people, maybe you'll have to rush if you take 2 day ticket. Take express pass if you want to jump to the front of line (It costs roughly $70 per person). We skipped small rides and kids section to cover famous rides of both the parks.  Despicable Me Minion Mayhem, Revenge of the Mummy, Harry Potters ride, Shrek 4D show, The Simpsons ride, Transformers 3D ride, Rockit ride are must. These are the best rides / shows in this park. MEN IN BLACK Alien Attack is an interactive ride. If you have a park to park pass, you must take the Hogwarts Express train that connects Universal Studios to the Universal Island of Adventures.  There are wait times for most of the famous rides. Over the weekends, the wait times will be even more. So, carry ample liquids to keep yourself hydrated and wear comfortable clothes. Be sure to check the weather. Rain ponchos and umbrellas are available for sale inside the park. If it rains, some of the rides like Rock It may be closed. I suggest not to carry big cameras and big bags as it may make you slow throughout the park. Some rides don't allow you to carry bags or loose articles on you, but there are some places where you can rent lockers free for an hour to store your bags.  Small amounts of food is allowed inside the parks. So, take your favorite food to avoid spending time in lines to buy food inside the park.

Universal Studios is a great attraction! There are many rides to chose from & things to do!  Harry Potter World is a must & I advise getting there early as they can sometimes block the "world" off and it can get busy.

Loved Universal. Spent 4 days there last week and it was really good fun, for all ages. The rides are very cool, so incredibly well done....we particularly loved he Harry Potter area. The kids loved buying their wands in Ollivanders! The Mummy ride was amazing as was the Gringotts ride. They actually were all really good. I'm still struggling to come to terms with the cost of food in these parks. IT's absolutely insane. My recommendation is bring your own. Go to a supermarkets gets some breadrolls with ham and cheese and bring them with you to keep you going. An alternative is to come out of the park at lunchtime and head to some of the cheaper eateries in the City Walk area.... we had some really good filling food from Panda Express and we simply walked back in when we were done! We also didn't bother to carry bottles of water around with us either as there are free water fountains everywhere there are toilets!! Some great souvenir shops throughout - with a really big one on the way out. Enjoy!

We had a wonderful time at Universal Studios, we got there when the park opened and it made it so much better. You can get on the rides with as little as a 10 minute wait. We were able to go on 5 within an hour. The Transformers ride is excellent, we went on this ride two different days. The best pass is to get the 2 day 2 park that you can go between both parks on the same day. If you are planning on going on the water rides best to save till the end of the day really get wet. We also saw the Blue Man Group definitely a must, most enjoyable.

My absolute best ride was found in this park. The transformers 3d ride. Oh my hat it was incredible. There is so much to see and do. An explosion of senses. Enjoyed the single rider option as it allowed us to skip many of the long queques, so if you don't have to ride together, I suggest going this route where you can. So many great photo opportunities. Food as always in the park is costly so if possible try and get a big breakfast in or take some snacks with you.

For anyone who loves movies, this is the place to go. This was our second trip because we're huge Harry otter fans, so Universal is now doubly wonderful with the Wizarding World and Hogsmead areas. Do not miss the Hogwarts express! It's different in both directions, so plan for it. The new Minions ride is also excellent.
This attraction is a movie theme park ride adventure! The rides are based off universal films! Nice!

We purchased 2 of these thinking it would be a good idea. We we wrong. We were lead to believe we had to use them on the day or loose the unused allowance. Having been told the parks opened till 6 & 8pm we thought would get our snack & drink towards the end of our evening...6.30-7.30pm. they failed to inform us that the stalls and most of the shops close by 6pm in Adventure.....we had to walk almost to the exit to find a place open! We made our complaint only to then be informed that we did not have to use ALL the deal up on the day, and could used in City Walk which was open later! We explained that we had asked several staff in both parks and they too believed we had to used it or loose it.

Great park for kids older than 7. Most rides are 4D video. Not many characters about. Get the express pass, otherwise you will just stand in queues all day. Restaurants were much better than at Disney.

We loved it! Plenty of shows and rides here. The Horror Makeup Show should be on your list. We also really liked the Terminator show, the Minions, the Mummy, and the Rip Ride Rockit. The Incredible Hulk ride was down while we were there, want to ride it next time. Highly recommended.

Be sure to get a pass for both parks with the Express Pass. Also, the 1 day Quick Service Meal Plan was a good deal. Lots it do. Harry Potter Area is crazy! We didn't know a thing about Harry Potter and Minions, but Harry Potter fans are a little different...

So I just realised I got my review mixed up with Island of Adventures lol, any who they are both amazing. Transformers was wicked, Halloween Horror Nights was crazy scary. Always have to visit this park everytime we come here.
The best theme park ever, so so much fun, rides excellent, Universal I can't wait to see you again!!

I enjoyed this park better than IOA, mostly for its themed sections though, not rides. Most of the rides are 3d/ 4d, motion simulated ones which dont work well for people prone to motion sickness. That's me. But the shows especially the Straight Outta Food Truck show, were fantastic! Ride times were short and the park is easy to navigate. Oh, and do the Dining Plan!! It was a great savings for my family of four and there are lots of options!

Awesome memories made here, I love all the rides and I love the fact that you have so many different things in the park. Different rides from all kind of movies, I love Universal a lot. I am still waiting for Universal to make new rides lol

We went to Universal Studio Labor Day week. My family and I had a wonderful time. The rides were unbelievable. The attractions especially Harry Potter action. I thought I was really in England. Universal studio was a perfect theme park for the entire family

We had a great day in the park, and have visited this and many other parks in the area over many years. The different areas are well designed and it is great fun exploring. Unfortunately we witnessed a few issues with people behaving badly and with no respect for other guests and families. Security sorted them on each occasion, but we have never witnessed this anywhere else.

We visited universal and adventure Island with our two kids and friends. It far exceeded our expectations and in my opinion was better than Disney. There were plenty of rides that our youngest who is 6 could ride but also enough to keep our 11 year old interested. The lines were very manageable. Harry Potter is outstanding at both parks. The mummy was another favorite. Shrek was our least favorite attraction. Rip ride was also very fun. The train both directions between the parks is also really great.

My granddaughter had a 10th b-day and since Universal had Florida residence special, we took the trip, my own kids are in their 30's and its been a while since I visited any theme park in Orlando, but it was everything I remembered, it is the off season (after Halloween horror before x-mas), it was crowded by the lines weren't that long, my granddaughter had on a b-day button so everyone told her "Happy B-day Shaniya" paid the extra $5 for preferred parking was definitely worth it, purchased a two day pass and I think it was a trip my granddaughter will never forget

Universal Studios is the modern version of an amusement park. More rides and adventure than Disney World. Also has better restaurants and most do not require park admission. Downside is lack of comparable resort hotels and few convenient off sight hotels and motels in walking distance. Which theme park is better? Chocolate or Vanillla?

BASICALLY: It is mostly theming and simulator rides, but they are amazing simulator rides. And the theming is really fun, especially for the Harry Potter fans out there. I was content to sit in Diagon Alley and people watch and just absorb the atmosphere.  MUST DO RIDES/SHOWS: Gringotts, Simpsons, Mummy, Minions, Animal Actors, and Tales of Beedle the Bard in Diagon Alley. Do yourself a favor and ride Rip-Ride-Rockit, it's extreme for Orlando, however as a seasoned Cedar Point-er, no big deal, but it is fast and fun! Oh, and get a wand, its fun for everyone.  DAY by DAY: We had 4-day park to park tickets, in the first week of November, I suppose you could do 3, but definitely opt for the park to park tickets (only way you can ride Hogwarts Express). Day 1 was spent in ONLY Diagon Alley and Hogsmeade. Day 2 we spent exploring Universal Studios. Day 3 at Islands of Adventure (getting wet on water rides), and Day 4 was revisiting our favorites.  LOCKERS: Most of these are free for the length of time it will take you to wait and ride the ride nearby. HOWEVER, if you go over the time limit, you will need some form of payment to retrieve your items. We had to beg someone to spot us a few dollars to get our items out.  FOOD: We ate near the Simpsons area and the food was decent, but expensive inside the cafeteria. Two of us got tacos from the taco wagon (which are less costly--and delish!) and took them into the indoor eating area. Get yourself the big pink at Simpsons, they're fun. There is a pastry place that was pretty good near the entrance. We also ate at the Leaky Cauldron, which was good and had different food options--all of them were good (breakfast items were OK). Get butterbeer frozen or hot, we all preferred them to regular.  BAD STUFF: 1- Day 4 there were a LOT of issues with the rides breaking down--in both parks. 2- Twister is a waste of time if the line is more than 5 minutes (it's a show, really, you watch a 5-minute animatronic tornado while standing up).  BEWARE: The splash zone for the end of the night light/fireworks show, we got SOAKED, and from all angles--no umbrella could have saved us! It was hot enough outside it didn't matter, but it makes for a COOL ride back to the hotel on a freezing-standing-room-only shuttle.
I have been before but the Harry Potter section was new, could have spent all day in there. Fire breathing dragon too!

Car parking is expensive . $20 for general parking or $25 for preferred parking. I think the preferred parking to closer to the park. It took about 5 mins to walk to the park for general parking. We did Universal Studio first. The park was amazing and the atmosphere electric. We went on all the rides. Most of them were simulator rides. The mummy ride was great. It was a rollercoaster, but not too extreme. The Simpsons and The MInions ride were the best. Also the Transformer ride was brilliant. The only ride that we weren't impressed with was The Terminator. They kept you in a room which was quite crammed and warm for about 20 mins, as a woman talks to you and then you watch a short film. You are then led into another room where you sit and watch a show. I wasn't very impressed. There were lots of eating places and we ate in the American Diner which was good. A disappointment that the little jukeboxes on the tables never worked. We went in November so the park wasn't very busy and the rides were only half and hour wait. We found that when we went back in an afternoon the ride times were a lot shorter. Some of the rides you only waited 5 mins. So we only went back in the afternoons. With the parking, if you decide to leave the park and go back later in the day, you don't have to pay again. If you buy bottled water in the park, you can use the filling stations around the park to refill your bottle which saves you money. Some of the rides you have to put your bags in lockers. The first 50 mins are free,after that it's $5. It took us about 7 hours to get round the park. Be prepared to walk loads !!

The park was kept CLEAN !!!!! Use your AAA for discounts in the park. The freestyle drink refill stations are a little hard to find, but you don't need a "Universal" drink cup for water. All of the employees know how to make you feel welcome and are extremely friendly.

While we went mostly for me to check out DIagon Alley, the newest addition to The Wizarding World of Harry Potter, the park is fun to have as part of the two park pass. I wouldn't recommend only doing one park. While one of the reasons to do so is so you can take the Hogwarts Express between the parks (which is handy even if you're not into Harry Potter), there isn't quite enough in either park to really occupy. Universal is relying too heavily on the 3D rides. They're an interesting experience, but they aren't as fun as traditional rides. My husband and I weren't fond of them as the disconnect between what you're seeing and what you're feeling caused some discontent, but as motorcycle riders, we may be more sensitive to it.  The Rip Ride Rock-it was a blast of a roller coaster. Definitely don't pass it up if you like thrill rides. It starts with a vertical climb and then you drop down the other side going 60+ mph. It was so much fun.  Diagon Alley was so immersive, it made the rest of the park pale by comparison. While there is only one ride (Escape from Gringotts) it's fun to explore the area. There are lots of shops to go in and explore. It feels like you're really there which for fans is cool, but then when you explore the rest of the park, like Simpson's town, it just doesn't feel as put together. They seem to be overhauling a lot though, so in the coming years, that may not be as pronounced.

Expensive, but worth doing once. No need to buy the express pass unless you want to go on the rides over and over again or if you are there when the park is crowded. The park hopper option is recommended. This park had a little less to offer than Islands of adventure for us, but if you are traveling with little kids, this is the better park (more kid friendly).
I will recommend it for a fun and adventurous day, roll it ,keep the beat up, it's the right place to enjoy good time while in Orlando .

This was our 12th trip to Florida and Universal never fails to be fab. This trip we did the Unmasking the horror tour for the first time which I'd thoroughly recommend, absolutely fascinating to see the details and effort that goes into the scare houses and our guides, Seth (Jack McBrayer...) & Kelly were brilliant, a great double act and total horror geeks!  Next time we go in October we'd do the full day of Unmasking the Horror we weren't sure this time if it'd be too much.

We have returned to Orlando after last visit some eight years previous. Enjoyed the new attractions, and most of the older ones, this really is a great park to visit, the fast pass was invaluable and we also choose the VIP parking at a small additional surcharge. My daughter attended the special Hallowe'en Evening and gave it a big thumbs up

The big benefit during this crowded time is the advantage of purchasing the Express Pass, which allows one to skip longer lines albeit for additional cost. Since we were only spending a limited time at the park and not staying at a park hotel, it was worth it for us. I only got the single use passes, though as we wanted to try as many rides as possible.  We enjoyed this park more than Islands of Adventure as well during this time period. There are more rides for the adventurous thrill seeker, like my older son, age 11. My wife and I personally could do without the many motion simulator rides - they seem to get me more sick than actual roller coasters. My younger son, age 8, really enjoyed Diagon Alley and the interactive spell wand (which of course costs more money). FYI, there are some secret spells that he had great fun trying out - just ask a part assistant for where some might be.  I thought we would also be "clever" and hit the City Walk after park closing for a late dinner (8p), but that was a laugh as pretty much everyone else does the same thing - so all of the restaurants were very crowded.

My husband loved it. We loved Jurassic Park and had pics taken with a dinosaur who tried to eat my hat lol. The whole Harry Potter part of the park was wonderful, from the train ride both ways, Gringott's bank ride, the roller coasters, and the interactive wand experience. My husband and I enjoyed universal much more than Disney. Wait times were fairly reasonable.

We came to Universal on a blistering hot day during the first week in November - the hottest temperatures for that week ever. Disney filled most of our days, but we did give one day over to Universal to see Harry Potter. Universal is dependent on the rides, and because of my back problems we couldn't get on any of them. It seems designed for 14 year old boys, so if you're one of those, enjoy.  Universal is not Disney. It's not even close in terms of comfort, class and value. The exhibits (less Harry Potter) are tired and in desperate need of an upgrade.  We were in need of directions several times. Disney has employees scattered all over, ready and willing to offer help. There was NO ONE in sight at Universal, every time we needed help. We finally entered restaurants and asked the hosts. Mostly, they didn't know the answer to our questions.  Harry Potter was ingenious and fun, although crowded, shoulder to shoulder with school kids and parents (first week in November - does anybody still go to school?) We took the Hogwarts Express to the companion park, Island of Adventure, which was a complete disappointment. It was so hot we were desperate to return to the main park, but... the train broke down.  I asked the attendant how we were supposed to return. She hadn't a clue, other than to tell us to walk to the other side of this park, cross over, and walk around to the main park. This trip was perhaps a half mile to a mile in 95 degree heat. My wife was fading. Could you offer a golf cart or anything to replace the train? Disney would have done that. You can rent a wheelchair, we were told. When my wife looked like she was going to pass out, they comped the wheelchair out of pity or fear of a lawsuit. I was then faced with the walk back to the main park. I've had a stroke, spinal stenosis and two shoulder rebuilds, so I was the last person to be pushing this wheelchair, but it was ALL that was available. It simply had to be done.  I arrived back at the main park an hour later and collapsed onto a bench. There were no attendants in sight to offer any help. After while I got up and we entered an air conditioned show which revived us. We saw a completely lame parade, nothing compared to Disney, and ate dinner at the single worst restaurant I've ever encountered: Monster Burger. The burgers were hockey pucks, overpriced, self-served on cafeteria trays and eaten in a room full of soda vending machines on a concrete floor which offered echoes of the mostly young diners' shouting.  Never again in this life. And we paid a fortune for the day!

First of all I have to say if you can afford the extra money to stay on this resort it is well worth it. Having the price include head of the line privilege is a huge bonus. Some of the lines were 120 minute wait time. I've never read or seen any of the Harry Potter series but I was amazed by the way Universal Studios brought this to life. The rides and scenery are just unbelievable. It was great to be able to leave the resort during the day and take a 10 minute walk or boat ride back to the hotel to relax. I guess the only negative was the price for the breakfast buffet. Though it was great and plenty of food to choose from the $22.00 price tag per person is extreme. It cost us almost $100.00 after tip every morning. Also City Walk only has Cinnamon Bun and Starbucks for breakfast choices. All in all it was a great 5 days and would highly recommend this to anyone.

Been coming for over 15 years and Universal has certainly improved over the years, but compared to Islands of Adventure, it's definitely for a younger crowd. The rides are more 3D, 4D experiences which, as an adult, tends to be more headache and dizziness inducing, even for someone who loves rollercoasters.

It is a great place for families especially with children. It is worth the money and time to come here. We enjoyed everything there. The food is delicious. The staff was very helpful. Plenty of things to do and places to eat for everyone's needs.

Visited the park during the Thanksgiving weekend for my sons 9th birthday. Was able to use the early admission due to my family staying at Cabana Bay. Unfortunately we didn't use it for Universal, only Islands of Adventures. But it wasn't really needed. We arrived at the park by our Cabana Bay Shuttle and it was a ease to enter the park. At first I wasn't sure where to go due to people being everywhere and the signs seemed to blend. But I was able to ask another person and was informed as to what to do. After entering the park our first ride was Shrek do to Rip Ride Rocket being at a 40 minute wait and the park was only open for a hour or two. Lets just say Shrek was creative but definitely for the little ones. My son enjoyed it though! Next we went on Transformers which was fun,the Simpsons which my son loved (the wait was long and boring),Then we went to the Harry potter ride which was just as fun as The Mummy's revenge. Extremely creative, and since I'm a Harry potters fan it made it so much better. We tried the Butter-beer which was so delicious but gave me headache. Its a sweet drink that comes frozen, as ice cream or a drink. Kind of reminds you of the iced lattes from Dunkin Donuts, but with butterscotch. Then off to The Mummy's Revenge. Which I thought was one of the best rides. You ride the whole ride in pretty much pitch black with 3d interactions but its still a roller coaster. I had a blast and so did my son. We waited till the next day to ride Hollywood rip ride rocket,The minions,Terminator 2 and they were a lot of fun. Now I will say I was scared out of my mind about the Hollywood ride. Its constantly moving and takes you on a lift that goes straight up into the air then plummets and turns. Awesome ride. I will say the food is expensive and next time we return I will purchase food from the city walk area or go somewhere else. The food is not that good at all. We ate at the Monsters Cafe I ordered the four layer lasagna which wasn't bad in price, but the bread stick was cold and the lasagna was salty. My son ordered the chili dog and that lacked flavor all around and his fries were cold. We purchased the Coca Cola Freestyle cup which came in handy. We used it both days and it only cost $13 the first day and $6 the next. My son and I would take turns getting the flavors we wanted which worked out great. By the time one of us finished with our drink the other would be ready for their drink. My son wanted a bag of chips which was almost 3 dollars. NO it was not the big grab bag, but a regular bag. 3 dollars for a bag of chips, "that's highway robbery". Majority of the rides required lockers which worked out great, they were free for the first 30 minutes to an hour, the time was normally the equivalence to the time it took to wait in line and ride the rides. I read reviews in regards to the wait and I will say if you could afford the express pass, then purchase it. If not then wait in line, or you could stay at one of the onsite hotels which will allow early access into the parks before it opened to the public. Overall I will say Universal Studios was my favorite out of both parks. Especially since the Hulk ride was closed at IOA. My Favorite in order was: The Mummy's Revenge, Harry Potter and Hollywood Rip Ride Rocket. ET and Terminator 2 are so old. I remember those rides from when I was my sons age. But it does bring back memories of when I was a kid visiting the park with my family.Overall My son and I had a blast and will be back in a year. Look forward to seeing what else they can come up with. Keep up the good work Universal Studios

Tickets were pricey but if you were willing to sit thru a timeshare presentation you could get them for a decent price. My family and I had a ball. We had the one day park to park passes. The only problems I had were the long wait times for the rides and the long walks from park to park. There was a train but it left from an inconvenient location. Will go back but will take food and drinks with us as you can imaging, that stuff was expensive.

Plenty of rides - Revenge of the Mummy, etc Shows to entertain you. If you go around Halloween buy the frequent pass as it is not to be missed. Being chased by a clown/zombie brandishing a chainsaw is truly terrifying and fun too!
I have to say I loved the holly wood rocket and the building where u make a hilarious movie commercials I highly recommend it:-)

We went to Universal Studios on 31st October and we were a little scared that it would be so busy that we spent longer queing that enjoying ourselves. I was very happy that we didn't "pre-pay" for queue jump passes. As we arrived early in the morning and by 11am had done most if not all of the big rides/attractions in Universal and Island of Adventures.  Its great to be a kid again for the day. The Universal Parade at 3pm isnt the best and lasts 5-10mins maximum. Disney's is a lot better, so I would miss this the next time I return
Because of the low season. There were some attractions closed. But thankfully there also was lesse people. So we could see all the attractiosn even without the FastPass.

Maybe I just got lucky, but Universal had much better crowd control then Disney! I never waited in a line longer then 20 minutes, it was easy to get around and the rides are awesome! I found the rides at universal to have much more adrenaline junkie options then Disney, and as a Harry Potter fan, the wizarding world was amazing. As I found the lines to be quite short I didn't bother with an express pass. I did purchase the dining plan which maybe saved me about $5? Not a huge saving, but was convenient to have my food prepaid. The universal app was the best, you can look up wait times and set alerts and everything so you never miss a thing, I highly recommend!
went with my 3 daughters. we had an absolute blast. we did the 2 parks for 2 days pass and went back and forth between Universal and Island of adventure. magical.

The new Harry Potter park is a must see both early and later in the evening -- a 1st class job in making the park appeal to all ages.
