Although we live in London, we own a home in Orlando and have visited Universal Studios many times. I am a huge Potter and so is my family. I've written a couple of reviews before and as this is vacation family season, my family suggested that I offer our collective insider reviews, tips and suggestions to help you get the most out of your visit.  I was at Universal again in September, when it was quiet (by Universal standards) and really had a chance to take in the details that you miss when rushing about. There is so much to see and do in central Florida and the theme parks are just a small part of it all. Still, if you can spend the time, Potterland is simply full of amazing things. Prepare yourself mere muggles...I know I've written a short novel. But they are the things I wished I knew before I visited - without stealing the magic. Have a wonderful time!  OVERVIEW: When we first went to Hogwarts and Hogmead, I was simply astounded. To date, Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey is the best theme park ride I’ve ever ridden – and I’ve been on many around the world. Even the flight of the Hippogriff is pretty good and the Duelling Dragons roller coaster has always been a universal favourite – well before Potter.  You’ll find the Hogsmead area itself is exactly how it was pictured in the books. And dominating the whole place is the splendid, breath taking recreation of Hogwarts Castle. It has been masterfully built in perspective from the ground, so looking up makes you believe you really are looking at a huge castle – the view was brought back to Earth when a pigeon landed on courtyard, giving away its true size! I was so impressed with Universal and pleased that they were giving Potterites such a wonderful experience.  It had a couple of niggles – minor nit-picking. The first was that Olivanders was a bit of let-down. You had to wait for ages, only to go in a wand-box sized room to enviously watch some very lucky 10/11 year old get measured up for a wand (they never select anyone older - drat!). The second was an over-sight, really. An opportunity that I couldn’t believe Universal would miss – there was very little retail space. They had two shops and these were crowded to overflowing.  Well, Universal corrected this with Diagon Alley. In fact, they’ve gone too far, in my opinion. Diagon Alley is a retail money spinner – and that’s about it. Yes, there is the Escape from Gringotts ride, but it is a poor muggle cousin to the Forbidden Journey. I had heard reports of people queuing for hours when the ride first opened – those poor people. To wait so long…we were on in less than 20 minutes and I was incredibly disappointed (more under rides).  The Alley’s look, on the other hand, is impressive, authentic and really well done. Florean Fortescue’s Ice-Cream Parlour offers nice (expensive) treats, Madam Malkin offers robes and other clothing (you’ll need a lot of gold from Gringotts), Ollivanders, Weasleys and the others you’d expect to fine are there. Knockturn Alley is also as dark as you that you’d expect. While there is some specific merchandise to go along with the theme of each shop, most of it is pretty generic. As far as I can see, the place was constructed to magically remove gold from your pocket. Still, the Alley is a ‘must see’ if you’re a fan.  OK, here’s some top tips, broken down bit by bit.  ACCOMMODATION: We’ve only stayed at the Hard Rock Hotel, which was brilliant, but expensive – and not! By staying on site, you get to enter an hour before the general public, plus, most importantly, everyone in your party gets a free Express Pass, good for everything EXCEPT Escape from Gringotts in Diago Alley and HP and the Forbidden Journey in Hogsmead. This is a $99 value and if you have 4 in your party, it makes it well worth it. I’ve heard that the other hotels are pretty nice, but I don’t think Express Passes are included in the ‘budget’ hotel.  TICKETS I’ve yet to find a really ‘great deal’ on tickets, and if you do, beware! There are many different scams. Also some sites show ticket costs which don’t include sales tax or ‘shipping charges,’ which can be astronomical. Some travel packages include tickets in the price, so it’s hard to see if you’re getting a deal on entry or not. The most straight-forward place I found was on Universal’s site itself. Purchase online and you receive a $20 discount for each ticket, and you can print them out on your home printer. If you’re visiting for a couple of days, make sure you print out extra copies – you have to show your ticket entering and re-entering parks. And put them in a zip-lock bag to prevent them from getting wet on water rides. If you purchase them with an AMEX card, you get some advantages, which I list separately below. Express Passes are expensive and can push a two day park visit for a family of 4 well over $1000.  THE PARKS: You need to get tickets to both parks, Universal Studios and Universal Islands of Adventure, the Hogwarts Express connects the two. Keep in mind that Harry Potter is only one area in each park – the remaining parts are brilliant in their own rights. Think of Hogsmead in UIoA as the ‘ride’ attraction and Diagon Alley in US as the shopping area, which, if you think about it, was kind of JK’s thinking. Hitting both parks in a day is possible in low season – you’ll be dog tired at the end. But really, especially at peak times, you need two days.  ENTRY: With a two park ticket, go to Universal Studios first. If you’re entering with the general public, get there at least a half hour/45 minutes before it opens. They’ll let you in through the turnstyles where you can hit the shops, but stop you short of entry into the main park (rides) area. As you pass the turnstyles, take the first road on your right and follow it around to the back entrance. They open both front and back at the same time, and slowly walk the crowd to London and the Alley. The back entry is slightly faster walk to the Alley and the crowd is usually smaller, so you’ll most likely beat the main throng.  THE RIDE ‘RUNNING’ ORDER: 1. Ride Gringotts first, no matter what the wait time (It’s unlikely to be shorter, except for THE HOUR BEFORE THE LAST HOUR THE PARK IS OPEN – people have twigged into the fact that wait times drop when park closure is imminent, so there is more flocking to Gringotts and the Forbidden Journey for the ‘last ride of the night.’). 2. After Gringotts, skip everything else and immediately proceed to the Hogwarts Express to Hogsmead – you can walk through the Alley later. 3. At Hogsmead, Ride the Forbidden Journey, then the Hippogriff then the Dragon Challenge (formally the Duelling Dragons BP – 'Before Potter'), in that order – not for specific enjoyment (Dragons is better than the Hippogriff) but for maximum usage of time.  THE RIDES: As I said, Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey is the best amusement/theme park ride ever. And this is no exaggeration. If you’re prone to motion sickness, there are certain times you definitely want to close your eyes. Escape from Gringotts is a disappointment – but you really need to ride it at least once. It’s a very tame 3D roller without the coaster and screaming and fast turns and such. The queue goes through the Bank lobby and it is really freaky when the goblins in the bank make eye contact with you – creeeeepy. Both offer free lockers and you must use for bags and such. At peak times, it’s pandemonium. Don’t forget your locker number, it’s a pain in the bum if you do. But if memory fails, don’t freak out, there are other ways around it, which a cast member can assist you with. They have child swapping – I tried to get rid of my two teenagers for nice models, but they said I’d have to take the originals back.  The flight of the Hippogriff is a junior roller coaster, which is ok, but not worth waiting ages. Young-uns will like it. The Dragon’s Challenge is a fantastic roller coaster. The red Chinese Fireball, in my humble opinion, is fiercer than the blue Hungarian Horntail. But both are best tackled on an empty stomach.  The Hogwarts Express is excellent transportation between the two worlds. Watch both the window looking out and the coach door – they are different depending which way you’re travelling – if you’ve purchased a chocolate frog, make sure to keep them tight in your grip (you'll see what I mean). And on the Kings Cross side, you can see friends and family pass through platform 9 ¾ - make sure one in your party hangs back if you want to film the sacred event.  EATS: Both the Leaky Cauldron and the 3 Broomsticks offer pretty much the same meals ¬- ribs, rotisserie chicken, turkey leg, cornish pasties, shepard's pie, and fish & chips. They are healthy portions – two small kids/per adult meal. Breakfasts are an English treat – for those who don’t know, black pudding is made from congealed pig’s blood! I believe that the 3 Broom Sticks is on the universal dining plan, which we’ve never used but others have told us it’s kind of a ‘break even’ value. At the Three Broomsticks, go outside to the back patio – follow it all the back. It gives you great views of the Castle and is a little oasis away from the crowds. Drop small bits of bread over the wall to the water below – you’ll see why in an instant.  DRINKS: You can get wizard beers – Witches Brew & Dragon Ale, as well as domestic favourites at the 3 broomsticks (I’m not sure about availability at the Cauldron). Pumpkin Juice is sweet and comes in a nice bottle. The fizzy butter beer is brilliant, kind of a butterscotchy cream soda with lovely creamy foam. If you get a souvenir mug, soft drink refills are 99 cents – a reasonable bargain if you’re at the parks all day. Water is FREE everywhere! I suggest bringing an empty water bottle and filling up whenever needed.  MAGIC STUFF: Wands – You can purchase wands that do actual magic for around $45. You can pick up a map of brass icons in the floor where, with a swish and flick (or was that a flick and swish - ask Hermione), you can demonstrate that, for a price, every muggle has a bit of magic in them. Spoiler alert: the wands cease to be magic and turn back into plastic keepsakes once you leave the park.  Pop-Up shows – In Hogsmead, watch the Beauxbatons and Durmstangs do their dances on the stage next to the flight of hippogriff. Great stuff, no queues, free and fun. In Diagon Alley, you’ve got free shows of Celestina Warbeck and the Banshees plus a shadow puppet show of the tail of the three brothers. I haven’t been able to figure out the exact schedule, but if you ask the cast members they’ll tell you when they perform.  12 Grimmauld Place – look at the windows, someone is watching you.  Phone Boxes – dial M-A-G-I-C and speak to the Ministry.  The Night Bus – talk to the shrunken head, he’s funny.  Dragon on Gringotts – she roars and breathes fire every 15 minutes.  The Money Exchange – You can pretty much as the Goblin at the exchange anything about Potter; he knows everything.  Owl Post – You can post postcards by owl post, with a special postmark. But remember to bring your own stamps. I couldn’t find anywhere that sells them.  The Cast – The Universal cast stay in character all the time. They are extremely help. Ask questions or just have a chat. They’re brilliant and full of tips and fun facts.  BOOK WITH AMEX Ok, this is not an American Express advertisement. However, AMEX is the official card at Universal, and there are some ‘privileges.’ When you buy tickets with the Card, you can use the Amex lounge opposite the Shreck Ride (BTW: a good ride for kids, not for adults). Airport quality, this ain’t, but they offer free bottles of water, some granola bars and crisps and some place to sit. Well, water is free everywhere and I think you’re better off stretching out by the stage near Rocket – the most amazing and scary rollercoaster I’ve every survived. You can also get 10% off food, 10% off purchases over $50 and 15% on purchases over $75 and there’s some sort of photo discount that I can’t remember. Is it worth it? Well, if you’re using a card to pay for everything, you might as well use Amex and get the discounts.  P H E W ! !  Just one final bit. Take your time and really have a good look at everything, especially in Diagon Alley. The detail is amazing. Have a great visit!

We were there with our 2 teenage daughters during the Christmas week of 2015. It was crowded but that's when my kids have school off. For $10 more a person, I got us 3-day park-to-park tickets which I'm really glad I did. With all the people there and my husband having a bad back, we just took it easy on all 3 days to visit the parks. I did not get the express tickets because only my older one loves the roller coasters (she only rode on a few by herself and she probably only really loved one, we are from Ohio and she's used to the Cedar Point great roller coasters and doesn't care too much for the simulators that many of them are at Universal). But if you are into the rides, it would save you a lot of time getting the express pass, even during the Christmas week when there were so many people. With 3 days, we went to the park around 9-10am and stayed until 4-5pm. Long enough day for us. I think they do a great job with all the shows and the buildings and structures. Loved our visit.

A great trip with older (20-24 yr olds) to Universal. Another Harry Potter addition is welcome, but losing some old favourites makes you feel time passing. The final show of the night reminds you of what is at Universal's heart ; movies. A great two day park to park experience !
This park wasn't to bad. It has a ton of 3D rides. (Which I'm not able to do often) 😲 But nevertheless I got a kick out of some of them.

What a place to be..completely fun filled & entertaining..thanks to the day we selected..hardly crowded so we were able to cover everything without an express pass..very well managed..hospitable & friendly staff..I have been to the one in Singapore but this one is a charm on its own..a must do place for people of all ages if visiting orlando..very clean and have enough shops for eateries..the Macys parade was fun..revisiting childhood..Harry potter ranks the top amongst all the rides seconded by Revenge of the Mummy..They have this wonderful system of providing free lockers for a duration depending on the crowd at the rides..Keep up the good work guys..

Best place to go over the Christmas Break. It is not too crowded, there is a dazzling Macy's parade, the attractions are fun for the whole family. Plan to spend the entire day there to get to everything.

Except from the Terminator which I highly recommend skipping, there are a lot of great rides at this park. The best ride in my opinion is Transformers. Universal does a great job with placing characters around the park too including a huge rendition of Optimus Prime. The night time light show is so-so in my opinion, but if your still at the park at night enjoying rides its worth staying for.
Long lines, poor food service and too many people in the park! Harry Potter Diagon Alley was highlight, almost worth the waits. Add on coats are a bit ridiculous especially Express costs.

This is NOT the Universal Studios I knew as a 20-something. Its is dingy, cramped, unfriendly, and has completely lost the heart of classic Universal without Jaws, Earthquake, Back to the Future, etc. Not to mention the lines and wait times.... 3 hrs to ride a roller coaster as a family? No thank you. I was bitterly disappointed with the direction the park has taken. I will likely not return.
This is a must-go theme park with lots of exciting rides, good food, colourful theme park for photos.

We had our first trip to Universal Studios Orlando December 2015. We only did the one park, Universal Studios. We did not go to Islands of Adventure. So, ~$100/person to get into the park. The park was at full capacity rather quickly and the lines came out of no where, so we decided to buy the express passes. $180 more/person on top of the admission already paid! We still had to wait in line, but it cut the wait time by 50%. The express pass is not valid on any of the Harry Potter attractions - we waited 2.5 hours to go on the Harry Potter ride (it was a great ride though). I highly suggest you get to the park at open, and go straight to the Harry Potter attraction in the back of the park to avoid a very long wait time. We rode a few of the rides twice, thanks to the express pass. Without it, I'm not sure we would have even been able to get on everything once. The merchandise was rather disappointing as there wasn't much that actually said "Universal Studios" on it other than some plain looking shirts or hats. Many of the shirts looked like something we could have bought at Walmart. We had forgot our Universal gift cards in our hotel room, but I had pictures of the back of the cards with the numbers on them, but we still couldn't use them as the clerks said they had to have the physical card. One gift shop was able to type the numbers in successfully, but the others would not even try. So, I have a lot of money in gift cards that I guess we'll be using online instead. You are not allowed cameras on any of the rides unlike Disney who is not real strict about gopros, phones, etc on the rides. Several of the attractions, you had to lock all your belongings (purses, bookbags, phones) in a free locker. The lines for the lockers were crazy as there's only so many and everyone is trying to get one. I can understand the safety concerns, but I had a small, flat crossbody purse that I couldn't take on the rides - had to be locked in the locker. Waiting in lines for the lockers throughout the day to get in to rent a locker and then get back in to get the stuff back out took way more time that I would have liked.

We were nervous about going during Christmas week - but figured out some tips to help in the future. #1 - go early. We got there about 930 each day (2 day passes) and left by 3pm on Thursday & Friday . The wait times were no problem at all before noon - in fact only waited 30 minutes at the longest. However, we noted via the phone app wait times that earlier in the week (Monday & Tuesday) the wait times were way over 120 minutes in the afternoons. Food is extremely expensive ($50 for two) - we took our lunch the second day. Simply wandering around Diagon Alley was extremely fun. The detail in the design is amazing. Enjoyed other parts of Universal as well - especially MIB, NY, etc. A wonderful park!

We went for the holidays season, and the park was very crowded. The fast pass system doesn't works for Harry Potter rides, so the single riders option is good. I compared their system to the fast pass experience in Disney and I preferred the Universal parks system.  This park is a great option for ages 8 and over. I think they are well organized and prepared for crowds.

I've visited Universal Studios three times and it's always fun!!! I highly recommend Staff is very friendly and helpful. Entertainment is great, worth the pricy tickets. Tons of restaurants and shops are available before the main entrance (therefore free to access). We had dinner at a mexican one and it was great!

A great place to take the kids for fun day. I would have rather taken my girlfriend to one of the other parks that are geared more towards the adults. However the crowds were unbelievably dense! Which is usual.  With any of the parks in Orlando, packing patience is a must.

We flew through this park from ride to ride where we waited and waited. And then waited some more. Express passes are a must in this park. The food is super expensive.  We stayed on site and got in early which helped but only for one ride. The rides were really well done. Everything was nice and clean. Plenty of bathrooms. Most rides are covered so rain is less of an issue.

Trust me... This is what a day at the park should look like:  Park opens- Get there ASAP... you will get the best & closest parking and more importantly, you will get to ride all the rides you want with a 10-15 minute wait!  Lunch time: LEAVE! Have lunch, hit the hotel pool, go shopping.  Sunset: Get back to the parks after eating & chilling and showering. Enjoy the park till closing time.  You will be able to spot the families that tried to pull an all day-er. Trust me. This itinerary works every time.

Universal Orlando is a good park. It's well worth the cost of admission, and it's worth dropping in to see it if you are already at Disney or another attraction. Harry Potter related attractions are clearly now the main draw. They are well with it, but they are also drawing record crowds and that's a little off putting. It's wall to wall humanity and you can barely move. It's a little unpleasant at times. You may even miss other sites of the park while waiting in line for Hogwarts or Gringots. The other sites like Shrek, Transformers, and Simpsons are all good. Universal is about 10 to 15 years behind it largest competitor in terms of technology and integration. It's desperately needs to move beyond paper passes and tickets to some sort of band system with RF capabilities. We fumbled with four separate paper tickets and passes for each member of our party while there. Additionally, they need to put more photographers on the ground at their signature spots around their attractions. Their Photo Connect program runs around $100 and it basically only extends to rides. If you want family pics, like you get at Disney with PhotoPass, you will only get one or two. At Universal we got a dozen or so pics. On our Disney Trip we got nearly 100 pics, only a fraction of those were ride photos. It made buying Disney's program well worth it. Universal needs to step it up on theirs.
Our family spent 3 days here on our last holiday. It was fantastic. We all had a great time on rides and at shows.

In this review I would like to talk about two things. 1. Front of the line pass 2. Compare it with Universal Hollywood.  There are two types of Front of the Line Passes. One which you can use only one per ride and the other which gives you unlimited. I would go with the latter as it is definitely worth the extra money. We went on Dec. 27th which was one of the busiest days. Front of the Line pass got us through 120 min wait lines in 15 minutes. Sometimes the wait was even 5 mins when the general line was 100 mins or more. Having the multiple entry pass helps when you want to go on a particular ride more than once (eg. Rip it Rock'it Ride) which had only 5mins wait for my 2nd and 3rd round of the ride. The ride was really fun and I could take it thrice within 30 mins. Caution: It doesn't work for a few big attractions, eg. The Big Harry potter rides in each park. However, it will get you through all the other rides very quickly, giving you enough time to finish all the rides more than once including the Harry Potter ride.  If you have visited Universal Studios at Hollywood, I would say there are a lot of rides that are similar and some of them are even the same. I have been to Universal Hollywood 4 times in the last 5 years and I remember every detail of it. This has a few rides that Universal Hollywood had years before. So if you have been there recently, this wouldn't be entirely the same. The other thing is that a few rides eg Terminator and Minions Ride are almost the same with a slightly more "modern" effects. The Mummy Ride however is much better in California .  Is it worth going to if you have visited Universal Hollywood recently? I would say yes, because of three reasons. 1. The rides that are similar are still not exactly the same. 2. There are different rides in this park, eg- The Hollywood Rip It Rock'it which is a monster of a ride, The Amazing Spiderman, E.T., Men In Black and a few others. 3. It has Diagon Alley!!! The Harry Potter ride including the Hogwart Express which is still missing in the park in California.

Having been going to Disney for years and this year we decided to go to Universal Studios particularly for the Harry Potter exhibits. We loved Diagon Alley and the Escape from Gringots ride. The architecture was good at Hogsmead but otherwise found this attraction area a disappointment. While interesting in concept Hogwarts Express was not worth the line wait. We had the unlimited tickets so went through the rest of the parks in pretty quick order. In hind sight we should have gotten the unlimited park to park tickets and covered both parks easily in one full day. We will not go back again since we feel there aren't enough quality rides but we're glad we checked the box of the Potter rides.

Love it, My family and I have the best time ever, not so many people, if you buy the express pass there is not waiting time at all. Love the Transformer ride, the Simpsons are the Best, the Man in black too.

If you are a big Harry Potter fan probably a must do. If your kids are younger than about 13 I wouldn't come here. Not enough for the younger kids for the price. Few young kids were here so most have figured this out. For the roller coasters all purses and backpacks need to be put in rental lockers. System is a disaster, not enough of them and spaces too tight where they are located. Another reason not to bring preteens, recommend traveling light with no bags. Which also means shop after the rides. Overall, I thought it was fairly well done, comparable to Disney. Comes down to the movies and characters you like. Glad I saw it, but would not go back. I have done Disney World twice and Disneyland once. Not inclined to go back to those again either for what it's worth. All too crowded. Went with my wife and son and daughter who were on college break. Came down to run the Disney Marathon the kids wanted to come. All depends on your perspective on crowds and theme parks. If Disney is the gold standard, Universal was much closer than I would have thought in quality and cleanliness. Hard to actually differentiate unless being very particular. If you just want to ride roller coasters, go to Cedar Point, Ohio in the summer.

I know better than to visit during the holidays. If it were up to me I would never have visited during the week between Christmas and New Year. But some relatives visiting from South America wanted to go so we joined them for a couple of days. Our day at Universal Florida and Islands of Adventure was a terrible experience. (I have visited both parks before.)  We purchased the park-to-park pass because we are big Harry Potter fans and wanted to experience the Hogwarts Express. I've got to hand it to Universal -- this requirement to buy park-to-park passes to experience this is a great money-making scheme. So, instead of $102 for a one-park pass, it's $147 for two parks, much of which you won't get to experience because the parks are too big (and too crowded) to do many of the attractions. But this was considered a necessary expenditure because Harry Potter is the only reason we were going to Universal at all.  I knew entering CityWalk that we were dealing with a crowd the size of which I'd never experienced before. (For the record, we spent the day before at Epcot, which I had dreaded due to it being the holiday week, but with efficient use of the FREE FastPass there, we were able to experience everything we wanted to, have a nice dinner in Mexico, and see an amazing fireworks show to cap off the day -- all without waiting in line longer than, say, 90 minutes -- and that was only for Test Track.)  The crowds at Universal were so large -- or maybe it is a combination of extremely large crowds PLUS smaller land area than the DIsney parks, plus a more convoluted layout -- that I was thinking as we approached the entrance that they would have to cap admissions (ha! as if they would turn down the money!). Of course they did NOT do that and the park was so crowded that the best you could do all day was shuffle along in a vast crowd, clutching onto your child's hand. Rides? Crazy. The wait times were astronomical. Enter the Universal EXPRESS pass. This is not free or included with admission. Instead, for the quite high price of $150 -- per person -- you can get the ability to enter the EXPRESS line at every attraction which, according to the guy who sold it to my husband and cousin, provided a GUARANTEED wait time of 30 minutes or less. This was the selling point -- it was clearly SO crowded that day that at best you'd get to ride 3 or 4 rides. So they fell for it and bought the pass, and we went straight to Minions -- the first attraction you reach and one with an EXPRESS line. Oh, but wait -- they CLOSED the EXPRESS line because there were already too many people in it, and the regular posted wait time was something like 180 minutes. What??? No way, we just spent $450 (3 in our family) (plus my cousin spent $600) for the privilege of NOT waiting that long! So we'll come back later, right? We went to Shrek, and the EXPRESS worked as intended -- we waited probably 20-25 minutes, which is maybe 30 minutes less than the posted time. I will also say that the EXPRESS worked beautifully at E.T., where there was a 60 minute posted standby, but we walked right in and waited just 5 minutes or so. We also used it at Men In Black, which was less successful, mainly because there was no way to speed up the process of securing a locker (and then retrieving your belongings afterward). It was a total logjam of people there. After lunch (1 hour wait time, at 2pm, because every eatery in the place, from kiosks to sit-down, was completely swamped), we went back to attempt MInions before finally getting to Diagon Alley (we had small kids who realllly wanted to do MInions, or I would have skipped it). We hiked all the way across the park, got to Minions, and ... wait! They had JUST "closed" the EXPRESS line again. An extremely rude, arrogant, and smug employee informed us that they would "probably" reopen the line in 10 minutes or so, at which point the line would be at least 45 minutes wait, and we could wait "across the street", and not anywhere near where the line was actually forming, and they would allegedly come fetch us and get us in the line when it opened again. The same story was being doled out to everyone else who arrived hoping to use their costly EXPRESS pass. My husband asked what about the 30 minute guarantee? She said there was no such thing as a 30-minute guarantee. She may be right -- I don't know who was right -- but if that's the case then my issue goes to whoever conned my husband and cousin into buying the passes in the first place, using the phrase "guaranteed 30-minute wait time or less" to really sell them on the idea. So, yes, after 10 minutes or so, the line opened, we got in it, and yes, waited upwards of 45 minutes to an hour. It was a good attraction -- similar to the one there previously but much cuter with Minions, of course -- and the pre-show videos in line were entertaining -- but by the time we got on the day was winding down and we hadn't even gotten to anything HP-related yet!!  Diagon Alley is very quaint and well done, as was Hogsmeade in I of A. However, in an effort to recreate the quaintness of the movie, the space is EXTREMELY small, crowded, and nearly impossible to navigate, at least with a crowd. I wanted to be able to enjoy the details -- of which there are many! -- which have been so well recreated. But you couldn't SEE them with so many people there. The line for Butterbeer was out the door and we waited for it. Also we waited an hour to ride the Hogwarts Express -- which, ironically, does not accept the EXPRESS pass (so, again, a waste) -- which was a lovely ride, beautifully done, and FAR, FAR too short, for the amount of time you have to wait for it. There are different scenes going the other direction, I hear, but I have to take someone's word for it -- there was no question of waiting in line again for the return journey.  By the time we emerged in Hogsmeade, it was dark out -- and I mean DARK. So dark, with such minimal lighting, that you could do nothing other than shove your way through the throng, clutching your family members' hands, and try to get to some open air. Actually it was fairly frightening.  I will leave the review there -- as the rest of our visit was in I of A. But I found myself extremely disappointed in Universal -- I would so much rather have been told "the park is closed", than feel all day as if I'd been suckered into a bad deal. There MUST be capacity limits. Had there been ANY kind of emergency, particularly in the small village areas of Hogsmeade or Diagon Alley, there would have been people crushed in a stampede. How could that possibly meet safety codes?  I expected "crowded" -- I did not expect "unsafe".

After reading multiple Trip Advisor reviews to try to figure out how to Navigate the Wizarding World of Harry Potter, I'd like to do my part, having just visited.  First off, they have taken a page out of Disney's book, and separated the Harry Potter attractions into two different "lands," - with two separate admission prices. If you are bothering to go all the way out there, just suck it up and buy the "park hopper," or whatever they call it. At least this allows you to ride the Hogwarts Express train from one land to the other.  Do not, I repeat, do NOT plan to visit Universal Studios the week after Christmas and before New Year's. My husband and I went on December 29th, which was the busiest day of the year for them, and it completely ruined my experience. The park was in complete chaos - we had to wait in a line (that was impossible to find), to obtain a ticket just to GET IN to the Islands of Adventure. If you are traveling without children, you can absolutely do everything in both lands in one day - assuming you heed my warning and attend during a non-peak day.  Here is something I didn't read anywhere - a good portion of the attractions at Universal rely on screens (simulators) to provide the thrills for the consumers. My husband and I went immediately to the " Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey" ride, because we heard it was the best in the park. I'd say that 60% of this ride involves the passenger watching a screen, as if you're flying behind Harry Potter on his journey, all the while being jostled in the strapped-in seat. My husband ran off the ride to the nearest trash can - the only thing that prevented him from throwing up was the fact that he hadn't eaten anything yet that day. We were both so motion sick afterward that it took us nearly 4 hours to recover.  Be warned that if you are sensitive to motion sickness, a lot of the attractions with simulators will be difficult for you, so ask ahead of time before waiting in a line.  The last tip I will give is that some of the rides (definitely "Forbidden Journey" and "Escape from Gringotts") require riders to place all of their belongings into lockers, which are secured by scanning your index finger. These lockers are free for up to two hours - it was nice for us to walk around, unencumbered, for a time, before going back and getting our belongings out of the locker.  If you are in the Orlando area, I'd highly recommend a visit to the Kennedy Space Center - it was inspiring.

Universal studios is worth visiting if it's your first time. We bought the tickets to Universal Studios and the adjacent theme parks for 2 days, express pass for a day and wet N Wild for 14 days - paid as package online for almost $1K AUD for 2 people. Expensive yes as we went on Christmas break and the lines to get into the rides is ridiculous. We bought the express pass to by-pass the queue but there's still line regardless, so buying express pass is sort of a moot point. Better I think to go on off season - cheaper and less lines. If you are keen on still wanting to go to theme parks, buy your tickets when you get there as it's cheaper than buying from Australia online. Most of the places in Orlando offers timeshare presentation and included in a much lower rate tickets to theme parks. If you don't have kids or keen to do this, you can get the tickets cheaper. Wet N wild pass for 14 days is worth it but they will be closing the park as it's been bought by Universal to be converted to another waterworks theme park; best to wait after June 2016. There are other new rides being completed as it seems to us that there's more food stalls than rides in the park. Paying for$99 AUD for fun pass for Seaworld is also expensive. Not sure if this is because we went during Christmas break. If you are going on cruise to Bahamas, best to buy food and other entertainment outside the package they're offering as it'll work out to be cheaper but planning ahead is required.

Family of 9 travelling from the UK - 8 Adults 1 child. I have visited this park several times over the past 25 years during the christmas holiday period and I have never seen a park so busy with ridiculous wait times for all attractions. Harry Potter world looked great from what we managed to see of it amongst all the crowds. Literally could not walk yet alone attempt to push a stroller. Staff not able to control lines, we left after just one hour. Do not waste money unless going off peak!

We visited on January 3, hoping for somewhat reduced crowds versus the holidays. Unfortunately, the crowds were really bad. Any Harry Potter attraction was so crowded that it was uncomfortable to be there. We bought an express ticket (for about $100 extra per ticket) and were disappointed to find that it was useless on any of the Harry Potter rides, and of limited usefullness on a lot of other rides.  Having said that, some of their rides/attractions were really incredible. The Hogwart's Express was disappointing, but the Hogwart's castle ride was the closest thing to actually participating in a Quidich match I could imagine. The Spiderman 3D ride is extremely realistic and immersive. However, the Transformer 3D ride is an exact copy (with different visuals)! Go to one, but not both. We rode two coasters. The Harry Potter dragon roller coaster was our favorite. We rode it twice - once in the front seat and once in the middle. I highly recommend waiting a few extra minutes to get the front seat, because otherwise all you can see is the back of the person in front of you.
The details in Diagon Alley are totally amazing. Lots of shops and interactive things to do with wonderful people working there.

Horrible place, dirty nasty! The day we were there you couldn't get anywhere...too many people! The wait times for rides were 3 hours long. If there would have been an emergency, people would have been trampled and emergency people would not have been able to get in. Hogsmeade area was way to busy couldn't see anything or do anything wall to wall people. Terrible place will not go back again!!

We visited Universal and bought a 3 day pass that allowed us to park hop. We probably only needed 2 days as we didn't go on many rides and also the parks were not too busy. The busiest ride seemed to be the Despicable me ride with wait times up to 110 minutes while we were there.  Springfield was my favourite because you can go into the Kwik-E-Mart to buy gifts and souvenirs; note this is not set out as the 'real' Kwik-E-Mart. I enjoyed ordering lunch from Krusty Burger and eating it in Moe's Tavern, where you can buy Duff and see Barney! Oh and buy a big pink if you are hungry, it's the donut Lard boy holds and is delicious.  The Wizarding World of Harry Potter was amazing. We've been to the Universal in Japan which is much the same as Hogsmead here. However, the Hogswart Express was MAGICAL (haha!) and lots of fun. Young and old were so excited lining up. Diagon Alley was really cool and not in Japan so that was extra fun for us.  In my opinion, the best thing about The Wizarding World of Harry Potter is the interactive wands they can be purchased. They are not cheap at about $50 each but you can choose any characters wand and walk around the park casting spells. If you do it correctly, you can see the magic unfold! (If you go to Ollivanders, you may be chosen and given a free wand)  The Macy's parade was on when we visited. It was gorgeous. The blimps were huge and the show was very colourful. Santa even lit up the lights on the Christmas tree when he passed it.  There are lots of characters to take photos with like in most theme parks. The lines were longish and the staff would tell you if characters had to leave and told you when they'd be back. Most people seemed happy to wait for characters to come back.  Lots of see, lots to do, lots of fun!
This is much better the Universal California!! 2 parks next door to each other. Simpsons is amazing! Harry Potter - we're not fans, but amazing and a must see - and packed to the gills!!!

My wife and I, both in our late 60s, had a brilliant time. Not being interested in fast roller coasters we chose this, more sedate, attraction. It was well worth the money, despite being sneezed on by Donkey in the Shrek 4D attraction, and the rain which was incessant during the afternoon.

Went in October 2004 as this was the last time I was in America. The rides and everything about universal studios is out of this world!! The staff were very friendly, plenty to see and do for all ages. Will definitely visit next time I go to USA! 💗
Diagon Alley was such a special place. It was exactly like the movie and so fun to walk through. I highly recommend visiting if you are an HP fan.

If you are a big coaster fan - this is your place. But be advised that there are only 2-3 rides for younger children. Most kids need to be over 40" tall for the adult rides. Harry Potter was amazing! The details followed to movie so well. Diagon Alley was superb. Very costly - food is very expensive.
Universal studios was an amazing theme park for all ages. The city walk attached made for a great ending to the night as well, i would recommend this for 21+.

Went for my birthday. I was at Harry Potter world as soon as it opened on my birthday. (Yep I was 36 years old that day.) And it was great! Everything looked just like the movies. We went on a wet but fairly warm day in February. (Warm for us as we are from Canada) and there was very little line ups - it was great! My one real complaint is EVERY ride ends at a store! There was more shopping then there was rides and/or activities. We came back the next day (we had a buy 2 and get the third day free pass to both of the worlds)and it was much warmer and full sun. There was a ton more line ups the next day and too be honest the majority of the rides weren't worth the wait.

The Harry Potter experience is out of this world but to see the different Harry Potter parts you also need a pass for "The Islands of Adventure" other wise you could not ride on the Hogwarts Express back and forth between parks. But regardless it has to be seen to be believed, this is technology from another world.......So get the 2 day pass to enjoy a fantastic time at both parks. Plenty of other stuff to do besides Harry Potter.

Me and my partner cannot stay away - We have visited the park 6 years in a row from 2009-2014 and it just gets better and better. There is so much to do in the park. It's clean and well kept. Food is great with loads of places to eat - The Irish restaurant is fab! Overall fantastic experience - I personally believe it's better than Disney :) Island of adventures if equally as spectacular and now you can get the Hogwarts express across from one park to the other - well - mind blowing :)

I absolutely love Universal Studios. I am a big film buff so as soon as I walked up to the gates and could hear Back to the future soundtrack I started to tingle. It's full of Nostalgia and great rides. Go early and stay late and see everything because there's so much OR if you have unlimited access through your stay .. All the better.  We stayed on international drive twice and it's really short taxi ride away if you don't like to be stuck to bus schedules.  Overall I love this place it's great!

Universal is by far my favorite Florida park. The attractions are fun and interactive and the park is very clean with friendly, helpful staff. We stayed at the hard rock hotel and upgraded to fast passes which I highly recommend.

Very interesting for amateurs of this type of entertainment. Experience of being part of top pop films, such as action, violence or fantasy; would say good for children and those who are never grown up (men:)?) Not my climate at all. Everything is artificial and supposed to be fun (not for me!). Expensive - single adult ticket $108 plus you pay for some additional attractions (the price is also appropriate). The quality of shows though is impeccable.

We were here last year and enjoyed ourselves immensely. We came back this year and enjoyed it every bit as much. It is ridiculously expensive but the fast pass was worth it. I personally hate waiting in line for anything and waiting at both Harry Potter worlds and for the Hogwarts express was about enough for me. None of these are included with a fast pass. Everything else in the park is however. The Simpsons ride was hilarious and the Mummy was very surprising. Can't comment on the roller coasters etc as that is too much for me! Just wish there was better food in any of the venues. Not a great place to eat but still a must see in Orlando!

Visited both parks and got exactly what i expected. -Up to date entertainment, apart from a few rides (like Men in Black which was absolutely awfull). I still like the California park better, because of the actual tour through genuine movie-sets, like the clocktover of Hill Valley :)
It has been a few years since we were there but I was surprised how much it had changed. They have a Harry Potter section that is a must see!!
Visited Harry Potter world of wizardry and it was nothing short of amazing. The rides are incredible and the whole family enjoyed it.

Cannot emphasise enough, the superb day we had at the Universal Studios. We were only in Orlando for 2 nights and my Fiancée insisted that we visit Universal Studios before heading off across to Clearwater. We both had a fab day on several of the theme rides; Terminator The New Harry Potter and Escape from Gringotts, Transformers - The Ride Revenge of the Mummy All of which were fantastic and although it states 45 minute wait, the queue moves steadily and time passes quickly. There were plenty of side shows, Blues Brothers singing etc with many eating and drinking areas. An absolutely amazing day. Our entire itinerary included 2 nights in Orlando, 4 nights in Clearwater, 4 nights in Naples, 5 day cruise from Miami and 5 nights in South a Beach - Miami and although a most memorable trip to remember, Universal sticks out as one of my best days.  Enjoy

The last time we came to Orlando was 15 years ago and my kids were 10 and 12. They weren't very impressed with Universal Studios and they absolutely loved Disney. We decided to go to Universal Studios again with the 14 day unlimited ticket and we did not regret it. The rides at Universal cater for the older generations as opposed to kiddies and the Wizarding World of Harry Potter is just amazing. (as is the Simpsons area). Would definitely recommend.

I recently moved to Florida and just got around to visiting universal. I adore it. If you're a Transformers and Harry Potter geek like me, you must go! The parade is nice and there's the Fear Factor show live. There's so much more fun stuff going on in the parks, go on and make the trip!

We came to Orlando 20 years ago with our children, we loved it then, so we are back celebrating 43 years married, this time no kids. The park has changed a lot, a whole new one in fact, new rides, end minions all over the place. Great to revisit, don't expect to be back any time soon. Wonderful two days need to cover everything.

Went to the park yesterday. Attractions are great, much modern than Disney, great effects (Transformers, MIB, Simpsons, among others). But the day did not end well. MUCH EXPECTED HARRY POTTER´S ESCAPE FROM GRINGOTTS WAS NOT FUNCTIONING PROPERLY, WHICH WAS NOT ADVISED TO VISITORS (we had a hint, as the line progress was very slow and when approaching the embarquing sector saw a convoy leaving empty but with a Park employee). THE RIDE STOPPED IN THE MIDDLE OF THE GAME, IN THE MIDDLE OF NOWHERE, AND THEY LEFT US THERE FOR 10 MINUTES!!!! MY WIFE HAD A PANIC ATTACK, AND ALTHOUGH WE ASKED FOR HELP, NOBODY SHOWED UP. Must say that Health Service was very efficient (sorry, don´t remember his name), and Sean from Customer Services was very polite and understood the situation, proposing a refund and new tickets. Briefing: the Park shouldn´t allow visitors to ride an attraction that is not working properly, or at least advise in advance....

This is a great park. And if you only have one day to visit a park I highly suggest this one. Like most parks unfortunately the food prices are outrageous. Only complaint I have are the people who are in groups going into the single rider line. Making the line a lot of times just as long as the main line. My favorite rides were escape from gringotts, the mummy and transformers. Though most of the rides were great. I would definitely come back here.
We always love going to this park! Never disappointed. Loved the new additions to the park and I would recommend to everyone!

I guess you gotta do it if you have kids. Its a bucket list item for every child and their parents. Seems that my bucket list checks this off about every two years though. In any case, we came and conquered it again. Lots to do and see. It is pretty amazing to see everything that the park puts into its property. There are lots of thrilling rides to enjoy. The food ranges from amusement park icons to amazing food like Emeril's. There is plenty of shopping to be had as well. You can do both Universal parks in one day, but you better keep moving and use an express pass. Two adults; one child; both parks; 3 express passes and you've just evaporated nearly $800. Seriously. To me, its cool but not that cool, but hey, you only live once and you know those kids are going to hound you till you give in. Just go.

This park was where we started and really enjoyed riding the movies! We started mid-day and at the front. Crowds were not thick here, and we did have the express pass so did not wait long anyway. Every ride is worth experiencing, and many will make you forget it is just a ride! Our party liked the experience of 3D rides better than most adventure park thrill rides because of the theme attached. There are many photo ops, entertainment on the streets, and places to eat.

What we loved the best #1 Harry Potter #2 Minions #3 Transformers #4 Shrek Where we ate - 3 Broomsticks - good food , great portions , do lunch, the lines are not as long. Jimmy Buffet's Margaritaville , it's a fun place but you have to make reservations.

We always get the 2-day / 2-park pass when we go to Orlando and we've been going back to Universal for almost 20 years. Now our kids are teens and we all love it more than Disney. My son is a huge Jurassic Park and Harry Potter fan. Here is the good and bad: Bad: You will pay $20 for parking, it will be 1-2 hours from the time you park, get through security, walk to the park, wait for the entry where thy use a finger print reader that doesn't work, then stand on line for your first ride. Very frustrating. Good: The rides are awesome, it is a much more adult place than Disney and the rides are more thrilling. Universal pays attention to intricate details inside the rides so you are amazed by the sets while you wait online. Tips: Use single rider lines if you have older kids (and no kids) and don't mind splitting up. That could mean the difference between a 60 minute or 10 minute wait. You'll still get on and off at the same time. Don't come with a backpack or bag. Seriously, why do people need so much stuff? It will only burden you - security will take longer and you will often have to stop at a locker to check your bag before getting on rides. Get the Butterbeer in any Harry Potter area. The frozen kind is delicious in the Summer, the hot kind is great on the rare occasion that it's cold in Orlando - it's like melted butterscotch.
Unfortunately most things in this area is expensive we had pre-paid dinner at Bob Marley had dessert at frozen yogurt and enjoyed mini golf. Only spent 50.00 as couple.

We took our kids to Universal a few years ago and we all absolutely loved it. They wanted to go back again, so we shelled out the $100+ apiece for tickets and looked forward to another great experience. Unfortunately, we discovered that Universal had changed and not for the better. In fact, it was a rather miserable experience.  Just getting into the park has now become miserable in and of itself. The metal detectors (not there last time we were there) were a real joy. Way too few for herding the many thousands of people through. It took a very long time to get through them.  Then, we stopped at will call and printed off our tickets and meal plan tickets (a total rip-off). We assumed since we were given meal plan tickets right before entering the park, those are the tickets we use for dining. Nope. As we found out at lunch time, you have to take those tickets and wait in line wayyyy back at the beginning of the park and exchange those tickets for other tickets. What??!!  Then, those tickets can only be used at the restaurants that accept the tickets and those restaurants have a symbol on them on the map. OK, good enough... at least we know which restaurants accept the meal plan. Nope again. After walking to the other side of the park to the restaurant we wanted (because my wife has food allergies and could only eat at a couple of the restaurants), they informed us that, yes they accept the meal plan. But not THAT meal plan. The meal plan you get "at your hotel". Not the one you buy "through Universal". What??!! again.  So we had to walk all the way to the other side of the park to eat at the only other restaurant my wife could eat at. When we finally did get our food, we discovered the meal plan tickets we purchased basically saved us nothing on the price of the food. A total ripoff and a huge nuisance to boot.  Later, we went to use the "snack"and "beverage" on our meal plan ticket and were told by the checker that we couldn't use them both at the same time. What??!! a third time. So we had to go through the line to get our "snack", then go back through the line again to get our "beverage". All in all, to save a dollar or so on each of our meal plans, we wasted a couple hours of our day.  And that seems to be the story at Universal. Everything is designed to waste your time. From the stupid new lockers that your forced to use (which requires waiting in long lines before you even get to wait in long lines for the rides) before virtually every ride, to the ridiculous meal plan tickets. We got to the park when it opened, left when it closed, were there on a Monday in January, and the kids still only time to ride a handful of rides.  Needless to say, we've had our fill of Universal. The only reason I didn't give it one star was that most of the rides we did get on were pretty good. On a side note, if you check my reviews you'll notice I rarely give any place bad reviews. Universal definitely earned this bad review.  And on a final note... DON'T BUY THE MEAL PLAN!!!

Still the best park for rides. Gringotts ride was brilliant. We had Butterbeer with a whisky shot. Well worth it. Harry Potter is very crowded. Transformers ride is really good and The Mummy is always. Favourite. If it's busy get in the solo rider line, so much quicker. And you sometimes still get to sit in the same car. We found character photo opportunities easy. A lot smaller lines than Disney. We got some great photos with Transformer Megatron.

We went to see the Harry Potter attractions. While the rides were good, in a way they were the same: 3D, move to another location, see another scenario. We enjoyed walking around the sites supporting the Harry Potter theme; nicely done. For off season on a Saturday we were surprise at the wait times of 50 minutes even at 9am in the morning. We did try using the singles line once and had a 25 minute wait instead. Pricey because to see all the Harry Potter stuff you have to get admission to 2 parks. There were local places or AAA that got us a better price than at the park.

Me and my boyfriend went here because I'm really excited for him to try the Transformers ride 3D. The rides were awesome since Universal offers more rides in 3D making the experience way better. I just hope that the park is bigger. Even though I know that the second park Island of Adventure is just beside the main park I still feel that Universal Studios should offer a bigger size theme park to make the park fee worth it.

The experiences to be found anywhere in the Universal Parks are fantastic, well worth a visit. Next time we visit we will be either staying at a Universal Hotel (where you have fast passes as part of the hotel and are able to buy on the park and have it sent to the hotel) or buying the fast pass option. Apparently from Harry Potter and Terminator the passes can be used park wide I believe.

Being a Harry Potter fan I suppose it is to be expected that I would award 5* for this attraction, but really it's fantastic.... With one exception... Paint the Hogwarts express a brighter red! Eating in this park is far superior to that of any Disney park. I particularly appreciated ordering food, then being shown to a table and my very acceptable food being brought to me. Train ride between parks is amazing. I suggest dressing up so as not to look too much like the muggles we are.

my wife and i wanted to experience the harry potter rides and areas. so we bought a one day two park pass, islands of adventure and universal studios. that way you get to see both sides of harry potter and get to ride the train between them. in universal studios the men in black ride was way cool as was the transformers. at closing there was a water light show with fireworks that was very enjoyable.

Our family loves this park. The kids love the Rip Ride Rocket, the Mummy and well every other ride in this park. MIB is lots of fun for everyone. Staff always seems to be having a great time and stay in character which is awesome. Fast passes make the waits short. Diagon alley is a must do. Florean Fortescu's ice cream is a must. They have some really unique flavours. My favourite is the lavender and earl grey. The chocolate raspberry is also delicious. The park is clean, fun and worth the money. Taking the Hogwarts express between the parks is also a great experience. The train is very well done.

The facility was very clean and well designed. It was quite small for The Orlando area but was equal in cost to the other attractions that are available in the same area. That made it a poor choice if the other attractions were part of a family choice. The walk from the parking lot to the attraction was very long and the parking was a little chaotic.
We love going to both of these parks. Going to both is a lot of fun. Two days is plenty of time to go. Depending on your energy level.

Let's start by saying the rides especially Harry Potter are fantastic. No complaints there. The problem is a lack of organization. From the entry area to lockers it seems no one really planned this well. A lot of time is wasted. I can say I went once and I'm glad I did but that is probably it!

The entire Universal Studios has something for everyone. There are rides for all ages, all types of rides and fun for all. I was just a little disappointed you had to buy special passes to travel between the two Harry Potter areas. Seems once you are in the park everything should be open to everyone. We liked that you can go inside the front area and eat lunch/dinner without having to purchase a ticket. WE had lunch at Jimmy Buffet's Margaritaville twice during our two days. The Corn Clam Chowder was delicious. Loved the "erupting" of the volcano every half hour. So much fun!!!! There is a live DJ there playing great Jimmy Buffet music all the time. Just a neat restaurant. We also had dinner at Antojitos Mexican Good-752 one evening as we let the park. It is just outside the ticket booths. Very neat place. Live music which was excellent. Good food.

Universal Studios was a nice outing. They are constantly updating the attraction to make it more up to date, and they need to! As my group of adults and I walked through some of the attractions I couldn't help wonder if today's kids had any idea of who some of the characters even were (Dagwood? Popeye? Really?). But the Superheroes were up to date (Transformers, Hulk and such). We really enjoyed the live animal attraction (dog actors). The rides using 3D were great. Non-3D rides now pale in comparison! If you have a chance to get a skip-the-line pass, do it.

I had not visited Universal Studios-Orlando in quite a few years and was surprised at the amount of growth that the park had accomplished. I only allotted 1-day to visit the park and found that it was impossible to experience all that the park had to offer in that time period. I think that a 3-day visit would be a better plan. The Harry Potter sections of the park are fascinating (not just for children). There is much in the park to attract adults. The location of the restaurants outside of the main entrance to the park is an example of the genius the was used in constructing this facility. Although I am not a great Theme Park fan, I do plan to go back to the park sooner than later in order to experience all that the park has to offer.

BUT... have deep pockets. You are gouged at every corner. From my 60 dollar lunch of burgers dogs and dry fries and gross pops, for 2 people, to my 13 dollar hot dog, to 6.00 popcorn, this place is engineered for one thing only. To seperate your money from your purse or wallet. SOOO expensive. tickets 500 busks, hotel 700 a night, dinners, around 200 a couple for a sit down nice meal, express passes 120.00 a day. And they are not express. Your only promise is "half the time of the regular line" So if the regular lines wait is 3 hours, your 120.00 passes will cut that down to 1 1/2 hours, which no one monitors. One time, I can't recall the ride, we walked past a family in the regular line to get to Express, and I happenned to recall them, they got on before we did in Express. These big theme parks are way more expensive than they should be. Also they should be limitied to how many people they can allow in the park. On our second day, we were in line to get in for over an hour and a half. Thats a good part of your day. It's off the bucket list, would never go again.
A must to visit while in Orlando. My favourite park,as Harry Potter rides are totally awesome,flying on a broomstick was amazing!

Great day out for all the family! Lots of rides and things to see. There is something for everyone here regardless of your age. Water rides are great fun long as you don't mind walking around wet for a few hours

I enjoyed sightseeing more than I did going on rides. The Harry Potter theme was well represented in both parks. The detail and activities related to the Harry Potter movies was great. Watching people doing the interactive magic wand spells was entertaining and very well presented. My only complaint was that I paid $30 instead of $20 to get a parking spot where an attendant could help me unload a scooter from the car, and I ended up in a regular parking place where I had to ask other guests for help. Shame on them.

We just took in City Walk - not interested in rides/lines/crowds and ill-mannered rugrats. Been there, done that. This is a small area of mostly dining/shopping with some nightlife clubs and shows. We saw Blue Man Group which is fantastic for adults and kids. Don't go for the "preferred parking" extra $10 charge. Its a ripoff. The $20 parking fee can actually get you closer to the park if you go early. Check out Margaritaville restaurant - prettly cool and the food was good.
The ticket price was confusing on-line and the staff at the ticket counters took forever and seemed to be car salesmen. Long waits and unfriendly staff. Would not return or recommend to anyone.
Visited both theme parks and had a wonderful time at both. Was a quick vacation for my daughters and I and we enjoyed every minute.

I could easily spend all day here. Even though they got rid of some classics like Jaws and King Kong, I love the new expansions they are putting in. I can't wait to see what else they add. My only complain is it seems to be all in 3D now. I'm hoping they keep some rides that aren't just 3D. I can only do so much of that in a day!

Love Universal Studio's.  I highly recommend for families with kids about ~6 or older. There's not a TON of rides for the little ones but it is still cool.  I go here about 4-5 times a year and i live in NYC, my 8 year old daughter just loves it.  Biggest tip i can give is STAY in the ONSITE hotels to get express passes PLUS early park admission.  As for the park itself its perfect and with recent updates of Diagon Alley, it's some of the most impressive fully immersive attractions in the world. for Harry potter fans or not. I'm not a Harry Potter fan and i still enjoy the area a LOT.

Did a one park one day pass at over $100 but seems it is just not enough for this place. So first the good, there are a few decent rides and have definitely improved over the older Universal studio rides. Employees at the park pretty friendly. Here is what seems to have gone down hill for this place. They seem to want extra for everything. Want to park a little closer, extra $10. We skipped paying $60per person for express pass figuring it was a Thursday and wouldn't be too bad. Well we did ok for a few rides but then one of the rides was down for an hour. This must have accumulated a bunch of express people because once we got into line, it was horrible. The wait time said 45 minutes but it turned out to be an hour and a half. They were letting huge groups of express riders on a time and only a couple from the regular line. The people in front of us complained and the guy said well the express line is a little long. Universal does not know how to do Express properly, they don't set up reserved times and offered unlimited yes unlimited express to lines. So people can really just hop off then get back in. So unless you'd like to pay almost $200 per ticket you may find yourself standing around most of the day.  So after that it was time to eat and we were excited to just relax at Margaritaville, well apparently someone must have paid huge $$ to close down not only Margaritaville for the whole night but a couple other restaurants as well. I can only image people that came out of their way, paid $20 to park and walked all the way to find out they are closed must have felt. This place has become very greedy. How can you close entire restaurants at your busiest dinner time. This is probably a last visit for me.

The positives: Transformers - brilliant! The so-so's: Terminator - dated. The negatives........ Most things else!  We wanted to go on The Simpsons ride, but a queue of 75 minutes ruled that out as we were only there for a day & couldn't justify so long a wait (especially when I had heard people complaining that often waits were longer than posted). Other rides also had crazily long waits..... It a all started on arrival: drove straight in having paid the $20 parking fee, objecting to paying more for higher priced parking. Walking to the entrance, we joined the queue which took 45 minutes to actually get into the park - crazy. At the ticket desk we were urged to pay another $80 each for "Express" passes - on top of the $325 entrance for both of us: we declined, thinking it was expensive enough anyway. Once inside, the queues were longer still. We talked to one family that had queued over two hours for a ride! We did several,rides during he day, but our highlights were the terrific Transformer ride & the Animal Actors show - which wuss good old fashioned fun! We lunched at one of the many burger bars - and it was terrible! We took the cold burgers & fries back to Havel them replaced with tepid ones. The burger was the cheapest, most tasteless burger I can remember enduring. The whole park seems to have sacrificed customer service for customer hard sell. Instead of gearing up to extract yet more money, I think they need to invest in actually giving people what they have paid for - and that is not queue after queue after queue! It is twenty years since I've been here, and whilst I do remember queueing it was never even remotely as horrendous as now. Would we return? Sorry - doubt it.
there was lots of noise but i delt with it very well it's quite a nice attraction and i would recommend it to people it is good for a holiday

Our visit to Universal Studios (both parks, park to park pass) was great although the competing park is still my favorite and has MUCH more to offer. The best thing Universal has going for it is the Wizarding World of Harry Potter and my review there tells all about our great experience. Outside of HP here are a few of our favorite things: The Minion Ride, the Jurassic World River Adventure (it was cold but we wore our ponchos and were soooo glad), Spiderman, We stumbled into our very favorite thing in the Jurassic World section. It was the Velociraptor Expo. It didn't look like much at first but we stayed in line. When we got in we heard a brief talk about Velociraptors then the real fun began. It was a very real looking animatronic dinosaur. Each visitor group got to stand in front of it and have a picture or video taken. It moved and roared and made you feel very nervous. LOL. The kids were great to watch and when it was our turn it was a lot of fun. We got a great video out of it. Don't miss it! Spiderman ride was great and MIB was a lot of fun. Suess Land would have been more fun if we had little kids with us. The Sinbad show was just so so. The worst: Shrek was a waste of our time. The Mummy ride was rough and jerky. The Posiedon's Fury is not a ride. You walk through and it is super crowded. You can't see much if you are not in front especially if you are short or a kid. I kept waiting to move from the room into seats for a ride but you stood the whole time. It was NOT good. I think the Simpsons are not for kids and am not a fan.  Overall we had a great time but we could do everything in one short day.(excluding WWoHP) The biggest draw to get me back is WW of Harry Potter and even at that one day would get it done.

We live in Chicago but business brings us to Orlando several times a year so we have Universal Studios Orlando.  There are two parks at USO, Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure, that are connected by a train that runs between The Wizarding World of Harry Potter's Hogsmeade and Diagon Alley. Make sure that you buy a two park pass so that you can visit both parks.  Our favorite park is Universal Studios where you "Ride the Movies" - even the kids rides are fun for adults. There are shows and parades, and characters are everywhere, all day long. During the holidays there's even a Macy's parade and the park is peppered with giant balloons. Look for the squirrel that's hidden in the huge Christmas tree that's located in front of the Macy's facade, next to The Mummy.  Beverly Hills Boulangerie, located in Hollywood at the front of US, has wonderful sandwiches, pastries, and fresh fruits if you are tired of traditional theme park food. And there are plenty of nice restaurants in both parks, and at CityWalk.  There are plenty of perks when you stay at a Universal hotel, including early park entry and free Express Passes - a must whe the parks are busy.  Universal hosts Mardi Gras events, and its Halloween Horror Nights is TERRIFYING.  Go! You'll have a great time!

Universal Studios is not to be missed! We had so much fun at all of the different venues. I was very impressed with each spot, but I really loved Springfield! The afternoon parade was worth the wait. The park keeps everyone entertained for hours. Don't miss this place

Having paid $30 for premier parking... We walked for an hr to the Universal Park we'd come to visit. Premier parking was in the furthest lot from the entrance to Universal.... Then you have to wander thru all the theme venus, restaurant areas, gift shops, stop to get assistance, and fumble with a less than user friendly map. Getting out of the park was no easier...

If you are planning on making a vacation, keep Orlando in mind because IOA and USO will be two of the most fun days you'll have anywhere!  The must-do attraction here is Harry Potter and the Escape from Gringots. This is my favorite attraction ANYWHERE in the US (my next 5 being Dinosaur [formerly CTX], Indiana Jones and the Temple of the Forbidden Eye, ToT [DHS version], HPFJ and Verbolten).  One must-do food item is the chocolate chili ice cream at Florean Fortescue's. You have to be in the mood for it, but the delicious, rich chocolate front end flavor gets married to back end heat. It's a 'once in your life' (minimum) must try (unless you're allergic to chocolate or chili pepper).  A must-purchase would be a wand (hopefully interactive).  One sleeper attraction is Men in Black: Alien Attack. It typically has short lines, and when it doesn't, the single rider line is practically nonexistent. It also has a lot of re-ridability (because it's a shooter).  Fast Food Blvd is the place to eat in USO. Your entire group can pick and choose from healthy fare (salads and wraps) to the clogger (a burger that could stop your heart). You could also get a flaming moe, and while small (10oz I'm guessing), it's a delicious and unique drink.  I've tried almost every restaurant in the park (with the exception of Kid's Zone) and haven't been able to find a decent meal (outside of Fast Food Blvd). Even Leaky Cauldron was a disappointment as the 3 times i ate there (because I love the ambiance) the food was cold every time. But I was told the Deathly Hallows beer was next level!  For dessert grab some Florian before you head out.  If I had to improve the park there's a couple things I'd work on: 1) Do something with Kid's Zone 2) Create better shows or replace them (Animal Actors and Fear Factor). Fear Factor could have been replaced years ago with 'America Ninja Warrior' for better results or a Ministry of Magic of Attraction could make better use of the space. 3) Absorb MIB:AA into Springfield and make it a 'Bartman' attraction. Superhero + Shooter = Success. Springfield has more that could be expanded upon and there's only 2 attractions in the area. Plus, what is 'World Expo's' overarching theme? 4) Expand Despicable Me (up to Jimmy Fallon) and make Super Silly Fun Land (incorporating RRR and the stage). It's a 2.7 BILLION dollar, three movie, franchise; with more to come. Also, it could become the kids area of the park, and Kid Zone could be easily replaced.

My 7 year old boys loved Universal! The park was clean and the staff was great! We had our faces painted by Max at Universal Studios! He did an amazing job and we never felt rushed. He was the absolute best! We did Harry Potter and the staff couldn't be nicer. Food was really good in Diagon Alley. Stay away from the "Monster Mash" restaurant. We went there our first day and the food was terrible. Tickets and food are pricey, so be prepared to spend some serious coin. We Would go back again.

This place is out of this world ,what an experience i loved every minute of it my son was very embarrassed of me and my husband as we had our photos took with all the characters .well worth every penny .Very busy and weather not that good in feb but i wouldnt want to go at height of season would be too crowded .

It's one of those gotcha entertainment places of course that for a family to go there like Disney, costs an arm and a leg. Was it worth the update in time. Yes. Didn't go to the water park at all. The new Minon ride would have been better with an electro magnetic push for the start. Still going thru buildings was fun. Potter area was okay unless you are a Harry Potter fan. Then it was over the top. Spent the day there and City Walk at night is breath taking.

First of all you have to start pretty early! So you can skip a little bit the lines! But the best thing you can do is to buy the express unlimited ticket! It will cost you! But it's worth 100%! For eating also I would recommend the Turkey Leg! Great taste and value!

Had fun! Very expensive! I would suggest splurging for the express pass as it drastically reduces wait times ( which were easily an hour + per ride). Transformers ride is the best!! Could use some new rides for the older crowd. But had a great time. Would definately go again.

My wife and I went to Universal for the first time and enjoyed it , especially the Terminator, the Men in Black, the live animal show, and the Harry Potter ride. Although, we took the train to the other park it appeared to be geared more toward younger kids.

I was so excited for Universal. I have 3 boys... 11, 9 & 6... The two oldest were definitely growing out of Disney. For what I paid.... For 2 days (got 3rd day free)... NO PARK HOPPER (that would be additional $50/ticket.... And no fast pass)... It was $900.... Add parking & food... Omg!!! AND HONESTLY... besides the Minion Ride.... That had ATLEAST a 60 min wait... The mummy roller coaster, and the Rock It roller coaster.... It was OUTDATED!!!!!!! The 3D (& 4D) technology for Shrek, Simpsons, Terminator, and Transformers is old!!!! It will be awhile before (& IF) I return. Not impressed at all.

Personally i only came as rest of family wanted to visit harry potter Once there though i did enjoy the park and had a good day there queues were ok but once again i think universal have been clever by making you buy a 2 park ticket to visit the whole of potter as it is in both parks Once seen personally i wouldnt rush back but i can see the attraction

Great fun for all ages! So much to do and such an enjoyable day out! Harry Potter castle looked amazing but way too long queue. The Harry Potter world was magnificent, even butter beer available to try!
Overpriced and most of the park is in dire need of updating. several rides were down. Wouldn't go again.

this is a park for every ages myself I love it as did my children the price was okay as I bought my ticket at a cheaper ticket stand love the firework nice customer services good food nice shopping don't forget take many pics

Had a wonderful time at Universal. We rode many rides loved Harry potter and The Transformer was my personal favorite.I' 61 years old and had a blast with my 5 grandkids doing rides. BY FAST PASS expensive but a must have for most rides.
top theme park with loads to do i could go on ofr ages here about how good it is but you really just have to go yourself and immerse yourself into the amazing rides and shows

OK my love for this park is only for Harry Potter lol. Im kidding... but have you noticed all the rides are the same?  The Minion Ride is a 3D motion ride, The Transformers is 3D Motion Ride, Escape from Gringots is a 3D motion ride, Spiderman at their sister park is also a 3D motion ride....notice a pattern?  Being someone that wears glasses its just annoying to have to wear this 3D glasses for a ride! And it seems that all these rides are the same lol.  I did like to walk around Diagon Alley, the stores are just too cute and my daughter got a wand that she got to play with there. My favorite is the train which we took back and forth. lol.
