Several rides closed or 'under construction' Restaurants all rammed full with long waits to just get in Park closes at 1900hrs for corporate activities I was disappointed in the lack of any real inteest for film buffs - just cheesy rides and plastic backdrops. maybe I expected too much, but for the entry price I expected much, much more - not a ratio of approx 20 tat outlets for ever ride
Great theme park for both kids and adults. Some of the rides are outdated but worth it. Mummy ride is the BEST!!

We went to buy our tickets and knowing that we might not make the other park in one day we wanted to buy a one-day, one-park pass. It was not posted on the sign board and when we asked, the gentlemen said that they don't encourage that ticket. That they want people to buy the park hopper since they have already paid 80% of the price (totally untrue - $105 vs $155). On the way in to the park American Express had a promotion going that if you sign up for a credit card you have a choice of two flex passes or two dining passes for meals, snacks, drinks, etc. We each signed up for a credit card so got free lunch, drinks, snacks and butterbeer. We also used the flex passes which was a nice feature.

Universal has a few awesome rides: Dragon Challenge, Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey, Rock It, and Simpsons (only if you are in the front row). The other rides are just duplicates of each other with jerky movements. People rave about the Spiderman ride, but it is nothing special at all. You have no idea how Spiderman catches his foes and what you are witnessing. In the end, if I had waited an hour for the ride, I had an Express Pass so I only waited 5 minutes, I would have been really upset. For the cost of going to Universal, I would only do 2 days because it is small and seems quite fake.

Universal Studios is a great park with rides and attractions to suit the masses. It is an attractive park and fairly well laid out. However, handicap access is a bit tricky for some rides and would definitely be difficult for those in a wheelchair. Not really a great park for those not seeking thrills. Go to Disney.

Review on Universal Studios Florida. For a better review on Diagon Alley, please see my review under Wizarding World of Harry Potter.  My sister, my 10 year old son and I were in Florida for 5 days in early December before the Christmas holiday. We stayed at Cabana Bay and love it there! 2 biggest perks of staying at an onsite hotel 1-free shuttle to City Walk and 2-you can send your purchases back to the hotel if you don't want to carry it.  Our first day was on a Friday and we just explored Diagon Alley and then went over and spent the rest of the day in Islands of adventures. We didn't use our early morning entry, which was just fine with us. By the time we made it to the park around 9am most of the people were well gone. Not as many people in Diagon Alley when we got there.  We came back to Universal again the next day on Saturday in the afternoon. We had lunch outside of the park and then came inside. There were way more people on Saturday than on Friday. They were also starting the holiday parades this day, so I'm guessing there were way more people because of that. We actually weren't very interested in watching the parade so we walked around for a little while. We did the transformers ride then we tried to leave the area but ended up getting trapped by the parade and we ended up getting ice cream at Ben and Jerry's instead and just waited for the parade to be over. After the parade was over we ended up leaving the park because there were just way too many people for us to handle that day.  We came back again on Monday, which was our last day in Florida. There was less of a crowd on Monday. We knew we wanted to do the minion ride for sure but the line was 45 minutes long, so we decided to do some other rides first. We did the terminator show, which was probably the worst attraction of all. We also did the MIB one, which was a lot of fun. And we saw Dora, Diego and the Scooby Doo gang too! Shrek also was not the best. After that we went back to the minion ride and the wait was still 45 minutes so we just went ahead and waited. The wait actually wasn't too bad and the line moves pretty quickly. The wait was totally worth it and I can see why everyone wants to do this ride. It's really a lot of fun. One of the best rides in both of the parks.  We then decided it was time for lunch so we left for City Walk and had lunch there. If you don't mind leaving the park, this is a good option, the restaurants are not busy at all during lunch because everyone is still in the park. We also made a pit stop at guest services and got a "my first visit" pin and we also took pictures at the Universal Earth sign. After lunch my son really wanted to go back to our hotel to play in the pool. We had already done mostly everything already, with the exception of the pink donut. So I went back into the park by myself to get the pink donut. I thought maybe I would have to walk all the way back to the simpson's area, but I checked the big gift shop in the front first and I was very lucky to find one there! Our adventure is now complete!  We had a great time at Universal Studios! The first day of the holiday parade was a bit chaotic but other than that the crowd wasn't too bad. Plan and budget accordingly and have a great time! Fun for everyone!

When my husband told me that he had a conference in Orlando, I immediately thought Disney. Realized that we were staying at property near to Universal and wasn't sure it would be a good fit for our 7 year old kiddo. Wrong! It was fabulous for every member of our party! So much fun that we skipped Disneyworld and didn't feel deprived at all. Loved the usage of Universal's Express Pass, which blows FastPass out of the water. Traded our tix for season passes so we might return next year.

Universal Studios in Orlando is an excellent park with a wide variety of attractions. There truly is something for everyone here...not just the Harry Potter fan.  The rides are a good mixture of varying levels of thrill...there are rides for all types and age of visitor.

First, we are not theme park people. We would rather be hiking a trail enjoying nature, but this is an experience that's fun to let your kids experience - especially if they love Harry Potter! We did a 3 day park to park ticket and had plenty of time to get everything done - could have done 2 days, but the third was free. We were lucky that there was off and on rain the first day so crowds were low and we never really waited for any rides. Download the app so you can keep check on the wait times. It's helpful!

This was our first to Universal Florida having done California a few years ago. Overall a great experience, but you need at least 3 days which can be bit of a drag. The rides are great with the Transformers, the Harry Potter rides and Hogwarts being the highlights for us. All in all great fun.

from Dr Seuss to Marvel heros, there are endless rides of fun for all ages. The evening parade is not to be missed, lines are made tolerable with all kinds of activities while waiting and mostly under the shade.

This was my second time visiting Universal Studios in the past 7 months and I thoroughly enjoyed it yet again! The main reason for coming both times was The Wizarding World of Harry Potter -- Diagon Alley. This place was simply amazing and the attention to detail was perfect! The rest of Universal was pretty cool as well. I really enjoyed the Mummy ride and the Transformers ride. I would recommend going during the week to get the most for your money.

If you're looking for thrilling rides- roller coasters, 3-d rides, rides that immerse you in movies and such, Universal is one of the best. The Harry Potter world experience is simply amazing. If you're looking for nightlife City Walk is a good spot, lined with clubs and restaurants and it also has good shopping. The total experience though leaves something to be desired. Have found some staff to not only be unfriendly but downright rude. Don't expect top notch service.

I was shocked at how poor our experience was at this park. Most surprising is that Universal is 80% trinket shops and subpar eating establishments and only 20% rides and amusements. Signage is shockingly poor and there is almost no staff to help getting around. The park, in essence, is very poorly managed. Park tickets are expensive enough but Universal deems it necessary to charge a minimum of $20 for parking...I found this the final outrage. The only slightly positive was Diagone Alley which was an exact replica from the movie BUT it is really designed to sell overpriced trinkets (expect to spend a MINIMUM of $40 for a wand made in China). I would never return...I felt ripped-off from the moment I entered Unuversal to the moment I left. You've been warned!

My entire family agrees that this is one of the greatest places in the grand old USA! If you like amusement parks, this is the place to go. We have done both the US Disney Parks, which are great, but Universal blew us away. The Harry Potter "parks" and rides are as good as rides will ever get. Period. Then throw in all the other awesome rides, food, people, shows, characters, winner winner, chicken dinner! I would recommend staying on sight and getting the express passes, and then go tear the park up! Your kids will thank you! And they will never forget it!
My 1st experience and it was invigorating, Pulsating, every other great and alive name that can be placed here. I thoroughly enjoyed myself!
We spent the majority of our time in the Harry Potter world - which was very, very crowded (the rest of the park almost seemed deserted comparatively).

Our 9 & 11 year kids prefer Islands of Adventure, but they also enjoyed Universal Studios. The Harry Potter world is impressive. Kids had lots of fun in the ball factory in Curious George section. Minions were a hit as well. I am a fan of the Simpsons so I enjoyed Springfield and all the show references.
We waited 120 minutes for the Minion ride when the sign said 50 minutes. It was outrageous. They let hundreds of Express riders in, I have never seen so many.

This was our 1st visit to both Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure. You can do the parks in 2 days (even on Spring Break, if you are not that "into" Harry Potter stuff). We did 3 days and saw everything and rode several rides more than once. Park was clean and staff were Excellent and helpful. Not as crowded (less people with strollers, wheelchairs & scooters) around the park compared to Disney. We did stop by the younger children's area that was practically empty - beautiful play equipment with Barney theme, Curious George, etc. The Dr. Suess area is very cool too. On the 2nd day, we noticed that any 3D rides we went on started to effect us and made us nauseous easily so we had to slow down and stick to other rides like Rollercoaster, water rides, etc. but there doesn't seem to be too many. The Harry Potter section is crowded, you have to "try" the butter beer as it's popular and sweet. Don't be scared of the long line time that is displayed as you can always head to the single rider line and get on quicker. The park has Free lockers to put your bags in during the time you are on a ride so this is a nice feature. Finding characters to get pictures are pretty easy -- I think most of them are around between 10 am and 5 pm. One of the coolest rides is in Jurassic Park area that is like a zip line, but disappointed that it's only for 54" and under unless you are with a child. I'm sure the employees are tired of telling people that as it doesn't display it as you enter near that ride. Cute Parade around 5 pm and it's not crowded so you can see it easily without fighting for spot. The park closed at 8 pm with fireworks. Nothing extravagant as it ran a bunch of clips from movies while there were a few pops of fireworks and a little bit of water fountain..if you missed this, you aren't missing much.
We live this place always so much to do. Go EARLY to get on as many rides with a 10-15 minute wait. Lines start getting long after 1pm

Thorough enjoyed our visit to both Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure. After our first visit in the evening to go to CityWalk to look around, we decided that valet parking was well worth the price ($40) for two reasons: it's at the entrance to CityWalk and we wouldn't have to hunt for our car once we traveled the walking distance to the huge garage. You have to go through CityWalk to get to both parks. CityWalk has plenty of shopping, restaurants, and bar/lounges and it is a hot spot once the parks close for the evening. We spent a good deal of time at The Lone Palm Bar in front of Margaritaville. The bartenders gave us great advice on places to eat in Orlando -- The Brick House and Seasons 52 were our favorites.  Harry Potter is both parks were our favorites but Transformers and Spiderman were close seconds. Even though lockers as provided for the Harry Potter Gringotts Ride, take your camera or smart phone (if you have a secure pocket) so you can take pictures along the way as there is much to see. Even though there was a 30 minute wait to the ride, all the walking lines take you through various areas that are entertaining so the "line" really doesn't seem like 30 minutes.  Lockers at the entrance at both parks cost $10/day but if you have a change of clothes or coats for when the sun goes down, this is worth the price rather than having to lug them around or go back to your car to retrive them. Lockers at Harry Potter rides are free, but the lockers by the water rides -- Dudley Do Right and Popeye -- are not free ($4)  For us smokers it was a nice surprise that both parks have several designated smoking areas. Our favorite smoking respite from the crowds was Universal Studios Park across from the Monster Café --This is aminiature version of Central Park located in the New York backlot area.  Definitely will be going back next year as Jurassic Park Ride was closed while we were there and next year The Hulk and King Kong rides should be up and running by then.

a visit to Diagon Alley is worth the price of the ticket alone (and be sure to get the combo ticket, so you can ride the Hogwarts express to the other side!-and if you have time, ride it twice-its a slightly different experience each way). In Diagon Alley, visit so many great things, like the Knight Bus, Ollivanders, Weasley's Wizarding Wheezes, the Magical Menagerie, and Knockturn Alley. The coolest part of this section is easily Gringotts Bank. Outside, there is a HUGE dragon that breaths fire. Inside, on the way to the ride, you walk through the lobby of Gringotts (which is so cool), then the ride itself is so cool...hard to describe but totally worth it, even if you arent normally a ride person. there are lots of other great spots to visit within the park- including Moe's Bar from the Simpsons, the Terminator Experience (which is really cool!) and so much more.

The park was a messy. Garbage for all place. Staff rude and the restroom at Jurrasic park was so dirty that was impossible to be used. The park was crowded and the wait time does not correrponded to the real time that you must to wait. In an attraction that was marked 60 minutes the wait time lasted even for 2 hours. People in the Express way went on and out repeatedly in the same attraction as the other people who were on the waiting list and does not paid for the express way but also paid for the ticket were let aside. In eight hours at the park I was able to visit just 4 attractions . It was a waste of time and money and I felt stupid. Universal Orlando Resort?? Never more. Já fui algumas vezes a este parque, mas desta vez ele estava imundo, mal sinalizado e os atendentes se portavam de forma absolutamente rude. Os banheiros do food court do Jussaric Parque estavam tao sujos que era impossivel usa-los. Não bastasse isto no sistema de express way adotado por eles as pessoas entram e saem de um brinquedo repetidas vezes passando na frente daquele que se encontram na fila de espera e se nao pagaram por este passe pagaram seu ingresso no parque que nao é barato: 100 dolares. É um desperdicio de tempo e dinheiro. A proposito, o expresso do Harry Porter é ABSOLUTAMENTE ridiculo, não vale a espera de mais de uma hora. Voce entra numa cabine e simplesmente passa um filminho na janela do trem, absolutamente sem emoção.

We went to Universal Orlando over March Break and visited both Understand parks. It was Mardi Gras and the park offered additional events and concerts including Fall Out Boy, Adam Lambert and Shawn Mendes. The rides are well suited to teenagers and adults. If you like thrills be sure to take in Revenge of the Mummy, Rip Ride and Transformers. They have taken 3D rides to another level and I would be surprised if the majority of your party weren't left feeling dizzy by the end of the day. Even the Despicable Me Minion Mayhem was fun! Other parks clearly offer more giant roller coasters and adrenaline, but I think Universal has the right mix of entertainment and fun for teenagers and adults alike.
was our first time in the park and our experience was awesome all the staff in the park was very helpful and friendly , we had a lot of fun see you soon guys thank you for everything

Travelled with a group of friends & our 11 month old baby. Was a bit worried about the practicabilities of it, but found it to be so baby friendly. There is child swap available, meaning that you don't have to queue twice. The child swap rooms often have the film of the ride playing & changing facilities.
We like Universal a lot because we are Minion fans. Even though the park gets very busy, the Unlimited Express helps shorten ride waits. The best way to go is to get a VIP tour

This is a great theme park for kids of all ages as well as adults! Harry Potter World is great fun. The movie themed rides are great if you've seen the films or not. The dining is great and the shops are great for souvenirs. BE AWARE though: Express pass does NOT include ANY of the Harry Potter rides, The Hogwarts Express, or the Pteranodon Fliers. All in all a great park for everyone!

Loved this place! A full day of fun! What was great: so many people working there to make your experience a thrilling one. We've been to both Universal Studios in LA and here, well, this one has a unique charm of it's own. It's bigger, more people, but it still very enjoyable. What was not so great: i was looking to get my tickets online beforehand and was told by a friend not to worry and just the tickets there. Which i did ((( and ended up paying $50 more per ticket at the door. So make sure you show up there with the tickets...

I took my daughter and her friend to Orlando for two days over spring break, and Universal jacks up pricing to $166 per person, and that doesn't include FAST pass. When I tried to upgrade to fast past, they wanted another $114 per person! That's ridiculous and should be reported to the BBB or some state agency for price gouging, it was spring break, not New Year's Eve or Christmas week! spring break is about 3 weeks in March depending on what school and level, and these are middle school girls. The parks are great, and the Harry Potter ride is fun, but the Hulk is under construction and two other rides had malfunctions and were out for more than a couple of hours, so did they give us money back, heck no! The good is lousy, unless you go to Finnegan's and have lunch. Otherwise fast food done poorly, and long lines and high prices. Overall, it was nearly 10 years since I last visited, likely another 10 before I go back and by then you will need a loan! The hotel is cheaper than the theme park!

Pros: The rides at Universal are better than Disneyworld parks. The Express pass is worth buying as you do get through lineups much quicker than everyone else. we went the first week of Spring break so the parks were very busy. There are also more fast/exciting rides at Universal and an assortment for all ages. The restaurant choices and food choices were also better than Disneyworld. The Star wars venues were awesome and there are characters with very realistic costumes and they interact with the crowds for pictures. Harry Potter was also an excellent attraction and our twin girls (16) absolutely loved the shops and HP venues. Cons: Prepare to take out a mortgage to be able to go. By the time we paid for hotel, flights, 3 meals per day, souvenirs, drinks, etc, the trip was very expensive and the food and drinks everywhere at the parks are very expensive. Want a Beer? $9 dollars USD which is about $12 Canadian so be prepared to have a lot of cash. As mentioned, the Express pass is great, but again, you have to spend money for these as they are $50 per person. Disneyworld is free for Fast passes, but limited to the number of rides and choices at the parks. Fountain water at universal is good, but Disney parks, the fountain water tastes like sulphur, so you will want to buy your own water at Disney. Lineups were atrocious as it was spring break. 1.5 hours for some rides if you did not buy an express pass. The lineups are all cattle gates with no sit down areas at most rides...your feet hurt and there are no washrooms or benches/seats at most of these lines. they could do better. Go early and hit the rides first that you want to go on, then do sight seeing and shopping for souvenirs after. There are FREE shuttles from pretty much every hotel to take you to either Disney or Universal. each hotel has an itinerary with their personalized schedule. ask for this when you arrive at your hotel.

Having trawled the internet we got a package which gave us 2 days in Studios and 2 days in Islands of adventure for $330 dollars for the 2 of us. On three occasions the accommodation we were staying in offered free shuttles to and from the parks. We drove just the once which was very easy with sat nav. Parking is $20. We were there during Mardi Gras on a Saturday and watched a very colourful procession with strings of beads being thrown into the audience. Kool and the Gang provided live music once the parade had finished- all included in entry price. The rides were of varying types. Roller coaster, trains, merry go rounds and a lot of 3 and 4D experiences. Queueing times can be up to 90 minutes on the more extreme rides and anything to do with Harry Potter. You can buy a fast pass but do not know how much this is as we did no bother as we knew we had return visits. If you can take your own food as snacks are expensive and time will be wasted sitting in restuarants. Note you cannot take alcohol into the site it will be confiscated at bag search. -it is a law of the Orlando Police Department or the OPD as like to be known as.
Expect to be entertained at Universal! My protip is to explore the park on the first day, then grab a fast pass for half price after 4pm and avoid all the queues, well worth doing.
We had a wonderful, nostalgic time acting like kids all over again. Good food at the local eats places too! A great trip; not to be missed.

A few newer attractions, including this amazing up and over roller coaster, but the place is getting a bit tired. It still has ET and Terminator attractions---and not many fans. Rides need updating--had problems with sound at both those older attractions. Has a new Harry Potter Diagon Alley in the back which was great--visually it's amazing and you have to ride the Hogwarts Express train to Islands (You need to have the correct theme park admission to both parks--be sure to ask when buying tickets)

So my wife and I are both about 60 years young. And indeed, our whole purpose for going was to pay a visit to Harry Potter. And we were not disappointed with Diagon Alley and Hogwoarts. But the rest of BOTH the parks.... we were satisfied after only one day. I could see spending maybe two days there. But if it is slow season, one day might even be enough.

First and most likely last time at Universal. The parks were ok and they do have some neat rides although too many of them are simulator rides in my opinion. Unlike Disney you have to pay for an Express pass unlike the free Fast Pass you get at Disney and even they we saw people lined up for an hour in the Express Pass lines. Food outlets were a gong show, none of them are organized at all. It's like it's everyone's first day on the job. Staff were unenthusiastic and clearly just there to collect a paycheck. Several rides had 2+ hour lines and a couple other rides kept breaking down. I understand it was March break but I think they could be doing a better job. Grounds staff are not keeping the park clean, I walked by the same discarded beer can three days in a row. If you have never been to Universal it's worth going once but it you are choosing between Universal and Disney. Go Disney, Universal has a long way to go before they meet Disney standards.

Love love universal!! How can anyone give them a bad review?? Universal is amazing and wonderful for anyone from young to old. Amazing stimulators rides. In fact I wished king kong, jaws,and back to the future were here. A little pricey with very few discounts. I would recommend that coming here on off season. Very crowded
This is a very fun park to visit for adults and kids, great shows and plenty of rides and attractions

We did enjoy the rides we were able to get on. We bought 3 day passes. However we still didn't get to see everything. We can't believe that they charge 40.00 for express passes EXCEPT during vaca and spring breaks. then they charged $150.00, that's right 150.00 for one pass for one day. So try to plan your trip so you don't get robbed. Also don't fall for the premium parking. The first day we paid the extra. The next day we paid reg. and our parking was 2 levels up. All it saved us was 2 escalator rides. Not sure this was worth the trip.

I make it my business to come here every year for Halloween horror nights. I've made it a tradition since 2009. I always go on a Friday but last year I went on a Saturday for the first time. If you are not purchasing express passes be ready to wait in line for 1-2+ hours, your feet & back will hurt. Harry potter world was open for the first time during HHN this past oct I last visited universal & islands of adventure in dec 2014. Harry potter world made my entire trip. ticketsatwork offer good deals such as buy a 2/3 day ticket park pass & get 1 day free. Express pass are not needed if you have muliple days to frequent the parks

Enjoyed a visit with family and Universal has the details down for this park. Amazing attention to details and perfect for all ages. Need to work on people movement and better systems for handling large crowds. Didn't like having to keep track of tickets the whole time and pulling them in and out so much.

This was an amazing night filled with fun and excitement we came here for birthday dinner visited a few places The surrounding were clean Well lit Alot of activities for children The food was amazing ambiance was priceless I totally enjoyed my time here I will definitely do this again ❤❤❤

Loved this Park of the 4 we visited in Florida. We did the express pass for one time. It was expensive but worth it as we were able to ride every ride In The park. It cost $358 for 3. My favorites were Transformers, Despicable Me, the Simpsons, the Mummy, and Harry Potter.

We had a blast riding rides all around the park. Let me just say that if you are subject to motion sickness DO NOT get on the Despicable Me ride. It made me so sick. I had cold sweats and thought I was going to vomit. It is not like the other motion rides. You are sitting, but the only thing that really moves is the 3D screen. It moves a little but is not a track ride like most others and combined with the 3D = No Bueno for me. MIB is old ride but still very cool. Woody Woodpecker coaster was fun. ET was awesome. I got my 8 yr old to ride Rip Ride ROCK IT roller coaster and it was so awesome. It was his first scary roller coaster and he said it was fun, it was scary and he didn't want to do it again.
One of the newest attractions at Universal Studios, they did such an amazing job , just like the what you saw in the "Harry Potter" movies. Definitely a don't miss

Universal studios in Orlando has added some great new things that definitely makes the visit worth it! The new wizarding world of harry potter is phenomenal! It is a great time. I really love the train ride between parks. It is very unique and has cool visual effects. Keep in mind that in order to do this you have to purchase the ticket that is multi park. If you like simulators, the minion mayhem, transformers and harry potter rides are fun. I still enjoy the Shrek show. This place is great for all ages and definitely family friendly. My favorite roller coaster is the Mummy. The transformers ride is very well done! You will have a good time.

The customer service is top-notch. The parks are beating Disney hands-down right now when you consider the level of detail - especially at Harry Potter. The rides are 2nd to none. Our family went on an 8 day trip to Disney and spent one of the days at Universal and we all regretted not planning for more. My 9 and 10 year old nieces and nephews couldn't stop talking about it. It blew them away. Personally, I think the Harry Potter rides are the best amusement rides I have ever been on. Wow! I was truly impressed with what this place has done. I thought there would be no way Disney could be beat.

Such a shame we were looking forward to visiting this park but found the staff ignorant! Rude! And totally unfriendly! Ride times were over 100 mins! As we stayed in a resort hotel we entered park at 7am to get to Harry Potter section of park but even so the place soon filled up! Beware Wizarding World of Harry Potter was so over priced! Had a drink of Duff and the server refused to serve us again because we didn't leave a tip after the first one!! Ha ha saved us a fortune that day!! Park was littered and had filthy toilets which had run out of toilet paper by early afternoon. Seemed the characters were outdated as my daughter only recognised the Simpsons and minions! The only saving grace was the Leaky Couldron which served a lovely English Breakfast! If only they didn't serve a cousant with it?

Universal Studios was by far my favorite over the 2 parks, however, get the park hopper. We got 4 day park hopper tickets and by day four, we had ridden every single ride and seen most shows at both parks. Tips: -Get the Universal Express passes, they are worth every penny, especially if you are going during peak season. (Check w/ Orlando uncover to see) Our family of 6 stayed at the resort and Express passes are included in your stay on site EXCEPT for Cabana Bay. -Buy a lanyard for your Express pass. I cannot stress this enough. Lanyards are $8.95 and come in every theme & color you can think of. It will save you time at each ride, and if you're staying on site, you can charge things to your room key. I never took my wallet or purse into the park! -Take lots and lots of water! Everyday, we took at least 8 water bottles and snacks and the gate staff was okay with that. -Wear tennis shoes. Trust me. We walked 10 miles plus per day, and I'm so happy I listened to a fellow trip advisor. There are only a handful of water rides, & we packed flips flops just for that purpose. Comfortable footwear is the key! -For cheap, non greasy eats, Bumble Man's taco truck wins hands down. (Lards Lad Donuts take the cheapest indulgence snack!) Best Shows to see... Horror Make-Up show, Animal Actors and Fear Factor live!! ET was by far our favorite ride, because it was one of last authentic rides left in the parks. Ride to skip.... The Simpsons Ride- Idk if it was meant to seem cheap w/ crappy graphics to fit the genre of Krustyland, but it worked. Everyone in our family got sick & my husband committed & spent the rest of the night in bed.  Don't forget to catch the 9:45pm water and light show. It will blow your mind as you watch years or cinema moments projected on a cascading water screen. Best seats in front of the smoking section front of Mel's Diner, besides the Transformers Ride. Get there by 9 to save your spots!

Long lasting family memories are created spending time on places like this,Chicken fingers at Mel's drive in are awesome, during daytime most of the rides has long lines, about 1 hour wating time, after 7pm lines are shorter for all rides, and after 9pm the get low to 15min and some just 5min. so take your day slowly and enjoy the rides late night
Our toddler was awe struck by the minions and Shrek. She loved the Nemo ride and all the characters. Loads of fun.
The Wizarding World of Harry Potter is a must for all fans. Muggles or magic folk alike. If you have anyone in your family that loves Harry, you must take this trip.

We went here and Islands of adventure on a 3d park pass. This only got 1 of our days and was enough. A bit more dated than Islands and no water rides. Hulk roller coaster was down (will be for months) so we unfortunately didn't get a chance to try that one. Our favorite ride was Transformers!

We were kids here! What a great time! It's fun to have a date day/ night at this park. We went on most rides. I would tell everyone, if you can afford it, express pass is a MUST. Avoiding time standing pays itself back with interest!!!! We did Islands of Adventures last year. Both parks are just as amazing. Again: buy express pass!!

We just lived the whole experience at Universal, and much preferred their Express pass system to the so called fast pass experience at Disney. We went to the Saturday night Mardis Gras parade and party . Brilliant! We loved it! Great staff too!
Truly AMAZING job with the Harry Potter attraction at Universal! We were lost in the attraction- so many things to look at and do and see!!! HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!
Absolutely fantastic a must for the young old you wont be disappointed,although the lines are long for some of the more popular rides it is well worth the wait.
Kids love going to these parks - all are so much fun! We need to get down here more often, but when we do...too much of a good time! Recommend to all!

March 31st, 2016.  Geared towards adults, but this time we have a little one and we were really pleased with the child swap option at some of the popular rides. This was super useful. There were also a couple of child friendly areas like Dr Seuss, Curious George and a few play structures. We came by the end of March (spring break) and no need for Express passes).  I'm not big on the Potter books or movies but I have to say what universal did was truly amazing. It is a must see for everyone but if you are into Harry Potter your going to love universal!  All around Universal is one of the best amusement parks and has some of the best rides and themes. If you are visiting Orlando I would suggest going to Universal.

If it weren't for the Wizarding World, I would think that Universal wasn't worth the trip. The Wizarding World really is amazing and the rides there are some of the most enjoyable I have ever rode on. The rest of the park though just isn't as amazing as I would have hoped for being that I have to travel a bit to get to Orlando. They all tend to feel outdated/not updated/such a weird mix of themes. Truthfully, whenever I return to Orlando in the future, I would just get a day pass for The Wizarding World and then go to Disney World for the remainder of the trip.

Universal has two parks next to each other. Both have amazing rides, shows, entertainment and food. You can buy a single or multi park ticket-the latter allows travel between the two parks on the Harry Potter express. If the parks are busy, an express pass is available so you avoid the ride queues, although these are expensive, so use the internet blogs to find the quiet days.Ideally as a first time visitor allow at least one day for each park, and wear good, comfortable footwear. Enjoy!

Didn't really get to grips with this place (sure I'm in the minority). Being Easter beak it was busy but not, I suspect, what it would be in summer.  Ridiculous locker system before most of the rides. (Go with someone who hates rides and happy to hold bags! ) you queue to get a locker for your bag before queuing for the ride, the. Queue / fight way back to get to locker!  Ride queues were huge. Fast passes cost a fortune.  Not sure if smells were 4d experiences, but it was not pleasant. Toilets were filthy, I suspect the mop being used to clean floor was merely spreading spillage around! Not pleasant at all (or was I just spoilt at Disney).  I like Harry Potter as much as the next person, but stunned at how obsessed some people are!!

Hi visited over the busy Easter period so some allowances need to be made for the big crowds. Both parks provide some good rides and even allowing for busy time the lines werent to bad. Bit of overdosing on the retail outlets. Biggest gripe was the breakdowns perhaps we were unlucky but 5 in one day inc. 2 complete shutdowns was very frustrating. Most staff very pleasant but equally some very abrupt.

Came here as a party of 6 ready for a great day of fun... Which it was, mostly. 2 of the kids didn't have skip passes so I bought them at the gate, and was sad to see they were more expensive because of Grad Nite... Okay fine. I bought them and we went in. Everything was going fine...eventually we made our way to the next park and continued the fun. At 6:00 we were told we had to leave, the parks were closing for an event. What? There was no mention of this when we bought our full priced tickets, no mention when we got on the shuttle in the morning, no mention when I paid EXTRA for (2 hours short) skip passes. Thousands of dollars spent between the 6 of us, extra money for skip passes (like double price) because of the event just to be kicked out before the event begins 2 hours before the park closes!? It completely threw our evening off and I just don't understand...we will definitely take our thousands of dollars somewhere that appreciates our business next time. Fun... But not worth it.

The superheroes and minion really spent quality time with my son. Captain America actually remembered his name by the after the second time of seeing him. We saw him a total of 4 times and each time he really talked to us. The minion was great - danced around with us, the stood for pictures.

Park is great but Universal and Islands of Adventure need to do something about the crowds in the Harry Potter area such as giving a specific time to visit this area. The interactive wands are incredible but cost over $100 for two kids and then to stand around and wait in lines in front of store windows to use them is just a waste of time when it is limited. We only spent time in this area later in the day when the crowds had died down but the rest of the park has some rides that are not to be missed.

We had a great time here , it was busy but did manage to get the kids on some rides, the only poor bit was Harry Potter which I reviewed separately as so disappointed with , they also had quite a lot of street entertainment and we meet a few characters unlike Disney , they seem to have something for everyone
I love this park! Lots for the whole family to do! So awesome that the characters walk around and you can get your photos taken with them. I will definitely return to this park next year :)

Went for the day, only went to the one park which we easily saw all we wanted to on the day. The kids loved Diagon Alley and all the Harry Potter themed stuff (they loved using their interactive wands!) The Dragon is spectacular perched on one of the buildings breathing fire every 10 or 15 minutes.  You have to go on the Transformers ride, was the best one by our opinion. The kids loved Escape from Gringotts and The Mummy ride as well.

Universals original park doesent fail to thrill with lots of fun thrilling attractions to visit and ride on its a magical place to be in and has my very favourite ride/attraction the escape from gringotts in Diagon Alley definitely blows everything else out the water for me

Three days in the park is perhaps one day too many. We loved both Harry Potter areas in the park....thank you Universal. The rest was take it or leave it. Was there with the kids 20 years ago; some of the rides have been retooled with modern themes (makes sense). The 3D rides are all very similar in the ride (obvious movie theme different). Soda refill was a good value but carrying the cup is a hassle  Many rides for safety precautions require empty pockets; which means using the dreaded locker rooms. Universal you need to figure out a better system; particularly in the areas of Harry Potter attractions. I did not mind the lockers; but the rooms are overcrowded and shoulder to shoulder. Suggest one way flow of traffic and encourage one person per party to use the lockers.  Safety never a concern at the park  Family friendly.  Staff at park extremely helpful and friendly.  I do suggest to families to eat at the restaurants and avoid the hot dog type vendors. Restaurant offer a better value, better food, a seat, cold water etc.

It's been a few years since we have been to Universal and they have added so much there. Harry Potter Diagon Alley was great, and liked the Hogwarts Express train ride that takes you to Islands of Adventure. Don't miss the Blues Brothers in the New York section of Universal, it was really great. The park is huge and overwhelming at times especially on the weekends. My favorite park is still SeaWorld Orlando though. It is more of a family park and less crazy and you don't have to wait hours for the shows and rides.

So much to do, you could spend a week here. Activities for all ages, the 3D rides are fantastic, we particularly liked Spiderman and Harry Potter. We went over Easter, but didn't have to queue to long on most rides. As usual in these places, the food and drink is well over priced, and there is a 'Gift Shop' on every corner, but despite this all in all we had a great time here. I would recommend going in the evening time as well, there is a different 'vibe'.

I visited the park twice in the evening and didn't feel this is a park that creates a sense of contemporary delight. Most of the stuff look ancient. For the Harry Potter portion, the color was on the dark side, making it a little bit depressing.  However, I saw the daytime photos of this park people posted and found that they are bright, vivid and cheerful. Therefore, I think the best time to visit the park is daytime not night time if you like to be amused.

My teen and I came here primarily to experience Universal for three days with Disney for one. Full transparency: I am not an amusement-park person but I have a teenager so...my expectation was we would be "bored" with Disney as too baby-ish and would really love Universal. It was rather the opposite. Yes, the Harry Potter attractions are done very well. However, on our last day, after 30 minutes in line, the Escape from Gringott's had some sort of delay-they could not tell you for how long-after the second announcement of the delay, without an estimate of when it would be resolved, we left the line, never experiencing it. The employees do not seem as well-trained as the Disney employees, there were a couple of off comments-nothing too bad, but one employee in costume that I was chatting with asked if I had flown my broom over. Really? Again, this would not happen with Disney employees. Also saw a guest who was a Kim Kardashian wannabee parading around with half of her posterior hanging out of her romper. People were pointing and laughing. It was funny and sad. Disney has "appropriate dress code" signage, don't know if they enforce it. Also many of the rides are too crazy for my middle-aged body. My kid loved it but we both were nauseous after the second Dragon rollercoaster ride. You really feel like you are flying on a dragon! Keep in mind-you might love it. But for me, it was the opposite of my expectations. And the gift shops everywhere are annoying-you see the same old stuff. LOVED the Simpsons ride, though-we went back to ride it a second time. Horror makeup show was very well-done, really enjoyed that. The audience participation made it extra fun, the guys who perform it are excellent. Would have preferred to do Universal for 1 day and Disney for 3, rather than the other way around.

Not cheap with an express pass but worth every penny. Awe inspiring rides and experiences. Took our 9 and 7 year old boys - they absolutely loved every second. We had a dual park pass (to include Islands of Adventure) and set aside two days actually - a single day for the two would have been fine especially with a little planning and a early concerted start.  Total standout was Harry Potter and the Escape from Gringotts - frankly jaw droppingly well done - no fast pass available for this so go very first thing otherwise expect a 120 min wait. Minions and Transformers also very good as was Simpsons "Crusty" ride.  Good tip to take an early lunch just outside at the dual park entrance - better selection of food. Fantastic day that frankly puts everything Disney into the shade.

I'm not going to lie, my boyfriend and I picked Universal Studios over Walt Disney World because of Wizarding World of Harry Potter. But we were pleasantly surprised. We went on a Friday morning/afternoon. Wait for rides were less than 15 minutes. Rides were interactive with lots of special effects (example: pyrotechnics). Of course, Wizatding World of Harry Potter - Diagon Alley was awesome! Not big, kind of small with one ride and a few shops. We ate at Leaky Cauldron, which was delicious (but pricey, of course). We were able to do/see everything we wanted within five hours. Although, we didn't visit Islands of Adventure.

Really fun for all ages!!! Many shows and interesting places & food. Cartoon costumes every where! Good for children and adult who love them. The place is big i recommend to take a day to all the studio universal and attend to some shows!
We had a wonderful time during the spring break season. The express passes were well worth the price. We never waited longer than five minutes for any ride. Highly recommend!

Something for everybody, fun, fun and more fun. Adults and young ones can spend hours of great entertainment with all the live parades, comic books superheroes, cartoons and movie figures. There are rides and attractions for kids and adults. Great restaurants, sports bars, movie theaters, live shows , day or night. Spend the day at the park or just hang out with friends at night. Amazing fun anytime!👍👍

We liked that you could walk into shops with a drink, and there is so much to enjoy even if you don't take in the rides. Unfortunately we did go on a Harry Potter ride at Wizarding world and both of us were sick for 45 min. after the ride, never again!!! So much to do an little time, we would return and be a little wiser.

It's amazing how much this park has changed since I first set foot in it back in the early 90s. That being said, I still have a blast whenever I do go. The attractions are top notch, food is good, even just walking around is fun. If only they'd kept Back to The Future. And Jaws. Sigh.  At least Diagon Alley is a great addition. The Hogwarts Express is awesome too.

If you are done making your rounds on the Peter Pan ride in Magic Kingdom and have had your fill of the Wizarding World of Harry Potter (if one can have their fill of that theme park) then you have to check out Universal Studios which I like to call the adult theme park. The rides here are geared more towards the young teenager/older crowd and it's a lovely break from the Disney madness. The shows like Shrek are also just as fun as riding rides like the Hulk, Spider Man and Transformers. Transformers is the best out of all of those three! Best thing about the park is that right outside are all the restaurants and shops, serving alcohol! Not only can you spend the whole day there riding the rides but you can cap off an amazing day with a lovely dinner and a drink.

All of universal is amazing. My family preferred universal parks to the Disney parks. Simpsons ride is really good. If you have a disabled guest with you you can get a ticket at guest services and go to a ride you want and they will write you a time to come back so you don't have to queue. Disney didn't offer this service. Had to queue for hours with wheelchair there. Blues brothers were brilliant! Such a great place.

We went as a company of 3 moms and 4 kids ages 12-18. Took multi parks tickets (buy 2 get 3rd day free from Undercover Tourist). Covered almost all of Island of adventures on day 1, Universal studio on day 2 and the rides that we liked the most on the last day. Suggestions: - use single rider lines when it's a long wait. Either way you not talking to your party when you are on the ride and it saves a lot of time waiting. You will be together anyway until you get to the entry point. - have a rain poncho for the water rides and flip-flops, you will get very wet. - use Universal studio app on the phone and check waiting times before planning what you do next - arrive early and use most popular rides then or during lunch when most people go for a lunch - turkey legs are THE MUST

Me & my son had a blast once again in Universal Studios-Island of Adventure theme park. The wait times in April or good nothing longer than 35 min...The crowd was not over whelming & the weather was just right..Just wish him & I was able to witness the new King Kong attraction this summer & the Hulk rollercoaster that is being reconditioned.But other than that everything else was great..being that my son is older now he really got a feel of all the rides.Last time he was just a pup running me around in Kiddie land.

Adults and kids alike loved it. We did not do the meal plan and were glad. The few places you could use the meal plan were very crowded and there weren't very many of them. Great park with great rides. If you're not a thrill seeker, there are plenty of "limited motion" rides that are basically stationary or semi-stationary seats with hydraulics that make you feel like you're in motion.

So much hype for these theme parks over the years I have grown up, finally at 27 I was able to make a visit to the universal areas. I was expecting something unlike any other theme park I had been to and it just didn't deliver. Yes attendants and the weather at the park were better than most but the rides were often pretty lame with a couple of exceptions, one being the Harry Potter areas which were better than most as well as being able to ride the hogwarts express. But I can get all this back home without the cost, is the extra £600+ cost of getting over to the states for the weather worth it when you can see all this in the UK?  Also never seen so many food outlets in one area before, they must have outnumbered all the rides and games put together.

This place is amazing.  It has two main feature park attractions, both are fantastic.  I prefer this place to Disney land.  We must have visited this place on 4 days out of the 10 days of our holiday!!!  There are many rides, attractions, theatrics, restaurants, bars, snack joints, ice cream parlours and much more.  There are rides and attractions for all ages, something for everyone.  After a fun packed day, I enjoyed the dinners we had at bubba grump shrimp and hardrock cafe in particular.  This is a must do !!
Great rides, fun for all ages. Lots of walking, plenty of food choices. Nice memorabilia for purchase.
Was able to see and do almost everything in both parks in two days. The large crowds are in Harry Potter so the rest of the park is pretty empty

We love to visit Universal Studios Florida. I just do not like the two separate parks. Universal Hollywood seems to be a better bargain. But we HAD to see the new Harry Potter attractions. It was worth it. You feel as though you are at Hogwart's. It is amazing and the rides are awesome and so real. The other attractions are also a blast. We love the ET, Men in Black, The Mummy, The Rock'n'Roll rollercoaster, all of the attractions and shows are Great - you have got the meet Shrek, the Donkey and the Transformers along with all of the other characters. It's worth the trip.
The Simpsons ride was our absolute favourite. Myself and my girls went on the 3D ride every time we visited the park.

The "Forbidden Journey" ride at (Harry Potter area) Universal Studios, Florida, is unlike any other ride in the world. The combination of state-of-the-art technology and story is astounding. And now there is an easier way to get on the ride! The wait for this ride can often be two or three hours; and some of that time will be in punishing sunshine. But now Universal has taken another tip from Disney and instituted a "Singles Only" line. If you do not care who you ride with, this singles line will get you on the ride within minutes on a slow day, and witrhin a half-hour on the worst of days. Yes, you do miss most of the atmosphere of the waiting line inside Hogwarts; but you GET ON THE RIDE SOONER. Go for it.

I took my girls to Universal mostly for Harry Potter World. Let me just say...It was AWESOME! The look on my girl's faces when we walked through the brick wall in Diagon Alley was pricless! We loved the books and to see the books you love so much come to life is an expression that has no words. From the continuous music to the food and the people working in the shops and the ones playing characters, it was truly prefect! The Butterbeer was everything I dreamed it would be! And the rides were unforgettable! Definitely a must even if you aren't a Harry Potter fan. This place has fun for everyone.

We r doing a road trip of Florida & our last stop is Orlando. I'm really not into theme parks but my husband wanted to visit Universal studio's so as we have done great shopping I had to agree. We looked at booking tickets before we left the UK but so glad we didn't. Got here & had some great offers on-line. Had lots of 'discount offers' from kiosks in hotels, shopping centres etc. Found the tickets we wanted direct just booked the day before. Brilliant rides, well run & really great fun!!! I'm converted, definitely worth a visit .
We had a a great time brought kids of all ages. Lines can be very long but its definitely worth it if you have never been. Kids really enjoyed the characters walking around. This is a must
Loved universal studios Florida, my partner and I went for my birthday and had a fantastic time going on all of the rides and getting pictures and just enjoying ourselves highly recommend

I hadn't been to Universal studios since the days of 'King Kong' and 'Jaws!' Wow, it has changed...and it us just as great as ever! There is a lot to do if you love rides and Harry Potter. We are huge 'Simpsons' fans who are addicted to the ' Simpsons Tapped Out' game, so we were in our glory!! Absolutely our favorite!!! Lots of fun shops, games, restaurants, rides and live entertainment. Shrek 4D was fun too! As my family is not huge ride fans, we didn't venture over to 'Islands of Adventure." But that looked just as exciting. My only one one 'negative' was security going in. There was little organization and it took over 30 minutes to get through it. Lines needed the dividers so folks knew where to stand. Not sure if all parks security is this chaotic because of metal detectors now, or because there was no organization and folks just confused. Other than that, excellent!

The parks are next door to each other and I started in Universal Studios. The rides here are generally either big rollercoasters or 3D / 4D experiences. Most of the rides are good but I'd especially pick out The Mummy which is a smaller indoor rollercoaster with some great fire effects, and Diagon Alley, Escape from Gringotts. In fact, Diagon Alley is an amazing addition to the park and well worth a visit although it's very crowded (even when you're not there at peak times). One of the best things is that you can now catch the Hogwarts Express from Universal Studios to Islands of Adventure which is a real bonus... no need to walk back up to the entrance and switch parks. A brilliant, brilliant idea. Overall Universal is well worth a visit, it's fun, it's clean and the rides are great. One comment I have is that as most of the rides are 3D, you can get a little nauseous after going on a few in a row. The second is that there aren't too many healthy eating options. Other than that, it's a wonderful day out.

We took a quick 4 day vacation. Used 1 day in Universal! Wow what a place!! It's so beautiful and you seriously become a kid all over again! We had a blast! Too bad you pay so much to get in and everything in the park is so expensive! Give people a break somewhere! A bottle of water shouldn't be $4.50!

This was my first time at universal studios. We bought the hopper, unlimited skip the line pass which is pricy but we were only here for a day so it saved us hours of time. It's not cheap but if your time is important you might want to think about it. I really loved universal.

We went with 2 pre-teens and we all had tons of fun. After the long lines at Disney and all the walking there, this park felt like a real vacation. Wait lines were not very long. If there are long lines go back at lunch time. Harry Potter had a line up of 45 minutes. We had lunch at 11:30 am. When we checked back closer to noon the wait time had changed to 10 minutes. The little parades throughout the day are cute with famous characters like Minions and Sponge Bob. Great photo opportunities for kids there. If you are using a taxi download the Uber app. It is way cheaper than Mears and the like. I wish I had known earlier. We would have saved some money. Overall, I would go back for sure.
Too much to do in only one day but excellent experience. Too long queues to get in needs improving. Once inside really good with a very good parade.
Great rides here too! Avoid Despicable Me, the line is not worth it. Other than that, fantastic rides. Be sure to get a two park pass to be able to ride the Hogwarts Express, which is incredible!

Universal Studios has far surpassed Disney in every way. Customer service, staffing, cleanliness and fun. Every staff member smiled, asked if we were having fun, asked how they could help, knew the park and smiled always. The express pass was easy and priceless. The park was clean and the food was very very good no matter where we ate. The rides were way too fun. We gave up some of our "free" days of relaxing because the parks were way too much fun to miss.

If you have older kids or if you are an older "kid", this is the place for you. I thoroughly enjoyed myself. My recommendations are Shriek, Terminator, The Horror Make-up Show (it's hilarious) and the Simpson's. You can spend the whole day and not see and fully enjoy everything, so get a two-day pass!!!

We spent one day at each park, no need for anymore. Disappointed that Hulk coaster was closed, it's the key ride in Islands of adventure . Other rides were good but warning the Jurassic Pk water ride you get soaked in the front . Also the log flume and family tube ride you leave looking like you took a shower in your clothes, good thing it was a hot day, but still not very comfortable to walk around soaked. Harry Potter rides were good. Worst part of many rides is putting things continually in lockers, many times totally not needed, same type rides in Disney you are not required to get lockers. Regular Universal side was fun , but a lot of Car , virtual reality type rides, after a couple it wasn't really fun anymore. Two roller coasters which were good . The photo pass photographers were hard to find. Food was more expensive than Disney and not 1/2 as good. It was fun, but no need to go again for a long time.

Universal Studios is one of the best places on the planet. Go! You'll feel like a kid again! The rides are insanely fun!! Spider Man ride, Harry Potter - OMG!!! I was there and flying through the air while playing Quittage!! (SP? sorry). Ten of us went in April 2016 and it was hot! I would not go in the middle of summer. I think the heat, people and exhaustion would take away from the experience. Oh! You have to eat at the Harry Potter place. Super fast, great food and by all means - order the butter beer! I still dream about butter beer. Bring a rain poncho for the water ride. You will be soaked from your shoes to your undies. Not comfy for the rest of the day. You have to go to Universal, at least once in your life. I noticed that the park was working on a King Kong attraction and Jimmy Fallon will be housed in Universal as well! I don't know when. I can't rave enough. Just go!! Expensive but worth every penny.

We just finished a trip to Universal. We purchased the Photo Connect photo package ahead of time to get the cheaper rate. Since we weren't going to the park on consecutive days I ended up purchasing the 14 day plan, even though we were there only three days over a seven day period. It would have preferred the three day pass. All in all it was still worth it. We were there with my daughter and her boyfriend. We were able to get all the ride photos and a few good shots at the front of the park, near the globe and a couple of other spots. We noticed more photographers early in the day than after lunch.  Helpful hint, when they ask you to put out your hand and you expect something to be added to your photo, you will not see this automatically on your phone when the pictures are uploaded, we found that if you go into one of their photo stores, they will add the characters there and they you will have the updated picture to download. Also on Spiderman they take your picture at the beginning before you get on the ride, it's on a blue screen, if you ask to view the pictures at the end of the ride they add all the special effects and add that to your photo connect star card. On the Rip Ride Rocket roller coaster, you don't get the video included, but you if you go to the photo booth at the end of the ride they will give you a code to download your still photo taken during the ride.  This could all be so much better as proven by Disney, but overall, I still feel having the ride photos and the other group shots we were able to have their photographers take made it worth getting.

I'm currently 23 years old and I used to absolutely enjoy visiting the Universal/ Islands of adventure parks. I went on a Thursday and Friday and the most I waited in line was 30 minutes, which was fantastic. The rides are pretty much all the same though. The Hulk, which I think saved the park, was closed down for revamping. The other rides rely heavily on simulators and less on actual motion. (I'm talking about both parks) I wasn't able to ride Escape from Gringotts since it wasn't open when I last went. The que is absolutely amazing but the ride was so underwhelming and short (for the amount of time you have to wait in line) I think currently, the best ride out of both parks is HP and the forbidden journey. Fantastic! I hope for the near future, they will make more rides that are more exciting with a lot more actual movement.

We went to Universal on a Sunday. Looked forward to just the two of us being there. It ended up costing $512 for the day. Two park passes and express. We went to the Harry Potter world and they weren't even honoring the express pass. They said everyone has the same wait. Wow. We paid $89 each for this convenience. Too busy. Not worth the money and especially not the extra express pass. :(
I love this park we used to get the I ride from our hotel to stop 6 then walk across the bridge to universal it took us about 25 mins and we are in our 50s
Welcome to the movies and action. Nice roller coasters like rock it, hulk and more. Many theme attractions, Simpsons, Transformers, Mummy Revenge, Minions, Shreck and more...

Universal is always a great time especially when the Florida weather is perfect. We went to Universal on a weekday which is ideal so the lines aren't ridiculous. I suggest riding the Hogwarts train in both directions since it's a different ride each way! We had some Irish food across from the Mummy which is one of my favorite rides! They serve drinks there too! Overall a great day at the parks!

Get there early and do the Harry Potter bits first as they will get the most crowded. Transformers is very good if the wait isn't too long. The Rockit Rollercoaster is also a good one. We did it on a previous trip as the queue was too long this time but we bought a video of the ride which shows the rider along with the ride and accompanying music.

Had a great time visiting Unviseral Studios. It had been several years since our last trip. We saw the new Harry Potter and Transformers rides. They were both done well. It was hard to tell which was computer generated, and which was live. We has lunch at Flanagan's, was very sorry to hear they did away with the beer flights, but that's just business once.it was explained how much time some of the beer pours took. We were sorry to hear none of the restaurants gave a military or first responders discounts. We were told it wasn't in the companies policy to give such things...seriously?! For the amount the parks charge per ticket and they can't give a discount... that was the stupidest thing we'd all day. Our server went back to her boss and asked.id she could give her employee discount and he said yes. That was very sweet of her to ask and we made the difference up in her . We went on a monday was as it turned out it was a really good day to go. The lines were not longer then 30.mins all day.

Unless you are into roller coasters that jerk and dip or motion sickening 3-d rides this place is not worth the visit. First of all there are two Universal Parks. Since there was no visible signage we went into the wrong one and then spent an hour trying to get it straightened out so we could go into the right one. The staff said it happened all the time. HELLO. Maybe you need to fix that problem, Universal. Second, there is very little to do with movies or movie making at this park. It is all rides. If you are in a wheelchair, under a certain height, or get motion sickness or have neck and back problems, don't even bother. There was very little to do or see. Just restaurants and shopping.Even the one show on horror makeup turned out to be cheesy. What a let down.

Our 100 member band traveled to Orlando to experience the process of doing musical score for motion pictures and the folks we dealt with were fabulous and very professional we had a blast I would recommend this to anyone looking for a future career in the motion picture industry at any level.

After being annual passholders, we came back 5 years later. The customer service has definitely declined which is disappointing for the price you pay to enjoy the park. With that said, we still had a great time with our 4 and 7 year old boys. The new Harry Potter Diagon Alley is SOOOOOO cool! The magic wands and interactive parts are so cool for Harry Potter fans. The train ride is really neat too; you need to go both ways to see it all.

I love going here, especially when they have new rides. Going in May was the best ever. The lines were quick. I was able to get on everything. The new exciting ride was the Harry Potter ride. Although I'm not a Harry Potter fan, my son loves it. Oh and how can I exit the park without getting a turkey leg. Omg!!!! It was the tastiest.

We visited with express passes and had an amazing day visiting characters and rides. Harry Potter ride and Minions ride should be done in first hour or last hour (even with express passes) The rest of the rides have little wait time allowing you to go on as many as you want. We saw lots of characters throughout the day and if you see one leaving - ask and they will tell you when they will be back.
So much fun the rides were all amazing however the Harry Potter rides were a hit! We got the park to park hopper but in future wouldn't buy this again!
Other than the park hopper pass to see the whole attraction, we had a great time. Graduation gift for our daughter as she grew up reading the book series

We split our time between WDW and Universal and the Universal parks win for us every time (but we have 3 children over the age of 18). This is especially true if you take advantage of staying at an on site hotel and use Express passes for rides.

Out of this world!!!!! Parades amazing!!!! For all ages!!!! So much to see, eat and do!!!! Staff make it all come alive with their enthusiasm! Rides are absolutely amazing!!! Would go back every year! Clean, tidy, for all ages! Can't stress enough if you not been then make sure you go!!!!

Universal Studios is a real must for anyone visiting Orlando. Universal have 2 parks: Universal Studios and Universal Islands of Adventure. The theme parks share an entrances complex, CityWalk, which is full of eateries, bars and shops to suit all tastes and budgets. Universal Studios has some amazing rides, the most thrilling of which is a rollercoaster called RockIt ... you even chose your own music to ride to! There is something to suit everyone, with many 3D and shows, meaning you can still have tonnes of fun, even if you aren't wild about rollercoasters. The recent addition of Harry-Potter-themed Diagon Alley is absolutely enchanting and ingenious! As a HP fan and a Brit, I can say this area of the park is very accurate to both the films and to London, even allowing you to enter Kings Cross station to catch the Hogwarts Express to Hogsmeade (located in neighbouring park, Islands of Adventure). My favourite ride is the Revenge of The Mummy, based on the move The Mummy. YOU MUST RIDE IT! Lots of fun and definitely worth a visit, or maybe two!

I don't even know where to start!! Universal was BY FAR the best theme park experience we had!! And we did them ALL!! The lines were much shorter and faster at both of the Universal parks. The rides are MUCH more fun and even more kid friendly. I found Disney had one extreme or the other for rides but Universal had it all! I LOVED all of the motion simulator rides as did my child who is afraid of everything haha. The Simpson's ride and Transformers were among my favorite's at Universal and Harry Potter and the forbidden journey, spiderman and the bilge rat barge at Island's of Adventure.....  my best ride overall in all of Florida was Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey!! Loved it! I am not a fan of going upside down but this particular ride was so much fun!  The service and interactions with the staff was unparalleled anywhere else. We were treated awesome here by everyone we met. Definitely #1 on my Florida recommendations.

Visited the park today. It closed at 6pm for an "event", turned out to be middle school graduation evening. Not unhappy to go back to my hotel. There were tons of school groups. But the express pass was a big help. Wish it worked on every ride.

An exciting day at Universal Studios. I had an a lot of fun with Caleb and my daughter Danielle. I was disappointed with the very expensive tickets over $200 each with limited park hours explanation given they had rented out park.
The park to park pass was worth it for us. We stayed until closing 2 of the 3 days we were there and had a wonderful time. The best theme park around!

Universal Studios is a favorite destination spot for my family. We love the rides and the different themed areas. I bought our tickets off of undercovertourist.com. I got three days for the price of two. The Harry Potter, Jurassic Park, and super hero areas are well themed and the people working in those areas seemed a little bit more into the theme and their characters. The Woody Woodpecker area is starting to show it's age but there are several water rides there which get people drenched. We paid over $300 for three Express Passes which included unlimited rides in both parks for one day. The lines were not all that bad and the parks were not that full. I probably would not buy them again for a May trip. There are many rides and shows that are in 3D and they kind of blended together after awhile. It looks like they are working on a new area that is King Kong themed and will open later this year. Universal could take some tips from Disney on how to run a theme park but the more adult rides make up for it most of the time.

I love this PARK - great for all ages. Shows and rides are terrific. Purchase your tickets with American Express and you can use the AMEX Lounge (across from Shrek 4D) Relax in AC Lounge with free water & snacks, after 4 hours in sun this "SAVED" my wife & me.
This is our absolutely favourite amusement park. We have been here several times and still wants to go back. It has something for everyone. If you go in late october the lines are not terrible.

universal studio is worlds best park according to my personel visit.  During may end crowd was moderate and lines were 30 to 45 minutes waiting which goes upto 2 hours during peak seasons I was told.  One can also buy express tickets inside the park everywhete after looking at the wait time.

This was my first visit to Universal Studios. A better rating for me would be "good", not "average or very good" Most of the attractions were great, but some were odd. For example, I thought the Krusty attraction (totally kiddie oriented) was good until I learned that this character from the Simpsons set a bad example for children with some of his habits. If you don't know what I am talking about, just look it up. So, I was a bit confused about what purpose it served. The doughnut food place, well, there are certain things I don't engage with even on the remotest level anymore since becoming more health conscious. However, people are free to make healthier food choices and options are there. It is a different ambiance. This is a place I would take teens, not little kids. I'm not a smoker, so standing or walking when it's hot outside with plumes of smoke is a bit nauseating. Staff did not smile as often and one was quite rude, but no wish to possibly cost her her job. I let it go and chalked it up to her having a stressful day-we all have them. The MIB, Horror Make Show, and Transformer attractions were awesome! Free lockers while you ride (my kids, not me) high velocity attractions were a winner.

Wonderful vacation with my daughters. The Wizarding World of Harry Potter was the best! The only suggestion would be to NOT eat at Three Broomsticks-YUCK!. We have been here in the past and would love to do it again in the future. Lines were not horrible And the beer was COLD!!!

I loved the themed areas here plus alot of nostalgia which I liked. Finally met doc brown and got a selfie with beetle juice...So happy :-) Simpsons area so much fun and very well themed and the ride is amazing Enjoyed men in black too although I lost! Food isn't majorly overpriced in the self serve restaurants and found souvineers although a little bit pricey they weren't totally over the top and of a decent quality... Will Def return next year
Paid for a one day ticket, not nearly enough time to enjoy all the attractions here but we're still had a good time!

We were lucky enough to get the Fast Pass and I recommend you do so too. It makes a massive difference with wait times down to about ten minutes. Be aware, it's not cheap though at about an extra $90.  Be sure to be waking into the park exactly when it opens and make your way straight to Harry Potter. Do the main rides and then go back to the entrance and start the park normally. This way, by the time you do get back to Harry Potter, you can afford to wait any time the main ride has to do it again. You can then see the rest of the world at your leisure and really enjoy it without time constraints.  The parks a lovely place to be. Kept extremely nicely and the staff are perfectly polite.  If you don't have a car and aren't staying on a universal property, here's some travel advice: USE UBER.  You'll see all the yellow taxis in Orlando are operated by a company called Mears. As they haven't a lot of competition, their prices are astronomical. Using Uber (an app you download) will save you hundreds of dollars. No joke. We saved over $350 on our trip and went everywhere.

We ultimately decided to spend one day at both universal studio parks. There's probably no way you can do this and see most main attractions w/o an express pass which unfortunately may double the entrance fee depending on the season. You'll walk a fair amount but it's not unreasonable, we didn't mind. We saw the vast majority of the main attractions but you should arrive when the park opens and plan on starting with the most popular rides. We were done by 4-5 PM. Several rides are similar in terms of effects/motion so don't be disappointed. Be sure to check beforehand if any are currently not running due to renovations and whatnot. One should consider staying at the hotels nearby where you may have a substantial reduction in fees as a hotel perk. Plus, you could leave mid-day to chill and come back early evening probably avoiding peak hours. Instead of driving we used Uber which may be a better deal than paying the parking fee of $20. However, be aware of the price increase during a surge of high demand, e.g. when leaving park. Please plan well because it ain't cheap-IMO :)

Thanks to a series of upgrades of old rides, this park is a our favorite of the two Universal offerings. Transformers, Minions, Shrek, The Mummy, and classics like the Simpsons and MIB are great rides. The Rip-it rollercoaster is smooth and has a great vertical drop.
My family of 3 went for the first time we had an amazing time , fun filled day the rides were great!! We will be back
We had a great time going here for Halloween Horror Nights (just my hubby and me this time). I love Gringotts!

Great place and sight seeing. Goods restaurants and attactions. During summer orlando can be very hot and humid so nake sure you take precautions e g. Sun protection lotion, water sources etc. Good for teens and adults. A++

I have been to Universal several years ago, and it was just OK. But in May when I visited I noticed a HUGE positive "grown up" Universal Studios. I was pleasantly surprised! There is so much to do there now and their Express Pass makes waiting in lines for 1 1/2 hours a thing of the past. Our express pass was part of our on-site hotel package, but I would have paid for it for sure. We walked by so many people waiting in long lines, and our adventures were so much more pleasant because of this. The park is clean and organized and easy to find things in. We had a blast there!

Our first trip to Florida and I cannot say enough about this park. Every employee was genuinely happy to make sure your visit was great. They really went above and beyond in cleanliness, technology and design.

This is a great park and the addition of Transformers and Rip Ride Rocket makes it even better. The Simpsons ride is also really well done. Still some great classics though like Terminator. Definitely not to be missed while in Orlando

What a great experience this theme park was to all of us !!  From the hulk to spider man to harry potter and so i can continue this park has just about everything for everyone from young to old!!  Only down side was as we are South Africans the exchange rate killed us from Rand's to Dollars but most definitely worth every cent spent here!!! Everyone has to go here at least once in a lifetime...
