The park is clean, well-kept, well-organized, with helpful, fun employees and lots to do and see. The food can be very pricey, and we experienced long wait times in line waiting to order our food. When you see four registers, and only one is open during peak eating times, with over 15 people in line, management should open up a few more registers.  The rides, live bands, entertainment, are awesome. It is a great park and worth your price of admission to experience it all. Be patient trying to access the park in the morning. They only offer one park per month to open early....they should rotate between the parks to open early every other day so park goers can enjoy early access to a variety of rides. Also, it is VERY slow and clumsy to have their park admission employees scan your bar code on your admission ticket, and then scan your fingerprint. Why don't they just take your picture on your ticket, so you don't have to have the double check at the admission gate? It is excruciatingly slow and you wait a long time in line to try and get into the park. We had early admission and it was still SO slow. Not a good first impression, especially for us first time Universal park goers. We had a 3-day park to park pass, and every time we left the park and came back, it was very slow to enter. They really need to focus on this issue.  Fun park, however, once you get in. Don't miss Diagon Alley, hidden from the main road. The train ride between parks is a nice, air-conditioned rest with entertainment!

More family oriented with less thrill rides. Under a lot of construction right now. Wizarding world is a definite. If you have a two park pass I recommend taking the Hogwarts Express to the next park.

Great roller coaster. Entertainment outdoors is so much fun. Food is great but make reservations early. We have seasons tickets and go out many times just to see the entertainment. Some top notch entertainers.

There is so much to do at Universal and it's so fun...you want to do it all at least twice. Plus, there is the Harry Potter experience at Universal, City Walk, and at certain times of the year special nights like Halloween Horror nights. This is a very fun attraction for all ages.

This was our favorite park so far. We only did the one side because we don't do roller coasters and we were able to do almost every ride. Loved Harry Potter ride and Simpsons simulator felt like a real roller coaster!! We did it in about 5 hours because we skipped minion ride, wait was to long.

Great value for money.. Busy periods are well managed.. So much to do so if you get the Orlando Flexi Pass you can split the attractions over a few days then come back and do shopping af end on a rainy day!  We usually stop off at Ihop on I Drive then walk over to the park. About 20 minutes.  Park itself is stunning. The rides are so good and the Harry Potter world is outstanding! You can take a ride on the Hogwarts express which is really cool, visit the Castle and greenhouses and say hi to Buck Beak at Hagrid's house! Great day out not just for kids! Make sure you take plenty of sunscreen with you and drink lots of water!

Visited here on my first ever trip to Florida recently. Love love loved it. So much to do and see. Could have went 2 days and got more in. My favorite was the Harry Potter exhibits. And loved the simulated rides. Definitely eat at the Krusty Burger and get a Flamin Moe drink

To fully enjoy, you have to get fast pass but 70$ + additional per head is ouchy on the pocket. If you can forget that then ride away! Harry Potter is special, can't use fast pass here, so do this first.

we stay on property to get the early admission and front of line access - so easy - boats take you everywhere! this park has things like shrek, minions, transformers, etc. the front of line makes it great! the best part of universal- you are under covers or in a/c while waiting - not like some other parks! this is topped off by diagon alley - a must see when in florida. and make sure to get a park to park ticket so you can go on the train for the complete harry potter experience!

My kids were bored with Walt DisneyWorld, so we changed over to Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure and boy, were we glad that we did. The kids loved it. Some of the BEST shows and rides that I have ever been on.

Brilliant loved it 20 years ago love it now. We are a family of 5 from 6 to 45. There is something for everyone. I would eat before and after the food is really expensive and not that nice pack a lunch and pig out after
I find the Universal Studios in Orlando better to visit than in LA. Its more airy and the attractions are a bit spread. Its my 4th time going here and I still would be back on my next Orlando trip.

Great park! Despite being stuck in a tropical storm, my family and I still had a great time at Universal Studios! The primary reason for our visit was for my wife and daughter who are lovers of Harry Potter. Diagon Alley and Hogsmeade were fantastic and really made you feel like you were in the story. Escape from Gringott's was a really cool ride and one that I hadn't experienced at other parks. The Simspons area was pretty cool as was the Marvel area. Unfortunately, due to the rain, there were several rides that closed down. The Hulk wasn't even open yet, which was really disappointing. If you go here, you absolutely, without a doubt, HAVE to ride the Transformers ride. That is hands down the best ride I have EVER been on. Very well done Universal!! I hope to be back soon!

Our second summer visit to Universal Studios. We bought the vacation package from Universal and I recommend it. Add the meal plan and transportation and your vacation will be easy. We stayed at the Hard Rock again and it was great. We had early park admission and 3 day park to park tickets. I took my daughter and her boyfriend as a graduation gift. We all had a blast.
I went with 16 friends and had express passes and early entry.  Great day out if you have the above, if you do not you may have a stressful day  The attraction itself is flawless

Universal is just as good as Disney - it now has a few outdated rides that could do with a facelift or complete change but so worth a visit. We got the express pass which even though crowds were rated 4-5/10 this was an excellent time saver. We whizzed round every ride in one day - I could imagine this would start getting expensive with a large family though.

Visited Universal once again, never gets boring even after all these years, Transformer ride is very very good as is Shriek, Harry Potter train ride to Island of Adventures is slightly different from opposite journey. my favourite is The Blues Brothers.

I haven't been to Universal Studios in about 5 years and the changes made this brand new to me again. Fear Factor was awesome and the street parade made this 49er feel young again (I danced and jumped with the characters). I had a great time with my husband, next time I'll have to do this with my grandchildren.

I'm from the UK, and after making the decision to go, O...M...G I'm so glad I did. It's great that Universal and IOA are linked up now by Harry Potter. You will not be disappointed, I promise you. Just walking through the park I can't help but be gob smacked and in complete ore of it all! Me and my whole family are completely addicted to this place, if/when you go...you WILL be too haha

We especially loved the Transformers and Harry Potter rides but the others were great too. Staff were helpful, friendly and we loved how they stayed in character with the area they were in. It really added to the experience. The only downfall with the park is the crowd. There were too many people and with manners at all. It seemed that most areas were over crowded and we found it hard to even find seating to just rest.  I would go again but plan it during a slower time.
As a family none of us had been here. we all loved it way better than Disney. It was cleaner and the pre-ride experience was much more enjoyable
Perfect place to visit! So much to see and do. The rides are incredible. Diagon alley is straight from the imagination of any Harry Potter fan - simply magical!

Best place in the world or so my 19 year old Harry Potter mad twins think...  Top tip if you ask any of the food places for free tap water you will get it and they will also full up water bottles so just take a refillable water bottle and keep asking for free water rather than purchasing more water or coke it will save you lots of dosh

I am a die-hard Disney fan and Universal was always like Disney's second cousin in my mind. I liked it, but it wasn't in the same league. Over the past few years Universal has really upped it's game and it is now definitely in the big leagues. Diagon Alley is out of this world - easily the best theme park "land" I have ever seen. That I knew I would like but I was impressed but how good the rest of the park was as well. Granted - this is not a great park for small children - not much to do, but for older children, teens and adults, this is great choice on how to spend a day or two of your vacation.
A fantastic park with some awesome rides - our favourites were Terminator, Men in Black, The Mummy, The Rocket - a FUN day out - we would highly recommend this park - it's #1 👍
The crowds and lines affected my impression of this park. It was really well done, but I guess I'm kind of done with hour long waits for rides etc. Plan your visit during a slower season if possible.

Universal Studios is a fun trip for a day. We stayed at Universal and visited the studios as well as Islands of Adventure for 3 days and it was probably a day and one half too much, as the parks aren't overly big. The attractions inside however were wonderful and we were big fans of the Jurassic Park ride.
WOW ! This place is amazing a must see, friendly and helpful staff and the ride experiences are truly fantastic!! :)
Outstanding day out - the Harry Potter fans in our group were enthralled. we had a ride on the Dragon Duel roller coaster as well which was awesome. Brilliant day out.

I was here for only 1 day but I planned it out and visited all of the attractions - it was a lot easier because I was by myself. I could go in the single riders queue and cleared most of the attractions in the first half, and saw the shows later. (many times, even groups entered the single riders queue to get in fast, so the effect reduced!) Diagon Alley is simply amazing, it does the job well of transporting you into the world of Harry Potter. The best of all was Hollywood Rock It, which many others seemed to dislike, probably because it was so good that it could be scary for some!

The Harry Potter experience was terrific and well worth the trip, but for the VERY EXPENSIVE price, I would have expected a "magical" experience as well as a professional, clean environment at all times.  All the rides were top caliber, and Harry Potter World in both parks provides an experience that transports even those of us who aren't experts into a fantasy that is hard to describe.  It's unfortunate that Univeral does require the professionalism and cleanliness some of the other parks in the area do to provide a complete experience for it's patrons. The price charged would indicate a similar experience.  During our day:  1.) Arrived at the park almost an hour before opening and the attendant immediately tried to get $10 more from us for "preferred" parking which was one level above the level in which we parked - a TOTAL rip-off. This seemed the be the name of the game all day long, trying to convince us we "needed" to spend money for conveniences that were NOT actually conveniences. 2.) We downloaded the Wait Times app before arriving at the park as advised. This was somewhat helpful in knowing where the longest wait times were, but none of these times were anywhere close to accurate. The times posted in front of the individual rides were at least 30 minutes lower than the actual wait time. 3.) Two of the major rides (Superman & The Dragon Challenge) were down for a significant amount of time as we waited in line. 4.) Patrons were able to hop into the Express line from the general line in one of the major rides because the queuing system was unmonitored by employees. 5.) Queueing system on the Men in Black ride is very strange. After waiting in a line outside in the heat, about 50+ patrons are pulled into a holding area, then move into an elevator which mixes everyone up. It seems the group is moving onto the ride outside the elevator. Unfortunately, the entire group pours out into a wide hallway where everyone gets mixed up again and more elevators of people pour in passing up those who have been standing in line. 6.) After finally getting to the Men in Black ride, several of the cars were leaving without being full, even though there was a singles line. Employees were allowing couples in the singles line to be seated together in the cars instead of seating them with other groups. We waited amost an hour to ride, and one of our guns was not functioning (actually was missing parts). We missed out on the intent of the ride after waiting in line for an hour. 7.) Signage is CONFUSING to say the least. On several occasions we could not figure out where the general line was opposed to the express line or the single line. We stopped on at least three occasions to ask an employee where to find something. The directions were less than helpful, and at one point, the employee had no idea what was going on in the area we asked about. 8.) During the heat of the afternoon, we stopped at three drink stands in a row to find the drink we wanted (Coke) and ice because they were "out". 9.) Overall, the employees in the Harry Potter World seemed to be in-tune with their job, professional, knowledgeable, and helpful. Many in other areas of the park were not as attentive or professional with patrons.  Overall, we had a great time!

Both parks were clean and staff friendly. The vast majority of attractions were thrill rides. Both Harry Potter areas were very well themed and generally much nicer than the rest of the parks. Universal needs to step up its game during the summer and stay open later. It's very hard to take advantage of cooler evening temperatures when the park closes at 9pm.

I really disappointed myself by not living universal studios! I wanted to but it was just missing something for me. One of the big downfalls had to be the fast pass situation we didn't opt to buy the express pass as we had already paid a fortune for the tickets so the queues were a bit if a nightmare with a four year old. The staff are ok but again just lack that little sprinkle of magic (maybe we were spoiled by Disney!). Harry Potter was fab and I glad I went even just for this. I don't think I would be quick to return here if I went back to florida. I would say it's a park that's aimed more at adults and again I had my 4 year old with me so this may also be the reason for my lack of enjoyment.

Both parks has different rides/shows scattered around. Roller coaster rides, 3D/Virtual rides, water rides, shows are scattered around 2 parks. I am lover of Virtual rides and liked Harry potter rides the best, Transformer ride, Spider Man ride, Despectable me, minions etc were bet for me. MIB(Man in black) was advertised as virtual space ride but is only good for kids and is not a VR ride. 2 days is generally enough and express pass helps a lot.

This place was amazing!! The rides were fantastic the new ones in 3D and 4D are definitely worth the wait. If I were to go again I'd get fast pass as waiting in line in the heat and humidity was awful at times. They do have a good deal on drinks if you buy a souvenir cup you get free refills all day so it's def worth it. The food was pretty grim tho especially the turkey leg that's nowhere near as nice as it looks! Fantastic place!

Seriously good fun and the new set looks fantastic, so much going on this place never gets old. Wouldn't do the food package as it takes a lot of searching to find out where you can get your drinks cup let alone refills and it saved us nothing.

If you like roller coasters, Universal is absolutely the best park to visit! My personal favorite is The Hulk!! If you aren't into roller coasters there are many other rides and attractions to keep you happy. Harry Potter is another great section and has an amazing ride! Don't forget to try the butter beer! I live in Florida and this is my favorite park by far!

I cannot wait to get back to Universal studios this was my first time here and I absolutely love it, mostly all of the rides were indoors and that is plus after being in the heat all day. I ate over were the Simpson's attractions was and had a chicken and waffle sandwich it was delicious. I will be back there soon!

Fantastic park with plenty of great rides. Transformers ride was excellent as well as rip ride rocket. Bought the photo pass and got some great pics really worth it. Would recommend getting the giant Simpsons donut

Beautiful scenery!! The attention to detail is amazing!! Gift shop and food every other store. Two days in the parks is plenty. Very crowded and the long lines wrap for miles in very interesting ways.

My sister and I were visiting my cousin in FL and took a day trip to Orlando to spend some time at Universal Studios to see the new Wizarding World of Harry Potter Diagon Alley part of the park. We were walking toward the back of the park trying to find the entrance. I was expecting some grand well-themed entrance, but no. They stayed true to the books and made a very subtle hidden entrance that you can easily pass by and not even realize that you did! Lol! Once you find the brick walls and enter, the view is awesome! To look down the street of Diagon Alley and see Gringott's Bank towering in the distance with a huge dragon on top that breathes out fire was very cool! We walked around for awhile just trying to soak it all in. The amount of detail that went into this place was amazing! You really feel like you are there! You can easily spend hours going from shop to shop looking at all the souvenirs, but you need to make time to stop by the Leaky Cauldron for lunch. That is a treat in and of itself! The que to order your food went very quickly and we received our food in a very timely manner. They run this place like a well oiled machine, which I imagine they'd have to in order to get as many people in and out of there as they do. Meals will run you about $12 and they have quite a few to choose from. Whether you buy it here or at a host of other places in Diagon Alley, you must, I repeat, you MUST purchase a cup of Butter Beer! This stuff is amazing! I've been to the Warner Bros. Studios Tour in London and had their butter beer...... not even close to the same! I've found recipes and made my own..... too sweet! Universal Orlando has this recipe down to a science! It is soo yummy! I can't quite describe it. It's not too sweet, just perfect!  The Gringott's Bank simulator ride was pretty cool too! Similar to the Hogwart's Castle ride at Island's of Adventure. As you enter the bank, each side of the lobby is lined with animatronic goblins at their desk. They look very real!  The only negative thing about the Wizarding World is that you must have a ticket to enter both Universal and Island's of Adventure in order to ride the Hogwart's Express. I did not have such a ticket so I did not get to ride the train! Boo! But I have heard it is very cool! I found a video on Youtube, but do hope to take my family sometime and experience it with them. Oh, and you can not use your Express Pass for the Gringott's ride. We had Express Passes for the day and they worked very well for most of the other rides in the park which was perfect since we went in the middle of June, one of their busiest months of the year.

This place is incredible from start to Finish Plenty of rides for the thrillseeker and the non-thrillseeker A must do is the rock it hollywood rollercoaster and be sure to check your video playback when finished it can provide some very funny moments(you can watch without buying) Most rides are brilliant for both kids and adults alike The que times for transformers and gringotts harrypotter ride are the longest so i suggest getting them done asap Other than than all rides are normally 35/45min waiting Be prepared to wait in line for drinks and food as those places fill up super quick Overall a must see attraction in general!

took family to universal studios cool was able to get to the major rides and shows in 1 day for both parks as long as you have a fast past, which i would recommend anytime you go during the travel season to any theme park...the only disadvantage is the king kong and harry potter does not use fast past since those are there newer rides so that is the only real waiting that we had to do, but overall was very fun!!!

Great thrill rides and fun shows throughout the park. Loved the Harry Potter attractions. Lunch at The Leaky Caldron, the shops and Gringotts was fantastic. Watch for the fire breathing dragon! Board the Hogwarts Express at gate 9 3/4 and travel to Hogsmeade. From ET to Mummy's Revenge there's something for every thrill seeker. From San Francisco to New York, Blues Brothers to Sponge Bob great fun. Can't wait to visit again.

Watch out when you purchase tickets on the site-they advertise that you get a coupon book but when you pick them up at the front office they tell you they never had a coupon book. When I picked up mine at the end of feb 2016 I didnt get one let alone the envelope supposedly that was waiting for me. All I got were the tickets. I only printed out 1 copy also -print out a second one to have on hand to verify that's what was said. I just went on their site to look at their deals for hotels since I am going their in oct 2016 and already have my annual tickets. It is again on their site about a free coupon book when you order the tickets online. spoke on the chat and told this and they wanted a copy of the reciept and what site I found this on. She didnt know it's on their own site. this is not right at all.
Its one of my family favourite parks. There was a lot of closed areas this year but i don't mind as they are putting a lot of new stuff in and it makes it worth visiting every year!!!

We really enjoyed this park but mostly because the crowds are much lighter than Islands of Adventure. This park by far has the better Harry Potter experience and rides but that in my opinion is the main draw. Much less thrill factor compared to Islands of Adventure if you are a roller coaster and ride fan. If you have the park hopper you don't want to miss this park but most with kids and teens will find themselves riding the Hogwart's Express to the other park. For those into 3D movie type rides this is your park. Leaky Caldron has good English pub type food but don't expect a fine dining experience anywhere in Universal.

My wife promised to kick my butt again because she won the challenge in 2014. Well it didn't happen this time, cause our daughter spanked her. I couldn't compete due to bum shoulder (wink wink), but all in all the children thoroughly enjoyed themselves.
So many things to do and see! And I want to do it all again already. The Mummy was my husband and daughters favorite ride out of both parks. Great fun!
Fun theme park to visit while in the Orlando area. Several ride choices for every age. Shows are corny but worth seeing. Many new upgrades coming.

Universal was my favourite parks 20 years ago and still is today! I feel they do a lot more to keep current than Disney do! Much of Disney was exactly the same as last time I went 20 years ago where as there was so much new at universal! Transformers ride is awesome, constantly rated 1 of the best rides in the world and rightly so! My advice would be to get there for about 8:30- the 3 times we visited the gates opened at 8:45 so it's good to be there early! Don't plan to do Harry Potter on the same day, it's too busy! Set aside a day just for universal studios in earnest! It's a good idea to work your way up, going minions and shrek first as you'll get them done within the first 30 Mins then head to transformers whilst the queue is still small. Probably less than 30 mins as opposed to 2 hours like it is for most of the day! Much of the early morning traffic goes straight for Harry Potter! Avoiding this and working your way round the park should mean you avoid big queue for most of the day! Brilliant theme park, by the way, duff beer is awesome! Unfortunately you can't buy bottles to take away! If you have a hot dog from the brewery then be warned it is massive, easily big enough for 2 if not more!

Went there for the first time a couple of weeks ago, there is so much there to see and do you really need to plan your days right. The only issue is the waiting times but that is to be expected when the kids were off school, I loved the Harry Potter parts and the Simpsons ride too, I would defiantly go again.

We were very excited to return to Universal when we realized it had been 13 years since our last visit. Sadly, we were very disappointed to see that very little had really changed. There were a lot of new attractioons (Krustyland, Minions, Transformers) that replaced some old ones (Jaws, Back to the Future, etc.) but by and large it was a lot of motion simulators. It got old to just get bounced around while watching a movie screen. Old standbys like ET and such are showing their age.  The new Harry Potter stuff was interesting. The Hogwarts Express was very impressive and really made you feel immersed. My son (who is 6'7") and I did not fit on most of the Harry Potter ride simulators (Escape from Gringotts and such) so could not experience those. That was very disappointing. There were other things that had seats too small for us. We watched a lot of people being turned away and you would think they would have some bigger seats at least every couple of cars.  Crowds were not too bad (surprising since it was the 4th of July weekend) and all employees we encountered were very nice and helpful. The Coca-Cola Freestyle cups were the way to go and we had plenty to drink. It did rain both days we were there but we were not impacted too much by it.

Visited in June for two days with family . Minimum 2 days needed to cover both parks . Staying in Universal studios hotel is advised as you are in close by vicinity and you are entitled to get FAST PASS which gives u priority entry to rides .  Ensure you stay for 2 days and get passed for 2 days with flexible entry to any park .  Light show / parades and adventurous rides with lot of fun programmes and good food options with shopping options all this you get to enjoy .

Visited in 1990, when it was first opened. Some rides did not work and we were given complementary return tickets.  Returned Easter 2016. Visited guest services (they call it “Will Call”). Presented our 1990 tickets, asking if it was possible to pay to upgrade my 1990 tickets for use in both parks. (In 1990 there was only on park). The clerk called the supervisor who furnished us with 4 one day passes, without any quibble and great curtesy. What an impressive start and amazing customer service.  Crowds and queues were again (like Disney) a problem, however, at least there was some entertainment while queuing and less shouting than at Disney (see my Disney review).  If I went to Florida again, the only theme park I would visit would be Universal and would spend more time visiting the many other attractions (Rodeo’s, Airboat, Alligator farms, etc) Thank you Universal for some enjoyable days out in 1990 with our children and in 2016 with our grand-children.

Stood in line on a ride for an hour, and watched them stop all but the express pass riders.  A disappointed 9 year old couldn't understand, and its is hard to explain the greed behind this.  On vacation again this year and US is not on the list.
This ride was the best! It was calm and sweet and nostalgic. Like it so much better than all the 3d rides in the parks. Old school does it best!
We go about once a month and it's a blast for all ages. There is something to do for everyone. The wait times are reasonable. It can be hot in the summer heat so make sure you drink plenty of water.
I love this place far more than Disney. All of the attractions are just more adult and entertaining for me.
Every time I go I feel like a kid again. The rides, the shows, the parades are out of this world. One of my favorite show is actor animals.

You can't go to Orlando and miss this park incredible rides and much more. Don't miss the Revenge of the Mummy indoor coaster or the Escape from Gringotts ride in Diagon Alley. Eat in the world of the Simpsons, try a Krustyburger or drink a Flaming Moe. Transformers is a stunning dark ride you don't want to miss.

If you like all the frills and adrenalin rushes here is the place to visit so much for every age to do The Harry Potter area is excellent and well thought up your imagination runs away with you. It's a lot easier than Disney world to enjoy as its not over packed Superb place to visit

AWESOME day! We had a one day park hopper pass, so we could ride the Hogwart's Express. We went too hard from 8-6 and ran out of steam. All things Harry Potter were just perfectly awesome. If you love roller coasters and are REALLY brave, do The Rocket! One of my favorites was The Minions. You are in a seat in a room the whole time, but after you are done, you won't believe it!
Wonderful time!! Harry Potter was great!! Will visit again, fun for the whole family!! We even got engaged this visit!!

First time being back to Universal since they updated the park. What an amazing experience! We arrived in the late afternoon and stayed until closing time. That wasn't enough time for all of us to enjoy everything at Universal. We will definitely come back to Universal next year!

Visiting the 2nd time to see the new Harry Potter. Loved it yes it's crowded but it is as expected. My twin 1 yrs old boys love the splash area especially during the hot days. Butterbeer Butterbeer is the best...

So our kids are now 9 and 13 years old -- thus Universal is now the center of gravity when we go to Orlando. This place has better rides, way - way better restaurants, allows booze and really clears out in the evenings with shorter wait times at the best rides.

Loved every minute. Had tickets for 4 days with express passes and early admission. Do your self a favor and get the lanyards for your tickets and passes. We didn't and were constantly pulling them out and putting them away. Diagon Alley is fantastic be sure to go down the alley next to the Leaky Cauldron. Pictures with Bumblebee are a must. Don't miss the Blues Brothers show really good.

Love this park - particularly the retro feel with some of the rides/experiences. T2 still doesn't fail and is a family favourite. The transformers ride is awesome and when we first arrived the queue was only 10mins but later in the day was 50mins. Simpsons ride makes you feel a bit queazy but is a fun simulator for he kids. We did the Harry Potter stuff separate as you wouldn't fit everything into 1 day. Disappointed the Beetlejuice has gone now! Mummy is a fabulous thrill ride. Yet again the minions ride queue was horrendous - 70 mins as was rip ride rocket so we gave these a miss.

Bought a multi day, multi park ticket on the official Universal website paying full price, tried to use on the second day and something was showing the my ticket was no good on the 2nd day. So had to wait in the line for guest services. This is not the hassle that a tourist spending this kind of money should have to deal with! Won't be visiting this theme park again, needless to say. The point of buying tickets in advance to avoid long lines became null and void due to this issue. Lines seem to be the norm in the 100 degree heat. They corrected the issue but the wait was totally unnecessary! They did offer some fast line passes for the inconvenience.

Rides are very good but queues are just too long. The new Harry Potter is amazing. It used to be that you could arrive in the morning and the wait would not be too long. However, arrived today at 10.30am and Harry Potter rides over an hour. Also, universal have started posting times which are underestimating real times. Dr who ride said 45 mins it took 70. Mummy 35 mins took 50. Shriek 35 took 45 mins, Men in Black single rider said 10 mins took 30 mins. The new Harry Potter attractions in Universal Studios are great. The train which travels from Islands of Adventure to Studios is unbelievable. The experience is so unique and you really feel you're in the film. Also the new street areas behind the London station signs is faultless in its replication. You need a ticket which covers both parks to get the train, don't miss out this attraction.
So much fun this was the best park in orlando. I can't wait to go back. I would recommend buying fast passes it's to dam hot to wait in line for a hour and half

The best park I have ever visited! It`s just amazing! The best thing is not just for children even you visit the Shrek, The Harry Potter part, adults can have a lots of fun there too. They have app to check the wait times which is so helpful not to waste so much time cos there is a lot of things to do. If you can, stay for more days. Most of the drives were inside buildings therefore we could escape from the rain and the humid hot weather. We enjoyed it so so much!

Crazy that we had to pay $20 each day to park! The cups with free refills all day sound like a good idea, but you can only get the refills at certain areas (limited). You then have to wait in line to fill it yourself, many times they were not working or out of ice/pop. Food is way over priced for what you get, no variety.

Personally, I enjoyed Island of Adventure better than Universal Studios. For my family (two kids: 2 & 8), Island of Adventure offered a bit more. However, there is still a lot to do here. Lines seem to be the longest between 10-5.

My son and I shared a great day at both the parks specifically for the Harry Potter experience. He absolutely loved it! I don't know much about Harry Potter but that didn't stop me from thoroughly enjoying the whole experience. My personal favourite was the Gringots ride. The queues at their worst were about 30 minutes but all inside, and so much to see during the wait. We booked express passes so our maximum wait for anything in the park was 5 minutes. Well worth it on a hot day but you did have to slow down sometimes because waiting in line is actually in some really great areas which you can miss if you are moving too fast. The meal deal was $21.99 which we upgraded to unlimited free non alcoholic drinks for an extra $6. So throughout the day we had a large pizza slice, bread stick and Caesar salad for lunch, Ben and Jerrys ice cream later in the day and unlimited drinks. Soft drinks are usually about $4 each and we must have refilled at least 6 times, so it was well worth the deal for us. The only down side was at the very end of the day when it was hard to find a machine that hadn't run out as it had been so hot! Staff were amazing and super friendly. My husband dropped us off at the drop off area and picked us up there at the end of the day, well sign posted and easy to do.
Loced the theme park. Lots of fun thrilling rises, many if them simulators. The Simpsons ride is hilarious. A great family day out.
This is a great place for young and old. Great rides, great shows and great live performances. The free drink refills are a great idea.

Universal Studios is the best park in Orlando. The environment is full of happiness. The attractions are carefully done and pass the sensation of reality. The decoration is perfect. I came many times and I am always enjoying. I love this park!

Being an adult Universal Studios has a lot more to offer then Disney.If you are a Florida resident you get a much better deal on yearly passes.The parks are easy to navigate and the hotel options are very good. It is very easy to get in and out of parking and if you just want to go to CityWalk its still a good value.
this place was amazing.Favorite thing in flodia.it is better than disney no offense walt.The ride were amazing the amazingness was real.The food great the sight how do I say beautiful.Go now
Great place, amazing attractions.  Visited it 4 times in 2 weeks, top rides: Harry Potter escape from gingotts, spiderman, transformers, rip rockin roller coaster.
What an amazing place absolutely loved it as did my kids aged 17,14 and 12. Harry Potter was by far our favourite ride

I can't tell you how much there is to explore between the two parks at Universal Orlando! It truly has been an amazing experience both times we've gone as a couple, and we just keep finding new things to explore each time we go!  I don't want to spoil anything too much for anyone so I'll give you a list of my favorite experiences between the two parks,and a few helpful hints... (My husband and I don't really do the big rides/coasters. To us, all of the following were very entertaining, just thrilling enough, and didn't make us sick). -The entire Harry Potter area(both sides). You must buy a park to park ticket to enjoy the full scope of the HP experiences offered. It's entertaining just to peruse the areas and shop, and cast spells of course! -The Hogwarts Express is a must do-also you can bring your drink aboard with you (even alcoholic drinks)! -Make sure you buy an interactive wand (IT'S WORTH THE MONEY)! -Floreans Ice Cream: Butterbeer, Earl Grey & Lavendar, and Salted Caramel Blondie were my favorite flavors! (We went there two times-you can get two different scoops of ice cream, or just one flavor of soft serve-Butterbeer is soft serve). I actually didn't like the Butterbeer when we tried it on our previous trip, but the ice cream is the way to have it for sure! -The Leaky Cauldron, The Three Broom Sticks, and Hogshead Pub- just go there and eat ANYTHING. You'll love it all! (I personally love the fish and chips, and the Chicken Sandwich. The American Breakfast at the Three Broomsticks is AMAZING as well)! Don't forget to try the specialty drinks- the Otter's Fizzy Orange Juice, and Lemon Squash were so delicious! Not to mention the adult selections... Dragon Scale, Hogs Head, and the Fire Whiskey Mixed Drink! -Gringotts (by far my favorite ride)! We bought the lanyards from our "ride photos" for this. It looks like a pass to get you into the bank, very creative, and a pretty nice leather and canvas souvenir! -HP The Forbidden Journey (This ride is almost impossible to get a good ride photo on. I would suggest riding it a few times if you plan on trying to get a photo for it). -Springfield: the whole area! Just play around and explore here, there is a lot of neat little nods to the show. We met the Simpsons when they came out too! Definitely go into Moe's (answer the phone if it rings), and try a Krusty Burger or a Ribwich! I also went to Lard Lads and got a donut sundae...way to much to actually eat, but I channeled my inner Homer to eat at least a 1/4 of it! -Simpsons Ride -Spider-Man 3D -Meet a transformer! (We met Bumblebee, I love him)!!! -Transformers 3D -The Raptor Experience (this maybe a little scary for kids-but we had so much fun and still cannot stop talking about it)! -Poseidon's Fury (walk through/show) -Sinbad Stunt Show (make sure you hang out in front by the fountain beforehand, it's really entertaining) -MIB: Yes, it's old and cheesy, but still so much fun! You can really get into competing with everyone for the highest score, and we actually got a really hilarious ride photo out of it!  Like I said, there is really so much to do between the two parks! It is definitely worth getting the 2 park passes, and staying onsite so that you not only get the express pass, but you also get in at 7am to the Harry Potter areas!  Also, if you are celebrating anything...your birthday, honeymoon, anniversary...make sure you ask for a celebration button. They can get you some really helpful perks throughout the parks and the entire resort as well!
I spent two days here while I was on a business trip. USF and IOA are in my opinion the two best amusement parks in the country. There is so much to chose from and something for everyone. Just Wow.

Our family had a great time at Universal Studios. The park was clean and the employee were very helpful. We spent an entire day enjoying the attractions. Plan to walk a lot - wear comfortable shoes. Take breaks to avoid the hot summer weather. The crowd was not too bad - most congested in the Harry Potter area. Harry Potter is a must see. You need to have a park to park ticket to ride the train from one park to the other - it is worth the extra money.

What a magical place,it can make adults into children again, there is no age discrimination only height, the atmosphere is breathtaking rides out of this world and can go every year and you must go on rocket it and the mummy its unbelievable. Best vacation ever.

Not a park for the faint hearted- great rides , we found not ideal for children under 1.2mtrs. We opted for transportation from the Hotel as decided to go later and heard the car parks could be busy- however not as busy as we thought- July seen as of season.
Plenty to do but very busy. Annoyingly all the new attractions that were supposed to be ready by the summer were still closed. EXTORTINATE, INEXCUSABLE and UNJUSTIFIABLE parking fees.

We heard so many great things about Universal Studios that we decided to take a trip to see what the excitement was all about. We had a tremendously wonderful experience! There are so many things to do and see. We were there first thing in the morning when the park opened, so we did not have issues with very very long lines and having to wait extended periods of time. We will definitely visit again!

My wife and I never get date time with two small children. When she surprised me this morning with a brief day date to Universal I was thrilled. She paid for a babysitter, just for a few hours, so we could ride the new attraction " skull island, reign of Kong". After parking and rushing through the crowds to get to the ride, we see a 90min wait. Knowing that we had limited time, we agreed that this was the one ride for us to wait for. 45 minutes in, we hear there will be a brief delay, we wait. It comes back up, then 30 min later, another brief delay, and we wait. Then we are told there is an extended delay, and then an announcement that the ride is down, and will be at least 40min until operational. We had already been there the 90min and were not able to wait any longer, and regretfully had to leave. I stopped at guest services to explain our situation, and hoped for at least a fast pass for a later date. Instead we are told that since we chose to leave the line, "there is nothing they can do". I find that hard to believe. Being in the service industry myself, I know better. However, because I know better, I left without causing a scene. Needless to say, I am very dissatisfied with the supposed "guest service" and will not be renewing our annual passes if this is how business is done. I'm not looking for hand outs, just a chance to redo a brief day date with my wife.
Great time was had by all,so much to see,great setup,very good for disabled.only drawback are the prices.far to expensive after what you pay for tickets.

We visited the Harry Potter when the attraction first opened years ago. As a big Harry Potter fan it was magical.Now we were back to experienced the train and the new addition with my 9 year old Godson. . If you a true Harry Potter fan it is worth it to take the train and enjoy both Harry Potter Worlds , if not just do one . Even though the attacktions have different names and visuals they seemed to be a very similar experience . The train did have much meaning if you ar not a fan. For the park overall we had a good time and took advantage of the early entry by staying at one of the on site hotels (Cabana Bay) it was worth the expense . Definitely get up early to take advantage even 10-15 min late at the start of the park and you can wind up with a long wait on you favorite rides . The 9 year old is a big Homer Simpsom fan so we ate in Homer land after 2 turns on the Homer ride. Food was so so and expensive. There are much better choices in other ares of the park.He had a good time. Next step is to compare the California Harry Potter

The most fantastic place! Tower of Terrors is a must, even if you're scared of rides, it's hilarious! And Rock n Rollercoaster must be done too! The park is immaculate and clean, very chilled and relaxed with a great selection rides for all ages, we loved it!
Always a good walk-bring good shoes! Always expensive-water and drinks especially over priced! However we find it better than Disney-and a little cheaper!

It was hot, busy and the queues were there wherever you looked. But and its a massive BUT, it doesn't matter. The heat is fun, the crowds make the atmosphere, the rides, restaurants and staff all try their best. You're on holiday and you won't do it all in a day. It's too good to rush and my family love it.

Let me say this as a couple who absolutely LOVE Disney and lived in Florida, worshipping at The Mouse on a scarily frequent basis. But Universal/IOA have stepped up their game while Disney hasn't done much. The Harry Potter additions are amazing, the rides are great and the food is much better than Disney. Definitely will be going back here again, probably not to the Diz as much.

This was my 10th visit to Universal. I brought 2 people who hadn't been there before. Harry Potter was great. we got into single rider lines in most every ride. The express passes are so pricey and it made me feel ripped off so I didn't get them. We paid $193 for a two day one park per day pass with two free days. The fact that we had four days made us not so urgent to rush to each ride and not so in angst of the time we spent in lines. Food was terrible/worst I have ever had in any park. I think the park wasn't so packed because the heat index was 107. The transformers ride is one of their best and escape from gringott's is really great. The whole diagon alley is really nice and you could spend a half day there easily. ET needs to be spruced up.

We usually book from the UK but forgot. Paid $1250 for four adults with express passes only to find the new ride (Kong) was excluded (90 minute wait) and most others had 15+ minute waits with the express pass, Minions was 25! Hulk as shut and Harry Potter has taken over, also excluded from Express pass!

A multi day pass is the way to go. We also got the Express Pass for one day at Universal Studios. The pass works for all rides except Harry Potter and the Train. If you don't mind riding separate, use the single rider line for Harry Potter. The rides here are better than Disney. We love Transformers, Simpsons, and Despicable Me rides. They are excellent and keep you out of the sun. We took the train over to Islands of Adventure.  On our second day, we went to King Kong first and waited only 45 minutes. The ride is new and popular so get it early.

If you're a fan of horror, screaming, adrenaline and all things tense then get yourself to Halloween Horror Nights. Yes some of the queues might be crazy long but once you get in the houses you completely forget about your aching feet. It is literally like walking through the movie. The Insidious house last October was so awesomely horrible. Never felt so scared in my life. I loved it! We were able to walk straight onto the newly opened Transformers ride about 10 times and of course all the rides, restaurants and shops are perfectly designed, clean and welcoming unless there's a guy with a chainsaw outside.  As for the park in the day time, it's just as good. Tips for certain rides like Harry Potters Forbidden Journey; GO SINGLE RIDER! It took my group 2 minutes to get on and some of us even managed to still get on together. That ride is hands down the best ride I have ever been on. WE'LL BE BACK!

This was our 4th visit here. It is always a great day. Really enjoy the selection of attractions here and am always grossed out at the Fear Factor game played!! The new Diagon Alley is just fantastic!!

We thought the Studios side was better than Adventure Island. The RockIt Ride is really scary - really!! Even my teenage daughter only rode it twice - so you are warned haha And best ride is the Minions Ride - really terrific. A great day out followed by brunch at Universal City Center.

Had a fantastic time at Universal Studios even though they have take out twister and disaster rides which was a little disappointing. Transformers ride was good however my youngest son was tall enough outside but after waiting 2 hours he was turned away at the ride even though he has been on lots of other 40inch rides at Universal. Harry potter ride was great and also the streets are good but very busy. Too many shops and restaurants and not enough attractions.

We came back, after having been there in 2012, to see Diagon Alley and it is amazing. We loved it. Get park to park so can ride the Hogwarts Express. We stayed at a Universal resort and could get in the parks at 7:00 and I definitely recommend that. Could do several things before lines got long. We did not have the Express pass as Cabana Bay guests did not get that perk and it is just too expensive for 5 people. Really though, we did not have terribly long waits and we were able to do almost everything we wanted. Do wish they did not have Express Pass and used a system like Disney Fast Pass. Utilized the single rider line when possible which helps although it is more fun to experience with your group and need to experience the entire queue at least once as the queue is usually part of the attraction. Most of the attractions are 3-D motion simulator type rides. Will come back again sometime but maybe not in the summer due to the heat and crowds.

This was our first visit to Universal Studios and we were not disappointed! We stayed at the Royal Pacific so our admission included Express Passes. The Express Pass not only lets you into a shorter line but also allows you to go from park to park and to ride the Hogwarts Express. Both parks were very busy when we visited but we really didn't wait more than 25 or 30 minutes even on the rides that were really busy. The Wizarding World of Harry Potter is absolutely worth the price of admission - this was our favorite area by far. We enjoyed the King Kong Ride which hadn't officially reopened but was open intermittently throughout the day and we just happened to pass by when it was open. We also enjoyed Jurassic Park, the Hollywood Rip Ride Rocket, Minion Mayhem, Shrek 4-D, Revenge of the Mummy, the ET Adventure, the Smpsons and Men in Black Alien Attack. The rides are lots of fun. Some of the rides require you to empty your pockets and leave hats, backpacks, sunglasses, etc. The park provides lockers (free) while you ride - just make sure you remember your locker number (they are assigned randomly) and which finger you used as identification (don't laugh - we saw lots of people having problems reopening their lockers!). Universal also has a "child swap" whereby part of your group rides while part waits with smaller kids - then you switch without having to wait in line again - that's a neat feature because there are height restrictions on a lot of the rides. We really enjoyed the park and spent 4 days between Universal and Islands of Adventure - we left the park in the afternoon to swim at the hotel and then came back in the evening when it was less crowded. Unlike Disney, if you stay in a hotel on site you can just walk back and forth in about 15 minutes or take the water taxi - very convenient.
It is an absolute fun for all my grandchildren. Riding all the rides with too much enthusiasm. Non stop running and it excited them to queue again.

We have spent a week with the children in the cabana bay hotel which is a universal hotel just next door. My review on the hotel you can see separate from this review (which is very good). First of all in summer I think it's too hot to go there, if you are in a universal hotel at least you have the nice option to stay at the hotel during the hottest part of the day between lunch and 6 o'clock in the evening. Then what annoys me the most was, that you have to make a line for virtually everything: to buy anything you have to make a line, to refill your drink you have to make a line, to get to the bus for the park you have to wait in line, to enter the park you have to make a line, it doesn't matter whether or not you come well prepared, even if you buy your tickets online you still have to make the lines, and last but not least you're standing in line to make a complaint; of course you have to make the lines for the attractions too, at least there you are usually waiting in the shade with a cooling fan on you or you wait inside an air conditioned room with something to see at least. To get a drink you have to stand in the sun. The attractions themselves are very entertaining very well done and to a very high-level, I really did enjoy them. if it's worth to stand in line for more than 25 minutes I will have to leave that up to you. The attractions I liked the most where of course Harry Potter both sides (One half of Harry Potter land is situated in Islands of adventure the other half is in Universal Studios- you can take the train from one side to the other). I noticed that a lot of people there don't really speak English so don't expect to get what you asked for. For example I bought a drink with free refills for the entire stay just to find out the next day that i misunderstood that the drink was only for the day. If you think you want to complain and stand in the line to do so it will be very disappointing because complaining doesn't get you anything, you get trained employees attending your complaints very professionally, but I noticed most people did not get what they wanted or needed. By the way there many people complaining about those drinks. So over all it was a very nice experience I'm glad I did it but I would not do it again.
I walked and rode so many rides and had a ball. It was such an amazing trip with my daughter and my 2 grandchildren.

We chose Universal as our kids had been to several of the other parks on previous trips to Orlando. Our boys are 8 & 9, so too old for the kiddie rides but not quite tall enough for the roller coasters at other parks. We thought Universal would be good because they were tall enough for everything they offer.  Showed up and two adult/two kids passes with FastPass came to $927. Sticker shock.  We entered and the FastPass lines weren't much better than the regular lines. Worse, the place is about as worn out as it gets....reminded me of a cheesy place somewhere in Myrtle Beach.  The roller coaster is good but beyond that, very unimpressive. The Mummy ride was okay, at best and otherwise it's just a bunch of those rides where they put a movie screen in front of you, 3-D goggles on your face, and the chair moves around in an effort to trick your brain into thinking you're on a ride.  I will say that the Harry Potter section is interesting but if you're not into HP, it's whatever. Even if you are into it, not enough to justify an afternoon there.  Finally, no energy whatsoever compared to any of the Disney parks. No music, no characters, nothing inspiring. Avoid at all costs.

Universal Studios is a definite must do while in Florida. My family loved it. The Harry Potter attractions are worth the wait time. We loved the Harry Potter and the Escape from Gringotts ride and the details in the Wizarding World of Harry Potter are a must see for everyone.
Amazing experience seeing transformes and the simpsons walking around. Best rides in the world. Its the best money you can spend for entertainment.

Every time I come here I vow never to do so again. There are some good rides but the queueing system is dreadful - if you pay a fortune or stay in a Universal hotel you jump the queue with the result the normal queues are crazy and you can't rely on the wait times.  It's also prone to overcrowding although not as much as Islands of Adventure next door which is far worse.  Shame as there are some good rides like Transformers, Revenge of the Mummy, Hollywood Rip Ride Rocket and The Simpsons.  I found Gringots disappointing too. Overall Disney is far, far better in my opinion.

Have visited here many times before and feel the addition of Diagon Alley and Kings Cross station with the Hogwarts Express between both parks is great. We moved between the 2 parks throughout the day and found it so much better as we could take the train each time and the queues were only about 10 mins each time. We were disappointed that the Hulk Ride was shut as its being upgraded, but really want to return next year as it was the best ride and so hopefully it will be even better.  One main criticism, please can the park provide more seats for people waiting for members of their party who are queuing for rides. I no longer go on roller coasters and have an injury and found that I struggled to find seating whilst waiting for my family. The worst of the lot is the ride Rip Ride Rocket, this is no where to sit, and NO SHADE so I felt quite ill by the time my family came off the ride.

We took the Harry Potter train to transfer to universal studios after completing a very enjoyable morning. We had a plan so we knew what we wanted to try out, the Mignons , Shrek, MIB and Transformers We had bought the express pass, which was very useful as the lines were huge. We expected a lot of the Mignons attractions but was as great as we thought, it felt just like another 4D experience. Except that the kids had a lot of fun, they liked the parade at 7pm and did not want to leave at the of the day

I have been to this park many times but today had issues I want to share so that others may not experience the same problems. Firstly avoid the rip off parking charges do not upgrade your parking. Just pay the normal rate you still get to the parks. Buy your tickets before visiting as I will tell you the issues with this. After clearing security we then formed into the queue to purchase the tickets. Needless to say this was slow as the staff were wanting to sell add on features. After an hour yes an hour got to the staff member ordered the tickets then handed credit card. Sorry cannot accept this without your passport. Who takes a passport to a theme park ? Next when proved a point that it is not a requirement to show a passport to use visa, and having purchased meals in the park with a credit card where no ID was required. Staff member then went into robot mode, have you any photo ID again I said it was not necessary as used card here days earlier and not required. Then the usual happens when faced with not in the script then says to a supervisor I have an issue with this man. I am now an issue not a customer.So by now I am not happy, directed to guest relations, who said it was policy to ask for ID when using credit card. Sorry used card in Universal Boardwalk no one asked for ID. Also pointed out to staff that no where does it state on entrance that I D is required to use a credit card. As we where meeting friends in park could I get a message to them to tell them we would be delayed. Sorry no can do. At this point even if I had ID no way was I giving them my money. Oh it took me another 45 minutes to get to see someone at guest services. For a park that prides itself on new rides maybe they could invest in chip and pin ?  So walking back to the car saw another guest service who were helpful in that they placed a message on. Their customer service screen that if friends asked for us they would find out we were unable to join them. Thanks staff. Universal how come I can buy merchandise and food bill using credit card without ID but not tickets can you explain ?  Or was it today your staff member got out the wrong side of bed and became a jobsworth ?  So to all visitors take ID just in case and enjoy yourselves if you get in. If you speak sense and put forward reasonable arguments do not expect the same in return. You will be met with a robotic reply.  Thank you Universal for ruining a family and friends day out.
Had a great time. So much to see and entertainment for the whole family. The Express Pass is worth it, it saved us so much time not having to wait in long lines.

I love that place there are so many at actions to see and food and rides. There are meet and greets with the minnions , superheros and villains. It's not a bad place to go so plan your next trip to Universal Stodios in Orlando Florida 😄😄😄

This was our second visit in four years, and it didnt disappoint.  I have two boys, a tween and a teenager and clearly Universal is far better geared to boys their age, than Disney is. In addition, I personally feel that Universal is better value for money than Disney.  In case you plan to visit Universal Orlando often, I would recommend the annual pass. Not only does it give you unlimited access, but you can also use the valet parking, get a fastpass after 4:00PM and discounts at the stores.  The new Harry Potter park and the hogwarts express were delightlful, and we were fortunate to have been able to go for the Reign of Kong ride that opened. It was a pity that the Hulk roller coaster was shut throughout our stay.  Will definately visit again.

We haven't been to Universal Studios since 2006. It was my favourite park on my last visit but on this holiday I have to say it is my least favourite. A lot of money has been spent on Islands of Adventure but nothing significant on Universal Studios. A lot of the rides are outdated now and the Terminator show was shockingly bad. Some of the shows I saw on my first visit have now gone but the excitement we experienced in such shows as Earthquake and Twister is not shown in other shows. A huge disappointment and would be along time before I visited again.

Third visit this year and we thought Escape from Gringotts was a great new addition. Miles better than the King Kong, and with much shorter queues. Good planning and an early start means you don't need to pay out for fast passes.

Had 14 day tickets and enjoyed the park as a family of 4 with kids aged 14 & 11. We did not have fast passes but did not have to wait too long for any ride by clever planning. I think the most we waited was for the Minion and that was only about 25 minutes as we managed to get in as last admission before it closed at 10pm. So we went very early or late in the day and went back to our hotel midday to recuperate. Because there is only so much of 3D rides you can cope with. This worked Out really well. I went on the Mummy ride 3 times in a row without waiting late at night using the single riders lane! so make the most of the single riders lane as you usualy end up getting on the same ride anyway. I loved the ET one, it was amazing setting. My 11 year old son loved the Transformers one and my daughter loved the big red roller coaster and went on it 4times. Ensure you have the app and make the most of it to work out waiting times etc. There is free wifi which is great.

Besides Harry Potter and rip rocket coaster there isn't enough here to spend more than 1day. Mummy ride is good and the line is usually not more than 30 minute wait. Men in black is disappointing for older kids. Simpsons ride is ok but not worth a long wait really. Food in Simpsons was pretty good, Chicken and waffle sandwich was good as was fried fish platter but was a long wait in line. Horror makeup show was funny and definitely worth it if you need a break to sit and cool off. Minions was cute but a long wait and show in the queue is a little long. I would not wait 60 minutes though. Rip rocket needs more song selections but it's a good coaster. Had a 4 day pass but next time will only do 2days as it was more than enough even without express passes. Too much walking and costs a fortune for mediocre fast food.

Arrived at noon and had to join a queue to purchase entry. After waiting 20 minutes and we didn't move an inch, we joined another queue. Another 20 minutes passed until we finally were at the front of the queue. This is unacceptable.  As we were only there for the day we purchased tickets for both parks and Express. For 3 adults and 1 child the cost was over $1100!!!! Madness.  We paid begrudgingly and went through the pay booths only to have to join another queue to have our bags checked and then scan our entrance tickets. Enough queueing already!!! This took another 10 minutes...  Express wasn't exactly useful. You jumped a few people but then we're merged into the regular queue which caused friction sometimes with others waiting in the queue who would do their best not to let you in.  We only attended the Shrek 4D in this park and decided to move on to the other park. I'm glad we did as the wait for the Hogwarts train took at least 45 minutes queueing. Bonkers.  When we finally got to the other park we discovered it was over crowded and walking around was stressful and not a great experience. We rode on about 6 rides and by this point it was 9 pm and time to go. We went to the Hogwarts Express and discovered the queue was winding outside of the building and stated a 45 minute wait. Having had enough we asked a staff member how we get out. Unfortunately it was a long walk but no where near as long as a 45 minutes wait while staring into space.  This place is a horrendous. Avoid if you can.

Easily the best theme park in the world. I would recommend spending more than a day here as there is just so much to see and do here! The best time to go would be during the week - try to avoid weekends as they are super busy times. The new addition of Harry Potter is excellent and really transports you to another world. Friendly staff and great location with so many facilities.
Need more than 1 day for parks and express pass. Lines 20-120 minutes. Worth it! Bring drinks/ snacks in line with you. Weekdays lines are slightly shorter.

After many visits to universal this year we booked our tickets with Virgin to get early access. On the day we arrived we decided to buy express park access for what we thought was on the day park access the a single park. Having bought the ticket feeling rushed by the sales person on the front desk we only realised getting back to the villa we actually paid for 2 park ticket express pass when only asking for one .  Really disappointed with the sales tactics by universal studios on this.  Had a great time in the park but just be aware if you are planning to do the same and check the ticket or buy inside the park !

Kept all the family happy and out and about all day. Loved the new areas and loved seeing my all time favourite ride (MIB) still there. Would recommend heading over for opening of the park - you can have breakfast in the leaky cauldron in Harry Potters diagon alley. I went twice within a week and could've done more without getting bored

One of the amusement parks you have to visit! There's so much to offer and rides, but sometimes the wait time can be long. The simpsons area was one of my favorites, but be prepared to pay some big bucks eating at moe's tavern.

Spent over $500 for two people for 2 day park to park passes. Due to extremely long lines we only got on about 5 attractions on our second day. I must say the park is beautiful and the wizarding world is absolutely magical but the lines are ridiculous. Even some of the locker systems are not set up very good. some rides don't allow you to have anything and you have to use a locker, some of the lockers are in tiny buildings with hundreds of people trying to shove their ways in and half the time, there's no open lockers available. It easy to get very frustrated here.

Now this is where the real magic happens!! Oh my, we came here back in 2009, but in 2016 it's just even better. Where else can you fly in a car through cities, have balls of fire thrown at you, get sucked into a vortex and get rescued by Spider-Man and bumblebee?! Where else can you ride 4 miles underneath gringotts bank in a cart fighting dragons? Or even better where on earth would you be able to fly over Hogwarts and play qui ditch with none other than Harry Potter?! Or ride through the jungle and get thrown around by dinosaurs and King Kong!!!! Universal costs a lot of money, but it buys you experiences you cannot get anywhere else, it is just amazing. Even in very hot weather universal have cooling fans and mist fans everywhere to keep you cool, the ques can be long but absolutely worth it! If you get there early you might find barely any que, next time we come I won't be buying other park tickets at all, it'll just be for universal!

Excellent family vacation spot. Great for everyone. First trip was in 2003, was with wife's family. Mother in law is wheel chair bound, and almost every ride she is capable of enjoying. Of course as any there are a few exceptions. I have been 3 times total over the years, each time it gets better. I do miss a few of the old rides, but with limited area to grow, I completely understand the need to update to keep the parks from getting stale. I could move to central Florida if my wife would let us, just to go more often.
This is a definite repeat destination for our family every time we go to Orlando. Your family will always enjoy a day at Universal Studios! Fun for all ages and lots to do!!
Busy place, certainly better for the older children and adults, it was still very hot when we went at this time of year but not as hot as the previous year in June.
This park is great.  Keep an eye on the small print on the maps for when rides shut.  Get yourself a priority pass, costs, but so worth it. If you stay in one of the on-site hotels this comes free.

We loved both Universal and Islands of Adventure. Not like any other park. Period. I like the rides with video, especially 3d more than any coaster. Very impressive. Cooling station, lots of shade, refillable cups (7.99 for the whole day), good shows, well thought out and a great experience. Both of these parks have set a new bar. Wish they were bigger.

We are disney fans but after today I think we may to switch channels . Is been a while since my last visit and still fun . Harry Potter is a total addiction . The entire town is so real. I have to say my favorite ride was King Kong , it made me scream for real . What an awesome ride . We had such a great time and went to both parks and end up completely exhausted . So worst it . Today temperature was like 99 degrees with heat facto or more it was brutal . I realized not a lot places to cool . Overall our 7 miles day walk was a big satisfaction for my birthday boy and the family . Now I need another week to recuperate .. But will be back ...

It amazes me to see people purchasing and/or bringing bottled water into the Parks. Granted it is extremely important to stay hydrated especially during the summer months. However, there is an alternative to buying a $3.29 bottle of water every time you get thirsty. Look for those places where they sell sodas using a fountain system and when requested, they will provide you with a plastic cup of water - with or without ice – with a smile for FREE!  You’ll be drinking the same filtered water the soda fountain machines use the dilute the soda syrup. No need to carry heavy backpacks filled with bottled water. Use your money to purchase and enjoy all those delicious goodies these amazing parks have to offer. HAVE FUN!

Family of 6 with 2 adult's. Great sets walking about,(transformers was the best) a couple of decent rides too, rip curl rollercoaster on which the boys went twice. Took our unlimited drinks cups for another days recharge for $7. Makes sense when a regular drink costs $3.17, pays for itself in no time. Decent shopping for those that like that. Met Beetlejuice, Ms Munroe, Bumblebee and Optimus.

It was amazing! I suggest getting there right when the park opens and maximizing your time there. I recommend at least 2 days there, one day is not enough to see everything. Harry Potter World was incredible! Took my breath away! Lines are long but most move pretty fast. If you want to eat, there are a lot of restaurants to choose from right before you enter Universal Studios.

Form the top. if you are planning a trip to Universal here are some of my tips for you.Stay on site if you can, the perks of staying on site are wonderful, free boat shuttle to parks so you don't have to park, early admission (only Annual Pass or hotel guests) to the park for select rides. Most Orlando hotels your going to pay about 150 a night. with on site hotels you get free express pass that allows you to skip the longer lines.if you like to eat, get the meal deal.Get the app, it gives you wait times.If you're there for a few days get the refillable souvenir cups.If youre going to drink,check out what places have happy our.If older group, single rider line gets you through the lines quicker.SUNSCREEN.free water if you ask for it.plan on going early in AM and then back to hotel in the heat of the day, recover and go back in the PM. eat the food, its good stuff.some rides wont allow personal items and u need a locker, check b4 getting in line. lastly, ride the rides, see the shows

Ohhh, that's place everyone should see, and experience that amazing feeling! Rollercoasters are breathtaking!🙆🏼 we enjoyed it very much. You need two days to see both parks. It's worth it trust me. It's plain to see that a lots of details and effort is put there. I've been there 2 times in each park and I would definitely go there few more time because it's worth it! 👍🏼

This is my first visit to Universal, I was expecting something amazing and it was more than I ever expected, we've been here nearly every night (for the 14days we were here!) All the 3d rides are out of this world, I'm not a big fan of 3d and 4d ride but this park has changed my mind to them!!! The Simpson section of the park is brilliant we spent hours in there!!! We tended to go in the evening as it's cheaper to park (only $5 instead of $20 after 6pm) and the queues aren't as long!!

After visiting Magic Kingdom and Sea World, this was by far the best park. Fantastic thrilling rides. Especially the 3D/4D semi-virtual coaster rides are great! Good food of all sorts, friendly staff. The 2 parks are a bit much for a single-day visit, but we knew that upfront. Lots of entertainment throughout the park. Some rides require the use of lockers to store personal items (metal detectors are used at the entry) but fortunately the lockers are free during the ride and are locked/unlocked with a fingerprint sensor; very convenient.

Simply Fun ! We spent 3 days from morning to evening with non stop fun and amusement. With previous planning and booking park to park tickets in addition to staying at Cabana bay resort for early admission hours we had the maximum of our visit to Universal World . The best part which really rocked our visit was when we got picked to be " the family of the day " !! That was a really awesome experience and surprise which made our vacation a memorable one . We were treated like VIPs having a special seat to watch the parade then we were walked to our attraction of choice with no waiting in lines ! That's how we did the Simpson's ride with no waiting. In addition to lovely souvenir badges and free water on the go . This was a real life experience and the parks were really full of thrilling rides and fun spots . I loved every corner of both parks and I'm now planning to visit Universal studios of Hollywood in LA without any doubt. " I never had this fun since I was a kid " 😉
T2, Transformers, and the Mummy are a must at this park. It's a nice place and good for kids. The food and gift shop are more overpriced than any park I've ever been too.

The park is great some brilliant rides the Simpsons is fantastic but Harry Potter is just out of this world, walking behind that wall and seeing potter world was just unbelievable it left us all gobsmacked.
We loved it make sure to get the EXPRESS PASS it saves you a lot of time in lines we look forward to going back
I first visited in 2005 and 2006 and loved it then. Came back this year and it was just as good! The Harry Potter section is amazing!! Food a bit overpriced but nice enough! Best holiday ever!

My family really likes this park. Don't send the Disney police after me - but we are starting to like it more than Disney.  It rained for a couple hours the day were were there but most of the rides are indoors so it wasn't a problem. We just bought a $10 poncho and kept on going

We enjoyed our three days of Universal Florida! The attractions and rides are really well done and many are absolutely thrilling. Loved the Diagon Alley/Escpate from Gringotts'. Most rides were above expectations. The only (minor) disappoint was the corn dogs. These had to be the worst corn dogs I've ever had! Otherwise -- everyone in our family was super happy!

Overall good time even with rain. Ticket prices are expensive long lines made us get the express pass since we were only there for the day. Train was broke down basically all day, disappointing. Not sure if it was worth the cost but rides are very good mostly couple older ones could have skipped.

We had 4 day tickets to Universal Orlando, spent 2 of the 4 at this park. This has been a long time favorite park of mine, with us returning every time we visit the Orlando area. This visit was far below normal standards. Within our first hour in the park, THREE different rides broke down, all three only after a very long wait in each of the three lines. I know things happen but to have our day start this way really set the unfortunate tone for the whole day. We noticed that the que areas and also sets for some of the rides had damage to them (done intentionally from guests), with all of the money that this park brings in on a daily basis I left there really wondering why they don't seem to bother keeping the park looking nice and better maintaining the rides, both to ensure a better guest experience. Not to compare parks but Disney would NEVER allow an area to look anything less than perfect and maintained. Really disappointed this time.

This park was amazing when we got there we didn't realized it was 2 parks bonus we thought smashed the 1st one then upgraded the 2nd park to fast track that was incredible ride so fast never had to wait longer then 5 minutes was a lot better then the LA universal bigger and so much more to do from photos to rides to food :)
4th of July: crowd, hot, no fireworks and no easy to get out, about 2.000 people wants to leave the park and the doors closed, was not only annoying was also dangerous

Good! Do go it is an amazing park. The new Harry Potter parks are fantastic. I LOVED the broom ride. Meals at the three Broomstick and the Leaky Caldron were really good and plenty of food. Butter beer is fantastic. Beverages and food were not cheap but …it’s a theme park so…no surprise, you should expect that it will cost. Speaking of ‘Lines’ I suggest you get a fast pass for 1 day and only 1 day. Dedicate that day to only fast pass rides. These are going to be the older exhibits and rides. A fast pass will cost almost 100 bucks but, at 60-90 minutes a line without it…do the math and pick which you want to spend more of. Time or Money.
