Also the get into the park an hour early was pretty great. We got to hit some long line rides before too many people were there, and it made us get our act together and get to the park. This gave us more time to play. You can possibly do it get the wizard photo, it was so much fun to do the green screen for it and it really is a good deal. The employees at the park were always friendly and easy going. Get one of those lanyards with a square plastic sleeve at the end. You can keep your tickets, passes, and ID in there and it is safe and available. BAD! Don’t fall for the “package” deal. It is horrible. You have no power when things are really messed up, and they WILL be messed up. Then nobody in the trifecta of screwing up is responsible for any of it. Allow me to spell that out. They book your flight, this will be the worst available flying times and even to the point of one Delta employee telling me it was illegal to book a connection like what we had. You will leave the Hotel at 4:00 am, and your connecting flights will be already boarding if not leaving when you land. Delta will say it is Universal who booked the flight and Universal will say it was Delta who set the schedule, but in the end it you who will either miss a flight or hurt yourself trying to get to a second terminal in 10 minutes whilst dragging children behind you. Packages are a get out of responsibility free card for all the businesses involved. They even charge you an extra “late booking fee” at the Cabana Bay when your flights are all screwed up. Also your room will be the very last room as far away from the lobby as it get’s. Buyer Beware The valet package service is a blessing and a curse. Yeah! I can buy stuff and not have to carry it around the park all day. They will deliver it to your Hotel. OMG did I really buy that much stuff! How will I get it home. In addition to either the hotel unable to find all of your stuff or the park failing to deliver your stuff. I do not know which is the case…see the Trifecta comment above. Don’t waste your time in the King Kong line…it’s a bit lame. Unless you are collecting Pokimon, it is genius that they have stocked the 90 minute line trail with them. It is NOT available for fast pass as of this post. If you get a multiple day ticket you have to hang onto it for the entire time. Do not lose it. I suggest again the lanyard with the plastic pocket. Keeps all the stubs you will need available and dry. You will need it a lot. Especially if you do multiple lands or days.

I would recommend going here. Lots of rides to go on and lots to see for the family also. Great to do a lot of walking. Shopping was excellent and great customer service also. Lots of water refill stations around to get fresh water.

First Trip to Orlando and absolutely loved everything especially Universal studios The wizardry world of Harry Potter was absolutely Fantabulous. Never thought I would would get to visit but loved it and really looking forward to planning another adventure. 💕

Visited Universal for two days - very enjoyable - second day much better as it was the day we visited Harry Potter world - outstanding experience - the tour plus the 3D ride - felt like we were flying - roller coasters also excellent - other good rides were Spiderman and the water rides - all in agreement that the Terminator experience was not good  First day the Mummy ride and the Simpsons were good and ET always enjoyable  2nd day much better and more to do  Had three good salads in Emerils - nice setting good food - service slow  Tip - if looking for a good hotel try the Hyatt on International drive - very good with large pool facilities
Great place. The kids love it, as do their parents. Gringetts, Minnions, Simpsons, The mummy, great fun. Go early and beat some of the queues. $20 per day parking adds up.
Harry Potter rides and the new King Kong ride not included in Quick Queue/Fastpass wristbands or tix. Wait times similar to standby. Save your money for Disney

We took 3 teenagers to Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure with a park hopper pass for 1 day. Because of the huge line ups 30- 90 minutes in 95F heat we paid a lot - $1500 - for the 5 of us for park hopper passes with the Express pass for 2 parks for 1 day!!! We looked at all the rides on the internet before we went and the kids picked their 12 top rides that they really wanted to go on the most. We did manage to get all 12 rides in from both parks in one day with the Hogwarts Express Train between the 2 parks. 6 of the rides were not included in the express pass including the 2 Harry Potter Rides, the train between the parks as well as King Kong and the Hulk. The wait for the 2 Harry Potter rides and the train were over 60 minutes each!! The Harry Potter - Forbidden Journey in the Islands of Adventure was the Best of the 2 Harry Potter Rides! The kids other favorite rides were the Transformers and Rip Ride Rocket. They found the rides much more exciting than the rides at Disney. I recommend paying the extra for the Express Pass especially in the heat and the long line ups and planning ahead so you can do the 2 parks in 1 day! It was more time and cost effective that way! With the express pass the lines were from 10 - 20 minutes!

As with all the parks be ready to stand in queues for long periods of time unless you invest in express passes. Great fun though, the simulator rides have improved so much over the years, they're so realistic. Particularly liked Transformers. Don't bypass the horror makeup show, very amusing.

We took a group of 6 to the park, 4 teens and 2 adults. We arrived at 10 AM and were easily able to see and do the things we were interested in before the park closed. I encourage everyone to use the single rider line on the large attractions to reduce wait time. You stand next to your group in the line and half the time you end up riding with someone in your group. Even when you don't get to ride with someone in your group the rides only last a few minutes. This process will save you hours of waiting in line and you don't have to pay the extra for the express pass. The food in the park was provided in large portions and I didn't feel that the cost was out of range. I did bring a bag of snacks and everyone brought a drink in with them to get the day started. There were lockers at most of the rides to put it in.

Park was nice. Lots of simulator rides but the Transformers and Gringotts Bank ride were great. Guest services staff were really helpful when we needed them. Park is small enough to see it in a day if needed. Food and drinks are expensive but buying a refillable cup is a good investment.
My favorite of all the Orlando parks. There is plenty to do for all age groups and if you stay a few of the onsite hotels you get free fast passes.

Awesome place for H.P. fans. You can't use express passes on top rides and you don't need them for the others, so don't waste your money. Watch for the dragon on Gringotts to spew fire - about every half hour. Olivanders is almost always packed so figure on spending some time to get a wand. $50 should cover most of them. Some are quite intricate in carving. Leaky Cauldron food is quite good. Hogwarts Express is nicely done. Would like to have ridden several more times, but too busy. Our group bought multiple boxes of frogs but they all had the same card in them. Hogwarts was a great ride in the castle - flying with Harry & friends. Loved it.! Gringotts is a good one too, my friends told me. Not as wheelchair or scooter friendly as Disney.

We went here 3 times and the above roller coaster is mental but very very good, may rides here are of the 3D variety but the kids love them and we took the option many times to go on the single rider lines and got to go round them all in 1 day. My daughters favourite ride was the mummy's curse and she adored this and the fact it went so fast and the dark she loved. The diagon alley here was amazing and universal have this so right especially with the wands features for the kids.... 2 nod best theme park of the holiday my kids which they were here now.

I have to say as a previous employee of Universal (which was over 13 years ago) I still love this place. I always feel like a kid when I walk through the turnstiles. So many things to do and see. You will have a fun action packed day. Things have changed since I have worked there and some great classic rides that been retired, but new ones have replaced them and you won't be disappointed. I'm not a Harry Potter fan, but the ride is amazing and almost make me want to read the books and or watch the movies. If you come to just mid Sept-Oct you must try Halloween Horror Nights (of course only if you like to be scared) It is absolutely a great experience. I would recommend getting the express pass to get into all the fast and avoid the over an hour long waits. I really want to get my nephew an annual pass, but he is still a little short for some rides and he always wants to do everything. Annual passes are the way to go though. You will get a lot of perks and save a bunch a money. I got the top one because if offers so many great benefits.

Not been for a few years so we did ten heights are a universal hotel cabana bay which is a brilliant place to stay. We went to see the diagon alley as it wasn't built last time we went. Well I'm not a huge Harry Potter fan but wow wow wow it was amazing every single detail was fantastic .

We visited Orlando for about the 9th time as a family with tots to teenagers and Universal is always our most visited park . There is something for everyone in this park . I have a walking problem and always use a scooter around the parks and there is absolutely no problems getting around as everything is well spaced . Lots of the Non-Red-Knuckle rides are wheelchair accessible . Obviously the larger rides like the Rocket and the Hulk are not suitable but the rest of our family enjoyed them . Definitely our most used pass is the one to Universal !

Visiting universal studios is NO waste of your time and money. Your children will have a great time and you the parent will be happy because it is money well spent. The movies in the theater using 4D glasses will make you feel directly involved in the act. The free coke refill was something we all enjoyed. The PARADE was done went it was still bright so we were able to record and share via Facebook and everyone that saw it said its a place to visit

I have used the VIP Services at Universal 3 times in Florida and once in California. It is truly the best way to experience a theme park. The Perks included in your experience: 1. Valet Parking - NO line ups, safe and convenient! 2. Continental Breakfast - Muffins and other sweet pastries, cereal, whole fruit, coffee, tea, hot chocolate. They also have free bottles of water for you to grab for the day. 3. Ponchos - for rain or for the wet rides! 4. Guide - this is the best part! I have never had the same guide and therefore, never had the exact same experience. They all come with their own tidbits of information though. Inside info and places that the rest of park goers cannot see or hear about. 5. Front of the line for all major rides - this is NOT Express Pass. This is back door into the attraction directly to the front of the line. No waiting. 6. Food Voucher Card - We were able to get 1 quick service meal (no sit down to be served restaurants), 2 drinks and one snack/dessert. I didn't end up spending a cent on food or parking the whole day. 7. Unlimited Express Pass - after the tour was over (about 5 or 6 hours) our VIP card allowed us to go through the express pass for all the rides that offer it for the remainder of the day. Not as fast as when you are with the guide, but 10 -15 mins wait, rather than an hour or 2. 8. Discount - after your tour, your VIP card gets you discounts on your purchases in stores.  Tips: a) Book ahead as busy times can fill up. b) If you have a big enough group, get the private tour c) Do both parks. You have the time, might as well save money and just go the one day. You will HATE having to wait in line after you haven't. d) If your guide does a great job, tip them! e) Be ready to walk a lot! You don't want to be the one slowing the rest of the group down. d) Shop and take photos after the tour. This tour is so you can get on as many rides as possible with the shortest wait. Do that stuff after, you will have time. e) Don't be late! This includes in the morning as well as after lunch. You are holding up other families :)  ***Additional ways to save*** -For anyone visiting Universal with an American Express Credit Card- *Use your card to buy your tickets and you will have access in to the American Express Lounge. It is a nice, air conditioned room with tv and couches as well as drinks and snacks. This was all free to us, just for having an Amex. -If you have an AMA or CMA card *Discounts given on food and merchandise purchases.
Wonderfull place to visit with family and friends e i will return many times because i love it! It's a amazing park!
we visited this site twice and really enjoyed it. the staff working there are all very helpful and friendly

Even a theme park where people often come with friends or families turned out to be the memorable part of my solo trip.I really had an awesome time visiting both Island of Adventures and Universal Studios. The Hogwarts Express ride from one park to another, took me back to the childhood.  I had to buy the ticket from an agent at my Hotel since I decided to visit Studios an hour before.  Biometric lockers at each ride area helped me keeping my stuff safe as being a solo traveler this is one's constant worry.  Staff is very helpful.

This place is some amazing fun! There is something for everyone, but it is seriously worth splurging for an express pass. Otherwise, you'll be stuck in massive lines for forever. There are comic book based rides and restaurants , Toon Land, The Mummy ride, and all kinds of fun to be had.

Please forgive my cynicism but I left two days of Universal Orlando thinking: I just don't get it. Sadly, I left the park each day thinking that the whole thing is just one giant scam to separate people from their money. I wouldn't mind if I felt as if I got value for the hours waiting in sweltering lines and up-sales around every corner.  While I simply don't see the magic, my kids (6 & 8) seemed to love the place. In the end, it's all about the family experience and watching the joy on your kid's faces. Universal Orlando (both parks) did make my kids smile a lot, and that may mean my review is moot.  I can only write what I genuinely feel and I just wasn't feel'n it! I really can't pin point why I enjoy the "mouse's house" so much more, especially when you consider the similarities between the theme parks. If you take your kids to Universal they'll probably love it, especially the Harry Potter areas, but this adult is one visitor who left the parks with an itch that wasn't scratched and a hunger that wasn't satiated.  One final note, every last employee I encountered everywhere at Universal Orlando were fantastically helpful, and friendly. The parks are very clean and felt very safe. I'd love to know the repeat customer numbers for the various big players in theme park entertainment because I won't be coming back to Universal Orlando.

I hadn't been here in 16 years since my youngest was 9. I love this place, the simulation attractions are among the best, with the best of all being The Transformers. However, the cost has become ridiculous! $!20 was our discounted cost. There is nothing about this park that is worth that. An average sized middle class family would have to save for years or go into debt in order to afford to bring their family. So sad....
Get there early to beat the long Harry Potter queues, waited almost 2 hours but was worth it. Loads of other great rides between the 2 parks.

Overall a good time at Universal. Loved the rides. Teens thought this was a great place for our family vacation. Universal has the potential to be an even better park than Disney if they keep up with them on a few areas notably service and technology.  The Good: Rides are amazing. Harry Potter area is so well done. Stayed at the hard rock hotel and was a short walk to hotel. Staying at universal hotel allows for express pass to reduce wait times at rides. Teens enjoyed universal more than Disney, but this is due to age and amount of rides available to them. Parks are walking distance to each other which is great.  The Bad: After visiting Disney with magic bands, the ticket and scanning process at Universal seemed cumbersome. We bought a 3 day park to park pass. Each day there was something wrong with one of the kids entrances. Either the finger print not recognizing it, to our last day one kid showed no days left, when the remaining 4 in our party were through already. Took 40 minutes to figure it out after being sent to a customer service line and were told it was due to the Kong ride express pass scan actually scanning park ticket. Seemed odd to me the park would have a system that would take 2 days off park entrance for the same day. Anyways, gave us express tickets for Harry Potter for inconvenience. These were not useful as kids working in ride area just sent us to regular line. Advertisement for early park admission if staying at hotel on site. When we went early, general public was going in also and were not checking for room keys.  Hard rock hotel was ok, but nothing like Disney contemporary. Doors slam and paper thin walls. Staff working at check-in were not what is expected for this price. Had to go to 4 areas to get tickets and checkin complete, which seemed ineffective. Disney hotel all done in 5 minutes and one person.

Visited Universal Studios with family - 6 adults and 4 children in April 2016. Spent one day (thank goodness that was all) there. Food lines were horribly long and took F-O-R-E-V-E-R. the food itself was just OK. I waited in one line where there were 7 people in line ahead of me, it took 45 minutes to get a drink! Seems that the person working the stand was more interested in asking everyone where they were from, if they had any grandchildren and talking about her grandchildren. I heard the same comments and questions 6 times before I got to the front of the line. Similar issue with lunch where the lines were SLOW moving. I do not complain when there is a reason for long/slow lines, but they were not that busy that day and seemed to have more than enough help to process the orders. Once we finally got the food it was just OK. The 'other' Orlando venue was great in both lines and food quality aspects.

What's not to like...well maybe the prices for food and drink. But this place has something for everyone. Harry Potter to Minions to The Simpsoms. I went on almost every ride! Oh, and get the Express Pass!! Well worth it!! Family Memories Made Here!
Great place for kids and adults!! Loved it here so much!! So many things to do here! Great from age 1-99 years old. lol

What an awesome theme park. My family and I loved it. The first ride we target for was the Transformers. What an awesome virtual ride. It felt so real the way the vehicle was moving around. But I have to say the Harry Potter & The Forbidden Journey virtual ride was the best. You do not need to wear 3D glasses to experience. You are riding a 4 seater sideways and all of the action was intense. It almost felt like you are flying together with Harry Potter.  You will definitely need at least 2 days for Universal Studios. There is a Universal Studios theme park which includes the Transformers, Terminator, The Mummy, Minions, Shrek, and the Simpsons. The other park is called Island Of Adventures which includes, Harry Potter, Jurassic, King Kong Skull Island, and Marvel Superhero Island.  Buying the express pass for these rides are definitely worth it. You will pass all of the long lines. Unfortunately not all of the rides accepts the express pass such as the King Long Skull Island or Harry Potter.  Great enjoyable experience. Definitely worth coming back
Love all the rides at Universal. The food is great, staff is nice. worth the price of tickets. bring your own food.

Had the best time of our lives. Harry Potter wizarding world was amazing. If you are going during a holiday weekend, plan on getting the express passes. The regular wait time for any ride is very long during peak season. We visited the studios for two days and had to wait for really long time (it was a thanksgiving weekend). Fireworks at the end of the day was pretty cool.

We came here the first week of September. It wasn't too busy and the waits for the tides weren't too long. We had rain for some of our visit but there were still a lot of people at the park and everyone (including us) had panchos. They have a good variety of rides. My 4 year old daughter and preteen sons liked the Minions and Shrek rides. There were a lot of rides that my daughter was too young for but that my pre teen sons liked.

I last visited Orlando 13 years ago and this was my favourite park. This time it was my worst day out!!! The queues were horrendous, most exceeding 90 minutes, for rides and attractions that didn't have the wow factor I remembered. I'm not a thrill rider, so the movie themed experiences are my thing, but too many 3D/4D based rides, which are too similar, have taken away that wow factor and replaced it with the 'not worth queuing for' factor. The Parade was very unimaginative, with many key characters missing, including Scooby Doo and Superheroes/Villains. Overall, extremely disappointed. Please note, this review does not cover the Wizarding World of Harry Potter or Islands of Adventure, both of which are excellent.

First of All, the walk from the parking lot to the main gate is about a mile or more & we got the 'premium' parking. there are people-movers for some of the distance, but it's still a long haul & you're not even in the park yet! The main attraction for us was the Harry Potter exhibit - but beware- you have to buy the 'park-hopper' pass to get the full experience. But that for us, this was the best part of the park. The roller coaster my son wanted to go on- the hulk- was out of service so he & my nephew were very disappointed. the walk-ways through both parks are very narrow so you feel very cramped; there's no breeze & on a hot day in july it was miserable. Everything felt very contrived, from the rides to the buildings to the overhead music. The big nighttime show was a letdown as well. We did have nice meal at the Italian restaurant that is just outside the main entrance.
Superb. The new upgraded hulk made this 47 year old feel like a kid again ! Harry Potter is amazing get there early if you can.

I can never remember which rides are at which park but here is my list of rides in order of preference. 1 being not too missed, 2 fun and enjoyable 3 can be missed. I am not big on extreme rides. My kids rode them so I just added their comments down below.  1 HP and the Forbidden Journey HP Escape to Gringoths Return of the Mummy Spiderman  2 Transformers - very cool Simpsons ride - quite fun, hilarious, I got dizzy Shrek 4D - funny and entertaining but the chairs move too much. Ripsaw Falls - you will be soaked for sure so try to go in the middle of the day when you can dry off. Skull Island Reign of Kong - Kong and creatures were very realistic.  3 Men in Black - you sit in a ride and just shoot aliens, kinda lame. Poseidon's Fury - this is a really a show not a ride, pretty boring and the host wasn't even funny Jurassic Raft Adventure - quite tame, just 1 dip. Flight of the Hippogriff - quite tame too, it's like the Seven Dwarfs Mine train ride at WDW  According to my kids, Dragon Challenge was the most fun, next was the Rip Ride Rocket and the most tame of the extreme rides was the Incredible Hulk Doctor's Doom Fearful was OK, not as scary as it looks. Hope you enjoyed my brief review.

Universal Studios is the original Universal park and our first visit was 1990, and it keeps us coming back. It is a movie goers dream as you wander through film set areas and indulge in the movies. It also has some fantastic thrill seekers rides including The Mummy, Rip Ride Rocket, The Simpsons, Transformers and now Diagon Alley which takes it to a whole new level. the whole area is spectacular and topped off with Gringotts and Hogwarts Express allowing you to move to Islands of Adventure park without leaving.

I thought that every I was dotted and every T was crossed when I booked our visit to take our grandchildren to Universal Studios. We were excited! Our reservations were made by the Universal travel agency so I thought we were covered. Yes, our hotel accommodations were wonderful and the ticket pick up was convenient, however, no one mentioned to tell us that if you choose to get early admission to Harry Potter, you must stay at Islands of Adventure. That issue almost cost us an additional $250.00 since we only bought a 1 day park pass and wanted to go to Universal Studios, not Islands of Adventure, which was not really age appropriate for our 6 yr old. With an Aug sun beating down on me, I was directed to guest services where I stood in line to see what could be done to correct this misunderstanding. No one told us that we couldn't re-enter our park of choice. Finally after 2+ hrs, our issue was resolved. Our grandchildren were hot, tired and bummed out. My husband was frustrated and somewhat stressed as he entertained 3 disappointed kids. By the time we entered the park, it was after 11:30am and the lines for rides were +30min wait. Even with fast pass, the lines were long. In addition, The Mummy ride was not operating. We also bought food passes for the day that offered us lunch and a snack. Everything that we ordered was inedible. The kids chicken fingers were like rubber, fries were cold and burgers were like hockey pucks. Finally, the kids asked to leave. We left before 3 pm and went back to Mia after spending well over $1000.00 ++ for an overnight and 1 day park pass at Universal Orlando. What a trip NOT to remember!
I visited Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure recently with my 2 teenage children and I had the BEST time of my life- absolutely FANTASTIC!!!!!!
The place is fantastic, a week wouldnt be enough time to see this place through. For a comic fan like myself it's an absolute dream to go here, the spiderman ride and Hulk are absolutely phenomenonal
Came acros Diagonal Alley quite by accident, what a treat. Fire breathing dragon on top of Gringots is brilliant. Then took the Hogwarts Express over to Howarts : )

Has been a while since we've visited. Probably visited 10 years ago. Lots of things have changed. Went on almost all the rides yesterday. Staff was friendly, although when you go to refill your soda, and you honestly don't know where to go to get your refill, the staff gets a little rude by telling you that you have to go to a different station when they could just be nice and fill it for you there. (Just saying!) Otherwise, the rides were great. Better to eat on the City Walk at the REAL restraunts though. You might pay a couple of dollars more per plate, but definately better than eating at the park.

This was my first trip to Universal in Florida. I must say that I was very impressed with how efficient the park is run. Upon entering the parking lot and being guided by the parking attendants everything was made very easy. Even the walk to the park from the lot was easy and quick. Security was very friendly and entering at the gate was fast and easy. And then there's the park.  I loved it all. My favorites are Springfield and of course the World of Harry Potter. It is just so well done and fun. I really felt like "I was there". And the rides overall were awesome. I tell my friends that while Universal is great for kids it also has more to offer adults than "the other place". And even though there is a lot to see it is manageable to do so in one day.  The food was also good and considering it is a theme park was priced pretty fairly.  I would definitely visit again.
Great park for what you are paying. Tons to do, and many great places to eat inside the park, and very reasonably priced.

Universal and island of adventure:  - The parking is great 20$, 30$ preferred. - The staff have this great attitude, really nice. -Thrills, are awesome, HULK the best, Dragon Challenge spectacular, the ReVenge of the MUMMY spectacular, Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit awesome. - 3Ds, Forbidden Journey is awesome, Transformers great, Escape from Gringotts very cool, King Kong really cool. Water attractions, you could buy a poncho and you will be really fine, no need to carry more clothes.  Overall, Universal is superior Walt Disney parks for adults, obviously children would love Disney!!!

So much to do with so little time! I would suggest going early or reserve for two days, unless you purchase the Universal Express Pass. We visited this theme park in September. It was a hot day, but fortunately the majority of the rides are in doors! If you are looking for fierce roller coasters, than I would say go to Islands of Adventure or Busch Gardens. Universal Studios offers indoor roller coasters (except Rip Ride Rocket), which are just as fun! We purchased a room at the onsite Portofino Bay Hotel. They offer great perks! One of the perks was the free Unlimited Express Pass. The express is definitely worth the money! However, September is not a busy month and some of the rides won't allow express pass. Such as, Harry Potter, Shrek, and Terminator. If you intend to go in September then I wouldn't spend the extra $89 for the express pass. Also, it's definitely worth purchasing the unlimited soft drinks! They are about $15 but each drink is anywhere from $5 to $10.

Visited primarily for all things Harry Potter -- and Universal did not disappoint. It was HOT, and HUMID, but plenty of places to get something cold to drink or stand in the shade. And outside of all things Harry Potter -- lot's of fun water-related rides. And yes, you WILL get wet. Glad we visited. Had a great time.

Started off with base one day ticket but upgraded to two park . Best decision ever . Best to have this spread out over a few days . Struggled to complete all rides in one day . Next time will get the 14 days option and plan using the universal studios app.
Love the virtual and 3D rides. Great for the marvel fans with a bit of Harry Potter thrown in. Nice eateries and reasonably priced as compared to Disney! Staff are really helpful
For one day is pricy if you're out of state. food and drink isn't to bad... but to get in is steep for people going for just a day.

Like Islands of Adventure, the Universal Studios park is excellent, particularly Diagon Alley. For anyone who has seen the Harry Potter films (and even for those that haven't) can surely appreciate the detail that has gone into the area. The Escape from Gringotts ride is excellent as well, the whole queue leading up to the ride is amazing too.  No detail has been missed, the Knockturn Alley, Olivanders, Leaky Cauldron etc. Besides Harry Potter, the other main areas of the park are the 'Hollywood' section, 'New York', 'Kids Zone' and 'Simpsons'.  While there are some great attractions, Universal seem to over rely on simulators quite a bit. Minions, Transformers, The Simpsons, (the new Jimmy Fallon ride) plus Spiderman area all simulators - in fact Spiderman and Transformers are nearly identical. That being said, Minions is very enjoyable as is the Simpsons (though they are both a bit jerky). The Mummy is also an excellent rollercoaster, and never attracts too long a wait. Also you've got to love ET, glad that its still here as its a classic.  All the team members we encountered were friendly, and the park was clean. Food could do with some improvement, the Krusty Burger really wasn't impressive. Besides that though, theres little to complain about. Definitely worth a visit.

Pretty neat ride but not having a any breakfast sure did not help. The ride does do quite a bit of sudden stops, spins and ups and downs. I had to shut my eyes to stop from having an unfortunate accident. I got my bearings and enjoyed the ride nonetheless. Great special effects!
Just reviewed Islands of adventure & this was similarly enjoyable. Simpsons, the rocket, terminator were all great. Would highly recommend.
When you are in Orlando you need to stop here. Harry Potter is amazing and City Walk is lots of fun. Great place to spend some time and money

My first time at this park & had a great time! Diagon Alley & The Simpsons Springfield were our two favorite areas of this park. Our favorite rides were RipTide Rollercoaster, Shrek 4-D (kid friendly), The Mummy, The Simpsons ride, Escape From Gringotts, and Hogwarts Express (kid friendly). As huge Simpsons fans, We love having a Duff beer at Moe's Tavern. We also very much enjoyed fish n chips & frozen butter beer at the Leaky Cauldron. The Blues Brothers show & car was also a lot of fun. We didn't get to do it all due to weather shutting all outdoor rides for about two hours but we'll be back.

If you have a choice to go to only one part go to Islands of Adventure ( the sister park) you will have much more fun. This park is getting a little tired and not being updated much. They need more rides. There is the new harry potter section which is good. For little kids this part is great.

So we spent 1 day here last year and weren't impressed. This year we spent 3 days here and had a BLAST!! We did everything (except Hulk which was closed and Rocket) we thoroughly enjoyed The Wizarding World of Harry Potter. Those rides were crazy!!! The funniest part was that we found ourselves ducking into rides we may not have thought about going on just to get out of the heat...then found that the ride was excellent!! Hubby did not feel that Kong was worth the 90 minute wait however. If you must do it and it's still hot in Orlando, do it at night like we did. Otherwise, had an awesome time and we will probably be back in a few years. We just hope they don't kill the E.T. ride by then, we still love it!!!
you will take parts in continuation of many of your favorite movies, they add you to the story in events of a live show or roller-coasters, very fun specially with the family

My husband and I traveled from Georgia to spend 2 days at Universal Studios. Friday we did Island of Adventure and Halloween Horror Nights, Saturday we did Universal Studios. Island of Adventure: Starting off, after waiting in line for 40+ min for the Hulk we decided to buy the Express Pass. It was worth every penny. Since we will likely not be visiting again anytime soon, this pass allowed us to easily ride everything in one day with minimal waiting times (no more than 20 min). We bought the unlimited pass for 1 park, but only used it more than once for the Skull Island Ride. You really only need the 1 time pass, its hard to do more than that in a day. Hulk was amazing, Skull Island was great, but not worth a huge wait line (the ride is short). If it rains they bypass the outside drive around to the entry of the cave too, which can be disappointing. Dudley Falls ride will get you soaked - so be prepared or you can pay $5 dollar for the human blow dryer, lol. Jurassic world was fantastic as always, and the Raptor Experience is a must do for all ages! Hint: give them your phone for free video recording! Harry Potter was great!! There was hardly any wait (a thunderstorm was looming) and the set house was built and designed so well! We missed out on the Dueling Dragons due to lighting in the area. Poseidon's adventure is awesome too. HHN 26: TERRIFIC!!! The Haunted Houses, costumes, sets, shows and make up were all absolutely Phenomenal!! It was an amazing experience and so worth it!! The Express pass is a MUST for this event. The wait times were ridiculous for the Haunted Houses (40+min). With the pass we only waited like 10 min tops each. HINT: If you wait until 10PM to buy an express pass it's 1/2 price ($50!!) American Horror Story was by far my FAVORITE! It was awesome! Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure Show - was HILARIOUS!!! Don't miss it! Universal Studios: Transformers, Ripe Rocket, the Mummy, & Harry Potter were all great. We had the Park 2 Park passes to ride the Hogwarts Express but after 20 min waiting in a 40 min line, they closed the ride for some issue - Very disappointing. That was the ONLY reason we bought the Park2Park pass, and NEVER got to utilize them. :( MIB was pretty lame and the Simpsons Ride was fun, but the line & getting in was not very organized.  Overall: The Universal App for wait times is total BS. Buy an express pass if you are visiting for a short time and check the weather! Park2Park passes are a joke! HHN 26 was AMAZING and worth every penny - Don't forget buy your express pass after 10pm for 1/2 off! ;P

Had a wonderful time here, lots to do for everyone We didn't have to queue for to long so that was a bonus.  Was a little disappointed that the park shut at 5 most days due to Halloween horror nights, we had tickets for 14 days and it didn't cover the Halloween nights which I was surprised about since tickets are quite expensive as it is and they expect you to pay extra for more tickets.  Park was clean and tidy and all staff very helpful and friendly.  You can buy a refill cup and fill it back up for free all day or there are plenty of water fountains dotted around where you can fill your bottles
Costly but we love it! The rides are amazing . Always a fun time. My son who is 5 was able to go on so many rides.

Stay to the right when entering the city walk entrance to go to the studios, you will see the Famous universal globe and arches.Studios feels more adult based with lots of architecture, shops and streets. There are rides such as transformers, MIB, escape from gringrotts, E.T, Simpsons, shrek, minions, plus diagon alley with the fire dragon and shops. You can get the hogwarts express at kings cross to islands of adventure which is also a good experience.

We came to Orlando for a conference and the welcoming party was at Universal Studios which was booked out exclusively for us. The Wizarding World of Harry Potter was amazing, with such attention to detail - the butterbeer, butterbeer ice cream and fare in the eateries were delicious, the rides were so much fun, with a good variety to suit everyone. Escape from Gringotts is super-fun, the Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit is an extreme coaster that just goes on forever. The Springfield section is a great representation of The Simpsons. Can't comment on ride lines as we had exclusive park access, but the fun to be had is unlimited.
Universal Studios is a great park to visit for older children in my opinion. It has lots of great 3d rides. We purchased the fast pass for the day which saved us lots of time not having to queue.

As an adult, I really didn't think I would enjoy this place so much. I really enjoyed all of the 3 D rides. The variety of restaurants was awesome as well. If you are thinking this place is only for kids...you are mistaken. This is truely a place for the entire family. I plan to return in the next few months and bring my teenage son and his friends.

We loved Universal Studios. The Wizarding world of Harry Potter was super cool, of course! We loved Ripride rocket and rode it several times. We also loved the Mummy and Transformers. A lot of the simulated rides caused us motion sickness so take some meds before you come if you're prone to motion sickness.  The park is small and an easy walk. We had hopper passes so we went from park to park. We bought the meal plan one day and winged it the next day. If you do the meal plan and save your cup you can buy unlimited refills the next day for $7.50. We did that and after buying our meals we saved money over the meal plan option. If you like donuts, they have a huge pink donut over by the Simpsons ride that was around $5 and we all split it. It was a good snack. We thought Butterbeer was way overrated and it was $26 for 4 cups.  We stayed at Cabana Bay and rode the bus in each day. The bus takes you to City Walk where you exit, get on an escalator, go up one floor, through security screening and onto a moving sidewalk to City Walk. It's then a short walk to the park.  Universal was our favorite and we will return!

Universal is fab. Great time with lots of interesting things to do for young and older couples. The park has a good balance between high speed thrills and shows to enjoy. Only disappointment is not as much opportunity to meet characters for photos to keep as memories as you find in Disney Would highly recommend this park

This theme park is packed with awesomeness. There is so much to see and do, I know we didn't get to do or see near enough as we only had one day. We stopped while passing through. We did get the park to park pass ( for HP 🙂) honestly our main draw here was the Wizarding World of Harry Potter but we quickly got swept up in the whole park. I can't wait to come back. I will say we had to purchase our tickets at the gate, as it was kind of last minute for us. The customer service was not great, they were pushy and kind of had the attitude of "move along" which was annoying but not enough for me to adjust my rating for it.

You need at least three days to get around this park and the Islands of Adventure park. Really worth getting a two park pass so you can ride the Hogwart's Express. Most of the indoor rides have 3D rides special effects and are really astounding - you really feel like you are part of the action. There is so much to do, but be prepared for long queues if you are going during school holidays - if you have a "must do" ride, get to the park as it opens and do that first. Then plan your route - it's a big place to walk around so visit each subsequent ride as you reach it, otherwise you will walk miles criss-crossing the park. The park has free wi-if and you can download an app which shows the location of the rides and real time information on waiting times. We found that very useful. Also be aware that a lot of the rides have height restrictions and are unsuitable for young children. I visited with my sister and cousins - all of us nearer 70 than 7 - and we had a great time, so no age limit on enjoyment if you are young at heart.

We visited this park 3 times in our 2 week stay, and we could have visited many more times, everything about the park is superb and the atmosphere is fantastic. There are so many good rides to choose from such as the minions, transformers, Men in Black, The Simpson's (my Favourite), and definitely the Mummy ride plus many more. After this you then have Harry Potter's Diagon Alley which is unlike anything you will ever see, after you visit the shops and buy your interactive wand to do spells around alley go on the Escape from Gringott's ride which is a sort of roller coaster 4D ride, i have to admit i was a bit claustrophobic on this ride as it has a shin restraint as well as a lap bar, but still enjoyed the ride a lot.  When it gets too hot, and it will, believe me, head to the curious George part as it has a wet play area for the kids to cool down, make sure you take swim wear and a towel for them.  If you go in late September and any time in October the park does close around 5pm for the Halloween horror nights, most people will then go to the Islands of Adventure park which is open later but will be packed.  This is definitely the best park in Orlando, and i cant wait to go again in the future,

With dozens of high quality entertainment options in Orlando, it's often hard to choose. However, absolutely DO NOT miss a visit (at least two days) to Universal Studios. We spent an entire weekend entirely focused on two Universal gems, Universal Studios and Universal Islands of Adventure. A two-day Park Hopper Pass provided the perfect combination of park access and connectivity. If you want the full Harry Potter experience, you'll need to visit both parks. Diagon Alley is located in Universal Studios. Hogwarts School is in Universal Islands of Adventure. The Hogwarts Express (fun train ride) conveniently connects the two parks. Again, two days is a MUST to fully see both parks and experience ALL the Harry Potter rides, shops and restaurants.  A few tips for your visit to Universal Studios Florida:  1) Parking is only $20 bucks per day. Traveling around Orlando is fairly easy. Get a rental car at the airport and lodge elsewhere to save money.  2) Be prepared for rain, humidity and water rides. Bring a light backpack with small umbrella, poncho, extra shorts, shirts and shoes. There are plenty of free (some paid) lockers to store your stuff while on rides or in restaurants. If not, be willing to get wet and walk around soaked all day. Not surprisingly, they offer human sized blow dryers all over the park... for a $5.00 per use fee.  3) Avoid the $21.99 Dining Plan. Food options are abundant but quality ranges from totally amazing (Mythos) to completely awful (Circus McGurkus Cafe in Seuss Landing). Generally speaking, the best food options are NOT included with Dining Plan. Don't waste valuable park time trying to figure out where the best food is located.  Finally, you can spend literally dozens of hours PRIOR to your visit searching for discount tickets. In the end, we found the best prices by contacting them directly. If you are staying three days or longer and want to include Disneyworld or another non-Universal park, then using a third-party ticket broker makes sense.
#1 attraction for me is Harry Potter! Try the butterbeer, it's not actual beer. Like always long lines and lots of people. But the view of Harry Potter world is 5 stars!!!

Been coming for HHN for quite some time and I must say this year made me fall in love all over again. Well done Universal you guys outdid yourself! If you're planning to go for just one night and want to do all the houses you need to buy an express pass. I also visited the park during the day and had a blast as usual. The park was not that crowded for a saturday and the lines for the rides where manageable. Saw my favorite show (Horror Makeup show) 3 times, I just can't get enough of it.

Went to Halloween Horror Nights. Planned the night out, paid for the fast pass. Everything going as planned and then you get to the end of your visit, 1 ride to go. What? ! The Harry Potter ride is closed 2 hours before the park closes. They said it closes early so they can get it ready to open early in the morning. So I guess the morning ticket holders are more important. If I would have known ahead of time, we would have gone there first. I feel cheated and it kinda left a sour note to the whole experience. Shame on you Universal.

This is my favourite park in Orlando purely because I like thrills. The park is quite far away from the Disney parks however There are many ways to get to universal you can take you're Car.The parking prices are $20 for standard and $35 for preferred unlike Disney the car park is located in a multi story keeping you're car cool ! Most hotels offer a free bus service to the studios to as well as the "I ride Trolly bus"  Universal can be very busy however security dose not take long to get through without a bag I can't make any comments on going with a bag . Once you get through you have to walk past bars/restaurants to get to the main entrance and to get through it is similar to Disney with the finger print however the ticket is kind of like paper witch I don't like because it's easier to loose/ damage. I have been on all the rides at universal the top 3 I would recommend are 1.) Hollywood RIP rocket This is a really Fun Fast Paced Ride and you can pick a song to listen to while you ride you have to remove everything from you're pockets but there is free lockers the wait times I experienced weren't to bad  2.) The Mummy  I wouldn't take children on this one as it might frightening them but don't let that put you off the mummy can have a long wait time but you can use single rider to speed things up once on the mummy you will be put in a cart and go past various parts of the movie the last room can get rather hot as there is fire involved in this ride.  3.) The Whole HarryPotter Area  This is a must see ! I am not the biggest Harry Potter fan but my mum is and she could spend all day there I liked it to you can walk round diagon ally however it is extremely congested/Busy You can pay a visit to the wand shop and the seem to have every characters wand available even some of the less know characters such as victor Krum and If you have a park to park ticket you can ride the hogwarts express which takes you to the castle and hogsmeed. The ride in greengots bank is similar to the mummy in the way it works  I could spend all day at the park. A few other rides are Men in black alien attack I really enjoy this one a bit to much that some of the staff were staring to recognise me but they were all very nice You can buy a fast pass at universal for $50 I believe but that only grants access for one day. The parade at universal is good also the only negative thing is the park closed at 5pm due to a Halloween night but this was only during my stay

Had to purchase a pass to be enable to ride attractions. The Harry Potter ride needs to be changed to ensure larger guest can ride. How hard could it be to have some seats that could accommodate these guest. I saw one woman rather large be told she could ride and my husband and grandson were told no because of their size. They are larger build but definitely not huge. to me this discrimination against people that are of larger build, unless they are charged a lesser amount, they should be able to ride as anyone else. My husband and grandson were embarrassed.

We had a family reunion of sorts at US/F. The weather was a little Iffy which kept the ride wait times down. Really enjoyed the Harry Potter rides, Spiderman, Hulk, but Kong was hands down my favorite. Not something I would do for a couple more years but definitely a fun time!

It's a great theme park. They have covered all the bases,Great for the little ones and the adventures type of people. If you can go May and September is the best months as the crowds are lighter. The lines moved much quicker. It is as good as Disney.

When visitors arrive @ universal studios; there are security to thoroughly check bags & bottles for weapons & alcoholic beverages. Caucasian male security personnel searched our bag pack because rolls of quarters looked suspicious for unknown reason(s); also asked, "why do you have so many quarters?". When we replied that quarters were for tolls & vending machines; he condescendingly said, "just so you know; everything is digital now". After security check point, visitors walk through city walk towards universal studios & islands of adventure. Then tourists wait in winding lines to purchase park tickets. Finally, friends & families with children wait in additional but worse muddled lines to have park tickets & thumb prints scanned. There should be electronic kiosks available to purchase park tickets & park members for assistance. We prepaid two (2) park to park passes via AAA website but we still have to wait in line to obtain our passes which defeats the purpose of prepaying online. There should be separate wait lines for visitors who prepaid their passes. @ universal studios park entrance on 9.30.16 in the morning; we were promptly informed that ALL rides were inoperable until further notice. Therefore everyone was going to islands of adventure. There should be LARGE electronic signs @ city walk & park entrances (similar to traffic & amber alert signs on the highways) informing visitors that rides @ universal studios were inoperable until further notice. On 10.1.16, we surrendered & purchased expressed passes. Therefore, we have less wait time for MOST rides. Unfortunately, express passes are inapplicable for NEW rides & attractions such as 3D Hogwarts railways to & from diagon alley & hogs mead; gringotts; raptor encounter & leaky caldron pub. Warning: dragon above gringotts roars & breaths fire. Children & visitors with small bladders might accidentally pee their pants. Before riders wait & enter gringotts bank; everyone must secure their bags & backpacks in lockers which is complimentary is riders stored belongings less than 1 hour. Harry potter theme parks @ diagon alley & hogs mead have expanded & improved. Sadly, we were unable to locate 3D ride in Mr. Weasley's magical flying car. City walk, universal studios & islands of adventure are clean. There are plenty of clean restrooms, cafes, restaurants & gift shops throughout property. In addition, universal studios has a great phone app which informs visitors which rides are roller coasters; water rides; 3D & 4D rides; shows; wait time for each attraction; navigates where you are located on the park to the ride/show of interest; alerts when your favorite ride/show has less wait time.

My wife and I visited Universal Studios earlier this month. Excellent place to visit and great rides. The Revenge of the Mummy was my favorite. The food is a little on the expensive side but the quantity an quality is good. My advice is that if you plan to visit please purchase multi-park tickets which will give you access to both Universal Studios and the Island of Adventure which you can take the Hogwarts Express to get to - another great experience. Plan you visit on weekdays as there will be slightly lesser crowds as opposed to weekends where I am told it is just crazy and the lines for the rides are extremely long...

Wow, the 3D and rollercoaster rides are for the serious thrill seekers. There are many restaurants with mostly junk food but a few finds and some great combos (donuts/ice cream). Harry Potter area is a do not miss...it's so well done. Tons of restaurants in the main area...worth a day while in Anaheim area.

this place is mesmerising right down to all the little details like the fish school on the water! I didn't get to go on all the rides but will remedy that when I come back next year. Also HHN are fantastic if you like a good scare!
So much to do here along with Harry Potter world. Totally worth it to get a park to park ticket AND take at least 2 days. Great rides and adventures.

Really had a great trip. We did 3 days with express passes, staying in a resort hotel. It was perfect! Myself and my 2 sons age 14 and 24! The hotel was great with just a short walk to the park. The express pass is definitely the way to go!

I enjoyed the trip very much just a little long with wait lines at Halloween horror nights. We had to wait 2 hours and another time 2 hours and more just to get into 2 houses. There was signs that you couldn't tell where places to go. I was highly upset I didn't make it to the Harry Potter area but for the most part the experience was awesome. I enjoyed myself for the most part and do plan on coming back again.

This amusement park has great rides, many food options and enough variety to make any day fun. The Harry Potter section of the park is definitely the favorite. I wish we could have had more time at the park. We will go back...

We recently visited universal in orlando and had a wonderful time. I recommend taking a full day for universal and a full day for islands of adventure. There is so much to see and do. We had the best time. It is by far the best theme park I have ever visited. A must do for orlando.

I visited the park with my 6yrs old son who is mad about transformers; we only visited one park as my son has epilepsy and it would be too much to do more than one park. I visited guest services after picking up my tickets as a friend had recommended getting a pass that allows him to get a time to return to the ride rather than standing waiting for a hour (if my son gets tired he can collapse and blackout). After a bit of grilling over my son's condition we were given the pass (which I did expect). We managed to go on about 4 rides during our visit (my son gets tired) and we did not have to wait too long for some of the rides the longest was 50mins to return back. The highlight for my son was meeting the transformers although he was a little shy he met his heroes. My only moan was when he met bumblebee I went to buy photos afterwards and the pictures were of the back of his head and they told me there is sometimes a glitch on the camera but lucky I had taken some on my own camera and I bought pictures when he met Optimus Prime. I bought the day tickets purely for my son to see the transformers and it made his day.  On a negative side anyone visiting any of these theme parks with young children like myself it is difficult for children to stay in line for upto 50 minutes and unsure what can be done to elevate these problems although I was impressed with Simpsons ride because as we waited there was some entertainment as you waited. It's s pity you can't have seating in queue but I suppose it would cause health and safety issues?  Good day at the park; expensive to buy transformers toys (get them a lot cheaper in U.K.) and was a bit disappointed there any transformer toys you can't get in the UK and I was looking for a transformers backpack for my son but when I asked in the shop they said they don't do them.
$11.49 USD for a hot dog..how can anyone justify that inflation? $11.49 USD for a hot dog. Thats all I remember from the entire day, I remember seeing the sign that said $11.49 for a hot dog.

We drove down from Minnesota for my brother's birthday, and we will never return. Staff was rude and egotistical, the majority of attractions were shut down or broke down during operation, food is overpriced, and wait times are long.

So many people have reviewed Universal that I just wanted to add this about my experience. Everyone had to leave Studios because of Halloween Horror Nights so the train ride back to Islands of Adventure was packed. For me that was nightmarish because of a tendency to panic attacks if I feel trapped. I was right up to the queue for the train car. Each compartment takes a maximum of 8 people. I could feel my heart begin to race. We were placed with another 6 people who also had a huge stroller. I was ready to exit and just walk the 30 minute walk when I thought to ask for some help. The young woman handling the line was busy of course. I told her I was feeling panicky and would it be at all possible for my daughter and I to be in a compartment by ourselves. Without hesitation, despite the incredible crush of people needing to get on this ride, she said yes. I couldn't believe it and I was very grateful. Having an invisible challenge is not always recognized, so compassion is not always given. But here it was given without question. That says a lot about this organization and its employees. I am a huge Harry Potter fan and love, love, love, the HP attractions at Universal. I will be going back soon.
We loved this theme park. So much to do and see with some of the best rides and good food. Went 3 times and still didn't do everything on offer. My favourite Florida park by a mile.
We enjoyed this place more than we even imagined we would. The rides were incredible. You have to ride the Transformers ride

I can honestly say I was expecting a little bit more. The haunted houses were done very well however whenever you see the monsters jumping out at the people three feet in front of you it doesn't scare you and it takes away the thrill. I did not pay for any Express passes because being a single mother I paid $565 for two tickets into Island of Adventure two tickets and two all day at Universal including Halloween Horror Night. This was just to get in this did not include the $20 per day to park and $20 per cup so we could have beverages. The only advantage of going all day was We Were released in the park and hour early before the General Public and that allowed us to go into 3 haunted houses for the lines got Crazy. However 12 hours on your feet it definitely brings a person. After the general public got in the lines became unbearable I missed out on a few houses because I wasn't going to wait an hour and a half. This was on a Wednesday night I could only imagine what it is like during the weekends. The scare zones were okay. I live near Chicago so I go to Great America Fright Fest quite often and they have the whole park decorated including the water turned Red, Scare crows and pumpkins all throughout the park it is definitely a more Halloween feel. I definitely would say the best part of the whole night was the Bill and Ted Adventure Show. Overall I am very glad I got to experience it with my daughter however my expectations were higher.

I was a bit unimpressed with this park not counting the Harry Potter portion. Most of the rides rely on 3D or 4D technology and while it can be very cool to experience, it gets a little unimaginative after awhile. My husband and I were really only visiting the parks for the Harry Potter area which completely delivered in terms of immersing you into the setting. We loved the food, drinks, and entire atmosphere. Otherwise, there wasn't really much we wanted to do in this park. It's definitely nice to have the express pass though. Using that or single rider made waiting nonexistant. However I really disliked their bag policy for some rides. It's not very obvious and is a pain if you're next to get on the ride and have to lose your spot to go lock up your bag. And if a handful of rides do this then they all should since it isn't clear when you can and can't bring them and the staff seem pretty PO'd when you ask. I get that the intensity of the rides might make having loose items bad but it gets pretty tight trying to shove your Olivander's wand in those lockers.

Once I got over the sore feeling from the price of the tickets, this was a great experience. There is something for everyone here and I don't ride roller coasters. Visiting this time of year the queue for rides was not bad, a few we just walked straight in, the longest wait was 35 minutes for the minions. Personal favourites were transformers which shows what the best modern technology can do for a virtual experience but I also loved ET, which must be one of the oldest rides and had no queue!

Universal is still the king of the parks for me in terms of style and all around family fun. It perhaps doesn't have as many thrilling rides as islands of adventure but it has a couple new ones coming next year and in "rip ride rock it" they arguably have the most exciting roller coaster in Orlando. If you can try and go whilst Halloween horror nights is on, if you are not with small children. This was my favourite part of the holiday with great scare houses and shows. We ended up paying the extra $120 for fast passes but I don't think I would do it any other way because the wait times are insane. They whole Harry Potter world is just visually incredible and i recommend you take the Hogwarts express over to Islands. I'm already looking forward to the next time.

Well, my wife is a horror freak. So much so, she asked for our son and fiancée to fly in from San Diego for the week to go to Universal's annual celebration of Halloween. Now his fiancée is a Disney fanatic, so a visit to there is also planned. Universal has different themed haunted houses that are located within the park as well as scare zones and two live shows on Halloween night. The park closes early during the day and opens after 6:00 and stays open until after 1:00. If you go, consider buying the express pass. With it, we visited all of the houses before 9:30. This left time to visit the scare zones, go on rides and see shows. Well with the money and we thoroughly enjoyed the park.

I could talk about all of the attractions but just enjoy Hulk and Harry Potter and the rest is almost irrelevant. However, it's all amazing.  A fantastic family day out and a must do in Orlando, even if I ended up doing it without my family!

First, be prepared to pay a LOT for this wonderful experience. Parking at a preferred (i.e. closer) lot will be $30 for the day. Tickets for both Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure with the express pass was $570.00 for one adult and one child. So for a family of 4, you are only $1000.00 to get inside.  The Express Pass is worth having in spite of the fact that they don't apply to most of the Harry Potter exhibits. Still, they will save you a LOT of time on lines for the remainder of the attractions.  The 3-D rides are simply amazing. This new technology sure beats the ride experience of a generation ago. Rides such as the Minions, King Kong, etc, should not be passed by - they are extremely well done.  Be prepared to be exhausted by the end of the day. There is a lot of walking and standing, besides the rides and roller coasters.

Visited for 1 week at end of October (UK - school half term holiday). We have previously been durring the summer months and by comparison, in October, the climate was comfortably warm, and the parks, less crowded. In October there is also a lot of Halloween stuff going on. Although we have been a few times and the rides / entertainment were familiar, we still thrilled to the extravagance of it all, especially the new Harry Potter attractions (Diagon Alley, Escape from Gringotts ride & Hogwarts Express). We stayed at the on-site Hard Rock Hotel which was not cheap but included entry to the parks 1 hour before they were open to general admission. Also included was a free Express Pass allowing fast access to most of the rides (maximum wait time for majority of the rides was only 10 minutes). All the on-site hotels are a short stroll or boat ride to the park entrances meaning that you can be in the park at 7am before the crowds and heat; go back to the hotel for lunch or a splash in the pool and return refreshed to the parks later in the day. Sandwiched between the 2 park entrances is City Walk, a collection of merchandise shops and restraunts, including the Hard Rock Cafe (the most entertaining place to eat a burger & fries) We purchased our tickets from an independant agency in the UK before travelling as it worked out much cheaper (14 day unlimited entry pass to both parks was cheaper than buying a 3 day ticket at the resort). To anyone who has not visited before, what ever your age and degree of adventure-seeking there is something to entertain everyone at both Universal Studios & Islands of Adventure parks. Even "Grumpy Old Men" like me will spend the day smiling with occasional laughing out loud.

I love the rides and the butter beer is yum!!!! The Mummy ride was fantastic! Didn't mind waiting in several long lines. But the food is such a ridiculous let down. It's very over priced, terribly over priced even for theme park food. The only food that was edible was at The Leaky Cauldron. It was breakfast and it was $16, but it was creative and good. Every place else was terrible. The absolute worse was, Thunder Falls BBQ. After spending more then $80 for cold cheeseburgers, dry chicken wraps, cold French fries, not only was my family let down but we left hungry. I'll visit the park again, but eat outside somewhere.

MOMsForUNIVERSAL!  I am a huge amusement park lover - always have been and I will ride rollercoasters, waterslides, and stand in line for hours until I just can't do it any longer. My kids think we're taking them primarily for their enjoyment...NOT! My husband and I have just as much fun.  I can't think of anything that I don't like about Universal and its adjacent entertainment activities. There is always parking. Shopping, movies, and restaurant options increases and improves every year. Inside the park, rides change and improve while old favorites stay the same. The Mummy, Rip Ride Rocket, Men in Black, Transformers, and my all time favorite attraction, Harry Potter/Diagon Alley, make this a must visit destination. I've been to the parks in California and won't even begin to compare the two because of course they're going to be different, but honestly I enjoy each for what they have to offer.  One recommendation I would make is this: it would be nice to offer a rental option for Wands in Diagon Alley, that can be returned upon exit from the Harry Potter area or exit at the park. Some kids just want to use it there for the day (heck, I would too because it looks cool), but don't necessarily want to own one (everyone's not a PotterHead).
Bring a change of clothes for the little ones because they will get wet in this area! My son we changed his clothes twice! He loved it!
a great place to spend the day. amazing experiences and the day went really fast. very high-priced tickets, but once in your life ... you should take your own snacks if you want save littlebit.

The Wizarding World of Harry Potter is totally amazing! If you saw the awe on Harry's face when he saw Diagon Alley for the first time in the first movie, I am sure my expression entering into it was pretty much the same! And I am 59 years old! I went with my adult daughter and we both became children. I had to play with my interactive wand everywhere I could. The only thing I didn't like about it was leaving the last day. I cried as I left Diagon Alley and knew that the Ministry of Magic would deactivate my wand so it wouldn't work outside the park. I am hoping to retire in 3years and live close enough to visit frequently. I am already looking at Central Florida homes on Zillow.

I enjoyed the outing. Great vibe, good food, toys the kids will love. I suggest you go during the day. We couldn't take any decent photos which was disappointing, but on us, not universal. Wear comfortable shoes (and try to stick to a budget, because you can get really carried away 😂)
I absolutely love Universal Studios; there literally is something for everyone here. Fantastic time bringing so many movies and characters to life; chick full of fun.

Great experience and detail in houses was fabulous ! Could have been more scare actors and being a brit I just didn't quite get Bill and Ted show ! Fave house AHS followed by 3D house -lot of jumps and fun. Don`t show fear as they latch on to you !!

Some attractions were closed and it seems like some attractions have been taken away since last time, so I was a bit disappointed. Otherwise it was a good day without any long waiting times anywhere. But still, I am glad we did not buy more than one day passes.Food and drinks are quite expensive inside.

Not being a fan of roller coasters or a big fan of Harry Potter, you would think that this was not a good idea!?! Wrong - loved EVER minute of if, some of the best simulators and experiences of my life, loved Hogwarts Express between the two parks, Hubby "picked" his interactive wand and walked around casting spells - great fun for the young at heart!!! A bit expensive, but loved it all :-)

Alongside the favorites rides that are still there, including Men In Black: Alien Attack, Revenge Of The Mummy, The Simpsons Ride, and Rip Ride Rockit Coaster, some new rides to experience that I haven't been on before were Transformers: The Ride, Despicable Me: Minion Mayhem, the expanded area of The Simpsons Ride, and the most popular area that expands the Wizarding World of Harry Potter, Diagon Alley. So much to see there, new rides, great food, and awesome entertainment. If you haven't seen it all yet, go there and see it all. So much to experience in Universal Studios Florida.

We purchased a 14 day unlimited pass and visited both parks about 7 times during our 2 week trip. We are a family of 4 adults and an 11 & 12 yr old. The park was very crowded for October especially the Harry Potter areas of both parks. Everything is very expensive in the park...$6 per game....$12 for a hot dog and chips?...c'mon. They are more expensive then Disney. The wait time for most rides were 30 minutes or longer with Kong never under a 60 minute wait. Our kids are heavily into Harry Potter but were a bit disappointed. The area was crowded and there were only about 4 rides in that area. The Hogwarts train was pretty cool! Some of the rides are outdated like MIB, ET. Kong was really good. We like the Simpsons ride too. Overall it was a fun trip but too expensive, too crowded and no "magic" feel to the parks like Disney gives you. We most likely will not be back anytime soon.

We went for Halloween Horror Nights, what a blast! They really go all out, I can honestly say I was scared several times and I don't scare easily. The best haunted house in my opinion was The Walking Dead, very scary ending. We also went on the Mummy ride, that was fun.

Not that big of an area. Luckily we were there on a day when there were not that much visitors so there was not that big lines... Some rides were great, some not so much. Park closed at 5pm which I thought was a bit early. That was because of horror nights.

The trip to Universal Studios was including as part of a large conference so I did not have to pay to attend. Since this was a private event not all the park was open. It was fun but the guides we talked to about the type of rides and what to expect was not helpful at all. The food experience was very lacking inside the park. We ate at Richters for hamburgers and would not do that again.

Another great year!!! The mazes and scare zones were amazing. Can't wait to go back next year. If you are going to Universal Studios in the fall this is a must do!!! Just don't bring the little ones. This event would be way to scary for them.

I was here during a time that the park was closed to the general public, but there was still about 20k people attending the private event. Harry Potter was very cool, kids loved it. The men in black ride is pretty lame in my opinion. Went on the rockit roller coaster and that was awesome!!! I love that you pick you own music for the ride, I went with beastie boys sabotage for my pick and it was perfect! Overall this is a great place to take the family.

This park was amazing! I was so impressed with the quality of rides! Best rides are hulk, Hogwarts castle, and two battling dragons. I would recommend to go to universal before park opening times (for some reason they allow people in and rides start working before park officially opens) and head straight to these!
visited in March 2016 as a chaperone on a school trip. The park is amazing fun, clean and not too crowded. Must go on the Harry Potter rides!!!!!
Even though the employees aren't has nice as Disney, the attractions and shows make up for it. This is our second time around!
Great park, not super crowded and the rides were awesome! Terminator 2 could go away as well as ET but the rest were fun!

Theme parks are expensive vacations, so plan your trip well! I signed up for deals on the Universal site months ago and did end up getting a "buy one day and get two days free" deal that I was able to use for our family of four park to park.  Spaced out our 3 days between IoA and Universal, making sure to do my research in advance. Did not need to do one full day morning to night at either park, was great to break it up over time.  For those who get motion sick, I highly recommend taking something before going on any rides. I had to load up before each visit into the park or risk making myself very sick. The teenagers were fine, but we did avoid The Simpson ride, since it made my teen queasy last year.  Express pass is a huge help and not sure I could give a 4 star rating if we didn't have it, since the wait times looked long for regular park visitors. Even on a Saturday, did not have to wait long. But be aware that Gringots in Diagon Alley does not have a fast pass, so we did that ride first thing in the morning with an early entry for resort guests. Harry Potter and The Forbidden Journey in IoA also does not take express passes either.  The biggest hassle I had was with the old school paper park tickets and express passes. My spouse refused to wear a lanyard, so I had to keep his park passes in mine, otherwise risk them getting lost. Having to scan your park pass and give the correct thumb or finger print each time you entered got a little old. (Disney bands are nice in this regard.) It also held up the lines frequently with passes getting mixed up or someone not remembering which finger or hand they used for the print. Hopefully Universal will upgrade this system at some point. With the two parks being so close and Hogwarts Express adding another mode to move inbetween parks, it would be nice to have some sort of express lane or faster method for park to park guests. Felt like I was constantly taking out my original park ticket which is separate from the express pass. Had to also keep my room key handy for early entry. My spouse never figured it all out and needed me to state what was needed and when.  As far as rides reviews, we enjoyed everything we singled out as "must do". There were a few misses, such as the Animal Actors, cute and interesting but not sure it was worth the time. The Terminator show was pretty lame and I'd for sure skip that one altogether. The 3D used is so old that it didn't even feel like 3D. Plus the Terminator franchise is kinda dated, my teens had no interest even during the show. The only ride that seemd over hyped was Kong, but was still fun. Not sure I woud've enjoyed it had we waited hours. Worth a 20 min wait maybe, but not much more in my opinion.  Favorite ride for my teens was The Mummy, they went on it muliple times. We also enjoyed all the popular rides like Gringots, Spiderman, transformers, Hulk, Rock it, Jurassic Park river raft (did get wet) and Despicable Me. Favorite show was the Horror Make-up show, which was very funny.  Sad that it might be a long time before we go again, but felt like I got a chance to see and do everything we wanted. If more time, would've stayed for a second Duff beer and maybe eat inside Moe's Tavern.

Loved every minute of our visit here, and our two teenage sons would go again & again. It was like walking around a film set & all the rides are great (us adults did not venture on Rip, Ride & Rocket 😱). There is something for everyone - def our favourite theme park.

Had an amazing week here, last visited 18years ago and it was just as magical. took our adult kids along and they sill loved it. The halloween horror nights were amazing, we stayed at Hared rock hotel so we only had a short walk and were in every night we could

This world has been done so well. So much thought has gone into every tiny detail. I loved it! Only downside was the price of merchandise... $110 usd for a robe or $48 for a wand was a bit steep. It was the busiest part of Universal too.....but still...fantastic experience!

It's a good day out, but ripping people off by charging people twice by splitting the park into two is disgusting, we had unlimited tickets, but they still rip you off by charging $20 a day for parking, if I ever return back to Florida again, it won't be to this place!

The Diagon Alley part of the Wizarding World here is Universal's saving grace. It is wonderful, and well worth visiting.  Outside of that, I was left disappointed by Universal Studios. I was really excited about the Despicable Me ride, but it was really underwhelming and nowhere near as immersive as their other simulator rides (transformers,Spider-Man, kong - although transformers and Spider-Man are practically identical). The terminator show was dull... I'm honestly struggling to remember what else there was there... oh and the parade was cancelled the day we went with no explanation or apology.  The Simpsons ride was a pleasant surprise, really enjoyed it!
