But it is so old that the load and unload design is just bizarre and makes the lines for it needlessly long for a ride that can hold so many people. It is worth the queue though, it is good.
The park is amazing it's a must to see can't say much more than come and visit Florida you will be blown away by it

We are two adults and we absolutely enjoyed this park! It was the best vacation ever! Especially if you are into Harry Potter ! Awesome! And City walk is great to! Especially the hard rock cafe which is the world's largest one! Highly recommend going here!

Not as big as WDW Resorts, but if one is a movie-goer, this is a must-visit park in Orlando, Florida for you. There's just two parks-Universal Studios and Island of Adventure with the "food courts" in between. We opted for Universal Studios since we're not really ride-freaks. Part of Harry Potter's Wizarding World is here (Diagon Alley, Grimmwald's Place, etc.), The Mummy ride is also here, Jaws is still hanging on a rope for photo-ops, Transformers are also here. Musical street-perfomances were awesome with "Marilyn Monroe" and her gang of sexy ladies dancing & singing on the street & encouraging audience participation. Tickets were a bit pricier than WDW Resorts though.

Combine this with a pass to Islands of Adventure and you have a fantastic day or three. Typically less crowded than Disney properties but possibly more fun. With a diversity of rides and coasters caters to all ages, Little (and big) kids love Dr. Sues Lands and some of the other roller coasters are the best in Orlando for the big kids. Food is more upscale than most Disney properties (Epcot excluded) and for Harry Potter Fans this place is a MUST SEE & DO!

I have to say that I was slightly disappointed with this Theme Park. There are 4 roller coasters in this park, the best being Harry Potter and the Escape from Gringotts. The other coasters are Revenge of the Mummy, Hollywood Rip, Ride, Rockit and the kiddie coaster Woody Woodpecker's Nuthouse Coaster.  Other attractions in the park are Terminator 2 3D (very disappointing), Shrek 4D (excellent), ET Adventure (OK), Men in Black, Alien Attack (a disappointing shoot-em up ride), Transformers The Ride 3D (average) and The Simpson's Ride (did not view as wait time was 50 minutes).  The best area of the park is The Wizarding World of Harry Potter and there is a train connection between this park and it's sister park Islands of Adventure.

We had such an amazing time at the two parks in Universal Studio. Not to be missed are King Kong, Harry Potter, and the Indiana Jones show. The comic strip is so colourful and really brings you back to your comic book heroes. Love the time we spent there. The place is huge so you should come early and just enjoy the night as well at the many bars and restaurants. We also took an express pass at an additional cost per person. This helped us go through the place without the hassle of long queues. This is a must if you want to enjoy the park. Have fun!

Visited uni several times over the last 15 years. Both parks never fail to impress. Great food outlets and blue man group was hilarious. Prefered parking looks like a rip off. We paid the extra 10 bucks only to be directed to park in 'jaws' where we had previously parked for $20.00 per day and was much further away from the entrance. I won't fall for that one again. Security at the entrance has been beefed up with increased bag checks and airport style X-ray. Allow a little more time for this but staff really got on with it so not too bad. Have fun😀
I have found the new week to go. Arrive Friday after thanksgiving, no park Saturday, pool day. Then park Sunday and Monday. No longer than a 20 minute wait for rides. Even Harry Potter

The Hulk is better than before. More trilling turns and 360s ! You could not miss that opportunity. Get your special pass or you will wait for more than an hour. Not cheap. But the special pass is not that good either. It is as long as a regular line at Disney. With fast pass you just wait max 10 min. At universal could be up to 27 min. We were looking forward to try the King Kong ride but it did not move the needle it is far away or behind dinosaur at animal kingdom. Universal is good at roller coasters. Not at trying to match Disney rides

We enjoyed the Universal Studios side of the park. The lines weren't too long the last week in August. Locals are back to school. During this season it can instantly down pour. We bought $1 disposable ponchos from Walmart and we are so glad we did. It would only rain for 15 minutes per day but it would absolutely downpour when it did. Our favorite rides on this side were Revenge of the Mummy, Minions, Transformers, and the Harry Potter rides! We also really enjoyed ET and Shrek.

We apparently chose a great time to visit as the parks were not very busy and wait times at the attractions were minimal. My favorite was Transformers, (I love Bumblebee), but all of the attractions were very enjoyable, we did several of them more than once. And we had several opportunities for pictures with characters in costume.

Other than the Harry Potter section, which was really wonderful, I found Universal Studios to be a BAD version of Disney World. If you go to Universal, I highly suggest you ONLY visit Harry Potter and then save the rest of your time and energy for Disney. You will probably be tempted - like we were - to mill around the rest of Universal after you see Diagon Alley, because after all you paid to get in and it can't really be that bad... right? Wrong.  Why? Really, it comes down to one thing: the quality of execution at Universal Studios is just really, really poor. The rides are convoluted and many of them are very similar. Almost all the rides we experiences involved sitting in a "car" and being shook around by hydraulics in front of a 3D screen. Add in a blast of hot air in your face when something exciting happens and a sprinkle of water and you've basically described all of the new rides in the park. Even worse, things like the volume or "how long should the employee talk to me at the intro" were REALLY POORLY THOUGHT OUT. One ride we went on had a huge group of people standing in a room for like 15 minutes while an employee screeched (they were in "character") and literally tried to annoy people as part of their schtick. The crowd got agitated and rude by the time we were let in the ride. Why would anyone think that was a good idea? Another ride had sound effects so loud that I genuinely think caused damage to people's hearing. I thought it was just me, but other people were complaining as well when exiting the ride. Another annoying, poorly thought out detail: after the parade, workers with lawn-mower type machines literally started weaving through the crowd vacuuming up the debris sent out by the parade floats. I get that they have to clean it up, but couldn't you find a way to do it that doesn't involve running a lawnmower type device right by me and all these kids?  The stores / merch were complete junk. It seems like Universal just outsources everything - the quality of the items and even the packaging varied wildly by the item. Pretty much the only items that were pretty decent across the board was the Harry Potter stuff, and I bet Universal's team didn't have much to do with that.  Long story short, GO FOR HARRY POTTER and LEAVE! The rest is no better than a permanent fair. And a kind of sad fair at that.

There's a point where your children are too cool for Disney. That will pass but, meanwhile, teenagers love Universal. I'm a fan of trying to find the right to time of year to miss the crowds. It makes for a totally different experience. Once you've walked straight through to a ride, it's difficult to come back and wait an hour in a line.  Universal has areas for little children but, I can't imagine how that works well for a young family. The parks as a whole seem to me to be geared to an older crowd; people that ride thrill coasters and 3D rides. In fact, entrance to the park requires passing clubs and bars.  We do love it there; so much we have annual passes. Harry Potter is, of course, the big draw. However, do yourselves a favor and wait until 10 minutes before the park closes and walk right on the Spider-Man ride. You might get to go twice in that time.

Visited the park for one day to check out Harry Potter World with family. Let's just say I was "culture shocked" and we'll leave it at that. As a military vet with a few deployments under my belt, I had a hard time dealing with the hundreds of little fat kids running around in their Harry Potter capes screaming and whining. Not to mention I get a little anxious around large crowds of people. I realized I was in trouble after the first five minutes inside the gate. I did manage to suck it up for the remainder of the day. I'm not a big discount hunter, but was a little disappointed that the military discount was only $3 off a $160 ticket. If you're a yuppy family from the mid west with a couple of spoiled fat kids, then you may enjoy this park. I did not.
Great day out but get there early and start at the back of the park and work your way back. Harry Potter awesome as is transformers Shrek and the simpsons Something for everybody

Universal is always building and expanding their parks and resorts, quicker and faster than Disney, but with just as much detail. Universal is really challenging Disney today with what is possible in a theme park experience. Redefining what is expected from a theme park. How guests experience and share their time there. The front runner of a true theme park experience is Universal. Disney holds the title for Family Fun, Universal holds the title for Family Experience.

We made Universal Orlando Resort our destination in Florida. No Disney World. No SeaWorld. Only Universal Orlando. After one day in the Universal Studios theme park, we felt as if we had accomplished most of what we set out to do. We had the Express Pass since we stayed on property and were able to walk on to nearly every ride. Our early entry into Harry Potter World: Diagon Alley was incredible as there were very few people there in that first hour of operation. The only problem was that there is only one ride in that area so our early entry amounted to two rides on Escape from Gringotts, then shopping in nearly empty stores. The park got much more crowded as the day went on and our express pass did come in handy later. We had a great day in the park, doing nearly all of the rides, taking in some shows, seeing the parade, and watching the closing show for the park. As this was our first time here, we really enjoyed the park, especially our time in Diagon Alley. We experienced some great, costumed cast members, but also found that many of the cast members were not friendly and acted more as security guards. Several were almost pushy and did not make us feel welcome in a few areas. Be prepared as food offerings in the park are not very good. It seems that you can get a simple burger or chicken sandwich in most diners, but there are few healthy, freshly prepared options. We chose to eat more meals outside of the park in City Walk. I am very glad that we went to Universal Orlando Theme Park, but we do not feel that we have to return. Perhaps we will visit again if in Florida, but this would not be our chosen destination.

The rip rocket ride is great - we managed to get early tickets to be let in the park at 8 so we got onto this straight away no queues, they even let us just go back on it again saves walking all the way around again because there was no one there. I would recommend this even just the once!  I did like the themes by cities but wasn't feeling it as much as I had with the IOA, I felt like this park didn't have as many rides at it but was still a good day out to walk around.  The rides that were there were great and interesting, again with harry potter world, if you're from the uk you can give this a miss, it's basically london with a dragon on a building with more people! My favourite area is the simpsons area, it was awesome complete with buzz cola, donuts and a krusty burger.  Both the universal parks are more adult friendly but still have plenty of things to do.

Excellent day out for all the family another one not got too much for the smaller/younger part of our party (2yr) but the area for younger ones was great. Brilliant rides, really well thought out and a must visit for anyone who loves the movies.

We visited universal and we had a great time. But there are some attractions like E.T and Simpson that are very old. You can even smell the old age of the buildings.  Download the app for the smartphone to reserve the fast past in advance for the attractions, also to have a map of the resort.  As a recommendation to the staff you should start including virtual reality attractions.
Many great things to experience. Theme parks great for adults and kids, City Walk great for food and drinks. Something for anybody, anytime!

We were able to enter the park early we stayed at Cabana Bay. We were able to do Harry Potter and Minions before park opened. All the rides are like being in the movies. Great time to go because we didn't have to wait in any lines and all the attractions were open. Loved taking the train to the other park. We started in Universal Studios and then went to Islands of adventure. Like studio park better. Either way, spend the extra money and get the park to park option.
Tranformers was a very close second. This park was amazingly clean and unbelievable. The service is amazing and is very involved.

Me and my family went here for Christmas like we do every year and some things were good/excellent and others not so good. We love the Grinchmas show , the Mummy ride , the butter beer ice cream except the prices have gone up. All the Harry Potter rides are good. The new Hulk is ok except they make you put your stuff in lockers which is annoying. The KingKong ride could be much better. Overall Universal is just ok.

We've done Disney so many times with our family. Our kids are getting older,so we decided to try Universal this year. Overall we had a very good experience. A few improvements would take some of the annoyances away to make the experience go from very good to great.  First of all the entry into the park takes longer than it needs to. We had paper printed bar code tickets that took several tries to get them to register on their scanners. Everyone seemed to have a different sort of ticket. Converting to an RFID system could make this so much more efficient.  Secondly, the Express Pass system needs to be fixed. We visited at a very high volume time of year. The waits for the top rides were consistently between 90 minutes and 3 hours. You must spend an exorbitant amount more to get an Express pass. If you could afford it, the express pass would be worth it, especially if you are there during a high volume time. The system seems patently unfair to regular ticket holders. A system like Disney's would make a trip to Universal SO much more enjoyable. At least you would get a few rides on the top attractions each day. As it stands, you need to be there at closing to have shorter wait times.  To close, I must say the Wizarding World of Harry Potter is AMAZING. Even though we couldn't get on some major rides, we spent lots of time just enjoying Diagonal Alley and Hogsmeade. The interactive wands were fun to play with, and shopping at the stores from the HP books was fun!

Whatever you do in Orlando a trip to universal is a must, although I was there for a work function the first thing I got roped into was the hulk ride, absolutely thrilling even though inside I was very apprehensive. Ride before eating 😆
Great time! Horror night was worth it! Wizarding world of harry potter was amazing! Will definitely go again!
My husband and I had a great time. The rides were great and watching the Macy's day parade was awesome. We loved seeing the Christmas decorations and we had no problem.

We stayed on site so managed to get free express passes which you can use on all rides except 2 throughout the 2 theme parks (both rides are in Harry Potter). We made full use of the express passes and for December close to Christmas the parks here were very quiet compared to Disney. We were able to get on all the rides we wanted by 2pm and then spent the afternoon relaxing by the pool of our hotel. Perfect. There is a good mix of rides here for all levels of thrill seekers.

It is an entertaining park, with good activities and many restaurant options. However, I really did not enjoy how dry and concrete the park seemed. It gets very hot in the summer and walking in the park all day with those surroundings got tiring. There was lots to do in the different buildings, but not much to see outside. I also ate a bad pasta carbonara in one of the restaurants and threw up three times the same day.  If you are debating whether you should buy a ticket for Universal's Islands of Adventure or the Studios, I would recommend the former.

Spiderman as been touched up and upgraded. The new King Kong ride is awesome and a must do. They have a train that runs between both parks between the two villages for Harry Potter. Way too much Harry Potter but they seem to have a strange following. Jaws is gone and is the Harry Potter village on the Univ. Studios side. The parks are always changing and adding so each year is always different. We highly recommend annual passes, it is $20 to park so you save with the free parking that the passes give. Also there are numerous discounts.

This was my first time at Universal Studios and I am amazed by your staff. I traveled with my children one of which is four and a die hard fan of the Transformers. My son was so excited and spent a few hours meeting each Transformer several times as he just wanted to talk to them as this was a dream come true in his eyes. Emily B (that works for Universal and was helping with the meet and greet) saw how much my son loved the Transformers and got one of them to shake his hand then took us straight to the front of the line for the Transformers ride let him go on it and waited for him so after he could pick any toy compliments of Universal. I was in tears as I know how excited my son was. Since being back home he shares that experience with anyone that asks about his trip as that is his favorite memory of our trip. We have been to universal studio 4-5 time and we love it everytimes. If you have teenagers then i will recommend single ride line which has shorter time otherwise long line sometimes more than 90 minutes.

Have visited Orlando for nearly 20 years and totally love this place. Universal Studios is always finding new ways to entertain families and I will definitely be back. Love all the attractions and entertain on offer and can't wait to do Halloween Horror Nights again

If you plan to go for multiple days to the two parks do the math and it may be worthwhile to get the annual pass to give you more flexibility. At first was not impressed as firstly the entrance price was extremely high, we were there really early but already the queue for the rides was 45 mins!!!  Warmed to the park eventually when we Found Harry Potter what a fab attraction.  It was pouring with rain and extremely cold the day we Visited so was amazed that ride wait times were so long. Other than fighting the after holiday crowds, we had a wonderful family experience. Our boys are young adults, we hoped they would enjoy going on a trip with their middle aged parents, and Universal didn't disappoint! It was great fun and lots of things to do for all ages!

Again forgot my phone for pic this place is alot of fun for adults also it is not just a child's activity. You will find Harry potter at universal the Simpson's are in there men in black stop tower and may other attractions you won't be able to do everything in one day.i would do Hollywood and universal as a two day pass Walt Disney would take you 3 days to see everything in just that one park all the other parks with fast pass you might be able to ride and see shows in one day.
Exciting with or without children. We love the excitement of the rides, we plan on going again very soon!!

King Kong, Spider Man, Harry Potter, even dinasours in the park. The Jurasic Park ride said "you will get wet" but it rained part of the day so we didn't care. It was the BEST ride of all. Loved Diagon Alley and the Harry Potter rides. Also loved Transformers, The Mummy and Despicable Me. MIB ride spins--if you don't do well with spinning, stay away from that one. Would love to go back soon.

It's always an enjoyable day to walk around Universal. From the character parades to the rides (ET being my favorite), to the shopping, the day passes very pleasantly. We were a group of adults, and enjoyed ourselves!

Some comments apply to Universal Florida AND Islands of Adventures, but the rides are only for Universal Studios Florida.  PLAN, PLAN, PLAN. Do not just show up there to buy tickets and figure out as you go along. As all the other theme parks in Orlando, Universal is VERY expensive, so to maximize your time and money, make sure to plan ahead well. Arrive when the park opens at 9 am and plan to stay until the park closes. That is the only way you will see the entire park, or most of it. If you are in a large group, bring texting devices so that you can co-ordinate meetups. DO NOT depend on the "free wifi," although out of the two (Universal/Xfinity), Xfinity worked better for our large group.  ** If going with young children, or pre-teens or anyone communication-disabled, take a full size photo of them and their clothing the day of adventure, so that in the case the group gets separated, the photo can immediately be sent to the staff to help you locate the lost party.  ** If you can help it, do not go on High Season Dates (see their calendar online). We were there on "Regular Days," and even those were so very busy.  ** Anyone with low vision, especially in dark areas may want to avoid this park, or go with someone who has good vision, as many of the lineups were in very dark areas and had very low lighting.  Do NOT go to this theme park if you have very young children. It suits pre-teens and teens the best. It is not well suited to young children with only one small area for that age group. (Way too expensive for that, unless you have other age groups in your party and are going to split up during the day to accomplish the most.)  Do NOT wait to buy your tickets at the parking the morning of your day.  Do NOT wear sandals or flip flops. Sensible walking shoes only.  Do NOT buy your tickets on craigslist, or other similar sites. The tickets are tied to your fingerprint, so second days cannot be used by other people.  Do NOT buy the 2 park tickets - it would be a waste of money, UNLESS you have two full days. You cannot do these parks in one day.  TICKETS - Tickets can be wide ranging in price, and some can be fake, so avoid spending important dollards by NOT buying at unauthorized dealers. CHEAPEST prices that are legitimate are found online at tickets2you, which is cheaper than buying at the door. BUT, the biggest reason is to avoid the long lineup, which will waste hours of your valuable time in the morning. Also, select the "Will Call Kiosk," - bring the credit card you used to buy the tickets because you will need to swipe it - instead of any other pickup options (where the lineups were also long), including the Guest Services where coupon exchangers have to suffer in the long line ups, too.  FOOD: You can bring in food, sandwhiches and snacks and drinks etc, but not large coolers. We spent the day: had a good breakfast before we arrived, packed lunches, then bought dinner at Monster Cafe, right in front of the large roller coaster. Much cheaper that way, so we didn't have to buy 2 meals for our group.  LINEUPS: It doesn't seem fair, but the Express Lineups are truly worth it unfortunately. Otherwise, we wouldn't have been able to see the whole park. It's just not possible. Plan to spend an entire day there 9-9 pm or close to that, to see the whole park an check out every ride. We had a group of disabled teens who have great difficulty waiting in lineups, which made us eligible for the AAP Pass, which is similar to the Express Pass. This was immensely helpful for our crew, which wouldn't have made it otherwise. Even on a regular day, the lineups are long, and you would waste a lot of time just waiting.  RIDES  **Very few rides for young children. **Only ONE extreme ride - the roller coaster. The rest are very mild rides and mostly 3D movies and simulators.  Mummy - excellent and enjoyed by all. Transformers - excellent and enjoyed by all. Rip-Ride - extreme roller coaster enjoyed by some! Men in Black - boring - do not bother if there is a lineup. Gringotts - Harry Potter - longest lineups but not better than the other rides ... disappointing. Terminator 2 - live action / 3D - kind of boring ... most in our group didn't like it too much.  Hope this helps! ENJOY!

2 week holiday and intended to visit orlando. Everything absolutely fantastic! Although July time proved to be very popular and waiting times for rides were, at times more than we were willing to wait. Fast pass offered but very expensive. Recommened to visit in march-May time to improve wait times and cooler too!

Just returned from a amazing time. We loved both parks - all the rides were top notch. I can't say enough good things about the parks. Smaller crowds than Disney but much better rides. Would return for sure !!

We bought two day tickets for Universal parks and what a bust. You are forced to use their locker system on most rides for teens and then getting your things out becomes a huge problem. Locker workers are few and far between. The lockers at the Incredible Hulk work other than that very frustrating. If you have someone that will hod your things while you ride it is worth a visit, otherwise skip this.
The rides were great once you got on but the wait was sometimes hours. I don't think I'll ever go back.

My husband, 5 year old son and I visited in November. I was very impressed with the staff and the cleanliness of the entire park. Every single detail was on point! Diagon Alley was awe inspiring, and my son absolutely loved Seuss Landing. We especially loved the Parent Swap feature. We were able to shoot past the long lines using the single rider line and then one of us with sit with our son in a pleasant waiting room most with a video relating to the movie the ride is designed after (if not the movie itself). Big time thumbs up! There is something for everyone here.

We were a group of nine. I have never counted to nine so many times in my life! The park was not crowded at all on Friday Jan 13 but Sat the 14 was crowded. We used "the touring line "from the unofficial guide to Universal. Get it; it is very helpful. The guide to how to see it all and save time is worth the price of the book. We had four children ages 5-9 and they all are into Harry Potter. So these two areas ( one in USF and one in IOA) were a big hit. Get your "magic wands" ahead of time save time and money. The other areas of the park are great as well. We enjoyed two full days with the two park pass. The train ride between the two is not to be missed!

This is an awesome attraction we went four days over our holiday the rides are out of this world and Harry Potter area was soooo Cool great value for money and an awesome fast pass system strongly recommend allowing 2 to 4 days at this amazing place

We visited Orlando for my 50th Birthday and purchased our Universal tickets in UK. Universal are by far miles ahead of Disney in terms of keeping things new with minimum disruption to guests enjoyment. We visited Universal Studios many times during our holiday and loved it as much this time as we have every other time we have visited Orlando (15 times in total now). Attractions at Universal Studios are fantastic and all about the guest experience as are their staff. Being able to hop from one park to the other is brilliant and we can easily spend a full day in Universal. Well worth every penny spent on tickets.

We went to the Make-up show expecting to see a demonstration of horror makeup effects or just plain old makeup effects and got a funny comedy show instead. We enjoyed it, but the "makeup expert" spoke very quickly and I didn't catch everything he said. They really only did one actual effect, and that was neat. I don't recommend this for very young kids or those who are scared easily. There's some fake blood and a relatively tame werewolf.

It's pricey but a "must do" at least once. To get the full benefit of the Harry Potter attraction, which is the most popular in the park, you need to pay a premium for a park to park pass. Attractions are all very realistic, food (especially Bubba Gump) is fantastic, butter beer is grand. We found the Chocolate Factory to be pricey but I had one of the best salads ever there. Had a brownie concoction for dessert and it was disappointingly dry. Lots of walking and lots of thrilling rides including water rides*you will get wet).
Long wait time, use your time to mingle, met jenny from the orlandodreamteamcom now I can visit anytime

We have been to 3 other Universal Studios but I think this is the worst. First, our family of 4 adults, got a ticket for a two days as advised so we can relax and be at ease no hurries for the rides around the park, one park one day. We chose to park nearer and that is coughing extra $10.00 on top of regular parking (total $35.00) even though we were there when the park opened 9am. At the door, we were offered front of line passes for extra $120.00. But since we thought 9am was early for us to go around and finish the rides, we opted not to. Besides paying $115 for a day ticket + another $120.00 seem ridiculous (total $235.00). Anyway, by 11 am, we finished 3 rides. By the time we got to the Harry Potter area, the lines were very long -- 120 mins. So we just let our teeners line up. My husband and I just decided to go around and wait at some designated area for our children. First I noticed that a lot of structures which I thought were stores turned out to be just facades, a little frustrated. Then after several hours we came to know that our sons had to line up 2 hours at most for each ride. We had no choice but to wait for them. Which made me think that if the waiting for each attraction was two hours, then the park has OVERSOLD ITSELF TO CAPACITY. Why sell that many tickets or allow a lot of people in if the rides cannot even accommodate them. 2 hours and more in line under the heat of the sun most of the time is ridiculous. So what they could have done was sell you $235.00 ticket in the first place. Which at that price I am sure nobody will buy. The marketing guru behind this entity is a genius. First they max out to capacity, then they sell you another ticket to make your life easier. So it is a win-win situation for them and customers end up grumbling. Hey and there's more, some rides require you to have empty pockets and bags be in the locker. Lockers are $3.00 for first 30 minutes. So the longer the lines, the more money you pay for the lockers. See I told you, they are the geniuses! So the next day, my husband and I did not go to the other theme park wasting our tickets (that was our choice though). I was telling my sons get the Front -of-line passes so they do not have the same experience as the day before. But lo and behold. The FOL ticket on that day turned out to be $180.00 per person and only the younger son bought as my older son thought it was just SO RIDICULOUS. So after 6 hours, they were out of the theme park. Younger son had 6 rides for $300.00 while the older son held on to his bags not to avoid the locker in some rides. We picked them up and we all swore that we will never go to this theme park again. And I promised to do a write up to make other families aware of our sad experience.
We had a great time! The park is clean, staff is polite and very helpful and at this time of year, it's not too crowded. I would definitely come back another time! There are attractions for all ages!

My family of 5 spent two days. Two of us had never been. It was a little disappointing after spending a week at Disney where they go above and beyond to please. The staff members we encountered were ok but not overly friendly with the exception of the breakfast with the Grinch staff and one staff member at Hogwarts Express. They have seats outside of the rides where people of size, like myself, can make sure they will fit in the restraints. Several times there were people just sitting in those seats waiting for people to get off the rides. I wish the people operating the rides would be more proactive about making sure those seats are used for measurement purposes only. One time I approached one of the seats and there was a couple sitting in them eating ice cream. They just looked at me and kept eating. I ended up walking away. As far as service goes I felt that US was like a Six Flags. I feel like they should be more like DIsney. That's just my opinion. I should also note the characters we took photos with were WONDERFUL!

You can tell when you arrive that there is a lot of cool stuff to see and do here, but 10 minutes into the place, you quickly realize that the wait times for things you really want to see/do are going to consume a huge part of your day and that your visit is likely going to end up feeling more like a really expensive walk though a downtown-like setting. If you're into that sort of thing, go for it! If not, you may want to consider other options.

Having time of my life walking around, The Blues Brother concert was a bonus. It's such an amazing place. The kid has a blast riding Transformer and other. Being Harry Potter fan walking to what you see in the movie is so exciting
The family finally decided to try this park and wow. So much to do. Minions, et,Shrek and transformers. Too much to do in one day. Definitely will have to go back. Highly recommended.

My husband and I went yesterday and had a great time. The park is easily navigable and friendly to both adult and children. Rides are a combination of thrill and 3D/4D movie related. Would highly recommend!

Be sure to know that there are 2 different parks, Islands of Adventures and Universal Studios. Universal Studios has more of the movie themed rides where as IOA has the Adventure themed rides. Both have areas for young and old! Of course US has Harry Potter and Fear Factor Live along with Transformers and Shrek. This is also where they have Mardi Gras starting the 1st weekend in February with concerts and parades. One of the things I like to do when entering the park with my kids is to take a picture of them prior to entering- this way I have a picture if we should get separated for some reason ( This is good for any age!) Also do this for your parking area in the garage ie: Spiderman 3 or Jaws , you will understand what I mean once you get there, that way you will not forget where you parked, and you know what your children are wearing should an emergency happen. Also, they have implemented metal detectors! Leave those fishing hooks off your hats guys- yes, they look nice but they will not allow them! Not even for an 11 y.o boy. If anyone in your family has a medical issue and can not go thru the metal detector your whole family can be wanded along with that family member, so that you do not have to split up. Only one member has to do the bag check! Hopefully, all this information helps!

This place is huge and the theming of the newer areas of the park is something else. The Hogwarts Express linking the 2 parks shouldn't be missed nor should Diagonal Ally or Jurassic World over at Islands of Adventure. We went at Christmas time and the queues were frankly ridiculous, go early or stay late but don't expect to do much by way of rides if you get there after 10am.

Universal in Orlando will make the effort and go to great lengths to scare you..  They have al sorts of tours and performers that look like they really love there jobs.. Very in to it.. (Great Actors)  Sounds effects and light shows are also great too..  You will never forget this.

We visit Florida most years and we almost always visit Universal Studios. Until my first visit, I thought I wouldn't like theme parks. Now I love them. It's not all rollercoasters - I'm too scared to go on them. There are loads of other rides that are great fun but not as scary. My personal favourites are Men In Black, The Simpsons and Escape From Gringott's. Transformers, Shrek and Minion Mayhem are also well worth doing.
20 years ago came here loved every minute of it, compared to what it once was this place is now garbage. Rather have a day in Blackpool and that's saying something
I would suggestion to visit this park after going to Island of Adventure. Also, purchase the fast pass for this park. I was able to experience all the attraction by doing this.

A great day out with some colleagues while we had a day off from a conference. Rides were excellent and having the express pass from our hotel was AMAZING!! With the park being split into two makes it expensive to try to see both in one trip. I still prefer LA universal over Orlando universal

Great place to spend a couple of days. So much to see and do, and all those iconic Universal attractions. Bubba Gumps, with Forest's shoes under the park bench to Harry Potter with a whole lot in between.

we went in january, so despite having premium tickets pushed at us to skip long lines, we bought standard tickets and queued for a maximum of 15 mins on each ride...Transformers kept breaking down and the Simpsons was closed, despite this, there was still plenty to keep us entertained

Best time!!! It was cold and rainy but there were NO lines, no wait!!!! Couldn't have worked out better. Road all rides by noon did character visits and 2nd and 3rd time on rides in the afternoon. Dinner at city walk and boat to hotel. Rides for all ages! Fun guaranteed for all.

We took our daughters ages 3 &10; both had tons of fun!  We went on Superbowl Sunday and the park was relatively quiet before 1-1:30pm, after that people began coming in at a constant flow.  Lines were roughly 5-15 minutes, which is great considering the popularity of the park.  Universal requires a great deal of walking/standing so be prepared and wear comfortable shoes.  The food court located on Fast Food Blvd. was anything but fast. It was terribly slow and by far my worst experience for the day. You are required to stand in line to then go to to the store you are interested in purchasing from; then line up again to cash out! The food was overpriced as mentioned in other reviews, however I had the pizza and it was good.  All of the employees were kind and eager to help! The grounds were very clean and well landscaped.  The Kids Zone - There are two areas where children can get very wet. The Curious George area is lots of wet fun.  Please note you need to have a multi-park pass in order to enter Islands of Adventure (which is just a walk/ferry away) and the Wizarding Word of Harry Potter.  Add this to your list of parks while visiting Orlando!

I think this park is absolutely best for people in their 20s. They won't be bothered by the fact that about half the rides have some feature that will annoy most other guests. And they'll like the Harry Potter stuff the best.  The designers of the Universal rides seem to think it's enjoyable to shake, spin or soak you (and, for the latter, then charge you $5 for a "human dryer"). I think almost all the rides would be better if they didn't gratuitously include these features. They also rely a bit too much on screens and 3D. That said, when they get the ride right -- and their newest rides like Kong and Gringotts seem to understand that you don't have to be physically uncomfortable to have fun -- they do the best theme park rides in the world.  The other small annoyance is the cost. Unlike Disney (where you can do things like stay a week and get a reasonably priced weekly ticket, get a free dining plan, and buy your tickets with discounted Disney gift cards) there's really no way to "game" Universal to get good value from them (well, maybe locals can buy certain deeply discounted annual passes). What you really need is a 2-day park-to-park ticket, but that's a pretty bad deal. You should probably buy it anyway. Three days is probably more than you need, at least in non-peak season, but it does allow you to take your time and go back to your favorite rides several times. And Universal tends to close earlier than Disney, so there's not quite as much time to enjoy the park.  With the early closing times, I highly recommend getting to the park early at rope drop. The hours between 9 and 11 are the best to do the rides.  Food is strangely priced in the parks. Fast food is ridiculously over-priced, and the Citywalk section (their version of Downtown Disney) is only marginally better priced. But the sit-down restaurants in the parks are surprisingly good deals -- they charge normal "street" prices. Mythos in Islands of Adventure will cost you little more than getting a hot dog from a cart and has very good food and excellent themeing. Finnegans in Universal Studios isn't quite as good but still a nice place for lunch. Even if you're only spending 2 days in the parks, you'll want to take a break and get off your feet. For dinner, I recommend taking the short boat ride down to Universal's Hard Rock Hotel and eating the half-priced bar meals from 5 to 7 pm (not on Saturdays). While drinks are overpriced (you don't have to drink), the bar meals are excellent value and the restaurant is an amazingly respite from the crowds and noise of hte park.

If you have a strong stomach, some of the rides are awesome, but for me, now that I am older (50's), all of the simulators made me feel queasy. But the Harry Potter part is more than awesome and they could do an entire theme park around it. Kids, and adults, could buy a wand and stand in certain spots and make things happen as "wizards in training." Very cool!! We really, really enjoyed the live animal show, try not to miss that. Very funny and entertaining. They had such a variety of trained animals: dogs, cats, pig, vulture, rooster, ducks, skunk, porcupine, parrot, and more -I won't tell. But the rest of the park has become so, so outdated that we were disappointed for the price. (Terminator 3-D movie, ET ride, King Kong, etc.) It is so overtime to update these old, old rides with new technology and new shows. We feel like we wasted a ton of money, and time, doing both parks but they have tied the Harry Potter theme so that you basically have to buy both parks to enjoy it. The ride from London to Hogsmead is more than unique! Again, if you get a little sick with simulators, you won't have a lot to do here. Fast Pass is not worth the price at this park, at least not today.

So, for those who don't know, the theme park has two parks: Islands of Adventure and Universal Studios. Studios, in my opinion, is the superior. It has the extremely popular Despicable Me ride, the best roller coaster (Hollywood Rip Rocket). Also, the best rides are the Mummy, Men in Black, and all of Diagon Alley (which is the best area in any theme park, Disney included).

It's been five years since I visited the original Universal Studios and was sad to learn their was no more Jaws ride, but hey they replaced it with Gringott's alley which is pretty amazing. The ride is alot of fun to boot. Transformers was just a jerky version of the Spiderman ride at Islands of Adventure but other than that we had a great time. Glad they still have ET and the Mummy ride is by far our favorite. Also with the train taking you to Islands of Adventure now it's very easy to travel between the parks.

Don't miss this. Thrill seekers please go. Great coasters. Harry Potter lovers please go. I'm not a big potter guy but it was fantastic. A must see!! Of course food etc...over priced. Just like Toronto!! Fully recommend.

It goes without saying that these parks make for a fun day out and are very entertaining. I just wish Universal would cease their practice of trying to extract every last cent from their guests. I have visited twice in the last week. The first time I decided to use the preferred parking option which I was assured by the girl on the desk was much closer to the parks and far less of a walk. This turned out to be a blatant lie. I was parked in the King Kong lot at the very far end of the row. It was an extremely long walk to the parks. On my second visit I was parked in Jarrasic Park lot (standard parking not preferred) and was much closer to the parks. Avoid preferred parking like the plague, it's a complete rip off. YOU SHOULD BE ASHAMED OF YOURSELVES UNIVERSAL. NO WAY TO TREAT YOUR PAYING GUESTS!
Spent the whole day here and still not enough time to see everything.  Fantastic place. Adults will enjoy it as much as the kids if not even more.

Awesome place for the entire family!!! We have been going to the parks for years and are annual pass holders. My family and I enjoy universal all year around and my kids can not get enough of it! Everyone should go the the amusement park at least once, you will not be disappointed!

I had a great time at Universal Studios Florida. This is a multiple day trip. The Wizarding World of Harry Potter will take a day by itself to see both Diagon Alley and Hogsmeade. So at least three days. One for Wizarding World, one for Universal Studios and one for Islands of Adventure. I also learned from my first trip to start the day early so that I can get as much in before the 5pm summer rain that seemed to happen everyday that I was in Central Florida. I will also take advantage of the express pass to help the lines go faster.
I like Universal. I have been there more than 5 times and it has different attractions for adults and children. They have updated several attractions and are excellent. I like Minions and the Mummy.

So. Much. F U N ! ! ! We had such an amazing time and got the quality couple time we needed. There are so many things for a young couple to do from rides to quiet sit down restaurants and just fun things to do together.

Universal puts Disney to shame much better rides fast passes work much better then disneys Minions ride is cool 4D Transformers ride is excellent, Shrek was not as good, the Hollywood ripe ride rocket ride was a lot of fun. A must do if in orlando

Very good day with the family..surprisingly not too much people in Feb. (We had the Fast Lanes pass - but most of the attractions had waiting time 20mnts in average). Attractions were amazing and we really enjoyed the mix of 3Dmovies/roller-coasters. The Harry Potter area is transporting you in another world.

My favorite part was the "impromptu" SING OFF in the middle of the street! There are plenty of people around to help, the only thing no one seemed to know, was where to see your photos! Also be prepared to rent a locker. You can't bring anything on the rides, so you can either put it in a locker and leave it all day or put it in and take it out after every ride. It's annoying and hard because of the amount of people, but if you need your bags between rides, you have to deal with it!

We went to Universal studios and islands of adventure for 3 days on an off week and it was basically as expected. Lines weren't terribly long food and drink were priced at where you would expect them. We weren't blown away by the park but we are mostly a Disney family and we know the attractions and the movies they are based on better. My wife get motion sickness sometimes and we never have a problem... She had a lot of problems with the rides at Universal, a lot of their rides are motion simulation type rides and that didn't agree well with my wife. Other than that it was a good time but we will probably Stick with Disney in the future.
Visited with family including a granddaughter. We had trouble keeping up with her. Had to go on every ride and adventure available of course. Very enjoyable indeed.

Disney is charming, but universal has rides that make you scream. It's a great time. We loved almost every ride we went on, and we even enjoyed the lines. Don't miss the Simpson's ride. The best food we had was at Cowfish. It's a great time.

It's hard for me to rate Universal after going to Disney. The staff isn't as friendly, the food is definitely not as good, and the whole atmosphere for me just can't compare. I do like the more thrilling rides here and Harry Potter world is great (although very crowded with small walkways). It isn't a place I say I want to come back to every year like Disney.

This is paradise for movies fanatics: all the best simulation for Minions, Shrek, Transformers, Terminator, Harry Potter, Men in Black and Simpsons are here (just to name a few). Most of these require 4d glasses (or at least 3d) which is not suitable to people with vertigos or other minor pathologies. My favourite was Transformers and Terminator: you will be dragged into a Hollywood screening - simply amazing !

Ridiculous, Absurd and disrespectful. Me and my kids, and a lot of people waited almost 3hours to enjoy The King Kong Ride, for only 5 minutes for the show time! The show was interrupted 2 times for technical troubles in the truck. Don't lost your time, it's terrible.
$600 for 2 of us two parks one day just not worth it a fast pass is absolutely needed unless you don't mind queuing for hrs Harry potter ride amazing
What an amazing experience Universal was! We loved all the rides, although the one Harry Potter ride did make us a little dizzy! ;) Well worth the money!  ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
I wasn't sure what to expect entering Universal Studios. THAT immediately changed ! I entered the Transformers attraction, It was so exciting, I never experienced an amusement park ride so awesome.
Definitely worth visiting in Florida. Plenty of mini parks to visit as well as great restaurants. Must go!

Whether you are a fan of all movies / characters ... or just a few ... you will have fun here! With forecast for rain all day, we almost didn't go ... but sooooo glad we did! Bring a rain jacket or buy a poncho there and it will be a great day (less crowded, short wait times on rides). Lots of indoor activities too - so you can escape the hot sun for a bit (or the rain). Be ready to do lots of walking - but there are plenty of benches to rest, places to buy drinks / snacks. We did afternoon pass (starting at 2pm) - and made it through whole park. Nearby city walk has plenty of restaurants.

First question people want to know, do I need 2 or 3 days? Park to Park admission? Short answer, if you're not in a rush, 3 days and yes get the park to park. We arrived Saturday morning, after check-in were able to get to the park by noon. By end of day we were able to at least see the grounds of both parks and squeeze in a good count of rides which is why you want the park to park. Wait times in this season were 5 min for older rides, 15 min for the newer, even Harry Potter? What I couldn't understand was the constant 60min lineup for Minions? Sure it was a good 3D experience but not proportional to other rides. Nonetheless, do yourself a favour, stay at one of the resorts to take advantage of the extra hour before opening. You can get more rides in one hour than all morning after opening. Could you do this park in 2 days? Sure, but it would be very rushed, take an extra day, it's worth it. BTW, best ride, ' Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey.' I'm still trying to figure out some of the effects.

our two sons are 11 and 9 years old. they loved everything. we enjoyed every part, rides and themes from comic strip, super hero, king kong, Jurassic world, harry potter, Sinbad, the simpsons, curious George , etc.

When I was younger, I visited Universal a few times, but I never truly appreciated it until now. I went for a mini 30th birthday getaway and had the time of my life! Going during the winter months was a great idea since the lines weren't ridiculously long. We arrived when it opened and for hours, the longest we had to wait for a line was about 20 minutes.  Make sure to visit Moe's Tavern for a Flaming Moe, Lard's Donut for a big strawberry frosted donut, and of course the amazing Harry Potter theme park...which as a Potter fan was amazing!
We went back and forth between universal and island of adventure so many times that hotels sort of run together but I'd do remember that the souviner shopping is better in. Universal

We visited both parks and traveled between them on the Hogwarts Express (recommend). There are rides for all ages and levels of thrill-seeking. The park is immaculate with plenty to see and do. Plan on spending the day to take it all in. Bring your appetite too because their are endless places to snack and dine.

We used to live in California and get the anual pass, so we are pretty familiar with Universal Studios. Nevertheless, while in Orlando, we were curious about the Harry Potter attractions and decided to visit the parks. We chose the 1 day, 2 parks pass and it was totally worth it. Maybe because it was an off-peak day, the lines were not that long (the Hogwarts Express only had a 10 minute wait) so we had time go on most of the rides we wanted to. I guess it would not work unless you already have been there a few times and can skip some of them.  The quality of every ride is amazing and they have recreated Harry Potter's world in both parks in an superb manner. It was the only day in forever that I did not hear my teenagers complaining... much. The only thing I didn't like was the food. Bad quality and expensive (as expected). They should offer fruit cups in the popcorn/drinks stands.

We always stay at an onsite hotel to take advantage of the express passes. Wouldn't go there without them, but then again, I'm spoiled. The cost of the room is expensive, but more than pays for itself with a family of four.  Do not miss the Horror Make up show. Absolutely hilarious.  We got a "immigration tour" at Men in Black. Was able to go on the bottom floor so that was really cool. All you have to do is ask! Although they only do it at certain times of the day.  Bought the Freestyle cup and was actually a cost effective option since my husband and I just shared a drink.  Got stuck on Reign of Kong for about 10 minutes. That is the one ride that seems to always be breaking down. They did offer to let us ride again immediately afterwards.  We will be back!

Myself, husband and 2 kids (9 & 11) spent the day at Universal Studios. We stayed the week at Disney and spent 4 days at those parks and 1 day at Universal. Our favorite day was the one spent at Universal. My kids LOVE rides and so this was perfect for them. On the day we planned to visit, I almost backed out because it was supposed to rain all day. It did! But, I think the rain kept a lot of the crowd away, so if you don't mind getting a little wet, then rainy days are perfect! I also purchased the one time express pass for each of my kids so that they could quickly re-ride anything they loved. In my opinion, even when it isn't crazy crowded, the one time express pass was worth the money. My kids also loved Diagon Alley. If I had to chose between universal and islands of adventure, then I would chose Islands of adventure for my family, but we could have easily spent a full day at universal alone and have a great time! We will be back...

We just happened to be at USF the night they decided to do a dry run of the new attraction featuring the Tonight Show, Ride thru NYC with Jimmy Fallon. It was well worth the wait. While waiting inside we watched our favorite Tonight show episodes and met #Hashtag the Panda.. We were entertained by the barbershop singers. It was a couples trip, without kids (ours are grown up now). We had a great day in this park. We stayed for the Mardi Gras parade that night. So much fun.

Group of 10 attended in January. Bought fast passes at the store inside, cheaper and you get them right away. Worked amazingly well, got onto rides immediately, line ups were short and staff extremely pleasant and helpful. Ate at one of the cafeterias for lunch, the food was hot, good and reasonably priced. Harry Potter is certainly worth seeing (even a second time). Would go back again.

While our daughter and granddaughter started at Universal Islands of Adventure, we met them as they left the Higwart's Express train into Universal Studios and then visited Diagon Alley. Great time and well done.

This park is so fantastic and gorgeous.....we spent at least 9 hours exploring and walking around. It wasn't too crowded, which is always a plus! The lines for the rides weren't too bad either. There are so many restaurants and food stands to choose from. All the employees are so friendly and helpful.

Park relies heavily on virtual reality rides. We went specifically to see Harry Potter area. Park is clean, well laid out and has many options for everyone's enjoyment. We spent about 7 hours in the park each day for 4 days in a row. It was the perfect amount of time for us.  When they make new attractions in future they need to add things that are NOT Virtual Reality. The VR format gets old quickly and most attractions are already VR. By the last day we were gravitating toward non VR attractions.  Ticket prices are very high, even for a theme park. Universal is far and away the most expensive theme park we've ever went to, and we have went to many. Prohibitive prices is what made this a park we waited a long time to do.  While other theme parks will get return visits from us, this one won't. We had a great time, but nothing about it, even Harry Potter, will draw us back for repeat visits.  The locker system where you secure items for free while you ride a big ride is ingenious and every theme park should do this.

So this was my first visit to Universal Studios. There was so much to see and do it is hard to know where to begin without writing a novel. I'll try to summarize quickly and in point form for easier reading; - you'll need at least two full days to go through everything - it is pricey - rides are newer and use different technologies to make 3D experiences - alot of rides are oriented around sit-inside simulators - we went a week before March break so longest wait was like 45 mins but doesn't feel that long and many waiting areas are sheltered from the sun... - rides / attractions for movies such as the Minions, Terminator, MIB, Simpsons, Shrek, Dr. Seuss and of course, lots and lots of Harry Potter. - Harry Potter castle and exhibits are very impressive - Harry Potter train is cool and worth taking- worth the extra $ - Harry Potter village also cool - Harry Potter ride MAY be abit scary for younger kids - may want to check out first before taking them in... especially if they have a dread of the Dementors (sp?). - Dr. Seuss village was very neat and had so much colour - brought back alot of my childhood memories of those books - Minions ride was good! - Simpsons ride was good - I liked it... but I like the Simpsons (unlike my wife who doesn't) - King Kong 3D ride was very good - the Animal Actors and Sinbad shows were good and we enjoyed the stunts - the Horror Movie Makeup show was very good - the makeup guy was hilarious and could be a standup comic - very sharp guy (Glad I didn't sit too close to him as they will pull people (victims) out of the audience). So funny. - fastpass (Express pass) was expensive but did cut down ride times and provided for early entry - Some rides may be hard on people with neck and back issues - make sure you check on that before taking a ride. They do have warnings posted. - Hulk roller coaster and other rides make you empty everything out of your pockets before going in. Some rides even check with metal detectors... so leave as much change, keys, metal stuff home as possible. Lockers they provide are small (mouth is like 1.5 x 1.5 feet wide) so would only take a small pack with you to fit into lockers... a standard backpack you send with your kid to school was too big so something 1/2 that size. - don't try to sneak something by them like keys or such in the roller coasters cause they have hand metal detector wands and will find it and make you go back out of line to locker to store... to which you gotta find another kid to open it specially and that wastes ALOT of time... I know...  Overall we really enjoyed our stay and did alot of walking in two days... we had the two of us parents and one 13 yr old... so if you have smaller ones, may want to take an extra day.  I will be going back to check it all again!

Universal hasn't changed much unless you are counting the Harry Potter sections, which are amazing. It is still a great park. I always go when I am in Orlando for the memories. If you only have one day or can't afford a hopper Island of Adventures is much better. The Harry Potter sections are a must see and I think that is what brings the crowds. You can't get to both Harry Potter sites without a hopper. My only complaint is that there isn't much that is new to draw you. If they consider Harry Potter it's own park then you shouldn't need to go through Universal to get to it.

We focused on diagonon alley. Be sure to check out the phone booth at the entrance to the ally by the night bus and dial the number found inside the booth.  We also enjoyed the other rides throughout the park. Use the app to guide you to the ride with the lowest wait time, that was a great feature offered by the park!  Be sure to ride the Hogwart's express in both directions to see both views

I love the memories, the older things they have and the newer, to stay up with the times. I am not a big fan of the Simpsons and it is a little gross to me but it is very colorful and I do like the ride, as an adult. I would, however, not allow young children to pay attention to the horrible things you see in the lines. The even enlarged the Simponville area so there are many things to see and do.. Its like a carnival area.  I love the Mummy Ride!!! Rip Ride Rocket is Thrilling!!!! Men in Black is super fun for the whole family. The Minion ride, even though it is thought of, as a child's ride, it is my favorite! It is so adorable and the graphics are amazing! Transformers is super exciting... Shrek is now a classic and fun... There are plenty of places to eat in the park and they even have a starbucks :) My favorite item is the dippin' dots.. though... and if you have small children or a child at heart then you would love Seuss Landing.  The newest addition is the Harry Potter area. It is my absolute favorite and you can never tire of it. The ride is thrilling and their are so many things to do while you are in the Alley. If want some extra fun, get a wand and practice around the park ;)  You can go back over and over again and you never tire of it.
lots to do. unfortunately lots of waiting and alot of delays after waiting. rides not working after waiting over 1 hour for one example..overall it is a unique place.

the Harry Potter train between the two parks was fun. The rest of the park was a waste of time and money - all shops and no entertainment. Quite a letdown after experiencing Disney. Universal was crowded, with no place to sit down and take a break.  I recommend saving your money and going elsewhere.
In general very nice. CLEAN, which was nice. The Hogwart's express was worth the park to park pass. Hogsmeade isn't as cool as Diagon Alley.

My boyfriend and I visited Universal for 2 days in March 2017. We had an express pass for one day. This was both of our first times at Universal and we mainly went because I wanted to visit the Harry Potter worlds. We stayed at one of the Universal Properties which allows you an hour early entrance to Islands of Adventure only! The hour early entrance basically means you finally get through the gate by the time the rest of the public can enter. Both days we went to the park we were very near the front of the line to enter and it still took about 30 minutes to get through the gate. We had no idea that we needed to have our finger scan to enter the park which turned both of us off. Not only does this add a lot of time to the entrance process is also does not work very well. The employees never tell you from the beginning to use the same finger which it seems like no one does and adds even more time because people apparently have no clue which finger they used to start.  The line management everywhere from rides, to lockers, to food were terrible. No employees around directing people. No stanchions anywhere to keep people queued. You needed to scan your finger to rent and retrieve items from your locker, but if your scan doesn't work there are no employees around to help.  The only way to get between parks other than exiting one and waiting in line again to enter the other is the Hogwarts Express which while we were there had a wait up to 60 minutes long and on the second day was down for part of the day.  The few roller coasters they have you are not permitted to have anything in your pockets at all. Coming from the Cleveland area where we frequent Cedar Point we found this very odd, because the majority of the coasters there you can have items in your pockets and those rides are way more extreme than the rides at Universal.  Everything from the ticket price, to food to drinks were way overpriced which I expected, but I also thought I would have a better visitor experience because of it. That is not the case.  I really did enjoy the Harry Potter worlds and had a great time there experiencing all if that, but I don't think that I would return to Universal.  I wish I would have researched the rides a little more so I knew that they were mostly virtual reality and 3D rides. I was looking for thrilling roller coaster rides which they do not have. I wasn't able to ride two of the coasters Rip it Rocket because it was down the first day we were there and the second day it was down for most of the day and when it finally came back up it was 140 minute wait. We also weren't able to ride the Dragon Challenge because of the mass chaos outside of the ride of people attempted to get lockers or their picture taken by the Hogwarts Express or in line for a butter beer. The Universal app told us the wait time was 15 minutes at one point so we walked over and right before our eyes the time went from 15 minutes to 60 minutes back down to 15 minutes and then back up to 75 minutes. After all of that we just decided to not ride.  Usually the bad sticks out more than the good. We did have an overall okay time, but we don't plan on coming back anytime soon.

The park is way overpriced considering it is the same price you would pay at Disney. Except for the newer Harry Potter areas, the park is just a bit dim and dated with 3D disorienting rides from 20 years ago. The workers did their jobs perfunctorily or a bit sullen with a "when is my break" attitude. I must give kudos for the Potter areas, but be aware that the very expensive express passes are not useable at the busiest and best Potter rides in the park. They are succeeding in getting Disney prices for a much inferior product. They try to get "extra" for every small perk or advantage. It is a nickel and dime scam operation and not really worth the price and outrageous if you sucker in or the $59 - $99 "Express Pass" which gives no advantage for the best rides and little advantage for the rest of the mediocre remainder of the park.
Good park if you arrive early, can be costly as you now have to pay for photos with the charicaters. Food also costly so advise to eat before arrive.

yep.for me it edges islands of adventure.just not going to see anything like this at home..never..again the entrance fee is bit steep.but in the end jus about worth it...try to go to the Halloween horror nights ..sept Oct November time..its that little bit extra aswell but again I've not seen this type of entertainment at home..enjoy

The whole place brings childhood memories and brilliant rides, men in black, simpsons, Harry Potter, we have been going for a few years so Jaws, the earthquake the twister were all good rides, mels cafe from happy days were all brilliant and through the day you get the cast doing different themes the blues brothers was all one of my favourites

I have not been to Universal in a very long time. It was great, Harry Potter World is amazing and they paid great attention to detail. Most of the staff was friendly and the park was clean and lots of ride/show options. We purchased an express pass so that we could enjoy both parks in one day, and we were able to ride everything we wanted in one day. We were exhausted afterwards but knowing we were able to do it all, was great!

My friend and I came to Orlando for a vacation. We spent 4 days at Disney, which was fabulous! When we got to Universal all we have had is problems. I got double charged for my reservation tickets. We had breakfast reservations at the 3 Broomsticks, I didn't realize that you need to print your reservation ticket but I was told by an extremely rude hostess that was the case. I went to the train station to get them printed out and was told that they couldn't find my reservation even though I had it on my phone in my email from Universal. I have worked in retail so I always try to be nice to others in retail so I know it wasn't me being rude.   I will never come here nor will I ever recommend it without letting someone what I have gone through here. We won't even go back to the park for our last day.  In my opinion, go to Disney!

Although there is a shuttle to take you to Universal Studios, we had a car so we drove. We were there in ten minutes, taking all local streets. How great is that?. Ticket pricing with discounts are super!! Be sure to ask your Resort or Hotel for the discounts. Our discounts were awesome at Westgate Lakes and Spa Resort. Be sure to ask about the discounts they are offering.
My teenagers love Harry Potter and liked that part, but said all the rides are boring. It's all about the theme leading up to the ride. Cedar point is way better for 1/4 the cost.

If you wanted a healthy snack all on offer is a pot of melon only (they call it a fruit cup!) at Starbucks or from a cart in The Harry Potter section. Not as good as Disney as for a healthy lunch,I couldn't even find salad, although it was very busy, so didn't queue for long in a couple of places.

Two parks, totally different feeling, Glad to see updates being made,some of the rides are getting a little stale. Most of the rides are of the 3-D sort, that just throws you around while creating a visual surroundings. Kind of rough for us older folks. A bit sad that the minions ride was so rough that there was height limits on it. The little ones would love a more gentle ride. MY suggestion is to create a more pleasant ride experiences to cater to all ages like Disney's Soarin'. Leave the thrills and bumps to the coaster riders. Not everybody enjoys that type of adventure.

We had a great visit to the parks. 4 day, two park ticket. Our 12 year old daughter loved both diagon alley and hogsmead. Diagon alley seemed to take the cake though and we spent a lot of time there. Best times are early morning or evenings when less packed. You almost have to purchase an interactive wand, which aren't cheap but gets you many interactive experiences in the area. The shops are super cool but small and do get full easy. Nocturne alley is off the side and cool. Escape from gringotts also very cool ride. Hogsmead also cool but for some reason less fun for us, however, Harry Potter and the forbidden journey is awesome and a one of a kind. We did the group VIP tour one day and really covered a lot of the parks and rides in a long day. It was pricey but by far the easiest way to do a ton of rides (at the discretion of your guide). Both Harry Potter rides we in our tour. The non VIP days we had a hard time (even with express pass unlimited) getting many rides in. I'm sure we skipped some long lines. So - at 269 per person per ticket per day (plus park entrance tix) the VIP Group tour was pretty awesome. Food in the universal parks and city walk were far better than Disney. By a significant margin. Disney rides and overall park experience may be better than universal though. Our favorite restaurant as well as best value (under 30 for a family of 3) was Moes southwestern grille. It's right near the entrance and we are there twice. Overall, Harry Potter fans will love the park. Souvenirs aren't cheap (robe 109, wand 50, etc) but high quality. Lows were the "unlimited refill drinks" for 13 or 14 bucks each. They actually can only be refilled every 9 minutes, which would be fine if they filled correctly. Ours malfunctioned more than not. I personally got one frozen drink and was unable to refill with water (machine kept locking me out). It's false advertising and faulty setup. Don't fall for it. We stayed at cabana bay and loved the hotel too. Overall, highly rated experience.

We spent Spring Break '17 at Universal Orlando. We really enjoyed both parks and all of the attractions. We were not aware of the park closing early on Friday for Grad Bash and had planned to sleep in Friday morning and spend the last half the day at the parks. My son really was hoping to ride Rip Ride Rockit at night and Friday was the last night of our stay. We didn't find out about the early closing (6 pm) until we got to the gate. It was just a disappointing end to an otherwise wonderful week. We were staying at a Universal Resort...seems like that would have been better publicized to allow guests to plan accordingly.

Universal is such a great place to enjoy the whole day I really have a lot of fun You buy the entrance and with it you have access to all the atractions , As a recommendation buy two days park to park so you can go to Universal and adventure island with the Hogwarts Express and see all the Harry Potter's atraction that are absolutely awesome.

It was so convenient and easy to walk a short distance or take a boat to either Universal or Islands of Adventure! The new New York ride was great too but our favorite was still The Mummy!!
Not impressed. The Harry Potter space was the only part of universal that we enjoyed. In order to see all of the Harry Potter world we had to buy a pass for both parks.
Wowzers is an understatement!! An awesome park to visit but be prepared to pay! I highly suggest getting the fast pass otherwise you will wait in very long lines.

We went to Universal City walk to get the feel the night before the big day!! We asked a friendly attendant by the gate to universal about getting our tickets printed for the next day. Most of the rides end in a gift shop meet your party there if u go on the rides at separate times.
We visited in 1998 and then again in 2016. Didn't recognise it. Full of great family rides. Fantastic how the 2 parks are linked by Harry Potte world.

Then the more we went to, the more we repetitive we felt and disappointed. Walking in the park, we felt like we were paid entrance fee of $300 to shop in a shopping mall.  Roller coasters are okay, not pushing the limits.  Total ripoff. Universal is so greedy and lack imagination and planning. Will spread the words. I bought my 4 teenage and we had a great time. Lots of great attractions. We loved the 4d movies. Favorites include Jimmy Fallon, minions, & the make up show.

We are at the restraint staff we're very friendly and efficient very good service. 10/10 to the chefs for the amazing food and brilliant portion sizes in the adult and child meals certainly have to visit here if u go to Universal....simply brilliant 👍🏼😁
Exactly how you expect it if not better. It doesn't matter what age you are, Universal will never fail to amaze you.

Tips: use the single rider like e with any kids over 10...and meet up outside the ex it. Super short wait times. Best value snack...5 for a giant donut in Springfield. Race Through NY with Jimmy Fallon ride is really a good & fun! Universal has the formula down with the 3-D rides. The pre-set arrival times keep the waiting to a minimum & the show highlights you watch are entertaining. After doing the ride - walking through the "streets" of NY are fun to explore. We headed to the Mummy ride & although more old school is still cool! Worth doing. Lots to ride & do & explore.

So much to see and do here! I recommend the following new rides: Minions, Race through New York, Transformers. Did Transformers several times as so much to see and understand. Diagon Alley with the train ride and Gringott's ride is beyond words exciting and fun. We rode the Gringott's ride 3 times, once each time we went. Saw something new each time! We were lucky, went in the morning and later in evening on a Tuesday and a Wednesday so longest wait was 15 minutes for Harry Potter rides. We had express passes for the other rides so walk on worked great! All in all the best time!

We used our early pass to go on Harry potters escape from Gringotts and then took our time with everything else. Something for the whole family from rollercoaster to 4d cinemas. We enjoyed the merchandise as well all reasonably priced including the interactive wands that our kids used. We loved the Journey on the Hogwarts express just a great day. No one watches ET, The Mummy, Terminator, Shrek or Fear Factor. I don't even know many people who still love the Simpsons. Transformers ride is okay, its identical to Spider-Man, just not Spider-Man. Everything is blurry, like im watching tv on my old tv from the 90s. I would think the technology is there to create crystal clear pictures and lifelike experiences now especially since we have crystal clear pictures on our Tvs. The kids area was fun. Most kids are watching Paw Patrol...which is Nickelodeon and I dont get why the only Nickelodeon characters there are Spongebob. Even he's a tad old. But there is just lack of imagination and no trying to keep up with the times. Why not have a Batman ride? Super man? Those never go out of style. Harry Potter is cool, but again, not work the money. A must see place for any trip to Orlando it's like an amazing place to remember and see the new can't recommend enough

My daughter wished to go to Disney World. We got passes to go to Universal. Which was amazing! Everyone was so helpful and excellent towards my daughter. She wanted to meet Spongebob and she did. She also made a friend that works with the cast of Dora The Explorer and Go Diego. She was a flower. Apparently, the flower's name is Abigail. Which happens to be my little girl's name. During the parade, the flower waved and blew kisses to my daughter. While trying to get back towards the Hello Kitty store so my daughter could look around, the whole cast surrounding Dora and Diego interacted with my daughter while she watched them dance around.  The lines were not that long, but we had a fast pass to get us through most of the rides. When we were confused, employees were there to assist us and help us have a great time. We didn't ride many rides due to her height but they made sure we knew where the kids rides were.  She also rode her first roller coaster and they gave her a certificate for riding her first coaster. Which was the Woody Wood Pecker Ride.  Thanks for making this a great trip.
