Returned after 16 years and loved it just as much. Mel's diner serves great food and milk shakes! Harry Potter diagon alley amazing. Missed Jaws though - I know it was dated but it was fun:))

My family and I love Disneyworld properties. In my mind, Universal Studies was a decent alternative to Disney but not comparable. Last year, I purchased an annual pass to Universal Studios/Islands of Adventure because the price is so low (compared to Disney). Over the last year, my family and I have visited Universal Studios nearly 20 times and the park never gets old -- we are total Universal converts. We love the value of the annual passes. Here's a few things we enjoy about Universal Studios:  1. ET: ET is old as crap but this does bring up major nostalgia for me (I'm in my late 30s and ET was the first movie I ever saw in the theater). I will literally, not figuratively, die if something ever happens to this ride. 2. The entire area around ET: Barney. Curious George. American Tail. This is a great play area for smaller children (I have a four year old and he loves this part of the park). 3. The Simpsons: Again, I'm in my late 30s so I grew up watching the Simpsons. The theming in this area is incredible. Stop by and get a Duff Beer and a Flaming Moe (but don't eat a Krusty Burger -- so gross). 4. Kings Cross/Diagon Alley: Diagon Alley takes my breath away each time I walk in -- it is visually stunning. Drink the frozen butter beer. It is amazing. 5. The Mummy: Outdated theming (but of course, this is coming from the person who loves ET); however, the ride is awesome. I'm not too big on rollercoasters but I do enjoy this one.  There's a few things I don't like about the parks: 1. Just about every dang ride has some component in which you wear glasses/goggles and stare at a screen. Minions. Jimmy Fallon. The Simpsons. Gringotts. At a certain point, I feel like I'm riding the same ride. Plus, the screens make me a little sick. 2. Jimmy Fallon: This dude just sucks. There's nothing funny about him. The Roots are awesome, though. Bring back Twister. Or just demolish the Jimmy Fallon ride. Build bathrooms over it. 3. Height requirements: When we first started going to Univesal, my son could ride very few of the attractions because of his height (even in Dr. Seuss land in Islands of Adventure).  While my family and I still enjoy our Disney vacations, Universal is near and dear to my heart now. We just renewed our annual passes for year two. Can't wait for another year of adventures at this park!
Best place ever. Love both parks. But, food is really bad. We tried most of the restaurants, but the kitchens are really bad. Be prepared.

We are Florida residents with annual passes. We are in our early 50's and live in Cape Coral/Fort Myers which is three and a half hour drive. We come at least 6-12 times a year and there is almost always something new to see! We love the fact that we can buy alcholic beverages all through the park! The attractions are tame but thrilling (with a few exceptions there are rides we are scared to go on!) and so well done! The new Jimmy Fallon Race thru New York is amazing with the latest technology and is the most believable and smooth 4d experience we have ever done!!! The food is way above average for a theme park and a multitude of selections! We absolutely love staying at the Royal Pacific hotel onsite and you get a precious extra in the form of express passes and early entry to parks! The express passes get you front of the line at most attractions! This makes it possible to ride five times as many rides and cost like 70.00 bucks a day per person so it's worth to stay onsite at certain hotels just for this benefit! All in all Universal is the best park in Orlando! It's better organized than Disney it's more adult oriented than Disney it's not as crowded as Disney and I've heard it's even cleaner than Disney go make your own opinion but you won't be disappointed, if your lucky you can catch the Blues Brothers performing on the streets of universal and they are awesome!!! They sound, look, and act just like the real deal we loved them and everyone was dancing in the streets!,
I loved it here to, but after you finish with this park, you should do city walk, there were so many different places to choose to eat from in city walk, I will say I feel they go hand hand

Just the right combination of thrill rides, kid friendly stuff and shows, dining options and shops. Can do both theme parks & Citywalk in 2-3 days with Express pass. Extra time gives you the chance to slow down the pace.  We stayed at Hard Rock Hotel & would definitely do it again. Very convenient, comfortable, excellent pool and free express riding passes!  We love Disney, but 6 days at Universal felt more like a vacation than 6 hectic days there.
We visited Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure 2 days each by buying the 4 day ticket. Had a great time and enjoyed the new attractions available.

We got tickets by doing a resort presentation. We loved Diagon Alley but it was all the way in the back and as a handicapped person it was a long way. I wasn't really interested in the rest so I'm glad I didn't pay full price. Is it neat? Sure. But very expensive.

I really wish they would be more creative and have less 3D rides and more old school rides. Bring back the old KONG and JAWS. Classics that really shouldnt have gone. We like going, but Disney would be our choice if they don't update things..
Universal Studios provides rides and entertainment geared toward tweens and up. The new Jimmy Fallon Race through New York ride and Diagon Alley are nice additions to some of the old favorites.

This was a wonderful weekend trip to Universal Orlando Studios and Islands of Adventure. We stayed at Cabana Bay Beach Resort, which is a light walk/ short shuttle from the parks. We enjoyed these parks much more than Disney because there were more adult oriented activities and rides. The Mummy, Transformers, and the escape from Gringots are all rides not to be missed. The Simpsons area is great for kids of all ages and I was pleasantly surprised how good the food was at Krusty Burger. The Harry Potter area is amazing whether you are a fan or not. Enjoy the non-alcoholic butter beer. Try and get to the park early and take the more popular rides. Mother's day weekend was a good time to go as the lines were not too long. One minor complaint I had was there were very few places that opened early to re fill the souvenir cup. The park was clean and the staff was excellent (they kept the lines moving).

The beginning of this ride is probably the best only because of the wait area. The ride itself is very similar to the Star Wars ride. Definitely try it out at least once but I prefer Skulls Island though

We arrived a little early and were able to get into the park early. We headed right back to the Harry Potter area. I would recommend trying food at the Leaky Cauldron in Diagon Alley. Also try the Butterbeer. I would recommend the hopper pass so you can ride the train. It is worth it!

We visited and spent the day at a Universal Studio as part of our honeymoon and I was so pleased we did so.  There were so so many things to go on (rides, shows and so on), and we spent the full day at the park.  A must visit, if you're in a Orlando for sure!

We had a blast!! My kids loved universal studios more than the majic kingdom. Love the rides love the food love the overall look and feel. I wouldn't advise anyone to go between 1 & 3pm as it's an open space and too freaking hot. I had a heat stroke.

I had never been to Universal before this trip and I felt now like I had been missing all the fun. This was a great time all of my family had fun, I found many blues brothers memorabilia which I love. The shows from small to large are fun and a blast to watch. Even the Harry Potter stuff although not my thing was a lot of fun and quite interesting to look and interact with. Even my kids now want to come here instead of Disney, which is fine by me as their resorts are way better in my opinion with waaaay more benefits to staying onsite and a more reasonable cost. I consider this a must do if you are in his part of Florida.
This is not my first visit to Universal. The Harry Potter rides and Diagon are amazing. Men in black is also a favorite.

Let your imagination go and enjoy the rides!! Universal studios and Islands of adventure provide sensory overload! We covered both parks in one day - recommend an express pass though to do that! Our fun filled day was topped off with a great dinner at City Walk. If you have to pick one - this is it!

My wife and I visited Universal park with some friends. It was great to feel like boyfriend and girlfriend having fun and feeling you in an amusement park.  Love the rides at Universal. Especially, the 4D rides. Of course our first date was 18 years ago when the first "Mummy" movie cane out. So we really enjoy the ride. The new "Jimmy Fallon" ride is fun and a great upgrade to replace the "Twister" show.

For $110, you'd think that Universal would at least include all the Harry Potter attractions in one park. But nooooo. I knew in advance that because the Hogwarts Express stops in the other park you had to buy a multi-park pass to ride it, but what I didn't know was that THREE of the other four Harry Potter rides are in the other park, even the Hogwarts one. All you get in the Wizarding World is the Gringotts ride and a bunch of overpriced shops. At least the frozen butterbeer was good. And no, I didn't buy a wand. I wasn't going to spend $45 ($50 if you want an interactive one) after finding out the "complete" HP experience would have set me back another $55.

This is probably my 20th or more trip to Universal Studios over the years and this time my partner and I went without our kids, we are in our 60's...we enjoyed every ride even the Rockit Roller Coaster. A favorite was the Harry Potter Attraction, although we walked right past the entrance, I felt it wasn't very well marked, I spoke to others in the park and they said the same thing. All in all we had a blast for seniors.

This past weekend we traveled to Universal Studios to specifically go to the Wizarding World of Harry Potter for my elementary aged son who like many kids is a huge Harry Potter fan This was a first trip for us to the park (both Universal and Islands of Adventure) and admittedly we are accustomed to Disney parks. Here are some tips that we learned that I wish someone had told us before we arrived: 1. If you are a Florida resident and have purchased Florida resident passes or specials, every adult in your party has to show a Florida driver's license when you pick up your tickets even if you paid for them in advance. This created a huge mess for us - because one of the adults in our party didn't bring his driver's license. Nevermind that we purchased the tickets way in advance, both of our names on the credit card which paid for the Florida tickets, and that they mailed information to our Florida address - this all meant nothing. It was an awful ordeal to go through and really started off the day as what was very happy into an anxiety driven hot mess. Fortunately, we ultimately were able to prove that everyone in our party was legitimately a Florida resident. Michael at the front gate at Islands of Adventure with his smiling face and kind words was a welcomed sight and helped ease an otherwise chaotic and rocky start to our day. 2. We were given so many tickets for each "event" that it was hard to keep up with them. For example, each person is given a ticket to get into the parks; then there is a separate ticket for express lines; then there is yet another ticket for your room key; and if you purchase any meal plan, then there is another ticket for that. I counted we had 12 tickets! Plus, a Florida driver's license you have to have on your person, and credit cards! The Disney magic band has got logistics on Universal beat by a huge margin on this. Wear the magic band and all is magically taken care of! I missed Disney at this point. I heard several folks complaining about the ridiculousness of all the tickets. Bring yourself a good organizing wallet or neck pouch to handle all of your tickets and don't let the kiddos be in charge, because lose them and oh, well - good luck on that front ... and the tickets all resemble each other and aren't easily marked as what is what. 3. Be prepared to walk in the range of 4 to 6 miles. I knew there would be walking involved, but I had no idea how much. We stayed at the Loews Hotel thinking we'd be closer, and it was, but still we walked 4 to 6 miles per day, and we were focused on simply the area of the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. Even my husband who walks 10 miles per day said he never dreamed there would be that much walking involved from area to area. The boats do not drop you off in front of the Wizarding World - so they were pointless. Walking was the "closest" way to get there. The upside of this -- if you are looking for a weight loss, boot camp of sorts -- head over there. When I returned, I felt like I was ready to keep up walking 5Ks. So, that was positive. Even after eating what I wanted, I had lost 2 pounds with all the walking. 4. Shady spots to sit in and around the Wizarding World of Harry Potter (in both Islands of Adventure and Universal) are few. I was shocked as to how few benches or places to sit there were. We stood over other people waiting for them to move so we could sit down on a bench. Some people were sitting on the cement ground, but I couldn't bring myself to do that. 5. Bring your extra cash and credit cards because Wizarding World of Harry Potter is a commercial marketing mecca from start to finish. I was surprised by how much Universal charges in the Wizarding World for everything. Want to do the interactive game with the wand? Well, gotta buy the wand - my son, picked out the $40 one. Yikes! And there are the shirts, the food, the hats, the shops ... everywhere we turned it was another cash machine. Again, I think Disney is actually better than Universal on this one. At least, inside Disney there are some complimentary things your family can do without being hit up again and again. For example, you can pick up COMPLIMENTARY cards to play a sorcerer's game at the fire station at the entrance.  With all of that being said, I did rate the experience as "very good." The reason being is that you do feel transported to the area you are in - meaning you do feel like you are in Hogsmeade or Diagon Alley. Every area of the park was that way - whether you were in Springfield, Illinois with the Simpsons or Seusville. I just think Universal needs to figure out some better logistics and creature comforts for its guests, especially for those guests who are over the age of thirty or who are families with small children in tow. A tram or transport vehicle, more shady benches or sitting areas, and a few complimentary activities/items would go a long way, and put Universal on the same par as Disney parks, if not better than Disney parks.

Universal has come a long way since the 80s. With the consistent expansion they are really trying to challenge WDW as a destination in itself. The old classic rides, unfortunately, seem to be going the way of the dodo to make room for new experiences. Jaws was one of my favorites as well as the back lot tour, but sadly they are gone. Now the Harry Potter areas area amazing (separate review) but there is something to be said for the nostalgic rides. E.T. had no lines while we were there and neither did Terminator. I can see some type of refresher for those rides before long. Overall, Universal is great as either an add-on to a vacation to Orlando or as a few day standalone trip. The ticket prices are very much front-loaded so if you are going for a day, you might as well extend. Get park-to-park as the two are so close and interchangeable that you would very likely want to go back and forth.

We enjoyed every ride. We're not big Harry Potter fans, but if you are this is the place to go! They have a whole section built to look like the town and real stores from the movies and several movie based rides.

had a wonderful time even though it was only for one day...I would have to say that some of the vendors were rude, giving attitude. But in the middle of the afternoon after 4 pm I came across A Security Guard named Jose from Puerto Rico a super amazing person that lead me to the Harry Potter Ride since I was lost. He made my day. and I was already ready to leave I came across Jose again and he asked how was my day going I told him...that I was having a hard time to get in at the Jimmy Fallon ride...he then told us to follow him and got us in with no problem....and it was an awesome ride. I love it

This is it third trip to Universal and we always enjoy it. On a day with the crowds are down you can easily do everything in a day. On a busy day it will be worth the extra money for the Express Pass. Unfortunately two of our favorite shows were down for renovation but we still had a great time.

We Loved Universal Studios... The Mummy ride was our Favorite we Loved having the Express passes and they were well worth the price.. We also liked the Transformer Attraction and the Harry Potter one. A boy 10 in our party misplaced his lanyard with his Express pass in it and the Customer service kiosk reprinted it for him. The Universal guy who did this for our young man was very nice Thank you

Absolutely loved universal studios. My favourite park in Orlando. Crowds weren't half as bad as Disney, the longest we waited for a ride was 20 minutes (escape from gringotts, amazing) my all time favourite ride The Mummy was still as fab as I remembered too! Our little boy loved woody woodpeckers coaster, he managed at least 5 rides everyone we visited and walked on every time. We shared a big pink donut between 5 of us, very reasonable price at only $4.99! Expected to pay around $12 for it. We took a subway lunch in the park with us to save money but meal deals were between $10 and $15. We also requested free iced water from any kiosks that do soda fountain drinks and just added our own squeezy squash rather than paying $3.50 per drink. Can't wait to return!

Universal Orlando is my family's favorite. We live the rides and attractions...The resort property is beautifully kept. The on site hotels are amazing, beautiful. We enjoy trying different restaurants at citywalk and inside the theme parks

Universal was a great way to spend the day. I will say that I prefer Islands of Adventure though it is really close. The lines were okay. Some would only take 5 minutes, and others would take us up to a 60 minute wait. The food was good although it was a little pricey. If you are on a lower price range, don't like waiting in lines for a while, or are just nit picky DO NOT even go to an amusement park just to complain. Go to spend time with friends or family.

Our family love love loved Universal Studios Florida. The rides are amazing, the food is great, and the shows are imaginative and captivating. My 7 year old son was called on to be a volunteer at the Animal Actors on Location show and it was absolutely adorable. We are already planning another trip for next year!
Fun place, not many attractions, very crowded this time of year, lots of shops, to many for me, but I am sure most people love it. I just enjoy the different attractions.

This place is amazing. We loved it so much we went for 4 days of our holiday. The rides are awesome and easy to find way around. When we went in May it was quite quiet so hardly any wait for rides so was great. Cannot fault this place at all, would go back again.

We loved universal! Can't wait to go back, the attention to detail is amazing! We loved the rides. Transformers, The Mummy returns and Jimmy Fallon were amongst our favourite rides. You must try the fat lad doughnuts and turnkey legs! The park is open all day and so much to do. The iPhone app is really good and informative. Fireworks were well worth the wait and the place is magical at night time!

i was glad we got the four day pass to islands of adventure and universal studios because you cannot do every thing in one day.came in the morning `before it got to hot then went to the hotel for a swim .buses took right to the hotel.if you get to hot head to one of the indoor rides you wait in air conditioning. GREAT.

Be sure to start at Diagon Alley to shop the wizard stores and ride the Grinngott's bank vault run. This is an amazing 3-D ride. The next best ride is Jimmy Fallon's New York 3-D ride. Then do the Trasformer, Mummy, Minions, and whatever your heart's desire. For the bravehearts, there is the Rock It roller coaster ride. There are good eateries in the park but be prepared to spend the $$. As example, spent $45 for four Auntie Anne's pretzel dogs with two bottled water. Overall, if you want your fix for fast rides then you'll find it here. Otherwise, take the Hogwarts Express train at King's Crossing to Hogesmeade (Island of Adventure) to do the Potter, Kong, and T-Rex rides.

We have been here twice and would highly recommend it, the best park in Orlando. Take the Express Unlimited Pass and safe time. It's really worth it's money. The 3-D and 4-D attractions are the best ones. This is the only theme park in Orlando we would visit again and again and again ...

Disney is for families with kids but Universal is families with teens. We love all the rides, Rocket, Minnons, Mummy, Transformers, Simpsons, etc. The park offers a variety of rides for everyone, we also enjoyed the Horror Make Up Show.

We are all in our late forties and early fifties but that made no difference to our time there. We had a ball. Would recommend fast passes though as the lines are quite long. You could end up wasting your day queuing.

We went here for my daughters high school graduation vacation. She loves Harry Potter. We had lots of fun. I like using the AP that tells what the wait times are it is very helpful. May is a good time to go before everyone gets out of school and vacations start happening lines where not real bad.
A great family vacation and something for everyone! My son doesn't like thrill rides and he still loved it.

My family had a great time enjoying the rides and events at universal, but my pregnant fiancé could only do 1 or 2 events and she did not have a good time while we went on rides. They should have some more activities or rides that expectant mothers can enjoy other than the shops while the rest of the family does the more thrilling adventures.
If you like Thrill Rides, this is the theme park for you! Every ride is thrilling and it's great for the thrill seeker in all if us!
Even though we had wet days here, most rides were indoors. Lots of simulator-action packed 3D rides. They were all very entertaining. Thumbs Up!

Amazing park - it's popular but not overcrowded; the sets are creative and brilliant and atmospheric. You are in New York and 'Thoroughly modern Millie'one moment and 'Harry Potter' london Islington the next. Universal has the best rides for me and and not too many queues. I love Simpsons and Mummy and ET. The rides are so creative and contain beautiful sets and lights . Love it .

First time visiting here with the family. All of the children were teenagers and thoroughly enjoyed Universal! Great day out and the rides were insane. We visited here on holiday and would totally recommend anybody with teenagers that are looking for something to do in Orlando, that Universal is definitely a place to go. Fun for all the family with great decorations and great rides that are nothing like I'd seen before. Plenty of places to eat with good food. Definitely recommend!
the best theme park we went to, waiting times much less ave 20mins most queues are under cover the rides seemed much better all in all a great day out

Something for everyone whatever your age. Our group ranged from 25yrs to 72yrs and we all had a fabulous time. There are rides for all ages and every taste, even me. Everyone is so polite and friendly. I obviously can't go through all the rides but you will find something you like Tips: Take a Poncho on Popeye or you will get soaked to the skin. Also found Parks a lot quieter on Sundays. Universal Studios is a MUST.

You'll still have tons to do at Universal! This was always my big fear because I'm not a huge coaster fiend, I prefer slower, more immersive rides (like E.T.). You can easily spend more than half of the day just roaming Diagon Alley or Hogsmeade, plus there's tons of unique food and beverage items to try out all over the park.  I really liked the Simpson's part of the park, especially Moe's. Plus the shows at Universal are very entertaining too. Make sure to get the park hopper so you can see both sides of the park. There's a lot of meet and greets to do too. I recommend the raptor encounter in Jurassic Park! That's a fun one. Overall, I will return to Universal but it definitely wouldn't be something I'd do every time I'm in Orlando.
We had a great time, but we hope management will retool the express pass and single rider situations.

It doesn't matter if you're a child or an adult Universal Studios has something to offer for everyone. We had such so much fun we had to do it again for a second day. The Harry Potter exhibit is great with the fire spitting Dragon and ride and the train ride between the parks was good. Hands down the Transformer ride is the best ride in the park. Lots of fun.

What a great place, doesn't matter what your age there is something here for you, I was here last year and had a great time but in the space of a year there is more to do, you don't need to go on rides if that's not your thing as the shows and scenery are amazing

Universal studios is the best theme park in Orlando, forgot the other parks. The park is easiest to navigate and has the most modern rides. I experienced less lines between waiting to go on rides and I never experienced any of these attractions breaking down. The park offers a drinks cup refill cup you can fill all day for 1699 dollars which is good value and you don't need to be staying in a universal resort to buy one unlike other parks. I paid £217 for a 14 day pass and I feel I got more than my moneys worth from this park. The location is only a 5/10 minute drive from international drive and is central for most visitors to Orlando. The park also has plenty of characters around the park to have your photo taking with which enhances the theme park experience.

The park was nice, staff ok, the lines are insane and their "express pass" is a scam for everyone that doesn't have one, unless you want to wait in line forever and have the wait time magically change due to people with express pass re-riding without any wait, you should buy a pass. We didn't and ended up not going on many of the rides. Didn't matter as we were there mainly for Harry Potter, where express pass is not accepted. If you don't care about Harry Potter, than I am not sure why you would ever visit these parks. Volcano Bay was nice, but again useless without express pass, 110 min wait that never got any shorter for many of the slides. The attendant told me it was because we didn't have express pass, I was like these tickets weren't free. Anyway, I am rambling. Harry Potter was well done, but crowded and the food at three broom sticks was better than leaky cauldron imo. If your kids are Harry Potter maniacs like mine, worth it, but probably only really need two days, otherwise save your money.

Went there with my wife and two young children about age 5 and 7. The came to the park for the children and surprisingly a lot of rides were allowed for them (remember there are height restrictions for each ride). We had a really fun vacation there.  We went there in June, so a little bit packed but still reasonable waiting time. However I would suggest to but ExpressPass so you can skip the line especially if you only spend 1 day for both theme park  Harry Potter Escape from Gringotts and Transformers were my Favourite in this theme park  Some attraction need to be updated such as Simpson's Krusty ride and ET.

I guess when it comes down to it, Disney will always be the standard that all other parks are marked against, to this end Universal Studios is no exception. The park itself is a lot fresher in its look, it hasn't been around for as long as the Disney versions, they are extremely well organised with spacing between attractions well thought out. Staff were extremely polite and very relaxed, whereas at Disney the opposite applies, the staff are extremely official and stick to the script. The studios offered much better access to the characters for the public to interact with, everyone from "Bettlejuice and The Blues Brothers through to The Despicable Me and my lady Marilyn Monroe". All of these and the rest that are far to numerous to mention will interact with you and pose for photos with you. That having been said, the one thing they lack, is MAGIC!!! The iconic ingredient that Disney has survived on for years and will probably do so for the next 50 years. They have tried to gain the icon with the Harry Potter theme and as well as that is presented it still isn't enough - its not magical. That folks and the rubbish food is the only thing bad I can say, but enough for me to give it a very good rather than an excellent.

Great great great!! We had a brilliant time here it's relaxed madness!! We spent a few days going around to see everything and revisiting some parts. It's easy to get in and out of with the city walk parking and buses and taxis. We had a great time and would highly recommend it for any type of holiday , couples , groups , family's!!

We've been Disneyworld vets for a long time now but made our first trek to Universal last summer. I wasn't sure what to expect. Was it going to live up to my Disney type expectations (especially for level of detail) or was it going to be more like Cedar Point (which is our local big amusement park)?  We were pleasantly surprised and loved it! Now we can't imagine being back in Orlando and not fitting in a visit to these two parks!  We got the buy 2 day, get 1 day free deal and went to Islands of Adventure first and then Universal Studios the second day. We had a really good time at the park and loved Harry Potter of course!  Since we didn't get the park hopper we did not ride the Hogwarts Express. I will say though that for our 3rd free day we did chose to visit the Universal side as opposed to Islands of Adventure but it was mainly because overall we liked the rides here better and Diagon Alley as well.

Universal Studios is a great theme park. If I had to choose, I would actually give a slight edge to Islands of Adventure, but Universal Studios is still a blast. And just considering the Harry Potter areas, Diagon Alley is definitely the best!  Do your research on the rides and shows using the Universal website and a map. Get the Universal app and play with it before you go. Check crowd levels and get Express Passes if it is going to be busy. (Express Passes are included with some of the resorts.) Use Early Entry for the Harry Potter area if you can.

Hello all, Let me start by saying I travel extensively for work and have the privilege of staying in the most VIP resorts worldwide. From the Ritz Carlton Hong Kong to private resorts in the D.R. my son and I are well versed in so called VIP service.  For Fathers Day, my son, his mother and I booked the private VIP experience at Universal Studios Orlando and with low expectations to say the least. What happens next blew me away.  The VIP Experience was incredible!!!! Renee from the VIP office was beyond knowledgeable, she made the experience truly VIP. From seamlessly reviewing what we were interested in doing, working time lines and expectations.  Renee was the Experience and made the park feel like our own personal playground.  I only have 3 pieces of advice if your considering this experience. 1- ask for Renee !!!!!!! 2- book early 3- ware sea bands or take Dramamine because you will not have any lines to wait in, you can go ride to ride .  Perks : No lines anywhere !! Private guide Renee, gave us history, advise and the perfect seat to maximize our ride experience. She took us into private areas, security rooms , ride maintenance rooms and personal back hallway .  Amazing !!!  Ask for Renee !!  Daniel from CT

I love people...but this was crazy. Long lines...it made it hard to do anything. Harry Potter was a BUST...Did I miss something? The rides were ok. Again the workers wee great. They made the park fun!

We really like Universal Studios, but haven't been for a few years and wondered if it would still be good. The answer is yes, with the rides and experiences providing really entertaining days out. The new Harry Potter elements are generally great, as are the Transformers and Minions rides. Some rides are starting to become old and tired, like Men in Black and ET, but they are still fine. My family liked to Hogwarts Express between the parks, but I found it a let down. The views are electronically generated and there is no control over seating, so people just push to sit in the best seats. In fact, this was the only Universal ride where the staff appeared to be disinterested. Having said this, the park is still great overall and is a must do if visiting Orlando.

My family and I love adventurous and thrill seeking rides and Universal Islands of Adventure and Universal Studios DID NOT disappoint! Purchasing the expedited passes if you're able to is a must though. This park gets quite a bit of attention but well worth it. We had a GREAT time.

The theme parks at Universal Orlando has always new attractions to surprise us and the new park Volcano Bay is absolutely amazing. Just make sure you get there early to be able to get in. The tapu tapu is a great way to enjoy your day without wasting your time in lines but sometimes the system did not work properly and it is a lit bit frustrating but they do everything to resolve the issue asap. The rides are thrilling, the lazy river is very nice and the rapid river very fun. The food is good but I would like more variety and at lunch time the lines to buy food can get really crowded. The safety it excellent too. It is an incredible addition to universal. The kids love it, I can not wait to visit it again.
This side was so fun. More kid oriented, but just as fun for adults. Didn't get the "fast pass", but the lines weren't super long anyways. I think that they had better souvenir shops on this side.

Universal Studios is a fun time. We went 6 years ago, and I remember Harry Potter being included, now you need to buy a 2 park pass to enjoy it, which is not cheap. This place is fun, but way overpriced. I spend $40 for a ticket to Cedar Point in Ohio and it has 4 times as many rides. The nice part, all the lines are indoor, and out of the heat, and the rides are unique.
Great park for teens and tweens. Express pass is a must if you don't like standing in long lines. Worth every penny.

Awesome movie atmosphere and Soundtrack. Great end of night show. Good mix of rides. Moes Tavern. A Delorean! Animal show was amazing, make sure to catch it. Buildings look great, New York!!! Best roller-coaster, Ripitriderocker. Good mix for old n young, brave and not so. Some kids shows like Minions and Shrek long queues. 10/10

My 13 year old son and I traveled with a group of other families with teenagers. We were hoping that Universal was going to be a fun experience for older kids. The rides were great, especially Harry Potter rides and the Jimmy Fallon ride, but the service is just not as good as Disney. Universal requires you to pay for fast passes, there are very few photographers, and the attendants are just not as helpful or friendly. After one of the Harry Potter rides, my bar would not lift, so I was stuck. My friends tried to help me, and the attendant told us "Just stop and move!" Very rude, and ruined the fun experience we all just had. I really hope Universal invests in customer service training.

The park is amazing. So much fun had by all. We hadn't been in several years so we were pleased by all the new attractions. Particularly, anything to do with Harry Potter. We took the train, waited in line for 2 hours, yikes! Diagon Alley and Hogwarts were incredable. You truly felt like you walked into the book.The only problem we had were the crowds. I can honestly say that if someone needed help, example a heart attack they wouldn't make it. There is only one way in and out and that is a problem. We noticed several employees, that looked to be higher ups writing on their tablets with paniced looks on their faces. If we go again it will be during a different time of year.

Apparently Universal and Adventure Island were linked at some time? Our group was expecting rides and part of Harry Potter to be in Universal but were not. Plan carefully. I also would not go in summer .

Fun day but very hot and crowded. There seems to be quite a discrepancy between wait times listed on the universal app, and what is listed on the rides themselves. Diagonal Alley was great, wish it wasn't so crowded!
Go here every year, do the rides, the sims etc, this year we found some hidden gems, a climbing wall and the blues brothers, just behind Transformers ride, a real go see thing...

Universal is for older children. If you like 3D rides, they specialize in them. I enjoyed them and so did the kids. My wife did not like because of motion sickness. The Harry Potter attractions is what drives this park and it is crowded. Simpson's area is fun. We visited on a Friday beginning of June and rode everything, some multiple. Food was average. Crowds manageable. My family agreed it was better then Disney. To say the least we won't be going back anytime soon.
The attractions were fun and entertaining. As to expect,in the summer the lines take along time to move. However, the food wasn't that appetizing.

Best rides, great fast pass policy (not the 3 ride "fast pass" from Disney. High tech rides (not a 1971 ride as Disney). And finally the most friendly staff. Now with the Volcano Bay, it is a must see in Orlando!

First visit in 16 years and Universal and Island of Adventure are still must visit attractions. If you do go try and buy your ticket before hand, not only can you (sometimes) get a good deal at your hotel but it will also save you from having to queue before you even get in! Adult admission for one day, two parks was $179, parking was an additional $25. We made the mistake of buying there and not only had to wait 1hour 30mins but it is also an up-selling opportunity for multi park/day/fast pass tickets. The popular rides always having wait times of 1 hour + in peak season and I can see the attraction of fastpass however at $303 each for adults this was way too steep for us. Here's my tips for the parks 1) Do go to both Universal and Island of Adventure 2) If you are not fussed about sitting with family/friends and just want to get on all the good rides try the single rider queue. When we visited, single riders skipped right to the front to make up the lines and you didn't need to pay the fast pass rate. 3) Outside coasters close in bad weather and storms - if you visit in June - Sept go on these first thing in the morning before the afternoon storms. 3) The Wizarding World of Harry Potter is mostly indoor so this can be busy during the rain storms 4) Ride the Hogwarts Express between the parks - it's a nice little rest and if you do it both ways you get to see different things each time. 5) Do check the signs before you join the queue as to what type of ride it is - don't be fooled into thinking indoor coasters are less of an adrenaline rush. Revenge of the Mummy and Escape from Hogwarts was a bit of a surprise to me. That being said (unless you have a specific condition don't let the signs worry you!) 6) The rides have height restrictions for children but I didn't notice age restrictions so try and find out if it is suitable. Skull Island Reign of Kong was one of my favourite rides but the queue itself was through dark caves with an animatronic witch and ritualistic chanting (plus a few other surprises) quite a few children (and adults) found this scary. 7) Don't let the wait times put you off - the parks do a great job of keeping you entertained, distracted and cool whilst you wait. There are lockers to put bags in but try and leave bags at home. Wear comfy shoes and if possible have a pocket to put your sunglasses away whilst on the rides. 8) My favourite rides: Transformers - I love 3D rides, Skull Island reign of Kong, Spiderman, Escape from Gringotts (although it's really short), Revenge of the Mummy. Shrek 4D was also great fun for kids and Minions 3D was also really popular. 9) City Walk has some great restaurants and bars and makes a nice evening out

We decided to do the park 2 park passes so we could do the Harry Potter train ride. I highly recommend the P2P tickets. The rides at both parks are pretty good. Some rides are a little dated (eg, T2. E.T.) but I will say I went home and watched E.T. again. Our son really loves Back to the Future. The train and car from the movies made his day! The food at the Mythos restaurant was excellent! The only thing I would say is don't go in July!!
Great place ques are ok we found if we went after 18.00 hours parking is free and rides are easier get on

We went here and to Epcot, and thought this was a much better experience. There are many enjoyable rides, and the entire feel of the place is quite nice. It is expensive to get in, and they have the nerve to charge an extra $20.00 to park. Outragious. There is an area called City Walk that has many nice restaurants and they are more reasonable than in the Disney parks.

Universal Studios is a great theme park. The Wizarding World of Harry Potter is awesome! However, they are well aware that they have a captive audience and they don't mind making you pay for it. If you choose to save on hotel costs by staying off-site, a single day, park-to-park ticket can run upwards of $175 for an adult - without the Express Pass (essentially a shortcut in line for most rides). Park-to-Park tickets are the only way that you can ride the Hogwarts Express so that increases the cost. Staying at an on-site hotel can get very pricey (especially the hotels that include Express Pass), but you get into the parks an hour earlier than the general public and that can make a major difference in wait times for popular rides. We visited before they added Express Pass to the Harry Potter rides so I'm not sure how that will affect the wait times now. Adding the Express Pass to a regular ticket is SUPER expensive, and its worth is dependent upon time of year, how much you hate waiting in lines, and how many rides/attractions you want to do. Whether a visit to Universal Studios/Islands of Adventure is worth what it costs is definitely a matter of opinion. Everyone's idea of value is different. Overall, expect to pay a lot of money - for everything.

Hard to find activities for 4 young adult kids (age 17-28). They loved it! Expensive but they had a blast. Bought the 1 day park hopper and they were able to ride Every thing they wanted. Loved the Shrek show and train! Ate a big breakfast and then stopped for a meal around 4. Husband and I enjoyed the Portofino resort. Only wish the tx weren't so expensive.

Universal is a great family day with rides to suit all. Download the universal Orlando app and see wait times and where everything is. They have a small parade. Some good shows and nice food spots however are more pricey than normal but your in the parks just like the uk. Staff are friendly. Great atmosphere and when you go into diagon alley you get the Harry Potter feeling.
You must purchase tickets for both Universal Studios, Florida and Islands of Adventure to get the whole 'Harry Potter' experience! Do not hesitate, as both locations are worth the experience!

Really great day, Transformers ride one of our best in Orlando overall and 9 yo loved rock it rollercoaster. More rides than themed attractions compared to Disney. Citywalk is right outside with lots to do and places to eat. We bought fast passes but didn't really feel they were worth the money as queues were not too bad.
This the park to visit! Way better than the mouse! Do not miss the Minions ride! If you like roller coasters you will love Rip Ride Rockit and The Hulk! Don't miss this park!

WOW...Diagon Alley...Hogsmeade is cool, but Universal perfected it with Diagon Alley! It is like stepping into the movie! This is a must see for any Harry Potter fan!!! From the dragon that breathes fire, to the goblins in the bank, to Knockturn Alley...no detail was missed!  Everything is a must see...it truly is like stepping foot on the movie set! You can take your picture with the characters from Shrek, Spongebob, Back to the Future. Recommend having a doughnut in the Simpsons area!  If you are going to get the full Harry Potter experience, you must purchase park hopper ticket. Make sure to ride the train both ways from Universal to Islands of Adventure and then from Islands of Adventure back to Universal!

I can see Universal Studios becoming the new family destination of the future. Disney had become outdated and in need of serious attention to many details. We truly enjoyed the King Kong ride. The only things I would suggest are adding more rides, more places to sit and misting stations.

After spending a fortune at Disney, walking around in the heat, and riding boring rides, I spent a day at Universal Studios. Wow! The park is better designed and organized. The rides were vastly better, the lines were reasonable, and you can still get discounts in town if you are willing to spend 90 minutes in a time-share presentation. Go enjoy yourselves.
Visited in July was by far the best park not to big but everything in one spot there were lots to do and see lots of smoking spots about enjoyed the Christmas shop was really good

My wife has never been to a theme park. This was her first. We had a great time. Rode all of the rides and saw a few of the shows. For older people, it was like we were kids again. Her smile was worth the whole drive from Savannah. Time to go to the hotel and grab a quick rest before dinner tonight at Capone's.

We are expecting a baby and we thought what better idea than to bring our son (17) to Universal/Islands of Adventure as our last trip as a family of 3 and to spend some great family time together.  The park has lots to do and see, overall the staff was very friendly and you can tell they enjoy their job. The park was very clean and well kept. I usually am not in Orlando at this time of the year but it worked out perfect because the lines for the rides were short (15-25 min wait) and my husband and son were able to ride everything. Plenty of places for me to cool off and relax while I waited on them. I was well entertained too by the characters!  The food is ok, expensive but that was expected. The nice part about drinks is you can buy a souvenir cup ($15 for one) and enjoy free refills throughout the day, I would recommend doing this because buying a drink each time will run you about $4. Plenty of different options for food.  Shopping is good too, lots of souvenirs and places to look at. I used the stores as a frat place to cool down and have a little retail therapy.  We stayed at a connecting hotel (Sapphire Falls) so we did not have to worry about parking. Quick water taxi from the hotel and we were dropped off at City Walk. Great experience!

This was the best surprise ride of our trip. We were just trying to get through as many rides as possible with our fast passes when we decided to take a chance. It was awesome. If you are a fan of Fallon, you have seen him challenge guests to races of all sorts. This attraction combines that experience with popular New York City landmarks and takes the riders on a hilarious and high speed romp through The City. I will definitely take another turn on this one.
We loved universal. I went to Disney as well and would pick universal over it any day of the week. The rides here are wonderful.

Go to this park first as everyone tends to go to Islands of Adventure first. Some great rides here, if you've never been then make sure you go to this park as well. But don't really need to go again. Do not go on the Men In Black ride, don't waste your time designed for kids but even the kids getting off the ride were saying how boring it is! *take your own water bottle and get it refilled for free at the food stands, there are drinking fountains around the park as well*

Spent 4 days walking around all 3 parks, and this is the best by far. They have rides for all age groups. The flow thru the park is great and the lines were never too long. Most rides wait time was around 30mins, but it went by fast. Loved the way Harry Potter section was hidden just the way it would be in real life. Missed a few of the old rides like Jaws and Back to the Future, but the new ones were great.No idea why they still have Terminator and not Jaws or BTTF. The one draw back, is most of the rides are kind of the same thing. You sit in a car, with glasses and just go from one thing to the other. Transformers, Mummy, DM were all the same ride. But overall a great park.

We love to visit Universal Studios Florida, I recommend this park for families with teenagers or children over 10 years. I especially recommend attractions like RRR, Jimmy Fallon, the mummy, King Kong, etc., The world of Harry Potter is spectacular, full of details that true fans like me, will appreciate. Eating is expensive, so I recommend you make a super breakfast before entering the park, bring snacks and eat when you leave, because it is really expensive to eat at the park restaurants.

My kids and I have been to this park every year since they were 8 and 12 they love it all the rides are suited to them and characters as well. We don't have a big meal here anymore but have a light snack of hotdogs and nachos and eat elsewhere for our big meals. Love this park and as long as we come to Florida we will always visit this park.

What a great theme park this is couple together with Islands of Adventure and CityWalk it's unbelievable. I guess I'm a little partial since I've been a season pass member for over 18 years but that should say something as to why I keep going back. This park has something for everyone from roller coasters to small kids stuff. The team members go out of their way to make sure that you've had a great day and I would highly recommend this venue for everyone.

Very expensive for what you get. Is essentially an over priced strip mall with a few rides, which are not worth the waiting time, between expensive stores. Staff is unkind and in consistent. We were told different information by different employees. The entrance scans your finger print which is in settling. We were told we may not sit in chairs while we wait for a ride that you had to wait in two separate lines to ride. Would not recommend.
Young or old this place has something for everyone. If you can imagine a older adult, a child, and a kid enjoying the time of their lives....Its at this place.

We normally go to Florida in May when it is quieter but this year we went in July, big mistake. We went to Universal Studios early in the morning and by 5pm we had only been on 4 rides. The airport security before entry set the tone when they bottleneck everyone in a small space to go through metal detectors and have your bags scanned, there was no distinguishable queues so just a mass of people standing about and edging forward every once a minute, they have the queuing system for the rides down so this mayhem is just so lazy and frustrating. Once we were in, the queues were too long which was made worse due to the regular queues being held back to allow express pass holders to go through, Disney allow 3 fast passes per customer and do not charge extra to get to the front which is fair but the way Universal exploit customers with greedy "We want more money" is unacceptable. I could understand if they gave out free tickets and we had to wait for the people that pay to go on first but the tickets are expensive enough that we should not be shook down on out way in for more money. The rides kept breaking down meaning the queues for the express pass holders grew longer than the regular queue leaving the regular one standing for long periods. With all that being said Universal still does have the better rides in Orlando but it is just far too busy in July which is a shame.

There are two theme parks under the umbrella of Universal. The Studios side is more of an experience theme park with a lot of rides relying on visual effects and simulators, and 3D, sometimes 4D. This can make you feel a little odd after a while. My favourite was the Shrek ride. If you can afford an Express pass it's worth it but not vital if you have multiple days. If you only have one day then do get the Express pass.

We loved the park and the area. the express pass makes all the difference and is worth the extra cost. The Harry Potter area is fun and the food in the park is actually pretty decent which is unusual.

We took our family to Orlando for Christmas. Some of the older kids wanted to go to Universal. We paid the inflated fee for both sides of the park so they could see all of Harry Potter. That is all we got to see. There was no way we could get on any rides as the wait lines were hours. Don't go there. At least at Disney you can get a fast pass to see your favorite picks and not have to pay extra like at Universal.

This was my first time staying at Universal Studios of Orlando. Their theme parks and water park are great. The people working in the parks are helpful. But when it comes to customer service when making reservations and getting help within the Caban Bay hotel you're on your own. Im used to Disney World, which is the gold standard of customer service. When I decided to buy the food plan at Universal, I was told very different and conflicting stories every time I called. Upon arriving I found out, unlike Disney, there is no way to link your meal plan to your room card. So now you have to carry around a dinner card for each member of your party. Not at all handy. When going to Volcano Bay, there is a nonstop ad on the TV in your room advertising their "bracelet" called Taputapu. Just link your credit card to the bracelet and go. No need to carry a credit card. Wrong! What they don't tell you is, the bracelet lets you charge everything via the Taputapu bracelet, except the lockers you need to rent. Also there is no way to link your dining plan to the Taputapu bracelet. So now you have to take your credit card and all your dining cards to the water park. Not at all user friendly. The front desk at the hotel is strictly for check in. If you have any other questions they send you to the desk that helps you buy tickets to attractions. The attraction desk is not equipped to answer all if your questions. No one in the hotel understands the dining plans. You have to rely on the restaurants to be able to explain the plan to you. Although I had a GREAT time at the parks, I will not be coming back to stay at Universal Studios in Orlando. Disney is cheaper and provides MUCH better customer service.

This is our second trip to Universal Studios Florida and my kids chose Universal since they have pretty much outgrown Disney. We purchased annual passes because the cost wasn't much more than a 3 day park to park ticket and we can return as many times as we want in a year for basically nothing. The pass also allows early admission, discount on hotels, food, merchandise and free parking. Harry Potter is of course amazing and everything a fan would hope for. We did Gringotts first thing during early admission and got right on no wait and then walked around Diagon Alley until the park opened. We followed a comprehensive tour plan from a popular travel guide that was for 2 days and 2 parks and were able to do everything we wanted. It's a ton of walking. Next time we would go early and then leave when it got hot and crowded in the afternoon and return in the evening. In July, the park is open until 10pm so you can get a lot done if you have the endurance. This trip my kids actually had seen most of the movies from the rides so they really enjoyed it. Springfield with the Simpsons is their favorite since they watch the series all the time they loved the experience. My son and I tend to have motion sickness so we took some Bonine in the morning before coming just to make sure. The Simpsons is a tough ride for those with motion sickness. Mummy is still one of my favorites. The lines for Despicable Me are crazy long so download the app and monitor the wait times. We did it early and it was one of the early admission attractions. ET is old and dated but it was fun to ride and then experience Kong the new ride in the other park and see how far we've come with what we can do with attractions. The food places close early at 8 so eat early or wait until the park closes and International Drive has any restaurant you can imagine much cheaper. In Diagon Alley look for the entrance to Knockturn Alley, it's easy to miss and also look for the house elf in the window of 12 Grimmauld Place.

For me personally I feel the Universal is not worth the money we paid . If you purchase an express pass it can bring the cost of one day to over 400 dollars. And then if you wish to go to the or parks that's more money !!! And then on top it's 20 dollars to park !!! We did enjoy our day and some of the rides are fun . You do need a day to see it all. One thing in their favour was food is reasonably priced.

Visited in Aug 2015 and this was our favourite of parks because of the Minions of course. Our son was 7 at the time and we took advantage of the pre booking system for the rides he would go on due to his ASD. Autism friendly and aware which was great for us.  Food was a lot more varied but very busy and prices were higher due to it being a theme park. We visited a few times as the park is so big and the best part was the parade with of course lots of minions. Parking was easy and charges less than Disney.  We bought a refillable drink cup with lots of dispensers in the restaurants with various sodas to choose from and lots of free ice as you walked around.  Our son wants to go back to see the Minions now despicable me 3 is out!! We loved it here!! 💛💛💛💛
The park is awesome with favourite rides being The Mummy, transformers, simpsons, Hollywood rip ride rocket and minions! Get here early to avoid the queues on the minions rides!

We've been here many times, but it's the first time we've be on the Jimmy Fallon ride. It is now only of my favourite rides, along with the mummy. There's loads to go here so be prepared for a busy day.

We spent three days at Universal--1day in Volcano Bay and 2 in the other parks. The important things to know about Volcano Bay is to be out at the bus around 7am if you are on property. This will make sure you are able to get in. They let us in about 7:45am. I am not much for water slides so I spent a lot of time in the Lazy River in an inner tube. There is also the Fearless River that I didn't know about. The grandson loved the body plunge (Ko'okiri) most of all. They did almost all of the slides and had a great time there. Our favorites in the other two parks were the Spiderman Ride, the Transformers, King Kong, Jurassic Water Adventure (sit in the middle of the car to keep from getting really wet), Hogwarts Express. In the Harry Potter Land, the Gringotts Money Exchange has a large dragon on it that shots out fire randomly. You can hear the dragon growling before he "fires-up" and you can see a pilot light in his mouth come on. This gives you enough time to start taping. Of all things we did that was helpful, was to purchase a Fast Pass. That saved us so much time waiting outside in the hot July sun and cut our wait time in half. Our grandson wanted to eat at the Crusty Burger (The Simpson's restaurant) and that was our biggest mistake. That was the most horrible food I have almost ever eaten. We most enjoyed going to Blue Man in City Walk. Getting a seat close enough to see their eyes is important and we sat a couple of rows behind the "Poncho Section" (must wear ponchos so you don't get wet). This was perfect. Get reservations as far in advance as you can. Be sure to use the bathroom before going into the auditorium as there is NO break and the show about 90 minutes long. Get there early (if you must pick up your tickets) as it is always a sold out audience. Stick around after the show and get free pictures with one of the Blue Men.

Universal Orlando awesome!!! Grown ups playground, great rides and attractions. Harry Potter just amazing Forbidden Journey a must but beware if you suffer from motion sickness you need a strong stomach to ride this one! Escape from Gringotts just magical just makes you smile so lovely. Best coasters are Hulk, quite gentle compared to Dragon challenge which we were told is closing in September for refurb. Hogsmead and Diagon Alley magical. Make sure you get park to park tickets as Hogwarts express a real treat. Also revenge of the Mummy just great with lots of surprises! Spider-Man and Transformers great but again watch out if you have motion sickness!!! Buy rain ponchos BEFORE you go in. Chances are you will need one and they cost $10 dollars each!!! $2 from Walmart so save yourself a few quid. The refillable drinks deal is worth taking up. One final word of warning, if you don't like getting wet avoid Popeyes's river rapids, you might as well jump in the lake you get that wet!! Great fun but even in Florida sunshine you will be soaked for the rest of the day!!!
If you go to Universal you must go to Island of Adventures and travel between parks using Hogwarts train.
You have to visit at least once especially if you have children.You connect so much with your kids because everyone in the park becomes 10 yrs old.It's fun and must go family vacation.

The rides are geared more toward thrill seakers. You will get soaked on the water rides and taken to a new level at Twister. If course Harry Potter is raging and I loved every minute. Dr Suess and Minions! Ready set go !

Best part of Orlando . Loved Harry Potter World. Had an excellent time. The mummy,Jimmy Fallon and spider man were a blast. Enjoyed show at park closing and the parade A great time for young and old. If you can stay at a Universal hotel it is well worth it to get the fast pass. Saved a ton of waiting time.

Universal is fabulous and great fun for all the family. The rides were amazing!!! Very busy in July and long waits to get in the rides some over an hour. Lots of choice for food and drink in the park.

For the 3 parks that Universal offers here, this one is at the bottom - but it's still good. The Harry Potter stuff is very well done if you're a fan. The only coaster in this park is decent, but nothing amazing. The ready are 3D and simulated rides. Just "meh" for me - but to each his/ her own. The food in the park is really quite good. If you can swing it, get the Express Pass - HUGE difference, but it can be more than the admission ticket for the day. Paid for the premium parking ($10 more) but unless you're driving in and out, don't bother - really not worth the ten bucks.

Loved loved loved it! We had the park hopper which allowed us two days at both parks. Although Island's Adventure has the more exciting rides, but Universal Studios was just as much fun! Jimmy Fallon's Race through NY was a lot of fun, as was the Terminator show. MIB was fun and competitive :) Harry Potter is hands-down amazing. There is a dragon in the park that blows out fire every ten minutes, it's a definite experience. We had lunch at Monster's Cafe, which is a fun place to eat. We did several meet & greets and got to take pictures with our favorite characters. The Transformers ride is also amazing. There is A LOT of hype on the Minions ride, honestly if you don't do it you aren't missing a lot. We waited almost an hour in line at the very end of the day, and wished we hadn't. It's a 3D simulator as are many rides in this park and it just wasn't worth the wait. So if you don't do it, you aren't missing much. Everything was amazing and I would definitely go back!
Universal never fails to satisfy. There are rides for all tastes and ages especially if you are into high tech virtual reality 3D experiences.

So the last time I went to Universal Studios Orlando was when I was 10. I am now 30+ and took my 9 year old son for his birthday to the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. A couple of things I will mention - 1) The website is kind of confusing but I enjoyed having our tickets ahead of time. 2) The VIP semi-private tour is absolutely worth the money IMO. 3) The valet parking gets busy at the end of the night so expect to wait. Both my son and I had an amazing time while we were there. It rained on our second day, but that just meant there were less people to fight and lower wait times. The park has so many options and there is so much to do that it's hard to fit it all in. I still feel like I could go back and experience things that I didn't this time. If you have the time I would definitely recommend going. Oh, and next time I will get the hotel package that lets you in an hour early and is easy to get to/from the park so we could have gone back and rested then headed out again. Live and learn.

It was so hot ever time i went back outside it felt like I was walking into a dragons mouth. I would suggest more fans and more misters.  The express is a must.  We thought there were too many 3D/4d rides. We all were getting motion sick by the end of the day. The first ride we went on was the minions and we had to wait until the next ride because the seats we were slotted for were vomited on right before we were supposed to enter.  I thought food prices were reasonable.

We have been to universal whilst on holiday 6 times now and this is the first time on the revenge of the mummy ride it's definitely a hidden gem and so good we rode it 3 times The something new is ride through new York with jimmy fallon which is really good fun even though we don't really watch jimmy fallon in the uk Universal is my favourite place on earth with so much to do one day just isn't enough time so we spent 4 days between here and islands of adventure

Last visited in August 2014 and thought it was ok then. When you compare this to Islands of Adventure there is no comparison . Universal has a few food rides such as Harry Potter and The Mummy but the place needs updating . Rides such as ET and Shrek need getting rid or and replacing !  The parade was poor and lacked any imagination. If you have a choice head to Islands of Adventure!!

Firstly if you have young kids from 2 upwards take swim wear for wet play at Curious George. It's a great place to cool off and parents have a break. Secondly if you have older teenagers and don't get Express passes then go into the rides as single riders. Within 10mins you're in and out! Minions ride is the longest wait so I would get into the park as it opens and head straight for it. Get that done and the others you can do through the day. Top rides we did were, Minions, Transformers, Mummy, Gringotts and we did a few kiddies ones like Woody woodpecker. Buy two refillable cups for the day and you can fill up at refill stations and various kiosks. $13 each cup but you can refill all day! There were 7 of us and we shared Diet Coke and Sprite. Take a rain poncho with you as afternoons can have rainfall even though it's baking hot. Factor 50 for very young children and factor 30 for everyone else. You will burn in August.  Buy your souvenirs at the end of the day so you don't end up carrying loads around with you. Harry Potter zone is really good and has live performers. It's where the Grongotts rise is. Loads of weird shops and of course Olivanders wand shop. $40 for a standard wand. The ice cream shop sells nice ice cream! Photo opportunities at the Night Bus! The parade is at 7pm so if you plan the minions ride later get on the right side of the road around 6:30 then while the parade is on queue for Minions as you may save some waiting time. We didn't do rip ride rocket that's for roller junkies!! Great day overall but it does close at 9pm. We had a 4 year old granddaughter with us but you do need a stroller for young ones and to carry your stuff and bags. We brought our own stiller from the uk and took the hood for shading from the sun. That was a good move. Make sure you write your names on the backs of your tickets as they associate you with your finger print at the entrance. Lastly you can take your own sandwiches, crisps, biscuits etc into the park. We ate ours while waiting to watch a live stage show. Always fill up your refill cups when you pass a refill kiosk. The cups are chipped so can only be used for that day. Keep the receipt in case you lose a cup. It's generally hot for everyone, for parents chill and enjoy and work together. Have sit down breaks. For parents with teenagers you can let them go and arrange to meet up at a set time. They can do single riders and fill their boots!

universal studios great place to visit has everything you can want in a park you from adventure to thrilling rides to the the greatest shows and actors on the streets you even have acapella groups singing in the streets if not bands playing good music for your entertainment. Got to love the minnions also cant forget about the transformers, there is so much to see and do at this park that it will have you busy for quite a while. very hospitable workers who help you for what ever you need. great place to enjoy and visit . No matter what age everyone will enjoy the visit to universal studios.!!

Me and my brothers absolutely love Universal Studios. So many rides and different things to see. What makes this park stand out from most other theme parks is the lack of outdoor attractions. The only big outdoor attraction is Hollywoood Rip Ride Roket. So this means even when storms are around, many attractions remain open. The simulator rides, particularly Krustyland's Simpsons Ride, Despicable Me Minion Mayhem and Transformers The Ride 3D are phenomenal and are firm favourites of mine.  For families wanting to compete in a competition, Men in Black Alien Attack is just for you. Keen Harry Potter fans will really want to go on Harry Potter and the Escape from Gringott's Bank.  It's not all thrill rides though, the kids would really like Woddy Woodpecker land and Barney. The ET ride is one to cool off and all the family.  Overall, I'd highly recommend Universal Studios to all theme park lovers. I would also recommend going if you know storms will come because only 1 attraction will close in storms. All the rest will remain open.

Visited both parks. Got there at opening and left at closing. All excellent. Rides were superb, no need for express pass. Lines were bearable. Had lunch at the Harry Potter restaurant and was excellent. Portions were huge. Great experience, awesome staff.

Well where to start! There is shrek, transformers, ET, Simpsons, Sponge Bob, men in black, Harry Potter to name but a few. The ET ride was my favorite. the children are well catered for. The San Francisco & New York sets are out of this world. A must to see is the Wizzarding World of Harry Potter and go on the Hogwarts Express which takes you to the islands of adventure. Great shops and places to eat. The drinks package is a must and very good value for money. Characters come out and about in the Beverley Hills area for example: Scooby Doo, Sponge bob, Marilyn Monroe & Betty Boo. Also action scene's are carried out giving entertainment.

I love the thrill of the rides at Universal. Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey is a truly realistic broom-flying experience! Not much a fan of roller coasters, I really enjoyed all of the simulation rides. Just as much fun and excitement! The entire Harry Potter world is breathtaking and with the smaller patrons roaming around with their capes and wands casting spells, it feels like you are really in Diagon Alley. The shops are great, selling chocolate frogs and all flavor gumdrops as well as wands and all the Gryffindor, etc garb. Compared to the other well known attraction in Orlando, our family will choose Universal every time. It is much more in line with the times and interests of this generation.

We have been to ALL the disney parks and wanted to try something new. Universal is very cool. The say we went wasnt' tho, haha, so hot. This has great rides (you MUST do the mummy ride). The Shrek one was awesome too. The lines are not too bad, better than disney. The photo opportunity with the characters is great and worth doing. Our favorite photo was with "Donkey and Shrek" (such a funny donkey!). We will go again. It's kinda pricey but well worth a day trip.
had a great time at universal as we had early entry to the parks so loved every min of it ,it did get very busy thou thats for sure
What can you say!? There is so much to see that you must take time to spend as long as possible on a visit. Dont' hurry and miss out.

Their are many great rides here, but Rock-It lets you select your own music and it syncs with the ride. I love rollercoasters and had never been on one that lets you play your own music, to enhance the ride. look up your song before you get on, and Rock it. I recommend 'Sabotage' by the Beastie Boys if you like that sort of thing.

We hit this park on the same day as visiting islands of adventure... We were worn out by hometime. The Studios are a little more sedate and slower paced than islands in my opinion. But still there are lots of thrilling rides to try!! The attractions are more theatre based things though. Lots of 3D glasses wearing and the likes. A few coasters can be found though saying that. Certainly a place that's worth a visit.... Can't wait for next time.

We finally went to Universal after putting it off year after year to go somewhere else. Why did we wait so long! This was the best vacation ever. We stayed at Loews Royal Pacific Resort and got the free fast passes which was well worth it. We got the park to park tickets with a meal plan and unlimited drinks which was well worth it in the 97 degree heat. We are already planning our trip to come back next year!

Chris was a great worker, my friend and I did the doom ride consistently and loved talking with Chris. He told he has another job but prefers working at Universal because it brings him joy. Great and friendly guy who made my day.
Buy the skip the line pass or get the VIP. It's not cheap, but It'll make the experience so much better and you'll get to see all the major attractions in one day.
I had a great time at Universal Studios with friends. It's a great tourist attraction with food, drinks, rides, shows and more....

We only had a day at Universal and so had to choose our park. We went for Universal Studios - not being 100% clear that the park is in fact split in to 3 parts. We went early and tried to do as many rides as possible early on. They quickly went up to 40mins+ waiting time. Minions was at 90 mins at 9am! Transformers was great and then we headed to the far side of the park quickly. Worth doing this. We then left at mid day for the hotel and came back at 7pm...we got two more rides in and there are lots of restaurants near by, so a good way of managing a day at a park.

Visited a couple of days ago and had such a great time hopping between the 2 parks. Ate at Richter burger - honestly wasn't expecting them to have a veggie option but they did a really nice bean burger with fries and a shake. Noticed quite a few of the food places had decent veggie options too, I was impressed. The only thing I would say that's slightly negative is they don't have a Disney style fastpass - you have to pay extra for this. But the rides are really good here, we loved The Mummy

This park was amazing! Could spend all day here, would definitely recommend the Transformers ride and Rip Ride Rocket. Great rides for both children and adults. The 4D simulator rides are incredible and give you an experience like no other.

This was the first day visit of our 2 week vacation. We are staying on resort so can enjoy the perks of early park entry and universal express. The early park entry was a disappointment (hence why 4 stars and not 5). Early park entry was advertised for select rides at each park. However we turned up at universal studios to be told that entry was for islands of adventure only. By the time we reached islands, it was already quite busy. Early park access was restricted to the Harry Potter area only, which again made the area very busy already at around 8.10. This really made the early park perk pointless. That all being said, we spent some time at islands until the studios, then hopped on the hogwarts train (fantastic ride) to universal studios. As we are travelling with a two and a half year old, a lot of our time is spent just soaking up the atmosphere, which is great. We spent a while at diagon alley and the London waterfront. Our boy loved the knight bus, and we enjoyed taking in all the details. I hopped on the gringotts ride, a fantastic rollercoaster/screen based ride, universal express was well worthwhile here. Only criticism was the dragon that sits above diagon alley is very loud and unavoidably intense. He roars and breathes fire every ten minutes, which caught my boy by surprise and really upset him. After leaving diagon alley we headed through the simpsons area and spent a few hours in the kids zone. The kid's area is a bit tired looking but still fun (rumoured to be replaced by Nintendo land in the future). Overall a fab few hours at the studios. Will be back for more soon

Visited the three parks with teenage sons/older children. The two teenagers loved the parks especially the extreme rides. The 3D simulator rides are fantastic especially the two Harry Potter rides/Spider-Man/Kong/transformers/minions and Simpsons ride. The islands of adventure is slightly smaller and easily managed in a day but Universal Studios will require a fast pass to complete fully in a day. The train ride in the Hogwarts Express is a must both ways. Volcano bay is the newest park and offers a great range of rides/flumes for all ages.
go early and beat the crowds and don't use the fast pass system its expensive and not much quicker. Use a shuttle bus or taxi and you will save a lot of time

Do yourself a favor and stay on property if you can to get the unlimited express passes. It made the experience a million times better. My son and I rode everything as many times as we wanted without having to worry about the lines.

Haven't been there in years, took my 5 year old for his first time. Once you get past the ridiculous entry fee and high prices for EVERYTHING, it is easy to have a good time. Long lines from 30 - 120 minutes, depending on the ride (we didn't have the express pass). My group and I all found the Rock'n'roll roller coaster too harsh and violent, not a good time. All other rides were cool, lots of fun. Takes a whole day to experience the entire park. Be prepared to walk a lot!

My daughter had been looking forward to our Florida holiday for a year and we asked her, where would you like to go when we are there?
