Of course, you can't go to Florida without going to a theme park. So she picked Universal and I thought "well you can't go wrong with that"  Let's begin.....  You start off with being offered 2 prices for parking. $20 for everyday I would of said or $30 for what would be nearer to the park. We should the expensive one. It is a walk away from the park, quite a walk away so for anyone picking the cheaper price I suggest you buy very comfortable shoes and limber up for months before you travel.  My husband bought 3 tickets, for him, me and our daughter. The queue for tickets was actually ok but the price was a joke. 2 parks for 1 day for 3 people is £600 + and we wanted the expressed ones as I can't stand for too long as I have a fractured knee and back problem. Thought getting the expressed tickets would save us alot of time in queues.  My daughter and husband went on some rides as I watched the Blues Brothers and Marilyn Monroe go round in their cars. I enjoyed that and took some lovely photos.  We took drinks in with us and this is a MUST for anyone on goes to Universal. I saw Hello Kitty, or should I say someone in a costume with a park official going around with them. There was also a group of people clearly doing a VIP trip. Park officials with them, carrying bags on pushy trolleys and having photos with the minions. What I didn't expect as I sat on a wall and witnessed was a young mum who wanted her daughter to have her photo with a minion and then being TD by official staff that no photos could be taken and that she should stand away from where they are. I couldn't believe it, because a group of people who clearly have more money than sense paid more for their tickets they and them alone are the only worthy people of getting photos with the characters. The mum was not happy and the little girl was crying.  My husband and daughter started off on the Shrek ride and then the minion ride. Both weren't traditional rides but sit down cinema like journeys where the seats moved. Daughter liked it, husband thought it Shrek was boring but minion was good.  What makes you wonder in this theme park are the things you don't see unless you look for them. There are a splattering of rides and alot of no nothing parts to this park. Done superbly but still no nothing. A New York part, a LA part that kind of thing, you get the idea. What they are are sets where you think things are but aren't. Dummy shops, fabulous in their looks and great photos to be taken but a substantial part of a walkway before you get to eating places which are more than expensive.  We went into a burger restaurant, ordered 3 "big ones" and a drink to go with it. Had to queue for a while to be served then another queue to pick up the item. No sauces or ketchups were offered and I couldn't even see one of those stations with napkins etc either. I put my cup underneath for a drink and there was a lot of drinks on offer so the choice was quite extensive. It was over 100 degrees the day we went and with very few places in the shade you need to be hydrated. The price of 3 burgers and a drink was over 40 dollars and the drink wasn't even refillable. Now that is a joke!  Going through the park there are some great eye catchers but my daughter wanted to see Harry Potter and we all excited to go on the Hogwarts express train. Finally, getting to the front of the queue and we got our tickets out. Only 2 of our tickets were expressed and my one wasn't. I was told there was a 20 minute wait for the other queue and told my husband "you 2 go and meet me back here when your finished" but Shania who worked there was lovely enough to see me go through as a family. The train did not disappoint and was a highlight for Universal. Clearly done and lots to see the journey from 1 park to another was great. I unfortunately couldn't and didn't go on anything as my ticket wasn't expressed and I can't wait in a queue as some rides were over 75 minutes to wait for. I sat and watched my daughter enjoy herself and that was the focus of all of this. Afterwards we go back on the Hogwarts express train and back to the original park after their enjoyment. I sat on yet another wall watching the attractions around me whilst my family went on The Simpsons rides and after being fleeced for 5 dollars for a bottle of water my daughter had a slushy drink for another 5 dollars. Over 50 dollars on food and drink, well a steamrollered burger and drinks shared amongst 3 of us was quite excessive at over 50 dollars.  10 and a half hours later my back is unbearable and we started to make our way back to the car. My husband wanted to talk to someone at customer services or what they call "guest services" but this is right at the front of where you come in so if your grievance is further in the park you'll have further to go to simply talk to someone  The young girl at the desk seemed a little unsure of our circumstances and went to talk to a supervisor 4 times before the supervisor finally came out to talk to us.  We told her we bought 3 tickets and only 2 of them were expressed. I couldn't go on any rides because they refused me entry in the expressed lanes even though my husband and daughter had their passes. I got on the Hogwarts train ONLY because of the niceness of Shania and was then told " sorry we won't refund you your ticket because everyone has to pay something to get into the park" yes they do. To simply walk through their turnstiles it's $140, can you believe that. We were told by this supervisor that I should of got a wheelchair if I wasn't able to stand. I can stand, I am not disabled but then again no one told us about the wheelchairs either. After a long and lengthy battle she offered me 3 expressed park tickets for another day even though I told her over and over and over again I was going home in a couple of days and I couldn't come back again. I was then offered $100 gift card for a dinner so I could have time with my family. Told her I didn't come to Universal for a dinner and then she offered us to refund the expressed parts of the other 2 tickets which was over £200.  She then gave me my original ticket back plus 2 ordinary tickets for my daughter and husband and told us "you have 3 tickets now if you want to go back into the park"  Does anyone at Universal listen? Other good people complaining it's a joke. Universal make millions of dollars everyday and they don't listen to what the very people who make them billionaires say to them  Our experience was a joke and I wouldn't go back again  Overpriced over hyped day out that costs a fortune and no one listens to you. That sentence alone sums up our experience of the day

We visited as a couple on Saturday. The park was crowded but the lines weren't too bad. The Harry Potter section is great and the ride was cool too. My recommendations are The Men in Black Alien ride, Simpsons ride, the Rocket Coaster, Jimmy Fallon race through New York, Transformers and my favorite the Mummy Returns Coaster. I would have given this 5 stars but we had an issue with a security guard when we left. I asked a cast member where the nearest bathroom was. He said it was outside to the left of the entrance. My spouse exited the park to go to the bathroom while I refilled the souvenir cup before we left. I then exited the park. My spouse told me the bathrooms were locked. He tried to get back into the park where the nearest bathroom was. You can clearly see it from the exit. The security guard, William got extremely rude and hostile with him saying and pointing his finger, "You're not getting back into the park." We weren't mad at the fact that he couldn't get back in, but at his nasty attitude. The cast member shouldn't have told us the nearest bathroom was all the way out there when there was one clearly by the exit. It seems as soon as you exit, and they have your money, you don't matter anymore. We had to go over by the Blue Man group theater to use the bathroom. They also shouldn't have locked those bathrooms so early. I'm sure the guard wouldn't like that if someone did that to one of his children. Everyone else at the park was great but unfortunately one bad apple spoils the whole bunch.

My favorite park. I went during a horror night event. I would suggest people to buy Universal Studio and Islands of Adventure for 2 days. Or buy 1 day with express pass. The lines gets really long and hot, so it's a good idea to do that.  MUST DO - HARRY POTTER WORLD! Eat at Mythos at Islands of Adventure.

Was very disappointed for the amount of money the tickets cost for a family of four. They have some new construction building new things somethings were close down and other things are just not there anymore

My 1st trip to Universal and it will be my last. This place has no atmosphere and I feel like I spent a lot of money for nothing. Of course Im comparing this to Disney. I've been to Disney probably 22 or 23 different times. Disney is far more organized and less chaotic.You get a lot more for the same amount of money. We had to wait 40 minutes to get our tickets at the entrance and they only had half of the ticket booths open. Some places in the park the workers awere rude to the ghast. Not to me personally, but I saw them snapping and other guest telling them to hurry up and get on rides without smiling or anything. Maybe I'm just spoiled but that is not the way it is at Disney. Of course you are periodically going to run into rude people everywhere you go, but here it seems like it's quite common. And this is just from one day at the park.
I love it here I am a annual passholder! I'm always coming here with friends for fun! No matter how many times I visit I'm never bored there is always something to do. Best ride is the Mummy!

So we liked Universal Studios but like Islands of Adventure there were too many simulators! Our favorite rife was The Mummy!!! It was not a simulator but an indoor roller coaster!! Our next favorite was Men in Black where you got to shoot aliens. The guns could use some work but overall a great ride. The Simpsons, Terminator, Jimmy Fallon, and many others were simulators. Make more real rides!!!
This is one of two parks that caters for everyone loved Hogwarts and all the rides. We keep on returning, five times now!!!

You can see all the hard work gone into the universal parks! We watched a horror make up show with the kids where they showed how some of the make up is done. This was only 20 minutes long and they do ask for a volunteer! We also all went in the shriek 4d together, this was good as a group activity. The minion 4 d ride was alway queuing there was never a point it was not queuing even at night time! Kids went on a few roller coasters and I even managed to go on the men in black ride. Which for none riders is on a straight track where you shoot aliens and the cart spins a couple times. Diagon alley was amazing and so realistic we were really impressed by this area. There also a train that goes between the two parks to each part of Harry Potter. There is also butter beer you can purchase the foam on top is super sweet but the liquid under the foam is nice.  We even came to the park later in the day and stayed till nearly closing which was amazing seeing the park with all the lights on and temperature a little cooler too.  Parking is $30 for prime or $20 for normal. It is a long walk from the multi storey car park to the security building then you have to walk through city walks before getting to the parks. I think the parking is expensive when you don't have any other parking choices. Volcano Bay is standard $20 to park.

This was a fun park, with smaller lines and bigger rides then Disney. If you go on a week day, you can do both universal studios and Island in one day. On a weekend, you'll have much bigger lines and probably need 2 days. Although if you're not ready to march 7-10miles you should probably break it into 2 days. Also get the refill drink cup because it's better than paying for multiple drinks to survive yet still being thirty. You can get a huge selection of drinks whenever you want.

We loved universal because of the rides! The cleanliness and friendliness of employees was not as good, but overall we had a great experience! Harry Potter is without a doubt the best part, but the whole park is very fun, even if you do feel like you are being "nickel and dimed" to death (good luck with the refillable cups!).

We thoroughly enjoyed our trip to Universal Studios. Harry Potter is done really well. We purchased an interactive wand and even though it was expensive it was worth it. The themed drinks are also worth trying. We also enjoyed the rest of the park but the rides are not kind to the motion sensitive as there are a lot of simulator rides

My child is a huge Harry Potter fan so a trip to both the Universal Studios and Island of Adventure is a must. This is a must place to visit for Potterheads. We were here for two days because we wanted to make sure we have enough time cover every inch of the Harry Potter World. We were able to do that and have enough time left to visit other great attractions in the parks such as King Kong and Jurassic Park.  We only cared about the Harry Potter world though to be honest. If we had to do it all over again, I would get an Express Pass, and do all the Harry Potter stuff in one day instead.

Went to Universal with my sister, we had a brilliant time, Lots to see and do. Harry Potter was amazing and then of course The simpsons, Jurassic Park, so many to mention. We had a wonderful time except it was really hot at the time but we got there.
We enjoyed walking around the park and checking out all the rides, everyone was very nice, and we had so much fun! Would love to return someday and bring our kids.

A gpod/great day out, the park attention to detail is amazing. Walking around some of the city replicas it's hard to remember the buildings aren't real. Springfield is mind blowing for the work they've put into it. Most of the rides are simulators, alot 3D. By the end of the day they are all getting a bit samey. The Rip Rocket is the only real ride in the place. They're good but there's just too many of similar rides. The customer service is ok but in the 4 days we were there only had a few staff were who were warm and pleasant. Quite a few made you feel as they were doing you a favour. I felt prices were a bit steep, I noticed a difference after Disney. Quite a lot of the time I felt as I was getting ripped off. $20 to park!!!!!! And there's still a huge walk to get in. If you finish your day at the back of the park it's a 45mins walk to the car. At least in Disney there are trams, monorails, parking staff & roads built to help you out... that's why THEY charge $20. Its chaos getting out of this place, no help at all and you have to fight onto IDrive! Universal is just greedy.  Would have been 3 stars, felt robbed & abandoned but Springfield won a star back.

The prices are higher than Disney to enter in and there are two parks; I think the price for both parks is $300. The lines are long and most of the rides are VR based--you sit and watch a screen. While the waiting areas for the lines are immersive and really set the stage, sometimes the rides leave you feeling a bit nauseated while watching the screen with a moving chair.

Never been to a theme park before, and not into this sort of thing (sad academic type), but not disappointed! (trip was really for my 11-year old daughter and wife).  Spent 3 exhausting days in Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure, 1 day in Volcano Bay water park.  70% of time was spent in Wizarding World. I'm a historian and have lived in England in the types of towns and buildings reproduced here: the whole thing is a fake version of this reality, but fascinatingly so. Not into Harry Potter either, but the place is still engrossing.  Escape from Gringots: sort of roller-coaster ride that throws you about a bit and stops at various big 3D projection screens to dazzle you with various Harry Potter related stuff. Mostly digital, CGI. Bit lame. Not always the real Harry Potter actors. Only lasts about three minutes. The queue however is excellent, as it goes through a very interesting recreation of Gringots bank (Coutts like). We got there before 10am in last week of August, and didn't really have to queue for any time.  Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey: better than escape from Gringots. Roller coaster again - type with your legs hanging. Same idea, but less digital and more animatronics jumping out at you. Again, bit lame, and only lasts about 3 minutes. Queue again is excellent though, as you go through amazing recreation of rooms inside Hogwarts, with animated portraits etc.  Flight of the Hippogriff: just a rollercoaster. Lasts about 2 minutes. Supposed to be for children but still pretty violent.  Dragon Challenge: big big rollercoaster. Got nothing to do with Harry Potter really. Turns you upside down a bit. Quite worried this would kill me. Felt a bit concussed afterwards. But just about survivable for the sake of the kids.  Hogwarts Express: fake GWR locomotive (4-6-0). Coach compartments very convincing, but the upholstery doesn't smell right for GWR. View from the window quite interesting. Includes Regents Canal locks.  Hogsmead and Wizarding World: fascinating. Do all the spells. Wands cost an astonishing $50 for a bit of plastic, licence to print money etc. etc. but the kids have to have one. You can change them the next day for free if they stop working. Interiors and exteriors of all the shops are beautifully rendered and very witty.  Food in Wizarding world: acceptable, but not particularly cheap. Drinks appear to have a lot of sweeteners in: beware. Better to stick to water.  Rest of Universal and Islands of Adventure.  Minions ride: Queued for ages. Not really a ride. Just sit in a theatre with a big screen in a seat that throws you about a bit. Bit lame but bearable if you love minions.  Holywood Rip Ride: big big rollercoaster. Bit scary and violent. Just about survivable though.  Revenge of the Mummy: classic rollercoster. Real flames. Not exactly a fair reflection of the richness of Egyptian culture though.  Rest of the place: lots of cartoon stuff (most American), Holywood kids films related stuff. Suit younger children but not of much interest to Harry Potter types. No mention of the fact that Dr Seuss is an alumnus of Lincoln College, Oxford (tut tut). Some interesting Orientalism in the Port of Entry and The Lost Continent.

This was such a awesome place to visit during the Halloween season. There was six haunted houses, plus several attractions and rides. So much to do with so little time. This was one of the best Halloween attractions I've been to in a long time. Definitely will be back!
Ensure you get park to park tickets and buy unlimited fast passes which are around $80 each. Yes expensive but it will make the most out of your day rather than queing most of it.
This Park is great if you really like movies all the rides are great! The new Harry Potter section of the park is very well done! Only thing I would say is take your own food&drink

This park was like dead !if the wisdom of Harry Potter didn't existed there I couldn't justify its existence!many years ago,at about 2004, I have visited Los Angeles universal studios which at that time was amazing !i was thinking if my review has to do with the thing that I am getting older but neither our teenagers had a great time at Florida universal studios.
If you go to Universal do not miss the full Harry Potter experience. Gringots bank ride is amazing, as is the train ride from Universal to Hogsmead !

So not so much of a big deal as advertised. If your staying at one of the resort hotels there is bus transportation, the only drawback I see in this is there is only one drop off for all the hotels. The point that I'm making is from that point to the parks you have to go thru the City Walk, which is at least 1/4 of mile. This way they can get your food money right off. Mostly high end restaurants. It is a beautiful park with many interesting attractions and many places to eat. Our average for two days was at least $40.00 for two people. So if your on a budget beware. The Cabana Bay hotel not any cheaper. Bring plenty of money or be prepared to quickly max or stretch out your credit card. I really can say without a doubt I will not be back. I'd rather go down the road 4 miles and have more fun. This only my opinion and you'll have to judge this for yourself. One last note bring sunglasses and some type of head wear there's not much shade.

Lots of walking and interactive rides. Lots of things to do. Staff's at park are super friendly that made me think they were related to Disney. Rollercoaster was my favorite, I really enjoyed and loved the ride. Don’t forget to buy the express pass, as it saves lot of time being in a queue.

Visited Universal Studios Halloween Horror night on 17th Sept. A really good evening at the park. Didn't manage to see everything in the one night even though the queues wasn't that long, maximum one was roughly 30mins. The Horror Studios were very good with some brill actors. Quite a lot of walking so comfy shoes needed. A few of the rides were shut were closed for evening maintenance but it wasn't a problem. Staff was helpful and you need a map to pick the bits you want to see.

Man, there was so much to do! So much so, that I have to go back as soon as possible in order to finish everything up. I was even invited to screen and survey some promotional trailers for shows about to premier this fall, for which I received a $20 gift card! This was hands down my best vacation, thus far.

It was a hot day but we dint care an d spent over 10 hours walking. My kids loved every ride and every show. Do not miss Harry Potter World, I couldn't believe how great and real life it looked. I suggest go there first thing in the morning and then work your way toward entrance. Jimmy Felon ride was also big hit, my son went 2x on it. The only ride my kids did not care for was the Mummy ride because there were sharp drops. Food is pricey so bring some snacks and you can store it in the lockers, and park is not that big so you can easily walk back to retrieve it. All stations that sell water will give you cup of ice water free of charge and on hot day its huge plus. Out of the whole food the only thing I recommend is roasted turkey leg, everything else was like any other park food.

I love universal.. food and drinks are expensive so I tend not to buy from there.. city walk is much more reasonable and I take a water bottle and fill up at the fountains. Queues can be very long but I still love it!!
This was my first time at the original universal studios park in a while. The rides have really improved. The Rock It roller coaster and the Transformers ride were the best rides.

This place is straight up legit and is totally worth visiting. The rides are fantastic. You must ride the Hulk! Harry Potter was also worth it. The park is very clean and well maintained. Food was good and staff is friendly. We will be back again.....and again.

40,000 (mostly) geeks descended on Universal for an evening of fun after a week long conference. What a great time we had. The park is clean, well organized and as expected, somewhat expensive. A great time was had by all.

Treat yourself by staying at a hotel on-site and you'll have the time of your life at Universal! We stayed at the Loew's Royal Pacific Resort. It was very nice. A lot less expensive than the Portofino (although that is very nice, too!) and a closer walk to Islands of Adventure and CityWalk. Take advantage of the early access by staying on-site at one of the hotels that offer it, and get an express pass. Well worth the investment. Helpful hint: a cup of ice water is free throughout the parks. Just ask! On a hot summer day you'll be glad you did. We were!!

Yes, we love this place. This is a great time of year to visit. We stay on property so we get express passes. We were only in the park for four hours today and we rode 6 attractions and had lunch. Note that if you come this time of year it is their Halloween Horror Nights so the park closes early to those not paying extra for the haunted houses. Wear your comfy shoes. You will walk a lot. Expect very warm, humid weather. Be prepared for rain showers. Plan to have a lot of fun!!!!!

Came here for our two week summer holidays and never got bored. There is so much to see and do. Love everything about this place. The atmosphere, the rides, the staff, the food. Cant wait to come back in 2019.

Be prepared to PAY!! There are two parks to visit. Each one can take a FULL day to tour. Lots to see, many rides for kids, teens and adults. We were mainly interested in the Harry Potter exhibits (TWO parks and you pay for both! Be aware that most of the exhibits are really gift shops! For example the magic wands, that one could make from Home Depot (for about $2) cost $50! Many places to eat both inside the park and outside (after you pay the $20-$30 parking fee). Plan to spend at least the entire day there.

My husband and I have been here twice now. the first time was in off season and the second time was during peak summer season so we have had very different experiences but totally amazing nonetheless.

Bought a 14 day pass for 2 at a cost of £420 only to find the parking is another $20 a day. Being a carer with a disabled wife in a wheelchair the only option for us is to drive. No concessions at all for disabled visitors apart from closer parking spots. Once in the park wheeling the wheelchair around we found the ground was laid in concrete slabs with large expansion joints which could stop the wheelchair dead if the front wheels got caught in the gaps. Some of the slabs were uneven which again caused problems. I can remember 10 years ago disabled visitors were given express passes so they didn't get caught in a long queue (sometimes an hour wait). Not any more. Express passes have to be paid for and no concessions at all. I could understand them being dubious about visitors renting one of their wheelchairs, but when you bring your own? Come on Universal have a heart! We waited in long queues and by the time we were near the front we needed the rest room so had to miss out as there are no rest stops near the queuing areas.
More than Disney. She likes the faster rides and this has good selection of her. She just hit 48 inches so could go on many coasters. The non-ride attractions are great too. Fun times everytime.

There were only two family bathrooms in the whole park- good luck if you are a mother out with your little children. Not transgender friendly either due to the same issue- felt badly for some of the teens/ pre-teens waiting to use the facilities. Otherwise, a fun park.

If you've been to any of the parks you know that although there are multiple restaurants the food menu is nearly the same no matter where you eat and the quality is typically mediocre at best. I don't know why, after having visited Universal studios so many times, that I had never tried this restaurant, but I'm so happy I did. The menu was different from the other "restaurants" in Universal and the quality was unlike any other restaurant I've been to in Universal. It starts with the fact that you actually sit down and order vs you get up and order and then sit down. This restaurant is located in the "wharf" area and there are other seafood restaurants in the same block/building there that I will have to check out next time I go.

Fab u loud Can't describe it From start to finish was unmissable Staff were the best ever happy and talkative all day Rides were fantastic and easy to get in without fast pass Food prices much better than Disney with free refills kept doing what ur doing Islands of adventure next then Volcano bay 😆

This is a great event for those who enjoy Halloween. This was the best year for the houses. The sound was terrific and the detail in each was great. The shows in the park, however were weak.  The event is definitely worth going to.
Amazingly friendly and helpful staff throughout! Excellent variety of themes from Harry Potter to Simpsons. Only drawback is limited options for little kids (under 40").
Love it here. Theming is great and rides are good fun. Wish they had more coasters however. My favourite is the mummy and gringotts.. the whole hp area is amazing!

Really loved the Star Wars movie for fans, also stage performance by the Star Wars celebrities, you can spend a whole day there, shuttle facilities to every Disney spring theme parks, free stroller parking, bring sunscreen & water with you. Favorite part,got to meet Kylo ren!!!
We had never been but finally decided to this year. It was a blast! All of the houses and the theming were great. Good job universal!

I went with a party of 10, we had bever been before to a rollercoaster park, and it was so fun, Simpsons Ride was the best, been in Springfield is something i will never forget, you fell like a child, there are too many things to do, and we found a very good deal for 3 day park (Universal + Islands of Adventure). I totally would go back if i return to Orlando!!

We visited in September and managed to go to the first 3 Halloween Horror Nights - we really loved this, lots of scares, plenty to see and lots of rides such as the Mummy and Rip Ride Rocket stay open. We would definitely recommend but not for the faint hearted !. Great fun 😀

We stayed at a Universal Orlando Hotel for 14 nights, and spent our time visiting the three parks (Universal Studios, Islands of Adventure and Volcano Bay). Our 14 days were full of absolute fun. Universal Studios has an excellent selection of world-class rides and experiences, obviously with Diagon Alley being a major attraction. Visiting in October we experienced virtually no queues at all, meaning that we hardly ever used our Fast-Pass included in our hotel stay. We can't wait to return!

I gotta say, I overheard the gist of this ride and thought naa I'll go ride the hulk again. But then I decided to wait the line and ride this. I am really glad I did. It is pretty amazing how they have designed it to feel just as cool, rough, in the middle of it all, etc. I would have rode again if the line wasn't so long.

Went to visit and had a nice time. There were great rides when they were actually open. It seemed like many were "closed" for maintenance which was disappointing. The hulk was amazing of course. Spiderman shocked me, I wasnt expecting it to be as good as it was. Would go back price pending.

Universal Studios is one of the technological and mechanical wonders of the world. It speaks for itself and is known the world over. If you're in the neighbourhood then it's definitely worth a day trip out.  Plan to go early, get your tickets and prepare to make memories you will remember for years.
Great loved the setup hated the fast pass people there should be a limit to that part but it was great love the hive house the most

We got tickets to Universal's 3 parks for 4 days and felt like we could have died from exhaustion after 4 days in all the parks, but it was fantastic! Tip 1: if you only have 4 days, skip Volcano Bay. It was nice, but the thunderstorms are unpredictable. Tip 2: Get fast passes if you can afford it. Our wait time was usually around 30 minutes, but more popular rides were longer. Fast pass riders walked right on to most rides with no wait.

We had not been to Universal Studios for about 10 years and my has this park changed. The 3D and 4D rides make you feel like you are part of the ride. Every section of the park has a treat or drink you must try before leaving. From Harry Potter's world to the Simpson's to New York will each transport you to that place. This was my absolute favorite park.

Universal Studios is a bit of an odd name these days, it may as well be called 3d world. Terminator, Escape from Gringotts, Shrek , Transformers, Minions and Race through New York - all require 3d glasses. Don't get me wrong they are all enjoyable but the park could do with some variation as that's almost half the attractions there.  It's a real shame that Jaws has gone and ET is still there, and at least the Horror make-up show is still going strong making up for the lack of all the other studio attractions that have met their demise over the years such as the Studio tours and the tributes to Lucille Ball and Alfred Hitchcock and many, many more.  Men in Black and The Mummy are both excellent. Rip Ride Rockit is good but getting really rough and the in car sound systems are starting to crack up.  The Simpsons is a lot of fun but if you are short try and get a front seat as with someone taller in front of you will seriously block your view.  ET is still there - can't imagine why.  The Harry potter train ride that takes you to Islands of Adventure is great and well worth doing.  It is a shame that Jaws, Earhquake/Disaster and Twister are gone as they were so very different to the newer rides. And of course we should all take a moment to remember the flying cow in Twister.  Needs a bit of a revamp.

Universal was the original of the three parks. There are plenty of rides and theatre like experiences, but it is worth the extra to do HHN. Our favourite Haunted House was "Texas Chainsaw Massacre", when you see panic stricken young men out side the house, mission accomplished.
Would never advise anyone to deal with the reservations staff, probably contracted, and totally unreliable.

We had our first visit to the Orlando area at the beginning of October and we loved Universal! Our girls love Harry Potter and I was genuinely impressed with the rides - the technology is amazing, truly! Overall, I liked that there were a lot of food options, many places to sit down and rest, and also enough to keep you interested. Every park employee I encountered was very nice!

I forget we're over 50 when we visit and that's a good thing we may not run to the next attraction now but enjoy the details of the park more now. we were lucky but sad to be there for the last day of The Terminator 2 3-D attraction. loved the new race though New York ride and always enjoy The Mummy and The Simpsons ride

Universal studios , without a doubt is a very exciting place to visit for all ages. I've been enjoying this park since the 1990's. I've never been disappointed. I look forward every year to Halloween Horror Nights.

Very disappointed by my recent visit to your horror night event, clearly a case of profit over guest satisfaction. You had obviously issued too many tickets for the event which resulted in a very poor experience in the park, horror houses were basically one big line of people meaning there was no scare factor to them as you could see what was coming as it happened to the guests in front, express pass was a complete rip off as you still had to wait over 30 minutes in line for each of the attractions. Cast member were miserable and clearly not interested in being there. Not the experience I would have hoped for having spent $1000 for 5 of us to attend. Guest services on the night were not interested in dealing with complaints.
Universal does it again. Everything close together and all the entertainment was good quality. We went Sept/Oct so didn't need a fast pass as waiting times were good. I may actually return here.
Was a great time again. Good time we had here esp at Halloween Horror Nights. Was a good new experience being first time there.
I am a season pass holder to Disney and this is my first trip to Universal!! I am so impressed with this place!!!! I actually like this tons better then Disney. Kudos Universal!!!!
My family went down there last year it has tones of stuff for older and younger people very up set that they are taking drangon challenge out great choice
Really enjoyed it, only spent one day here so definitely had to rush to see everything. Prices are expensive but a great day of memories for our family.

Excellent 10 hours here.  Queues surprisingly short even for the numerous headline rides. There are loads of these.  Must do:  Both Harry Potter Worlds Hulk rollercoaster Rip Ride Rocket The Mummy Spider-Man Minions Loads more.....  Despite cramming in 20 plus big rides we will be heading back for those we missed.  A truly brilliant day.
We spent a day here - nice place and we were glad we went - however, the rides are very similar to each other. After a while we got a bit bored.... Harry Potter is amazing though...

We visited Universal Studios with our kids (7 and 9 years old). They really loved it. We stayed at the Loews Royal Pacific Resort and it was a perfect choice. Staying there, you get an early admission (they let the hotel guests in an hour before anyone else), you can use their water taxis to and from the hotel and, the most important of all, you get express passes for you and your family. If you're staying somewhere else you can still buy an Express pass but I don't know if you get an early admission then. Now, take my advice, you will need an Express pass if you don't want to waste your day standing in a line. The queuing times seemed to vary from 15 to 75 minutes but with the pass, it was usually just a couple of minutes.  I loved the Harry Potter area, everything was just perfect. Especially in the morning when it was still dark and there were not many people around it was almost magical. We bought our kids a wand, they have three kinds. Go for the interactive one (it's the most expensive but the difference is not very big compared to what you get). My advice is, arrive early (it does feel funny to go to a theme park at 7 a.m. but it's worth it), buy the wand and wander around Diagon Alley doing your spells before lines start to form. That way it'll be a surprise what happens when you use your wand and it feels more magical. You can do the rides later because the Express pass will save you from queuing.  Another thing my kids loved was the Animal Actors show. They also have meet&greets and my daughter was delighted to meet her favorite actor (he's a dog).  The rides were fun but I think they have too many 3D/4D rides. They soon start reminding each other even though the theme is different in every ride. There are only a couple of "traditional" rides in the Universal Studios park. There could be more variety. This is why I'm giving a 4 not a 5. Our favorite rides were Harry Potter/Escape from Gringotts and New York.
Always a great day in Universal. I do wish there were more rides and not the simulator / 3d glasses / watching a screen while riding. If you have been on one you've been on them all.

We had a great day here. Primarily attended for Harry Potter attractions, and could have spent all day there! However, we had a good look around the rest of the park and got most of the rides done in the 8.5 hrs we had without express tickets. Definitely get the app before you go to keep an eye on wait times. Food was ok, parade was short but sweet.
Absolutely love universal there is so much to do there....it's just a lovely place to be the kids loved it and we were never bored.

We visit the park every year for Horror Nights and this year did not disappoint! The haunted houses were good, scarecrow being the absolute best! Unfortunately it looks like Bill and Teds show will be done after this year, that is very disappointing as it has been so great, hopefully they will have something just as good in the future. We bought annual passes this time so we will be back more often and next Halloween this will still be a must!
This was poor!  The rides closed at 12 yet advised it was open till 2.  Over booked and over advertised for what it could have been.  Very disappointing

It is very interesting for teenagers who have never seen this before. But, it is very expensive! 100 bucks for entrance, even for 14 years old. 20 bucks minimum for parking. 70 bucks p. P. if you want a fast track pass. You need this, especially if you have only one day time. Otherwise you're waiting 50+ minutes for one attraction. Considering November not a high season, waiting time then might be even worse. But kids love it and it might be worth once in a lifetime 😎

I'm not sure why but my first visit to the park wasn't that much exciting or thrilling, Went on the 2 Roller coasters, they where okay, but the park it self just seemed it was missing an atmosphere. The food in the restaurants was fantastic tho.  Not sure I'll be revisiting next year as £220 for 2 roller coasters a bunch of out dated simulators lol.  Anyhow, I'm sure I'll return in years to come when they have a huge renovation.  This is not so much of a dig at universal, I was just expecting more from what I've herd from others.

Out of all the parks I prefer this one. The fast pass is essential if you want to get on more than 1 ride otherwise 90 mins in a queue. Still extremely busy but much better than MK, MGM etc. We had tickets for Halloween. It was 'Ok worth the extra money, emmm not sure. I think it could have been alot better. Queuing for the haunted houses for over 60 mins a time gets tedious after the first 3 houses ( so 3 plus hours for what equated to about 6 mins of being inside. Watching other people's reactions was funny but came predictable. I gave up after 4 houses...the best for me was the hive. Universal is the only park out of all of them I would again ( 2nd time in 10 years ) however not a lot has changed. But it's the best of a bad bunch so to speak.

2 weeks in Florida and it was the only park we wanted to do twice! It's absolutely amazing, awesome and we had a ball there. Queuing was easy we went early both days and did every ride with only a 5 minutes wait, Hogwarts is unbelievable, the express train was fantastic taking us to Hogsmeade, the rides were totally brilliant were big HP fans and the attention to detail in both parks was just fantastic. Our son is 7 and was so disappointed at Magic Kingdom but absolutely thrilled to bits with Universal we were totally chilled enjoyed every second of both days. Hulk, Spider-Man, Kong, return of the mummy and Transformers all amazing rides, Dr Doom was untrue, Fantastic park worth every penny.

I must admit that this is an awesome vacation spot. It is good for the whole family and kids. There are plenty of rides. I have taken MIB alien, Harry Potter and few other rides. They are all very good. Of course some are not good for the sick and weak. Lot of good food and happy faces. Its an happy place.

The whole concept of this park, is based on some highly popular movies. The rides are really good, but a lot of them are based around 3d or motion simulators. If like me you suffer from motion sickness on simulators you will probably not totally enjoy all the rides on offer. Don't despair though there are a couple of the more traditional rollercoasters to be found. The Rip Ride Rocket is brilliant and is a "must do " ride. Also try The Mummy's Revenge as that's quite good as well. A visit to the Harry Potter section is an essential visit but be warned that it is very busy and should not be rushed as there is so much to see and yes there is a ride to experience. Make sure that you have a Two Park ticket so that you can ride the Hogwarts Express over to Islands of Adventure to visit Hogwarts itself. Food is varied and I'm sure that there is something for every palate. One of the best shows is the Blues Brothers and this takes place out in the street and you really must make time to watch it as it's brilliant. Overall this is a really good park and well worth a visit or even two.

I love Universal Studios. It's a very funny and special place. But I think so, it's time to change some attractions, some are already boring. Not to mention that on some occasions you find several professionals discouraged and moody.

For older children and adults, there is no place that can beat Universal Studios Orlando. We traveled with another family in October, the weather was around 82 every day with less humidity and only one half day of rain out of 6 (pack your dollar store ponchos and put them in your purse for this reason!). We stayed at the resort, so ease of moving back and forth between the hotel and arks was great, and we had express passes included, which meant we literally had no wait time on at least 90% of rides. On the few we had to wait for the max was 20 minutes. We rode everything, did everything, ate anywhere we wanted (no reservations needed) and well, had a wonderful vacation! Again, bring the tiny dollar store ponchos in case of a pop-up raincloud, bring a folded up plastic bag to throw belongings in for Popeye's Bilge Rat Barges in Islands of Adventure, keep your bags small to fit in the lockers required for may rides, wear comfortable shoes, and bring an empty water bottle to fill at the water fountains to stay hydrated, and you are good as gold. I cannot say enough about how much I love this place!

Go to all three parks and CityWalk. CityWalk has great restaurants nightclubs and stores. It is one of the safest places to go in Orlando. Everyone goes through metal detectors including cast members and hotel guest!

I’m a big Disney fan... but Universal Studio is so well designed, and as a result, I loved this place!!  I have never been to Universal Studio before and I became a huge fan... sorry Disney, but rides were more exciting, each town was designed and well organized! Lockers use the finger print system to recognize you (so no keys are needed), and security system is like an airport. Only negative is Universal is more expensive...(all the merchandise products.., everything’s more expensive than the ones in Disney..!)  Universal collaborates with many stores and restaurants. So you have more variety to choose from. (Disney only have Disney food (burgers and pizza mainly), and Coca Cola’s drink). But Universal has many restaurants inside and outside of the park.  The highlight of the Universal Studio in Orlando was:  Harry Potter (Diagon Alley and Gringotts 3D ride) The Simpson Town Despicable Me 3D ride Revenge of the Mummy (3D ride) Hollywood Rip Ride Rocket (really long & high Roller Coaster!) Transformer 3D ride Men in Black shooting ride Terminator (it was closed when I went)  Diagon Ally (Shopping town for Wizards) was so well designed! Just like a movie! They did a wonderful job!  It is so hard to choose between Islands of Adventure and Universal Studio. They have both different features.  Islands of Adventure has Hogwarts castle as a main attraction, 3 water attractions and Jurassic Park, and Marvel town. For little kids, there is a Dr. Seusses town.  Universal Studio has Rip Ride Rocket Coaster (this was even scarier than the Hulk coaster), The Simpson town, The Mummy ride, Despicable Me and Shrek. For little kids, Woody Woodpecker’s town and water playground.  Both parks are amazingly fun! Use Express Unlimited if you have a day to visit here, it is worth it.(Otherwise use Single Rider lane to shorten the wait time). Average wait time here was 20-30 min. “Escape from Gringotts (Harry Potter)” ride was the longest, 45-50 min wait.  Many of the scary rides (roller coaster, Harry Potter, The Mummy) require you to your bags to put them in a locker. It is busy and take some times.  Harry Potter town is always busy so go there first in the morning.  You must go both parks when you are visiting Orlando!!!

Went there for the first time and was nothing else than impressed. Once again the Americans handled cues and logistics around the park perfectly. So much to see and do. We were only there for a day but we probably should have gone more days.

Yet again we had a great time at Universal STudios. The rides are brilliant whether you like Coasters, 3D & 4D We were staying at the Royal Pacific so had Express queue included but it was fairly quiet anyway. All the staff (apart from 1!) that we came across were happy lovely people. The huge donut from the Simpsons area really must be tried. I shared one with my son and it was delicious. Not too sickly either.

We went to Halloween Horror Night & loved it. Next day, from Island of Adventure, we took the Harry Potter train to Universal Studios. We couldn't find the Harry Potter area (though it was on the map) until we followed the crowd into another dimension!

Yet again I thoroughly enjoyed my recent trip to Universal Studios, Islands of Adventure and Halloween Horror. The parks are just amazing and we always have a brill time.  Halloween Horror We have learned a lot over the years of attending and got it just right this time. We got the add on so we didn’t have to leave the park when it closed from during the day and we stayed in the holding area. I would recommend doing this to anyone attending as you get first access to the scare houses a wee while prior to park opening, it allowed us to go to 7 of the 9 houses over a couple of nights. The scare zones were amazing - the purge especially. It was incredible, it felt as if you were in the film. Scare houses were ace - it’s amazing the amount of work that goes into them.  Universal Studios and IoA The parks themselves you cannot fault but one thing that I have noticed since my last visit is that prices have gone up significantly for food and drink. We don’t mind spending money at all and when your in the parks they are incredible and you just want everything but it got to the point where you get fed up paying significant amounts of money for juice, water, snacks! Think this really needs to be looked at. We’ve already paid a fortune to get to Orlando as well as park tickets but the additional blow of the high prices just started to get annoying. Merchandise prices also - $15.95 for a keyring - I don’t think so. Overall like I say parks are amazing and can’t wait to visit again but I’ll defo be rethinking whether I just bring food and drink with me.  Big shout out to the cleaning staff, Road sweepers, street cleaners, restroom attendants - they are a credit to the parks as the parks were and always are immaculate!!!

Any trip to universal Orlando is always a great time we had such a great time from the moment we stepped foot there. The entertainment is excellent and the food my god so many great places to eat. I love the food the resturants are awesome city walk is great just a good time all the time can't wait to go back in 2018 😀

10 years ago we brought my 5 year old grand son 9 and 12 year old grand daughters to Florida they all three said they lived universal so much more than other Florida attractions.  So this year we brought my 7 and 5 year old grandson and they were absolutely thrilled with universal and said they only want to visit universal and they don't even want to go at all to any other Orlando attractions . We are coming back in February 2018 and they are so excited! Non Of us Can hardly wait!
We found out the hard way. They fixed the problem there for us but we burned up time getting new ones because both places have the same name.

Compared to the Disney parks the Universal parks are much better. A lot of the rides, and there are more here, are sims/3 or 4 D including Dispicable Me, Transformers, Shrek, The Simpsons, ET and the Hogwarts Express to Islands of Adventure. The most extreme ride is the Hollywood Rip Ride Rocket whicd starts by going straight up, vertically until your at the top then all speed round the coaster, a real thrill ride. The indoor coaster Revenge of the Mummy also good. The parade is small but very enjoyable but dont miss it as it was only one a day. The queue for the Hogwarts Express to the other park was over an hour but this may have been down to the time of day as we went at 16.15 as the park officially shut at 5pm and Islands of Adventure open until 8pm. It is only about a 3 min journey and you wear sim glasses as the windows are computerised. It would have been quicker to walk between the parks

Visited Nov 2017 as a couple. Rip ride rocket is fabulous, you choose your own music to ride and they video you as you ride and you can record it on your phone when you get off Transformers is very good. Minions was good but more for kids. Harry Potter ride not as good as IOA. We visited one afternoon arriving about 4.30 pm and there were no queues at all with longest wait being about 5 mins. well worth using single rider lines

I wanted to take a minute to write a review on how the park handled a terrible experience at the park.  My wife and I tried to eat at The Leaky Cauldron. They handled her food allergy very poorly (see my review of the restaurant). As we know how hard it is to eat out with a food allergy we wanted to inform the park so that it doesn't happen to others. Aimee in Guest Servers was very attentive and did what she could to make it right for us. She went above and beyond to fix the issue for us and ensure that our trip was still great. We really appreciate how the park handled our complaint.
The lines to ride a 3-D experience were no less than 60-80 minutes. Red Rocket roller coaster would be fun if not for the whiplash and bruises.

We visited here first when Islands of Adventure first opened. We loved it! So many years later and we still always do it when visiting IOA. It is such a fun ride with great music and atmosphere. This was probably the first of this type of ride in the area and the style has been copied now across so many new attractions. But this one is still good!

Best Rides Harry potter, Transformers, Jimmy Falon, Shrek 4D, Minions....busiest maybe more than Harry potter, Mummy was also good but felt more like a rollercoaster ride than about theme. Shows are good...not to miss the superstar parade, horror special effects.. For kids ET is not miss able. The holiday parade at evening is really good...not to miss.... On Express if you come on opening n do busiest rides Harry n others first..n have one full day for Park...express not required. Suggestions for Universal...Allow people to atleast see the actual Hogwarts express n take pics as a small section of visitors take multi park tickets.

I came here when I was about 3, so I don't remember much! But coming back at 23, was the best.  each and every person that worked there was amazingly polite, every one said happy birthday to my mum. She was treated like royalty!.  We ate everywhere! But I most enjoyed the monsters cafe! I was a little piggy and had a hot dog with pizza! And wow are them slices huge!!!  The place offers sooo much for all ages you don't feel silly walking around in all Disney or Harry Potter clothing your like part of the family!.  the ques for either food or three rides went down very quickly!!.  Thank you very much Karl! You were awesome! You got the best pictures of the family together so thank you for that!!!!!
wonderful park loved the rides thought that this was better then universal's island of adventure and the macy's day parade was great
We took our 4 year old on his trip to Universal he loved every minute of it and so did we as the parents. Looking forward to our next visit next summer.
Very fun way to spend Thanksgiving break. Not too busy and lots to do for all interest levels. Would go back again!
Love this park, lots of rides- we had a fast passes and we glad we had them - regular lines are really long. Lots of fun for the whole family. parade was great, lots of places to eat! love it

Loved this park. Harry Potter area amazing. Every detail is special for all fans. Ride train. Mummy ride was actually one of our favorites there. Lots of different areas for all ages. My only complaint of both parks is how 4D has taken over. Way too many nauseous glasses wearing rides.

We have been to Disneyland several times and have always enjoyed our experience with our children, however upon learning about Ollivanders at Harry Potter we were intrigued by it, after an hour wait we thought it was going to be worth it with good reviews about the experience, however it would have to be the worst time wasting experience ever- unless your a Harry Potter fanatic and even then it would surely disappoint many. Upon entry you are greeted by a lady who talks a few words about wands, then thinking we might be entering into an exciting room we are taken into the gift shop and that was it. I could not believe it. I won’t ever get my wasted one hour waiting in line again but unless you have time to spare this is a complete disappointment to Disney.
Diagon Alley, San Francisco, New York, Spiderman, Race Through New York with Jimmy Fallon, The Mummy. Lunch at the Leaky Cauldron was yummy!
A must for Harry Potter fans. Lots of walking but express passes made the waits easier. Rides fun. Early access worth using to keep queues low.
Very nice and expensive lol. Overall a great place for family and to walk around. Definitely a lot of shops, lounges and restaurants.
We have the best time visiting universal studios, we have season passes and we go twice a year. Halloween horror nights is a must go!

On this ride, they make it very 3D and realistic that makes it look like you are speeding through the New York streets in a street car watching the fights between Spider-man and all of the villains, and with my experience, it seems a little scary for younger ones because there’s a lot of screaming, and there’s one scene where it looks like fire is coming towards you, but it’s really not.

Such a great place! The kings cross and Harry porter world is amazing! You get to choose your wand or a wand can choose you! Fun rides and a great place to visit! On crowded days you need the express pass or you would just be waiting! Simpson’s, jimmy Fallon, Harry Potter rise, MI-B, despicable me are some of our favorite rides! But Mummy is the best :)
Had such a fun time here. No lines except for the Harry Potter world. I can see the place gets crowded, so don't know if I was just lucky or if off season.

We had the 2-park hopper tickets and started our day at Universal Studios. With front of the line passes on a Friday in early December (park was not busy) we easily got through the rides we were interested in by 11 (entered the park at 9). Unfortunately one of the shows we wanted to see didn’t start until 12 and we were ready to head to the other park well before that time.  One thing that was rather surprising / disturbing…. I put my bag in a finger-print activated locker while we went on the MIB ride. I could not get the locker opened after the ride (that’s ok – technology is not fool-proof). I got one of the workers to help me and she just opened the locker and let me take the contents without even attempting to verify it was my bag.

Really enjoyed this park, specifically diagon alley. Very busy Friday-Saturday, decent crowds during the week. Fav rides MIB, Gringotts, mummy. Least fav ride transformers - too jerky kind of nauseating. Diner food and service was subpar. Duff beer decent and service was good.

My family went and purchased the two day two park pass. We only lasted about 6 hrs, when it first opened the waits aren’t too long as they get later in the day. I recommend Jimmy Fallon, the mummy, and of course diagon alley (which is the first place you should head too because it gets packed.) If you’re pressed for time I would definitely skip transformers.

I was not aware of the extensive amount of different characters/themes that were available until I got there, but each has it's own charm and enjoyment. Well worth every step.

Overall, the visitors are nice, and so are the ride operators and service staff. They helped me form a more favorable impression of this park than the Richeter's Burger place did.

We visited Universal Studios (and Islands of Adventure) four or five times during our two week stay at a Walt Disney World Resort in October / November 2017. We purchased in advance 14 -day passes for the three parks (which you need to do if you want to enjoy fully 'The Wizarding World of Harry Potter', experience, as this part of the theme park extends over both Universal and Islands of Adventure). So rather than subjectively wax lyrical about what you should or shouldn't see, I'm just going to give you some pointers to help you maximise the enjoyment of your visit. 1. Be realistic about crowds. It's going to be crowded whenever you go (we were there over Halloween), and whether you like it or not, so prepare yourself for either forking out extra for Express Passes (we didn't) or waiting in long lines. The longest we waited was 50 minutes at 'Despicable Me Minion Mayhem'. On a couple of occasions we arrived at the park relatively early, and headed to the newer and popular rides and attractions first, such as Transformers The Ride-3D, and The Wizarding World of Harry Potter; wait times were not extortionate by any means. For other rides and attractions we waited no more than 30-45 minutes - and we did most of the attractions on offer. 2. Devote plenty of time to 'The Wizarding World of Harry Potter'. Of all the theme park attractions in the Orlando area (including Walt Disney World), it is by far the best. Experience it over a couple of visits if you can. It's been superbly created - full marks to the designers for their creativity and attention to detail; you'll miss all of that if you rush. The 'Harry Potter and the Escape from Gringotts' multi-dimensional thrill ride is a triumph, And the recreation of London's King's Cross Station, complete with departure boards and train announcements, is mind-blowingly accurate (I live in London and use King's Cross station frequently). You'll need dual-park entry to take the Hogworts Express to Hogsmeade Station, as it's in Islands of Adventure. 3. Check daily schedules for parade times, and get there in advance to secure a good viewing spot. 4. If you drive, you'll be parking in a vast multi-storey car park; take a photo of your location indicator, to help you find your car at the end of your visit! 5. Be prepared for security searches at the main entrance; minimise the amount of stuff you are carrying to speed the process, not only for yourself but for others. Enjoy your visit!

My family just returned from an amazing trip to Universal Studios Resort. We went to both Universal Studios and the Islands of Adventure during the busiest time of the year between Christmas and New Years. Based upon our experience, here a few survival tips: 1. Many online sources suggest staying at a Universal Resort hotel. Admittedly, there are benefits depending upon which hotel you stay at. All resort hotels include 1 hour early park admission. However, be advised that the early admission is to the Harry Potter sections only. Also, three of the hotels include the benefit of an Express Pass (more on that in a moment). We chose to stay a much cheaper hotel 4 miles away and paid for our own express passes. In the end we saved money. The resort hotels, while very nice , are insanely priced from $229 to $654 or more per night depending upon the hotel. In addition, they do not include breakfast, and charge $22 per night for parking. We saved approximately $1000 by not staying at a resort hotel. 2. Go to the park early. The throngs of people do not arrive until 11am or so. For the first few hours, you can get a lot of rides in prior to the herd arriving. Plan on getting to the park 30-60 minutes before the gates open especially on the crowded days. You can Google a crowd calendar to know that those days are before you go. 3. Pay for better parking. We paid $30 per day for Prime Parking. Standard is $20 per day. Again, the hotels still charge for parking at a rate of $22 per day. The Prime section gets you closer to the gate. You will still have approximately 10-15 minute walk to the security gate followed by another 10 minutes or so the park entrances. But, the less walking the better as the parks are huge. 4. Regardless of whether you may or may not think it is fair, the Express Pass is worth it; especially on busy to very busy days. For example, on time the Spiderman ride had a standard queue wait time of 120 minutes. However, we got on the ride in about 10 minutes with the Express Pass. Yes, you have to pay extra for the pass. Yes, the rate increases according to the time of year. However, you have to ask yourself if you want to wait in lines all day or ride the rides. You have two Express Passes to choose from, regular or unlimited. We paid for the unlimited version. The difference, the unlimited allows you to ride each ride as many times with the Express Pass as you want to (you do have to reenter the line each time). 5. Make reservations for all park restaurants for dinner. You will regret it if you don’t. I recommend at least eating a Mythos in the Islands of Adventure where the food, service, and atmosphere are top notch. We had a reservation and I overheard people who do not have one were being quoted waited times over 1.5 hours. 6. You may want to purchase either a Quick Service or Full Service Dining Plan. We used the Quick Service Plan = Meal and a snack each day. 7. Many rides have required lockers i.e. Hulk, Rip Ride Rocket, Revenge of the Mummy etc. When required they are free (time of the estimated wait for the ride plus a cushion). The locker sizes are 10x10x16. The one exception is the Hulk where the free lockers are half the size. 8. Use the Universal app which gives wait times. The lone deceptive wait time is for Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey. The estimated wait time is only valid once you are in the ride entrance line. However, what they don’t tell you is that there could be a mile or more line just to get to the ride entrance within the castle. 9. Use a plan. We purchased a book. In general, visit Harry Potter sections first on very busy days. The parks are extremely fun, have very good food, and excellent customer service. But please, plan, plan, plan ahead.

Thankfully, we went on a quiet day (11-29-17) because the line waits were just a few minutes. The Potter parks are SMALL. The rides & wand ceremony are SHORT. We both got motion sickness on the rides but they were fun. Shops lack variety but we liked the food & candy, e.g., frozen butterbeer & green fishy ale. IF YOU GO, CHOOSE A SLOW DAY. Research the Potter parks BEFORE you go in order to enjoy all the little gems, e.g., ask the goblin in the money exchange what his favorite color is. Maps are lacking & there are no staff to guide you so know what to do before you go! It was so quiet we did both Potter Parks by 2 PM & were able to explore the rest of Universal. We loved the King Kong ride & Dudley Do-Right (it's also fun squirting unsuspecting park ride visitors with water blasters). My friend loved getting a wand & casting spells but I was not impressed (you can see what the spells are before doing them when seeing what the person in front of you is doing). We enjoyed the bus driver/skull the most. Basically, the ONLY reasons we enjoyed the park is because we didn't have to wait in lines & did research ahead of time (to know how to find the little extras in the park). We are Potter fans & think you will like it but not love it due to the price (cost for 2 ~$500), how small the parks are, how short the rides & experiences are throughout, & the lack of variety in the shops. Could have been SO much better! They should consult with people like us because we have a lot of ideas to improve it!

My party paid over $800 in entrance fees for this park. We’ve traveled from the UK, Ireland, New England and the Midwest to get here together for Christmas and attend this park. This will rank as THE worst experience for a visit to an attraction, ever. We arrived promptly at 9, and went straight to the first ride. We exited the ride at 11:30 am. We walked through the park, looked at shops. went to the second ride. Got in line. Stood in line for nearly four hours. Exited the ride at 4pm. No access to bathrooms during this time, so my mother had to exit the queue and never got to ride. My brother, who, admittedly, is a big man, is a semi-pro football player: he could not fit on a single ride. Not a single ride. Which meant his travel to FL to go to this park and his entrance ticket were completely wasted. Nor could he, had he chosen, purchase a t-shirt, as the largest size he could find was an XL. He’s too tall for a regular XL. We waited another 45 minutes in a queue for a sub-par burger that cost $15 per person. My mother and brother and his wife spent $120 on two slices of pizza -SLICES- and pasta. I can’t express how infuriating it is to spend this kind of money on terrible food, with terrible service, and nowhere to sit once it was purchased. After the 4 hour wait for a ride, it’s not even worth reviewing the ride itself, because who can enjoy it after being held hostage in a queue for that long? Please, travelers, spend a grand on your family with flights, or dinners, or buy a used car and a small pony. Whatever you do, don’t go to Universal Studios.

My husband and I are big Harry Potter fans, so Diagon Alley was our main focus here. That alone was worth the visit. We rode the "Escape from Gringotts" ride, which lasted about 5 minutes after a 45-minute wait. However, the wait is interesting since you are guided down into the Gringott's bank as you get closer to the ride.  Since our visit was near Christmas, we saw the afternoon parade down the main street of Universal, which was really entertaining with great music. We had some snacks and drinks in the main street section after having been all through the Islands of Adventure Park (before coming over to Universal). Even though the scenery was done very well, right along with beautiful holiday decorations, we noticed that most of the storefronts were just facades rather than actual stores. We think it would be a much better experience if more of those facades contained actual stores. The Ghirardelli Chocolate store, for example, was a huge building, but you couldn't even buy chocolate there - it wasn't a real store.  We enjoyed our visit but probably won't go there again unless friends or our kids really want to go.  ***Also, and I'll mention this in my review of the Islands of Adventure Park, the Harry Potter features are split between the two parks, Islands of Adventure and Universal Studios. That means in order to see all of the Harry Potter-themed attractions, you have to buy a two-park ticket. The Hogwart's Castle and Hogsmeade are located in the Islands of Adventure Park while the Diagon Alley with Gringotts Bank is located in Universal Studios. You can ride the Hogwart's Express train between the two parks to get from one Harry Potter area to the other but don't think that all Harry Potter areas are in the same park, that's all.

This resort is more for kids. Loved the area around the Studios though, great places for food and drink and to just chill while people watching. Great times!

(You still have to wait a little for Butter Beer). It exceeded all expectations! We were able to by-pass lines with a 3 hour wait, and we could re-ride if we wanted. We got in 20 rides in one day! We got to see all of Harry Potter on both sides. Again, huge thanks to our guide Ed who made the day perfect!

Most popular ride 200 mins waiting time which is around 3 hours for a 2 min ride is totally unacceptable and why should people pay over and above the admission ticket too still queue for over an hour too many people allowed into the parks during xmas and new year management have got it all wrong and we will certainly not be back to Orlando Parks again. Its been awhile. Jaws is gone. Back to the Future is the Simpsons. Hitchcock is Shrek. But everything they replaced the classics with are worth it. Obviously Harry Potter is awesome. The Gringotts ride was my favorite from both parks. Leaky Cauldron food was fantastic. Jimmy Fallon was a lot of fun. Can’t wait to go back.

The weather was great, and the crowds moderate on this Monday. They were offering a discount on the fast pass, but the lady selling tickets said we could wait to buy them later inside the park. Our 2 tickets were about $240 without the fast pass. We chose cheap parking for $20. $30 premium parks you a little closer, but after walking the park all day, saving the extra walk was not worth $10 to us. We installed the Universal app to track ride times. There are other apps available but the ride times are NOT accurate. Keep in mind that the universal location map is only so, so... meaning it works some times. The park is not that complicated, and you will figure it out quickly! We headed to Transformers 1st with a 10 min. wait, then the same with Jimmy Fallen. We strolled through Diagon Alley and then went to MIB, also 10 min. We waited until Gringots was 45 min, but most of the other rides we caught with 10 min wait. Our favorite was the Mummy which we rode consecutively. The Minion ride was also a 25 min. wait. We missed the large roller coaster at the front, but it always has a longer wait, and you MUST store everything before the ride (change in pockets, cell phones, chap sticks, and medical devices - I wear an insulin pump that must come off). They offer free lockers for this, but I suggest memorizing this code with 2 people. The other rides that require just purse and backpack storage are the Mummy, MIB, Gringots. I put those codes in the notes in my phone because you have to remember so many. Gringots lockers are the worst, as they are cramped, and sometimes you have to wait for people to remove their items in order to find a free one. I should also note that you can bring in a few light snacks and 2 liters of water. We ate one meal there for about $38.... let’s face it, it’s just amusement park food. Expensive and less than average....If we had another day we would have done both parks, but for one day only, this one is our favorite. It should be noted that this time of year, there were fewer kids, and primarily foreign travelers. A very polite, easy going crowd.

We were so amazed with Harry Potter Worlds. If you are a Potter Fan then this is the place for you!! Our son was lucky enough to be picked at Ollivander's . The magic and the wizards and Hogwarts Express were so good. Tip: Go on a rainy day. We did and there were like no lines. We went on a sunny day and we could hardly get through the lines. We got the dining plans and they were worth it (get the one with the souvenir mug) Butter Bear is like $7 or $8 alone and it comes with the meal plan Eat at 3 BroomSticks! Way better food selections and better prices than any other place. The other Potter Restraunt was okay but did not have the same food choices. Go early, less lines Bring hand sanitizer  Overall, all of Universal Studios and all the parks were amazing. A lot of work and worth the money to go at least once in your life. I suggest going 2 days if you want to cover everything, especially if you land on a busy day.  One thing I did not find fair is the front of line passes. I think Universal should do the same as Disney with Fast Passes so that everyone has equal opportunity. It cost us like $1000 to go and it was like our money wasn't good enough to the people who had more to buy the front of the line passes. Some lines were 4 hours to wait on (so we didn't go) so if you had front of line passes you wouldn't wait that... not everyone has that kind of money to spend so much more and so it makes a person feel that the money they saved and worked hard to go to didn't matter as much as the people that had more. Disney gives Everyone the same opportunity. Universal cators to the higherarchy when it comes to rides that can afford to cough up more.  All in all, it is a must see and a place to go to

We have had it with theme parks. We had some bad experiences with regard to excessive crowd sizes/wait times at parks in some other states, but we thought A world-class resort like Orlando Studio's would have figured out how to mitigate that somehow, right? Nope.  There was the 385 minute wait to ride the hulk coaster...over 6 hours...seriously? The shortest line during our 2 day visit was 30 minutes for E.T., which is an old, obsolete attraction that did not impress.  We did "pre-register for Jimmy Fallon's New York ride, which was awesome. We registered upon arrival, were given a time to return, and then the line was actually enjoyable based on the live entertainment, the video entertainment and so forth. The ride itself, while short, was excellent.  However, we only rode on 3 ride in 2 days, plus observed a live performance of "Fear Factor".  Universal Studios: Here's a thought....raise your ticket prices so that you reduce the load in the park while still maintaining revenues. Maybe if you double your entrance fee you'd cut your load in half?  Also, hire a flow analysis engineer to figure out ways to relieve bottlenecks at the attractions. Perhaps the Jimmy Fallon ride is a glimpse at the future?  Otherwise we enjoyed walking through the park, it really is a cool place. Was it worth $800 to do so? No.
