We spent a few days at Universal studios and had an amazing time. There is so much to see and do with many great rides. Unfortunately for us we were there during a peak time and had to wait in the long lines for many things. Overall we had a blast and are looking forward to going back one day.

For a great meal with the Jimmy Buffett feel this is the place. The food is good, the service was excellent. And you get a bonus of 10% off merchandise if you show your receipt that you ate there. Hint. If you just mention it they will give you the discount! Get onion rings on a little plane.

It’s a great park, BUT I have to tell you a pair of issues.  FIRST. As you buy the tickets, they will offer you a 3 park hopper ticket that is really expensive, the thing is that actually you will hardly finish two parks in one day; so, you can buy a two park ticket and it will save you a lot (most if you’re traveling with family).  SECOND. There were waiting times on attractions as long as 240 minutes (YES 4 hours). We actually only got to ride en 4 attractions. So, as you can see, it wasn’t a very fortunate experience.  They sell a fast pas ticket that cost twice as the regular, but you have that option...

We were lucky enough to visit during the Christmas holidays so everything was beautifully decorated leaving such a fun festive feeling. Hogwarts and Diagon Alley were my favorites however with the holidays come really big crowds so lines were long and admission prices were really high. If I knew I could experience Universal with much smaller crowds I’d go back but I’m not sure it’s ever not crowded. The employees were awesome. They were professional and really did a great job. It’s an incredible place.
We traveled to universal to see the Harry Potter attractions, and were thrilled at the overall experience. My teen son really enjoyed the rides and coasters, and we had a wonderful family experience.
More for kids and Harry potter fans, but buildings were beautiful Needed to be updated on some things
Interesting sites for all ages. We had so much fun. The Harry potter exhibits were our favorites. I would recommend this place
Fun Theme park. Lesser known that Disney parks but just as fun and has a great atmosphere. Love the ET ride, it's my favorite and so nostalgic. Can't wait to visit again.

Universal definitely has a wide variety of rides, most of which are really good. Some areas of the park are dated however for the most part most areas are well themed and very clean. I would recommend this for anyone over the age of 5-6. Many of the rides are much to intense for those younger and many will not meet the minimum height requirement.  The Wizarding World of Harry Potter was exceptional. The theming and execution is extraordinary and not to mention the rides, which topped off the experience and immersion. This is a must see for Harry Potter fans. Even if you aren’t a fan you will still be amazed.

Loved our time here compared to Disney World. The food was better (Monster Cafe), there are more places to sit and relax and it's cheaper. More rides for the teens and definitely a lot of magic in Harry Potter's world. I appreciated that most of the rides have lines that are in a building so you're not exposed to the weather. They have a refillable cup for drinks which includes Icees. We spent an equal amount of days here and Disney World and the kids and I agreed that the experience here is much better. This is our new park when in Orlando. No more Disney World, they no longer value their guests.

My wife and I have been here before and really enjoyed the park. Lots of new upgrades and some stayed the same. Very crowded because of the Harry Potter weekend but still bearable. We used the Express pass that we added to our package. We used the water taxi to the park from Sapphire falls hotel. Great time. City Walk was great also.

This place was amazing with so much to see and the Rides were Fantastic .We found it was more geared to adults not much but a little than the Magic Kingdom ,we spent 3 days covering Universal Studios ,with the City Walk and Bubba Gump Shrimp or Margeritaville ,So much for your eyes to take In and the variety of Foods to choose from .There were no long waits for the Rides here and the Rides were longer and so realalistic, and fun ...Would definately visit again
Wish I could have stayed longer perhaps next trip over but I only had a few hours free. Lived up to expectations
Not many rides for todddlers to enjoy unless they are 40” tall, not many cool attractions either but loaded with shops which contains mostly same stuffs.

We spent Christmas Day in Harry Potter world - very well done and immersive! You should get both Universal and Islands of Adventure as the Harry Potter experience is split and the Hogwarts express runs between. The train ride is really cool. Watch in the line up for the part where you can go through the wall at platform 9 3/4 - it can be easily missed. One tip - share one butterbeer if you have to have one right away. We liked the frozen one. If you drink a whole one yourself it can contribute to making you queezy on the rides as they are very sweet. Loved the shops in knockturn alley! Get to the parks early and line up for the most popular rides first. We didn't buy a wand ( they are quite expensive), if you do, you may just end up lining up to do the wand things. We just would stop and watch as someone else did and move on. I was there with my husband, 18 year old and 20 year old kids. I suggest you do Universal when your kids are 12 or up and you are under 60. The best rides involve roller-coasters in the dark with lots of computer generated images and abrupt motion. You are all more likely to enjoy it if you are old enough not to be terrified and young enough not to be terrified. DO NOT do the Side Show Bob Simpson ride if you are prone to motion sickness. It is haywire and a bit too long. All 4 of us got off thinking we would Barf! Get to Volcano Bay on a sunny day early in your trip. Be warned that they close down on cold days for good reason. Travel light in Universal (cargo pockets). There are water fountains by the bathrooms so you don't really need a backpack with water bottle. Stopping for the lockers will slow you down. Towels cost quite a bit to rent at Volcano bay - we brought our own microfibre towels. There are little baskets at the base of each ride to leave your sandals and towels at. I suggest you all bring a very small change of clothes for after and lock that and your cell phones in one locker and just stick together. The trapdoor tube drop is crazy and involves a long climb up the Volcano but is highly recommended for daredevils by my kids and husband. If you don't want to do it, watch the riders come shooting down the tube from the wave pool or warm pool. That's where they come out. DO NOT waste your money on the PREMIUM Parking. It isn't that much closer! Just come early and walk quickly. MYTHOS restaurant in Islands of Adventure is excellent! Pop by and make a reservation and then go do a bit more. It is such a cool place and a nice spot to sit and rest. The food is excellent and is only a bit pricier than the pizza and other crap. It has won awards. We ate there twice it was so good. Don't be deterred that they don't have the prices posted. Just ask to see the menu. Also just a fantastic building to see as well. We headed to the parks early, stopped at the Starbucks just outside the gates in Universal City Walk and grabbed coffee and a breakfast sandwich to eat on the go. Worked well for getting in and ahead of the crowd. If the weather is bad, grab a coat and go early! We did about three days worth of rides on one rainy day! I loved the Men in Black ride, the Mummy and the Marvel ride with Spider man. Prepare to just relax and visit in the lineups. I hope you luck out as we did with 60 minutes being the longest wait we had and most of them being 30 minutes or less. They are very organized. We had some good meals at Universal City Walk - plan to stay for dinner after the park visit for a couple of times. Above all HAVE FUN!!1

Cold day in mid-January, and the park was easy to traverse. Lines short if you visit a kiosk and pick some popular places/times and it's easy to gain entrance. Live characters; shows, backstage fun & antics for all ages. Never a dull moment. Loved getting photos with Chewbacca; Kylo Ren was a "meanie" but oh so much fun. Lots of laughter and excitement.

So disappointed Long lines to get in Food awfull Staff awfull in Harry Potter shop when buying nightwear for myself when I told her I already had one set ,she told me impossible as only sold at universal. News for her I bought some at Harry Potter Watford in the U.K. I went to get food daughter went in the line to order I went to sit at a table,twice I was asked to move by your staff ,I am in a wheelchair and was taking medication,so I said no ,daughter had to get her food from one counter ,then get to another counter to get mine result cold food. Parade I was in the front with wheelchair a character on roller skates virtually fell on me The member of staff very near me did nothing Went to customer services to make complaint all he could say was have some free passes ,it's not about the free passes ,I still have 3 days on ticket ,I will not be back , I have a bad wrist now where the character fell ,I have been in a wheelchair a long time And have learned to fend things off with arms and wrists and moving quickly. My point is it's unsafe at some points in your parade And you have rude staff  Update

I highly recommend Harry Potter World! The simulation rides are all amazing! Very well put together. Speed passes are definitely recommend though other wise the lines. Jimmy Fallon, King Kong, the minions, transformers, rides were all great! All simulation though I wouldn't suggest if you get sick easily or have anxiety. Very large park with lots of options as far as food and drinks. Good for families and younger kids. Super fun, great for friends! I went for a friends birthday we all had a blast! Mardi Gras is happening now parade is awesome good alcoholic beverages. We will be back soon. Universal Citywalk is right there with great shops and tons of restaurants.

I enjoy going to Universal Studios pretty often. I was there for a day during Celebration of Harry Potter. I like the different events you can enjoy like Mardi Gras and Halloween Horror Nights. There’s plenty to do besides rides. You can go to the shows as well. There are plenty of things for the whole family.

This is the family fun place for the kids and adults, don't forget to buy your drinking cup for $11.99 you can save a lot, visited in mid January lines where great a bit cold but didn't wait more than an hour for the attractions. No trouble in bringing your snacks in your backpacks. Very clean and organized and well directed, bathrooms very clean. Lines to enter park was very fast.

Trip # 2 and counting. Stayed at an "On Property" Hotel and that helped us enjoy each of the three parks to the max. One benefit EXPRESS PASS That only saved about a week of queuing time! Hate queues.. Brits really don't like them, we just have world class ability to make them painful and slow.  Universal LA is the iconic one with the back-lot tour etc, Orlando resort stands on its own as a great resort to come and have as much fun as possible in a day or 10 in our case,  The place is just awesome on a planetary scale. If I was American, (which I'm not, but this place makes me wish I was) I'd keep it quiet before the whole of the rest of the world works out how great this place is and then turns up for a party!  Only downside, being north of 50.... the beans run out before I'm ready to quit!

My family and I try to come here once a year. Never too old for this park! Something for everyone. The fast passes are well worth it, and if you stay in certain hotels (we stay at Hard Rock) they are included!!

We went for the Celebration of Harry Potter and had an amazing time! But there’s so much more to do at the park! It’s family friendly and there’s something to do here for everyone, young or old! Clean, well organized and staff is very helpful and friendly! We will definitely be returning for another visit!

Spent a day alone at the end of a business trip in Orlando. Bought a ticket online through the Universal’s app. Took a shuttle from my hotel which was 5 min drive to save parking fee. Great place, with many things to see and do so I would recommend not to divide 1 day for 2 parks. Most rides are 4D rides and the Transformers is the best one in my mind. The app is useful for waiting times as well. Do the despicable me and Harry Potter early in the morning as the lines might be crazy later. Since I was alone I used the single rider lines which was excellent. Had a really good time and spent all day (11 hours) without any problems

We did 2 days at Universal Studios and Universal Island of Adventure! I'm not a huge Harry Potter fan but the Castle and Train were so cool, I could get enough. Every detail was perfect. The rides and shows were the perfect combination. Get the park to park pass so you can ride the train back and forth. You will need at least two days. I will definitely be back, but next time we will stay on Universal's properties!
Harry Potter areas were amazing. Go as soon as the parks open and go directly to the Harry Potter area before it gets full
We had a great time, but the park was oversold. Hard to find the Harry Potter rides, and had to use Express Passes to get on rides. Otherwise a 30 min to 2 hour wait.
Shrek. Really enjoyed this 4D ride. Sit in chairs that bump, drop, move back and forth. Get sprayed when Shrek sneezes . good fun for all. Wait time 10min.

My husband and I opted to pay the extra for the VIP experience. WORTH EVERY PENNY to not wait in any lines alone, but the cost also includes valet parking, breakfast, lunch, and a snack. Our guide, Cyndi, was so sweet and informative. She kept the group going at a good pace with enough breaks, but also trying to maximize our time, as you can do minimum 8 attractions to max 10. I think we got in 9. The tour starts at 9:30 in the morning and goes until 2:30. Plenty of time to go back and use your VIP credentials as Fast Pass for the rides you really liked. My favorites were Transformers, the Rock n Roll Rollercoaster, and the Mummy Tomb. I just thought Harry Potter ride was ok, although the HP “town” was very cool. Also was just ok on the New York with Jimmy Fallon. Most fun we have had in a long time.

We split the time from Universal and Disney for New Years Week! We spent most days at Universal Studios! We had a blast! Get there early for the Harry Potter Section and you should be good to go. We enjoyed the shows as well. Really like the Animal Actors Show. Weather was a bit cold but okay. We will be back again and so glad we went for the lights in Harry Potter World it was so amazing to see....
Thought our teen would go directly to Harry Potter, but he didn't. In fact, we didn't make it there until the next day! Great family fun for everyone. Absolutely as good as Disney!

Hated my experience! I took my family to Universal Studios. I read from experienced amusement park fans that to really enjoy the experience you need to pay the extra $69-99 Express pass. I figured $124/day/person/park was good enough. (X 4 people = $500). No. You wait for hours while the express pass people blow by you. So we would have to spend $800/day just to have a decent experience! Crazy! Of course lots of people do pay that and don’t mind. But despite being a nice amusement park, the overall experience for me and my family was NOT worth it. You really need to ‘upgrade’ to the 1st class experience $200/day ticket to avoid being disappointed. But of course that’s EXACTLY what Universal wants you to do. So it’s a rigged deal. 1st class = great. 2nd class = miserable. Unless you have the money to upgrade to Express Pass. Skip it!

We recently returned from a week at Universal and are already planning our return trip! Diagon Alley is simply amazing. There is nothing like a massive dragon breathing fire to make your vacation complete. The Escape from Gringotts is a great ride, although the locker situation is a nightmare - surely there is a better way?!?! Knockturn Alley is a cool place to get out of the Florida sun, with tons of interesting details that bring the books to life. No visit would be complete without ice cream from Florian Fortescue's - try the Apple Crumble. Outside of Diagon Alley, there is lots to do. My family's favorites included The Mummy (which could be scary for younger riders), Jimmy Fallon (the show clips are hilarious!), ET (classic!). and Despicable Me. We enjoyed the character parade in the afternoon and catching beads at the evening Mardi Gras parade. We had lunch at Richter Burger, which was overpriced and somewhat gross, and also at the Simpsons Food Court, which was similarly overpriced but less gross. The prices are what you would expect at a theme park, though. We can't wait for our next visit!

This park looked great! Fun place to be! If you and/or your children are Harry Potter fans you will love what they have done for the books/movies. We didn't do any coasters but they were impressive. This place went big in many ways!  We were impressed by the all the ride we went on but especially Despicable Me Minion Mayhem, Transformers: The Ride, Shrek 4-D, Race Though New York Starring Jimmy Fallon, Harry Potter and the Escape from the Gringotts (the Simpson's Ride was well done but it made me extremely queasy...it was just too much for me!).  We attended on Universal 2 Parks/1 Day Pass but I would recommend that each park gets it's own day...there really is a lot to do and we skipped or missed some stuff we would like to have done. Another thing is there are a lot of 3-D rides...I felt really queasy after some of them. I also would like to have seen them keep up with cleaning the bathrooms better...every one we walked in was dirty. Also...if you can get an Express Pass you should as the lines were long!  All in all...the Universal Theme Parks were a great time! We plan on coming to Orlando again and, of course, will go to Universal again.

My inner child emerged in the magical place.... the discarding world is amazing and so much went into the Hogwarts express.... however wish it was more disabled friendly... when I go again I will get the xpress pass as we waited too long in all the ques... me and my dad went on the Jurassic park ride just because it was a short line however I was so scared and my dad did not make it any better and maybe need some more heaters available for the winter... can't wait to go again and I'm definitely waiting on the trolls section

This is one of the best theme parks in Orlando. Going in Feb meant it wasn't as busy as the Summer months. Still recommend buying Xpress passes though so you can skip the line at most of the attractions. Staff friendly & courteous. We had smiles on our faces all day. Highly recommended!

We usually go to Disney parks but I finally convinced my family to go to Universal and they are all so happy we did. We had a great time. Our 5 year old son loved the simulated rides, as a parent I felt safer with him on them as opposed to a regular rollercoaster. I suggest buying the two park pass so you can take the train over to Islands of Adventure. There is beer for adults so that makes it even more fun! The food is decent and moderately priced for a theme park. Get the fast pass it's worth the extra money!

Hey! So I was really excited for Universal for my birthday, they gave me a button and everyone was saying happy birthday. That part was really cool..  UNFORTUNATELY I had not been in a while and every ride is a 3D simulation ride now. I dont like the 3D simulation rides at all - esp one after another they make me disoriented and nauseous. I go to theme parks for coasters and thrills! Unfortunately, there are no coasters left between two parks except Hulk - That's right ONE roller coaster. between TWO parks (There is the mummy which is a small indoor coaster if you count little ones.)  Basically, this place is to walk around as a novelty; cute shops and decor. It's great for children especially if they like 3D rides and not actual moving rides. For teens and adults this place is a major bust. You can grab a coffee and hang out, if you want thrills you wont find them here. They tore down the dueling dragons, the best coasters they had. There just isn't anything left at this point except one coaster the Hulk which gave me whiplash really bad.  BUSCH GARDENS is really where it's at for thrills. They have a ton of coasters and they are ultra smooth and never give you whiplash especially Montu and Sheikra my two favorite coasters. Bush Gardens is MUCH better for couples, teens, and adults. If you like actual rides that move and not just simulation cop-out bs then just go to Busch Gardens - Universal sold out.

We visited Universal Studios during Mardi Gras and the parade was awesome. Very beautiful floats and lots of beads thrown out.  The park was nice and clean but like some other reviews, I thought the number of 3D/4D rides were overkill. Having a nice mix of thrill rides that didn’t require glasses would have earned 5 stars.  The Hulk roller coaster is one of the best I’ve been on, yet, the red Rip one was rough and can make your head hurt. The Kong Skull Island and Spider-Man rides were great and the Jimmy Fallon area was fun. Overall, we had a fun trip and it was a nice change from the Mickeys.  We are not huge Harry Potter fans even though their areas in the park were cool but I would not pay extra for tickets that include the train ride next time around. It just wasn’t worth it to us. However, be prepared to walk a lot.  Citywalk is cool and having an actual parking garage is top notch. It’s worth $20 just to have your vehicle protected from the weather. Just know that after 6 pm, it’s free.

Universal really has grown since the last time I've visited. Most everyone we encountered who works there, was friendly, informative, and outgoing. Diagon Alley is great, and should be visited first thing in the morning. Some attractions can be skipped (like Race Through New York Starring Jimmy Fallon). Saw the Mardi Gras parade which was surprisingly good. Having Universal Express would have been nice, so I recommend staying at an on-site hotel that includes that.

Favorite out of the two parks. Handicap parking is in the prime parking section but $10 cheaper. We bought the express tickets and all thought it was worth it. Just walked up to every ride with no wait. We also had the meal plan which included refillable cup, 1 snack and 1 quick me. The cup was great. Free refills all day plus unlimited icees was great. We had 6 in our group so we shared snacks through out the day. Best snack was Lad Lards giant donuts! We bought the wand and Harry Potter but wish we hadn’t. Every kid there has one and there was lines to do the spells. Felt it was a $50 waist of money.
Good selection of restaurants at the park entrance. Blue Man Group shows there too. Great rides! Best for teenagers not small kids.

It's a great place with interesting rides and attractions. Wait times for rides can be long on certain rides but lines continuously move. I like how they incorporate the 'ride theme' in all the rides so you have something to look at while waiting in line, it's really smart. That Harry Potter area is really cool. I liked The Mummy indoor coaster ride it was so fun. That Rip Ride Rocket coaster... it took me all day to get the courage to go on it, it really is something. Service from all staff really good - Americans get it right when it comes to customer service. There are areas/rides in the park that are dated which should be replaced like MiB and Simpsons, did not like these very much. Overall I had a great time, but I liked Island of Adventure better.

The big 'misser' of this part of the Universal Studios park is not being able to actually go inside of the Hogwarts Castle. The various other shops in Hogsmeade are fantastically realized in amazing detail, but I really wanted to see the castle interior. Perhaps the most entertaining experience I had was watching the park staff at the Raptor cage convince two young kids that the raptor was real. Never broke character once! The Skull Island ride had too much going on to catch everything in a single ride. Note: If you take the express lane, the wait is /really/ boring. They didn't add in the unique features that you get if you take the regular line. Of all the rides, I think I liked the Hulk roller coaster best. I waited to go into the front seat, but I think it would have been even better to be near the back of the coaster. Hogwarts Express was down nearly the whole day, so I was glad to have used my park-to-park extensively the day before.

I hadn't been here since I was a kid myself so it was an interesting prospect bringing my own kids along for a trip. Some of the attractions are new, having replaced older and unpopular or dilapidated rides, etc. The highlight was undoubtedly Harry Potter, even though we were stuck on a ride for 45 minutes and were given tickets for the next day, along with meal and drink vouchers and VIP parking. It pays to spend more and get the backstage pass (or whatever it's called) so you skip all the lines. A must for movie buffs with kids.

So many good things to say about Universal. My wife and I love Harry Potter, and being local residents we are able to go often. Finally broke down and got Annual Passes!! So excited for a year of unlimited trips to Universal. Hogwarts is amazing!

Visited over several days. Most rides had relatively short wait times. Many rides combine 3D effects with moving rides. Also some fast roller coasters and smaller track rides. Some rides require lockers and some are not open to all body types. Enjoyed fear factor live and Horror Make-up show. Mardi Gras parade was fun as well. Would recommend for families with older children and adults.
Two full days of enjoyment. Lots of fun and new experiances. Good start to our holiday I would fully recommend.

I heard Race Through New York Starring Jimmy Fallon had poor reviews. The line was short so we decided to try it and I loved it! Not sure why the reviews were bad, it was an action packed flight simulator, lots of fun.

We had a great day our here, we had the VIP pass for the rides which was the best thing we did being able to go front of the lines! We saved heaps of time. The rides were great fun. We got stuck on one of the roller coasters but that was okay we weren't stuck upside down hahah The whole day was very fun and going between the two parks was great

Must stay to see parade and get some beads!!!my favorite universal activity is islands of adventure the Harry potter ride!!! Best ride ever and don't forget to get butter beer a butterscotch slurpee or frozen ice worth every penny of 8 to 12$ depending on size!!!
Excelent park for family fun. This park have amazing machines, games, fun and splash zones. Ideal for all seasons of the year. Im going with my kidz and friends. I want go all days.

Loved universal but its not for kids under 10. Too many of the rides are design for older children. There are some like Seuss land but that's about it. Save your money and wait till they are older. They will enjoy the park a lot more. There's also No charging stations anywhere.

The park is nice. My 7 year old liked Despicable Me, we all enjoyed the Simpsons and the Animal Show  Compared to Disney, the photo package is horrible for $89. In two days, we had less than 20 photos and I don't think any were good. 1. There are very few photographers. They're only with the characters half the time 2. Often they are standing in the middle of the street. I'd ask what background, they would say whatever we want. No photos by any of the iconic spots 3. The photos just were not good. They would take one quick foto, to get back to doing nothing. 4. Hit the photo shop earlier on your last day. The shop closes sharp at park close, we couldn't get our photos (not that there was really anything we wanted printed)  Two park pass... We got it, but it was a bit of a waste. If your not a Potter fan, the train is lame. We bounced each day, but it wastes a lot of time  Btw, food tip. We enjoyed the Simpsons, Krusty burger with a flaming Moe.  Let me know if you have any questions. If this was helpful, click on the thumbs up  Les y Yulie

Enjoyed our visit to Universal Studios after 3 days at the Disney park. Not knowing exactly what to expect after a two not so pleasant days at the Magic Kingdom & Epcot, we were pleasantly surprised at the friendliness from the park staff, the very clean surroundings & of course the theme park itself. Lots of space to maneuver comfortably even with the large crowds; not a jillion baby strollers & park scooters bumping you; exciting up to date attractions unlike the old, dated & overly crowded Magic Kingdom & Epcot. Thoroughly enjoyed the “Harry Potter” village & the kids using their wands to perform a few magic feats. The Shrek 4-D program was amazing! This park had attractions that our 6 & 9 year olds could relate to: Dispicable Me, Superman, Cars, Shrek, many more! An absolute must see! Our 6 year old could have ridden the Woody Wood Pecker roller coaster all day! Fantastic restaurants & beverage stops & shops all over the park that you didn’t have to wait for 2+ hours to get seated! I didn’t feel gouged with exorbitant prices & overwhelmed with the pressure of buying like I did at Disney! Totally amazing experience for all of us! Now this is a theme park that the entire family will enjoy!!

...but it is impossible not to have a good time. Totally recommend the express ticket, especially for grumpy old gits like me! We had a great day, despite my best efforts! That has to be high praise indeed.

I’m not sure where to begin. The park is truly fun for everyone. There is something to catch your eye wherever you turn. The rides range from the most exciting to laughable fun youngsters. As in all commercial parks the food is expensive but pretty good. You are allowed to take in bottled drinks as long as they have not been opened. No coolers are permitted. The park is very clean and there are plenty of restrooms.

This was the first time we have taken our two sons (8&11) to a theme park, and everyone had a great time. I didn't realize that so many of the rides were 3D/4D, which made me pretty queasy, which was unfortunate because they were so elaborate and well done, I wanted to keep my eyes open! Since we were visiting over Spring Break, we opted to stay at the nearby Hard Rock Hotel so that we could the Express Passes, and we were so glad we did. We waited at most about 30 minutes for the most popular rides while those without the passes were waiting 90 minutes or more. We spent a day at USF and a day at IOA and then went back to Universal for part of a third day for everyone to do their favorite rides again. Since we had Express Passes, we thought a day for each park was adequate. We loved the Harry Potter areas of each park, the attention to detail was fantastic. Unfortunately these are probably the most popular areas of both parks and were packed with people during our visit. We would like to return during a less busy time of year to explore them a bit further. We really enjoyed the Hogwarts Express, but if you aren't a HP fan, you could easily skip the extra cost of the Park to Park option. We were only disappointed by a couple of things, one was the lack of healthy dining options. There was a couple of stands with fruit and a few salads available here and there, but otherwise it was all fast food (pizza, burgers, corn dogs, pretzels, chips, sweets) at the "quick service" places. We opted to bring in healthier food for lunches/snacks, water bottles to refill, and were so glad we did. The second was the cost of everything at the souvenir shops. As I mentioned, having never visited a large theme park before with our kids, we expected prices to be high, but we were disappointed to see just how much Universal charged for all of the merchandise. My kids wanted to buy a few small souvenirs with their own money and there really didn't seem to be much they could afford, you were hard pressed to find anything for under $20. There seemed to be plenty of people who were willing to pay the steep prices for food and merchandise, so I understand that's why they charge as much as they do. We found the parks to be very clean, and the employees friendly, we will definitely return sometime in the coming years.

As a surprise for my daughter, we drove the 2 hours from Sarasota to take in Universal Studios and especially the new Harry Potter world of Diagon Alley. I know we chose a busy day so we expected it. We took our time, enjoyed the queues and rode solo when we had to. Full size locker up front took my backpack so that I wasnt trying to jam it into the small lockers. We enjoyed our butter beer and even enjoyed old favorites like MIB and Transformers.  We went on the Dining plan and added a soda cup. It really worked out well all the way around. Dinner in Diagon Alley with Bangers and Mash and lunch in Springfield with Chicken and Waffles were both tasty.  We skipped the Mardi Gras parade and managed one more ride on Gringotts before the park closed at night. It was 50 minutes and so we opted to run the full queue instead of solo riding. It was well worth it. The story setup was very enjoyable.  Look folks, if you goto Universal over Spring Break and you fail to check the crowd boards ahead of going, it's on you. We did not use Express Passes and we tempered our expectations. It really is just planning ahead and knowing that this fairly small park is going to be busy.  Yes, it's very busy and no, you don't and probably shouldn't do both parks on one day on a Spring Break day. We enjoyed ourselves and got to do everything we wanted to do. It was a busy, expensive but completely enjoyable day.

I spent two days at Universal with my husband and seven-year old son. Two days was the perfect amount of time—we rode everything we wanted to ride.  We bought park-to-park tickets so we could take the Hogwarts Express train (we took the train twice-it’s a different experience in each direction).  Both of the park entrances (Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure) are at Citywalk. It only takes a few minutes to walk from one park entrance to the other. The parks are small compared to other theme parks like Disney. They’re laid out in a circle so they’re easy to navigate.  We stayed on property one night since express passes were included with our room, and we also had early entry to the park. We were very glad to have the express passes and early entry since it was peak season and wait times were long.  We loved the rides. They are different from other theme parks. Like Disney, there is a lot of attention to detail. The Wizarding World of Harry Potter is especially great.  Wait times for food varied. Restrooms are plentiful and I rarely had to wait for one. We found plenty of spots to sit when our feet were tired.  Some rides require that you put your belongings in a locker. Ride lockers are free. I took a small purse—the lockers are not big. My son got a Harry Potter wand and we were sure to get a short one so the box would fit in the lockers. (Wands come with or without magic; most styles are the same price.)  Before you enter Citywalk, you go through security. If you take a water taxi from a hotel, you go through security before getting on the water taxi. At the park entrances, you scan your ticket and scan a fingerprint.  There are lots of great tips online for visiting Universal.  My only complaint is the cost. With the express passes, it was almost $200 per person per day just for park tickets.

Spectacular experience as always. It is my second time to go & It felt like the first time. Same comment as in all other parks the queues are abnormally long and the hours spent in line are horrendous. Other than that everything is perfect & my favorite park in Orlando by far. All the rides have a theme or a story which makes it way more interesting than a basic theme park. I personally loved the hulk, rock it roller coaster, Harry Potter, & the mummy.

Our 3rd visit as parents to Orlando- and with kids who are now older- this was the first time we spent more days at Universal than the other big theme park in the area. My daughters who are big H. Potter fans and myself- who is not- were blown away by the harry potter related attractions. Get the park-to-park just to ride the potter train. The castle looks like the real thing.  Sure- the lines are long- but only for a handful of the really busy rides- harry potter, hulk, rockit, mummy- about 60 min plus. But for a majority - 30-40 min. Depends on time of day. But, we had a good group with my kids and nephews- so time flew.  King kong was a disappointment- don't waste your time in line there- Really short.a few glitches- waiting to move from one section of the ride to another- the screens power down and it is just half a minute of quiet and silence.  Friendly park employees- one of them was cheering on my young son doing the rock climbing- and even bought him an ice-cream when he finished!!!  We caught the mardi gras parades by pure chance on 2 nights- so much fun.  Regarding the smoking- The smoking areas are a joke- right off the main walking locations- depending on the wind you could walk straight into a cloud of smoke. In one area- near the voyage of sindbad- the stroller parking and the smoking zone are right next to each other- I had to take a double look thinking it was some kind of joke. I caught one person smoking outside in the main areas- but she was shut down quickly when I complained to a park employee. Why not make the entire park smoke free?- but for this issue- would have given 5 stars.  Overall positive- would definitely visit again.

There will be plenty of other reviews explaining all the attractions, so let me try here to do something different.  First all all: the rides are all great. Universal went all in on the 4D experience, which means you'll see a lot of 3D (like) movies during which you're shaken around in your seat to make the experience more lively. Universal excels at this. The newer the attraction, the more spectacular the effects. But that does not mean that older attractions are not boatloads of fun either. The Transformers effects are the most immersive. The Harry Potter rides are the most magic. The Simpsons and Spiderman are the most fun. And do not overlook the Blues Brothers show - one of the longest running in the park.  Second, the fast-pass. I am no fan of the whole idea, but it exists so here we go. The fastpass allows you to pass most of the lines. A day was plenty of time in either park (we visited during Spring Break in March). Plenty of time to do every ride we wanted and some multiple times. Cool. It is worth noting that if you stay in a Universal hotel, your room key doubles as a fast-pass, and that you can really walk from the hotel to the park in 10 minutes, eliminating the need for a rental car and parking fees. It's still very expensive, so you'll have to do the math on whether it's worth it. It's worth noting that tricks that you can find online about the variations in the wait times during the day play out pretty well. Come early and go for the popular (Harry Potter) rides first. Lines are shorter during lunch and parades. A lot of people poop out towards the end of the long days.  Having said that, here are some improvement points for Universal.  First, it appears that Universal ordered most rides assuming that all visitors are under 6'2" and 200 lbs. That (rightfully) pissed of a lot of tall and fat people, and they wiggled in some larger seating, but as a 6'8" adult, I still didn't fit in the Mummy ride, and while I fit, I was not comfortable riding the Hulk. So, if you're on the taller or wider side, be aware: you will be squished. However, staff will accommodate you as much as they can. Most rides have one row of slightly larger seats and in some rides they'll give you two seats when you point out the obvious. We found staff very accommodating, even though they did shove us in the front row of the Jurassic Park ride and drenched us ;-) An unrelated tip is to avoid a backpack if you can. You can not ride certain rides with one. Wear cargo pants and shove a bottle of water in there that you refill at the water fountains.  Second, the food. We could see Universal is trying with the quality, but most meals remain the standard American staples of fried stuff with cheese with no veggies in sight. The portions are way too large. No one needs three of those meals a day. What is needed is small on-the-go snacks and meals. There is is copy King's Cross station, so go to actual King's Cross station in London and see what they offer train riders in the UK and offer that to your visitors. Fresh simple sandwiches. Fruit cups. Simple healthier snacks. Smaller snacks. Not all meals have to be supersized. Especially considering my point above.  Third, where are the female heroes? Harry Potter, Spiderman, Jimmy Fallon, Popeye, Hagar, Poseidon. Are all heroes white men? Sure the Minions and Simpsons are yellow, but in reality, the only non-white heroes are the Hulk, the Men in Black and Marylin Monroe. You can do better Universal, especially since we did note that your staff is very diverse, including some handicapped people, which was great to see.  And the same commentary goes for Islands of Adventure park.

I've been to Universal many times but I hadn't been in a few years so my mom and I took a quick down to Orlando to see the new attractions that Universal put in (Harry Potter).  I am glad we did!! We had a lot of fun but I was a little disappointed about a few things. Universal got rid of Jaws, Back to the Future, and the Dueling Dragons roller coaster. I get that rides get old and people do not know the movies anymore but Jaws!!! Even if you don't know the movie who isn't afraid of a giant shark popping up all around!!  Besides being bummed about those rides, the other rides were fun! I really enjoyed both the Harry Potter locations! It is amazing how feel like you're in a whole other world when you step into those locations!  I definitely want to go back but I will be waiting util 2019 when there a few new rides that they are putting in.  Also, the prices are so expensive! I wish they were a little more affordable so that I could go more often!!!  Also, if you have AAA I would bring your card because you get discounts on food and merchandise!

I had never been to the parks before, as I was a Disney fan. However, the Park was amazing. The Simpson area was wonderful, the rides were great, and the only issue we had is that we didn’t get to ride the Transformers ride because it was closed due to an issue. But that was just us not wanting to wait for it to fix. The staff was mostly interested in talking with each other and several times there were supervisors chastising them to interact with the guests. That didn’t bother me though, so it still gets full stars from me!

For adults Universal is soooo much better than Disney. So many more adults rides. What else is nice is as you walk to each ride or adventure there's entertainment in the street. I love the Mardi gras parade at night and there is always big entertainment for concerts.

We spent a day at Universal Studios and had a fantastic time. We went on the Transformers, Men in Black, The Simpsons and Escape from the Gringotts and had a blast. We never realized it was spring break and the park was extremely busy with lineups between 90 to 120 minutes but well worth the wait. Lots of eating options, parking was a breeze and great weather.

There are hundreds of ways to go about the park, but after today, here are some tips on what worked for us, or what didnt: 1. If you can do it, do get the past pass, it is worth every penny, we never stood in line for more than 10 minutes. 2. Do bring munchies, it helps a lot. 3. Dont rush in the morning. Most of us rushed in the morning, and rushed to go everywhere, and by 3 pm we were pretty much done... Take it easy, enjoy the park, the walk, the scenery.. 4. Sunblock, hats, hidration... Must! 5. Expect park food, lots of pizza, burgers, hotdogs, nuggets, etc...  We did go in peak season, and you can just do the park in one day, and enjoy it, without rushing.  The rides are incredible... Dont miss them.

Price was a little high for the few rides to enjoy with older kids. But still really fun. Spend the money for Express passes if you can swing it, well worth it to ride all the rides multiple times. With the express passes we were able to ride all the rides at least two to three times in a single day. In fact if we would have known we would have only purchased a single day 2 park pass with express. After spending 6 hours at universal and riding some rides multiple times we rode the hog warts express to adventure island and had time to even ride a couple rides there before leaving.
This seemed like a bigger Six Flags to me. One exception was that it had longer lines than most amusement parks. I felt there was not that much to do for the cost, but Diagon Alley was fun.

Busy time during spring break. Harry potter world is excellent. Go early in the morning. Need park-to-park option to ride the Hogwarts train between parks. Each direction has different views and stories. During spring break, have the express ride option is very helpful to reduce waits. Would be worth staying at one of the Universal hotel to get free express passes

Ww had a amazing time at ALL THREE Universal Studios Orlando parks!! Volcano Bay was amazing, The ride HONU, was the best. The One I enjoyed the most was the Fearless wild river! Like going through the white water river. Has everything to think your on a fun Island. Then the park Island of Adventure was a blast from the Hulk, Kong, Spiderman to Harry Potter. Try the butter beer and eat at Three Broomsticks. We got a family platter of food thats fed all four of us with left overs. Universal Studios Orlando also had a Harry Potter that made you feel like you were there in the movie!I loves Men in Black, ET the ride and the Mummy was a BLAST!! We all stayed at Cabana Bay resort, loved this hotel. Will reveiw that hotel soon. If Your feeling over the Disney parks, them You must go to a growen up parks that Universal Studios Orlando has to offer. Now go have fun!!

My husband, daughters(11,13), and I visited USF in early March. We were not sure what to expect, as I was the only one who had visited before, and it was many years ago. Due to budget restraints we visited both Universal parks in one day. We arrived early and headed straight to Diagon Alley. We walked right on Escape from Gringotts and were able to see Olivanders before the crowd started to grow. This was the highlight of the park. It was amazingly detailed and an exciting start to the day. The ride was my favorite from both parks. We left Diagon Alley and circled around the park with a goal of returning to ride the Hogwarts Express to Islands of Adventure by early afternoon. Most of the family enjoyed the rest of the park. In my opinion there were a lot of rides that were exactly the same (motion simulators) with only the theme being different. By afternoon we did not have time to ride some of the larger attractions (Minions, Shrek, Rip a Ride Rockit, Transformers) due to wait time and our goal of visiting both parks. This may have shaped my opinion, but overall I was disappointed in the majority of the park. The rides were repetitive and the food subpar. I wish we would have just spent the day throughly exploring both Harry Potter worlds and avoided the rest of the parks. I did give a four star rating because the rest of my family seemed to enjoy the majority of the park more than I did, and also because Diagon Alley is worth a trip all on its own.

The Wizarding world of Harry Potter is way better than LA's. The dragon is sick. There's way more stuff to do so plan on going for more than one day. And get your tickets for less form tickettorides.com website.
The park is a joke and their guest service is even worse! Go to disney! Dont waste your money here. This is a waste of time and energy

A little busy because of spring break but we had great time. - arrive early (right when the park is open is ideal) - have your ticket print/ready to go (so you won't be in line to but/pick up, etc) - don't bring backpack or bags if you can help it (some rides required items to be lock in the free locker during the ride) so you can go directly to the ride - go to the ride you want to ride most so you won't miss it (for us it was harry potter escape from gringotts ride) - whenever possible, go to "single rider" line. You won't sit together with your party as they are filler seats...so you can save time (we did this to many popular rides and get to go twice back to back) - Do lunch early or late (avoiding the rush hour 12-1 pm) - stay for the night event (for us was the mardi gras parade)

Memories are always gonna be made here lets be honest I have had so many fab times here each is always amazing and always better than the last time I could spend my hole life there it would be amazing and so much fun the food is good for a theme park

Group of 5, kids aged 10 and 8. This park should take a day to get round and has plenty of rides for all the family.  Highlights were Harry Potter diagon alley which is really well done hidden behind what looks like a service entrance.  We enjoyed the 3D rides, transformers, minions, shrek, Simpson’s and nbc studios. One ward of warning the visual and audio assault can give you a headache if you go on them too often.  There is also live entertainment from the blues brothers which was good.  For older kids there is an mummy rollercoaster and the rip rocket coaster.  Great days entertainment but prepare yourself for noise

This park is set up as studio sets: 1. Harry Potter, Diagon Alley 2. Production Central: Transformers, Minions, Shrek etc. 3. New York: Jimmy Fallon, Revenge of the Mummy, Blues Brothers 4. San Francisco: Fast and The Furious (not yet open) 5. World Expo: Men in Black, Fear Factor Live 6. Springfield: The Simpsons and Twirl N' Hurl 7. Woody Woodpecker Kids zone 8. Hollywood: Horror Makeup Show  If you are a Potter fan, this is by far the best part of the park! The buildings, the visuals, and all the parts of the book that come to life before your eyes in the buildings and while you wait for rides are truly amazing! The shops have very creatively recreated shops from the book and food and merchandise brings the book's magical items described in the book to life as well! So much fun discovering.  Gringots bank was stunning inside and out. The giant dragon sitting atop the building breaths real pyrotechnics every 15min and will briefly roar to give you warning or time to prepare your cameras.  Word of caution: wizard wands are roughly $40 for non-working replicas, and about $54 for "optical interactive" capable wands, each! Also the wizard robes were roughly $115 each! Our kids, 7yo and 9yo really got tired of waiting in line for all the spots where their wands would perform "magic". However, no matter the temperature, they wanted to wear their robes and enjoyed the hidden want pocket inside their robes! Not sure how much use the robes will get back home.

If you have recently visited Disney, you may be disappointed with this park. For the cost and crowds, you will get a much better value at Disney. We paid $149 above the ticket price we paid for an express pass unlimited. This should have decreased wait times considerably, but apparently the number of passes sold is not limited. We still had to wait over an hour for the Harry Potter ride even with the express pass unlimited. Also, we stayed in a Universal resort and still had to pay to park at the resort. The only benefit to staying at the resort was a shuttle to the parks, and an extra hour at Harry Potter, which we were not big fans so it was not a big draw for us. Also, communication is poor; it was difficult to try and figure out how everything worked with the crowds, which the park cannot handle very well.The rules for what you can and cannot wear/take on rides is very inconsistent. For example, I was made to put my cell phone in a locker for a ride, yet 4 people in front of me had phones and were taking pictures throughout the line. This was our first trip to Universal Studios since 2005 and we missed many of the themed movie rides and demonstrations and shows they had at Universal Studios. Also, you can cover the park in a day...not a lot to do.The food is very expensive and all our meals were cold, hamburgers/fries were not even warm. Keep expectations low when visiting! Next time, we will probably go back to Disney.

Our family had a great time at the Universal parks. Although I have been to Universal a few times, it was my first time since they opened Diagon Alley. They put so much detail into everything. It is really impressive! I loved the Gringotts ride. I also love that the Hogwarts Express takes you from Diagon Alley at Universal to Hogsmeade at Islands of Adventure. The Mummy was also a really cool ride. We stayed at one of the Universal Resorts so our fast passes were included. It was definitely worth it! Universal’s fast pass system is so much better than Disney’s. There is no set time and you can go on as many rides as you like. Your wait time is cut down tremendously allowing you to go on more rides. I highly recommend getting fast passes.

Went here this week with wife, 2 daughters and grandson. Despit being one of the busiest days of the year for the Orlando parks, wait times were reasonable and the rides themselves were mostly very good (avoid Shrek, an unpleasant unwatchable waste of time). The Harry Potter city was fantastic and the ride was great. The ET ride is dated compared to the other CGI rides. The streets, a mashup of NYC, Chicago, LA and probably others was delightful. My 7 year old grandson enjoyed every experience, he couldn't get enough of the the magic wand tricks. So whats not to like? On the Harry Potter, the ET rides the waiting lines are mostly in a very confined and darkened place with minimal exit signs. If there were to be a fire or other incident egress would be extremely difficult. The other thing that struck me was there was an entertaining performance of the "Blues Brothers" on one street. Joining them was an instrumentalist and a woman blues singer, why was the (black) woman dressed as a maid?

We recently visited Universal Studios in Orlando and it was great! My family had a blast and the park employees were so friendly and helpful. Surprisingly, the prices for food were reasonable along with the souvenirs we purchased. We’re already planning another big trip for next Spring break! This place has thought of everything it’s amazing!

This place is awesome..both parks. Great roller coasters and water rides. Very friendly employees..love the food. They have 2 Harry Potter areas..one in each park that are wonderful. Lots to do not only inside the parks, but enjoy the miniature golf course and many restaurants on City Walk. I highly recommend.

My daughter loved the Minions ride and ET (which she rode many times). Shrek is a good option, but the 3D doesn't always work. I found it hard with the glasses and I don't normally have issues. The small kids area was mostly playgrounds. My sons loved the Rip Ride Rockit and did that multiple times. The Express pass made that possible during a busy time. The whole family enjoyed racking up point on Men In Black. One suggestion for The Simpsons, try to get on the lower levels. We rode the top once and it was hard to see the whole screen. Diagon Alley is amazing. The immersion is unbelievable but I did get uncomfortable with the crowds. I am not claustrophobic, it was just too many people for me. Overall, this is a great park.
New Jimmy Fallon ride was awesome. Harry Potter area and ride well worth the wait. Kids loved the mummy and transformer rides!

When I first went it had all the classics, Back to the future, Et, Twister rides and so on, some of these have now gone, but replaced by more up to date films, but it doesnt take away from the fun and games. its a cracking place, full of fun, yes be prepared to queue for a few hours for a ride, but they are superb rides and really do take you by the hand for a fun filled adventure.... roll on 2019 for the return
Enjoyed universal, OK - but id wait till kids are over 12 for here as most rides are for big kids.  Fastpass scheme is extortionate expensive. Not worth it.

We stayed at the park which is great. Get to go in 1 hour before opening. Get express pass, which made wait time for rides less than 5 minutes. Rides are excellent, my favorites are the water rides. Customer service was great. The only thing that was a disappoint was king kong ride, it should be a kiddy ride. Overall worth the time and money.

We just returned from celebrating my son's 7th birthday at Universal. Both he and my 9-year-old daughter agree it was a blast, my 40-something husband and I loved it, and my parents in their mid-70's had a wonderful time. It is truly a destination for everyone. Our favorite ride as a group is Men in Black. I think we rode it 10 times. On our very last ride, the operator had everyone in the queue shout out a "happy birthday" to my son, and we got our black jackets! What could be better?  I think between all of us we rode every ride, saw every show, and enjoyed every moment. Universal, thank you for a great vacation!!

...Oh my word it is fantastic!!!  I thought it was 'just another theme park', a nice spinny wheel with the Universal logo on, but oh no, I was definitely, certainly, wrong!  It's a special place, and we did the "Two Parks for One" thing. Not sure how much since my Dad paid.  Parking was great, but get there early so your car isn't in the sun all day on the top floor of the car park. That's a bummer. There's even airport style security, which is a massive bonus.  Even when it's busy and extremely hot, staff are still so lovely.  Best rides would be the Jimmy Fallon's Race Through New York, Transformers and The Simpsons.

I was there with my 9 year old daughter and wife for Spring Break. Prior to going, I told my daughter how magical this place was. I told her how you get to ride the movies and be a part of the movies. When we arrived, we were all very disappointed to find that most of the classic rides that made Universal famous, were gone. Now, every ride is simply a 3-d simulator. We went to ride the movies, not sit down and watch movies. Even my daughter was not impressed by the simulators. She watched videos of earthquake, jaws, king kong, twister.......it's shameful what has been done to this once amazing park. Disney has maintained its classic rides and added new ones.

Universal studios, Orlando presents a relaxed fun experience. During our visit we were able to ride on every attraction with less than a 15 minute wait. The only ride we choose not to ride was the roller coaster. The staff were very helpful when we asked questions about a particular attraction. We enjoyed a delicious lunch at Fisherman’s Wharf. The only negative factor in the pricing was the excessive fee to purchase an express pass. The high fees for parking, entrance and express pass make it very difficult for people with limited income to enjoy this facility.

After paying for our tickets on line we found out we paid $192 for express not tickets. After going to 3 different people we paid an additional fee of $54 to get in. We also paid for valet parking which we were told was $25, but when we left we were charged $45. The gentleman that helped me unload my chair gave us the price so we did not question it. If you go it is $25 for 2 hours, $45 if you stay longer...

We have been to Universal Studios many times and we are glad we went again. We went early in our vacation so the park wasn't as packed as we thought it might be later in the week so the lines weren't too bad and you could actually move without running into people! It was a beautiful day and we truly enjoyed our visit.

Universal Studios is a fun place for the entire family. Who doesn't like the minions and they're out in full force here -- both in their adventure and in a parade. Our whole family loves them from Grandpa on down. Lots of other fun things to see and do here as well. How about a ride through the jungle with King Kong lurking about? Or maybe you want to see how Shrek met and married Fiona. Again, lots of things for everyone to see and do here including a wild water ride.

They often get new rides when we go every few years but still love going on the originals like ET! Oct was a great time to go with hardly any queues and good weather, hardly any rain and still hot. Only downside is the cost and quality of food

We were there on a two day two park ticket. We added a one day express pass which was definitely worth the extra cost. The rides were great, but a bit much for my wife - she got nauseated in the Harry Potter ones. The food was relatively inexpensive compared to what we expected. We were also impressed by how much was new compared to ten years earlier.

Tips 1: don't pay for fast pass. Go on the single rider lines.  Tip 2: go around park anti- clockwise - Much quicker if in early.  Tip 3: mornings much faster as are weekdays.  Tip 4: online tickets cheaper.  Tip 5: bring some light snacks with you - food average and expensive.

Took my fiancé here as a portion of his birthday getaway. We had the express passes that made a TON of difference. We were able to navigate the park and ride EVERY ride during one day. It really makes a difference when you wait 15 minutes vs 1 hour. It is a bit pricey but it’s worth it in my opinion. We also had the food passes and that was also a great buy, one entree with drink and snack. We were joined by some friends which made it even better. It was nice to let loose, ride the rides, and just have fun. Universal will never get old and always be a good time.

I’ve come to this place since a child every year until now. The theme park has amazing scenery and really feels like you’re somewhere special. The rides are amazing although I wish they still had the jaws ride as it was my favourite. Can be fairly expensive but if you get there early enough you do gets your monies worth! Can’t wait to go back

This is my second trip to Orlando and to both Universal and Disney, both times with my significant other and no kids.  Attraction wise I wouldn't necessarily rate one above the other as it depends on your taste, but I can definitely say that Disney has better staff/cast member. I will give you 3 incidents that I can distinctly remember which put a dent on our days at Universal, which was why I gave this 4 stars and Disney 5.  It's a little long so TL:DR Disney has by far better staff/cast member. As if Universal has lower customer service standards.  1. My wife waited in line for a soft serve ice cream with 5 people in front of her. It was 20 minutes later that she received her soft serve. The 5 people in front of her each only got one soft serve and I had no idea what took so long. The server lady would frequently disappear into the back doing god-knows-what, and really look like she doesn't want to be there serving ice cream, which I guess explains the slow service (but doesn't excuse it).  2. We bought a butter beer and made our way to the Horror Makeup show. I will tell you first that the show is good and not to be missed. Before we made it into the theatre, the old lady in front of the theatre wiggled her index finger and stopped my wife, saying she can't bring the butter beer inside. Okay, I get it, it's an open container and you don't want us spilling it inside; I understand. I asked if we can put it on the counter and just retrieve it after the show. The lady said no, and told us just to put it on the street floor outside the theatre. I don't know how you feel about putting your open container drink on the street floor unattended for an extended period of time, but we didn't feel it was safe. So we either had to chug it down on the spot or toss it, instead of putting it on the counter with no danger of the drink being spilled. By far the most inflexible staff I've met in the parks.  3. Waited in line to order our food at Leaky Couldron (food is not that great, don't go). There was no one there or organize the line, guessing because it's half hour before park close at 7pm, so there were individual lines for each counter. When it's our turn, the staff told us her register is closed and told us to line up at the register to our right where there's someone else standing behind. Well ok, not a big deal since the register just finished serving someone. We got to that register, and a minute later the lady behind the counter finally stopped what she was doing, and told us to go to another register which are serving someone because hers was closed too. We got to that third register only have it close too. We eventually got served by the first register and the first lady who told us to go elsewhere. What the fudge. We are one of those annoying customer who stepped in after closing too. It was only 6:30.  I guess the above incidents would be business as usual for other theme parks too, but I've been spoiled by Disney and had high expectations. So 4 stars instead of 5.

We love Universal, however, the suggestions I have is for 1) the security area.... They need distinct lines for the screening like at the airport( it was just a free for all) 2) Will Call Area.... They have kiosks to pick up tickets - but if they don't work(like for us) we were told that someone was helping us next.. However, when it was our turn - they took someone else and told us to get in a line... They should have just told us to get in line in the first place. 3) getting into the park... If the tickets say ID required - They should have someone before the line or a sign that tells people to get out their ID... It became a bottleneck due to people that didn't have id out. The rides were amazing and we only waited 15 minutes max for any ride.

If you like amusement parks and roller coasters - you will love this place. I only went for the Harry Potter World which was awesome but remember that only half the HP World is in Universal - the other half is at Islands of Adventure. You can see both sides if you do one park one day, and the next park the next day. If you want to enjoy the Hogwarts Express you need to purchase a park-hopper pass. Another way for Universal to take your money.

Had a ball at Universal studios.  Rides were fun. Don’t let the crowds put you off especially as you arrive at the first security check point.  My tip is to ride solo where you can and don’t purchase the fast pass before you go. You can purchase it on the day if needed from most of the ride gift shops.  You need to be moving to see it all and ride the rides you want and while you could do both parks on one day I would think to enjoy them allow a day at each of you can.  Heaps of fun for teenagers and their parents!!!

I travel the world riding roller coasters and theme parks. There are few places on earth I would rather be than at an amusement or theme park...and I've been to all of the major parks in the US and many around the world. Universal Studios Florida is my happy place and my favorite park of all!  First of all, don't compare Universal Studios Florida to any of the Disney World parks. They are two different resorts that are catering to two different customer bases. Disney goes after the families with kids ages 12 and under, whereas Universal targets families with teenagers. Disney is a resort filled with attractions that the entire family can ride together; Universal goes for more "thrilling" attractions. There are rides and attractions for little kids, senior adults, and people who can't handle riding rides...HOWEVER, their offerings for these demographics are a little on the weak side as of the time of this writing (May, 2018). Don't panic! Comcast (parent company of NBCUniversal...the owner of Universal Parks and Resorts) is shelling out BILLIONS of dollars on their US theme parks. Universal Orlando Resort (where Universal Studios Florida is located) is building major new attractions annually, along with its sister park, Islands of Adventure. Family attractions designed for all-ages are opening, and major new family attractions are on the way. Universal REALLY wants to take the fight to Disney and they are developing their Orlando and Hollywood properties in ways never seen before!  Disney fills their parks with attractions, meet-n-greets, parades and shows from their content. If you want to meet Mickey Mouse, Buzz Lightyear from "Toy Story," Anna and Elsa from "Frozen," or characters from the Star Wars universe, that's what you'll find at their parks. Universal reaches into their movies for experiences too...but you'll also find third-party characters and IPs from movies/TV shows that they didn't produce. Harry Potter is one of their biggest draws and The Wizarding World of Harry Potter: Diagon Alley "land" situated in USF is utterly amazing. The detail and design of the land will genuinely make you feel like you are IN the Wizarding World with Harry and the gang! There is a small "Springfield" section themed to the legendary Fox TV series, "The Simpsons" featuring a 3D simulator ride, numerous food and beverage locations and some limited retail and carnival game options. Their KidZone "land" for children is rumored to be closing in the near future to make way for a new land themed to the world of Nintendo video games. New family attractions themed to The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon (a 3D simulator) and The Fast and the Furious (a family ride) have opened over the past year. Thrills can be had with "Revenge of the Mummy: The Ride" (an indoor roller coaster), "Transformers: The Ride - 3D" (an aggressive 3D dark ride using the same ride system as the AMAZING "Spider-Man" attraction in Islands of Adventure), and the "Hollywood Rip, Ride, Rockit" outdoor roller coaster. Character encounters/experiences and parades are located all over the park. Exciting new shows and rides are on their way over the next few years. It's an exciting time to be visiting Universal!  While a day at Universal Studios isn't cheap, I feel that you get better value for your money than you do a day at Disney. Disney charges you for EVERYTHING and each year, they find a way to make you pay for something that has always been free. Universal wants as much of your money as they can get too...HOWEVER, they still give you more "bang for your buck" than Disney does. Spend a few days at Disney World, then go spend 2 days at Universal Orlando Resort and you'll see what I mean.  If I have one major gripe about Universal Studios Florida, it's that their ride offerings are far too reliant on watching video screens and wearing 3D glasses. At least half of their major ride experiences are in 3D, whether you are wearing 3D glasses or experiencing "glasses-free 3D technology" like you do in the new-for-2018 "Fast and Furious Supercharged" ride, it gets to be a little overkill watching screens all day long...especially if you suffer from motion sickness easily. Happily, new screen-free and 3D-free attractions are in the pipeline and will be rolling out over the next several years.  If you're a Harry Potter fan, a visit to Universal Orlando Resort is a no-brainer. With major Potter lands in both Islands of Adventure (Hogsmeade) and Universal Studios Florida (Diagon Alley, with an actual Hogwarts Express train ride to connect the two park lands seamlessly), the magic of Potter is alive and well. If you have very young children or your party consists of people who can't handle 3D rides (or rides in general), you may want to hold off on a visit to Universal until you can attend with people who will enjoy the rides.  Highly, HIGHLY recommended. It's my favorite place on Earth!!!

I’ve just finished an 11 day holiday in Orlando and for some unknown reason I had placed the Universal parks as inferior to the Disney offerings. How wrong I was.  We did the four Disney parks first and they were good fun. But I realised that a lot of the attractions were the same as I saw when visiting 20 years ago. Yes there are new additions but they seem to suffer very long lines and I’m not spending 3 hours in a queue.  We then went to Universal Studios/Islands of Adventure we were blown away. Why? A number of reasons.  Line length. At Disney we got used to long lines or missing out on attractions we were not prepared to devote 2+ hours waiting, especially considering how important the precious time we have in these parks when considering the cost to get in there.. At Universal we didn’t see any lines of that length.  Attractions quality. WOW. They are brilliant at Universal. They seem a lot newer and therefore are more high-tech. By combining 3D and clever cars going through amazing scenes you come out buzzing and wondering just how they did that. And there are several rides of this quality. And they have proper rollercoasters which are amazing to go on.  And that’s before mentioning Harry Potter. This area is the best of anything in the Orlando region. In the Universal Studios Park, the scenery of London was breathtaking and King’s Cross station, which in the books is the starting point of Hogwarts Express, was so realistic. There is a fantastic ride here as well.  The excitement continues when boarding the Hogwarts Express itself, a real steaming beast pulling a long train to the Islands of Adventure Park where you arrive at Hogsmeade, again an amazing reproduction of the town in the books. And the best of all is the castle like Hogwarts school which sits high above the ground on artificial hill inside of which is the most amazing ride of them all. Again based upon Harry Potter, it simply is breathtaking.  Universal also has a better buzz around the parks, good topical music, and lots of mainstream shops such as Starbucks etc.  So from my point of view there is only one place to go in Orlando, and that is the Universal parks and if you have more spare time only then go to the Disney parks.
