This review is for you if you qualify for one or more of the following (otherwise don’t waste your time and move along to the next review): - Have a (mild/moderate) fear of enclosed space (claustrophobia) - Have a (mild/moderate) fear of being trapped/scared (agoraphobia) - Hate roller coasters in general (big drops, speed, spinning, etc.) .. BUT you do appreciate a good theme park ambience and/or want to have fun with your thrill-loving family.  Know that I am all of the above. Please don’t judge, this review is meant to be helpful!! Again, if you’re not interested, just ignore it !  THE PARK First of all, let me say that, even if you don't try any ride, this theme park is, by itself, SUPER FUN !  It is absolutely gorgeous and beautifully themed, the park being separated in zones (New York, San Francisco, Hollywood, Production Central, Diagon Alley/Harry Potter, World Expo/Men In Black, Springfield/Simpsons, Woody Woodpecker). Universal does have attention to detail, because each zone really resembles the real or fictional place that it is based upon. As Dr Hammond phrased it, they "spared no expense".  Here is a list of activities that EVERYONE can enjoy at Universal (no stress involved):  - Meet famous people/characters and take pictures with them.They are super friendly and fun to meet.  - Attend shows.  - Watch the parade. I LOVED the parade, more that I thought I would. It's small compared to Disney's, but it stops twice and when it stops, everyone involved in the parade will jump, dance and smile, and wave to the kids. They are talented dancers and they put out a great show ! Look at the map and locate the places where the parade stops, I would recommend standing there as to not miss the dance.  - Explore every nook and cranny in the whole Harry Potter area.  - Shopping ! Shopping ! Shopping !  - Looking for a place to eat / eating. The Simpsons area has lots of Simpson-themed food like the famous Krusty Burger and Duff Beer.  - Take pictures with the fun props (look for Jaws in the San Francisco Area).  In short, you can have PLENTY of fun in the park even if you don’t. ride. a. single. ride.  This being said, you might want to try a few rides.. here are the rides I tried and my honest anxious person's review about them !!  HOGWART'S EXPRESS - From Diagon Alley to Hogwart This ride LOOKS like a walk in the park. I looked it up on the Internet beforehand, and it is described as a nice train ride, fit for anyone. If you are reading this review, then you are either claustrophobic, or agoraphobic, or hate anything roller-coaster related, then hear this: This is *not* a nice train ride. But you can probably talk yourself through it (as I did). Again, it depends of your level of claustrophobia. I would totally recommend you go watch the ride POV video on youtube before riding anything. Then you can be the judge and decide whether or not you feel like you can do it.  At first, the queuing area is a large (covered) open space, but the line zig-zags for a long time, so if it's VERY crowded and you get stuck in the middle of it all, you will probably feel trapped in the crowd. When I visited, the crowds were low so I just walked through the zig-zags.  After that open-space area, there are stairs, and at the top of the stairs there is a corridor and a nice photo opportunity where it looks like people disappear through the wall. After that part, the passage gets quite narrow, and people have to walk one behind the other, single file. The passage is made of brick walls and makes a few turns - the line sometimes slows down/stops. Know that it doesn't last long. You emerge onto the platform and it's a big open space area again.  Then you board the train. You are guided into a train cabin (the staff is super nice, by the way). The cabin holds 8 people, so depending of your party size you might be seated with strangers. Also the cabin is small, so you are very close to your neighbors, and the lights are dimmed. A team member comes to close the door and LOCKS IT (help!). The door has to be locked for the ride to work properly - no spoilers. The team member tells you that in case of an emergency, there is a big red button to unlock the door.  The train starts moving (you do feel the movement) but there are no windows - there is a fake window that is in fact a screen. It can be a little disorienting but not much (the train makes no drops nor turns - not that I could feel anyway).  The ride is only a few minutes long and it's fun, and the special effects are great. There is a moment with ominous music and a tiny jump scare.  MINIONS MAYHEM When I was there, the queue was super short, I got into Gru's house after just a few seconds wait, outside the house. The house itself has a very high ceiling. A team member directs you towards a numbered line. There is a stationary option, you should mention it to the team member and follow the 'S' line, if you are interested. While you are in line you watch a funny intro video, and depending of the moment you got in line, you might be stuck there for a few minutes.  After the video, doors open automatically and all lines move towards the next room. This room has a lower ceiling, is kinda dark and is very crammed. Team members will ask everyone to move forward and every inch of space is occupied. The doors will close behind you. There are no windows. There is a giant screen with, again, a super fun pre-show video of Gru and his minions. At some point there is a loud alarm sound.  Then the doors open automatically and you enter the last room. This one is like a movie theater, the ceilings are high, the room is large. The room is filled with ‘vehicles’, each seating about 4 persons. The stationary seating is at the front. Basically, stationary seating is a long wooden bench - the same as watching a movie but you’re sitting at the front. During the ride, the whole room is dark. For the moving seats, there is a safety restraint on your lap. A team member will ask if everybody feels comfortable before starting the ride. That’s a nice gesture.  The moving seats will jerk you around a bit, but they stay in the same spot (they are seats, not vehicles). According to the internet, Minions Mayhem is like the entry-level simulator, so it must be the least jerky. I felt like the ride was much less stress-inducing than the pre-show.  TRANSFORMERS THE RIDE This one is a big step-up from Minions, because you sit in a moving vehicle (a transformer named Evac). Evac is shaped like a box with the left and right panels (i.e. the doors) being higher than the front panel. When you are seated, you see in front of you, but you are blind on the sides. If for any reason you don’t feel like looking at the screen, you can only look down towards the floor - then again, it is hard to not see the screen, as it is so overwhelmingly big. There is a lap bar, which you lower by yourself with the help of the other persons on your seat (4 persons per seat).  Once again, I recommend you watch the POV on Youtube before riding. But beware, the ride is much jerkier than it looks on the videos. If I remember correctly, there are special effects like heat and wind. And the ride is long: about 4 minutes. I have nothing to say about the queue, the crowds were low and it went by very fast.  This ride is super entertaining and a fun experience. I did not regret riding it even though I had to talk myself through it (again, lol).  FAST AND FURIOUS SUPERCHARGED This ride has NO LAP BAR and NO SEATBELT, yeah ! The queuing area is large and open, there are cars on display, it’s a cool and relaxed environment. Stress-free. Until you reach the pre-shows (oh no). BOTH pre-shows take place in a closed, crammed room with automatically-opening doors. The pre-shows are narrated by a person, not just a TV screen like Minions.  The ride takes place in a moving bus-like vehicle. There is a TV screen aboard, the bus is large, fits a lot of people (maybe a few rows of 6 persons each ?) and has windows on both sides, allowing you to see the giant screens where the action takes places. There is a party, and a car chase going on, explosions and guns and missiles ! A lot of action going on on the screens, but it’s only simulated speed - the bus itself does not move fast. It does get jerky at times, but not too much, and the ride is short.  That’s it, I haven’t tried any more rides. There’s plenty of fun to be had at Universal Studios, even if you despise roller coasters. I had a blast and would go back anytime !

I find all Universal parks worth the visit when in Orlando. This park was great and we had fantastic weather for it. Whether you love Minions, Harry Potter or Fast and Furious you will be happy. It is fun for all the family, I wouldn't recommend the 3D rides to Motion Sickness sufferers unless you find some medication that helps it. I suffer and had taken tablets for this park, I still avoided The Simpsons ride as this didn't go down well with me in Hollywood Universal. Diagon Alley is a must here, watch the flames come from the dragon mounted on top of Gringotts Bank! On that subject, Escape from Gringotts is a great ride, alongside Men in Black, Fast and Furious (this is the same as the one in California) but still worth it! The Mummy and Transformers are also great rides. Race through New York with Jimmy Fallon is a great 3D ride i recommend also. Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit coaster is fantastic, you get to choose a song to have playing in your ears throughout the ride. They are strict with belongings on this one, so much so that you have to go through metal detectors AFTER putting items in a locker so you wont get away with a camera/phone etc. The locker is free for this ride. Whilst on the subject of belongings, these are checked through scanners upon entry into Universal resort as well as walking through metal detectors so be prepared for that upon entry if you have anything you shouldn't. Bottled water is allowed, with regards to snacks I would check their website. There is plenty of food choices within the park, and of course you can leave to go back to City Walk if there is something there you would prefer. Entry to both Universal parks requires a short walk through City Walk so you can see what is on offer for the evenings.

Nothing what we imagined. Purchased tickets online just to find out that they require upgrade because it’s Saturday. Some rides like Mummy was awesome but some of them like “fast and furious” was not worth at all. One time visit - check.

VERY DISAPPOINTING!!!!!! Horrible ride....this review does not reflect the park at all, for all the other rides are great. We have Premier Annual Passes, and frequent Universal almost every major holiday and long weekend.  I was at the park for Gradventure (middle schools’ night). I was with a huge group of teachers and a bunch of teens. You wait in line in a “garage”, wait some more amongst cool music and movie set decor, then you think you’ve gotten somewhere, and then you are in a room where an actor has you watch a memorial homage about how we are now all “family”. It’s to make you feel ‘part of the team’. Then you are shuffled into ANOTHER ROOM to hear another actor have an imaginary conversation with the actors. At this point we were all like OK....😕then the doors open to (wait for it) another EXTENSIVE line. This line was slowwwwwwwww. 😮😮😮😮  It’s finally time and like everyone who has not ridden is shocked to see it’s a ‘party bus’. Now at this pt everyone thinks it’s going to be like Transformers or Test Track (Epcot). Nope! It starts with you watching a screen of the actor booty shaking at a club of strippers. Then the screen becomes a parking garage. Of course the bus is hydraulically moving. There’s a blast of the fakest exhaust busting your ear drum and Vin Diesel appears. Mind you the visual presentation of the actors looks soooo fake!!!!! It’s all computer generated. Finally, you are on a high speed chase watching these actors jump from cars, grabbing a helicopter in mid air (no BS), and performing maneuvers that defy Newton’s Laws of Physics!  You are pretty much watching a movie while the bus moves around, wind blows at ur face, and water sprays you!  At the end all the people did a WTF and the teens all said this sucked. Not one person clapped, whooped, or cheered.....  I hope this review was informative for you 😉

This was our first time ever to Universal Orlando. We have been to Busch Gardens, SeaWorld etc....This was by far our best theme park visit ever! Be sure to check out the Horror Makeup show. It’s definitely a best kept secret! Best ride: The Mummy. Diagon Alley was my favorite area but I’m a Harry Potter Fangirl.

From the parking, to the gate and with locker rentals, it's a mess. Super long wait times and the rides close if it rains even a bit. Lots of in park carnival games (that cost). Not impressed and won't be back.

There are lots of water fountains located near the restrooms/toilets. We are from the UK so took diluting juice with us to add to the water.  2nd tip - I wasn't too impressed with the early park entry an hour early. Practically the only ride open was Harry Potter so everyone was heading there. When we got there, the queue was about 30 mins. Baring in mind we all had express passes, it was actually quicker to wait until the main park was open and go anytime during the day and we never waited more than 15 mins.  3rd tip - On your way out of Diagon Alley, stick to the left which is signposted as Exit. That was you can avoid the masses of people coming in through the main "wall" entrance.  4th tip - Definitely take advantage of the late park opening. Its an obvious one really but it means the queue's are less and its nice to walk around as it starts to get dark. Universal Studios doesn't open late often though so might not be an option.  5th tip - Use the Universal crowd calender before you plan your trip to make sure it's not going to be too busy when your there.  6th tip - If you're staying at a on site hotel, get any souvenirs delivered to your hotel room to save you having to carry them around the park. I'm sure as long as your not checking out for 2 days, its fine to do this.  When it comes to the rides, my kids loved the usual Harry Potter rides but also loved Jimmy Fallon which surprised me. It was actually really good so don't miss it out.  Other than that, the park was spotless and the staff were all great.

Universal tickets are always money well spent. The place is magical. Both parks have great attractions and plenty of space to lounge in the sun. City walk is fantastic for a bite to eat after a day in the parks. We never visited volcano bay, which was a shame, but for anyone visiting Orlando, ensure you do get tickets here as there isn’t a bad word I could say about the place.

What ever you do avoid the fast and furious ride. Without doubt the worst ride I have ever ridden. The que was more exciting than the ride. Biggest waste of time. I waited for this ride for 3 years when I first visited and I'm so disappointed

We originally were only going to do Universal Studios but ended up having time to also do Islands of Adventure and were able to upgrade at Guest Services at the discounted price. Of the 2 parks I would have to say I liked the layout and scenery of Islands of Adventure...but...Diagonal Alley was a must for me since I'm a Harry Potter fan. I recommend getting the unlimited drinks package which also comes with complimentary cup. They have character actors throughout the park and most of them you don't have long lines to wait like Magic Kingdom. The Men in Black guys called my husband Live Action Shaggy 😂. We missed the parade unfortunately. 1) Springfield: Home of the Simpsons was cool since my husband and I like that show. The Simpsons Ride made me a but motion sick. 2) Transformers 3D ride was my favorite ride at this park and did t male mme motion sick. 3) Hollywood Rip Ride Rocket I won't ride again. It jerked me around too much and I ended up with a splitting headache at the end of it. I've ridden a lot of roller coasters and this one was by far one of the roughest. 4) Diagon Alley. Talk with the Knight Bus conductor and and shrunken head they're fun to talk with. Go into the red telephone booth between Knight Bus and King's Cross for a message from the Ministry of Magic. As soon as you enter Diagonal Alley you're overwhelmed by how amazing this place is. I went into Gringott's, Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes, and a few of the other shops. Butter beer tasted just like a cream soda but I hear the frozen version is even better. I didn't go into Ollivanders because of the line but it was neat to see other people using their wands to do "magic spells" at select locations. I was lucky enough to catch the dragon breathing fire. We tried eating at Leaky Cauldron but again lines were too long. I could've spent all day at Diagonal Alley!

The place is wonderful! There are plenty of rides for the children . Please check you child’s height before entering rides because the safe doesn’t pay close attention. Bring drinks and snacks and sunscreen. The drinks can range for $6 a beverage , keep in mind food is pricy as well. You will get your moneys worth. We met backwards in the park and this cut down wait times by 30 mins. We went to both parks also keep in mind the land of Harry Potter will be most congested .

really worth the visit. We love the Minions simulator and the parade of all the children's characters. It is a quiet park but I felt lack of being better visually signposted, even having maps available.

To start off it's so nice especially in the night. The only negative is there is nothing but one little area near barney land for 2year olds. My 12 year old daughter definitely enjoyed it.

Love universal studios and iOS, both gòod parks. Great rides however, for me and the wife we found Islands of Adventure alot better. Some of the rides like ET need either replacing or updating but on the whole there is something for everyone. We love the CGI rides so liked the HP Escape from Gringotts, Revenge of the Mummy and Transformers to name a few.  As expected eating and drinking there can be expensive so make the most of the daily re-fillable mug option you can pay for and re-fill and drink a selection of cold drinks till your hearts content.  Expect the usual queues for rides however, we found that going first thin in the morning is best as the parks get busy towards lunchtime onwards. We had a blast at all 3 Universal parks. The boys had a blast. Simpson’s land and Jurassic Park were spot on! Harry Potter was everything I could have wanted! Great destination for tweens.

VIP Tour is the way to go one day and then on your own the next. The VIP tour gets you straight on the popular rides. The next day will be more leisurely because you are not stressing to get on everything and now you know way around better , can go on what you missed and repeat what you really want to repeat. We were there 4/29, 4/30 and 5/1 right after all the Spring Breaks ended. Not empty by any means but not overly busy.
if you like thrill rides then this is the park for you. Forgot how bad they beat you up..lol..still a fun place
Great park...very short lines  Almost everything is put you in front a big tv and shake you around.  Staff is friendly and good pricy eats.  Make sure buy the MUG

The park, overall, is clean and offers many great attractions for all ages. We decided to not go for the express pass option, which worked out great. I was pleased that the wait times for most attractions were never more than 30 minutes, with only a handful being more than that. I was also impressed with the Harry Potter attraction and and roller coaster. My only complaint, (which is why I gave a 4/5 rating) is this: Prior to getting in line for the Harry Potter roller coaster, you are required to place all bags/backpacks in a locker. A great option and the locker is free for the first hour BUT when I went to retrieve my items from the locker bin, there was a technical malfunction that made it so I couldn’t get my stuff out including drinks we had just bought. It took almost a full hour before tech support arrived and was able to get the lockers open. A huge disappointment. Our schedule got all screwed up and park staff who I talked to about this didn’t seem to care. They said this happens from time to time. If that’s the case, they really need someone who has a master key and can access the lockers. My advice is to be aware of this in the event that you’re on a tight schedule. Despite this, we had a really great day at Universal.

Of course you also have 1/2 of "The Wizarding World of Harry Potter" here with the "Escape from Gringotts" ride that is complete with Goblins at their desks as it is in the fist Harry Potter film (and book). In fact, the Goblins look eerily similar to those you see in the movie and so does the bank itself. Beware: The newest ride in this park is "Fast & Furious" which we found to be neither. Of all the rides and attractions we took in over the 2 days we were at Universal Studios, this one comes in last. I think they were expecting large crowds starting the day it opened which might explain why you walk forever to get to your bus-like vehicle you ride in but the day we attended you didn't need to use your "Express Pass": to get on in a reasonable timeframe. Honestly...the term "lame" comes to mind. Even the computer generated graphics were poor. I don't know what ride that replace but we both think Universal needs to either come up with something different. Our advice is to skip this one do "The Mummy" or "Shrek" or something else. Staff are great and the place itself is beautiful and very clean. All the attractions are great but i think our family favorite was Spiderman..WOW! We visited universal with our children in their 20’s and grandchildren aged 5 and 7. It was a great day the rides were really good loved the Harry Potter one and so did the kids. Had lunch in the Irish bar. I preferred this park to the magic kingdom rides were better didn’t have to queue so long. Really recommend

So, let's start with the positive. This park is awesome from an interactive experience kind of perspective. Yes, many of the attractions are glorified simulators, but they are really well designed and many of them have great scenery and props to view while standing in line.  And that's the drawback...the lines. Get express pass with an upper tier universal hotel, break down and buy one for an additional 500 dollars a day for a family of four (yes.. this is on top of the ticket price) or suffer the consequences if watching the 10 percent of people with express pass enjoy the park as you wait 1-3 hours per line. (even though the time estimates on the app or at the front of the line would list ridiculous estimates of 30-60 minutes. Do not trust the line wait times universal posts!)  So, unlike Disney, Universal has not figured out how to give priority to those with express pass WITHOUT making it miserable for the rest of the patrons.  Disney does two things much much better with their fast pass system. First, Disney makes them available to all. So, you can wait for some rides while having fast pass to others. You actually don't mind a long wait time or two because you know it all evens out during the day.  The second thing is that the attendants at Disney seem to merge the fast pass and regular lines with much more common sense than we observed at universal. Disney seemed to be more of a one to one ratio when you got to the merge. In many cases at universal, we would see 10:1 (let in 10 express pass holders in for every 1 commoner). What this results in is express pass holders riding a ride 5 times in 2 hours while you wait in line and watch the same people pass you over and over.  Believe me, I'm all for capitalis and don't bemoan universal for trying to make some extra dough or incentivize staying at their resorts, but just change the way you handle the merge and for heaven's sake, understand how to estimate wait times better so you are not off by an hour or more!

We purchased a 2 park one day pass with an unlimited express pass. First and foremost, the express pass was worth every cent! This was our third day in a row of parks, and I would highly recommend searching for another time of year to visit Orlando, if you love amusement parks. They are all packed. But, if you choose to visit in June, I highly recommend the express pass. We did not wait more than 15 min for any ride. This made a huge difference. It also allowed us to get through both parks in one day. The roller coasters were a blast. The big coaster in Island of Adventure, Rip Ride Rocket, was our favorite. We could have rode this ten times. The Hilulk was fun, but it was a bit jerky. We really liked the Transformer ride, the Mummy ride, and the Harry Potter ride in the castle.  Our only criticism is that there are a ton of simulations, and after a while, they all start to feel the same. It would be nice to throw in more variety. We were disappointed by the Fast and the Furious ride and King Kong. Both could have been really fun, but they were simply okay.  We also bought the dining pass with the unlimited drinks. That was worth it for us. However, it did get old carrying the cups around all day.  All in all, we had a lot of fun! We would go back!

We went in mid -June and it was not quite as busy as it normally is according to a park staff member. Lines were about 20 min on average so it wasnt bad, however Harry Potter world (on both sides of the park) was shoulder to shoulder with people, luckily we didnt spend a ton of time in either. Ate lunch inside the park (Flannigan’s) and it was not worth the $200 bill for fish and chips and a couple adult drinks. Dinner was no better, $100 for slices of pizza and powerades. So as a tip for others, go just outside the park to the boardwalk area (you pass it on the way in) and eat, more options and better prices. We learned this on the way out ( you can leave and re-enter w.no issues). All in all it was fun, but plan on dropping about $800-$1000 for a day if you have a family of 4 or more, including park tickets, food, water, drinks, etc. A little pricey for only a few thrill rides (Hulk was the best), and alot of walking. All the staff we ran into were very friendly and the park was clean.
Universal Studios caters for all ages and has one of the best rides, The RIP-Rocket. If you go on it then play ‘I will Survive’ by Gloria Gaynor, the song is so apt for the ride.
This was one of the most amazing places I have ever been to! I loved every ride and every experiance. I wish I had two days to cover it all properly

Great place to spend a couple of days! Lots of rides, shows and food! There is enough for all ages young and old! The Express passes are a little expensive but they are worth having. Look into the Universal hotels where the Express passes come with your room.

My wife and I have older children and had the chance to visit both of the parks while in Florida. We decided to make it a fun for just the 2 of us. I enjoy the City Walk area and the energy of the parks. While I enjoyed the great rides and experiences I could help but leave extremely disappointed in the lack of service and general lack of concern for the guest experience. This is one area Disney cannot be beat. From the painfully slow and disorganized line to get our tickets to the disinterested wait staff at the restaurants in the park, It made it a poor experience. The line to get our tickets took about an hour. When we finally got to the window it closed for the worker to go on break. We waited again for the window to be reopened. At multiple times we stopped to get food or drinks. It was rare anyone made eye contact with the customer or (for most interactions) didn't even stop there conversation with their coworker. Money was just taken and change placed on the counter without stopping a sentence. The crowning failure was when a worker on a Harry Potter ride pulled us out of line rudely because my wife had a small purse worn cross body. He ignored the families in from and behind us that had diaper bags and back packs, and rudely directed my wife to the lockers and then sternly walked me out of the line area (like a 3 year old) and told me to stay there until my wife got back. I asked for his name and he said Noah. When I repeated it back to him he said Noel. I guessed he was lying about his name. When I questioned him about pulling us out of line like he did he got very upset, raised his voice and yelled "DO YOU WANT TO SEE MY MANAGER". I remained calm and told him how he was acting I would handle it through Customer Service. After going back and forth with him yelling, another worker came up (I assume it was his manager). He screamed in front of everyone “this guy wants to talk to you.” By this point my wife returned. I told the other person that I would deal with this later. Noel/Noah stood in front of me and would not let us rejoin the line and repeated that we wanted to talk with the manager. I repeated my statement and had to physically shoulder by Noel/Noah for us to get back in line.  I tried to let it go, but finally decided to us the customer service link and sent an email regarding my experience since we spent the extra $125 per ticket for the express pass. In my complaint I asked for the money back for the express pass if their staff can just pull us at will. The week following out trip I get a voicemail that customer service reviewed my complaint and since I had used my express pass multiple times that day I obviously had enjoyed the pass so she would not refund my money. She said if I called her back we might be able to “work something out”.  If you are looking for great customer service, this is NOT the place to visit.

So much fun to go be a little kid again! The Wizarding World of Harry Potter is really cool. They do a great job of immersing you the Harry Potter world. The rides that are part regular ride/part roller coaster are done really well and so are all the "4D" rides. Lots of inside rides so there is still plenty to do when the daily thunderstorms roll in.

This is our third Universal and it was different and familiar at the same time This was a visit on the 2 July so busy but not too bad with a fast pass. Front of line is essential as the crowds swarm the likes of Minions and Harry Potter  We saw everything we wanted to and I enjoyed a cold beer at Duffs The parade was a bit short compared to Disney and to be honest I didn’t really think the characters were all that  Highlight is Harry Potter escape from Gringots which was excellently recreated from the film

Loved it i had since a long time. The workers are so friendly. The dices are crazy fun many different kind

We purchased a 14 day three park ticket prior to travel to give us flexible access to all three parks. However we could not visit Volcano Bay as on the three occasions we tried it was full to capacity. In these circumstances multi day ticket holders are not given priority and those with one day passes are. We were advised to be there for 9am to ensure admission which was not possible for us. If you want to visit Volcano Bay in the summer months you need to get to city walk early or are probably best getting a day pass for it. Queues for the popular rides in IoA and US were long and not helped by the sheer number of visitors admitted and closures due to rain. In 12/13 hours we spent at the parks over three days we managed a total of 15 attractions/rides which, despite getting a small refund, equated to about £49 for a family of four for each attraction what is expensive. That said there are lots of great things at Universal and the scenery and .effects on the rides are great. Buy the bottomless drink which is $16 for the first day then $8 for each additional day.

Second visit, loved that they have so many indoor attractions! We went for 7 days, some half days, others stayed all day. We had to visit during June/July, due to work and college visit schedules. So many positives, but a few negatives. We will definitely go back, but in the off season.  Large crowds, and rain every day, sometimes heavy. Outdoor rides close when lightning is within 8 miles of park. Ponchos are definitely a must (got ours at the dollar tree, they lasted all week!)  Food is pricey, but you must try the butter beer and salted caramel blondie ice cream at Florean Fortescue's! Amazing! Frozen butter beer, delish, we shared because, brain freeze! Bought the refillable popcorn bucket, kept us from chewing our hands off in hunger between meals, only $2.12 per refill and fed 4 of us. I gave it to someone else on our last day so I didn't have to carry it home...they had like 5 kids, I am sure they made good use out of it ;-)  Maybe Universal should limit the number of Express Passes per day? It seems like we waited a very long time even with them on every ride. I know it is summer, but then why not limit the number sold, so that you don't have a lot of angry people on line? It got to feel like it wasn't that special a deal to have them. You need them in the summer however, because with them was half the wait time of the regular lines. After 2 days of use (we stayed on property to get the passes for free), we did the single rider lines, which seemed faster. Being nearby (Hard Rock) was great because you get in park 1 hour early, but not all sections are open. The commute 'home' is also much easier staying on property. Hotel was nice, but pricey.  They allow you to bring snacks, so take advantage; load up on as many snacks as you can, it is worth it to carry a small backpack/drawstring, the free lockers outside of certain rides work great, and if you time it right, you can go to other rides without switching lockers and carrying back and forth. Lots of shady places to sit and eat your snacks.  Every stand will give you ice water, so just ask! Bringing your own is better though, because water there tastes weird, and you will have to wait in line for it.  I suggest getting a copy of the park map before you go and ask your family what they consider a priority for each day of your visit. It made for little arguing when we had a plan. Download the Universal app too, checking wait times made it easier for us to go to plan B if we needed to.

We booked the Tickets Online for a weekly Pass. 750 Dollars for 2 !!!! Arriving at the Entrance at .ca. 11.00h we were told our Tickets ( Printed out in Germany) we're not valid and we had to change them at Customer Service. We joined a Queue of app. 50 persons with identical problems. We (and the other persons had to wait in a zig-zag in the sun (no shade at all) at temperatures of 95 F. With these tickets we made our way to Hogwarts-express only to be told we can't use it as we had only Base-Tickets !! Then after queuing for 70 mins for the Gringotexpirience we had a 2!!! The good bits are great - Harry Potter, Simpson’s, Hulk rollercoaster, Jimmy Fallon, Fast and Furious. But there’s a lot of awful stuff too, so awful you’d think several Universal Vice Presidents should be sacked for failing to do their job. Amongst the worst ride is ET (embarrassingly purile), but it highlights a recurring theme at Universal where the rides have a common backstory - you the audience are here to help us save the planet / beat the baddies / solve the problem. This is risible nonsense driven by terrible script writing which simply undermines the ability to suspend disbelief. Universal has succeeded in turning everything into an episode of Dora the Explorer. And as for the parade in Universal Studios....I’ve seen better parades at a nursery school. 4 floats? You’ve got to be kidding. Come on, guys, you CAN do better than that. Food at theme parks never ceases to amaze, but its the same at Disney, Seaworld and Busch. How on earth can they make ‘Fast Food’ so slow, how can they make it taste so bad and how can they charge so much for such small portions? Three conundrums that turn an otherwise great day out into a mediocre and slightly disappointing experience. 25 years ago, Universal cost $33 to get in, car parking was free and the lines never more than 30 minutes. Now it’s $150, car parking is $22, some lines are 2-3 hours. Yes it’s fun but it’s just a money-making ripoff now. All pretence at anything else is long gone. Go, go once. Then spend your money on locally run Florida attractions next time.
GET THE PARK HOPPER PASS!! also get the express pass! Our day with the express pass was so much more relaxing and we were able to hit every ride in one day!

Loved the train to go from park to park. Universal is a favorite and the girls loved it as they had not been since they were little. Such a big change for them.

So I read different reviews about this ride. I even read that is was a party bus and somewhat like the king Kong ride. Suggestion, walk through and see all the good stuff then find and exit.

Spoke to supervisor and she listened to the recording and said that the representative did not quote me in Canadian dollars. I was super stoked to take my kids to Universal because of the variety of attractions it could offer my family, and it did not disappoint. There was something there for everyone and it was not overly crowded. We opted for a 2 day pass, which I would highly suggest 2-3 days to experience the park to park experience. We will definitely come back again.

Our family visited Orlando for a day at the park and while overall the experience was fantastic...on our first ride, the Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit Roller Coaster, our daughter's very strong (and expensive!) prescription glasses fell off of her face! With no expectation, we made a visit to lost and found at the end of the day only to discover that they were not there. We were advised to call in and check though as the areas around the rides are checked for lost articles when the park closes. After seeing all of the articles retrieved in the past that were shattered and damaged, displayed in the case as a warning to those needing lockers, we had little hope. I was also told that in the event they were located we would have to make a visit in person to pick them up. This would have been possible but not ideal as we live a couple of hours away.  On a whim I called customer service a few days later only to be greeted by Linda, who turned out to be our guardian angel of lost glasses!! Linda took a lot of time, expressed true understanding and concern for our situation and then proceeded to not only locate our daughters glasses, but then went the extra mile to have them sent home to us. Whoever up there that is listening...Linda deserves a pat on the back, an employee of the month nod, maybe even a raise! Our travel group included myself, my husband, and our three kids (ages 7, 5 and 2). My husband planned the entire trip through Costco travel (great deal, included hotel, airfare and 5-day passes to Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure). We all had fun, but with several hiccups along the way. We learned a lot, and I'm happy to pass along the following tips:  1. Arrive early. Parks opened at 9:00am, and there was already a line at the gate to get in. On our first day, we arrived at 10:30am and Hogsmeade Village was almost impassable. We arrived just after 9 the following day and made a beeline for Hogwarts castle - practically no line at all. My biggest pet peeve of both parks was the "rush" to get to everything. From the moment you parked your car, there seemed to be a mad dash for everyone to get into the park as quickly as possible. I'm not sure if this is a marketing scheme developed by the park itself, or the guests. Everyone always seemed to be in such a hurry to get to the next ride, which created longer lines and cranky kids.  2. Use the app. The Universal Studios Orlando Resort app will give you a full map of both parks, with wait times and/or weather delays for each ride. We were able to navigate our way through both parks and ride everything we wanted to with the help of this app.  3. Be prepared for rain showers. We learned to seek shelter as soon as we saw the dark clouds moving in. We would either head to a nearby shop, or get in line for one of the indoor attractions. We also brought emergency ponchos which helped a lot.  4. This park is not designed for little kids. While there are a few attractions for them in Dr. Seuss land and Curious George world, that's about it. Both parks are definitely designed for bigger kids.  5. Use the Child Swap! I don't know why more amusement parks don't have this feature (or maybe I have just been living under a rock). We had 3 little kids with us, which meant someone always had to sit out. The vast majority of the rides offered Child Swap where one parent could sit with the non-riders in a holding room while the other parent rode the ride with the other kids. Once the ride was finished, the non-riding parent could swap places and move to the front of the line. Some of the Child Swap holding rooms were equipped with TVs and changing areas for babies. Brilliant!  6. Seek out assistance from the cast members. They are AMAZING! We splurged and purchased the $50 interactive wands for our two boys, but were having trouble getting one of them to work. This very friendly witch approached us and suggested we take the wand to Olivander's and tell one of the assistants we needed wand repair (it's free!). We did just that - the assistant took it all very seriously, saying she would have the shopkeeper take a look - then returned it to us a few minutes later. We found the witch again and she helped us navigate through Diagon Alley with the interactive spells. Her name was Ivy and she was AMAZING. *Hint - be sure to ask a cast member about the secret spells!!  Along the same lines, the Superheroes are a must-see. They interact so well with the kids! We got to meet Captain America, Cyclops, Spiderman, and a few others. My absolutely favorite was Captain America. He got down on their level, took his time interacting with them, asking engaging questions. He was in no hurry to get them through the line. The whole thing only took a few minutes, but it did not feel rushed at all.  8. Have FUN!

Not sure how to properly organize a review of a trip to Universal Studios, so Ill just start with the weather:  Don’t go in the end of July. Unless you like bathing in your own sweat. If you do like that, then you’re sick, and Universal isn’t your cup of tea. Unless you are a devoted parent like me, then you’ll go anywhere/anytime to please your children.  So, with that out of the way, Universal was a great experience. We stayed on site at Loews Royal Pacific. The grounds are amazing. Pool is gorgeous, there is a beach with zero entry into the pool, and there are no less than 4 lifeguards on duty to give you a false sense of security.  Our kids (14, 12) said that the hotel reminded them of an all inclusive we frequent in Mexico. I agreed with them, except the all-inclusive part. For example, just yesterday, at the pool bar, I ordered a Jameson and Seven for me and a chardonnay for my wife, and it came to $24.00. The path to sobriety begins at theme park pools.  Anyways, I digress. The grounds are gorgeous. Unfortunately, as I stated before, July is a horrible time to visit Florida, as we had storms EVERY day, which led to the pool closing multiple times a day. Kind of a bummer when you pay a lot of money for the pools at your hotels.  Which leads me to getting to the actual parks. We opted for the park hopper, which used in conjunction with the “early entrance” is usually a good deal. However, you have a couple options to get to the parks from your hotel. You can walk 10-15 minutes. You can also take the complimentary boats which are much quicker, but also are subject to weather holds. Apparently there is also a shuttle?? However, none of the transportation options were explained to us when we checked in. We kind of just figured it out on our own. Which brings me to my main fault with Universal...  The employees just do not have the level of dedication that Disney employees do. We have been to Disney World/Land several times. We were spoiled by the level of attention that is offered there. There were also several moments that I thought “you wouldn’t see that at Disney”  I called for dinner reservations at one of the restaurants in City Walk. Apparently all calls to City Walk go through the City Walk operator. She was very rude and unprofessional. I called her out on her lack of politeness, and was promptly yelled at.  There was garbage and candy wrappers throughout both main parks  We rode the Hogwarts Express several times. There was always the standard safety presentation from the ride operator. On our last ride, the operator was obviously bothered by us and as the doors were closing to our compartment, she yelled, “there’s emergency unlock buttons in there somewhere”. End of briefing.  As we were leaving our room this morning, there was a large floor/carpet cleaner plugged in and charging, in the way of people walking, that was leaking fluid all over the floor. Nobody seemed to care.  Again, none of these are major, but...you wouldn’t see them at the other major park.  So, what does Universal do better? The rides. They have something for everyone. If you are the least bit interested in Harry Potter, this place is amazing. The attention to detail is incredible. Daigon Alley is impeccable. You really won’t believe your eyes. The main ride there is “Escape From Gringotts” which is a 4D masterpiece. If you have park hopper, you can then take the Hogwarts Express to Hogsmeade. Again, the detail is amazing. Definitely try the butterbeer.  Outside of Harry Potter, our favorite rides were Transformers, The Mummy, and the Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit roller coaster.  So, in summary, Universal does offer great entertainment, but they lack in customer service. If you have young children and you aren’t sure where to go? Do Disney. They still set the bar. If you have done Disney or have older kids, try Universal. The rides are geared towards an older crowd. Just don’t go in the end of July😉

Visited both parks (Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure), great fun with 2 teenagers. Here are some tips I wish I’d known ahead of the trip -  - I booked the 2-Park 2-Day ticket; I was originally wondering if I could fit both in to 1 day but in the end we really needed 2 days to do it justice  - You need to visit both parks to experience all of the Harry Potter world and rides, since it’s split across the 2 parks. We found riding the Hogwarts Express train from Island of Adventures had shorter queues than riding it from the Universal Studios Park  - I booked unlimited express fast pass, but since we had 2 days we could have probably done without the unlimited since we didn’t really repeat any rides on the same day given there is much to do and the queues still take a while (see below)  - The express pass was worth the money during peak periods if you can afford it but note we still waited between 10 and 45 minutes for rides, it’s not instant access  - Try not to take too many (or any) bags as on a lot of the rides you have to painfully find lockers available to store them ; lockers get very busy in peak times  - Car Parking - you can queue in the car for a while to pay; best to get in the left most lane as it’s quicker. Only pay for the premium parking if you want to keep the car out of the sun, otherwise I didn’t find it saved us much time at all

Universal Studios, Volcano Bay and Islands of Adventure are what you expect Entertaining parks with good rides, 4 out of 5. We got on all the rides without the express pass. I do not agree with the express pass system which is elitist. Those who are wealthier and can afford the extra $149 per day per park will pay and for everyone else who can’t afford it you just have to wait and explain to your kids why there are two lines. For this I would I would give Universal a 1 out of 5. A shameful system for a oral which should focus on family fun for all. This is system which is totally wrong. I have been to Disney World 3 times and this is something they do not do. Everyone is treated equally and entitled to the same Fast Passes regardless of how much you pay. Universal’s strategy is how to maximize profit and this is obvious and there bottom line from what I saw and experienced. I’m sure other parks also want the same but they do so in a respectful manner. Regarding the Cabana Bay Resort I would rate it a 4 out of 5. Very good and fair value. Regarding the dining plan I would give it a 0 out of 5. Absolutely a waste of money. We were told we would save about 25-30% compared to menu prices but actually that’s not true. We actually paid more than if we paid directly for what we purchased. They are deceptive and misleading about the meal plans. What is even more upsetting is that you cannot use your dining plan at your Universal resort hotel. How absurd and ridiculous. This is not mentioned to us at any point, neither over the phone when we booked or on check in. This means you have to go off resort to redeem for a drink, a snack or a meal. They shouldn’t even offer this since it’s neither economical nor convenient. Plus, it says dinners include dessert. But our first dinner at Vivo restaurant, we had no choice. And our second at Finnigans Irish Restaraut we were over at small sample size dessert. Neither time were we allowed to choose off their dessert menu. In addition, we were told tips were included in the meal plan but right on the receipt at the restaurant it stated tip was not included. The amount suggested was on the receipt with the total price of the meal. Hence, my overall rating of my experience was a 2 out of 5. Unfortunate, since the parks are good but the elitist express pass and the meal plan system both left a sour note and ruined my overall experience.
