The queues wet too Long , food and drinks too expensive some rides were okay , some a waste of time , i was expecting so much.

We really had a great time. We did not buy the fast pass which was okay. We kept checking on the app the times. Just depended on the ride how long you had to wait but we did an entire day and 1/2 day. We did buy park to park so we got to ride on the train. Place was clean, workers were very nice. Harry Potter area is just amazing. We spent 2 hours there just walking around. My son who is 10 and the biggest Harry Potter fan and the most wonderful time.
Always a wonderful place to visit but the evening is special and the laser and firework show are tremendous

My family and I are all enormous fans of Harry Potter, so having the opportunity to feel as though we had actually stepped into the books and movies was one of the most magical things I've ever experienced. We've gone twice now (the first time just for one day; this last time for 4 days) and it's magical each time.

We enjoyed our August adventure to Universal Studios Florida. We had park-park-park tickets and we spent most of our time at this park.  First of all Diagon Alley (Harry Potter) is far better than Hogsmead. The level of detail from the Knight bus outside the alley to all the interactive wand spots is worth it. Far more people wandering around helping (cast) and even hidden wand spots. The nice touch of having movie music in the background to even Kreatcher looking out the window at Grimmauld place is worth it. For food in Diagon Alley you have the Leaky Cauldron. It was ok but I actually preferred the three broomsticks better. For rides here you only have Escape from Gringots. At 6'6" I could not ride it. When I sat in the test seats my knees were already at the front of the car seat before even thinking about pulling the bar down over my legs. Nope, no go. At least I could ride the other Potter ride.  The other rides in the park were fun.  Men In Black: Fun laser shooter game, but forgettable.  The Simpsons: Ok. So we thought it was ok. Glad they had the original cast voices back (BoB) etc. We felt it was a bit of a crappy ride. Then we realized that this is what they were going for with it being Krustyland. So then we appreciated it more. Don't pay for a Duff Beer later on in the area, it is forgettable as coors light is.  Ran into Doc Brown from Back to the Future. Great interaction. Great Character.  Fast and the Furious: Ok ride. Good theme. Origional actors back. Not a big fan of the show so it was ok.  The Mummy Ride: Wife and child loved it and said it was wild. Once again I had the leg bar issue of not fitting in the seats. Almost like me being in a sports car, love to drive them just have way too long legs to do it.  Transformers: Awesome.  Minion Ride: AWESOME again!  Shrek: Forgettable. You have to wait WAY too long to actually get into the real ride and not the staging area. Feels tired and in need of renovation or removal.  Rock'n Coaster: Shut down due to storm the night we were going to go on it.  ET: Fun little ride. Wife loved it! Showing it's age but good for memories.  Get the popcorn bucket that is a souvenir. The cheap refills help you stay hydrated by giving you salt. We loved the Blues Brothers driving by and singing. Seen the real car/etc in Chicago so we felt it was good but could have been better.  The silly finger print reader to enter never did work for me. So I had to constantly show my ticket and my ID to get in. Not the end of the world but just interesting. Don't forget your ID if you are staying in park.  Overall we'd go back here and just skip certain rides next time.
Terrible. The best past was seeing the cars in the que. Don't bother going on it. You are in a bus like the Kong ride. Not thrilling in the least. It's actually silly.
Lovely and fun day with my mum and bro. Loads of exciting rides with lovely theme buildings such as Italian, Irish etc. Foods at restaurant are not cheap although. Plenty goodies from gift shop.

First time in the park for over 10 years. Some rides totally changed others not. The reason for 4/5 is the poor ET ride which is very outdated and also lots of similar simulator style rides. Plenty choices and attractions and also the Hogwarts express to go park to park to Islands of Adventure. Plenty of food and drinks options although very surprised that none of the NY outlets served hot dogs only corn dogs. Highlights would be Wizarding World of Harry Potter - Diagon Alley and the Escape from Gringotts ride. Also Men in Black, The Simpsons, Revenge of the Mummy and Rip Ride rocket. Be mindful some rides go off when weather poor. Also a very good evening show - the cinematic celebration.

It's hard to describe just what it's like at Universal, so much going on everywhere you look. I thoroughly enjoyed every second of it. Going in late August it's an idea to take an umbrella as you do tend to get the usual afternoon storm and of course if you are going on water rides take something with you as it's no fun walking round in wet clothes all day.  The rides are fantastic and all different, the Harry Potter area is amazing and really detailed if you are a fan you'll know what to look for. Kong was the best I went on closely followed by the Jimmy Fallon ride All staff are friendly and helpful throughout the park. Take your time and enjoy all the different areas, Simpsons is great fun!  Note that it's a far old trek from the car park to even get to the gates so comfy trainers are a must! Take drinks too or pay for one of the cups you can refill as much as you like as it hot work walking about.
City Walk at the entrance to Universal Studios is almost as good as the Park itself! Plenty of good eats to be had! The Park is a good time...plenty for everybody.....

A great day spent at the park and a lot quieter than our visit to Epcot yesterday. The rides all had shorter wait times and the general volume of people was lower than expected which was a nice surprise. We chose the Prime parking which for $35 was $10 cheaper than Disney although there is a dearer option in Valet parking. Prime parking meant we only had a short walk to the security gates and we were processed through these quickly and then on to our choice of park. My sons done several rides and whilst we waited on them we seen a Despicable Me parade and for any fans of the film's it is fantastic and the interaction with the smaller children was great to see. If arriving early I would recommend getting the refillable cups for drinks as you can fill them as many times as you wish during the day plus it's a great memento of your visit. The cup coats about $15 and considering one bottle of soda is $3.49 it can work out great value if spending the whole day in the park. We did not look at food as we were heading to the Hard Rock Cafe so no idea on what the prices are like. Overall a great day and looking forward to doing the other park soon

Of all the rides in Universal and Disney, this was my favourite. If you are a Harry Potter fan, you MUST go on this ride. We rode it 6 times in one day, and I never wanted to stop. This ride is the stuff of my dreams, and absolutely raises the bar for theme park rides in general.  One word of caution for those unaccustomed to modern thrill rides: your first ride will be very disorienting. Go on it a second time right after your first, and you will have a much better time and become used to the movement and sensations of the ride.

I had a blast. I wish some of the old rides were still in the park (like Jaws). I had a great time. The park was very clean. I didn't have to wait more than 15 mins for any ride. I was able to ride everything at least twice. I will be back.
Revisited with family Excellent fun for all ages he writes and hints to see for everyone. Great day out well worth the money spent. A good day to see all the shows and rides.

We went to Universal as a last minute stop on our week long vacation in Orlando. We got the 2 park pass but were soundly defeated by the size of the park on a hot muggy day. That being said, the park has something for everyone yet we suggest you plan your visit carefully. Plan first for the size of the park as we went directly after getting off a cruise which was not wise. Always take an opportunity to plot the timing of your visit as we had an opportunity to get on many of the rides due to the low off peak season attendance. Plan for the activities as we went early but much of the shows are later in the afternoon/evening. There are some rides with restrictions due to the size of the seats but there are sample seats outside to try so you do not wait in line for nothing. Only real complaint is that there is not an outlet or charging station in sight to charge cell phones which was the primary reason we left earlier than we wanted to. We could have brought portable charge packs but it would be smart for park to think about this going forward.

I loved most attractions. You need, at least, 4 days to visit most of the attractions and places on all 3 parks. I loved the Wizarding World of Harry Potter, and the Volcano Bay water park. Do not bother with their Fast & Furious ride if there is a line over 20 minutes for it because it is not worth it (unless you are a really big fan). One downside is that I think they have too many rides where you wear 3D glasses and get shook around a bit. After you get on a couple, it gets a bit old. Best rides were the Rock It roller coaster, the Hulk roller coaster, Harry Potter Forbidden Journey, Escape from Gringotts, King Kong Skull Island, Transformers, Jurassic Park, Men In Black. Roller coasters are very good and thrilling. Download their app to get help on the wait times and maps. They have free WiFi across all parks. During up season, queue times can get ridiculous. Either go off season or buy the Express pass (it is worth it when lines are huge).
We adored every second. Especially Diagon Alley. Memories for life. Outside of the Harry Potter areas, The Hulk and Rip Rocket were our favorites. Get the express passes. Life savers.

This review is ONLY regarding the HHN 2018 production. After attending opening weekend, I am extremely dissapointed in the technology and support systems Universal has in place for this event. From the manual entering of id codes that slowed the entry gates, to the incredibly outdated photo pass system, I can't help but wonder why this gets so much hype. The scare zones were lame and predictable. Hay monsters??? Really? Stranger Things was very well done, and its too bad they can't manage the crowd for this event better. You shouldn't have to pay an extra $100 for an express pass to avoid wasting 90-120 minutes in line. Take a lesson from Disney and figure out how to allow patrons to enjoy other parts of the park while waiting for their turn to experience your main attraction. On our second night, we arrived at 5:15 thinking we were plenty early, but didn't get through the gates til 6:40. we went straight to stragner things because it was a 120 minute wait the night before at 11pm. We got out of Stranger Things at 8:45 and left the park exhausted from standing in line with no water or drinks. The only picture we got as a group also cut my daughter off. Thanks for the memories...

This park is designed with the entire family in mind. There are rides for the teenagers, smaller children and adults. We only went to Universal Studios and not to the other two parks. The park is like being on a movie set everywhere you walk. There are of theme restaurants on every corner, even Mel’s Diner and, of course, plenty of gift shops.

We had a great time exploring Universal Studio! A Simpson's and Harry Potter fan must!  Lots of rides, shops, food and shows!  Loved catching the blues brothers show. There was dancing in the streets.  We went in January and the lines were not very long. Always less than an hour and mostly under 30 mins. If you have time do a few days. if you don't have more than a day then get a fast pass.  Also look out for the all day drink cup. Handy to have even just one active for a drink between meals.

We went to Universal in July as my daughter is a huge Harry Potter fan. The Harry Potter area is amazing. The attention to detail is just extraordinary. I felt like I was really there. We had a park to park ticket so we went to both parks. We found it a little hard to navigate where everything was, there aren't a ton of signs explaining things. (not just in Harry Potter, we understand why there isn't there) My daughters and I all suffer from motion sickness so there aren't a ton of things we could go on. I felt like every ride had a sign that said if you have motion sickness etc. We aren't big fans of the 3D simulator rides anyway if we could go on with a Dramamine. Security was seamless and so much quicker than at Disney. I wish their maps had more detail as to where to see shows and characters as it was our first time and we really didn't know what was there. I wish it listed the stores as well since we went in a lot of those since we weren't able to go on that many rides. They allow you to walk through the ride ques so you can see all the neat effects! We were able to wait for my husband to get off the ride, right where it exited which was great. We didn't have to wait outside in the heat.

You can't go wrong with taking the family. Recommendation is that you purchase either a meal plan or if you don't plan on eating in Universal that you buy the refillable cups at 15.99 you fill all day long with no extra cost. Universal now has Coca-Cola products and use the Freestyle so you can choose from over 1,000 varieties. We like Sprite Zero and it is hard to find but with Freestyle you can get it. If you go with your family try to stay at a resort that is affiliated with Universal as you can get in 1 hour prior to opening, makes it easy to get on the popular rides with little ones.

had a 14 day ticket and went most days, had the onsite early hour entry which made so much difference. highlights were the two sides of harry potter. i enjoyed all the simulaters except fast and furious which is a waste of space, gringotts was awesome
This place is great every ride the way its all laid out. I will def go here again . Staff friendly nothing to much trouble. Food was nice here weather great.
Some of the rides here are still just bumpy and jerky. We liked the new Skull Island adventure. Food is very overpriced.
We love this park but too many 4d rides,fast and furious is awful,you need to change that and i wouldnt wait in a long quene for it,my fave is the blue brothers singing

Get ready to have your hand consistently in your wallet. Universal is simply overpriced. Food, drinks & tickets to the parks. Too bad because Harry Potter is just great. Once you have been on one of the 3D rides they are all the same. EXCEPT for Harry Potter Gringotts & Forbidden Journey. Enjoyed Jimmy Fallon. Hogwarts Express cool but bad for people who are claustrophobic or hot (no AC) Went with friends who could not go on any of the rides because of the warnings..motion sickness, blood pressure and back and neck problems. (Every ride has this warning) Sometimes not necessary. Park should provide a pass for people who can't do the rides. Disappointed and won't be back. Staff also not friendly. Twice the price as Disney with half the fun.
I've done this ride several times but if there's a queue I don't bother. It's a bit of fun and good for groups with kids. There are better rides however

Absolutely brilliant park. Love it here every year something new opens. Harry Potter is fabulous. If your going next year it's well worth looking at an annual pass. We paid $5.00 last year. As long as you go 2 weeks before it runs out.

This park is less intense than Disney World. I was able to walk around the park and see all of the sights without the overwhelming crowds. The rides are well done and the characters are out more often. I love the extensive selection of items in the stores and the food in Diagon Alley was extremely well done.

We still love this place and all the rides even though we are a mature couple in our fifties. Parking is free after 6pm so if you plan well you can visit the park most evenings when the queues are shorter. This meant we didn’t feel the need to pay extra for express passes and got on most rides within 15 minutes. Atmosphere is best during the day when the shows and parades are on. A must do park when in Orlando.

Besides all the rides, restaurants, and shops, this is the place to go if you love Harry Potter. If you can afford to by a magic wand, you can find "magic" in many windows. Be sure to car chase the firey dragon in Dagon Alley! Whoa!

Universal does it right! Scare zones are cool. characters roaming the streets. The haunted houses are MOVIE QUALITY. This year they have STRANGER THINGS house.. WOW!!! You feel like you're in the tv show. My only complaints are.. the price for a FAST PASS is $79 per person and i wish we had them because the lines on a SUNDAY night were over an hour for most the houses. I Can't imagine how bad they are for a Friday or Saturday. Tickets are $20 more on Saturday nights too. Parking $22 -- Ouch! But expected from a theme park.

Both this park and Islands of Adventure are worth the ticket price. There is lots of walking so wear comfortable shoes! My general advice with any Orlando theme park is to limit the time spent there are go on several days as it's hard to cram everything into a day. We did a full day across both parks and stayed for one of the Halloween Horror nights and this was too much. Please note that my rating is for the parks during normal hours and not for the separately ticketed Halloween Horror Nights. The food and drink in Universal is more expensive than Disney and OK but not amazing. Disney allow packed lunches to be taken in whereas Universal don't and the rules of what you can take in are a little ambiguous.

Me and my partner spent a few days at this park as the rides are so amazing have to go on them more then once! And make sure you don’t miss anything! We paid to go back in the evening for the horror nights as it was around Halloween time, I would say it’s not for the under 16 age mark,( am I 24) it’s jumpy and the mazes are scary, absolutely amazing though!!! I have been the fright nights before but nothing repairs. Atmosphere is insane, if I go back to Florida I’d try and go at the same time of year just to experience the horror nights for Halloween

We really enjoyed Universal Studios. From the minute you enter and walk through the Citywalk with all the restaurants and shops it feels welcoming. We loved the Simpsons ride and land with all the familiar sites and the Escape from Gringotts ride was amazing! While I appreciate queues can be huge at times, using crowd calendars online to plan your visit the rides were 10 minutes long which was brilliant! We would definitely return and even considered staying onsite in the future to be in the middle of all the action.

Park mostly paved over with little green spaces for sitting and relaxing in cool atmosphere as in Disney parks. only recommend for ride attractions . Best food in area near Eathquake attraction. Lombards for seafod was or favorite, otherwise, dining here is not too varied or good.
Expedia is the worst way to book this trip. Their website is clunky and customer service is not good. Universal is great. Book through them and you'll have a better trip.
This ride was so disappointing. The park has many other similar simulation rides that are much better. Even the old Spiderman and Transformers are more entertaining. A low point for a very good park.

I absolutely love Universal Studios and have visited many times over the last 30 years. Staff are always friendly and happy to help. Rides are amazing and something to do for all the family. This year though, I noticed a big change in the price of everything within the park, it’s got really really expensive to eat/drink there. Won’t stop me going back though.

This place blew me away. I always said I would pay my sister to take my kids to Disney or Universal. I don’t like crowds & get nervous someone might snatch my kid in the crowd & disappear. I guess we went at just the right time because I was told it wasn’t crowded by normal standards. We had express passes included in our hotel stay, so that helped us cut our wait times significantly. What I was so amazed with was that almost every employee seemed to make it their job to ensure that our boys had the time of their lives! And they did! They call it “The trip of a lifetime!”

As always a wonderful day, we managed to do every ride we wanted to. Rip ride rocket as always amazing, the mummy one of my favourites, a train ride on hogwarts, shooting aliens on.MIB and what i always worry will be my last ride on ET...(so many rumours its closing). Lots of places to eat, nice and clean. Looking lovely as Halloween approaches. Definitely a place to visit for all ages.
it will save you money trust me is a little expensive to come here. but take the presentation nice park great rides worth it.

Universal park size: personally I was a little surprised about the actual size of the two parks after estimating the need for four days to do both. In reality we did both parks in two days. They really are not that big!  Food: over priced and under sized, $5 for a donut - $30pp for a main.  Water: $4.50 Ummm....  Parade: Simply a joke when compared to magic kingdom.  Attractions at both parks: majority are motion simulators mixed with two good coasters and lots of children's rides.  Water parks: tapu tapu is stupid, the system dose not work as it should for a million dollar plus company. You end up spending the majority of the day sitting around waiting for a 2 second water slide. They actual park looks impressive and the slides are far better then either of the Disney parks, however the day was a little ruined by the tapu tapu system.  Parking: PLEASE if you are staying outside of a universal accomodation you must read this!!! For some reason universal feel the need to charge a parking fee of $25 per day for either universal studios, island of adventure or volcano bay!!! So for a 14 day vacation expect to be paying an excess of $350. ( Bare in mind this parking charge was $22 per day, just two days ago...)  Conclusion: obviously the whole experience is good, but the reality is that by the end of the day you feel robbed and a fair amount of frustration for Universal's greed and lack of ability to deliver.  Thanks for reading and I Hope this helps you decided on your vacation.

This park gets a solid 4 stars. Personally the rides were a bit too much for me. If you get motion sickness at all, this place will bring it out. However those that love fast exhilarating rides this is the place for you. While my kids road the rides, I learned to back off from them after riding one of the many roller coasters. In my opinion this park is great for teenagers up to middle aged individuals. However there are activities and rides for all ages. While not my favorite park in the area, I think that there is a solid market here.

Not a spider man fan but I really enjoyed this ride.  It’s a simulator like most within the 2 parks and it’s great!  Didn’t queue long for it as we used the single rider, great option if you don’t want to wait in the normal queue.

First time I went on I was so mesmerised by this ride, I thought it was amazing!  The theming throughout the castle is great and doesn’t feel like you’re waiting long.  The ride itself is fantastic, I absolutely loved it. Needless to say I went on it a few times during our visit to the park.
Best horror experience I've done. Immersive and scary. RIP Tour was worth every penny would recommend

People who are giving this park a good review must of had combo tickets or just don't know what a good park should consist of! $125.00 for LITERALLY about 12 RIDES is shameful! I felt sorry for my son, but he was a trooper and didn't really complain concerning the lack of rides at this money grabbing park!

Spent two days at Universal Studios with the family; two adults, teenager and kid. Everyone had a great time and is wanting to go back again, but next time with an express pass. The two parks at Universal Studios are enormous in size and offer a huge range of entertainment for kids of all ages. As to be expected, the lines for rides can be quite long and that can try the patience of young and old alike. Also, the food places can get very busy at times. So, while visitors should by all means enjoy the great park, arriving early and staying late can reduce wait times and eating outside traditional meal times makes the food more enjoyable. As an amusement park, Universal Studios is great fun and very much worth a visit (or two).

This is the best of the two parks. Obviously the main attraction is the Harry Potter Diagon Alley which is well done with the escape from Gringotts roller coster ride and the numerous shops ready to releave you of your $. But also the Mummy and Dispable Me with the minions causing havic. Shrek, Fiona and donkey have a great 4 D ride which includes movement and the contents of donkey's sneeze! The Simpsons ride is great fun and the surrounding area including Duff man and Moe's tavern. You need a duel pass to be able to travel on the Hogwards Express between US and I of A and it is worth doing the journey in both directions, similar but different experience. Expensive but you can easily spend all day here.

My ride highlights were Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit (liked this better than the Hulk and you can choose what music is blasting in your ears while you hurtle down the super sweet drop), Revenge of the Mummy (a bit dated, but a welcome break from all the screens), Harry Potter and the Escape from Gringotts (admire the bank's interior while waiting in line), Transformers and The Simpsons Ride. The screen-based attractions made me a bit dizzy. I would still recommend getting a Park-to-Park ticket especially for Harry Potter fans so you can ride the Hogwarts Express. The highlights of Islands of Adventure and Universal Studios are doable in a single day, but only if you're an early bird, can eat on the go and willing to rush. Ideally, you should also go alone and/or have an express pass which can cut down on your wait time. You can ride single at some of the rides (some single lines move even faster than the express pass line). Buy tickets in advance online and get your game plan on. When you're there, use the app. It has an interactive map, approximate wait times and notifications (super helpful when you want to be notified when a ride has opened). Most of the more thrilling rides have free lockers (for a limited time) since they don't allow you to bring stuff on the rides. Oh, and don't forget to drink butterbeer and eat the big pink donut from the Simpsons (which tastes like Krispy Kreme).

This is such a fantastic park, I visited with my children, my teenage daughter loved the hulk, as did her grandad ..,we all liked The Mummy and Harry Potter was the highlight for us. Don’t miss Harry Potter and the forbidden journey , also the escape from Gringotts. Try the cinnamon pretzel nuggets from Aunty Anne’s , very tasty.

This years visits to universal were on the whole average we enjoyed the et ride as always and the Simpson kang saucer ride the over to men in black went on as single rider fantastic in and out in 10 minutes got some photos taken with Marylyn Monroe what have universal done with the beetle juice character and betty boop not seen her for 2 years now the transformer ride was missed as queues way too long even single rider onto fast and furious this was a joke I decided to get ticket for the time which was return at 1230 the time then was 1140 I saw they had single rider so opted for this instead well I walked in joined the back of a queue and waited and waited and waited seems the person letting people on was only letting those in the main queue on leaving seats available but not filling from single rider queue the ride itself was ok but I when I got out it was 1225 not impressed by the wait we missed minion ride as queue too long having been to the park many times we knew what to expect some of the rides are a bit dated know and too many little shops selling same merchandise (maybe universal needs to spend more on the parks and less on building hotels all over the international drive area) will return as we find Disney to full on in your face

If you're looking for a park full of simulators & roller-coasters - this is it! Harry Potter, Revenge of the Mummy, Men-in-Black, Transformers, and many more - you can really get motion sickness after all of them... If you don't want to wait four hours on lines, buy the Express Pass (although on some rides such as Harry Potter you wait even with it...). If you don't have time you should probably skip the train to Islands of Adventure - it's a very long line even with the Express Pass - you can walk much faster than that...
Great park. Great rides. But without an Express Pass you will be in line for most of your day. Costs extra but it is a necessity. Can make or break a vacation to Universal studios!

What can I say what an amazing park ! Currently sat in moes having a duff beer !  Miles better than the Disney parks!  Amazing service for my son who has additional needs !  We love it here and can’t wait to return !  If your staying in a universal hotel get up early and hit the parks at 7 !

HHN: We would have appreciated time to really see the haunted houses properly. We took small-ish children with us, which is it not recommended, but they LOVED the 4 houses we saw and the scare zones. The chainsaw roaming horde was their favourite. The grown ups in our party felt rushed through the houses. There is no time given to take it all in and we were badgered by staff in the houses to keep up with the people in front - we were nearly running at some points! Within a couple of hours of opening, all the houses were at 45 minute+ queues. So after wasting precious time watching the thoroughly awful academy of villains (total rubbish) we left.  2 week visit to parks: too many simulator rides for us, all the newest rides are disappointing - jimmy fallon and fast and furious declared rubbish by the kids and they wouldn’t ever get on them again. Kong is the same style of ride too - please bring back more big roller coaster rides Universal. 2 of best 3 rides of our holiday now at SeaWorld (rip ride rocket at Universal came in at number 2). We have high hopes for the new park that seems to be in the works - but we won’t be back until that is open. Oh, and don’t bother with Volcano Bay - go to Aquatica.

This event was great the only bad thing was the wait times would suggest getting there as early as possible there are 10 houses and we were only able to get in 5 but out of those five they were all great definitely recommend this event

Plan again before you arrive! If you like to be scared then you want to come here but please plan ahead. There are days that the Halloween Horror Nights are not offered so check their website. This attraction is very popular so expect long lines for parking and for the haunted houses. We arrived near Universal Studios on a Sunday night around 6:30pm and were faced with a traffic jam to get into the parking garages. We sat in traffic for 2 hours before we were able to park. That cut into our haunted house time. We purchased our tickets on-line at the Halloween Horror Nights website. We did not think about paying extra for Fast-Pass tickets and we regret that because the lines ranged from a 45 minute wait to 130 minute wait. Due to the long line, we only got into 3 out of the 10 haunted houses. We also learned you can purchase early entry tickets. To make the most of your experience, research ticket prices and invest in early entry tickets or fast pass tickets. The three houses we went to were scary and we screamed a lot.

This ride is absolutely amazing! If you and your family are Harry Potter fans then this is definitely the ride for you. The line alone was worth it! The attention to detail is amazing. The only regret I have is that I didn’t get to ride it 100 more times!!

Came in the evening as part of a convention group. Hard to figure out what was open. Got the harry potter ride which was great. Most stuff already closed. Got to listen to some cute singers lead by Hermionine. Though we would die before we figured out how to get out and then had difficulty finding our bus back to the hotel. What a zoo. Hope never to go here again.

This Theme Park has rides and shows for everyone.  We visited twice to ensure we went on all the rides. I particularly enjoyed Men in Black, Transformers and the Animal shows (other than Harry Potter)the best.  The line waiting times ranged from 15 minutes to 60,which is apparently good.  The park is well organised, although The app is not synched to the rides and is totally inaccurate.  My partners son got his arm stuck in the railings at the Simpsons ride doing a spell with a wand and needed first aid. The first wider was excellent and extremely helpful, although this shouldn’t really happen.  There are lots of eating options, but I didn’t enjoy any of it. It’s very over priced and not particularly nice food.  However, if Theme parks is your thing then this is a must.

Universal studios is a must great day out for everyone lots to see and enjoy the Harry Potter is a great experience great theme park overall we went Christmas time and the parades were great the kids love it it really made the holiday

Do not go at 9 am. Everyone is in a hurry to be first in long lines. Instant 45 minute waits. Not good for mobility challenged individuals. From one end to another it is food and stores. All rides except the train come with warnings that exclude a large number of people over 60. We ate at 3 Broomsticks. The fries were okay, but the fish tasted oily and was cold by the time we got to a table (with very low chairs). I paid $1500 Canadian for 4 x 2 day, park hopper passes, and after 4 hrs we were at the exit and will not be returning for a second day. What a waste of money!!!!. You get nothing for your entry fee. Go to Disney instead, where there is street entertainment everywhere, so much more fun.
Ithought thr tickets were a little pricey I could not have paid for us to do universal and disney on the same trip

This was our annual family getaway - and it was fun as usual! We saw the Blue Man Group at City Walk! It was fun as well! There is always so much to do: rides, shop, eat, live music, photos, and so much more!

We really had a wonderful time here, although it was VERY expensive. We had to buy admission to the two different parks, plus fast-passes (which really are a must if you don't want to stand in line for hours.) and it topped nearly 650 bucks for just my husband and myself. That aside, it was a great experience. I do not recommend the dining plan, didn't really seem to save us time or money.

Have to do 1 day Park to Park. Start at Universal Studios. Head right, past front of Hard Rock, to find entrance. We entered Island of Adventure, this is backwards for Harry Potter. Start in London's Diagon Alley, take train to Hogmeades, in Island of Adventure. For fans, plan to spend entire day in the Harry Potter attractions.

Have visited Disney many times with family, tried out universal (original) and was a worthwhile experience, not as busy as disney, parking is closer, and moving walkways are nice, but the experience is more 3d virtual...best rides are 1.mummy- cool roller coaster effect ride with one medium drop, speed and effects, goes fast but cool 2.transformers- the first time on this ride, whoa! After that it's cool but not the same 3.fast and furious- unexpected, but very fun and immersive 4.simpsoms-funny story type 3d .. Harry Potter was a little disappointing, the world seems like a giant cash register experience for the park Worth a visit with kids 7 or older!
Wow everyone must visit this park, Harry Potter world was amazing, the hulk rollercoaster, every ride was breath taking 100% the best parks in the world

We went in August for thr first time and had the best vacation ever. Fast Pass was well worth the money. Park was very clean staff seemed to be very helpful. Fopod is pretty pricey no matter where or what you eat not really worth the cost. gettiong in a hour eary was a great bonus we did not expect. Harry Potter was mind blowing so realalistic. Ride were pretty good Hogwarts Train has to be experenced round trip, Butter beer was fantastic frozen was the best..Pl;anning our nest tri[p to Disny will update after our trip is complete..
Amazing day out. Got a 14day pass for around £260 but so worth it. A must see if your in florida. Island of adventure is the better side but must do both.

We were in town for the IAAPA Convention (International Association of Amusement Parks and Attractions and we returned to Universal Studios for IAAPA’s private party. Universal went above and beyond to make it THE best IAAPA party ever! From the variety and amount of food to the entertainment (Bare Naked Ladies) it will be hard to top. Of course the park is great on regular visits as well!
I know that Disney is a must visit but I was amazed that I prefer Universal that Disney. As an adult, you'll find the rides here more exciting.
Very good ride. Long lines. We discover the single ride line. We do the ride 3 tomes in a row using it. No family photo, but triole fun.
We had a fantastic time. Love the rides and the park is very clean. Staff was extremely helpful and friendly.

Before you think I am bias please keep in mind I’ve lived in this area and have visited all the attractions for the last 31 years. I have 2 daughters now ages 10 & 6. In this last decade the Disney theme parks was our thing primarily because the girls were to young and small to really enjoy the rides here at universal studios. Now I thought “YES!” finally I get to have fun with my daughters on a more grown up level... Finally I get to ride real rides again!! Lol! ;-) Honestly the rides are awesome!! The place is kept clean!! Except every restroom (wife said women’s was the same) that seemed like a truck stop. BUT.... the employees are so rude and nasty. Please and thank you is not in their vocabulary. They are not polite. Don’t ask any questions because you will be met with aggravation that you’ve asked. The wife and I made no remarks so the children wouldn’t notice, but both my daughters asked on several separate times as to why were we being spoken to rudely. Even poor elderly folks trying to move on and off rides were told,” sit down it’s not that hard”. Honestly I was hoping to be an annual pass holder and move up from the kiddie rides to the pre teen and adult rides.... but no thank you. I don’t want to be treated like a piece of garbage and spoken to like I’m nothing. We spent well over $2,000 on 2 days between tickets, food and Harry Potter stuff. This was our 10 year olds dream birthday and we pulled it off and had a ton of fun. Just ignored the indifferent employees. Retraining would go a long way. Or take a page from Disney’s guest relations play book.

2nd time to hhn. We went in 2015 and came back this year. Pretty much same type of venue. We had a good time but was terribly disappointed in the new cyberpunk show. Loved bill n Ted hated new garbage.like before details are great. We have never had a bad experience at universal just this year not a great one. Staff in the park itself wasn't near as welcoming as in past and we have visited hear over 10 times. Usually when we leave we are already making plans to go back.not this time. Just felt like after they got our money we were forgotten about. How about instead of coming on tripadvisor and saying how sorry everyone is you guys just fix your problems instead of talking do something. Rides stayed down to much also.
We went for Halloween Horror Night it was a blast and had the best time ever, only thing lines where kinda long but was worth the wait.

Good selection of rides and not so crowded as Disney.  We have visited several times over the years, and agree with most reviewers that this is a good attraction.  However, there is one issue that has not been resolved since it opened and visitors should be aware of. I can see that this has been mentioned by other visitors in the past within reviews.  The journey from the entrance of the Mummy ride, to the ride itself has varying levels of lighting, of which some is too low for many people to have a clear view of the way forward. One of the worst areas is just before you get on the ride, where there is a flight of metal steps. The bottom two steps had no lighting. My wife tripped and fell, bruising her leg. I also tripped behind her. My wife has difficulty walking the rest of the day due to the bruising. This was reported to Guest Services.  I should also add that we had a similar problem in Skull Kingdom in IOA.

We were so excited to check out Universal .... it seemed expensive... we knew it would be busy .... we had no idea it was ridiculous. People were completely jammed ... everything was so expensive and wait .... wait wait wait. Wait for a beer wait for a ride wait to get in wait to get there... not fun. It was like $13.00 for a pizza slice... for Canadians that’s $17.50 ... there’s 5 of us. It cost us $77.00for lunch. 🤪 . We got the buy 2 days get 2 day pass... one day we went on 3 rides... we got there at noon and gave up at 7 pm .... 3 rides. That to me says they just want to make money and do not care about your experience. The staff aren’t friendly. They are just putting people through ....next.... Some of the rides are really fun .... Harry Potter part is so neat but it was claustrophobic it was so busy. We had a super cool experience with Beetle Juice I guess that made it worth the $2000 🤪🤪🤪🤪
Universal had something for everyone. The teens loved Island ofAdventure and especially the Harry Potter rides and attractions.
We had a really good time here. I am a big Harry Potter fan so I was always going to be fairly happy but the rest of the park was actually very good too. We had a good day.

Saw several shows and rode a lot of rides. Some favorite rides were Men in Black, Transformers and Despicable Me Minion Mayhem. I definitely faced my fears riding Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit. I was excited to finally see Diagon Alley. Loved the dragon on top of Gringotts that spits fire, seeing the knightbus and seeing Kreacher peeking out of Grimmauld Place. Was a little disappointed in Harry Potter and the Escape from Gringotts. It was short and I thought they could have done more with it. The Hogwarts Express was great. Be aware that you have to have tickets to both sides of the park to ride it.

Our Daughter decided that instead of a Quinceanera, she wanted just us 3 to go to Universal Studios together. OMG, what a great time. We had a park-to-park 4 day ticket. It was fabulous!! So much to do and see. The timing couldn't have been better- we never waited long for any ride. The park is so clean and everyone that works there is HAPPY! It was our first time there and we are sooo going back again some time.

My sister and I have come back two years in a row at Christmas time because we’ve had so much fun. This year my sister in law joined us for then fun! Harry Potter World is amazing and I would recommend it to anyone fan or not.

We took my teenage Son to HHN for the first time ever. He had such a blast. The lines we not too long and they moved fairly quickly. The haunted houses were very well put together and choreographed. We also enjoyed the dance team show more than anything! We will be returning in years to come.

We stayed in Orlando for 3 days before traveling onto the Caribbean. We decided to visit both parks on a day pass just to say we had been as we were unlikely to travel there again. Well for someone so keen on not going i ended up absolutely loving it! The park is amazing there was so much to see and do I wish we had gone for longer! The rides were fantastic and once I’d been on one and had got a taste for it I wanted to do them all! Luckily for us the ques weren’t long at all and the longest we had to wait was for Kong skull island and that was 40mins. Even the queuing areas are themed with things to see and watch so the time actually goes pretty quick. Food & drink as to be expected was quite over priced. We are now looking at coming back and doing the parks again!

The family loved this park, with 2 parks there is so much to do that you will Need more than a day to visit and do the rides! The restaurants are great...a bit expensive but it’s a theme park so to be expected... food was decent and for marvel lovers it’s a must!! Well worth a visit

Universal is much fun. The trick I’ve found is to stay at a park hotel that offers a fast pass just for one night and you get the shorter lines for two days. But we went in both March and December and even the lines without the fast pass were relatively short. Another thing is if you get the meal plans in the end it saves you about 5 bucks. I’m gonna be honest, we did share some of the food because the entrées are large, but I feel guilty about it.

Universal Studios Florida has lots of 3D rides that can give you a good adrenalin flush. Fast & Furious, Racing thru New York with Jimmy Fallon, scary rapid Mummy ride, Transformers battle ride, Minnions Despicable 2 wonderful ride, upside down vertical up and straight down roller coaster and the not yo he missed Diagon Alley where you get immersed in Harry Porter's world. Lots of other places to go and have fun. Do enjoy and do whatever you fancy. Be brave. Go have your optimum adrenalin flush

We went universal Orlando Wednesday, what an amazing day with my Granddaughter we found the world of Harry Potter, you have to get the 2 park passes to really get the full effect of Harry Potter, you take a train from the movie of Harry Potter it looks so real from park to the other. If you want to see all the shows one day will not be enough time I wish we would have done 2 days. We are from Oregon and have always gone universal California, Orlando has more rides but California has the back lot tour.

My husband and I had fun time at the Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure parks. For the two of us, our favorite part was the Universal Studios, we went on way more rides there. The only one that was a huge let down was the Fast and Furious one, there was a lot of build up, but it very short and not very thrilling. The end of the MIB ride was a let down, but had the potential to be a lot of fun. I wish more rides were interactive like that one. I'm a Harry Potter fan so I enjoyed the rides at both parks and the immersive experience at the Universal Studios Park. Would recommend for people to go.

Went on the Orlando informer meet-up night. 1 price gets you in and gree food and beverages all night with free play in the arcades. No waits for the rides as its limited access. Best way to do the park but anytime the park is still great.

We visited for the second time this year just last week. It was such a great time even though the weather turned a bit cooler than expected. The Macy’s Christmas Parade was simply gorgeous and we enjoyed the Grinch performance so much. The costumes and acting and music were so professional. Wizarding World never disappoints and the closing ceremonies in each park should not be missed. We definitely visit Orlando during off seasons since crowds make me crazy! My only request is that a bit more seating is added in the Wizarding world. I want to just sit and enjoy the area especially in Diagon Alley! And enjoy my Butterbeer.

We are a Disney family so I know this will be biased to some extent. It's hard to explain our experience in negative terms. We stayed at the Royal Pacific hotel which was beautiful, with a great helpful staff. The location was a quick 15 minute talk to CityWalk and both theme parks. The parks were clean, very cleverly decorated and the staff at the parks were nice and helpful. We all walked away just thinking that we didn't get the value for the price we paid. The prices for parks, hotels, food, etc, are right in line with Disney, but we didn't feel we got the same value for our money at Universal. For every one attraction that you could experience with your park admission there were 10-15 other areas that you had to spend money. Those areas were restaurants, stores, and believe it or not there were carnival games available which really looked tacky to us. Just didn't get the value we are accustomed to at Disney.
We had a great time. The park is well done. The fountain light show at the end of the night is good. The lines were short when we were there. Most were under 15 minutes.

What an awesome experience! Super clean, interactive and something for everyone. After spending a very dissatisfied day at Disney with my wife and four adult children, Universal saved the day. Since we are DVC owners, until today we were all about Disney. What we learned today is that Universal is geared for older ages and has a TON of rides for adults. For nostalgic reasons we wanted to do Disney for most of our vacation. After just one day at Disney, I realized that it was outdated and boring for my millennial children. I thought the vacation was a bust, however Universal saved the day. We had a blast! Plenty of simulation rides and rollercoasters. We also attended Blue Man Group, which was fantastic! Yes, it is an expensive place, however we we're here to have fun and dollar for dollar, way better than Disney (again, for adults)! We all have a different perspective now. We came here for a great time and Universal delivered. We had also payed for the fast pass and if you are coming for just one day, I highly recommend it. Again, not cheap but with it, you can do this park in a day. I liked this option over Disney's method.

We purchased annual passes for our family of 5 which had a deal for 3 additional months, we decided to go to both parks December 18-19, 2018. The Harry Potter world at both parks were fantastic, they truly out did themselves. We were only able to ride a few rides including Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey 👌🏾, Hogwarts Express was perfection (different train show each way), Diagon Alley is everything and in my opinion the only reason to visit Universal Studios which is where we spent most of our time including dining there at Three Broomsticks 🧹 🧹🧹. The food is on point, healthy and the venue is something straight from the movie. The entire town transports you into the fantasy world of Harry Potter 💯.  Please listen to me carefully and stay away from the Fast and the Furious ride, it’s a complete waste of time, a total let down and it should be removed completely. I suggest the Harry Potter double decker bus with the Caribbean talking dead heads as a ride 👊🏽😎I know Universal has the money and the power to make that happen. In case you’re wondering because you will be if you don’t know but the Butter Beer tastes like sweet butterscotch, you can get it cold or frozen, we got 1 frozen and shared among the 3 of us which was more than enough. You’re welcome!

We had a wonderful time at Universal Studios. There were 5 of us ranging in age from 7 to 70! We purchased the 1-day, 2 park ticket option, as we wanted to visit both parts of Harry Potter World, and ride the Hogwarts express. We did think it was a bit expensive for both parks, but found that we didn't really have a choice if we wanted to visit both parks in the same day. One tip I would give anyone visiting Universal Studios is to arrive early. My fiancé and his daughter rode the Hulk ride 2 times early in the morning, with only a 5 minute wait, and this was after all of us had already been on the Spiderman ride! Plan on lots of walking, as you find at any amusement park. By around noon, you definitely noticed wait times increasing. I also found it much easier to meet characters, like the Cat in the Hat & Spiderman, much easier than at Disney World. We didn't wait longer than 10 minutes to meet any of the characters. We did miss thing 1 and thing 2, but will make that one of our priorities next time! My one complaint I had in the park was their non-smoking policy was not something that seemed to be followed very strictly. They have designated areas for smoking, but on multiple occasions I was around people who just smoked wherever they wanted to. Overall, we had a great day and the next time we visit we plan to stay at one of the resorts and spend more time at Universal Studios!!

It had been raining the day before and we were excited to get to Universal Studios. We got to the park early and it was a made rush. Going through the security checkpoint was a madhouse. There was not really a line just a mass of people pushing towards the security checkpoint. Had to work to keep my family of six together. Once we finally made it pass security it was free reign as you walk to the park of your choice. We of course chose Universal Studios. As we walk through the City Walk we saw a lively area that was fully staffed and full of tourist. Be sure to take a picture in front of the Universal globe.  After that we came to another checkpoint that turned out to be the gate. Again this area was so packed and unorganized it seemed like we were just in a mass of people going no where. After about 20 minutes we made it to the gate. They checked each ticket and scanned the fingerprint of my family members to associate with a ticket. I asked if they purge finger print info. The gate attendant said they do once the ticket expired. I don’t want my finger print held by a private company so I hope that is true.  Once inside I took the advise of other reviewers and went to the back of the park. The best rides for us were the Mummy Revenge and Fast and Furious. We tried the Simpson’s ride and found it to be very dated and it seems the simulation is not synced properly. The movement of the ride did not match the screen which resulted in motion sickness. After that the kids waited in line for 45 minutes to ride the Woody Woodpecker rollercoaster. It was a 2 minute ride and they said it was not worth it. I appreciated their honesty.  The big catch was when we were hungry and didn’t want to leave the park so we decided to eat at Mel’s Diner. Big mistake the food was very basic and we ended up paying 80 dollars for food. I get it it’s park food, however they should do a better job with the quality of food. We ate because it was warm and we were hungry. The next day we planned accordingly and ate outside the park at City Walk and had better quality food at a cheaper price. Overall our visit was good and feel like we got what we paid for.

Overall experience was fun and for a family with a special needs kid the day was great and smooth  But OMG the prices , we had to say goodbye to over $400 US for 1 day, 2 adults and one kid just to get in.  Lines are crazy (some over 3 hours) as well as the restaurant are all packed up.  Never again on the high season

It's easy to get caught up in all the fantastic experiences at Universal studios! This is my family's second trip, coming down from Massachusetts. This trip the parks were much busier, which is totally understandable being Christmas vacation week. Aside from long lines for food and some drink stands things were great. I would totally recommend staying at one of the onsite hotels to get the unlimited express pass. Wasting time in lines is no fun! Totally worth the extra $$ Also we got to meet plenty of characters. Beetle juice was my favorite
Long lines but rides were fun! Would've preferred longer rides, more attractions, and shorter lines.
My first time at the resort and must say that it was worth it.  Entire family had loads of fun.  Lines longer than at Disney but expected that being the Christmas holiday period

Very enjoyable despite heavy postchristmas crowds. Express pass was pricey...but worth it this week. Saved us hours in line and we used the unlimited option to ride several rides multiple times including Hogwarts Express and Men In Black. Tried all three types of butter beer. Discovered frozen, normal or hot is purely personal preference. All are good. Enjoy!!

As much as the rides were thrilling and some were really awesome, be prepared to queue up to 3 hours for the popular rides. Most rides will also be at least an hour or so. Express Pass may be the solution but since there were 5 of us, it would have doubled the cost.  Probably it was due to the peak holiday season but I still felt the waiting time was too long. We bought the 3 days, park to park tickets so we can ride on the Hogwarts Express and take our time but we really struggled.  Queue for food can also go up to 30 mins even not during meal times. Staff looked tired and some were no longer friendly...  It was so crowded in Diagon Alley that stopping to take photos or getting inside the shops became difficult cause of the traffic.  Overall was a poor experience this time at Universal Studio Orlando.

Shuttles that take you to citywalk from the resort are crowded and hard to stand in.we got on ours the first night and i asked the lady where it was going, thinking like disney there were dirrent buses for different parks. She asked me where I wanted to go, when I replied one of the parks she said this will get you there now move back. So end of ride that dumps you in citywalk we are getting off and I ask where the bus back to the resort is she says read the signs...
