I visited Universal Studios for only my second time and with my godson (4yrs old), niece (15yrs old) and potential stepdaughter (7 yrs old) as well as other family members and I must say......I'm 6'5" 380lbs and felt like a 3'8" kid when I seen the Star Wars attraction and the various other things in the park. I was harassed again by a couple stormtroopers but boy was it a blast! My godson and potential stepdaughter were blown away with the Toy Story ride and their first ever experience with elephant ears and funnel cakes. My niece tried to play grown up but when the minions came around she broke down to our age....(at this point we were all pushing 6 years of age). People let go of your youth and let it flow, this place at least for me is truly MAGICAL!

We were there Dec 26 to Dec 29 three day park to park, Harry Potter Forbidden Journey and Escape from Gringotts are both fantastic experience, but you need to get up very early to be there otherwise waiting line can be up to 300 mins, 180 mins is normal waiting time if you get there after 10 AM. So please use advantage of your early admission if you have. We found that two roller coasters Hulk and Rocket are a little less popular than KingKong or Minion, so after finishing the Harry Potter experience, you can take your Kingkong or Minion before the roller coasters. Also, after 8PM which is the Parade started happening, the coasters can be less people, you can rush to there for your second time. Here is the general suggestions from our three days trip, hope can help you guys. Also, the employees in Universal are very professional and dedicated. They are very good at organizing the long line. Thank you guys. Last tip is download the app Universal from your google store or apple. You can reverse your virtual line, check waiting time and even order food etc. from the app.

We came here during the off season during mid September. We also bought the express pass for an extra cost, but wasn't needed during the off season. We could have probably also done two parks in one day. It is probably recommend it during the high season though. Universal parks are more movie and more adult oriented than Disney. The rides were amazing, and the environment was very nice to wander around in. It felt like being on a giant movie set. There were also live acts around every once in a while and I enjoyed interacting and taking pictures with some of the characters. the rides that got crowded the quickest were the Minions ride and the Harry Potter rides. Either way, I would definitely recommend coming during the off season. It's a much more enjoyable experience whizzing through the lines and riding everything in one day.

So, we spent about $750 for 4 tickets and got on 5 rides over the course of 11 hours. The one ride my daughter really wanted to try was impossible to get on (Gringotts). The wait time at one point was 240 minutes! It never decreased below 200 minutes for our entire 11 hour visit. If I wanted to spend another $800 we could have used the express pass but people with express passes had to wait at least an hour for some rides. Unfortunately, greed has ruined Universal. They let far too many people in to the park so it's impossible to really enjoy the rides. You must wait in line (standing - no where to sit while you wait for 2.5 hours) for the majority of your park visit.

Getting fast pass in USS is a must even though it is pretty expensive. Nonetheless, it was worthwhile otherwise the queuing time is really ridiculous.  The parade was nice with good performance on show. The only lacking in this theme park compared to Disney which was their competitor is the fireworks.
Came during the blackout days so it was obviously very busy. Otherwise it was a blast. Wait times were not always crazy and the kids had a great time. We will totally be back in the future.

Had a great day here with my son! The rides were all fab - just a shame some had to be closed due to the weather (thunder and lightning) but all in all it was a great day out.  Loved the marvel themed land and the superhero parade - he loved the spiderman ride and the dr doom fall.  Will visit again and hopefully the weather stays nice!

We visited New Years Eve. Great way to end the year and ring in the new. Lots of activities for families or for young adult clubbing. Expect a long day and be prepared to wait about an hour for each ride during peak season. Loved they have free lockers to store belongings during rides. Would go back again.

We visited on 12/27, family of 14. We purchased Express Passes in the uk before arriving. When we arrived at the park we were sent to 3 different queues - everyone said there had been a problem recognising the passes the day before but no one was able to sort the problem very quickly. Having spent a lot of money to buy the passes we were kept waiting over an hour before they finally issued our passes. This lost us valuable time in the park and the world of Harry Potter was impossible to access by then. It was far from an express service and contrasted sharply with our experience at Aquatica where they had a problem with accessing there cabana bookings and just said ‘go through and enjoy the park and we can sort out payment later’. Even with the express pass we were denied access to some rides in the World of Harry Potter as we were told the queues were too long to let us in. The fast pass system at Disney is so much better!

Don't waste your time, or more importantly, your money on any of the Disney parks. Everything is outrageously priced, and the distance you have to walk from the drop off point to actually get in the park is ridiculous. Thank goodness for our bus drivers, they were fabulous, informative, and courteous. Although the parks were a huge disappointment, the customer service and staff were wonderful. Don't be like me and assume everything's like it used to be, because it's not. Do your homework. "Fast Pass" is a joke. We were there for two full days at two different Parks, and we were only able to ride three rides between the two parks because of Fastpass. Everything was priced ridiculously high, and for the money we paid to be there, we were extremely disappointed and let down. Walt would not be happy about this at all.

What can I say about Universal Studios. It brings out the child in you. I enjoyed every ride or set. I enjoyed transformers, fast and furious set . I would advise buying the express pass. But be forewarned, Universal Studios is an expensive place to go to. But the experiences are outstanding. and I can see why it so expensive in one way. But they need to bring down prices some. If you are a Harry Potter fan, this is the place to be. If you have walking issues please get a scooter to get around. This is a large place. Do one park a day.
Wife and I had so much fun. Much bigger than Hollywood CA. Would come back. Rides are awesome. Lots of food options. Do recommend paying for the VIP tour.

As you can imagine there is a pile of walking here. We did over 10,000 steps in the park. I have problems walking. We were four adults (Granny, Grandpa, Mom and Dad), plus two children 6 and 2. So, helpful hints: 1. Go Early, if you book your tickets online you can access the park earlier (8am). 2. Make sure you have downloaded the PDF on your email for the park entrance if you want to do it electronically on your phone. They don’t like screenshots. I had to open up my email and show them the original PDF. 3. Head to the back of the park to see the Harry Potter stuff first. Even so, the queue is about 50min long. Remember you have to dump your back packs st a locker first, or use Grandpa as the walking locker for all the gear. The queue for the lockers was about 10 minutes plus. 4. When you get through the entrance veer to the right and go up through the Simpsons area and then across the bridge. It is not crowded going this route. 5. Work your way back to the Minions ride and if you want to cut your wait time down, use the stationary ride queue. 6. We then went to the Simpsons (Krusty Burger) and had lunch, then did the ride. I would recommend doing the ride first, then lunch, as it is a bit bumpy. 7. Then do the ET ride, it isn’t busy. Bags can be taken on this ride. 8. Then do the Woody woodpecker roller coaster ride, again using Grandpa as the locker for all the packs. 9. Bring a small stroller, even if the kids may not need it. You can use it as a shopping trolley, carry all thing. 10. Walking back out of the park, don’t stop until you get to the boardwalk tshopping area, then stop and get an ice cream. Take it to the Starbucks outside seating, as it is in the afternoon shade. This gives you a break, before the final push to the car park. Enjoy!

I loved visiting Universal during the Holiday season. My 18 year old, 22 year old and myself loved it. We visited both Universal & Island of Adventures. Opted to take the shuttle offered from the hotel but in the future will just use my car and pay to park. During my trip the weather was in the 40s and made waiting over 30 minutes for the shuttle bus unbearable. Love that Universal offers you to bring snacks in the park, it helped save us money, also you can bring in water bottles. In the future would love to go duing the week, we went the Saturday before Christmas the wait times weren't too bad, but definitely want to go during the week. Will definitly go back!!!

We absolutely loved visiting Universal Studios. Every area is so well themed. We really enjoyed the Jimmy Fallon ride -which was the surprise of the day. We knew the Harry Potter bit would be amazing, and have been on the Simpson's ride, Mummy coaster, and MiB before - but what they did with JF and crew was just so trippy and fun. We also really, really appreciated the virtual line. Great idea. Too bad it's not available for Minnons - which we never did get to see because of lines, and don't get me started about the insanity of trying to even get close to the Gringot's ride. Our fault though, we knew that the holiday rush would be on, but seriously... wow. Too. many. people.  To their credit, the employees were absolutely fantastic. Friendly and willing to help even when people were not being their best. I sat in the Central Park area and just crowd watched for awhile. If you have time, do that. It's so entertaining. I was also impressed at how much there is to do and look at. I am glad they haven't completely dismantled the old Hollywood area. Looking forward to seeing what goes into the old Terminator ride. BTW - fan boy alert. The gift shop that was the exit for that ride is off the beaten path and chock full of cool things to look at and buy - it's where the DC comics can be found as well as Star Trek and Dr. Who (!) stuff.  We also always enjoy the Monster Magic/make-up show. It's the same old script and gags, but they make it work, and it's a wonderful break from the crowd. We remember when there was more backlot/movie insight shows - like the one on sound. Wish some of that were still available. I know it's not as whiz bang cool as the HP stuff, but it added something unique to this park that you can't find anywhere else.  Speaking of Harry Potter. Wow!! Magic. Take time to go talk to the conductor and "head" on the knight bus. That may have been the highlight of that day.  As the management continues to update the Studios, I hope they do more with the water- seems under-used now. Glad you kept Lombard's Landing - make a reservation and treat yourself to an excellent sit down, seafood meal.
For those who love movies, this is the place. Although in December the lines were way too long, it worth the visit.
it was really crowded that day and its hard to get to the rides since the line was so long. but overall it was a great trip

Excellent family friendly outing. Very entertaining and safe. While easy to say expensive, what you get for well maintained services, rides, property and not showing signs of age, are reasons to pay top dollar.  The fast pass option is better managed than Disney and far easier. Would suggest the park to park option with Islands of adventure as well.  Note the following: Mythos Restaurant for lunch a must! But book in advance. Arriving very early like Disney early park hours not needed with the ultimate fast pass option. But only needed in Peak Season. The minions ride is awesome. Put your head against headrests for roller coaster rides. Heavy vibration will lead to discomfort  Enjoy!!!

Went during Mardi Gras time and the lines on most rides were non-existence, except for a few popular ones that took hours. The parade was fun and festive. Weather was perfect in 70s. We stayed at a near by hotel that provided a shuttle bus back and forth. We also took Uber rides and the service/price was good. Foods options were decent and the prices weren't too expensive. Harry Potter was a big hit for our tween, make sure you get the park-to-park ticket in order to ride the train. Of course, HP merchandise and HP theme restaurants are way overpriced.

Well themed, great rides. We got a special access pass for our disabled daughter which was a simple process at guest relations. ET ride, meeting the transformers and simpsons ride were favs and the mini parades with characters like spongebob were fab. No where on the scale of Disney parades but short and sweet. Definitely recommend for families or singles/couples. Some big rides too. Id say not as good as Disney for young children. My youngest daughter was 4 and I wouldn't have taken her without older children as alot she could go on but for older children great

Visiting Universal was my daughter's desire for her 9th birthday, and decided to take that challenge. She wanted these theme parks cause she is Harry Potter fan, of course the area of Harry Potter world is done amazingly! We visited in the middle of Jan, it was crowdy but ok. The longest we had to wait was 40 mins. I would say this park is not for young kids, my 9yrs old could do all rides except the Hollywood rip it roller coaster, my youngest 4 yrs old could do 9 rides, which was ok. For me personally there were too many 4d/3d rides, by the end of second day I was feeling sick. I am more roller coaster person, but in general I really enjoyed our visit.

First let me say i really enjoy most of the rides at Universal Orlando. Rip Ride, The mummy, transformers, escape Grigots and others are all very well done. But my recent experience on Fast amd Furious was awful. Found it to lack imagination amd i felt that it was an attempt to utilize the kong technology in a way that really doesnt work.  In my opinion i would say that it woukd have been better to combine the budget of Jimmy falon and fast furious into 1 outstanding experience rather then 2 separate mediocre rides.  Really was a let down!!

We visited in May 2018 as a family of 6 adults and 2 under 5's.  We were lucky to have Express Passes for both days and this really helped us enjoy our two days as we got to see and do so much more.  Where to start, the Universal experience is second to none. The staff are incredible, so friendly and attentive and the customer service is first class.  A huge mention of thanks to Corey at the Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit for explaining to our 5 year old why he could not go on the ride, but then giving him a pass for the next time we visit when hopefully our son is taller. A really nice touch.  And a huge thanks to Gary the US Veteran who assisted us getting on the Skull Island: Reign of Kong Ride. Gary was chatty, friendly, helpful, and just a real credit.  There are so many rides, and we loved the majority we went on. The only let down of a ride for us was the Fast and Furious ride. I really did not enjoy the experience and was pretty let down by it, but this was a minor snag and the only snag over our two days at the park.  My son loved it, and there was loads to see and do for an inquisitive 5 year old, and he loved being able to go on the rides with all the family.  In my opinion on this holiday to Florida Universal can show Disney how it is done. Thank you to all the staff we encountered

Once you accept to pay the price for it, you can enjoy a wonderful day at the Universal studios! You are plunged into the atmosphere of all those different movies, from Hulk to Jurassic park and off course the unbelievable Harry Potter! You have shops, roller coasters, sceneries all perfectly in the themes. Seeing the potential waiting lines, I would still advise to miss the busy days to enjoy the park at the fullest.

Although we did have a fun time I found that the rides were pretty much all the same. Yes they have different themes but most of them are 4D where you wear glasses, which goes with the overall idea of universal but you can get a better mix at some of the other parks. Also the prices were absolutely outrageous. In order to not have 2 hour wait times we decided to purchase the express pass (which if you don't expect at least hour long waits for every attraction) with that said - my husband and I went just the two of us for one day and spent almost $600 I find that completely ridiculous and not worth it.
This place is amazing, it makes you feel like in a movie, is perfect for family trips, the best part is the world of harry potter!
I love this theme park. Its well laid out, clean and all the staff are so helpful and so in character. The clapping at the ends of rides and hyping up the park goers is fun.

The express ticket very expensive but only way to do all the rides !!!!!! Great fun - very clean - park ! Some rides (et) very dated !!!!! Many rides on same theme - spray with water - burst of flame but hey still fun !!!!!

No matter which park you go to Express pass is a must! Line wait times were cut from 60 minutes to 10! This park can be done in a day completing it in a clockwise/counter-clockwise rotation with or without the extra hour. Characters pop up for meet and greets throughout the park and a cute parade takes place during the day.

This was my first visit to Universal Florida. I enjoyed being there for 2 and a half days. But overall I was pretty disappointed. Most of the rides are 3 D or 4D where you see the movie and your chair moves around. These moving chairs are pretty hard on my back. Many of the rides have long lines for a very short ride. They had a parade of 3 floats. I do not ride the big rollercoaster or the children's rides so there was limited riding for me. The parks are crowded and very few signs telling you where are are going. I rode my scooter from one park to the other twice trying to find my way to City Walk. Each day I was there I had to ask how to get our of the parks. I was staying at the Royal Pacific and I spent 15 minutes looking for the entrance to the hotel walkway. It is hidden and very difficult to find. Harry Potter is very crowded and difficult to enjoy.
Excellent lay out and parks and rides. Great prices and fair prices on food and merchandise. This place set the bar for expectations of theme parks.

This one is definitely meant for the teens and adults in the group. We had a two year old and could only do a couple things with her in Simpsons and that was about it. Harry Potter is an absolute must see though

We have no idea how so many folks can afford these amusement parks. If you don't get the Express Pass you rate as a second class citizen that has to wait in line, and that's not good! Fortunately we had free passes from our hotel. Our favorite ride was the Fast & Furious attraction. Excellent atmosphere and the garage area was well done. The activity with the live cast members was typical corny but cute. No one was here early in the morning and we went on it twice. Try to sit on each side to get different experiences. The right side is best with Vin Diesel action. For lunch we made the right choice at the Monster Cafe. This was totally cool with themed dining rooms called Crypt Dining and Swamp Dining. Clips of old monster and sci-fi movies were being played on the TV screens like 'Creature from the Black Lagoon', 'Frankenstein', and 'The Invisible Man'. We ordered BBQ Brisket Sandwich with coleslaw in the sandwich ($15.49) and seasoned fries that we split. Also we purchased a Chocolate Sabayon cake ($3.29) for dessert. It was a light, not too sweet, cake with whipped cream frosting. Everything was quite delicious. We also recommend getting the all day drink which still is pricey at $15.99 but the combination soda fountains are a blast to try. Most flavors were excellent! After lunch we went on more rides. The ET ride is really getting old and definitely showing its age. It's amazing that it hasn't changed in decades. Skip it if you have done it before. ET wasn't even spitting out the names at the end of the ride. Time to retire this relic. The park was not too crowded in late January and we couldn't imagine visiting during holidays, spring breaks, or even during the summer heat. Plan accordingly and you will have fun, just bring the $$$$.  Show less

Brilliant 10 night visit to universal studios! Suitable for all ages and rides are amazing! Harry Potter is amazing and all the rides never disappoint! Got busy the week before Xmas so make sure you do it before hand to make the most of the park!

I have been going to Universal Studios Orlando and Islands of adventure for many years, and I have always enjoyed their parks since I was young. I visited both parks yesterday and came to a very disappointing conclusion, Universal has gotten very lazy with effort they put into the design and execution of their rides.  Universal has many great rides from the past. The mummy with it's mixture of practical effects,CGI,and roller coaster element make it a truly remarkable ride. The wizading world of Harry Potter is a crowning achievement of human ingenuity and imagination. Universal also offer many other excellent coasters. Sadly though, for the newer rides like the new Fast and Furious ride, Kong , Jimmy Fallon's race through new york, and the Transforms ride, Universal had decided to use a rinse and repeat format.  Each of these rides follows the same basic principle. They put you in a car that then moves into a room that has a giant screen, then a CGI movie will play and the apparatus you are in will shake and bump until to CGI movie is over. These may look aesthetic, but offer no depth or ingenuity. It feelS as though the creator wanted to take the cheapest route possible. From a business perspective I understand their line of thinking, but as a consumer I feel very let down. If you add in shrek and descipcable me that would make a total of 6 rides that follow the same format!  Since I have been attending Universal for many years, I have noticed in these new rides that many aspects of them are reused from older rides. For example, in Kong you see a giant Kong from the chest up that is the exact same Kong from previous Kong rides in the 90's! Same pose and everything! The Fast and Furious ride slap a new coat of paint on the previous earthquake trains from the previous ride in that location, and the list goes on.  The is not what I have come to expect from a multi billion dollar theme park. We come here to see something truly remarkable, not watch movies in a moving chair. Me , my wife and all 3 other couples felt the same way.  Universal I ask you to put forth the same effort in any future developments you have in the Mummy , Hulk, all of Harry Potter and many other great rides. Throw away this all CGI mindset and offer a mixture of practical effects, CGI, and imagination. When you release a new ride it should be just that new.

Took my granddaughter age 6 she loved it...the technology, 3 D rides interactive rides. She loved the superheroes, they had arcades, and of course Harry Potter she had to get her magic stick...this is definitely exciting heart pounding rides...

We had several people who worked hard to fix a problem with our tickets. Jorea, at the hotel guest services and Drew at Park Guest services. They went out of their way to fix the problem fixed and were very friendly while working on it. Also at the Leaky cauldron restaurant, Ernest was taking our order while wearing his invisibility cloak. He was very entertaining and staying in character. He was never silly just so much fun. Also Simon who works at the Knights Bus with a talking head kept us entertained. When he was there he always drew a crowd and was so much in character you just knew he was right from the movie. While at Universal look up these people they will all make your day happier

Such a fun place to visit. My daughter hadn't been there since she was 5 so it was so fun to take her again now that she's 12. She had so much fun and it was so great we were able to get a lot of pictures with the characters who were walking around. Lines were great, most rides it took us longer to walk up to the line then to actually get on the ride. Another great trip here!!

I’m a big fan of the universal studios theme park in Orlando. This was my 4th visit to the park and I was blown away even now as an adult by the sheer scale of it all.  Diagon Alley:  You will really feel you have entered the world of HP as this area has been faithfully recreated from the ground up based on the films. There are classic HP locations and the butterbeer tastes great. I would recommend having the frozen variant. There are shops where you can buy souvenirs and robes from the movies and wands based on every character. You can even take a turn down a creepy road and wind up in Knockturn alley where Borgin and Burkes shop of horrors awaits. Later on we checked out the Escape from Gringotts dark ride. This is where my criticisms come in as the ride stopped 3-4 times while we were on it due to technical difficulties. It ruined the immersion of the whole experience as we waited several minutes each time for the ride to start again. Luckily we got an immediate re-ride but perhaps this ride can use some maintenance.  If you are a Roller coaster fan I would highly recommend the Hollywood Rip ride rock it coaster (hope I got the name right!). Its a crazy thrill ride in which you can pick a song to jam to as you zip and zoom on the coaster. We went on this twice!  Other great rides are Jimmy Fallon race through new york and the simpsons ride which are both 3D.  Rides that aren’t worth it:  1) Fast and Furious Supercharged: Total waste of time. We were put on a lame bus which was very slow while screens next to us showed characters racing in cars. As its based on the fast series I expected a high velocity car chase but most of the ride is spent watching Ludacris talk from a screen. SKIP!  In terms of photos you can purchase awesome Moving photos from diagon alley just like in the HP movies but they are around 80 bucks which was too expensive for us. Pretty cool however.  Overall an amazing trip and we cant wait to come again!

Here’s a list of good and bad attractions if you had to queue more than 15 minutes. Good:- - Ripe Ride Rockin’ Rollercoaster - Escape from Gringots - Transformers - Shrek - Simpson’s Ride - Mummy Ride - Men in Black Bad:- - E.T. - Fast and the Furious - Jimmy Fallon Race through New York  What’s good is that if your only adults then you can easily do the park in a day by just going on these key rides. If your with kids and the weather is good then just do some of the rides but spend time in the Curious George splash park in the kids area. This and the Horror Makeup show are the best things about this park. Beyond the splash park there’s an indoor play area for smaller kids. An easy hour of fun. My top tip is to go on the disposable me ride as soon as it opens as it’s always got long queues and therefore haven’t been on it because I didn’t want to wait an hour with kids.

The layout is massive, plenty to do for every interest, LOTS of walking. Very relaxing way to spend a day. Expensive, but once in a lifetime trip. Harry Potter lovers will be in heaven! Street shows like Blues Brothers awesome!

As a Florida resident I go to Universal Studios/Islands of Adventure more than I’d Like to. When I first went, many years ago, I felt like it was all fire in my face and head thrashing. I didn’t care if I ever went again. Years later a group of friends wanted to go, so I went, hesitantly. It was better, maybe because it was friends and not family. I ended up getting an annual pass. The pass ran out and I again stopped going. Last year I went once, and again last month. I’m back to feeling like it’s all smashing you around and banging your head. It’s just not for me.
Had a pleasant day, only couple of rides rest was stimulators, over price in shops, over price tickets for what we had and food was abit pricey, I can go to a cheaper theme park!

Just finished 4 consecutive nights of Universal’s new Mardi Gras 6:15 pm parade. Runs from Feb to April. What a great show and parade. Our kids(and us)could nt get enough of it. 10 floats one better than the next with thousands of beaded necklaces being thrown to the spectators. Dancers and side shows. Just a great family time. Cudos to you Universal for creating such a great show We will be back. If you are in the area it’s worth the trip in addition to the simulator attractions.

Spent most of the day at Universal Studies in Orlando today. Must say it was horribly disappointing. Where Disney parks have charm, whimsy and seamless operations, Universal seems to delight in extracting maximum money for minimal entertainment. Even Harry Potter worlds, while lovely in their authenticity to the books, left me cold with their endless merchandising. Worse yet, Universal seems to think that moving platforms and 3D screens are an adequate replacement for real roller coasters. What a let down!

Something for all ages. It was worth it for us to purchase passes that allowed us to go through the express lines. Many of the rides had warnings of speed and elevation with drops but we avoided those and did find a few that we considered better for our age group. Lovely watching the families do activities together!

Nom and I went to Halloween Horror Nights 2018 during the week, after a great experience in 2017. Sure it costs a good chunk of change, but it's fun and worth it, especially if you splurge on the express passes, which shorten the wait time in the, at times, VERY long lines for the different houses. Every year they have a theme, and in 2018 it was based on some classic haunts - Halloween (the movie), Child's Play, etc. The houses are short but have great detail, and there is plenty of things to see, like the scare zones, that also entertain the guests. So yes, easily over $300 for two people, but it's worth the visit! Nom and I love it and will be back in 2019, our third consecutive year!
Go to universal at least 3 times a month as we are pass holders. We love it there between and rides, shows and parades. We love watching the blues brothers show. We always have a great time there

Second visit to Universal. Tried different rides to previous visit. Transformers ride was out of action for about 40 mins until announcement informed us the ride was broken, with no advice of resume time. Left the ride, and of course so did many others, making the next rides a huge wait. Not a great experience that day. Really good idea to plan what you’re doing, and what you can’t go home without doing, it alleviates the walking around aimlessly, and safeguards your time. Do the Fast n Furious, it’s NOT scary, but great fun.

We loved this section of Universal Studios. All of our favorites- the Simpsons, Diagon Alley, transformers, and the Mummy were in this part. I highly recommend staying on site so that you can take advantage of the early park entrance.

I was able to experience Universal for three days in February. I traveled with two daughters age 13 and 11. I was surprised by the lack of variety in the rides, everything is pretty much virtual reality. I was also surprised by the adult nature of the rides. They were loud, intense, scary, and slightly mysogynistic, really Fast and Furious, is that what women look like going to a party? There was a lot of public drinking, which leads to a lot of public intoxication. Though I will say the park is nicely laid out, and can handle crowds well, and Harry Potter is amazing, the experience was nothing unique or spectacular. All the employees we saw, with the exception of the Harry Potter employees, were high school and college students who seemed to be going through the motions rather than happy and excited about their jobs. In all the Harry Potter locations that was different the employees really were enthusiastic, helpful, and of a variety of ages. I also couldn't help notice how unaccessible it was for anyone in a wheelchair.

Had one day to visit Universal. Huge fans. Then get up to the gate and it is just shy of $1000 CAD for a family of four for one day! 10 hours, 1000? Such a rip off! Come on. Why do you hate us Canadians?

Our 3rd trip here, and again we had a great time. The Harry Potter areas are fantastic, especially now that your Express Pass works on those rides too. We have always stayed at the Hard Rock to take advantage of the included Express Passes, and HIGHLY recommend it. Not inexpensive, but the wait times can get very high without Express.. The Fast and Furious ride was a letdown. Could have been so much better. Food choices are noticeably better than at Disney. It's nice to not have to plan ahead to get into a restaurant.

DONT WASTE YOUR MONEY!!! We went to universal studios near Halloween 2018 so if you had a standard park ticket, they kicked you out early for ‘fright night’ ticket holders. These cost extra to the standard park tickets, so just another way to get more money. Don’t go over Halloween if you plan for a normal visit basically, your day is cut short and price is the same.  SHORT HOURS don’t listen to google!! After googling the parks opening hours, it stated the park was open until 7 but at 5, they shut all their eateries and restaurants so we couldn’t even get anything to eat. My husband and and I were starving after a day in the parks but all cafes were closed. When I asked a member of staff if I can buy an ice cream, they said I’d have to leave the park to do so. I was told by Universal customer services that the reason they shut all their restaurants 2 hours earlier is so staff can get home in time.  RUDE STAFF!! The staff were SO RUDE which I found disappointing as everyone we came across in Florida prior were lovely. I’m from London so I’m used to people being rude but it was a huge shock even for me!! We were shoved on and off rides, people were actually shouted at by staff, they’re short tempered, extremely rude and very unhelpful. They’re busy fooling around with each other and generally don’t want to be there! Generally ruins your experience and your left feelings a bit bullied.  CR*PPY FAIRGROUND GAMES $$$ Too many fair ground games. They had lots of basketball hoop games, the ones when you win a cr*ppy prize for getting a ball in the hoop. For some reason there were loads of these scattered round the park. You had to pay extra for them and the prizes were terrible!! I can get that at Brighton pier, don’t expect to see it at such an infamous, expensive theme park like universal studios. You already pay enough for entry & they want you to spend money winning a cheap nasty teddy. Really ruins and cheapens the whole experience.  DOESNT LIVE UP TO THE LEGACY! Took away their classic movie ride!! I’ve always wanted to visit universal studios, being a huge movie fan, it’s been a dream of mine. They took away the jaws ride, terminator ride, back to the future ride & other classics which was quite sad. After saving for our anniversary trip, I can not stress how disappointing the whole entire day was! Please PLEASE beware before you go! It’s far too much money for what you get! And universal studios DO NOT REFUND regardless of your experience. I’ve had to give it 1 star purley because of the price compared to experience/ disappointment
Great venue. Great rides. Get the Express Pass to move up in the lines ($50 but worth it). Don't miss the Harry Potter attractions. Great fun.

While we had a nice time at the parks overall, the prices are ridiculous and the parks are just "good". More shopping and dining than shows and attractions. Visually the parks are neat, but if the lines weren't so long there would be little to do to fill a whole day. If you bring a family, dining in the park gets as expensive as admission. All said and done, with parking $, admission $, and dining $ we do not feel the value is there. Glad we saw it once, but won't be coming back.

Some very cool rides. My 8 year old son even liked Fast and Furious ride.. What made even better was the Mardi Grass, perhaps the only time you can be to such type of event with kids. The Mummy, Simpsons, Harry Potter rides are a must.

Universal visit is not cheap… at least not for a swede when 1 dollar costs over 9 SEK. We paid over $400 for a day pass for 2 to 1 park and 1 pass to both parks for 1 day. Of course the park is awesome and fun to visit once, but there are probably many other parks at least as nice as this for half of cost… Then you need food- a slice of pizza $10, slush $6, Little icecrem $6-7 etc. We had luck that there was´nt so long waiting times for the rides when we were there (ca 10-15 min), but we heared that there could be waiting times at 2-3h sometimes, then it definitly would´nt be Worth for going there if you could just try some attractions during the whole day. We found all the attractions we tryed intresting so.
Always worth it for 2 reasons. Harry Potter rides and The Hard Rock cafe. Never disappointed in these areas.

This was our first time here. It was AMAZING. The rides were so fun, and brought back memories of the movies and television shows they were based on. The buildings and sets were so detailed that it was entertaining just looking around. The food was delicious. Highly recommended. Here's a tip if you're going. You could spend a whole day at either Universal or Islands of Adventure. If you try to do both parks in one day, it will be difficult to see everything. You need the 2 park ticket to ride the Hogwarts Express ride. If you have a couple days to spend (and if you can bear skipping the train ride), I would skip the 2-park option and do one park per day. If you have extra money, an express pass will save you a LOT of time in the queues.
My grandchildren loved all the different areas. Their was areas for toddlers and older children. The food selections were great. Of course Harry Potter area was fantastic.
If you're a Harry Potter fan, which we are, you'll love it. Jurassic Park, Kong and Spiderman we're good too. I feel like it's all about Harry Potter though.

I've been to a lot of theme parks but this one tops them all, especially if you are a big film buff like me. Ensure you DO NOT visit on a weekend unless you would like to queue all day, we went on a Tuesday in February and the longest line was 20 minutes for Transformers in both parks. Although you need to plan carefully and definitely start off in Diagon Alley. The tickets were worth the money. The only negative points are that E.T. & Men in Black badly need to be removed, totally outdated rides and unenjoyable compared to the rest.
Went there with my family and the top attraction was the world of Harry Potter, it was like being a part of the movies!
You'll have to save your pennies, as this park gets more expensive every year, but Harry Potter soothes the sting a bit.

I thought there was no way I could spend a day and a half st Universal, but I was really wrong. In addition to the rides, there are pop up shows in the streets and lots of parades. There’s always something exciting happening there! Diagon Alley is breathtaking whether or not you’re a Harry Potter fan (and be sure to try that butterbeer!), and many of the rides are excellent — worthy of riding more than once. The roller coaster requires that you use a free locker before you get in line, and there is a metal detector, so be sure to use it. The Mummy was surprisingly good, as was the Transformers ride. And don’t miss the Escape from Gringotts! However, I highly recommend that you get a Universal Express pass. We were able to ride three to four rides an hour while regular park patrons were able to ride that many in one whole day.

We bought the 2 day PTP tickets and lucky there was a promotion that gave us 2 more free days. As a result, we didn't have to rush. We didn't buy the FastPass due to the promotion. It was a fun place overall. GOOD - water fountains everywhere, restrooms are clean (check out Moaning Myrtle in the ladies' washroom near King's Cross). We are big fans of HP so for sure ride on Gringotts. The dragon on top of the bank gave out fire once in a while so stay for it. Must try the butter beer soft serve ice cream at the ice cream store at Diagon Alley. Try butter beer as well (hot and cold), both very good although expensive ($7.5). There is a phone booth in front of King's Cross, dial MAGIC and listen to the message. My teenage daughter stared at the rotary phone and didn't know what to do! Do single rider if you can, it's faster than Fastpass and it's free! You however, will bypass all the displays that lead up to the ride but you can ask the attendant to let you inside to see the sights without riding again, saving a lot of time. We enjoyed the show "tales of Beedle the Bard" very much. Mardi Gras parade was also fantastic to watch. BAD - not enough restaurants/food stalls near Wizarding World, slow service.The outdated technology in Shrek 3D needs to be replaced. We waited over 70 mins for Minions. Just felt like we were waiting/standing in line all the time and the ride takes less than a few minutes.
We went as a family on spring break. It had everything we expected. The newer Harry Potter section is a little confined/cramped. But it is a great addition to the park.
Love love love this place. If you follow the app, you aren't waiting for very long. Early admission is the way to go. I dont like eating inside the parks. Too expensive and not the best food.

Universal is better than Disney hands down for older children! They also have parks for the little ones too! I’m a travel agent and we had free park to park tickets. Universal studios and Volcano bay (water park with universal) super fun! If you’re a Harry Potter fan, this is the place to go!
amazing 3D rides like transformers,the latest Jimmy fallon ride, harry potter- efg but 3 hour wait time. Must go on thrilling rides such as revenge of the mummy

If you're a big fan of Halloween, then this is the event for you. Universal does it right, costumes, theming, shows and most importantly the haunted houses. I will say it's not the event for kids that frighten easy or even adults because it is crazy scary. The wait times for the houses were somewhat long but it also depends on the night, research a bit before you go. Some of the rides are closed but not many and those wait times are fairly short, check the Universal website and it will list them. The scare actors were fantastic and always stayed in character, and the Academy of Villains show was outstanding!!! I would go again in a New York minute.
The simulators are so much fun. The shows are a nice break. Bring your patience, comfortable shoes and clothes. Lots of picture opportunities.
Please make park passes out of plastic, NOT paper! Paper park passes just can’t survive water rides & rainy days!
We love making Universal Studios one of our theme park choices when we visit Orlando! Lots of simulator rides. One of our all time favourites is The Mummy. Can’t wait to visit again!

The park is fine and clean, the staff is friendly and dining was moderately priced. On the other hand, I found it very expensive and the lines were very long. However, If you are going for the popular rides, then it’s worth getting the express pass but again it is not that cheap. The mummy, men in black, harry potter, the simpsons and the roller coaster are the ones I enjoyed.
Awesomeness ! Great characters, great fun. A must do for all Orlando fans. Something new every time we go.

Been 10 years since our last Orlando trip - so great to see changes to the two parks universal has. The Harry Potter additions are very popular with all ages and have to say well worth the trip.  Tips: if you are going - do take a lanyard with card holder as the way the express fast pass system works now it will help if you have them so you can have your passes easily to hand. The rides now need you to stow your gear into lockers so keep your stuff small so you can use the free lockers.

Universal studios Florida is a great vacation destination for the family. I have 3 kids 10 to 15 and they loved this place. There are different ride levels for all ages. Great food choices and selection and we found that the food venues were very helpful for our gluten free needs/allergies. We had tickets for the two parks (not the water park) and easily spent two days trying to do it all and there was still lots to do that we will have to do next time. This is a great place but it can be crowded and so be prepared to wait.

Our last visit had 3 of the main attractions inoperative. We left early because we were not finding much to do. Now that you have to pay a hefty up charge to visit both parks Universal isn’t anywhere near the value it once was.

You should know if there is a q line at a restaurant it going to be a long time  3 in the afternoon lines of 45 minute in restaurants we tried 3 different ones all the same  Don’t waste money on 15.99 refill cup many stations long lines then no ice in machine and warm drinks after waiting in drink line  I guess I am a long time Disney fan 300 visits in 25 years only 2 visits to Universal most-likely my last  Right after arriving the up escalator not working and had to climb 3 flights of stairs not even to the entrance yet

Lots to do, see & eat for all ages. We stayed at one of the resort hotels to make the most of our 2 days there. The Harry Potter light show was amazing! We had a 3 day pass so chose to go back on the way to the airport to kill some time, just avoid the water rides if you do so. Would go back for sure

We came as a family of four in the first week of April. Although it was fun I wouldn't say it was worth the expense. My advice would be to get there as early as possible, allow plenty of time to pay for parking and to walk from the car park to the entrance. We managed to get quite a few rides done between 9 and 10.30 before it got too busy. We didn't buy fast track passes but I think on a really busy day you would have little option but to buy them. Personally, with the exception of those with disabilities, I think everybody should wait in the same queue.

By far one of the best parks in our view. But you need to get up early and get to the park for when it opens . Parking very easy albeit $25.dont be puffed into premium parking $40-50 on season its really not worth it to save 5 mins walking time.  Need to visit Harry potter world, just like the film, attention to detail is very impressive. expect to que 45 mins+ when busy for rides. Best rides  Simpsons, minions, transformers and mummy..., avoid E.T its 30 years old.  Quick Q tickets 2 options $100 to skip que for every ride once, or unlimited $130. if u can afford it, good luck, we got there early and waited about 10-15 mins each ride. Afternoon 45-55 mins. One trick is to go into single que riders which can cut times down to 10 mins, dot worry if u have kids as all rides finish in the souvenir shops, we did with our kids 9/10 yrs where they just waited for us.  conclusion ,its ability to put a smile on your face matches it's ability to destroy your wallet!!
We all loved this park more guided to the "big" kids, loved the all the shows and rides, highly recommended

I am writing this review while I wait in a 120 minute queue for 7 Dwarfs Mine Train at Magic Kingdom... yes, 2 hours! My husband and I are late 20-30 somethings, no kids, and we were totally spoiled by our visit to Universal Studios earlier this trip. The single rider line is AWESOME! We went on Escape from Gringotts TWICE in about 20 minutes when the park first opened. We also rode Rock It Roller Coaster 3 times using the single rider option (and once we even got to sit together!)  Diagon Alley is awesome, go to Ollivanders at the end of the day, no one will be there. People say the staff at Disney is more enthusiastic but so far that has not been the case for us, the staff at Universal were awesome! Special shout outs to Mr. Ollivander and the Knight Bus conductor, Jimmy Fallon’s barbershop quartet and Hashtag the Panda, and the guys doing the Fast and Furious pre-show.  Be warned, if you get motion sick (I do) there are a lot of simulator rides that might not be super fun. I survived the Mummy and Transformers (which got stuck twice when we rode it but they offered single use express passes to compensate) but Race Through New York was hard to get through and we skipped the Simpson’s altogether. ET was super cute though. If you stay later into the night you can get through the lines faster... and DO SINGLE RIDER WHEN AVAILABLE!!! :)  Ultimately I wish we had done 2 days at Universal so we could have also done Islands of Adventure and Hogsmeade! It’s expensive but it’s good value for your entertainment dollar (cheaper and less crowded than Disney, too.)

This is a Very Good Attraction; Advantages: Lots of Nice Restaurants! Fun Rides! Excellent idea of a Park-to-Park Train! Nice staff! Good idea of Kid-friendly amusements! Disadvantages: It's Expensive! It's usually very Busy! It takes at least 45 minutes to get on each Ride! There are even massive queues to get (a) Snack(s) and/or Drink(s) (about 30 minutes)! It's quite difficult to find a place to park a Car!

Had a 3 day pass at Universal Studios. Have to say compered to Disney it was not very good. Long walk in from the car park. If you don’t pay a lot more for a fast pass don’t bother you won’t get on a ride. As with Disney every thing over priced. We went at night to see if it was any better it was not. You expect to queue for the rides but I did not expect to queue to get into Hogsmede at night 😡. At night they do a light show on the Hogwarts castle Very nice. Expect you have to see it from the bridge in to hogsmede or around the entrance to the rides there. This blocks hogsmede off They won’t let you in to get to the shops or to get to the train. So if your thinking about going at night don’t bother. The park looks good but it is so disorganised you would not believe. With all the planing that goes into these things how could they get it so wrong.

We love Universal ! From Harry Potter land to The Hulk ride it's all worth the wait and money spent . Easter wasn't that busy at all and the weather was amazing which was all an added bonus . Food and drink expensive inside but good quality.
Need more restrooms Restrooms dirty and smell  Need healthy food options Limited food options Unless you like turkey legs, hotdogs, chips

This was a great day for all ages, we had my eldest nephew 14. Then my sister was there with my other nephews 7 & 9. Also their in-laws - this place is amazing, for all ages! A variety of rides and really is something for everyone. Jimmy Fallon racing through New York is super fast though I was shaking after!
We had a great time, make sure to book tickets early to do the fast passes. Wait time is extremely long for rides if you dont ( we learned this lesson).

Stupid regulations compared Disney, almost everything forbidden for them. Very simple attractions forbidden too, despite the similar are allowed at disney and other resort around. Volcano bay is even worst!! Allais y nothing for kids. We didn’t enjoy.  Without kid is great.

An absolutely fun place to visit for the whole family. Rides for all to enjoy. Drinks and food stalls, water is available all most stalls and refillable.Fast passes must be bought in advance as they sell out quickly. I really enjoyed every ride in the park. Tip:The line for singles are shorter and move fast.

The two universal parks are quite expensive and you also have to pay for parking each time you visit, even if you are just going to the cinema. A lot of the rides are simulators. Don't get me wrong some are good, Skull Island is probably the best. Fast and the furious is the worst. Harry Potter is great but is always insanely busy. Disappointed that there are a couple of roller-coaster spread over both parks.

It was a good day but preferred Disney. Too long to wait for most rides we wanted but made the very most of the day. Very expensive for one park for just one day. Our grandchildren are 6 and 9 and I definitely think this park is more suited to older children/teens or grown ups.

Took family here for the day, 2 park ticket - YOU ABSOLUTELY NEED FAST PASS. Queue's were long but with Fast Pass manageable. Lots of 3D/4D rides which suited me. Harry Potter World was quite amazing - Castle and train was superb. King Kong ride long queue and not worth really time, - Transfomers good, Shrek Good, Despicable Me good, Simpsons good, Kids liked Mummy ride, they didn't rate Fast and Furious. Tip bring sandwiches or food as expensive and queues very long for food in park.
The rides rock in the park. You must do Rip Ride Rocket, The Mummy and Diagonally. Harry Potter area is much better on Universal side.

I had a blast and stayed like 8 hours. The Potter part of the park was cool. Rides were all fun. Did get stuck 160 ft in the air on rip rock it coaster for 5 minutes which was anxiety filled but no real other complaints. Even had some tacos which were good. But damn man....122 dollars...per person. My wallet was fighting me trying to stay in my pocket
I have been there with my family , it was amazing and both children and adult were happy over-there.

Lines were less than 30 minutes on all reds, midweek in spring for a family of four. Wish we knew about the $80 photo pass where you get all your photos taken while in the park. Seemed like a good value but we weren’t offered that until later in the day. Also wish there was a better meal plan, but overall we had a good time.

My wife and I wanted to see the Harry Potter rides and shops. So we visited Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure on a Saturday. I enjoyed the Escape from Gringotts ride. We rode the Hogwarts Express in both directions. We did walk though the brick wall at Platform 9-3/4 at the King's Cross Station. I called the Ministry of Magic from the phone phone outside the train station, but the Ministry was closed.  I did many of the thrill rides (Men in Black, Revenge of the Mummy, Fast & Furious, Transformers, etc.). My impression is that the rides were imitating each other (go forward, go backward, spin around, stop, etc.), but with different scenery. That made the experience a little less enjoyable.  I was disappointed in the quality and variety of the merchandise at the Despicable Me Minion gift shop. I was hoping to buy some t-shirts or other items, but didn't find anything that appealed to me.  My wife and I enjoyed several of the shows such as Blues Brothers, and Celestina and the Banshees.  We opted to eat dinner outside the park at City Walk. There were many good restaurants there at reasonable prices.

We've spend a few days between Universal studios and Island of Adventure this May. We bought the tickets for 14 days using the 3 parks(the previous 2 and the Volcano bay which is a water park and was in the price ) and for 2 of these days we’ve had an express pass . (Which was a life saver).Universal is a place for children older than 6 for most of the rides and its very fun. The Harry Potter area is really nice but the train connecting the two parks is not worth the money. In general everything there from food to toys was very expensive.If you wanna avoid the crowds go there after 1800 and then you don’t have to pay for the parking

We chose universal after booking out accommodation in Kissimmee. Had great weather apart from a couple of days with some heavy shower's. Reccomend transformers, shrek 4d, kong skull island, fast and furious ,hogwarts express and many more. So much to do. And Hard Rock Cafe has to be added to and foodies list

What more can I say??  The only "blot" on an otherwise great park is the constant increase of simulator rides. I get space is more of an issue, but the Fast & Furious ride is meh at best.  Boy do I miss Jaws..

This was my third visit to universal. Stayed at cabana bay for 11 days, using their transfers to the parks, with our own early access entrance to volcano bay.  We did early access once but mainly went back in the evenings, walking straight onto rides. We did Disney a bit but now, as no kids, that universal is my favourite. I find it so much more organised, more space to walk around, better food outlets, better ques especially entering the park. I love the atmosphere and everything about universal. Roll on the new park coming in 5yrs time!!! Disney have nothing on this place

We absolutely loved Universal! It was expensive to get in but well worth it. Make sure to pay the extra to get into both parks on site. We went from open to close. The rides were fantastic! Not sure I’d recommend for small children but definitely great for 10 and up.

This was our 4th trip to Universal. We are not roller coaster people but we always find lots of great rides here! We love the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. Get butter beer you won’t regret it. There are many great places to eat. Recommend Mythos and either the leaky cauldron or three broomsticks. The crowd size and lines are always better than Disney even on busy days and we love that you can buy express passes and skip the lines.

We went to USF in December to celebrate both Christmas and my wife’s birthday! The highlights of this park were for our family!!  #1 Draigon Alley #2 Despicable me Minions! #3 The Christmas parade! #4 The Revenge of The mummy roller coaster!  We highly recommend these rides and experiences when you visit USF!
It was fun and awesome.The rides were absolutely fun. I really enjoyed it. I loved the Harry Potter ride.

Had a fabulous evening out with NTI attendees. Would have been better if there were more venues open for adult beverages....40 minute wait for a beer. Did have an awesome evening with new found friends!

The parks are great as long as it is not too busy, loved all the Harry Potter stuff, very impressive. The major downside with this place is the $25 parking charge which is daylight robbery considering how expensive it is to get in the place. They should offer a multi-day discount.

We started our day going to guest services to find out about accommodations for my daughter. She was just diagnosed with type 1 diabetes. Her doctor said to bring a letter to get a guest assistance pass. Dean, Kelly and Miguel said she didn’t need one. They were condescending, rude and talked down to me. They told us every que was inside with air conditioning. That was a complete lie. We were in several lines in direct sun and others inside that were stifling with no fans. They said workers would be there to give us a wheelchair if she needed to sit down. They said a worker would let her leave to go somewhere private to give herself her shot or to go to the bathroom and could get back in line. That wasn’t true either. We went from 40-60 minutes without seeing someone in multiple lines. We were told there were many places to get a drink or fill up water bottles in the lines. We saw a couple water fountains but they were hot. We were told we could bring our bag and use the medical locker. That was the only thing that was true but that added up to 10 minutes to our waiting each time. I feel like I was lied to about the “accommodations” just to get me out of guest services. Disney helped us with no questions asked. Stay away from Universal if you need accommodations of any type. They will not help you!

My experience in Universal was amazing! The people in the shops and conducting the rides were very welcoming and friendly. The roller coaster "Escape from Gringotts" is the number one ride you should try. It takes you through the scene when Harry, Ron, Hermione, and Griphook are stealing Gryffindors Sword from Gringotts. Take the magical Hogwarts express to Hogsmead! Visit Honneydukes to load up on some magical sweets! Or the Post Office to make an owl delivery! And to wrap it all up, go reward yourself with a steaming hot mug of Butterbeer! This is the best vacation Me and my family ever had!

This was our first time to visit Universal Studios Florida as a family and we had a great time. We mainly went to see the Harry Potter areas as my daughter had just finished reading the book series and they did not disappoint. We stayed onsite at Cabana Bay which was very convenient with the excellent bus service and also allowed us to access the park one hour earlier than normal.  The Diagon Alley area was our favorite part of the main park but we also enjoyed the Transformers ride, the Minion ride and my kids loved the Jimmy Fallon ride. Many of the rides utilize 3D technology along with the ride which is fun but somewhat repetitive. The waiting area for the rides is generally indoors or at least shaded which is very much appreciated.  Some of the rides and areas are looking tired and probably need to be reevaluated. Unless you are a huge Shark fan you should skip the ride. The technology is outdated and very glitchy. The entire kids area could use a refresh and we hope that area will be replaced by the planned Nintendo land.  Overall we had a fantastic experience and look forward to returning at some point in the future.
The rides and attractions are better than you think. My faves were the Transformers and Spidey Man. This is a fun place to go, but make sure you get the Express ticket. It's worth every dime.
love universal studios, not as hectic as island of adventure but still good to go and see. The blues brothers are not to be missed, a great day out.
The water rides at this park are by far the funnest we have ever ridden!! The food options were great and all park workers were very friendly!!!

Recently over the past 2 months I have ventured to the “other” Orlando theme park Universal with friends and family. Being annual pass member at the “original” Orlando theme park I have high expectations about service and experience. Universal did not disappoint on either. They are very different experiences for very different reasons. Universal does a great job of channeling people within the park. Also they have single rider lines that mover very quickly. Down side it is an expensive day for both parks. If your a Harry Potter fan it is Mecca for the enthusiast. Though you need a two park ticket to get the full experience sense the HP experiences are in both parks. The visual perspectives of the different areas in Universal are amazing. If you do one thing in Orlando it should be two words...The Hulk! I recommend checking out this park who put a great shopping, food and night life right in front of the two parks called City walk is a lot more convenient than Downtown Disney is to the Disney parks.

🧹 🏰 UNIVERSAL STUDIOS 🏰 🧹  We did the VIP experience, with Sean today and highly recommend it. *Saved waiting in ques for 60minutes *covered everything we wanted in the two park *best seats on the ride (for effects or the seats less likely to get wet) *walked around the back lot studios *learnt how the rides operate and safety measures taken *breakfast and lunch included  Was such an amazing day, the detail in the rides especially Harry Potter was mind blowing. Most rides were 3D/4D - simulators and felt like you were part of an experience. One of my favourite rides would have been the Harry Potter forbidden journey where Harry takes you on a trip high above Hogwarts and the castle grounds, where you are chased by Hagrid’s pet dragon, while the Whomping Willow and a hoard of dementors try to spoil the trip. It really did feel like you were flying over hogwarts and trying to get away from the dragon. Another good one was the jimmy fallon, where you actually felt like you were racing through and over New York City. Just amazing the feeling you get.

Although this visit was originally planned for our kids...we loved it even more I think! The Harry Potter section was just the most fantastic display I have ever seen at a theme park. The rides were great, easy to get around and we were able to see most of everything in the one day that we had to do two parks. If you had more time then spend the extra day. We rode the water ride at the end of the day...perhaps do it in the middle so you can dry off better...

Had three generations in the park. All enjoyed most parts of the park. Kids liked the Harry Potter exhibits. Adults enjoyed the rides and shows. Finally got to ride the "Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit" roller coaster, it did not disappoint, it was quite exciting!! Other rides liked by all were: Transformers, Minions, Simpsons, Men In Black, Race Through New York starring Jimmy Fallon. Of course it is very expensive to eat and even grab a soda or water, but what can you do. We all enjoyed the park overall.

Just got back from a two day visit to Universal. Traveling with two teens in over 90 degree heat is not easy. There is plenty to do and plenty of places to go in and cool down. Recommend taking an empty water bottle to refill during the day. There are water fountains everywhere. I brought a misting fan and cooling towels for myself because I don’t handle heat well... kids got the refillable cups and feel they got their money’s worth. Planned on staying until closing but everyone wasn’t exhausted by 5ish... use the app for navigating around the park and for wait times. We felt Universal Studios had more things to do.

Universal Studios is exactly what you would expect it to be. Plenty to do for the entire family. Rides that satisfy the young and old. Our first day at the park was a Monday and the lines were very short. We paid for express passes, but I’m not sure we needed them. Average wait time was about 5 min. So much to do, take your time and explore all the little things tucked away, especially at Diagon alley. Make sure to get some butter beer. Even if you aren’t a Harry Potter fan, the experience is really cool. Warning: if you are someone that gets motion sickness, be prepared. The thrill and 3D/4D rides will definitely cause some nausea. Take a water bottle and get refills at the water fountains or restaurants for free. You should also take a small backpack with snacks, that alone could save you a lot of money. If you have a multi-day pass, I highly recommend that you get some clear plastic ticket protectors on a lanyard to keep your tickets in. The ones in the park at $10 each. Overall a wonderful experience!

My favorite of the 2 parks at Universal Orlando. You can immerse yourself in the movies or enjoy a walk thru NY, San Francisco, or Rodeo Drive. Check out the concert series throughout the year that are free with admission to the park. If you are fortunate enough to visit during Halloween, make sure to purchase a ticket to HHN!

It's been years since we've been as our son hasn't been old enough, until this year.  Universal did an incredible job with their haunted houses. Stranger Things and Poltergeist were by far the best!  My son loved his first experience at 13 years old, and really loved all the special effects and jump scares (as he calls them).  We will be going back in 2019.
My favourite part is the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. I could just hang out in Diagon Alley or Hogsmeade all day!

Staying in Universal Cabana bay we visited frequently over a 2 week period. Only took advantage of the extra hour once, it’s not as you would think as many rides still don’t open until 9am.  Queues were varied depending on time of day. Gringotts ride was the longest we experienced - just over an hour. We found going to the park later in the day was best as it was less busy. My daughter aged 11 loved the Simpsons and Men in Black rides. We didn’t think the Fast & Furious rise was worth the wait and wouldn’t go back on this in the future.  We bought refillable souvenir cups, you can use them throughout stay recharging them each time for about $10. I thought food/drinks and merchandise was expensive in the park.  Light show around the lagoon at Park Closing time was fantastic, sorry I only stayed to watch it once on our last night. Really recommend this.

There is so much to do, you definitely need at least 2 days to do everything - unless you get an Express Pass. My kids, 8 & 11, loved Rip Ride Rockit and Diagon Alley...just be prepared bc the wands are between $46-52. The ice cream shop on Diagon Alley is fantastic.

We bought a 4 day park pass through the military so we had plenty of time to explore the parks. Most of the rides are indoors which is useful since we had afternoon thunderstorms. We spent most of our time in the Harry Potter section of the park. Be prepared to put out some money for wands and robes and food.  PHOTO PACKAGE: it costs $99 for a 3 day photo package but it’s worth the cost if you are into family photos. You have digital access to all character photos, ride photos, and photographers around the park. The downside is there are not as many photographers as Disney has.  AMEX Lounge: if you purchase your tickets with AmEx, there is a lounge available near Shrek in Universal studios.

On our holiday we’ve done the 4 main Disney parks, sea world, discovery cove and both main Universal parks. Universal Studios definitely won over Disney. It wasn’t too crowded, the facilities were well kept, the rides were fun and it didn’t come across like such a money grab as Disney where everything is there to get you to buy something.  My only real complaint (and this is true of Disney also) is the over reliance on 3D/4D “rides” where rather than build a proper ride, they cheap out and whack a screen in front of a “simulator”. This can work well (transformers, Simpson’s) or it can be just awful (fast and furious, jimmy fallon). It’s a shame to see rides like Jaws replaced by these simple, less creative ride types. Fast and Furious was probably the worst ride of our vacation due to its long boring build up followed by sitting in a “bus” full of other people to then just watch a screen while being bounced around a bit. Sitting st the front you’d assume would be the best position to rule out looking over everyone except I could see the rails the bus sat on so had next to zero immersion.  However overal, impressed and really enjoyed it

On the website, after reviewing the details over + over, I pressed Confirm and purchased 1 Day 2 tickets + 2 express passes for Universal Studios for JUNE 25. Then I received the order confirmation and looked at the mobile tickets and they were dated for JUNE 18 (the day I bought them @ 11:00PM, which technically shouldn't even be an option that late). I called customer service and they switched the dates with no problem (but no mobile option, have to do Will Call Kiosk...)  However, I am leaving this review here in case this happens to someone else as the customer rep says that this "happens often". I would be understandably upset if I didn't check my ticket dates when I did and was denied at the gate after spending all of this money. So in short, PLEASE CHECK YOUR TICKET DATES AFTER PURCHASING.

We visited both Islands of Adventure and Universal and had a great time. Food was good, the rides were a lot of fun. We had a pretty wide aged group(7-70) within our party and everyone seemed to have a great time. We only ran into one ride the closed down while we were in and we were able to use our fast pass on everything we wanted and had a blast.

3 adults and two kids with parking, tickets and fast pass it was expensive. They (universal) missed the mark in many areas. For example: ticket wickets are for too low for average height people, restroom layout could be improved for little boys in a hurry, not enough sitting room for those waiting for their party to complete a ride, gift shop layout not conducive to shopping when a ride lets loose. Maps just give general location. If you are into Harry Potter the layout is very well done, narrow streets, dark buildings, creepy things all about. You have to buy a two park ticket to ride the train and see all of Harry Potter. Universal is a great place if you want to wonder around aimlessly and wait in line now and then but it is not for me. Obviously there are many who enjoyed it because it was crowded everywhere. I am a bit bias because we did a day at magic kingdom, day at Epcot and a day at animal kingdom. I would recommend if you are doing Disney and Universal, do Universal first, let the fun and enjoyment build.

Bought the military appreciation tickets that allowed you to visit both parks for 4 days. You can honestly get done with both parks in 3 days unless you’re trying to do the new Harry Potter ride. That ride will make you wait for hours unless it rains then all outdoor rides stop due to safety reasons. Do the popular rides first so your wait time isn’t as long during the middle of the day. The last 2 hours in the park you can do more rides in a shorter wait time due to everyone leaving the park by that time. Stick around at the end of the night for the fireworks in either universal or island of adventure.

Park is not gay friendly. Many of the crew members are rude and have an attitude. They won't answer any questions without an attitude. My partner and I even overheard a crew member mocking us and telling the other crew members we were "the gays over there". Extremely poor for 2019. Charge slot. Express pass on Universal side is a joke. They have two separate lines to throw you into a line without everyone else anyways. Waste of money. Not the best experience do to a lack of training and personality with its employees.

I love theme parks, all of them. I first went to universal studios about 20 years ago, I loved it then but I loathed it yesterday. Mainly because I felt everything about it was based on a plan to extort money out of visitors. This may be there aim but it was relentless.  The park is split into two. Universal studios and islands of adventure.  We paid $130 each to get into universal. To buy a ticket to “que jump” was an extra $200 each! We declined. However, the number one attraction at universal is Harry Potter and the Hogwarts express. You CAN NOT take this ride unless you have a ticket for BOTH theme parks. Outrageously unfair.  There are few places to escape the heat. Restaurants tables are full of “reserved” signs, for those people who were lucky enough to know you could even reserve tables and how to do it!  You que for at least 50 mins per ride. 70 mins for Harry Potter. Apart from rides I couldn’t see what else was there to go for. All the back stage tours and family rides have gone. So your stuck if you don’t want to que.  Drinks and food are sky high in price, really sky high. And if you doubt my review, just make sure you have the $25 you will need to park before you get to the gate and pay $130 to get in!  Many theme parks in a Florida, Disney World is the number one of course. My advice? Leave Universal until last on your hols. If you have done all the others and have some cash left to spend then go. I won’t be going again.

Before visiting Orlando, everybody said, that Universal Studios was a "must see". Because of the very high price, I DID doubt whether it was worth it. It was! Yes, it IS expensive. And it should be cheaper. But I wouldn't have missed it. Out Family consisted of three kids (15/17/19) and they all loved the experience. I was warned about the waiting time. Expect one Harry Potter-experience, that had a wating time of 180 (!) minutes throughout the Whole day, everything was decent (=waiting times from 30 to 60 minutes). In general: Don't miss these themeparks (we went to Island of Adventure and Universial Studios … you can do both in one day).

We made this trip to celebrate our son's 10th birthday with a bang. Since he was entering his tween stage, we wanted to celebrate this milestone just as a family. Universal Studios turned out to be the perfect way to have a blast and eat some fun food. Obviously, our favorite section was Hogsmeade and Hogswart and I suggest you take the 2 park ticket to enjoy the Hogswarts Express ride both ways. The park is nicely runned, the staff is professional and courteous, and there are ample places where you can enjoy a good meal when you need a break. We loved the rides and we purchased the Express line ticket for one day. We appreciated having it although the Minions ride still took over an hour to get through. Most of the time, the wait in line was non-existant to 15 minutes which is quite acceptable. However, the cost of this ticket is quite pricey if you also want to enjoy the surroundings, take breaks, without running from one ride to another.
