Early admission from staying at a Universal Hotel made going into the minion ride a breeze! I was able to see the water show (which I wouldn't have known about unless I had gotten lost and stumbled into the Beverly Hills area! So wonderful - all of it. Restaurants are ample enough that you can get a great meal anywhere.

I have visited Universal Orlando yearly for 17 years. In the last few year arthritis has caused me bother standing for a long time. Last year I was given a Pass by guest services which allowed me to get a return time for rides and not have to stand in a long queue. This worked well and I used this only on the bigger queues for my holiday last year. This year I went to guest services with my expired pass from last year and asked for it again to be told no I wasn’t entitled to it. I was told to use a wheelchair if I couldn’t stand in a long queue !! For someone who may in years to come end up in a wheelchair I was mortified that this is how universals option for someone in my position. The girl (Stephanie) at guest services wasn’t interested and couldn’t give me an answer when I asked how last year I was entitled to it and now with a generative disease like arthritis which only gets worse, I was not entitled to it this year !! Having read a few similar reviews on this exact subject I think universal are doing a poor job at assisting people with medical conditions. Not all conditions are noticeable and should be dealt with with respect and compassion neither of which was done in my case. Universal should take a leaf out of Disney’s book as to them I am entitled to the option of not standing in a 3 hour queue but can be given a return time. I appreciate that people with disabilities probably make up a small percentage of universal guests but surely we should be treated with respect. One very disappointed universal customer.

So much to do here! Great fun for riders and non-riders alike. The street shows and meet and greets are awesome and there is plenty to see. Take the kids or leave them home, either way you will have a blast!

A great day out with plenty to do must ride the mummy , minions and spent time with The Simpson,s and Terminator. A park with something for all the family , keep an eye out for character appearance throughout the day as well as the main parade in the afternoon

This place is so fun. Loved all the rides. The Harry Potter Diagon Alley was fantastic with a fun ride inside the bank! We all loved the Mummy Ride went on it multiple times. If you can buy the express pass or get one at a resort your staying at do it its more than worth it considering we never waited more than 20 min for any ride. Been to Disney and I’ll take this place along with Islands of adventure and city walk any day over Disney. Personal opinion!! Have fun.

There is a lot to do in this park. Diagon Alley is an awesome addition. Some classic experiences still hold up. There are several fun entertainment shows (Horrow Show, Beat Builders, Animal Show, Blues Brothers, Parade, etc). The light and fountain show at the end of the day is great. If hot, go to Fievel's water slide (great for kids of all ages, and an easy head dunk fountain for adults). The movie characters roaming around are fun (especially the Men in Black). Schwab's was a good ice cream stop.
We had a fun filled day. Seeing the characters was a highlight. The water rides were a must on a hot day. We had a great time.

We visited both Islands of Adventure and Universal Studios. As a couple with out children we loved visiting both Universal Studio parks. This was our first visit in about fifteen years. We had always enjoyed all the rides both thrill and non thrill rides. We were very disappointed that some of the old rides had been retired: Jaws, Earthquake, Twister, old King Kong( which the new ride is awesome!). We couldn’t get into Hagrads ride after five days of trying. We tried early, late, mid day etc. what was so disappointing was they couldn’t give us an opening day or time. Couldn’t tell us if we waited in line for two hours if it would stay open or close abruptly. That wasn’t even our biggest disappointment!  We loved some of the less thrill rides as a break like jaws twister Earthquake etc as a ride to take a break from the roller coasters. We have the disposable income and not many of the rides are set up for us aging ex roller coaster folks that like a break between rides. If I’m spending 5 thousand dollars for five days of fun it needs to be a bit more balanced. When you teenagers want to come back to enjoy your favorite rides in ten twenty years or so and there all gone? Oh well enjoy being an old fart. We are still into some new rides but also a few of our old favorites too.  The hotels at Universal are much better and have awesome services now and we loved that just the parks are in a transition. Maybe all the construction might be a positive but too many areas are closed to construction or are simply boring now. Eric and Adele

Bought tickets on line before leaving UK,paid a great deal for the family to find out you had to pay more to beat the queues which I find a con considering what you pay(moan over)parks have plenty to do and plenty of intentive staff all willing to help.Super rides in Hulk and Harry Potter and plenty of reasonably priced food outlets(you can take your own packed lunch) and no issues with security check.Cheek to charge you 25-35 dollars 💵 to park your car(😡) considering the costs of tickets.Thunderstorms in the 2 days we visited but they sell you rain covers at £15 dollars each.Seen it done it,won’t rush back as exspensive family days

Visited as a family of 4 with 2 children age 4 and 7. Great for my 7 year old just frustrating paying almost an adult price ticket for my 4 year old as she was only tall enough for about 3 rides which felt like a waste of money for her. On the other hand if your travelling with children older it's brilliant myself and my son loved the thrill rides. Waiting times are quite long especially if you don't arrive at the park on opening. Some great shows for the kids they loved the parade seeing some of their favourite characters.

Important tip, before visiting the Park, download the Universal Studios App and familiarize yourself with the App and maps on the app. You need a whole day to enjoy the different rides and adventures. Park opens at 09:00 and closes at 22:00. However, we were exhausted by 17:00. Lots of walking, waiting, fun and laughter. The Jimmy Fallon Race and Hollywood Rip Ride were the best. Try and carry the least amount of things. Majority of the rides do not allow cameras (of any sort), phones, sunglasses etc. just you and the clothes you wearing. Lockers are available for free while you on the ride (up to 30 minutes) but if you have a big bag, you will need a big locker which cost $2. Lard Lad Donuts is a must try, picture attached.

Great location that draws many people. I would recommend looking up area details so you do not have to ask security. They seem to be preoccupied and very rude. I asked two questions on my trip there about directions and was met with very rude comments. That is sad as this place is vibrant and great for all ages. It probably explains why it has taken second place to Icon Park and Disney.

I'd like to start by saying that the gringotts and Rockit rides are awesome.  Now, I understand that prices at theme parks are naturally higher, but my experience here was disgusting. Regular drinks are 4.19, no refills allowed. Universal sells a refill Cup for 17 Bucks (only Works for a day). That means If you are not a heavy drinker you are going to pay a ridiculous amount to drink. I think this is a very mean trap, especially for those on a budget. For comparison, a refill drink on Disney os about 3 dollars, even though they sell refills.  The employees are also less friendly than Disney Parks. Overall, better rides, Very worse service .

VIP Vacations Inc. helped me get exactly what i wanted out of my universal trip. Early access to the parks and all! I was able to get on the new Hagrid's Motor Bike ride, despite having to wait in line for close to 5 hours: it was totally worth it!

Having pre purchased a ticket for all 3 parks in advance and not liking to queue, I discovered if you book a room at one of Universals top 3 hotels you are given unlimited "express passes" for your party. Seeing the purchase price of the passes was $600 for our family of 4, the price of our one night stay was $450! No brainer and hotel duly booked. The Studios and Adventure Island are a must visit if you are in Orlando and both offer a great mix of thrill rides and 4d rides. These are world class rides and you will come away smiling for sure. We loved the Harry Potter experience with the Hogwarts Express proving transport between the parks and The Simpsons land, the Crusty Burger and Duff beer were to die for! It is worth getting to the parks early, however, with the unliited express passes the longest queue we experienced was 15 minutes when regular queues were in excess of 1-2 hours for the popular rides. We didn't manage to visit Volcano Bay but understand it is a top water park. All in all, take a minimum 2 day visit to Universal and you will be blown away. Cant wait to go back.
Timely to declare Universal Studios the number one amusement (theme) park just before DisneyWorld opens the Star Wars themed park in August?! Just wait acouple months and reassess that determination.

My wife and I went in July 2019 and we had a blast! I would highly recommend getting the express passes as you might end up waiting for hours for a ride! The express passes pay for themselves and I don’t believe we waited more than a half an hour for even the most popular ride!

Been there with friends after experiencing Universal in California 3 years ago. Incomparable! Nevertheless it is still Universal Studios. So My tips are: 1. We were staying at Disney World resort but when booking the holiday we planned a day at Universal and booked tickets to go and when we arrived we paid extra for a single fast pass to each ride so we could get through as much as possible so although it was expensive if you only plan the one day if you can get it it’s worth getting, there’s no way we’d have done as much as we did with out it. Our hotel booked a private car to take us and pick us up as there was 6 of us this worked out cheaper than getting the coach that picks up from the hotel. We enjoyed all the different areas of the park, loved the Simpsons area and ride as well Harry Potter World and all the rides there and walking around the different parts and going on the Hogwarts express to get to “Hogsmead” was magical. We had disappointment on Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey as it stopped on us a few times during the ride and we weren’t given another go which was annoying as we only had one fast pass for it and queues were ridiculous. Other favourite rides were the Rip Ride Rockit and The Hulk which were brilliant and other rides like The mummy and Spider-Man were great too and many more. All the rides were but we did expect there to be more big roller coaster rides but the majority were more virtual reality rides which I suppose makes sense as Universal is all about movies and shows etc and they were actually good rides apart from maybe the E.T. ride (sorry). The park also boasts plenty of places to eat, drink and shop in all areas and staff were great we had a great day from start to finish.

We had planned our vacation for more than a year to Universal Studios parks in Orlando. Liked the rides, the shows, the food. A few tidbits: If you are going, go for three or more days -better price tickets. We found a deal where we bought 3 days and got two free with Park-to-park tickets. Price averaged to less than $60 per day. Take a backpack with water for everyone, then refill the bottles at any location that serves fountain soda. They will refill them with the filtered water. If you go in Late July, early August, it rains most days, bring umbrellas or a raincoat. Rip Ride Rocket is Awesome - you get to select your own tunes for the ride. Rides at the front of the park get the longest lines first - Minions, Shrek, Rip Ride Rocket, so head towards the back if you get there early. You need a park-to-park ticket to ride the train -well worth it, at least for 1 trip. The two amusement parks are connected by City Walk, so it's easy to go from one to the other if you don't want to wait for the train. Plan to stay late as the ride lines get shorter closer to closing time. We had an enjoyable time at Universal Studios in Orlando.

What an amazing couple of days in the two parks! We benefited from staying in the Universal Loews Pacific hotel which gave us unlimited Express Passes for two days for the one night we stayed there. The rollercoasters are awesome and we enjoyed the other entertainment on offer. We returned for the evening entertainment and really enjoyed that too!

As much as I loved the Disney theme parks in Florida as a kid, if we're being honest, I was always more of a Universal guy. Even at a young age I was more of a classic movie guy than a cartoon guy, so out of all of Disney's parks only really MGM came close for me. As such when it came to return to Florida as an adult, I had to make a cost based decision on where to go and Universal was always going to triumph.  It's important to get this out of the way early, but yes the tickets into these places are very expensive. However, you can secure a deal on entry to the main Universal park and Islands of Adventure which does significantly lower the price. Truth be told if you're travelling to Orlando, chances are you're going there for this, and you do get what you pay for.  Now, I'll be honest, there were a LOT of changes in the 25 year gap between my visits to the park, but the one thing I cherish more than anything is that the general layout really hasn't. Including the main 'small-town America' street and 50s diner that I'd have been heartbroken if they'd done away with. While the ride is long gone, there is still the giant Jaws shark hanging by the lake to pose for photos with too.  That actually hints at my biggest gripe, if you want to call it that, with the park, it's the more modern nature of the ride's themes. As much as I know they need to try and keep stuff relevant for the kids, things like King Kong (that thing in Islands of Adventure doesn't count, its based on the worst remake and pales in comparison to the proper ride) and Back To The Future are genuine classic, timeless movies...the kind of pillars you build a park around. The fact that they still sell merchandise for these characters tells its own story.Thankfully E.T. is still there.  As if to make matters worse, some of the franchises they currently cater attractions to are the worst; The Fast & The Furious and those awful Michael Bay Transformers movies where Optimus Prime looks like he is comprised 80% of paperclips and has cringeworthy turn of the century boy-racer flames painted on him.  I understand the lasting appear in the Simpsons, but still feel they could have put it somewhere that wasn't the corpse of Back to the Future. Especially when you take into account the now basically dead, financially and culturally of Men in Black and the Stephen Somers Mummy franchises still hold large attractions  But you know what? Even though it caters mostly to films I don't like, even if there's a massive Harry Potter section and I can't stand Harry Potter (I'll at least accept it is a pretty massive pop culture phenomenon and warrants its place)...I still loved it. The Transformers and Fast & Furious rides, while basically simulators, are far more entertaining than any of the films they take their premise from. Revenge of the Mummy may be based on a franchise that outstayed its welcome and has had an attempt at a reboot die already, but it's still a fantastic thrill. Long story short these guys are rubbish at picking films but great at building rides.  I'll even reserve special mention for the Harry Potter section. As much as I think having sections in both the main park and Islands of Adventure (joined by the Hogwarts Express train) is excessive, as much as I'd rather set myself on fire than watch a Harry Potter movie...they haven't half done this right. Featuring an entrance from a faux London street to a wizardy street full of Harry Potter themed shops and cafe's selling various wizardly themed things and a giant dragon above the one big ride in this part of the park that sporadically breathes fire.  The real nifty part about this section of the park is one that would have entirely passed me by had I not been with someone who falls on the other end of the spectrum when it comes to all things Potter. There is a wand shop, which even without seeing the films I could appreciate, a small store devoted entirely to the sale of wands based on surely every one seen in the movies, but presented as a rustic old magic shop. The kicker is that there were 2 varieties of wand, standard replicas and more expensive (she wouldn't tell me how much) interactive ones.  The gimmick here is that at various points of the Harry Potter area there are symbols which denote an interactive wizarding point. At these points, waving the interactive wand in the correct motion for a 'spell' will cause something to happen e.g. a fountain to fire a random stream of water out, and small pile of armour will form a knight and do a dance. Little things but the things these places do so well.  Also of special note is the Rokit Rollercoaster, which while lacking any sort of movie theme redeems itself by being 1. An excellent rollercoaster and 2. The first one I've ever been on that lets you pick a soundtrack to have blasted into your ears as it rolls you around!  There are a variety of eating options throughout the park ranging from actual restaurants to fast food vendors to confectionary stalls. All are every bit as overpriced as you'd expect, but that kind of thing rather comes with the territory. The quality in most cases is absolutely fine.  Overall, it may seem like I've done a lot of moaning about Universal but it is worth noting that it had almost impossible expectations to lead up to based on my experiences there as a child. Truth be told it is still an excellent day out, I imagine especially so if you actually like any of the movies the rides are based upon now.

Bought tickets from the official office. Explained that we wanted one day at each park, plus a half day at each, but not bothered about the Hogworts Express ride. Was told that a 4 day ticket was best option and that on day 3 we could use a day in each park. When we tried to do this today we were told that we couldn’t without paying another $50 each. 3 rides had been closed due to ‘technical difficulties’ for the whole day (including Spider-Man which is indoor) It was pouring with rain, and we had only 3 hours left in the park - all we got from customer services was that we had been given incorrect info when we were sold the tickets. No apology. No compromise. Just pay $50 or go away. We will go away and not come back. The food was also appalling. After 20 years of visiting every year, we will not be giving you our cost on again. Shockingly bad treatment of your guests.

We had a blast here our kids are getting older and the draw of Disney is no.longer there. The Hulk was an awesome ride. Get a 2 day pass. Pay to get to the front of the line and laugh at everyone standing in line!

My experience of Universal Orlando is OLD (2000) but i still have it in a corner of my mind because it is simply an unforgettable experience when you enter that amazing world you feel as if you are an important part of it you have to try it to understand what it means

My wife and I have been coming to Orlando (Disney World), since we were little. The is our second time at Universal Studios - Island of Adventure and our kids first time. We were so excited to bring them here but we will NEVER return. I was so disappointed with Guest Relations and customer service we received from the staff through the entire park.  The day started off when we first attempted to get our daughter a medical pass from the Guest Relations in the front of Universal Studios. We explained to Guest Relations that our daughter has a rare syndrome called POTS (Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome) and she is unable to stand or sit for long periods of time because her blood doesn’t circulate properly. She has to drink 100 oz of water a day which of course means she has to use the restroom more often. She also overheats quickly which causes body tremors and passing out. When we explained our daughters medical condition we were offered a wheelchair. We told Universal that we were able to get an extra fast pass at Disney allowing us to be “virtually” in the line for any ride. Guest Services proceed to tell us that they’re a newer park than Disney, more ADA compliant and more accommodating. We tried to understand how Universal “believes” they’re more “accommodating” when they only offer a virtual line pass for 3 of their rides. We decided to enter the park and speak with someone else in the park that might be able to assist us and understand our daughters medical condition.  Our second attempt at Guest Services was near Men in Black with a supervisor named William. We explained our daughters medical condition and all William kept saying was I am not a medical professional, I don’t understand, help me understand what you need, we offer a variety of accommodations. We kept saying the same thing over and over. If he is not medical trained then how can he deny our request? How is this person a supervisor? He said they can offer us a wheel chair or we can spend money to purchase their “express pass”. What is really frustrating is they kept saying we don’t judge anyone based on how they look but having gone thru this experience they clearly do. We asked for a supervisor and he told us we had to go back to the front the park to find one, no assistance was offered and wouldn’t provide a managers name we can talk to. He was so rude and nasty he made our daughter so upset that she started to cry. Since our daughter doesn’t have a visual medical condition they made an assumption that we were trying to “cheat the system” and get the express pass for free. We simply wanted to have the ability to virtually wait in line on all rides, not just 3. My daughter wasn’t able to ride several rides because they would not accommodate her medical condition.  I have one question for you Universal. How has Disney, Bush Gardens, Kings Dominion figured this out? Shame on you for treating people with disabilities/medical conditions different and trying to up sale customers with a disability/medical condition to buy your express pass. The entire experience was a complete disappointment and maybe it’s because we are used to the service we receive at every Disney park.  Universal CEO and other senior management how would you like your families treated this way?  We will never return and I am severely disappointed to have spent so much money on admission and money in your park.

Many people on here saying the price is way to high but I paid £310 per person for 2 weeks park hop ticket which got me entry to both parks and volcano bay which works around £22 a day which is an amazing price I think. I’m from England and drank the water from the fountains which saved me a lot of money on water. They also have a water dispenser in Starbucks in universal studios if you wanted cold ice water. I went in peak time during six weeks holiday and the most I ever waited is around 30/40 minutes a ride. It is all about planning the biggest rides need to be done either as the park opens or later on in the evening. If you go to any major ride at peak time in the afternoon then your going to obviously be looking at 90 minute wait. The afternoon is when you need to have lunch and do some shows as it’s to hot to be queuing. We also went on the Hagrid ride which was amazing!! We queued for around 90 minutes which was divided up from waiting at the entrance gates at 8clock as the park didn’t open until 9 and then 30 minutes in the actual queue once the park opened. To save time dont take a bag as you will need to put evething in a locker which puts you behind in the queue, although we had bags and still got on in a great time. If you try and go on in the afternoon you have no hope because it’s around 5 hour wait
It is a friggin nightmare with teenagers( and adults who do not know how to act ), later in the day...Go EARLY and get your ride on!

Great, great place. We were lucky in that we booked our day after the American children had gone back to school, so the longest queue we encountered on a ride was only 45 mins.  I had a real Krusty Burger in KrustyLand though I was very disappointed that the Flaming Moe drinks were not being served. The Buzz cola was great, however.  Loved all of the rides, especially The Hulk and The Mummy. Fast and Furious could have been better, but all in all a great day. The park is open until 9pm so we were able to go back to our resort hotel room in the afternoon until the Florida rain had stopped and continue on the rides in the evening. Loved the water taxi service which runs very regularly. You will walk lots, and get many blisters, but totally worth the pain!
Keeping this simple, go it's great. Food on site, expensive. MIB not a great ride. Universal App very good. TAKE YOUR TIME and don't rush, so much detail to see, so take it easy.

As our kids have gotten older they just don't feel the same about Disney as they used to...so Universal was a great change that seemed to be more inline with where they are age wise and interest wise.

Bucket list for me for sure. It was all I hoped and more. Stay on property, gets you express pass and that matters. Best ride is Harry Potter inside Hogworts. Flight of the hippogryff is tolerable, but wouldn’t stand in line. New Hagrid motorbike ride is excellent (no express pass). Do NOT pay for the photo package - hard to find photo sites, printing service is S....L....O.....W and rude. Not worth your money at all.

Come dressed to walk a great deal and have fun, especially if you have kids with you. My grandkids enjoyed the rides and food. Plenty to do and see. Be prepared to spent the whole day. We started at the Cowfish Restaurant where we met as a group to celebrate our first annual company picnic. The food was great for the adults and kids. The deserts brownie with ice cream got us all sugared up for the long walks through the park. By the end of the day the my grandkid were tired and slept on their way back home.

When you are in the mood to ride theme park rides, yet you HATE to wait in line (even with the Fast Pass,) enjoy your hotel's amenities during the day and ENTER the park just after 6pm. You can get in an entire DAY's worth of rides in the hours before the park closes because EVERYONE is in a mass exodus to LEAVE. Trust me on this one...we have been multiple times and AFTER 6pm is THE BEST time to GO INTO the park if you want to RIDE, RIDE, RIDE without a wait!

This was my 8 year old son’s first trip to Universal Studios and the Islands of Adventure (IOA) theme parks. We had a wonderful time. We spent 4-5 hours per park each day for 2 days. The express pass is highly recommended. In fact, I would not consider going to the parks without an express pass option. Our favorite Universal Studios rides were despicable me minions, terminator, ET and men in black. The worst ride was Shrek 4-D because there was at least 10 minutes of listening to a boring preamble while standing before entering the theater and the moving chairs were rough and annoying. Our favorite IOA rides were Spider-Man, King Kong and flight of the hippogriff.  Parking was easy to navigate. Park hopping was not realistic for us because of the fatigue factor. There is plenty to see and do when visiting just one park per day. The ticket process was a little confusing initially because we had 2 tickets for park entry and 2 additional tickets for the express pass. Lastly, the evening fire works show was outstanding!

Fantastic park. As soon as you walk in the energy and the sights hit you, giving you a sense of excitement that is hard to describe. Had a list of rides to do and got on all of the ones we wanted in the time we had and then came back for a second day to do some others.
Hung out on the Universal city walk for my birthday, Dinner Drinks and People Watching. It was a GOOD time.

We went numerous times over our 10 day stay at cabana bay hotel as park tickets came with the package.  Although it was so hot and humid we loved visiting here and would come all the back from London again. From blues brothers shows on the street to harry potter experiences it has it all here. Great merchandise shops throughout. Purchasing an unlimited drink cup for the day is recommended and great value. Loved the rides, from a 3d transformer to a faster paced to a inside roller coaster The Mummy, great fun for the family.  Cant wait to go again to be honest!
An amazing place all rides from children to adults there is so much to see and do here and the little shows that are going on everywhere and street shows going on fantastic

Personally I really liked Universal studios it is definitely a 5 star park but if I had one negative it’s that there is too many 3D rides but they are good. The transformers ride was our favourite ride.

I love this place. There's so much to do. Many different rides that cater for all different kind of thrillseekers. Me (tame) my wife (loves roller coasters). I'm not a fan of coasters that make you go upside down. Thankfully there's a lot more to the park than this. Lots of 3 and 4d rides and coasters I can go on. Plenty of good places to eat and drink. For smokers, you can still smoke inside the parks at designated points unlike Disney. I'd definitely recommend coming here.
Never disappoints. Amazing rides, great beers and lots of shows to keep everyone entertained. Queues never too long.

This was our 6th visit to Universal Orlando. Always had a great time until this vist.We found the staff much less helpful than previous visits. The new locker system was also an ordeal and the staff at them less than helpful or friendly. I contacted customer service by email to give my option. That didn't go well either and after waiting 4 weeks for a reply to something UNIVERSAL asked me for I tried again. Was fobbed off. As I said disappointing.  On a positive note Hagrid ride wad great.

Completely not what we expected. Haunted houses not even as good as ones in my city. Wait time was hour plus on each and 100 minutes on Stranger Things. To upgrade to fast pass was $130 each when tickets were $60 to begin with. Ridiculous. No maps or signs to indication direction of attraction. The only thing we did worthwhile was Harry Potter which wasn’t even part of that 👎🏻👎🏻
So many great things to see here! Love the parade they have! Street performers are amazing! Great rides!

I’ve visited once a year for the past three years and Universal never disappoints.  After reading the reviews, I just wanna advise people to use the many tools provided to plan your vacation! Universal has an app, a blog, a website, and multiple helpful social media accounts. There’s no reason to not know everything that’s happening while you’re there if you use those things. Their app has wait times, event information, and especially the park closing times! You have all of the information in front of you, and if you’re planning a trip in advance, you can check the park hour schedule on the website. If you go without even bothering to check, it’s not Universal’s fault that you didn’t take the time to research anything about your vacation.  Stay on site! I cannot recommend this enough. The past two times I’ve visited, I’ve stayed at Cabana Bay Beach Resort. I absolutely love that place. The shuttle back and forth to CityWalk is invaluable. Buses are there basically at all times, we never even had to wait for one. The pools are great. If you intend on visiting Volcano Bay, the entrance is so conveniently close. The diner near the lobby has great affordable options. My only complaint would be that every year they continue to raise their parking prices for guests. I think it’s $17 a night as of now, and if it goes up much more, it’ll be pretty ridiculous.  Know how to plan your vacation. When you stay on site and buy your tickets all at once, you’re gonna get the most for your money! We personally planned our trip when Universal was running a deal for “Buy 2 days, get 3 free” and we opted for the park-to-park passes. This gave us plenty of time to enjoy both Studios and Islands of Adventure. When we purchased our vacation, we also opted to do the pay-by-the-month option through Uplift. That’s a great opportunity to space out one big payment and give you way more chances to spend money in the actual park. Also, know the down times of the year! September is a slow month. We never even waited more than 15 minutes for a ride, and nothing in the park was over crowded. If you go in summer, of course you’re gonna have a less enjoyable time with longer waits.  Safety. These days it’s scary at times to be anywhere, especially somewhere with wide open spaces like two giant amusement parks. But Universal really puts that fear to ease. Before you’re even allowed to go to CityWalk, you go through a pretty thorough yet fast security process. How serious Universal takes this truly makes me feel secure and well taken care of while in their parks. Thank you for that.  Lockers. I was a little apprehensive about the change that had bigger lockers cost money and smaller lockers the only free ones. But, with a full sized backpack and multiple cups, the small locker was more than enough space. And you can always spread your stuff throughout your group.  Halloween Horror Nights was a blast. It was my first time and it was so neat to experience the park at night. The rides that are open have such short wait times. Diagon Alley was almost empty which was a great opportunity to look around and take pictures. The houses were amazing. I made the decision to visit HHN because I absolute adore Killer Klowns from Outer Space. And let me tell you, Universal brings your favorite movies to life. The Ghostbusters house was amazing too, and I’m not even a big fan of the movie. Universal Monsters scared me half to death. A word of slightly expensive advice, GO FOR THE EXPRESS PASS! My friend surprised me with the passes, and we didn’t even wait at any of the houses for more than 2 minutes. Seriously. Beyond worth it. The scare zones were great, especially Zombieland. Marathon of Mayhem was insane!! They had a lot of food options and they weren’t too expensive either. My only complaint, and it’s a very small one, is that for the collectible cups, they come out one at a time periodically. I wish they were all available from the jump because I really wanted a Killer Klowns cup. Seeing as I live in Tennessee, I can’t really just pop back to complete my cup collection.  Veggie options!! I can’t brag on universal enough for this. As a vegetarian, I find it hard to have an enjoyable meal at a lot of places. I usually end up getting just side dishes. Not at Universal! They offer vegan chicken, vegan burgers, vegan meat crumbles on top of spaghetti. You name it, pretty much. At the Monster’s Cafe they even have BBQ jackfruit! Amazing. Thank you for not only having options, but having delicious options.  Overall, I have an absolute blast every time I come. This company does everything they can to bring you a great vacation. You’ve truly made a fan for life, and I’ll be back frequently so long as you don’t get rid of my favorite ride, Revenge of the Mummy!! Thank you for everything.

This was a great place for a family vacation. The Harry Potter stuff is amazing. The other rides were a lot of fun as well. The movie nostalgia was great with the posters and props to see. The characters are awesome and fun to meet and get pictures with. We got a great deal on the photo package and it was great to have so many family pictures. Shutterbuttons was awesome and a fun keepsake from our trip to the Wizarding World. My ten year old loved every minute of our 5 days at Universal and can't wait to go back. My husband loved the coasters as well.

I love universal so much. This place literally has something for everyone!! Wether it’s riding rides all day or watching shows or just wandering the park looking at all the wonderful details. I grew up here and I can’t wait to bring my family here for generations to come! I love all the new attractions and the classic ones *cough cough* E.T. The team members always make my day and I truly appreciate them for their hard work!

I loved the fast and furious ride along with the hulk roller coaster. The lines were long but these were my favorite rides. The Simpson doughnuts were huge and delicious! I wish I lived in Florida I would definitely get annual passes! Halloween horror was a blast.

Don’t get me wrong, I love Disney World! But let me tell you, Universal Studios is the place to have fun with adrenaline! All the marvel rides, the Mummy, Simpsons Land and Harry Potter… I mean you can’t go wrong! Prices are fair and generous and customer service is utterly fantastic… Stay on one of the properties and take advantage of the amenities. Highly recommend!

This is one of our favorite parks. The rides are incredible starting from when you first walk in its the Hulk-roller coaster, then it's the 4-D Spiderman, and it only gets better. Harry Potter land is a must, MIB is a must, BOTH of these parks are a MUST. If you have a vacavtion coming up you cannot go wrong with Orlando!

The best haunted houses in 2019 were Famous Monsters, Ghostbusters, and Yeti. I have gone to HHN every 2 years since 2013, and liked the houses this year the best. I went on a Sunday night, with good weather, and never waited more than 30 minutes even without having an Express pass.  One negative that I noticed this year is park staff rushing people through the haunted houses at times. When it happened, this was really annoying, both for the feeling of being rushed, but also because their very presence ruins the illusion of being in a horrible place or environment away from reality. But the creative work in the houses is great, especially these 3 houses, and without gore which is just gross and not scary. I find that seeing about 5 houses to be enough, as there is a certain sameness to some of the houses after awhile (i.e. jump scares).  The shows were a mixed bag. The water fountain show was a mild diversion, maybe good to take a break from all the scares, but did not have any real plot. Academy of Villains had a fantastic juggler, aerial acrobat, and contortionist. However the rest of their show was repetitive dancing (albeit good) and overly loud. They seemed to be trying to communicate some kind of mad scientist plot overall, but were not successful, at least for me.  The scare zones, where zombies and ghouls walk up and scare you, were not as good as some of the past scare zones that I recall. The most interesting one had a Viking or Norse theme, and cool costumes, but the actors seemed to not interact as much as one expects from a scare zone.  Universal Studios is finally offering vegan food, and I was glad to see they had the Beyond Burger at Mel's Drive In restaurant. However, it was not fully cooked, so they need to work on preparation. I also found $6 for a pretzel to be over priced, even for a theme park.  The locker policy at the Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit is really terrible. You must go to a locker if you have practically anything at all in your pockets. The staff says the lockers are free, but when I scanned in my ticket at the locker area, it wanted $2, so I went elsewhere in the park, and had to miss the ride.  On the plus side, I lost my shirt on the Mummy ride, but was able to get it back at the lost and found at literally 2:30 AM, just as I was leaving the park.  I don't understand why the Horror Make-Up Show is closed for HHN. It fits right in and even has Horror in the title, and was a really fun and enjoyable show when I last saw it. I hope they change that in the future. Note: the Gringotts ride closes early on HHN, roughly around 10 or 11 PM, so go early for it because it is one of the better rides.

We've been coming to the Universal theme parks in Florida for many years. The roller coasters, waters rides and entertainment are good. However the costs at the parks are getting ridiculous. $26 for parking then we were over $70 for 5 hot dogs and soft drinks. I see these prices as unjustified and I don't think we'll be making holiday plans here for the next few years.

After spending over £100 each for a ticket you then have to pay $26 for parking!!!!! You have to queue up To 2 hours for a ride and heaven forbid you want a drink approx $8 and a hotdog $11.99. There are more shops there and food outlets than rides!!! They let thousands of people in so u can barely move. The only positive thing I can say is that the toilets are clean. Worryingly though they have boxes on the walls in the loos for syringes (sharps), all the ones I saw were full. So my advice would be don’t waste your money like we did!
I come here at least once a year from Michigan. I prefer this park over Islands of Adventure. I wish it didn't close so early when we were there, but I understand it was for Halloween Horror Nights.

Haven't been here for a few years. Visited for the two parks and horror Nights in our 14 day stay. Parking is ridiculous what a rip off $26... Cheaper to get Ubas if your doing the park and horror Nights. Food prices weren't cheap and the quality was poor. Drinks were way overpriced, people are thirsty they have no choice but to purchase them. The rides were the same and we had fun on them and carefully selected unpeak times. Never managed to get on Hagrids, not sure why they are making people queue why not use virtual waiting times. Horror night times too busy now and we won't do them again, over priced alcohol and rude security bossing us about unnecessarily. The queues were awful and seemed on purpose so people would buy fast passes which they were. Whole place is a cash cow for maximum profit and to fleece holidaymakers of hard earned cash. Never going back.

This was the first and last time we ever come to this park! Unless you have fastpasses which cost you almost the price of the general admission ticket, they treat you like a 2nd class citizen. Our family of 6 spent over $700 on the park tickets this past Friday and we rode on 3 rides! The fastpass holders get treated like royalty, they don't wait even a minute, and the general line could stand for over an hour or 2 for a ride like harry potter. My husband and my older boys stood in line to harry potter ride for 2 hours, when they got close to the gate, the guy opened it, told them to go and take pictures, while they were taking those photos, which they didn't ask or need, it was bad enough that the fastpass line just endlessly goes in, he let the people in the general line go and by the time the photos were done the people who were in the back of them initially, were already in! With 4 kids ages ranging from 4-16, we've been to a good number of theme parks including all 4 Disney parks and such disregard I have not experienced anywhere! So unless you're willing to pay double price by buying a fastpass or okay being treated like a nobody for $115 + tax a ticket, go elsewhere...it is not worth it!

Surprised to see how nice and clean the park was. Bug free too. Everything is overpriced but I think that is pretty standard. The kids had a great time and I got enough walking put in to maintain my daily average. Lots of scantily clad women. I saw way too many nipples, butt cheeks and cleavage that needed covering. Not the fault of the park but a dress code wouldn't be a bad idea.

We (3 adults) visited this month. Stayed at Universal’s Endless Summer this time. Check in was very smooth and staff member Christine at check-in was super friendly and informative regarding pedestrian access, WiFi , resort’s facilities etc. We do not drive while in Florida so location on IDrive is ideal for shops/restaurants. Hotel is fantastic, room decor is bright. Separate bedroom suited our needs and kitchen facilities with refrigerator & dining table was nice bonus. We enjoyed the pool facilities and Starbucks each morning with friendly welcoming staff. Our TV in room stopped working briefly and guest services called to room within 20 minutes and resolved the problem. Fantastic! Hotel transportation to parks was regular so we never waited long for a bus transfer and buses are clean with friendly drivers. For parks this year we only purchased for UNIVERSAL. both parks plus Volcano Bay and separately HHN on 2 nights. As usual enjoyed both universal and IOA. Our favorite is the Mummy and we still get a thrill from it after all these years. Visited Jim Fallon experience for the 1st time and thoroughly enjoyed this. This year we did the Minions as the queue time was short. Really enjoyed this also. Enjoyed all except ThE Fast and the Furious as wait time said 20 minutes but was actually about 50 minutes wait. This aside we found the experience very boring (sorry to be negative). I would have kept Beetleguise! We enjoyed all events and houses for HHN especially Ghostbusters. The unexpected highlight for our group was catching Marathon of Mayhem. Whom ever thought this idea up is an evil genius. Marathon of Mayhem gets a 5 Star rating from me. Loved the Stranger Things music playing throughout the park also for HHN. Our trip to Volcano Bay was only for a few hours as we wanted to get to the outlets but we really enjoyed our time in the pools and lazy river. Really enjoyable and will aim to visit Volcano Bay for a full day next time. We love the Christmas Store near the entrance to IOA and Voodoo Donuts is a real gem. 5/5 all around! Already planning our next visit to Endless Summer Resort & Universal’s parks.

We had went to guest services first to upgrade our tickets to the annual pass holders, we’re celebrating our 20th wedding anniversary so we had been given a badge from the hard rock hotel, one of the character members congratulated us and told us to go over to the other guys services to get the Olive and Popeyes anniversary badge as it’s a limited edition so we did and it’s lovely. All the staff are so lovely and helpful. We had a good look round today and did a few rides, done for the first time the fast ride which as big fast and furious fans we loved it and another first was the pets show around by ET ride which was really nice too watch. We’ve been coming to Orlando and Universal Studios for the last 17 years and we still find stuff we’ve not done before, can’t wait to do IOA later in the week. These are our favourite parks. Also did some of our other favourite rides, mummy, shrek 4d, minions, MIB, to name a few but we did more. Just love it.

I think people make mistakes at Universal that will cost them their experience. Note that it’s a huge, hot, and expensive park. Duh. You also have to go during a time of the year where you won’t sit in line for 2 hours and you have to use the app to plan your day. We never stood in line for more than 30 minutes and we rode Hagrid’s Magical Motorbike ride, which was amazing! If you’re not a theme park person, then take your money elsewhere. You will have to wake up early, walk a lot, bring snacks, plan, and move quickly. You are allowed to bring your own snacks and drinks so do that. You can set notifications when the ride you want to ride has a wait time under a certain time on the app, do that.
Visited this venue for the first time and I was very impressed with the attractions on offer, but quite shocked by the high price of tickets...some good rides - very impressed by the Mummy ride..

From the moment we arrived here there was a more relaxed atmosphere than other parks... all very high tech getting into the park through an airport security like system but the park cards we’d been given for our 14 day use were cardboard! ( not ideal for wet rides or kids!) however all staff members were friendly & helpful & with our eldest son having ADHD they have a brilliant system where you can obtain a come back time for rides with longer than 20 minute wait time! I can’t tell you how much of a difference this made to our few days at universal & islands of adventure, the stress was taken away as we were all prepared for the waiting for rides situation! So we thoroughly enjoyed every minute enjoying all the rides & especially the 3D simulation rides they were amazing we couldn’t chose which was our favourite! The Harry Potter worlds in both parks were outstanding even my husband who’s not a HP fan loved these areas & there rides! I would thoroughly recommend a visit to these 2 joint parks to anyone visiting Orlando just a shame we didn’t have a babysitter so we could have experienced the night life in city walk which was filled with bars restaurants & clubs as you enter & leave the parks! Next time!!!

I forgot what it is called but get Universals form of the fast pass. It cuts down wait times in lines by 60%. All the rides are really fun except I did not enjoy the one that has the party bus. That one is a waste of time in my opinion. Overall, great time we had!

This was our first trip to Florida and Universal, needless to say, I doubt that we will go back there. The admission was expensive enough but then they add an extra fee for a fast pass. We waited in a line for over three hours after a rainstorm to get on Hagrid's motorcycle ride only to be told 15 minutes before the park closed that the ride was closed for the night. I understand that you can't predict the weather and safety is important but they should have some kind of proceedure in place for bad weather to get guests out of the ride line and give them some kind of pass to enjoy the ride at a later time. We could have been given a pass and apology after 30-60 minutes max and been able to enjoy the rest of the time at the park. Instead we were told the park is closing in 15 minutes here is a pass to come back at a later time. No apology and rude employees when they were questioned by several guests about policies and proceedures in regards to weather.

This was our third visit. Cannot believe how the food and drink prices have escalated. The average price for a bottle of water was around £3. Also, the queue for Hagrid's Motorbike Ride was three hours one day and unavailable on the other days we visited. The Harry Potter parts of Universal were heaving with people whereas the rest of the park was fine. There were several breakdowns, which then had a knock on effect to other rides. We generally love our visits here but this year was a bit of a disappointment. The park was very clean, and the staff friendly.

Universal Studios has its enchantment in many of the areas. Diagon Alley is fabulous. Gringots ride is great fun. Simpsons area is like being in the TV show - a bit wild and wacky as is the ride. Men in black was great fun, although not quite sure what you are shooting at! After that, many of the rides going clockwise round the park are 3D experiences and too similar in experience to stand out - bit of a jangled body and headache from too much 3D Rip rocket roller was a pretty good thrill ride as a brain jangler (head knocking against the head rest with lots of thrills). A few good side shows as we headed round the park Deffo worth a visit

Went with my daughter and with the fast passes we rode RipRideRockit 3x, the mummy 2x and other rides as well as rides in Islands in just one day. Use to work at Universal at such an important time in my life and always love to come back!

Came here will visiting Orlando. Great park and lots of rides to go on and things to do like Harry Potter wands.  Had a great time while here came a few days. Did not go onto hagrids ride as too long a wait just around 3 hours. But won’t complain it’s a new ride and everyone wants on. Went on all the other rides and enjoyed it worth the money.  Only negative thing I would say was $21 dollars for 2 hotdogs and staff attitude at the hotdog stall was not good and price is a bit steep but apart from that good rides good park and will be back

The two Universal parks have been family favorites since their inception. Still prefer the original park over the Islands of Adventure one—especially when the weather is cooler—the water rides aren’t fun when it is cold out and they are all at Islands of Adventure. The Harry Potter themed parts are quite magical—even for people like myself that are not manic about it and aren’t too familiar with the story details. Fun to watch families try their wands at the various windows. Gets VERY crowded by late morning so best to go super early or late in the day—not just for the rides there but just to enjoy the experience. The flavored drinks and ice creams are worth a try for sure!! Miss the old Back to the Future, Twister and Jaws rides. Skip the new Fast and Furious ride unless the line is short. We were all very disappointed that it was all pretty much computer graphics and not much else. Just not too exciting. Fear Factor, Animal Acts and Horror Makeup Show all worth seeing. Men in Black is still a fav and lots of fun. Great to see all the characters out and about. If you go, ask about a scavenger hunt—we found out about it from another guest and they were having so much fun with it. Disappointed no one told us when we arrived. So much to see and do. Will go back—we always do.

Parking at Universal was $26 for regular parking during my stay, Nov 17-23, 2019. If you pay for regular parking, take your long receipt into the park with you, and buy two tickets to any matinee showing at the universal cinema that shows before 6pm that day, you will get free parking. If you buy tickets for movies showing before 1pm, they are $8 a piece, which means you will save $10 on parking...even if you don’t go in and watch the movies. I went to a 1:30 showing and I ordered two tickets, even though i was there by myself, handed the box office lady my long parking receipt and no payment, and she handed me back $6 and change. If I had bought an earlier ticket, My total cost for parking would have been $16. I’m just sorry i didn’t read the offer on the receipts until the last day!
While the heat of the day kept us spending more time at our resort, we really enjoyed HHN for two of nights. Try a R.I.P. tour for a truly memorable eperience.

I very much enjoyed my trip here. Universal Studios is one of 3 parks run by Universal in Orlando. This park is separated into major cities like New York, San Francisco, and London. Each area has landmarks from those cities. The street shows like Blues Brothers and the one where they use garbage cans for instruments (I don’t remember the name) are very entertaining. The Today Show Cafe has great food.  I can’t recommend the Rip Ride Rocket coaster as it threw me around too much. The Revenge of the Mummy was a blast (literally, there’s a blast of heat during the ride). We enjoyed the Men in Black ride also. The Transformers ride was also exciting.  The entrance to Diagon Alley in the Wizarding World of Harry Potter is kind of hidden in the London section. You can sit on the steps of 13 Grimald Place and watch for Kreacher to peek out the upstairs window. The Night Bus is parked here. Enter Kings Cross Station and pass through Platform 9 3/4 to ride the Hogwarts Express to Hogsmeade. You do need a park to park ticket to do so.  Honestly, the only drawback is that there are far too many shops and not nearly enough rides and attractions in the park.  We found team members to be friendly and helpful. The park is clean and well-themed for each area.
We usually go to the seaworld parks but thought we'd try universal. We went during thanksgiving holidays was busy as expected,didnt get on everything due to the queues but will be back

We enjoyed our visit to Universal Studios - but you definitely need comfortable shoes. Not only for the long walks everywhere, but also standing for so long in line ups waiting for rides, sore feet are almost guaranteed!  Rides were great - except for the long waits, and so were all staff that we saw and interacted with. Very friendly and helpful.

This was just a one day layover in Orlando, but had to visit Universal and see Harry Potter; and Dr. Seuss - the Grinch. All the Christmas decor was up and beautiful. I saw Grinchmas and it was great! The parade was fun and Mannheim Steamroller did not disappoint. I would always recommend going to Universal Studios. There are attractions for every person. Just go and have FUN!

Many of the rides were 3D ride-through special events, rather than true rides. I'd rather visit Six Flags or Cedar Fair parks, pay less money, and enjoy more thrill rides. I'm just not a "special effects for the sake of special effects" person.

If you r going to visit Universal Studios/Island. It's best to get the PARK TO PARK passes. That is what we did and we had a BLAST going from one park to the other any time we wanted to. We WASN'T STUCK in one park all day. We can't wait to go back and do it all again!! # LOVE IT

This is my first time coming to universal as an adult and overall I like the park and would definitely come back when they open their 4th park.  What I concluded from my trip:  Do not compare universal to a six flags or highly known rollercoaster park. This is an entirely different kind of theme park. If you do, you will be disappointed.  They do not have a diverse group of rides. A lot of the rides are the same thing. Either a 3D ride in a moveable car or giant team with a story theme around it using giant screens. Or a movie theater type ride with moveable seats. The exception would be the Hollywood rip ride rocket, mummy, and Men In Black.  They all love to squirt you with water on the ride. Not a lot but where the ride has a character “spit” and they squirt some water at you.  A lot of the lines have a giant room or “elevator” in the middle of the line where you are no longer in line and it allows the people behind you to move in front of you. Not sure why they couldn’t keep the queue line in these rooms so that doesn’t happen  The positive We went during a slow week and waited 5-10 min per ride. Seeing how much of the line we didn’t have to wait in, I can’t imagine how disappointed I would be if we had to wait hours for these rides. Definitely do your research and find a slow week. No need for fast pass. We were able to do the whole park in a couple hours.  Harry Potter world was pretty much the only crowded place but even the ride wasn’t a bad wait. Mostly people running around with their wands and robes yelling spells at things.

We’ve spent our holidays in Florida since 1988, over the years we have watched Universal grow and now with the inclusion of Islands of Adventure and Volcano Bay the entertainment value we get from the cost of the tickets is far better than Disney.  The cost of a visit to Florida is now higher than ever when factoring a higher cost of living in the US and a weak Pound, but it didn’t prepare us this time for some really high price hikes, parking from $12 to $26 dollars a day and $5 for a bottle of water.  We visited in October and managed to do all the major rides, our favourites are the Diagon Alley and Hagrids Magical Creatures which is probably the best ride in Florida.

I really enjoyed universal. Eat riding the bike and helping ET get home. Also the TV animals stunts. Meeting the characters and getting a photo with each one. Disappointed couldn’t just see Harry Potter train platform without paying extra. Would have been fun if the dirty home had opened door just to shock you.

For those Harry Potter fans you need to experience this. I recently took my son to Universal Studios for vacation. Entering Diagon Alley and touring Hogwarts Castle made me lose reality for a bit and to see my son's eyes light up in wonder and amazement was worth the trip alone.

This was my first visit to Universal Studios. While I liked the rides better at Island of Adventure, I liked the Universal park better. It was less crowded & laid out better. I came in to this trip thinking it would be similar to Disney, but it’s not even comparable to Disney. I felt that the park, the attractions, & the rides were more similar to Six Flags; just on steroids. Just like I thought with Islands of Adventure, Harry Potter’s Daigon Alley was the best attraction. The Simpsons attraction was a close second. The wait times at Universal were not as long as the wait times at Islands of Adventure. I enjoyed my time at the parks & would definitely go back
A Magical place for every group of People . The fun loving land people will remember for lifetime . Must go place .

Visited on the December 18th and everything was going great. Wait times weren’t high and the weather was so nice! Towards the end of the night by 7:20, we decided to do Transformers before heading out. As we got to the loading area, we heard two girl employees yell loudly at other people. They were being very rude for no reason and even rolled their eyes at them. I get that you wanna leave and you’re tired but that was no way to treat people! Everyone else was so wonderful so we were very shocked to see that. They had such an impatient tone and would not stop yelling. The ride was empty there’s no need to be that rude!! Please make sure they get spoken to as no one should be treated like that.

Improved a lot since last visit years back. It was an amazing experience for the whole family. Kids thoroughly enjoyed it. The gringotts ride and transformers ride is the highlight. It was raining but still there was a huge rush. Definitely worth visiting. Christmas break time it was crowded.

This was the first time our family had been to Universal. First off we did not know the difference between the parks. We went to universal studios and Island of Adventure. Universal Studios had one roller coaster and mostly 4D type rides. There was so much to see and do for all ages. I hate roller coasters, as does my 6 year old, but my 13 year old loves them. There was enough to do and see that everyone had a good experience. One thing I had wished I known was that we could bring outside food. That would have really helped with cost inside the park. (One corn dog was $10.) I would have brought a backpack as well to more easily carry out stuff. We had lots of fun! Definitely will go back. If you’re a first timer like me and cheap, check with your hotel about shuttle service as parking starts at $26/day. There is a lot to be said about being picked up vs searching for the car after a long day of walking.

I purchased the tickets to the park whilst they were on special offer, 14 days for the price of 7. This was a park hopper ticket for the 3 park ticket, which gives you entrance to Universal Studio, Islands of Adventure, Volcano Bay along with evening access to the bars and clubs in City Walk.  Universal Studios as I’m sure you can imagine is based around a film set and really has some excellent attractions. Bearing in mind that we were two adults visiting the park I can’t really comment on the kids ride. It’s fair to say though that at Universal Studio there are a lot of rides and side attractions for kids.  Due to the time of year that we attended the queue times were really short which allowed us to ride more than once..  The Simpsons Ride has been upgraded from the Back to the Future Ride and is based on the Krustyland theme park. This is a must for any Simpsons fan.  Revenge of the Mummy Based on the film, this is a high speed rollercoaster ride in the dark with sudden twists, turns and surprises.  Men in Black Is now a little dated, but is still good fun. You are appointed as a rookie agent as you make your way through the top secret underground headquarters. You then board a training vehicle and shoot "the scum of the universe" who have escaped from their intergalactic prison transport.  E.T. Adventure Although the film was released years ago, this ride is still as good today as it was when it was opened. On this ride you help ET save the green planet.  The Transformers 3D You are recruited to save Earth from Megatron and his Decepticons.  The Hollywood Rip Ride Rocket Listen to your favourite tracks whilst being taken up at 90 degrees, before dropping down and accelerating to 65mph in this very intense rollercoaster.  This park is so much fun.

We have been to HHN at universal studios several times. Our Disney/Universal expert, Robyn, with Dream Makers Vacation Services, really came through for us on this trip. I consider myself pretty good on knowing the ins and outs of Universal, but Robyn gave me some great advice on new restaurants at Citywalk, and rides at the parks. Stranger Things and Us were two of our top houses this year. Always get the express pass for HHN. And the new Hagrids roller coaster is the best I’ve ridden!!! Amazing!!

We had 3 day 3 park tickets. We didn't go to Volcano Bay, so that gave us extra time at the other two parks. We mainly spent a lot of time in Harry Potter areas. I didn't go on that many rides, but my daughter and her friend went on most of them. They avoided the Hulk one though. I went on the Jurassic Park ride and nearly had heart attack!! The light show at night was magical. It repeats every hour after sunset, so if you missed one you can wait for the next one. We thoroughly enjoyed it. The newest ride was either had a long que or closed every time we tried. We ate at the Leaky Cauldron and Mythos. the girls purchased multi day Halloween Horror night tickets and went 3 nights. They said it waas fantastic.

My family LOVED Volcano Bay. Loved. Everyone had such an amazing time, there were activities for all of us (5 people). My thrill seekers loved the drop water slides, while my oldest and I found our happy place with the water coaster and wave pool. The staff were helpful and pleasant, particularly Carl. We met Carl our first day assisting with lockers, and again another day offering help to those who needed it. When we booked our trip going to Volcano Bay was not high on our priority list, as it felt like an unneeded bonus to Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure. It quickly became a favorite and was our first stop Christmas morning! Highly recommend for anyone one the fence about going to Volcano Bay...do it!!! PS We had no little ones (9 was our youngest) but it seemed there was plenty for them to do. Yes there were rides that catered to older kids and up but the area for the littles looked fun. I’m sure if our kids were younger they would have still enjoyed Volcano Bay.

Universal studios Harry Potter world was fantastic! The only down fall was Hagrid’s motorbike ride had a 3 hour queue at 9.15am! And through the day, the lowest queue time for this was 1h 30 so we didn’t manage to get on it.  There were lots of virtual 3D & 4D rides / shows which is great for those who don’t like roller coasters.  We didn’t have time to do both islands of adventure and universal studios so did have return for a 2nd day.

We toyed with the idea of a VIP experience or Express passes for Universal Studios and decided on Express. I’m glad we did this as there wasn’t anywhere near as much to do here as Island of adventure. They were well worth having as went straight to the front of the queues as it wasn’t hugely busy. I personally really enjoyed the rides here although a bit samey. Kids enjoyed it less and was more interested in the churros but had a lovely leisurely day all the same.
Realy nice "town" from the Harry Potter-movies! Great Service and personal working there and we will not forget!

We went to Universal Studios Theme Park in November. It was a good time of year to go there, warm but not too hot and cool in the evenings. Although it was warm in the day, as soon as the sun went down it got pretty cool. The first day I was there I had to buy a hoodie. We discovered that we could get on the rides as quickly as the people that bought the fast pass if we went into the single rider lines. Many of the rides you can't really converse with your friends on the rides anyway and it made the time waiting a lot less. The down side of this is that in some cases you miss part of the experience. For instance in the Harry Potter Castle there is a lot to see as you wind through the line. The singles line bypasses many parts. For me the sacrifice was worth the time savings!

When we plan a trip to Disney world, we usually set aside a day for Universal. But many things disappointed me this time and I wanted to post this review to have people consider if they really want to spend the money for a day there. At least so your homework. 1) First if all - if you want to see all of Happy Potter - you will need to pay to get into 2 parks. We payed $185.31 ($174+tax) for a 2 Park one day ticket per person. It costs more if you buy at the ticket booth in the park. I used a mobile delivery and had the ticket delivered to my smartphone. That’s a lot of money for a family of 4.  2) This time of year - the park is only open until 7pm. A lot of ground to cover for 2 parks and considering how much you are paying g for a ticket. 3) So you would expect the rides to be in good working condition. Especially the widely popular Harry Potter section. When we got there, the 2 rides in IOA: the new Hagrid’s Motorbike ride was closed. Harry Potter and the forbidden journey was experiencing delays. So we headed to The Eacape from Gringots ride at Universal. Wait was posted as 55 minutes. The line went slowly. We wished we had our backpack with some drink and snacks - but we had to put it in a locker ! We got to near of the end of the line after waiting in the queue for more than a 90 minutes and they “flushed the queue” due to technical difficulties! They did give us a FP on the way out - but it didn’t seem to cover the time lost (I could have went on 3 Other rides), sore feet and back from waiting in line that long (hey that’s messing with my Health and ability to do other things as a result of pain); needless to say - everyone was very upset. Not to mention that the People in line flooded the streets and now everything else was impossible to get into. Even Hogwarts express train - wasn’t an express and had a 55 minute wait. So we quickly Rushed to the Leaky Cauldron - which had really filled up. We were able to get some good food and rest a while. My Cottage pie came with a salad and was very good. We also got the bangers and mash - and my so. And his GF enjoyed those. Hubby got the fish pie and enjoyed that. We also got a kids Mac and cheese with a side of grapes and applesauce which also was good. They do seat you - maybe because it was busy. But we ended up getting a seat against the wall that was quiet. After we were done - we checked the time for Hogwarts Express - and it was still long ! So we headed to the front of the park where we could use the Front entrance to switch to the other park (IOA) since the Hogwarts Express lube was too long.. Disappointing. I used the opportunity to visit with guest relations.  4) Guest relations and what they can do: I’ll start out by saying the young woman who assisted us was very nice. However, the best she could do was offer us each another FP. I would have preferred a partial refund or another FP. I also brought up the fact that we had to pay for a locker for the ride - she didn’t bring it up on her own. Practically had to beg to get the $2 back. But She did give us $2 cash.  5) which brings me to the lockers. Most of the thrill rides have the lockers. It’s a pain and time consuming to get your stuff in and out. It requires the code from your ticket - but the code doesn’t work from a smartphone and you need to get a paper one from an attendant in the area. On top of that - If you need a Large locker - you need to pay $2 for it. We had a large backpack -So we had to pay it. They don’t take cash. You need a credit card. And you need to spend this $2 for each ride !!! What a way to make even more money after robbing you the cost of your ticket !  6) we finally got into IOA thru the front entrance. We bypassed the Incredible Hulk and the Spider-Man ride so we could get to the back of the park to check out the Wizarding world of Harry Potter before it was dark. On the way - we also noticed the King Kong ride was partially outside. So after taking some pics in Harry Potter world I’m the daylight - we back-tracked to the Skull Island King Kong ride instead of using a FP to ride Harry Potter and the forbidden journey. Since the line was long and the ride is inside, we figured we could come back. We waited a little while in the FP King Kong line - and it was very cool - albeit a bit shorter than I expected.  7) the Hagrid motorbike line was over 100 minutes and had closed on and off thru the day, so...  8) we went back to Harry Potter to find the Forbidden Journey ride closed !! It was 6pm and they were closing in an hour and we had not ridden any Harry Potter rides! We made a bee-line for the Howard’s express - but we first had to wait in line to go thru the ticket line to go to the other land in Universal. After waiting for 10 minutes in the ticket line we the. Went to wait in the Hogwarts express line. I checked the wait times one more time to see if Escape from Gringots might have reopened - holding out little hope - since it was closed most of the day after our wait. Miraculously it was open with a 25 minute wait. We made a bee-line to it after our Hogwarts express ride. We barely made it Into line at 6:58. And after waiting the allotted time - we finely were able to ride the ride! So we didn’t go home totally disappointed.  8) on a positive note - after we were done the ride - we wandered around a mostly deserted Diagon Alley. We also finally saw the dragon breath fire. The dragon didn’t breathe fire thru the day. Which is another negative. I believe the dragon breathed fire all thru the day when we were there last 5 years ago.  Thru the day we also managed to go on the Mummy, MIB and the Simpsons.  That’s 7 rides in 8.5 hours. That’s $26.47 a ride. I guess you have to also account for lunch and ambiance... but still... I can understand that the new Hagrid ride might be done because it’s new - but the other 2 have been around for over 5 years ! They shouldn’t be down. If they need maintenance - please do the maintenance in the Off-hours when no one is in the park. Also note that I read that one of the Harry Potter rides will be down for maintenance Jam 16-17 - so consider that if you plan to go on either of those days.  9) did i mention that you can save some time and get FPs for all the rides by staying on property ($$) or buying a FP ticket for all the rides for a mere $96 on top of what you’re paying already... thanks Universal ...  10) we won’t be going back any time soon. The old rides we’ve done and we’ll wait for the Harry Potter rides to be fixed or for the popularity to wean... if you really need to go - I recommend you do your homework. Download the “Universal wait times” app and monitor it a few days prior to going... check and see thru the day if the rides remain up. And buy your tickets online a day or so before you plan to go when you know the weather will be good and the rides are running. You can use the ticket they send you to your email from your phone.  Good luck !  ... And I hope to see some better ticket discounts and or longer hours from Universal for their customers. Otherwise I believe they are just thinking of making the most $$ for themselves.
We only had one day so we paid extra for fast passes. We had such a great day. The highlight was all the Harry Potter rides & worlds but the Jurassic Park ride was fantastic too. Greatly recommended
Crowded beyond belief..prices has gone sky high. Tickets and food was 1500$ for a day of parkwalking in Line.
180.00 each to get in. Would never go again. Too many other things to do around orlando. Pay 750.00 to wait in lines for 2 hours and so many rude people I couldn't believe it.

Only the Harry Potter Part was convincing, for all other attractions we had to wait almost ages to do them, the waiting times varied between 1 and 4 hours for one attraction, thats definitely too long, finally i was very disappointed, fazit: not recommandable
My family and I had a great 3 days at Universal. The rides were great and the lines were minimal. Harry potter world was beyond incredible!

Love Universal. Great rides we chose Universal over Disney so we could do the new Hagrid Motorcycle Ride. We figured we don't have any little kids so Disney wouldn't be too much fun and we aren't really big Star Wars Fans.

AMAZING! Had Douglas as a guide and he was incredible. He knew so much about the park and was very attentive to our needs. Great ambassador for Universal. Had enough time to do two parks in one day and not feel rushed. Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure were amazing. Loved Hagrid's Motorbike ride. Great time of year to go not super crowded. Was our first visit and we all had a blast!

We stayed in Orlando & visited the studios & Islands of Adventure every day for 6 days. We had an amazing time, the staff were friendly & helpful, the interaction with the characters was incredible & only down side was very long queue's on some days but all in all it was better than expected plus we got to see the Macy's Christmas parade which was brilliant.

In some ways, yes. The rides are more aggressive than most of what Disney offers, and the lines move faster. Of course you can also purchase a pass to bypass the lines, too. The best way to see all of the biggest attractions in one day is to purchase a guided tour.

Hi. Our experience in Hagrid’s Magical Creatures Motorbike Adventure today was the worst memory ever. We wait more tham 90 min, my kid RAFAELA BASTIAN was measured 3 times before our turn and all of them say “ok, have a great ride” for her. The last staff, before 90 min waiting, tell us that she isn’t tall enough! Why let her wait so long? Why others staffs tells that she can? Why they are so cruel with her? If the first guy told us that she is not tall enough we will lose our time in other part but they prefer lie to us until the time of the ride! Very sad pay a lot of money, spend a lot of time To see my Kid cry like that. You destroyed our magic Hogwarts memories today.

We love to visit Universal Studios. I had read many bad reviews lately about security but they checked our bags at all the entrances. Most all the employees were very nice and helpful. Most of the lines moved quickly and the laser light show was neat to see. There were a few complaints we had that the park needs to improve upon. First and foremost the park hours. As much as you pay to get in and they close the park at 6PM and 7PM??? WHAT! One night closed at 6PM for a private party. Why should all the people who paid full price have to leave early because of a private party. This should be AFTER HOURS! Weekend hours were 8PM. The park hours should be at the very least until 8PM every night. Secondly, all the restruants and food venders close an hour before closing. So on a night they close at 6 all the food vendors are shut down at 5. Again...poor planning on Universal's part. Food should be served up until at least closing time.
