Don't send your customers away hungry. Thirdly, I love that the parks open early and have fast passes for those who stay in the resorts but only one park is open early. Shouldn't it be both? So past those few things we were happy and had fun. The park was also very clean and maintaince on rides shut down were announced a head of time.
Harry Potter was amazing! It was absolute perfection! The rest of the parks are very fun as well. Everyone is friendly and it is clean

There is a lot to pack in here and recommend starting with the Harry Potter attraction first because you will want to spend a lot of time there. Stay at a Universal-related hotel for an hour early admission. BIG benefit! Be aware that many of the rides are immersive 3D rides with a lot of rocking and rolling. They do a good job of putting you in the scenes but after a while they can get a bit repetitive. A fun experience overall and a totally different vibe than Disney. Much more adult-centric here.

We went at the end of January. The temps were chilly in the mornings and evenings, but very nice once the sun got up and going. Jeans and long sleeved shirts would probably be enough for most people but, if you’re cold natured, take a light jacket or sweater. Going early in the year avoids the crowds of Summer. I think the longest we waited for any ride was twenty minutes. For most of them, we walked all the way to the front of the ride without stopping.

We took our kids(5,8) to Universal while we were on vacation and opted to spend a little more and get the VIP tour. It was an extra $189 added into the $160 ticket, it included breakfast and lunch.   When we arrived it was 9am and our tour started at 9:30a. We parked valet(included in price of VIP ticket) and asked where to go. There was a walk to a small cafe for breakfast, no one showed us how to get there or escorted us to the cafe. It was a little bit of a walk and some confusion on where to go but we found it! The girl that greeted us was very nice, showed us where our table was and sat us down with a couple of families. We were confused because there was open tables and she didn’t say “Hey! These guys will be on your tour with you also!” She just walked away lol. The breakfast was fine, nothing fantastic. Had all the basics..eggs, bacon, bagels, pastries etc. Our tour guide showed up and asked what we were excited to do today and if we had any preferences. We did say we wanted to do the Jurassic ride, but told us it was too cold for that. So, we couldn’t go on.  We started our tour right at 9:30a. Our guide was super nice! She took us right to our first ride and from there we didn’t stop for 7 hours. We did 12 rides total. It was a lot. I was hoping to go to a show or something to break up the rides but there was no break except for lunch(45min). By the time we were done I think everyone had an upset stomach because of all the rides and running around for 7 hours. My 5 year old was so tired and so wasn’t my 8yr old that they didn’t even want to stay for the Super Hero dinner we had planned, they just wanted to leave.  I do like that she got us in front of all the lines and we literally didn’t have to wait at all. But, in the future they should take a survey on what people expect out of the experience. Our group was not ride focused 100%, and our tour guide was. She had us running all over and everyone was just exhausted by the end. I think we would of all liked to have time to stop and take some pictures, try some butter beer etc.  Over all it was fun! And my oldest really enjoyed it. The tour guide answered every single question he had and was so kind to him. She never once got annoyed with him lol. We would def do it again!

We had a great couple of days here. Its great just to walk around here. Much slower pace than disney, the rides are excellent and the special effects are awesome. We watched the the light and projection show at the end of the evening was great.
Amazing place to visit and takes pictures everywhere. Super magic and fabulous park in Orlando......

We have been coming to this park since our kids were teenagers and 11 years later we still come as a family along with our seven-year-old granddaughter. The most popular part of Universal is definitely the Harry Potter theme area. It gets busy fast so head there first if you are interested. I don’t have any interest in Harry Potter but it was still really cool to go into this area. We missed the entrance to this so pay attention to the map. When you enter, you are in a whole different world. You feel like you are actually in the books\movies. Make sure to try some butterbeer (we prefer frozen) and ride Harry Potter and the escape from Gringotts! If you’re a fan of The Simpsons, there are rides, restaurant, and a whole section dedicated to the show. The rip rocket is a fun roller coaster and you get to pick the music you want to listen to while on it. The Men in Black ride is another favorite and if you go in as a single rider instead of a group, you get on quicker and avoid the longer lines. If you are in a wheelchair, you can ride this. Universal studios has 3-D / 4-D attractions that I was able to go into with my wheelchair. They include the Despicable Me Minion Mayham, Shrek, and The Jimmy Fallon ride. There are other rides and shows that will help fill up your day also. We usually spend the shorter day at Universal and we will spend a longer day at Islands of adventure. There’s no way we could ever do both parks in a day with our whole family so we always get the 2 day 2 park pass. We always make sure to catch the Halloween horror make up show and The Animal Actors on location. Both are great for all ages and very entertaining. The animal show uses rescue animals and showcases their different talents! Some of them have even been in movies or TV shows. My husband is a big Blues Brothers fan and they have a cool little show with actors singing songs from the movie. The universal superstar parade is also worth checking out while characters from different movies and shows dance and sing. There are several different theme restaurants to check out. They are not cheap when it comes to their meals. However, they have a family meal deal and a refillable cup deal. The refillable cup deal is great and definitely saves money on drinks! You are allowed to bring in bottled water, sandwiches, bags of chips, etc. (full details on website). This is definitely a money saver.

After the walking and stair climbing we did in one day, we felt like we completed the Universe! Would not have changed it for a thing. Universal definitely has the whole fast pass thing over Disney. Yes it is expensive, but only having one day to do it all we did 17 rides in 8 hours. This was worth every penny. Highly recommend going to Universal and spend the money if you don't have the time.

We last visited about 5 years ago, so there have been many additions to both parks since our last visit. We love the new additions for Harry Potter. We enjoyed Diagon alley and Escape from Gringotts, the train ride connecting the 2 parks and our favorite was Hagrid's motorbike ride. We love that there are also food chains within the park so you don't have to eat the same old park fare. We had pretzels at Aunt Annies and a turkey leg at Thunder Falls. We enjoyed riding some old favorites, like Men in Black, The Mummy, Rip Rockit, and The Hulk. Be sure to get a fast pass by either staying at a resort hotel, or purchasing since it allows you to get on many more rides and avoid the long lines.

Universal studios is the place to go! Spent several days at Disney (unfortunately) and were very disappointed and felt cheated. Universal was wonderful! No ridiculous lines, lots of fun rides intermingled for all ages. Good restaurants with nice variety and fair prices. Can’t say a bad thing about. Employees were friendly, helpful and playful.

Universal receives A++++ in regards to their customer service. My son has a seizure disorder and the Park was amazing handling his needs. He received a card with return times for lines greater than 30 minutes. If line was less than 30 minutes he was able to get right on; and they gave us multiple return times at the same time so we could do an area of the park and move on to the next when done.  Hats off to you Universal for making my son feel like a King for two days. He finally felt like he was “special” and not “different” I wish I could say the same for Disney.... where we could only reserve one “fast pass” with the DAS at a time. We spent most of our day sitting around doing nothing.
Indoor rides are really seeing the videos at each turn , swoop or stop of the car you ride in- not for preschoolers, in my opinion. Wait till kids are 8 years old and up! Expensive and worth it!!

Our son loved it. Our pockets hated it :) Yes, its like in the movies, yes you feel the magic. However, for me, an adult joyning my son and not interested to get into any of the carousels or other experiences, I felt extremly frustrated that I had to pay 170 USD just for being a pedestrian in this park. I think there should be lower price for the accompanying adult who is not interested in the experience as such. I spent anyway money on food, merchandise etc.

Was not impressed with Universal theme park. Not enough rides as Jurassic Park was blocked off. We had no warning that a big part of the park was closed. Gift shops were all open as were food and drink stands. 1 day ticket for 1 person cost $195.00, same $ for each theme park. We have been in all of the other parks and LOVED everyone of them. We now wish we had repeated another park. Universal was sorry!

This was a nice park with fairly good rides, but the experience was somewhat ruined by the "express pass" concept. This was incredibly unfair, and Disney handles this so much better. What they don't tell you is that your tickets do not guarantee you get to ride their rides, they just get you into the park. At that point you essentially have standby tickets. If there is nobody in the express line, they will let some of the regular people (90% of the park population at least) onto the ride. It's maddening to watch these people cut in front of us again and again, and they make no effort to hide the express lines from view. They just walk right by the normals over and over again, while we wait hours for a major attraction. If you don't pay for the express tickets, you are limited to either the lesser rides in the park (and still waiting 15-60 minutes), or to waiting as much as 4 hours to go on a major ride. Yes, I saw them at 240 minutes. Meanwhile, the express passers can walk right onto any ride. If you don't pay the extra for the express pass, you've basically been fooled into buying standby access.
Universal in Orlando is a great time!! Parking is efficient. I had trouble finding the uber station. Package pick up was great and easy to use highly recommended instead of carrying all your stuff.

We spent four days in Orlando and went to Universal on our second day. We loved it! We have two teenager boys who also really enjoyed it. Because it was Thanksgiving week, we purchased a fast pass. It was a great investment to be able to get on the rides quicker during the peak tourist season. The Christmas decorations were a fun touch too.

Our family LOVES Universal! Here are the favourites for us... Harry Potter World (all of the rides, the feel of the area, the Hogwarts Express between the two parks, and the dragon), Transformers, Shrek, Minions, Marvel everything, the Simpsons, and MIB.  The food options are great! The parades are fun for the entire family. Unlike Disney the characters properly interact with the kids and will stand still for a photo op where you don't have to buy a photo package.  Wait to purchase the Express Pass until the day of your visit. If the park isn't packed, then you may not need it. Here is the comparison of Express Pass vs Disney's Fast Pass. Because Disney allows you to select your Fast Pass uses up to 60 days in advance you may not really get the fast pass experience for a lot of rides. The day we went we could only use fast pass for 2 rides. Universal has Disney beat on this where all of the rides (except for the new Hagrid's Motorbike) are eligible for Express Pass. It is so much more value and simple to use than the Disney system which is prone to a disappointing experience.  At Universal there is just so much to do and it is fun for all ages!
Visited here for one day, the awe this park offers never dies, would highly recommend a visit here, even if you have been before.

My husband and I just returned from 5 fun-filled days at Universal Orlando. I've been on a ketogenic diet (low carb/high fat) for seizure control for more than 5 years. I was concerned when I looked at their online menus bc everything is high carb. I emailed Universal prior to going and asked about keto options and never got a reply so I packed my KetoVie just in case there was nothing I could eat. Turns out I didn't have to be concerned. Starbucks prepared my 2/3 coffee, 1/3 heavy whipping cream every morning. At the on-site restaurants (Leaky Cauldron, 3 Broomsticks) I learned that when you order the cashiers/waitstaff at Universal can not stray from the printed menu items but will gladly call for a head cook (who knows whats in the food) to come out and discuss your needs with you and have the food prepared just for you. I have been on keto so long that I follow rules and don't need explicit carb counts so if you are counting carbs it might be a problem. For example, at the 3 Broomsticks I ordered the American breakfast and they substituted bacon, sausage, and sauteed mushrooms for the potatoes and bread. They did the same for me at Citywalk's BigFire restaurant where I had delicious grilled brussel sprouts, grilled mixed veggies, and trout. My order included only the veggies I can eat - no picking out potatoes, carrots etc... BigFire had lots on their menu I could eat and the food was delightfully fresh and simple.
So much fun for kids and us. The lines were not too long, except 1 attraction. it was our 3 time and kids still want to come back again.

Islands of Adventure is a great park to spend a day. My wife and I went early on a Sunday in February. Not crowded, maybe a 20 minute wait for the Hulk roller coaster - which, btw, is a ridiculous thrill ride, glad I did it, would never do it again! (but that's just me). I love the references to old cartoon characters throughout the park and there are super heroes around every corner for the kids (and kids at heart).  The park was not crowded until the afternoon at the Harry Potter Hogsmeade town which is the most popular area. Loved the Popeye raft ride (you WILL get soaked!) The Jurassic Park River Adventure was another highlight. The detail in the Harry Potter Hogswart castle is amazing.  We ate lunch at Captain America Diner because they had the Impossible burger for my wife. I had a regular burger which was pretty tasteless and way overpriced.  The shopping is pretty good - if you're a comic book buff, they have a great store for that with great prices. All in all, a great day and you can easily take in the whole Islands of Adventure area in one day.  We didn't bother with the express passes and really didn't need them - longest line was Harry Potter - but I can see how they may be worth it if the park is more crowded.

We decided to take our grandson to Universal Studios for his seventh birthday. What a great choice! We all had a wonderful time. The park is very well run! Strongly urge the express pass. It is well worth the investment!

I decided to take my wife and three daughters (6, 4, and 18 mo) here for an extended weekend trip and we had a blast. We stayed at Loews Royal Pacific for three nights and spent three days in the parks. We used Xpress Passes and park hoppers which allowed us to experience everything multiple times and meet most of the characters. There was something to do for the whole family. The best part is that there’s a child swap room for every attraction, so it doesn’t matter if you have small ones who can’t ride. They can relax and hangout right off the loading area. That’s a big deal for families.  We held the Disney annual pass for a year and visited all the parks many times. Somehow it always resulted in frustration at their guest service, construction, crowds, fastpass system, and so on. We would be exhausted before we even entered the park. Not at Universal! No rides were down and no glitches that caused us precious time spent at guest services. As far as transportation goes, water taxi was able to get us in the park in less than 20 minutes from our resort. Fantastic. To receive this level of service at Disney, you would need to spend at least 20K on top of being in their vacation club.  I feel that we definitely got our money’s worth at Universal and this will be our new family destination. My kids are still talking about our trip and are already planning for next year!

So we came here because we had a cheer competition to attend and decided we’d make the most of trip and stay at one of Universal’s premier resorts so we could get free express passes to skip the lines. We also purchased Dining passes since there is 5 of us, 3 children and 2 adults which my son son who is 10 is charged as an adult. That is $69.95 per person per day for the full dining plan. We purchased 2 days worth. I thought that would help me save money rather than paying the overpriced food at the park but I wish I just would have paid while at the park because we would have paid less. If you do the math on what I just said for the dining passes it comes up to $700 for 5 people in 2 days. When I added up all the money of what we actually ordered with our passes including some expensive meals at Margaritaville 2 nights in a row with some meals that cost over $20 a pop, it only came up to like $495. So really I feel like I’ve been robbed of $200. It’s all good, I know now. Thanks Universal for everything that you do to overcharge families. Everything else about the trip was great, but I don’t like the feel of not getting my money’s worth or feeling cheated which is what I do in this situation.

Universal used to be my favourite park, however now every single ride is a similar 4D experience -- typically some moving car, 3D screens, and at least one moment where you'll get hit with a squirt of water. Wish they would offer some more varying experiences. Still, the rides are a lot of fun.
Loved going round Universal, they have put a lot of thought and detail into their streets and rides. Spent an extra day (than planned) here as we enjoyed it so much.

Universal is a full day out. The rides are mainly geared towards children 8+ and adults.  Parking is easy and costs $25, cost covers the whole day. Make a note of your parking space because the lot of huge.  The best area is Harry Potter, we are not fans but thought the area was very well visually designed with a lot to see. It’s easy to miss the entrance to the area, close to Kings Cross train station. Definitely worth trying the Butter beer, it’s sweet with an milkshake texture.  Harry Potter train was very good and recommended. You will need a 2 park ticket as the ride takes you to Adventure island’s park next door.  We didn’t have Express passes and managed to get on most rides easily in a day. Most rides no more than 20-25 mins.  A lot of the rides are 3D or simulator rides. Some great rides include: Transformers- simulator ride while is a very jerky but fun. Mummy - roller coaster in the dark Simpson’s - 3D simulator fun ride Men in black - shooting the Aliens while in a car ET - helping ET escape while on a bike Sherk is a show - good fun  Fast and furious was boring and not worth the wait.  Plenty of places to eat and drink, we chose to wait and eat at City Walk.

We were in Florida for the last two weeks of February. We enjoyed a three day park to park passport at Universal Studios. This gave us a day at each of the attractions. We also purchased the Fast Pass, as I have a disability that made waiting in lines painful. This was well worth the cost, as we spent little time in lines. The park was clean, bright, a little loud for my taste, but it didn't bother my son or husband. We enjoyed everything we could squeeze in each day. The rides/attractions are very interesting and fun, though my son was too large for all of the Harry Potter rides on both sides of the train ride, and that was the main reason that he went to Universal.He has Autism, and this was very distressing for him. We found lots of various souvenirs to purchase, including our family crests and histories! My son worked on his key chain collection, and managed to get several items from the Harry Potter collection for his "House". We had a fabulous time, tried all different kinds of food, went on wonderful rides and attractions, saw amazing things, and can't wait to come back?

Just mind blowing. They have 3 parks; Universal Studios Florida, Universal’s Islands of Adventure and Volcano Bay. Volcano Bay is a water park, other two are theme parks. If you are a crazy Harry Potter fan, you MUST visit both the theme parks. We went during a non holiday season in February during a week day. We were able to finish both the parks in two days without taking express pass. There is a Hogwart’s Express train that takes you from one park to another but for that you need ticket to both parks wherein you can visit both the parks on same day. Butter beer in the Hogwart’s castle is a must. I would suggest finishing Harry Potter rides in Universal’s Islands of Adventure first as soon as you enter Universal. Go as soon as park opens, lines start growing between 11 to 2. Shreik in Universal Studios Florida was a literal torture, we did not like it. You WILL get completely wet in Popeye’s ride, so make sure you carry additional clothes for the ride. There is a dryer outside the ride for a $5. Volcano bay water park was just fun. It has multiple tube rides, they check your weight every time before you ride so that it is safe to ride. Aqua Coaster ride was the highlight. It is a roller coaster water ride which allows minimum of 2 and maximum of 4 riders per tube. They have a wave pool with beach like sand and chairs. There is a lazy river that you can relax on a tube. There is also a crazy river with water flowing at a faster rate, you have to wear life jacket to go in. There is a 80 degree slide from the top of volcano mountain. You stand inside a tube and the floor beneath your legs opens and you slide down fast. Almost every one complained that it scratches your back, I could see everyone’s back getting red rashes. Overall universal studios was a total fun. I highly recommend if you are visiting Orlando.  There is a Bus stand for Universal. This place is between universal studios entrance and universal parking. Free shuttle buses run to universal hotels. There is also a to and fro free shuttle for Volcano Bay park.

Be forewarned, if you are a person size, as I am, you will not be able to ride 50% of the rides. I can ride every ride at WDW without issue, the rides at Universal were made for people no taller the 5' 6" and under 250 lbs. If you are outside of those dimensions you are out of luck as far as rollercoasters, or strap in rides go. It's a shame their main competitor can accommodate individuals of all shapes and sizes, but Universal decides to cut out people of size. If you have a choice, go elsewhere.

Had Fass Pass from the Hard Rock Hotel.These are suppose to be good up to and on the day of check out. On our day of check out we stowed our bags and headed to the park. The first ride was to be the HULK coaster. Showed the Fast Pass Hard Rock Room card and the attendant said it was expired and took the card and told me to go to guest services if I wanted to "get ahead of the line" as if I had done something wrong manner.Needless to say lost 2 hrs park time lost doing the social distancing thing while wondering what went wrong. Long story short also it rained half the day so we missed alot of new rides because of someones error. I have saved alot and sacrificed alot to make this vacation happen for my family and park personnel seem to not care one bit.

We bought military universal tickets $204 an adult for both parks and it was OK, the first day and yes social distancing was in full force. The food app. doesn't work in every restaurant a fast pass was useful it wasn't to crowded. The next day was better but for what I paid the fun just wasn't like universal fun. I 'd recommend waiting unless you want lots of peace and quite.

Universal did a great job with keeping the parks clean! Here are the things they did: - Morning parking is every other space, so when we got out of our car, we are distanced from other cars. Eventually the spots are filled, as there are cars next to us when we return. - temp check upon entry - Continuous disinfecting of moving walkway railings. There are people at one end of each walkway, continuously wiping the railings - 6ft social distance on most places - using ID (instead of fingerprints) for the ticket identification - virtual lines for long lines, so even if you wait, most of the waiting is outdoor. The queue move swiftly indoor, limiting the time spent in a crowd indoor - 12 ft distance on indoor queue, often skipping a row, so you are always at least 6ft away from other parties - mandatory hand sanitizer prior to boarding every ride - roller coaster: roughly 3 rows apart between parties - theater like seating (shrek, bourne, etc): at least 3 seats apart between parties and every other row seating - compartment ride (hogwarts express, gringotts, simpson, spiderman, etc): one compartment per party. - Rides are sprayed after every rides. - Most store doors are open to minimize touchings - door knobs, surfaces, railings are wiped often - order food via app and we take the plates from the tray to minimize touching - everybody wears masks inside the park - some decor are removed to provide more space for people - reduced crowd, I am not sure if this is intentional. There might be a crowd entering the park, but once inside, the crowd dispersed throughout the park.  We had a great time there and felt safe. Thank you Universal! We especially love the Wizarding World of Harry Potter, the low crowd really enabled us to enjoy the details of Hogsmeade & Diagon Alley.  And Bourne Stuntacular is really awesome! They just opened last week and it is a must see!  I hope this helps with your decision whether to go during this time!

I was highly satisfied with their safety precautions during the entire time there. Every ride we got on someone was wiping and spraying after every group.There are signs and everywhere about staying ft apart and there pretty vocal about it if you don't. We went there to surprise the kids for there birthday.This might sound crazy but going during COVID was pretty tight. Although some of the parades and shows was not going the lines to the ride wait was 20 mins at max. Only ride we wasn't able to make it to was the mummy it was virtual and speed pass only and it was all booked up so if you go download the app and virtually book that first.
Our trip to universal Studios was very awesome the characters and the rides was great.seeing spiderman. dinosaur s and all different characters you can imagine.
lots of fun, noy very crowded did IOA and universal in the same day rode all the atractions some twice, lots of social distancing, felt safe the entire time, friendly employees. just an awsome time.

My wife and I went to Islands of Adventure and found that social distancing was largely ignored. The rides seem to be a bit better, but people can't seem to read where the social distance line is and stop piling on top of you. A couple of the rides weren't even wiped down after people exited the ride. We thought the access to the parks were supposed to be limited at this time, but that did not appear to be the case. Universal should take a hint from Disney and keep people who are drinking and eating stationary. The wait times for rides were ridiculous. You really can't get on most without a long wait unless you spend the extra money for the express pass. The Hulk coaster had an 85 minute wait 2 hours after the park opened. Hagrid's ride was a 2 hour wait. We are Florida residents and probably won't go back for a while.
Overall, lots of fun, but make sure you get the two-park pass and take the Hogwarts Express between the two parks. This "ride" is a hoot@

We visited Universal on August 25 (Tuesday). We arrived around 10:00 AM. We experienced everything except the ET ride and Bourne. We stayed until 5:00. We did not have express passes. It was quite empty. If we waited, it was because we had to wait until the next show, etc. Which was never more than 20 minutes. We had been here five years ago. Nothing seemed new. We enjoyed Diagon Alley because no one was around. So easy to navigate. What we did notice is that the qualify of the virtual rides have diminished. We loved the Simpsons five years ago. Rode it many times. This time, just once. At first I just thought it was my eyes getting older :) but my teenage daughter complained that the screens were not that clear. Even the Harry Potter was blurry. We were really disappointed by this park for that reason. They need to invest in updating the graphics every few years apparently. (Spider Man was great at Islands of Adventure and that was updated recently) Jimmy Fallon was the clearest one at Universal.. We ate at The Leaky Cauldrin. It seems they want everyone to order with the app. It took us a bit of time to figure it out but it worked nicely. Butterbeer, $8 REALLY! The food there was okay. It was a nice place to cool off and have nice scenery. Wearing masks is very hard in the heat. Be aware. There were times when someone in our party felt ill due to it. The staff is great at cleaning. Great at reminders to distance. Since it was really empty, it was so easy to distance. We stayed at Surfside because it provided transportation and early entry. However, we found out that early entry is one park for a whole week. It was Universal Studios all week. So do not pay the extra if you want the extra hour until you know which park will have this when you visit. We visited Volcano Bay, amazing place without crowds on August 26. Islands of Adventure 27, 28 and no lines until later in day Friday. No need for Express tickets. Loved Islands of Adventure!! Also, there are areas where concessions are shut down. We just wanted water once and could not find a place. Loved they have lockers at each ride for free. Without crowds it was great. Could see it being annoying if you had to wait in lines to go to lockers and pick up stuff.

We visited Universal Studios in late July to celebrate our daughter's HS grad. We want to commend Universal for how safe they made us feel at the parks, hotels and on citywalk. Everyone kept their masks on, socially distanced and kept things clean. The only part I would have them improve on is the hand sanitizer they use in the parks smells very bad. Disney's hand sanitizer is like purell and adds something to it to make it smell pure or good. I think they must be using a cheap version and I would say for them to review what type they are forcing people to use as it stinks and feels terrible on your hands. We didn't stay at a hotel this time to get the free Universal Express as there were no huge lines. We rode rides multiple times and had a great day. There are places to rest if you want to take off your mask and eat/drink and I would advise to do a sit-down lunch. We ate at the Leaky Cauldron and the only part that was strange is you are seated and order at your table as they don't want lines outside otherwise everything was really good. The only other suggestion for Universal in general is stop making people use lockers on rides like Men in Black. I do like the new locker system since our last visit to get your items in/out as it was much quicker than the thumb scan but make sure you keep your park ticket with you to reopen your locker. Weekdays are less crowded than weekends if you are from out of town like us.
I sang there with my chorus it was really fun because afterword we got to do the whole park we had so much fun with my family.

The magic was gone with all of their restrictions. Certain attractions were closed almost no characters walking around and interacting with the kids. Better to wait until worth full price. It’s a scam I felt cheated out of my money.full park price is not worth it.Face painting is still full 15$ price for half the face when it should be whole face. Also the new policy of keeping masks on during your ENTIRE stay in the hot Florida heat was very very difficult. They do have rest areas where you can take your mask off, but that didn’t make the experience better. The entire time we were there we were being harassed by employees about the masks. You can be 10 ft away from someone or no one around at all, and there will be someone to harass you about pulling your mask up. It took away from what could have been a waaaay better experience. My husband was playing and talking but with our daughter and they told him to not lower his mask. He flipped out because he was enjoying the moment counting owls in the Harry Potter side of park with our 2 year old and the moment was ruined. Felt like we were in jail or school. Definitely won’t be coming back until restrictions are lifted.

There were many rides to go on and with the fast pass I was able to do many rides over the curse of the day. I loved going to The Wizarding World of Harry Potter as I felt it was a good representation of the movies/books and was very cool to see. The lines however can be long sometimes and the food is expensive. I feel as though it's worth it for the memories you make and the overall experiences you gain from this park. I think it is very worth it, to visit and travel here and you will not regret your decision.

My husband & I visit Universal every year. This year we were excited as we've purchased tickets in advance and planned to both have the day off. but we don't have a smart phone. Without a smartphone there are issues eating in the restaurants and going on ride because we are unable to virtual cue anything. Tried to ask this question on your website but there is no link to e-mail. We always have a super time visiting Universal Studios. This year was a disappointment. Next time we will consider spending our money somewhere else. Thanks for nothing.
Loved it, unfortunately a lot of people didn’t stay the 6ft apart, but everyone wore masks... lines were longer and took forever but for health and safety reasons I completely understand!!

Considering COVID Universal has taken great precautions with social distancing and sanitizing everyone’s hands prior to boarding rides. Feels safer than going to a Walmart. Also they still have express lines and a few virtual pass lines. They even have Characters come out and people can get selfies a safe distance away.  Sure hope CA lets them open.
The Harry Potter Theme is the best! We drived with the Hogwarts Express from one park to the other park and back (both drives are different) it was so much fun!

I was a little nervous going back to Universal as they have begun to re-open their parks again, but I greatly appreciated all of the precautions they have taken on their behalf to allow everyone to feel safe. Before we are allowed to reach the main area that checks our bags, everyone's temperature is taken and if it reaches a certain temperature, they will not allow the members to enter the park. What was great was the way that at each ride, there are painted markings on the ground that express where each person must stand to be 6 feet apart. I thought this system worked wonderfully without anything needed to be said. Everyone followed these guidelines the 4 days I was on vacation. What is also great is the way that the staff always has hand sanitizer on them and squirts a fair amount in everyone's hands right before entering the ride. Masks are required as well and everyone was doing their part. Wonderful experience overall and I felt super safe the whole trip with everyone doing their part to take the precautions that include the guests and staff!

Going to Disney in Orlando is a confusing and problematic affair. Above that the parks have been neglected for decades. But there is a new king in town and it is Universal Studios Florida. Both Universal Studios, the movie park and Islands of Adventure are worth a visit. Customer service does remind you to the old days when WDW was amazing. The team members are a delight and a spontaneous exploration of the stunning attractions and food offerings is just wonderful. Both parks offer Harry Potter themed lands and yes they are the new standard in theme park experiences with stunning decor and world class attraction and shows but the resort has so much more to offer and you would do yourself a disservice not to visit the many wonderful attractions these resorts have to offer. My favorites In Universal Studios: Harry Potter Escape from Gringotts, The Hogwarts Express (you need a 2 day or hopper pass for this one, take the 2 day pass and thank me later) The Jason Bourn stuntspectular, The Mummy, Man in Black, Transformers and E.T.. And please don't miss the Horror and Make-up show and The Blues Brothers. My favorites In Islands of Adventure: The Hulk, Spiderman, Popeye, Kong, Jurassic Park River Adventure, Hogwarts, Hagrids Motorbike Adventure and the high in the sky Seuss trolley train ride (especially at night when the Christmas decorations are up).

Absolutely adore this place! Universal Parks are definitely my theme park of choice in Orlando area. Harry Potter world is just incredible, especially Diagonal Alley that’s in this specific park. It’s jaw-dropping, literally feels like you’ve been teleported into the movie. The Escape to Gringotts ride is a great ride too. The Mummy and Rip Ride Rockit are my other favorites, just great classic roller coasters with a little added touch. Men in Black is fun to get a change of pace and go shoot down some aliens. There are a bunch of fun virtual rides like the Minion ride, Transformers, Fast and Furious, Simpsons, Shrek and more. The ET ride, hidden at the way back is super cute too and a great one for the kiddos. They also have constant shows being performed and different movie characters walking around taking pictures and interacting with people. Covid-wise I feel that they have done a great job being organized and taking needed measures. If you aren’t wearing your mask properly they are sure to politely correct you. Social distancing in lines and on rides they make sure to separate each party. They also have “U Rest” areas where you can go sit and take your mask off and get a break from it, I think that’s super considerate and I definitely used those areas a few times in my visits. I just love Universal, even though everything is overpriced (like all theme parks) the experience is always worth it and such a great time.

Harry Potter pavilion is over crowded and nobody from the administration seems to take care about it. There is no way to keep the distance because nobody controls the amount of people who are coming into the Harry Potter part of the park. If you want to get infected go there

I did not like the reservation system at Disney until I saw the alternative at Universal studios. During the holidays and probably beyond, Universal was operating at reduced capacity. Universal’s solution to determine who got in was first come, first served. Once capacity was reached, entry was closed which meant that we had to get there well before park opening time or our one day prepaid tickets would be worthless!!  The Good: At each attraction, staff applied hand sanitizer to all guests hands before and after the rides. There were plenty of hand sanitizing stations located around the park. The Leaky Cauldron had good food. The four-D rides such as Escape from Gringotts and transformers were fun. Once in the formally designated queue lines, social distancing was more achievable.  The Bad: Harry Potter World was a non-socially distanced mosh pit in the morning. Richters Burgers was mostly disappointing. The action in the transformers ride made one of our party nauseous with motion sickness.  The Ugly: The area between the security check and the entrance was a disorganized mess with no COVID protocols and two lines mashed together for the two separate park entrances.due to the urgency to get inside the parks before capacity was reached led to some bad crowd behavior. Fortunately we didn’t have to try to get a refund of non refundable tickets because we got in. We entered around 7:30. The park reached capacity at 8:10 AM, ten minutes past the published opening time! If we hadn’t heard that they were letting people enter early, we may not have made it in. The TV new ran stories on the rush to get in the day before we visited and warned people to get there early, which probably helped overwhelm the entry lines.  Clearly Universal was not prepared to handle crowds while trying to limit park capacity. Fortunately nobody in our party has contracted COVID in the subsequent weeks after our visit so we made it through. However we were worried about the potential exposure we faced at Universal.

Unfortunately we wish we would have done something else with our day. Long lines- two hour waits (we didn’t pay extra for express pass) for rides. In 9 hours (and $400 plus for three people) we experienced two “rides”. Loved the Harry Potter area and the butter beer- some rides were “at capacity” and so we were turned away after waiting in line??? Even with long long long lines.  To be successful at Universal and see everything - you need to pay more to get the express tickets.  Rides were socially distant - lots of “hall monitors” who were reminding people about mask wearing at all times. People seen cleaning but without limiting access to the park overall- it just made lines longer and longer with socially distant rides.  At least the weather got better - after it poured with heavy rain that morning- but overall a waste of time and money. I was looking forward to going, it’s unfortunate that it wasn’t a better experience.
Excellent it was well worth the money. Be careful though. We accidentally entered Adventure Island and meant to enter Universal Studios.

We are staying on resort for four days. The accommodations are comfortable and convenient. Where things go south are at the theme parks. Poor signage that makes it difficult to navigate the parks. Overcrowded! We were under the impression that the parks were open but with reduced capacity. That did not appear to be the case. Wall to wall people with ride times that were 1-2 hour waits. There was always the option to purchase Express Passes, but due to high demand Universal jacked up the prices for 3 Express passes to $900+. Not that the Mouse is less greedy, but it’s more organized and they still offer limited Fast Passes. We won’t be returning. Moving forward we will stick with the Mouse.

If you purchase your ticket at the gate please keep in mind that no discounts will be honored for a one day visit. It doesn't matter who you are a member of. They push for multi day and multi park specials. There are some attractions that are closed for the kids. Wood Pecker Village was mostly closed. We spent one day at Universal and Islands of Adventure with the park to park tickets. 2 adults and 2 kids age 11 and 8. We stayed one night at Hard Rock Hotel, which included the Express Passes and despite the high price they were worth EVERY PENNY! As expected, the parks were packed because of it being spring break season. We never would’ve been able to ride all that we did without the Express Passes. We had early access due to staying on Universal property and went straight to Hagrids Motorbike. The longest we waited all day was 2 hours for Hagrids, but no passes can be used on that ride. Otherwise, we waited between 0 and 15 minutes the rest of the day, riding every ride we wanted to. It was a great day with lots of memories made!  I would like to give credit to Nelson and Dan at the Raptor Encounter. We waited in the line for about 25 min and were rushed through by the man running the encounter. I wanted a photo of my kids together and then one of each of them separately. My son also wanted the separate photo because he loves Jurassic World and didn’t want his sister in his picture with Blue! Lol. Anyway, we were rushed through before I could take the separate photos. My husband spoke with Nelson and Dan at the entrance to the encounter about what happened and Nelson told us to come back at a specific time and we could get our photos. When my husband brought the kids back, Nelson gave them a private encounter with a baby raptor, as well as another chance at photos with Blue. He went above and beyond for us. Amazing customer service!!!! We were beyond pleased!

TLDR; They don’t observe or enforce Covid safety precautions and the limited park hours and long wait times make the trip a waste of time and money.  We went on April 26th and as soon as we walked up to the entrance, it was chaos. I wish I had taken a photo because I hadn’t seen a crowd like this since before Covid. I was shoulder to shoulder with unmasked strangers and did not see a single Universal employee in sight until we were at the main entrance to City Walk getting our temperature checked. At that point, the poor women checking temperatures were screaming at people to form a line. Everything in me was telling me to turn around and just ask for a refund, but I hoped it would get better once we got into the park.  Trying to get into the park wasn’t any easier, there were no guides to show us where to go and things were extremely backed up.  Once in the park, we figured we’d wait until wait times for Harry Potter rides went down and decided to ride some of the rides closer to the front of the park. The first line we get into was stress-inducing and made me want to leave right away. We begged people to observe the markings on the ground and keep a safe distance from us, but it wasn’t happening. People were taking their masks off in line when Universal employees were out of site (which I rarely even saw employees anyway) and even eating in line. We were unable to distance from the people in the lines to the left and right of where we stood and much preferred Disney’s plexiglass shields in these situations to Universals lack of dividers. It was loud (even for a musician that is hard of hearing) and the people in line with us were obnoxious and rude.  The whole reason we came to Universal was for Wizarding World of Harry Potter, but wait times were always over 75 minutes (or higher) and the Harry Potter parts of the park were always over crowded that we decided to keep our distance. It’s obvious they weren’t limited capacity. Everywhere we went, we were dodging people and trying to distance ourselves from others with no luck or reciprocated efforts.  After riding ONE Harry Potter ride (and not even the one we wanted to ride), we ended our day early and literally ran to the car to get out as fast as we could. Our experience was not worth the money for the ticket or the stress we endured throughout the park.  Honestly, we were shocked. Our experiences at the Disney parks were incredible as the staff went above and beyond to make sure Covid safety precautions were being followed and enforced. We never felt uncomfortable and rode every ride we wanted in every park with wait times under 45 minutes.

My husband and I visited Universal a couple years ago and had a fantastic time. This trip didn’t meet those expectations. The rides IF/WHEN you got to them met our expectations. Several were closed for most of the day. Temps hit 95 all days we were there. You were forced to wear a mask all the time except when you were “actively eating or drinking in a stationary spot.” The Express Passes ruined our visit. I get it the Express People paid extra, but there needs to be limits to give the Gen Pop a fair chance at the rides. A 25 min wait at the train turned into a 70 min wait in the hot dungeon with our faces covered. People were dropping from the heat.  Places to eat and drink experiences long, slow, never-ending lines of people waiting in the sun. Since our last visit, Universal has added two huge hotels and two new, modern rollercoasters, but no new places to get food and drink. The park has limited infrastructure and the visitors needs need to be addressed too.  We stayed at Endless Summer hotel which was very nice, but the lobby stayed warm due to all the people. (It was only 1/2 full too.) Pier 8 offered some reasonably priced food items. Some items we wish we could have used, but we had no microwave in our room. :.( Staff members were friendly and courteous. We also had to buy coffee in the park since we don’t drink Starbucks and we also didn’t have a coffee maker in our room.  We chose this time because school was still in session. Ha! Can you say “virtual learning!” We cut our vacation short by a day. Between the heat, masks, and crowds, we’d had enough.
